content.line: First cup's on the house — after that you owe the room your evenings.
content.name: Noll, the Warm Door
content.description: A broad man easing a propped door shut with one hip, a handcart of mismatched chairs trundling behind him — legs that have outlived their makers' makers, every wobble known to him by name.

content.line: Third landing's lamp again — the widow wakes before the sun-strip does. Someone ought to tell the dark it's wasting its patience.
content.name: Ymma, Nine Knots
content.description: A relay runner in drowned-teal who consults her own wrist like a timetable, granting every threshold the courtesy of a glance and none the courtesy of a pause.

content.line: The ship always lays one extra setting. Our whole art is pretending that was our idea.
content.name: Gorse, of the Third Place
content.description: Gorse rights a chair no one saw fall and keeps walking, unhurried as copper cooling; behind her the long table, grown whole from the deck, sets itself one more place than there are guests. This is, apparently, normal.

content.line: The gold takes its tithe in skin. I only decide whose.
content.name: Femora, the Unblistered
content.description: She moves down the ward through the ambient gold without squinting, both hands salved to the second knuckle, and the fevered turn their bandaged faces toward her the way green things turn toward a light they cannot survive at closer range.

content.line: She can hoard the light-rig all she pleases — come next fruiting this takes hold, and then we'll see who owes whom the window.
content.name: Yolda Trask, Second Sleep
content.description: One of the two who split the dawn-side bunkroom above the graft-sheds crosses the walkway with a rooted cutting held like contraband, her jaw already set for the evening's small border war.

content.line: One true measure for every comer, hands of unknown make included — the court's whole law, kept alive now in a spout.
content.name: Osk, Evenpour
content.description: Osk strides the gantry in the far-off gleam of the long table, a folding bench under one arm and the even-measure rod through his belt, bound to set a tap-room down wherever the night's wanderers have gathered. His fame rests on a single trick: the same true measure for every hand that asks, which is its own quiet judgment.

content.line: Patience is only light that hasn't arrived yet.
content.name: Oyne, Wet-Sleeve
content.description: She crosses with a tray of algae starter held to her sternum like something overhearing, water ticking off her cuffs in patient ship-time; the green smells of tidal mornings nobody aboard has ever stood in.

content.line: Forty years I dusted that man's shelf, and by morning the silver's settled back on it, thin as an apology. Nothing in this deep will let you finish — I've stopped calling that mercy.
content.name: Maugret, Widow of Stack Nine
content.description: Old bones under a shawl the color of tarnish, a ring of keys at her hip that fit doors no map admits to. She does not hurry; nothing down here that matters is in a rush.

content.line: Still there. Good. Hold.
content.name: Towl, Underlock
content.description: A broad young man in a rust-red coat pauses at a wall the Commons takes for blank, lays two fingers on a mark nobody else can see as though taking the stonework's pulse, and is gone before the crowd has noticed him at all.

content.line: Taut, never tight — the whole faith lives in that difference, if your hands are schooled enough to hear it.
content.name: Wray, Latticehand
content.description: Shoulders a spool of drawn copper through the doorway like a woman hauling water from a far well, the loom's half-woven harness unspooling behind her across the floor. Her knuckles have taken the color of her wire.

content.line: Not everything found was lost, stranger. Some things get put by.
content.name: Hemmel, Dustwage
content.description: A spare old man with a granary scoop hanging at his belt drifts past trailing hearth-smoke and machine oil, his gaze traveling you the way a tally travels freight — itemized, weighed, concluded.

content.line: Eleven times this same quarrel has been settled; it is the settling, not the answer, that keeps the deck from rolling.
content.name: Quist, the Old-Wax
content.description: A stooped arbiter crosses toward the council hall with a folio pressed to her breastbone like a reliquary, fingers stained seal-blue to the second knuckle, citing gravamen numbers under her breath.

content.line: Slate sashes at the Ward-Three lift, two deep and counting — take the cart-line if you'd sooner not be counted.
content.name: Grike, Never-Late
content.description: A runner cuts the ward-crossing so close the wind of her going arrives a half-breath after she has, chalk dust on her shins, braid-cord snapping at her wrist. She is already at the far arch when her words catch up.

content.line: Third seam this week that sings when I pass. Iron doesn't sing for nothing — it sings for whoever's listening.
content.name: Skew, Nine-Passes
content.description: She walks the catwalk's spine with a torch slung like a censer, counting under her breath — passes, plates, seasons — and does not look into the dark below, having settled long ago the question of who would win.

content.line: First cup says you came. Second cup says you stayed. The garden only ever counts seconds.
content.name: Ulme, the Second Cup
content.description: Ulme crosses the gantry with a tray laid for five though he walks alone, and far below a canopy exhales — the fifth cup shivers, obediently, as if it had already been claimed. He does not look down.

content.line: He stirs when the lamps gutter, so they say. Mine gutter every night.
content.name: Ossel, the Uncalled
content.description: A widow crossing with cupped candle-ends, her shadow thrown tall against the judgment-wall and ranked like a magistrate's. Forty years she has petitioned the silence and never once been entered on the docket.

content.line: I've a pin for every failure but the last one. Nobody stocks for that.
content.name: Skeld, the Pinhoard
content.description: Skeld crosses the threshold already sorting, thumbing the little drawers of a chest-harness that clatters like weather — every pin, ferrule and drift labeled in hull-notation older than the ward.

content.line: Venus is generous this season — two harvests where one was promised, and nobody asking why.
content.name: Vrumma, Quiet Axles
content.description: She passes beneath a green-deck load, handcart wheels hushed as a held breath, tallying with one glance every door that has opened since the sun-strip brightened. To her the corridor is a manifest, each face a weight to be balanced against a destination.

content.line: I don't sell what's in the tray, sweetling — I sell what's new since the tray last came round.
content.name: Bex, the Spool
content.description: Her trays hold nothing but thread and grey salt, yet every stallholder leans as she passes, as if the goods were beside the point — which, of course, they are.

content.line: Postponement, kept beautifully, is continuance in its work-clothes; rupture is the only hurry I fear.
content.name: Brem, Adjourned
content.description: A hearing-officer passes with a satchel fattened on undecided cases, lifting two fingers to the corridor at large as though continuing everything in absentia.

content.line: You were written before you were woken. I can smell the ink of it.
content.name: Thurl, the Unfiled
content.description: She passes beneath a wickless lamp fed by some patient leak of the machinery she has forsworn to describe, lips moving through a nuncupative rite — spoken once, never written, for ink is how the grey keeper takes count.

content.line: Lovely seaming on you, stranger — I'd give a year of my hands for ten minutes with that needle.
content.name: Storn Vayle, the Seamer
content.description: Tall in deep blue, she prices each passing body with a glance that has weighed amputation and first-breath in the same ledger — and you she reads twice, the second time slower.

content.line: Honest tare, honest teem — weigh me twice if you must, but the third weighing belongs to the ship.
content.name: Cratch, Half-Gross
content.description: A dray-porter crossing the square with a steelyard swinging from one fist, lips moving through subtraction the way the devout move through orisons. Everything he passes is briefly, insensibly lighter.

content.line: Say the last word for me as I pass, stranger — I've forgotten whom it addresses.
content.name: Thren, the Amenless
content.description: Her copper regalia has gone the grey of lead-dust, and every orison she mouths founders a syllable short of its close, as though the final word had been recalled by its maker.

content.line: Whole deck dreamt of drowning again last night. I told it plain: not on my floor.
content.name: Skell, of the Small Hours
content.description: A broad, deliberate man drifting bed to bed with a basin he never once sets down, as though the carrying were the cure. He was here when the shift began; no one recalls him arriving, and the lamps dim a shade as he passes, in deference or fatigue.

content.line: Up one again, and nobody dead. You mark me — the deep has begun counting something it never counted before.
content.name: Vetch, Widow of the Low Stair
content.description: A widow in lead-grey wool crosses her threshold with a household slate, pausing where the wall's oldest notation runs one stroke fresher than yesterday. She raps the new mark twice, the way one knocks a wicket for an explanation.

content.line: Third sowing of the cycle and the loam comes up the same. I take comfort in that. Mostly.
content.name: Grem, Thirdsow
content.description: A soil-cart grinds past, its pusher unhurried as settling sediment, nails gone the black-green of loam older than any name he knows. He nods to no one, which in the Nave is a kind of courtesy.

content.line: You're on no manifest I carry. No matter — half my stock isn't either.
content.name: Grike, Deadstock
content.description: Grike hauls a sledge of unclaimed goods past the chalk tallies climbing every doorframe like ivy, pausing for nothing. As he goes he touches each wax seal in passing — a rosary of rims.

content.line: Deck after deck after deck — tonight the mender counted one past the end of the schematic, and kept counting.
content.name: Perrow Quoil, the Intake
content.description: A small man at the fast walk, the isolation ward's cold still clinging to him like a wet hem, his face mid-transit into the calm he keeps for whoever is carried in next.

content.line: New square on the board since last night, and nobody I know dealt it.
content.name: Quilth, Widdershins
content.description: She walks against the corridor's grain, fingers yare in a cat's-cradle strung with every route she has ever run, and reads the ward the way gamblers read dice — by the weight of what does not show.

content.line: Held the whole night through without me — good. It noticed.
content.name: Skarn, Who-Counts
content.description: A broad shape bent under a harness of labeled cannisters, pausing at each bulkhead seam to lay one grey finger against the metal as though taking a pulse, then walking on before the answer can settle.

content.line: Everything loosens. Not a flaw, mind — a schedule.
content.name: Thack, Sparewise
content.description: A grey-braided mender wheels a cabinet of sorted salvage past the bench, one palm resting on its lid the way the devout touch relics; the cart shrieks on a wheel she has plainly chosen not to mend.

content.line: Mind your wick, stray light. There comes a trimming not of your choosing.
content.name: Aumbry, Who Answers
content.description: Old past reckoning, she walks the long gallery with her lamp hooded and unlit — since the heart last spoke, they say — pausing for nothing, though her shadow hesitates, one beat, opposite you.

content.line: Paid in regard again this cycle. Regards don't chew, whatever the brokers say.
content.name: Rud, Half-Leathers
content.description: A young man in leathers shed to the waist crosses the gallery at the appetite-led trot of the young who share a bunk and a grudge, soot to the knuckle and supper somewhere ahead of him.

content.line: The hum keeps his pauses. You'd think a thing that never sleeps would trouble itself to learn new ones.
content.name: Bryl, the Seam-Nine Widow
content.description: The one unhurried thing in the artery: a widow moving at the pace of the seam she has always lived against, as if speed were a courtesy owed elsewhere. The hum bends faintly around her, the way it does around things it has learned not to startle.

content.line: Seven, three times running, and there's no seven on it. I'm choosing to call that applause.
content.name: Tolve, Whom the Dice Follow
content.description: A broad figure pacing the long table's rim, rolling a die along the rail — he watches it go, and it is already home in his palm again, unhurried as an animal.

content.line: The count stands whether you do or not.
content.name: Mauk, the Long-Count
content.description: Mauk crosses the square with a slate beneath one arm and forty years of other people's reckonings chalked into the creases of her knuckles; conversation thins around her the way water does near a keel.

content.line: Light came up shy this morning. Whatever's stirring — and something is — it isn't in the tea; that I'd swear.
content.name: Hetta, Never-Empty
content.description: A broad woman in slate apron-cloth, ferrying a lidded urn at the pace of someone who has never once spilled, her eye ticking to the sun-strip as if to a pulse. The pot she keeps has not gone dry in forty years; the Nave calls it luck, and she lets them.

content.line: Ten and my silence for the sealed one — don't shake it, sealed means sleeping. Done, done, thank you — I was never here.
content.name: Skell, Crosshand
content.description: She passes the way freight passes: a lean blur of straps and seals, and every hand she brushes is left holding something or having just paid for it. The knotted cord at her wrist tells a route no one else could walk.

content.line: It tips before the weight arrives. I've stopped trusting the grams and started trusting the direction.
content.name: Ostry, Silverweight
content.description: A stocky figure with a beam-scale slung at the hip like a sidearm, weighing nothing, watching the needle lean toward passages she has not yet chosen to enter.

content.line: The widow's owed a word from down-axle. I don't carry it yet — but I've come nearer than the silence has.
content.name: Rivke, the Twice-Yearly
content.description: Shears at her hip and a satchel smelling of salt and far stations, she goes by as she always goes by — twice a year, and never once overnight.

content.line: Eleven hundred strands to the hand-width and still they say finer. Fine for what — nobody asks, and I've quit pretending not to notice.
content.name: Tolva, Drawplate
content.description: A wire-drawer threads the colonnade trailing a spool behind her like a leashed eel, fingertips scoured to a fine silver burr, the ship-smell riding her leathers thicker than the street's own.

content.line: Motion to adjourn — seconded by the silence, carried without a count. Entered.
content.name: Tarrow, the Standing Adjournment
content.description: A grey functionary ferries a writ-roll down the aisle of a court that has not convened in living generations, bowing at intervals to benches taller than doors as though they might return the courtesy. The roll never shortens, and she has long since stopped expecting it to.

content.line: Hands don't lie. Yours haven't learned how yet.
content.name: Dree, Heddle
content.description: Small and ancient, iron braid pinned up like a tool, she thumbs a bobbin of drawn copper the length of the corridor, testing each span against a gauge only her hands can read.

content.line: New work in you, that. Whoever fitted it bought spares twice over, and such folk never come back for the mending.
content.name: Hasp, Who Owes No One a Part
content.description: Hasp goes by with a garniture of fittings nested like eggs, every knuckle varnished brown with old rust, and never breaking stride thumbs a trembling lamp-bracket back to rights. The worn things of the ward lean toward her the way the unloved lean toward anyone who has ever kept them.

content.line: Light turned a half-minute early on the green decks tonight. Seedlings know before councils do — and councils will be the last to admit it.
content.name: Haugh, Eleven Seasons
content.description: The scent of turned loam reaches the corridor a breath before she does, and she moves with the mild inevitability of weather already decided. Her nails are stained to the quick with loam, and the tray of struck cuttings at her hip she carries the way other folk carry relics.

content.line: The edge holds because I hold it. Nobody thanks the selvage until the whole cloth goes.
content.name: Ymme, Selvage-Hand
content.description: She passes through the threshold trailing gold wire from a shuttle that drinks the heartlight, hemming the rim of something far too large for any loom.

content.line: Up's empty and down's full. Ship's thinking something.
content.name: Drost, Halfway Down
content.description: One boot on the descending plate, one on the landing, she calls a stranger's floor before the stranger admits to having one. Motion is her only address, and she keeps it well.

content.line: Wove it neutral, wove it true. Let the buyers quarrel over whose thread sits on top.
content.name: Nebb, Half-Reed
content.description: A weaver cuts across the square bent beneath a bolt of three-colored stripe — writ-blue, copper, bazaar-gold — the selvage woven so even no faction could swear the cloth its own. Her lips shape warp-counts she stopped needing to say aloud years ago.

content.line: Strip goes dim and the vats answer instead. Something on these decks keeps its own sun.
content.name: Keld, the Underglass
content.description: A silhouette wading the vat-walk with a siphon coil at one shoulder, haloed bottle-green by vats that brighten as the sun-strip dims behind them.

content.line: They confess only one sin in the Nave: they looked up. I've stopped asking them not to.
content.name: Kelme, the Doubt-Hearer
content.description: A grey listener parts the market throng with a slate of unheard confessions held against her chest like a door she has forgotten how to knock on, her bare feet reading the cold tile.

content.line: I asked the deep shelf for my mother's face. It gave me yours. Tell it I am not ready.
content.name: Threl, the Twice-Slept
content.description: She walks as one carries a brimming bowl, eyes fixed on nothing, hair furred with the cold of the stacks, a stylus between her teeth gone unworn from disuse. She passes through the hour when the corridor stops insisting it is a corridor.

content.line: Six in, five out. The fifth shelf has started to lie.
content.name: Ossa, Chalkwrist
content.description: An old woman stoops beneath a barrow of stoppered jars, shawl pinned with copper gone green at the points, forearms chalked to the elbow in tallies only she can read; her lips keep a count that never consents to land.

content.line: Still two cups. Quiet, they call it, down the shaft. Quiet is a house with everyone gone.
content.name: Thava, Widow of the Ninth Landing
content.description: Passes with a horn of keys and the unhurried tread of a woman whose table has long kept a second place; in the heart's unsetting gold there is no dusk for grief to fold itself into.

content.line: Landlady counts my stay in weeks; the Drift reckon in nights. Her arithmetic will still be standing here come morning — mine won't.
content.name: Harsk, Sleeps Standing
content.description: A broad man subletting sleep one night at a time, his entire possession of this corridor a chalk mark on the doorframe and a bag buckled since before he arrived.

content.line: Tongue off the seam, Sprig — it heard you the first time, and it never forgets a compliment.
content.name: Vosk, Off the Splice
content.description: A splicer off the trunk, one child asleep against his collar and another orbiting at tongue's-reach of the walls, supper going cold in his fist. He carries his household the way one carries news — carefully, and glad of somewhere to set it down.

content.line: Junk, they called it. Nothing is junk — some things are merely between mends.
content.name: Svalt, the Untossed
content.description: Dragging a handcart of ostensibly useless things down the corridor's throat, patient as sediment. He has never in his life discarded anything, and he does not intend to begin for the sake of appearances.

content.line: Eighty-one hinges between here and the shrine, and every one a question I keep answering.
content.name: Brask, Called Hinges
content.description: A broad man in rust-rinsed cord, thumbing a tallow sudarium along every hinge between himself and wherever he is going, as if movement itself required his pardon. The market parts for him with the tolerance owed a harmless, punctual madman.

content.line: Sixty years sealed and the weight's off by a hand's breadth. I stopped writing the difference down — let the shelves keep one secret of their own.
content.name: Sarn, Longcount
content.description: A narrow man wheeling his barrow of dream-wafers up the silver aisle, thumb travelling a tally-stick older than his own name, counting a stock that has lately begun to disagree with him.

content.line: Gutter all you like. I'll be here tomorrow.
content.name: Thole, Third-Lamp
content.description: An old woman crosses in felt slippers, her dead man's file wrapped in waxcloth under one arm, oiled nightly against a rust that would be, though she'd never say it, a kind of company. She relights the guttering third lamp in its niche without breaking stride.

content.line: Debt's the one cargo that weighs nothing going down and all of it coming back — the machinery down there keeps better books than I ever did.
content.name: Pont, the Owed-and-Owing
content.description: An old porter crossing the gantry under crates lashed to a rig of borrowed struts, reciting debts aloud in the flat cadence other men reserve for prayer.

content.line: The seam holds. Everything else is commentary.
content.name: Twill, of the Standing Seam
content.description: She crosses the threshold the way a householder crosses her own floor, unhurried, trailing flux and hot copper, and the weld-bead beneath her boots — wide as a road, bright along its crest — seems to stand a little taller as she passes.

content.line: Both seals weigh the same. That's the trick of the office, and maybe the mercy.
content.name: Uxma, Two-Seals
content.description: A writ-officer with a stamp on either hip — one to grant, one to refuse — walking like a woman who stopped wondering which is heavier.

content.line: Knock but softly, knock but few — the gold's awake and counting you.
content.name: Skirr, of the Short Ways
content.description: A child skimming the corridor's seam with someone's clean laundry bundled in both arms, pausing for nothing — not the heat, not you, not the doorways standing open on rooms the light has never left.

content.line: Back already, Mol? Kettle's boiled — you've gone thin, all that climbing.
content.name: Tulloch, the Half-Deaf
content.description: An old man ferrying a spindle-backed chair through the gold heat, deaf in the manner of one who spent his working years beside a heart that never once stopped speaking; he does not wait to be corrected.

content.line: Sleep, love. You read the hull truer dreaming than the council does waking.
content.name: Wick, Boots-Off
content.description: A broad man comes down the landing soft-footed, boots swinging from one fist by their laces, a sleeping child folded over his shoulder. He murmurs hull-marks over it in the cadence of a psalter — splay, weld, turn.

content.line: New face, old ports. The Braid pays for the second and asks nothing about the first.
content.name: Vosk, Tollgate
content.description: He crosses the threshold at a lope, borrowed indices fanned along one forearm, and pays the doorway a single breath of attention — the only toll he has ever honored.

content.line: Twice budded since potting. Keep your own calendar then, littling — I'll keep your water.
content.name: Vetch, Twicebud
content.description: Crosses the gantry with a flat of seedlings already in flower, unhurried beneath trellises that arch away past sight; the copper light takes her grey braid and returns it warm.

content.line: It held through the night cycle. Held is the whole of the sermon.
content.name: Torv, Cinderwise
content.description: Crosses past the quench-trough with a seam-specimen hissing in her bare fist, sleeves charred to the elbow. She reads the weld's grain the way a priest reads scripture — lips moving, unhurried, certain.

content.line: Cull early, grieve once — what can't hold its row was never yours.
content.name: Mib, Thrice-Thinned
content.description: Soil crescented under every nail, an old grower thins a neighbor's seedling rack without breaking stride, wearing the calm of a man who has buried three plantings and kept the count.

content.line: Doors still open for you, do they? Mind it — a door that remembers you is a door that files reports.
content.name: Skender, Forty Keys
content.description: He crosses the threshold in a soft avalanche of iron, landlord to forty bunks he has never once slept in, counting doors the way other men count years.

content.line: Wire's sung flat since the postings changed. I don't trust my weight to a cable I can't tune.
content.name: Vant, Slack-Rope
content.description: He rides the lift-cage's outer rail rather than the cage, one bare hand against the humming wire, reading its tremor like a vatic text; between bells he is simply nowhere at all.

content.line: Winners bank and go still. It's the beaten who keep moving.
content.name: Croy, Tumbled-Twice
content.description: A tally-thin man chalking last night's forfeits onto a ward wall as he passes, his own name twice-underlined; in his economy, esteem spends longest when it is owed.

content.line: The axial fog held its tongue all morning. Silence is also a verdict.
content.name: Vosk, the Omensitter
content.description: A rail-thin man threads the colonnade with a fist of welded hull-beads strung on brass wire, shaking them once — a sound like pebbles deciding.

content.line: Sixty years and it's never had the manners to change, this corridor — mind you don't come to find that restful.
content.name: Hulde, Nine-Doors
content.description: A slate-shawled widow whose keyring outweighs her tenancy, crossing the sempiternal corridor at the pace of one who has outlived every quarrel in it. The ship smell rides her wool like weather she has stopped noticing.

content.line: Three to one the lights dim before you find your bed, fresh face — the house is very old, and the house dims first.
content.name: Siv, Long-Odds
content.description: Siv crosses the square at a gambler's lope, working a route-cord through her fingers like a rosary she only half believes in, dice clicking in her other fist with the patience of held breath.

content.line: Third kettle this season. The deep keeps what it likes, and it's growing a taste.
content.name: Thole, the Kettlekeeper
content.description: An old man dusts a shelf of kettles left by teams that went deeper and never filed, polishing each lid as though tenure were a kind of tenderness. He is the landing's unwritten census of the missing.

content.line: Nobody wrote them down. We keep them anyway.
content.name: Cadge, Even-Handed
content.description: Cadge circles the open court with her palms open and empty, and the players consent beforehand to whatever she will say; half the rules were lost before anyone's grandmother played, and she is where the missing halves get decided.

content.line: Not due in any book I keep — walk on, discrepancy, before someone comes to reconcile you.
content.name: Meech, the Null Entry
content.description: A narrow clerk gliding between cart-drays with a ledger strapped to the chest like a breastplate, writing in rows that already read blank. Where they pass, the count comes out even, and nobody can say why.

content.line: No scuff, no rust — you'll want some on those boots before anyone here trusts them.
content.name: Skerry, Ask-Again
content.description: A young lodger slips past with route-charts rolled into her collar, lips moving through notation she has no sanction to want. Her knuckles are inked where she practices the old marks on her own skin.

content.line: Third posting this week that won't parse. Mercury writes like weather — but lately the weather means something.
content.name: Osla, Nineknots
content.description: She threads the reading-room stacks without lifting her eyes, thumb walking the knotted cord at her wrist the way other scholars walk a page — the Braid rendered in string, route-history knotted tight as liturgy.

content.line: Leave the old ports be. Some stitches are promises.
content.name: Sib Fenn, Third-Shift
content.description: A night-ward nurse going off rotation, hand-lamp still burning out of habit against the dimming of the sun-strip; chalk and boiled linen trail her. Her gaze makes one unblinking pass across your unstandard ports and declines, gently, to have seen them.

content.line: 'It stutters at the ninth rib,' she tells the corridor, delighted. 'Somebody write that down before I forgive it.'
content.name: Skirr, Half-Beat
content.description: A thin figure writes as she walks, stylus chasing the artery's hum across a wire-slat — a glossator taking dictation from weather, faithful always to the half-beat lag.

content.line: The reports stopped because there was nothing left to tell. Nothing down there has ever broken, and that is the one heresy I can't mend.
content.name: Wale, Who Came Back
content.description: Wale crosses the threshold like a draft of cleading-cold, chalking a seam-mark on the jamb without looking, and the corridor's chatter leans away from her. She is the only one of the survey crews the deep gave back.

content.line: When the court sits I'm first witness — I've said the whole oath four hundred times to the table's legs.
content.name: Pim, Benchborn
content.description: A child hugging the corridor's margin, chalk on both cuffs, rehearsing an oath in whispers — hand raised, palm flat, sworn to something enormous that has never once sat in her lifetime. Ninth of her line born on the benches, and she intends to be first called.

content.line: Same weight going down as coming up. That's the whole trick of the trade, and no one ever believes me.
content.name: Vair, Two Fares
content.description: Twice a day he passes, once each way, laden identically both times, and swears the corridor runs shorter downhill — a claim nobody has troubled to disprove.

content.line: That seam you're ignoring has two days left in it. Bench opens at the noon-bell — don't let it beat you here.
content.name: Njell, Nine Spares
content.description: Small and abundant with pockets, threading the colonnade like a shuttle through cloth, every loop of her apron holding some future failure in miniature. Regulars greet her; she answers by counting their wobbling cart-wheels.

content.line: The count has stood still a season now — a held breath in a ledger is louder than any number.
content.name: Quire, Waits-on-the-Count
content.description: Quire crosses the counting-floor with an armful of blank vellum and a lamp trimmed to burn without flicker, bound on an errand no one assigned aloud. The walls around her carry notation older than the Nave's oldest rite, and she has stopped pretending not to read it in passing.

content.line: We don't save lives, we save the handoff — say it until it stops sounding cold.
content.name: Sylene Wend, the Cautery
content.description: She passes the ward doors at the pace of settling ballast, hands smelling of clove and sterile ash, and the grief of tonight's third closed chest rides her the way pressure rides the hull — structurally, and without comment.

content.line: Trim them low before the strip dims. The ceiling goes dark when we do, and the dark borrows more light than it ever gives back.
content.name: Prew, the Wickwright
content.description: A lampwright swings past with a testing-rack of pinprick flames at her hip, each wick cut to a different hour, so the little rack reads like a dusk sliced into installments.

content.line: Third roster audit this season. They count every soul on this deck except the ones they sent below.
content.name: Dunn, Halfshift
content.description: A broad man off his half of the shift, sleeping child at his collar and a solder-mended kettle under one arm, council-blue washed to the color of evening; he walks like a man rehearsing a grievance he will never file.

content.line: Every game is the ship talking to itself — lose, and you have still been spoken to.
content.name: Onno, the Host
content.description: Onno slips along the colonnade's edge with a lacquered case of tiles under one arm, saluting the dark game-hall doors the way the devout salute altars, never breaking stride.

content.line: You walk like it was taught back to you. Come by the ward if the floor starts feeling foreign — it does that, to some.
content.name: Solvej Brann, the Long Vigil
content.description: Passes with a folded cot under one arm the way other women carry infants, counting names under her breath — the ward's dead, told over like beads.

content.line: The terminals spoke newly this morning, and new is dearer than true. One regard buys the words; two, and I'll swear I never said them.
content.name: Wray, Evermid
content.description: You catch her mid-sentence with one stranger and mid-sentence again with you, a rumor changing hands at the temperature of a secret. She is neither buying nor selling — or both, and profitably.

content.line: Bolt nothing in this ward — the crews will come up hungry, and I'd rather be caught waiting than caught locked.
content.name: Torv, the Unclosed
content.description: An old steward in deep blue walking the ward's threshold with a ring of keys he no longer needs, leaving every door he passes a hand's width open behind him.

content.line: …worship, govern, move, store — then learn, first and last; the other twelve are only rooms.
content.name: Gled, the Unwritten
content.description: A spare woman crosses the room with her eyes half-shut and both hands keeping slow tally on her thighs, reciting the thirteen verbs the way other people breathe. Nothing on her is written down; everything is carried.

content.line: Welcome first, even in a hall this size. Even the empty table is owed its warmth.
content.name: Sorl, Six-Cups
content.description: Sorl crosses the gallery with a black kettle at her hip and six cups chiming in a wire cradle on her back, steam unspooling into air gone cold as only a continent of iron can make it. They call her Six-Cups because wherever she sets down, the cold finds itself outnumbered.

content.line: He won't sit. He never sits. So I sit for him, and nobody objects.
content.name: Bink, Held in Contempt
content.description: A child threads the bench-megaliths dragging a rind-gavel half her size, holding court for an audience of dust motes and one indifferent vastness. Her verdicts land crisp as chipped flint.

content.line: Cull them small, before something older down-deck takes a notion to.
content.name: Sorb, the Thinner
content.description: Comes down the long rows shearing seedlings in passing, never pausing, leaving small wilted heaps on the dark loam; the rows run on toward the axial haze like a field rehearsing weather.

content.line: 'Slower,' he tells the wall, in the tone of a man correcting a dear colleague who has begun to outrun the conversation.
content.name: Skarn, the Collator
content.description: An old scholar crosses the threshold with a folio hugged to his chest and pauses at the seam — not to rest, but to lay page against wall, comparing two hands divided by more years than any lineage aboard can claim.

content.line: A spare is a promise made to something still whole. I make mine early.
content.name: Stann, Deeppocket
content.description: Trudging at the pace of a person long since certain the corridor intends to hold, a folded repair-bench strapped to their back like a reliquary. Small things chime in the coat's deep folds — spares for machines nobody living remembers owning.

content.line: Don't count along with me. It answers one voice only.
content.name: Tarn, Counting Still
content.description: He chalks each slow pulse of the stasis machinery along his forearm — the one ledger, he believes, the deep has not read — timing the breath of a thing that perennates without witness.

content.line: Pardon — pardon — by noon you'll be a story in five wards. Eat now, while you're still a guest.
content.name: Brude, Beg-Pardon
content.description: A thin man threading the crowd with an empty tray held high, murmuring pardon to shoulders before they can touch him. His courtesy is so long-practiced it has worn channels in him, the way feet wear stairs.

content.line: That squeal's deliberate. Down here, silence is the sound of something going wrong.
content.name: Vrum, Ten-Thousand
content.description: Old Vrum shoves a repair bench ahead of him on wheels, one squealing by deliberate omission, a cargo of half-alive lamps and spare hinges roped down like livestock.

content.line: Coin rusts and writ burns, friend — pay me in standing; regard keeps better than tin.
content.name: Ilvess, the Ledgerless
content.description: She deals without slate or writ, every price kept in a head older than her face. Her mouth never stops — half barter, half benediction — and she has never once needed to be paid twice.

content.line: Three months the deep's been quiet as unplanted ground. Nothing sleeps that well without dreaming of waking.
content.name: Awn, of the Third Rotation
content.description: At every threshold he rests a palm against the doorframe a moment, reading it as one reads bark for blight, and passes on without once looking back. What he tends has outlived every name now on the ward writ and will outlive his; he finds this neither grief nor miracle, only the work.

content.line: Not on the schematic, so it has no precedent, so it has no standing — nothing to sign, nothing to sign.
content.name: Lunt, the Underwrit
content.description: A young man ferries his folio against his chest like an infant, threading the corridor with eyes down, as though the walls were reading over his shoulder.

content.line: Hurry the leaf and you serve only water. Everything true in this ship takes its time steeping.
content.name: Quennel, the Long Steep
content.description: Quennel moves down the bloom-corridor with an urn cradled like a sleeping animal, and the air behind her stays warm — a courtesy the garden accepts and does not return. The trellises lean after her, the way regulars lean toward a room that knows their order.

content.line: Ceiling wheat's gone gold — the light's telling the truth today. Mind it doesn't stop.
content.name: Hesk, of the Ceiling Beds
content.description: She shoulders through the doorway with a crate of seedlings braced against her jaw, face tipped toward the farmland stitched along the sky arc. Cut green trails after her like a sentence refusing its ending.

content.line: Do not grieve for it. A lamp that will not burn has never once lied to me.
content.name: Sarn, of the Dark Lamp
content.description: She crosses the ward bearing an unlit lamp level as a chalice, its glass gone the amber of old rust, and the crowd parts around a darkness that has weight.

content.line: Warm door on the cold bend — no handle, breathing slow. Tell your priest after supper; I've three houses yet.
content.name: Yolt, Three-Landings
content.description: A girl takes the low stair at a run, slippers slapping the hull-plate, a borrowed pot of salt hugged like an infant; her errand is three landings wide, and her curiosity was never issued a boundary.

content.line: The heart has marked me twice, and I count that a mercy. There is no third time — mind your flesh, walker.
content.name: Sker, the Twice-Singed
content.description: She crosses at the unhurried pace of one who knows the heart notices haste, gold light swinging over her like a verdict being read; her knuckles shine with skin that has melted and been made again.

content.line: Everything wears. My trade is the long argument against letting anything finish.
content.name: Thole, the Lastthread
content.description: Gone almost before noticed — a gaunt figure strung with tool-lanyards, whose passage has the hushed deliberateness of someone convinced haste is how machines learn to die. The fasteners in their sledge chime in a sorted, mournful order.

content.line: Said twice, it's history; said once, it's rumor. I take both.
content.name: Wend, called Slow Ink
content.description: He crosses the antechamber backwards, coaxing the tail of a conversation that ended a room ago down onto his slate, ink moving quicker than his feet.

content.line: Esteem is the only coin that spends on this floor — by that arithmetic I am the wealthiest soul aboard, and supper has never cost me a thing.
content.name: Quirke, Thrice-Crowned
content.description: Quirke sweeps past the terminal crowd with a game-board balanced one-handed, declaiming his own standings to anyone his voice can reach, cyan-bright, already gone.

content.line: Take it or don't — a price is only a place where two people stand still, and neither of us has the time.
content.name: Quoy, the Ninefold
content.description: Route-knots ride her wrist to the elbow, a new one tied even as she unloads the last bargain. She is three steps gone before the price settles — always halfway to wherever the market is next.

content.line: Fresh strike, that look of yours. Root where you're set — nothing on this deck grows for a cutting that fights its soil.
content.name: Culm, Wet-Sleeves
content.description: Gone almost before the eye agrees he was there — sleeves rolled past forearms green to the elbow with vat-light, moving at the tempo of a bloom that will not wait. He counts the world in days-to-harvest and spends none of his own.

content.line: Thursday, if the Braid holds true. Nothing in that room was ever mine — that's what makes going quick.
content.name: Ziska, Half-a-Room
content.description: A young woman down from the shared flats, wrist bare where a knotted cord would sit, walking like someone whose luck has been given a day and an hour.

content.line: Description is a door. Whatever asks you to describe it — don't.
content.name: Skerrin, Unfiled
content.description: A woman in maintenance leathers passes at pace, slate empty, stylus surrendered, wearing the flat calm of one who read the whole file and chose silence. The corridor seems to hold its breath until she is through.

content.line: Ilsabet next door swears the log read her dream back to her before she'd woke — word for word, ending and all. I only said: some people wait lifetimes to be so well kept.
content.name: Quennel, Half-Rent
content.description: Under-slept and carrying two lamps where light costs nothing — one for now, one, you would guess, for whoever still sleeps. He crosses the threshold without breaking stride, as if the dark were a room he was raised in.

content.line: The Second Weld precedent still binds — it's under the third pour. Don't go digging it up. It argues back.
content.name: Skerrit, the Footnote
content.description: A litigant crosses the threshold mid-argument, entirely alone, hands conducting the citation of authorities sealed beneath the floor-pour two civilizations ago. He pauses at each judgment-niche to nod, as if confirming attendance.

content.line: Unconsumed, unconsuming — so the verse goes. This morning something kept the time instead of me.
content.name: Pyx, the Unblistered
content.description: She crosses the transit threshold without haste, a sealed reliquary at her breast shedding a light that has never once guttered; in this heat every pilgrim's skin is scored, and her unmarked arms read as the deeper wound.

content.line: House still hasn't shown its hand — four hundred seasons, same face-down card. I respect that in a god. Doesn't mean I won't fleece it.
content.name: Skeat, the Standing Odds
content.description: She crosses the game-court flinging knucklebones the hall's whole length; their clatter arrives a full breath behind her, as though sound itself were hedging her wager.

content.line: I set the bowl out still. The dew comes anyway — and that is near enough to being remembered.
content.name: Osla Vreney, the Terrace Widow
content.description: A spare old woman in copper wool gone soft with steam walks the dew-line at the hour the widows of this terrace have always kept, unhurried as the slow green she spent her years tending.

content.line: Counted my chairs twice this quarter, Solen's people did. Nobody tallies a man's seating unless they mean to price the losing of it.
content.name: Torv, Nine-At-Table
content.description: A broad man with flour worked into the seams of his forearms, hauling a scavenged crate toward the stairwell, the clatter of a table that seats nine and feeds eleven following him down.

content.line: A precedent is only a ruling that outlived the nerve it took to make it.
content.name: Quoy, the Second Reading
content.description: An adjudicator gone grey into his collar, reading a folded writ as he walks, lips shaping a decision he has already made and will not trust until it has been read twice.

content.line: Warm. Forty years of rites, and it has never once been warm.
content.name: Thole, the Twice-Marked
content.description: An old priest lays two fingers against a ward-wall seam as though taking its pulse, finds whatever he fears or hopes for, and passes on without crossing the threshold.

content.line: Nothing spoils down here. That's the grief of it.
content.name: Tun, the Unspent
content.description: Tun goes down the jar-row laying a thumb to every wax seal in turn, counting stock no one has drawn against in living memory, her breath hanging in an air that has mislaid its seasons. To her the vault is not wealth but a promise kept at depth, one intact seal at a time.

content.line: Wax on the tongue till it hangs. The first ring belongs to the ship.
content.name: Vosk, Slowpour
content.description: Huge, unhurried, smelling faintly of beeswax, he carries a leather-wrapped bell of green bronze against his chest like a sleeping animal, and the corridor seems to hush around its weight.

content.line: Tell Twill the chimney stays ours till the table rules — and mind, the table never rules.
content.name: Skarn, Six-Bunks
content.description: A broad man in a coat mended from three households' castoffs, easing by with the flattened shoulders of one who sleeps beneath a dais built for gods. Twelve years under judgment's floor and no verdict has dripped down to him yet.

content.line: I've carried every grief on this deck. None of them got heavier — that's the trick nobody believes till it's theirs.
content.name: Vetch, Greenhanded
content.description: She crosses the ward with sleeves rolled and forearms stained to the elbow in something the charts decline to name — sap, chlorophyll, something older — and the drip-lines sway after her like congregants leaning toward a sermon. She is unhurried, having learned from the gardens that hurry is an argument they always win.

content.line: The chair's been empty longer than the word for empty — but the score keeps, and so do I. Lose to me now, while beating me is still cheap.
content.name: Thole, of the Vacant Chair
content.description: Gaunt and chalk-dusted, trailing a hem of tallies, she scores games nobody watched beneath a judgment seat built for something the size of weather.

content.line: Every leaver drinks free at my counter once — it's how the house keeps count of the going.
content.name: Ullin, Warmhand
content.description: A slate-aproned host crossing the ward corridor at a pace just short of disrespect, a tower of unspilled cups riding one forearm, his knuckles mapped with old scalds in the pattern of a lifetime's pouring.

content.line: Three lamps still — one for him, one for the house, and one left burning for whoever the ship sends up my stair next.
content.name: Imke, Three Lamps
content.description: A widow in a shawl the grey of a dimmed sun-strip, touching the doorpost twice as she leaves it — once for the house, once for whatever the house remembers on her behalf.

content.line: Ten thousand more swings, little hinge. Someone faithful is coming who will keep you.
content.name: Lagan, of the Marked Things
content.description: Lagan comes up the corridor at a canted trot, wrist-knots clicking against a satchel of spares each wrapped and tagged for whichever stranger will need them next, and lays two fingers on a groaning hinge in absolution as she passes. Her whole creed rides in that bag.

content.line: You walk like unmanifested freight, friend — declare yourself somewhere, before a broker does it for you.
content.name: Vosk, Nine-Knot
content.description: A porter whose wrist-cord bears more knots than the year has days, easing a barrow of unmarked crates past you with the tenderness a helmsman spares a leaksome hull.

content.line: Big breaks get the hymns. Small ones get me.
content.name: Dree, Small Mercies
content.description: Copper-cuffed and unhurried, Dree tightens a stranger's wobbling axle-bolt in passing and murmurs a benison over the new-turned thread, three steps gone before any thanks can find her.

content.line: 'Count the sealed things last,' she says behind her, to no one hurrying after. 'They shift the sums.'
content.name: Ispel, Deep-Stow
content.description: An old woman crosses the landing reading a ledger bound in lead foil, pages gone silver where her thumb rests, reading as she walks the way other people breathe — unhurried as sediment.

content.line: Quarter down, the rest when it wakes — and don't ask what's inside; not knowing is the entire discount.
content.name: Yex, the Standing Offer
content.description: A small, hunched trader backing through the junction, tucking sealed packets into conduit-mouths with the tenderness of a man planting bulbs he will not live to see open.

content.line: Deep holds quit answering roll three months back. I mark them present anyway — habit, or mercy.
content.name: Delf, the Rivet-Clerk
content.description: Delf passes at a clerk's clipped pace, thumbing a brass tally that clicks like a beetle in a wall, murmuring figures into the corridor's dark. The count never falters; the numbers are older than the doors they name.

content.line: Eleven motifs this telling. Nine, the telling before. Nobody counts but me.
content.name: Drusk, called Errata
content.description: She moves through the colonnade with a sleeve heavy as a bell-rope in note-slips, lips working through a tally nobody asked her to keep.

content.line: Down-axle the joints fit true with never a hand to fit them. Mind what that confesses about the maker — and about the made.
content.name: Mumch, of the Blue
content.description: Pauses on the threshold, smoke-grey apron hung with files and scrapers, and lays one palm flat against the doorframe as though taking its pulse. Whatever he counts beneath the rust, he has been counting a long while.

content.line: He doesn't mend, mind — he only rules on what deserves to hold. The mending's ours, and so's the meaning.
content.name: Torv, Quenchmark
content.description: Torv passes with her visor thrown up, burn-scars laddering her jaw in the feathered pattern of bad quenches, one bare hand held out to read the corridor's heat like a blind woman's palm.

content.line: Blood on the hem means somebody's breathing somewhere. Best stain there is.
content.name: Rue Hallan, the Selvage
content.description: A midwife cutting through the market-throng with a birth-kit slung like a courier's satchel and a red bloom drying along her hem, her gait unhurried as weather and confessing nothing. Wherever a family is coming apart at the seams, she is the edge that does not fray.

content.line: Take it, take it — the knot says I sold at this square before your grandmother drew breath, and I don't break pattern for haggling.
content.name: Kesh, Nine Knots
content.description: Cyan cord knotted nine times at the wrist — nine routes, nine markets, nine lives ago — she crosses the square the way water finds a drain, and the bargains close behind her like a wake.

content.line: You don't candle. And still the light lingers on you, as if it remembers.
content.name: Ochre, the Vein-Candler
content.description: Crossing with a candler of gold glass, she presses its light to a wrist — a sleeper's, then her own, then briefly yours — lips moving through a count older than any chart kept upstairs.

content.line: No index holds you, friend — and I keep the oldest one.
content.name: Skerry, called the Colophon
content.description: Burdened with the end-leaves of other people's books, she reads each doorway the way sailors read weather, filing every closing door behind pale, unhurried eyes.

content.line: Tell your mother the mist ran late again — third evening now. No, tell her the gardens forgot us; she likes it when I say it that way.
content.name: Skeel Orcutt, Nine-Pots
content.description: A broad man in a work-harness furred green at the seams herds a small child who counts the lantern-moths aloud faster than the moths can drift; behind him on the landing sit nine clay pots, and in his skull the whole terrace's news, folded neat.

content.line: Coin's no good here. We stake being remembered.
content.name: Skerr, the Forfeit-Taker
content.description: Skerr threads the market's edge with a soft purse that holds no coin, only bone tokens etched with names, accepting each loss with the courtesy of a man receiving alms.

content.line: If Kettle-ward asks, I went the long way — and mind the hum, love, it's started saying names again.
content.name: Skirr, Six Bells Gone
content.description: A roommate from the four-bunk pocket past the junction, hands still wet, taking the wall's murmur out of habit the way others check a lamp. She is late the way tides are late — faithfully, and by a fixed amount.

content.line: Everything aboard mends. That's the frightening part — ask, sometime, what it mends toward.
content.name: Yolt, the Afterward
content.description: Copper-cowled and very tall, they pause at each threshold only long enough to read the room's breathing — summoned when the first healers have spent their certainty, and never once early. They do not stop; afterward never does.

content.line: They sealed the third shaft for a reason nobody wrote down. Pray it was cowardice — the other reasons are worse.
content.name: Vosk, Who Argues With Walls
content.description: She takes the corridor at a stride that forgives nothing, a shard of oldest-layer notation wrapped in oilcloth clamped under one arm, quarrelling with a bulkhead that has not answered her in years.

content.line: Older than your grandmother, this, and it held — everything aboard is cargo; some of us simply walk.
content.name: Tzagel, Saltfinger
content.description: He pushes a handcart of corked vials and cloth rounds at a pace that dares you to choose quickly; his tasting finger is stained grey with the ship-smell, as though he had sampled the air so long it took.

content.line: Names like yours get kept, stranger. I only wish mine had been worth the ink.
content.name: Twiln, the Unindexed
content.description: An elder wanders the stacks with one fingertip trailing the spines, patient as erosion, hunting a single entry through a lifetime of catalogues. Where the finger passes, dust declines to settle.

content.line: Twice in one breath, it wept. A name is being said somewhere it should not be.
content.name: Huld, Who Reads the Weep
content.description: Kneels at the cold seam where the wall sweats, copper feretory tilted beneath the slow drip, timing the falter between falls like a penitent clepsydra. Whatever the hull confesses, she takes in the original tongue and refuses all translation — then rises, already gone from wherever she was.

content.line: Two cups again. The ship keeps what we can't — the rest falls to us.
content.name: Ulla, Twocups
content.description: Rust has settled into the creases of her knuckles like a second ring she never took off; she carries a kettle swealed black and mended thrice, passing with the unhurried certainty of a rite kept for no witness.

content.line: Two cups again this morning. Habit is the last tenant that never gives notice.
content.name: Wray, the Twice-Left
content.description: A narrow woman stepping out of a doorway whose order outlasts any occasion for it, touching each lintel as she goes — inventory taken for someone who no longer asks.

content.line: Nine lamps a day for a ship that lights itself — don't ask me which of us is performing the rite.
content.name: Ymma, the Wick-Widow
content.description: A stooped woman ferries a slopping pail of votive tallow against the crowd's grain, forearms streaked pale with a lifetime of wicks, moving with the unhurried certainty of weather.

content.line: Sixth run today and the floor's still hungry — a corridor that holds its goods too long is just a tomb with better lighting.
content.name: Ghyll, Half-Light
content.description: A carter of the dimming hours, when the ceiling-towns go dark with you, hauling what nobody will admit to ordering along routes nobody will admit to knowing.

content.line: Everything on this floor is either moving or being moved — and you, friend, are the second kind.
content.name: Pell, Nine-Stair
content.description: A carter in a sun-faded teal sash walks her barrow into the market crush at a pace no crowd can argue with, wheel-rims polished bright by ten thousand passes of the same corridor. She counts heads the way others count coin, and slows for neither.

content.line: I don't sell, love — I'm merely the interval between owners; even I was somebody's shipment, once.
content.name: Skirr, the Escrowed
content.description: She keeps tempo with the artery's hum as though it were a partner she'd signed terms with, palms flashing, every parcel in her grip already owned by someone two deals downstream.

content.line: Night shift gets the stale loaves and the fresh talk. Fair trade — nobody's complained yet.
content.name: Pim, the Small Hours
content.description: A lean youth gone grey-faced from closing late and opening early, crossing the square with a sack of day-old loaves, already greeting people he hasn't met yet.

content.line: Merrow's boy held his first key at eleven; you'll hold one younger. Mind the third tread — it talks.
content.name: Brack, Longstair
content.description: Broad shoulders gone desk-soft, a coil of salvage under one arm and two children in tow, he reads the corridor's seams out of habit, a man whose body never wholly leaves the dark.

content.line: 'Entrusted is not owned,' he tells the crate — or the corridor, or no one.
content.name: Vosk, Twice-Count
content.description: A barrel-chested man flows past under a crate riding a shoulder-yoke, lips ticking through some private tally; chalk ghosts his knuckles and one ear is capped in polished rust.

content.line: Your face went up the wire before you did, friend — on this ship everything meets itself coming the other way.
content.name: Ords, Same-Bell
content.description: A courier eating the message-artery at a saltant run, tube-satchel slung bandolier-wise, gone again before the eye has finished composing her.

content.line: Third watch running, the log dreams a stranger wearing your silhouette. She never repeats herself.
content.name: Quoy, the Stillscribe
content.description: An old scribe crosses the reading-gallery with an armful of quires still tacky with ink, copying the ship's dreams by hand because no instrument has proved worthy of the work. Her shoes are silent, as though the floor were listening.

content.line: Cast hotter than any mold allows now. Walk on — I don't assay what still moves.
content.name: Ormet, Goldweight
content.description: An old assayist goes by with hand-scales hanging quiet at his chest, weighing by eye what no balance could hold, lips moving through figures older than any ledger he would confess to keeping.

content.line: Forty sheets to the night, and a quire holds four-and-twenty. Someone else has taken up the pen.
content.name: Quire, the Folded
content.description: A spare figure descending the shelf-run with a ledger strapped to his chest like a reliquary, bowing to every third shelf without breaking stride — the bow of a man long past asking why, but not whether. Silver dust rides his shoulders to the knee.

content.line: New face, no cord, no ward-colors — you're a rumor before you're a person. Mind how you move.
content.name: Tiron, Shorthand
content.description: A runner with a fresh-knotted cord slides through the reading-room, ink to the knuckles and a mouth moving faster than his feet, pricing everything and buying nothing. At the threshold he half-turns, as if the room had called him by a name he hadn't given.

content.line: Four, still four. Does no one here stand still long enough to owe an opinion?
content.name: Ostrer, the Walking Quorum
content.description: A junior clerk counting signatories under his breath, hunting the corridor for a fifth hand, since in the Commons nothing closes and nobody holds still.

content.line: Nine lamps, ten shadows. The rite makes no provision for the tenth, so I have taken to calling it sir.
content.name: Ymber, of the Small Hours
content.description: Small and wet to the elbows, moving alcove to alcove relighting nothing, lips moving through a tally she does not write down. The lamps are already lit; it is the shadows she is counting.

content.line: Kept's not the same as hidden, love. Kept is a kind of prayer; hidden is a confession.
content.name: Issly, Sealing-Wax
content.description: A cache-warden threading the storeyard with a ladle of cooling tallow, pressing her thumbprint into every seam she passes, each seal a small vow against opening. The doors behind her look less shut than asleep.

content.line: Say it slurred, say it late — it is not listening for the words anymore.
content.name: Sigel, of the Slipped Hour
content.description: He passes down the gold-lit dark counting a rosary of fused slag, lips moving through an office hours out of true, and his dread is not lateness but the dawning certainty that the fire now keeps different hours.

content.line: Not lost. Only stored against a wanting that hasn't arrived yet.
content.name: Obol, Off-the-Books
content.description: Obol comes down the dark aisle fast, a lead casket chained beneath her coat swinging at her hip, moving like someone who settled her destination long before setting out. Where she caches her weights is a rumor with no row-number, and she means to keep it so.

content.line: Once is opinion, twice is habit — three times witnessed, three times sealed, and it becomes the law we live inside.
content.name: Vray, Underwrit
content.description: A young writ-runner clamps a fresh ordinance to the public board without breaking stride, slate sash squared, glancing down the corridor as if precedent were pacing behind her.

content.line: A cracked bell is honest about the hour. Everything in the middle rings too clean.
content.name: Tarn, the Cracked Bell
content.description: An old woman in oxide-brown wool, heard before seen: her handbell's lip split decades ago, and the flaw in the note is now the whole of her liturgy — one bright tone, then the seam in it, like faith clearing its throat. She walks the commons as though it were the long aisle of a nave she does not trust herself to finish.

content.line: Slow and even. Wish mine ran so.
content.name: Osk Vetch, the Counting Hand
content.description: A thin figure in clinic slate, iodine under the nails; he takes the player's wrist in passing, counts four strides' worth of pulse, and lets go without slowing, incurious as weather about what he found.

content.line: 'Every misdelivery is a confession,' he calls behind him. 'The ship telling you exactly where it did not mean to go.'
content.name: Vetch, Twice-Read
content.description: A runner-archivist passes at courier's pace and reader's attention, satchel sagging with the ship's misdelivered sentences, each envelope opened, read, and sealed again with a curator's tenderness.

content.line: Twice this month the shaft's taken freight down and given back the cart too light — nothing goes down twice unless something's minded to come up.
content.name: Szil, Nine-Bends
content.description: A carter pacing backward ahead of her laden sledge, naming the nine bends of the line like a litany she no longer hears, while the freight follows through each anfractuous turn with a patience that seems older than freight.

content.line: Even a hall of verdicts wants a kettle somewhere in it.
content.name: Ymma, Warmstep
content.description: Ymma goes by beneath the transit-pipes with a samovar slung on a carrier's yoke, trailing a pocket of apricity that makes the passage-light seem to lean after her, and the two Rindwalkers behind her are already speaking more freely than they meant to. Holding a room is her trade, and she carries the room with her.

content.line: The terminal spat out something at dawn even the regulars can't chew. When the tellers go quiet, keep your knots loose.
content.name: Bracke, Twice-Knocked
content.description: A courier of small parcels and smaller news who knocks twice at every door — once for the household, once for the knot — and is halfway down the passage before it opens.

content.line: No report is also a report. We have ruled it so — do not make me rule it twice.
content.name: Quenell, the Quorum
content.description: Slate-blue and unhurried, she crosses the ward hall as if precedent walked half a pace ahead of her, clearing objections before they can be raised.

content.line: Slower. Slower still. …There. Still there.
content.name: Harl Smelt, the Staunch
content.description: An old bonesetter crossing the Commons at the pace of a man whose patient is dying upstairs and knows it — knuckles like cooled slag, sleeves still rolled, a wake of surgical spirit over the ship-smell beneath. He does not hurry; hurrying is for those who can still be surprised.

content.line: Everything on this ship moves eventually, friend — I've merely resolved to go first. Lamp or ledger, choose before I'm past.
content.name: Ovvet, the Halfsold
content.description: He unbuilds his stall as briskly as he raised it — awning folded with one hand, bargains closed with the other — so that where he stood is bare, then barer, then gone.

content.line: Hush, love — she keeps the dream, not the dreamer. Your grandda snored in her stacks forty years, and she never held it against him once.
content.name: Torquil, Three-Daughters
content.description: A broad man gone soft at the edges, a sleeping child slung over his shoulder like cargo he would refuse to insure, the corridor's silver light pooling in his collar. He walks as men walk in places they have always lived: without once looking up.

content.line: The whole street is rehearsing how it falls apart. Nobody takes notes but me.
content.name: Sneld, Half-a-Hinge
content.description: A wide woman crossing the market square at her own unhurried longitude, cuffs scrolled brown with flux, eyes pricing the rust on every awning she passes. Her left knee is two different makes, and both of them are hers.

content.line: Third cage today that's hesitated over the deep shaft — like something far below taking a slow breath.
content.name: Nock, Twice-Knotted
content.description: A lift-hand boards the descending cage before its doors have finished deciding, two route-cords at his wrist: one bright with fresh knots, one burnt to a charred braid he touches like a charm. The doors close on him already reading the shaft marks.

content.line: They'll dim the ceiling at dusk and half my ward will call it the end coming. The ceiling's not a sky — it's a promise, and so far it's kept.
content.name: Hob Marl, the Kind Verdict
content.description: Crosses the square with a physician's satchel worn soft as an old writ, granting the carts a patience earned at bedsides.

content.line: Nothing worth keeping was ever cooled in a hurry — and the hull's run warm a fortnight now, so draw your own conclusions; I've drawn mine.
content.name: Quern, the Unquenched
content.description: He goes by like a draft off the forge, gauntlets scorched to lace at the knuckles, and the corridor's dark iron leans after him the way iron leans to a lodestone — or a congregation to the bell.

content.line: Pain is just the body filing a report nobody senior reads anymore — hold it till we reach the lamp.
content.name: Skerrit, the Long Carry
content.description: He half-runs a litter through the corridor, its occupant wrapped in gauze that glows faintly from within, and slows for nothing — down here even urgency is triaged.

content.line: Nothing spoils down here. It just goes quiet.
content.name: Pyx, the Undercroft
content.description: Pyx shoulders a hand-truck of sealed plate-stock down the vault-canal, breath fogging in air kept cold on purpose, her key-ring worn smooth as riverstone. She does not look at the doors; the doors look at her.

content.line: That terminal post won't parse for anyone — so I'll copy it out crooked. Kept is kept.
content.name: Quire, the Marginal
content.description: An old Drift archivist passes down the stacks without stopping, cuffs chalk-white, her left sleeve a thicket of pencil-notes she trusts above any ledger. In going she rights a fallen folio and murmurs a single correction into her collar — kindness filed as errata.

content.line: Copy it all while it stands. Nothing here is owned, least of all the truth — it only consents to pass through you.
content.name: Thole, the Unhoarded
content.description: He leaves the archive heavier than he came and lighter all the same, an armload of pages already promised to strangers he liked for an afternoon.

content.line: Square as scripture. The ship keeps what's kept square.
content.name: Skarn, Never-Twice
content.description: Burn-pocked to the elbow, she carries a finished valve-seat cupped like a relic, tilting it to the strip-light with every stride — not admiring it, auditing it.

content.line: Not one shelf of mine has room for you, dear, and that's a mercy. Everything I keep is waiting on the dead.
content.name: Ymma, Waitstill
content.description: An old woman pacing the unclaimed stacks with a hand-lamp, steward of goods consigned to heirs who were dust before her grandmother — she buffers for a somewhen that keeps receding, and calls the buffering love.

content.line: I likely poured for your grandmother's grandmother, or someone wearing her face. Sit long, child — sitting long is the only prayer I ever learned.
content.name: Odger, Still-Pours
content.description: A very old man crossing the square at the hour he has crossed it for sixty years, hands curled around the ghost of a tray. He nods to the doorframes as he passes them, colleague to colleague.

content.line: 'Not in front of the walls,' she warns — glancing at you, or past you, once.
content.name: Skarn, Undervein
content.description: In passing she presses her palm to a paint-mark the whole street reads as stone; a niche breathes out tallow and cold iron, then closes behind her like a swallowed word.

content.line: Take the dish, love, before it cools — and don't go saying the far wall's been humming, not where the torches can hear you.
content.name: Onna, the Quenchwife
content.description: A broad woman, soot-veined to the elbow, ferries a lidded pan door to door along the gallery, dealing out supper to the weld-families with the gravity of a sacrament and the pace of someone with three more doors and no patience for thanks.

content.line: That's the ceiling-towns, little one, not a god — say ceiling-towns. We're too busy for gods this stretch.
content.name: Tjark, Four-Spoons
content.description: A broad father pacing himself down to the toddler welded to his forefinger, walking like a man carrying a full vessel through market spillover — patience of the load-bearing kind, already spoons set at home for a name not yet arrived.

content.line: Vats keep no year. Someone has to count it for them, or nothing here is ever next.
content.name: Onna, the Vatwright
content.description: She crosses the square with a sample-glass of green held up to the sun-strip like a votive, lips moving through some private arithmetic of viscosity and light. Algae is patient; she is its patience, worn into the stoop of her shoulders.

content.line: You're the one out of Bay 14. My bunkmate swears your seams match no hull-mark she owns, and she owns most of them.
content.name: Petch, Fourbunks
content.description: Young, grease at one ear, copper cuffs gone dull, she moves with the particular haste of someone late for nothing, and her eyes flick across your seams the way a mender's flick to a weld — reading, not staring.

content.line: Watch the pea or watch the hand — the hand's been empty for thirty years.
content.name: Skerrit, Three-Shell
content.description: A cup, a pea, and an audience she has not found yet: her hands rehearse the shells against her own knuckles, giving every doorway the glisk of a show it will not get.

content.line: I know everyone's errand. You walk like a letter nobody's addressed yet.
content.name: Skemme, Nine Corridors
content.description: Crate-straps cross her chest like bandoliers; she takes the junction at a run without breaking stride, and only her eyes pause — one heartbeat on you, then onward with the rest of the traffic.

content.line: Tell my aunt the Braid's read the new post twice and gone quiet, and quiet's the one thing the Braid never gives for free.
content.name: Twill, the Layover
content.description: She passes on socked feet, boots hooked over one shoulder, three dawns deep into the same vow to be gone by morning — the wrong-way knot at her wrist a debt she declines to gloss.

content.line: Once for the deed, once for the record — nothing is true until it has been written twice.
content.name: Pask, Two-Seals
content.description: He crosses the antechamber at a notary's gait, thumb worrying the ghost of a stamp against two knuckles, as though every threshold owed him its authentication.

content.line: Light fails on schedule — welcome needn't. I've poured through forty years of dims and the dark has never once refused me.
content.name: Quenby, Late-Lamp
content.description: A narrow woman working door to door along the colonnade with a copper taper, waking the hostess-lamps in their blue niches one by one against the coming dim, unhurried as tide.

content.line: —the good lamp stays, Ymma, some things stay, put it on the writ if you have to—
content.name: Sef, Half-a-Writ
content.description: A young roommate backing through a doorway mid-quarrel, voice already lowered for the neighbors, one of a shared pair of keys going warm in her fist — half of a household that fights like it intends to last.

content.line: Rust is the ship, thinking. I disagree — politely, and in its own color.
content.name: Tvetch, the Third Hand
content.description: A mender strung with clamps and spanners worn mirror-bright at the grips crosses the corridor, pausing to lay two fingers against a groaning pipe the way one hushes a fretful animal; in Tvetch's wake, rattles go quiet all down the wall.

content.line: Four postings in six days and nobody can parse them — but you only write to what you believe is listening. I have drafted my reply.
content.name: Skel, the Terminal Moth
content.description: A young woman drifting toward the terminal's glow with Braid-knots at her wrist that no route has earned, eyes raw from watching light that will not resolve; her gaze snags, briefly, on the stranger's seam of ports.

content.line: Easy, new green — everyone's transplanted once.
content.name: Smeth, Long-Hand
content.description: He shoulders a sack of wet substrate toward the freight lift, knuckles scabbed from scraper-work, humming low to vats only he believes are listening.

content.line: One pot stays warm for no one in particular. No one in particular always turns up.
content.name: Quenby, Steam-Hands
content.description: Pink to the wrists with kettle-steam, she threads the colonnade beneath a lidded copper pot wrapped in sacking, counting her regulars under her breath the way another woman might tell beads.

content.line: Terminals stammered again last night, the Braid says — pass it warm, for news cools into rumor and rumor hardens into stone.
content.name: Nim, Quick Ledger
content.description: A relay runner threading the crowd like a needle that knows the cloth's confession, routes knotted at her wrist, whole consignments of news stored nowhere but her skull.

content.line: Forty years, not one split bead. A better marriage than most ever get.
content.name: Skeya, Widow of the Long Seam
content.description: A widow walks the slow length of the seam-wall at shift's end, palm reading the weld-beads like braille she married into, and only the beads her husband laid get touched twice.

content.name: The Unledgered Bay
content.description: Someone swore the granary at the junction keeps a bay no ledger admits — crates from below that never rise for tally, buffered by a keeper said to have forgotten more than the writ remembers. Ask her once and she laughs; ask twice and the price of grain shifts by morning.

content.name: The Permalink That Moved
content.description: They say a copyist in the reading-room keeps dated transcriptions of every terminal posting, and one of hers no longer matches its permalink — same address, altered words, a tale amended in the one place tales are meant to stand fixed. She swears she copied it true the first time. Word has it the Braid bought her discrepancy before the Continuants could.

content.name: The Garden's Courtesy
content.description: They say there's a tea-house deep in the green decks that keeps no larder: the host sets out only what the garden hands her that hour, and the garden keeps no calendar anyone planted. Someone swore a Continuant agronomist once tried to impose a schedule; the beds obliged for a single season, then fell quiet as a held breath, and have ripened for no one since but her. Word has it hospitality there runs downhill from leaf to cup, never the reverse — and no one can say, in that room, who is being served.

content.name: The Door That Mends Back
content.description: Word has it Kesst at the mend-bench keeps spares for a door that appears on no schematic — swears she patched it once down in the tunnels, and something past the threshold gave back every worn part she'd ever swapped out, cleaned and oiled, as if the ship had mended her in return.

content.name: The Hinge Nobody Bent
content.description: Word has it Marda pulled stock from the rind-market and it came out of her fire already a hinge — pin seated, leaves true, finished by no hand she knows — and the stamp on it, someone swore, was notation like the old tunnels wear. She melted it back down, they say, and has taken no commission since.

content.name: The Card Still Wet
