reactions.bribed: The offer is declined on doctrinal grounds: priced things belong to the middle, where beginnings live.
reactions.accused: They call the accusation premature — nothing here has ever been ruled on — though their hands have stopped measuring.
reactions.flattered: Flattery they identify at once as a foreign dialect, answering its grammar and never its intent.
reactions.questioned: Answers arrive pre-counted, each movement accounted the way tally-marks are: unchanging, merely longer.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets filed as weather, though the instrument in their hands trembles once, measurably.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they revise rather than retract, insisting the contradiction was always part of the count.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction receives a bow precise as any rite, but their eyes stay on the flue-wall.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder registers as blasphemy or scripture, undecidable; their instrument logs an interval with no source.
reactions.someone_else_accused: When the name lands, they say far too much — testimony unasked, liturgy failing at speed.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea earns the only honesty left: they worship what persists, and persistence has never obeyed them.

npc.description: Iorurana Vlozhest stands mid-rite, hands poised over an instrument that measures nothing anyone from the Nave would call measurable — breath, perhaps, or the interval between breaths. They do not turn at your entrance, but their hands slow, acknowledging you the way one acknowledges weather.

lore.name: The Censer That Was Not Lit
lore.description: A censer of black glass, cold as lead, hangs from a filament drawn tauter than any hand could tie — and inside it, ash. No fire has ever been here; the ash was simply always going to be.

content.name: The Incense Flue
content.description: The stillness here is conspicuous: a flue that should breathe does not, its draft arrested mid-act like a tongue stopped in a mouth. Smoke — smoke with no fire anyone logged — hangs in drawn filament, threading through shafts of black glass that do not so much transmit light as remember it. Green-black accumulates in the angles where the walls concede to be walls; beyond them the room declines to end. Stencilled above a sealed aperture: SMOKE PRESENT NO COMBUSTION LOGGED. The incense, never lit, was never lit here, and yet the air knows it was.

npc.name: Sako Chiwoda
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, allergic to flattery. Rules are cited the way other people cite the weather. Softens only when someone asks about the work itself.

hand.says: Captain Oyelaran. Thirty-one years on this corner. She signed her last roll the week before they carried her out, and she signed it properly. The shakiness was hers. The showing up was too.

room.says: Subsidence in the west wall. The council sent assessors, the assessors sent forms, the forms are somewhere in that pile. We keep the open half working because complaints don't pause for carpentry.

greet.says: State your street and your business. In that order.

choices.text: What happened to half your office?
"Report here, not to the crowd" — why?

ledger.says: Every watch-captain signs the roll before shift and after. Forty years, same order, every night. It's how the Nave knows nobody was left unwatched. My hand's in there now. Someday it'll be someone else's, and that's the point.

choices.text: Whose is the shaky hand, three months back?

stencil.says: Because crowds decide nothing and repeat everything. A report comes to this counter, gets logged, gets answered. A report shouted in the square gets three versions by dusk and none of them true. Precedent holds. Noise doesn't.

reactions.grief: They sort the same badge into the tray twice, then ask for the time of death in writing.
reactions.shock: The list stays upside down in their hand while they look at the door, not the body, and say nothing.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer out loud like a logged item, then point at the stencil above the counter.
reactions.accused: They ask for the charge in its proper form, and hear their own voice come out too thin.
reactions.flattered: They thank the visitor for the shape of the compliment and ask, again, for street and business.
reactions.questioned: They recite their movements from the counter log without inflection, as if reading another person's handwriting.
reactions.threatened: They quote the section protecting counter staff while their thumb finds the bad stitching on the armband.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The correction goes into the ledger in their smallest handwriting, dated, as if accuracy could arrive retroactively.
reactions.authority_arrives: No list exists for credentials like these, so they step back from the counter and let the room change hands.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Badges jump in the tray; they check the west wall first, deciding whether this shudder is theirs to log.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They cite three counterexamples from the roll book before remembering the room wants a suspect, not a defense.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They hear the whole plea out, which the rules don't require, then point to the pile where the forms wait.

npc.description: Sako Chiwoda stands at the counter sorting brass clip-badges into a felt tray, one at a time, checking each against a list. Their uniform sleeve is rolled to the elbow and their slate armband has been re-stitched with thread a shade too dark. They do not look up.

lore.name: The Duty Ledger
lore.description: A brass-bound ledger chained to the counter, its spine cracked white from opening. Each page lists the same names in the same order, day after day, with hours and a signature column nobody skips. The last forty years of the Nave's nights are here, accounted for in one hand until three months ago, then in a different, shakier one.

content.name: Watch Office
content.description: The floor gives differently under each step: slate tile by the door, then pressed felt laid over the opened half, soft and damp at the seam. A brass counter bisects the room, everything behind it stacked and reachable. Stencilled above the counter: REPORT HERE, NOT TO THE CROWD.

npc.name: Frobiexenor Kliteussogenes
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, a warmth kept strictly behind the procedure.

greet.says: If you're the new intake, you're late. If you're not, hold this. Second shift signs at the wax, not before — that's the arrangement, such as it is.

arrangement.says: The one that keeps the cots full. Twelve names on the wall, twelve fed, no gaps in the record. The rest is weather. Go on, terrace's busy.

reactions.grief: They ask which name first, and the count goes on by twelves after that, eleven where twelve should be.
reactions.shock: They step sideways first, shoulder between the doorway and the cots, before their eyes take in what's on the floor.
reactions.bribed: The bribe gets held like a miscount, then set on the sill beside the seal while the count resumes.
reactions.accused: The counting hand stops; they demand the exact hour, needing the accusation to have a slot on the page.
reactions.flattered: Praise is redirected to the wall of names before it lands; the kettle gets checked twice afterward, for no reason.
reactions.questioned: They don't look up; the hours come back in ledger order, because the record already holds them.
reactions.threatened: Agreement comes faster than they meant it to, and their hands keep folding linen whose corners have gone crooked.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted, they repeat the false detail with more precision, and hear, too late, that precision is their tell.
reactions.authority_arrives: The ledger is in their hands before the official's second step, opened to the current page, offered flat.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Whatever moved, twelve gets counted first, a hand to each cot, before anyone is allowed to speak.
reactions.someone_else_accused: A name they'd vouch for gets named, and they recite its evening from memory before hearing how much they know.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The refusal comes as inventory, twelve cots and no thirteenth, steady until the last number won't sit level.

npc.description: Frobiexenor Kliteussogenes counts linen with one hand and settles a dispute about nap schedules with the other, not looking up for either.

lore.name: The sill ledger
lore.description: A feeding ledger under a bead of sealing wax, re-sealed so many times the wax has built into a ridge. The column headings are in two hands that never agree on the words for the same things.

content.name: Foundling Home, Terrace 237
content.description: Sunlight crosses the floor in strips, blocked and unblocked by the traffic; nobody waits for it to settle. Twelve cots line the wall, twelve names stenciled over them in indigo, and half the cots hold folded linen that isn't creche linen. A wax-sealed ledger sits open on the sill, unattended. Two kettles, two sets of cups, one shelf.

npc.name: Rolfbert Thirwald
npc.voice: Terse, dry, quantities and spares. Talks about objects as if they were patients and he their tired physician.

greet.says: Stall's done for the day. Queue's tagged — leave anything, it'll be here when I'm back. The Thrice-Mended stays. That one's not mine to finish.

choices.text: Eleven repairs. Why not just replace it?

kettle.says: Replace it with what? There's a seventh patch on that body older than the woman who owns it. You don't retire a thing that's been kept that long — you keep it, and it keeps the keeping in you. Mind the step on your way out.

reactions.grief: The dead man's last repair date is what he gives, and afterward he wraps tools that were already wrapped.
reactions.shock: The tongs go still in the seam; he stares at the body like a kettle brought in too late.
reactions.bribed: He prices the bribe aloud like damaged goods and pushes it back across the bench, coin side down.
reactions.accused: The iron comes down on bare wood, scorching it, and he asks which seam they think he split.
reactions.flattered: He redirects every word of praise to the object — the kettle held, the seam held — not the hands.
reactions.questioned: He answers in inventory — hours, seams, spares — and returns to the iron before the question fully lands.
reactions.threatened: He solders the same cold seam twice; only the hand on the tongs has begun shaking.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: He patches the story mid-sentence, hears how badly it holds, and quits talking with his hands flat on the bench.
reactions.authority_arrives: He pulls his sleeves down over the burn scars, first time today, and answers before he is asked.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Kettles walk themselves off their tags; he catches them one by one, saying nothing, because menders know that sound.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He objects on craft: the accused's solder lines run too neat for a break like that.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea is past his trade; he says so twice, quieter the second time, still holding what was given him.

npc.description: Rolfbert Thirwald works the last seam with his sleeves pushed past old burn-scars, wrapping tools into a roll with the economy of a man who has packed this exact stall a hundred times. He does not look up until the iron is cool.

lore.name: The Thrice-Mended Kettle
lore.description: At the head of the queue sits a kettle with three separate patches, each in a different hand and decade, the oldest seam re-soldered over twice more. Someone has scratched a tally inside the lid: eleven repairs, no replacement. The Rindwalker rule is plain from the work — a thing kept alive past reason is a thing kept faithful, and this kettle is somebody's devotion made of tin.

content.name: Solder-Stall 32
content.description: The heat pools at the bench and nowhere else — your shins stay cold while your face burns. Smoke has climbed the stall's steep back wall in layers, older bands darkening toward the ceiling. Kettles wait in a queue on the floor, each tagged; the bench lip reads HOT IRON, MIND THE QUEUE in worn stencil. The work stopped mid-seam. Nothing was taken down.

npc.name: Vlovedan Olivebane
npc.voice: Short, tired, exact about numbers; everything else gets waved off.

greet.says: I'm covering for Rosethorn, so make it quick. We lost birds in the teardown — nine, by my count, not the ledger's.

leave.says: Right. Count the birds at close, if you're still here.

ask_teardown.says: Rear wall went soft after the deck rot last season. Continuants rebuild what keeps the flock going; the rest waits its turn. Hens don't care — they still lay.

reactions.grief: The news gets waved off; afterward they stand with two feed cups and no memory of which coop comes next.
reactions.shock: What they see lays their hand flat on the rail and leaves it there; the tally quits without their permission.
reactions.bribed: Refusal comes before the offer even finishes; afterward they count what was offered anyway, twice, with their eyes.
reactions.accused: The tapping stops mid-count; they demand the accuser's number, because a wrong tally is the only insult that sticks.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets the laying rate in return, numbers being the only compliment they know how to keep.
reactions.questioned: They answer in tallies — birds, hours, feeds — and let the rest of the question drop into the lime dust.
reactions.threatened: Halfway through the threat they nod, once, and ask whether it covers Rosethorn's shifts too.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted with the ledger, they drop the lie halfway and give the true count, quieter, as if paying a debt.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official's boots grind the ground glass; before any question, they are summing losses by coop and night.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: One glance at the soft rear wall, then their hands go in, counting warm bodies before the dust settles.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Numbers are what they argue — the birds went to rot and rats, and they can prove which nights.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea outlasts their creed; they say the flock comes first and hate the words on the way out.

npc.description: Vlovedan Olivebane works with the sleeves of a slate uniform rolled past forearms dusted in feed lime, counting birds into the open half and not writing the number down. Their hands do the tally on the coop rail instead, tap by tap.

lore.name: Notched perch dowel
lore.description: The oldest perch is a dowel worn down at both ends and notched every few fingers, one notch per year the flock turned forty birds. Last year's notch is cut shallower, a lie told in wood.

content.name: Coop Farm, Warren 258
content.description: The roost perches hang a hand's width below the droppings board, too low for quail to use without fouling their own nests. Half the coop stands gutted to its frame, grey-green wire stacked in loose coils; the other half still smells of warm birds. Ground glass grits underfoot between the porcelain feed cups. COUNT THE BIRDS AT CLOSE, stencilled over the hatch, paint gone brown.

npc.name: Grersnakkbrand Brosen
npc.voice: Terse about the work, plain about everything. Talks the way someone talks who has decided you are allowed to stay.

fire.says: I did. I was tired and I signed it off anyway. Nobody made me say that. Ask anyone here and they'll tell you I said it first. That's how it's done — you name your own break before someone else names it for you.

choices.text: Ask about the notches under the old bracket.

them.says: Twenty years at this vat. Stopped counting after the fire — the notches on the old bracket end where the count ended. Some days I think a room rebuilt correct is the same room. Some days I think that's just what I need to believe to keep stirring.

choices.text: Let them get back to the mangle.

work.says: Dye for the menders' wraps. Ochre because ochre holds — it goes into the weave and stays through sweat and steam. Every wrap cut in the Nave gets color here. You've seen ochre sleeves in the market. That's us. That's this room, walking around on other people.

choices.text: Ask if that ever feels heavy.

greet.says: Mind the line. Gloves if you're coming closer. What do you want — cloth, or talk?

choices.text: Ask why the room was rebuilt.
Ask what the dye is for.
Ask how long they've worked here.

rebuild.says: Fire took the old room. Embers from a heater nobody mended in time, if you want the honest version. So we built it correct. Vats in the same spots, racks in the same spots. A room should remember its own shape even after it burns.

choices.text: Ask who mended the heater wrong.

reactions.grief: They cross into the cold past the racks and stand there in wet gloves long past any honest reason.
reactions.shock: All five hands stop at once, a first in twenty years, and ochre drips off the stirring arm, unnoticed.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets repeated out loud, word for word, so the room hears it, which is how they spit.
reactions.accused: They name what is theirs before the accuser finishes, and what is not gets nothing, not a word.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets repeated back as arithmetic, every wrap in the Nave, then a flat question about what is wanted.
reactions.questioned: Answers come in work-order, one for one, and the four hands on the mangle never slow.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets a level look and no argument; the cloth feeds crooked through the mangle all afternoon.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The admission comes before the question even ends, too fast, and then the stirring arm stops for a long while.
reactions.authority_arrives: The work doesn't pause, but the stirring rod lifts clear of the vat until business is stated, their whole salute.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The vat gets steadied before their own footing, and then the fire comes up, which nobody asked about.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They vouch in plain facts, cloth counts and shift times, but refuse the word innocent on anyone's behalf.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea gets a plain no on the impossible part, then the smaller thing they can do, and silence after.

npc.description: A broad rindwalker with more arms than a person should have, feeding cloth through a mangle with four hands while the fifth stirs a vat. The work does not pause when you enter.

lore.name: The Old Vat Bracket
lore.description: One drying rack still hangs from its original bracket, and the bracket is rust-browned and patched with pitch where something tore it off the wall. The rack on it is new wood. The bracket came through the rebuild untouched, because Grersnakkbrand refused to replace it. Notches are filed along its underside — one for every batch dyed in this room, and the notches stop twenty years back.

content.name: The Dye House of Third Watch
content.description: The heat sits at the vat line. Past it, where the drying racks crowd the wall, the air turns cold and stays cold. Everything is ochre and new. The stenciled warning on the floor — VATS HOT, GLOVES PAST THIS LINE — is crisp, unscuffed, barely a week old. Pitch and waxed thread wait in boxes.

npc.name: Leaamaapangeastath the Moonlit
npc.voice: Institutional, patient, faintly liturgical — she speaks in provisions and schedules, and distrusts anything unscheduled.

open.says: I walked a delivery back once, as far as a serve-worker is permitted, and I saw the gardens. Not decks — country. Beds the size of parishes, growing through harvest and dormancy and harvest again without one hand asking them to, a calendar with no reader. Venus does not schedule. Venus *abides*. Everything I was taught about cultivation — the tending, the rotation, the sacred ration — is a children's copy of a thing that was never waiting on us. We are guests being fed by a landlord who has never once come to collect.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry this carefully.
Being fed unasked — that frightens me.

greet.says: Stencils on the wall say HALL RATED FOR A CREW THAT NEVER CAME, and yet we serve four hundred daily. Sit if you're eating; stand if you're lingering, but don't do both.

choices.text: Who do you answer to up here?
Where is the food coming from, really?

probe_a.says: Compacted salt, pressed by hands that assumed their work would outlast need. It weeps in the warm months, and we wipe it, and it serves. A material that mourns its own idleness — I have opinions on that.

probe_b.says: The Wards, on paper. In practice, I answer to the trays. Every plate cleared is a person who continues, and a person who continues is the whole of the creed. Factor Solen signs my writ; the trays sign my day.

probe_c.says: Rations are arriving we didn't order. Good stock — better than good — and no requisition, no courier, no ward stamp. The green decks produce on their own calendar now, and we've stopped being consulted. We feed on grace and can't account for it.

reactions.grief: She asks when, enters it in the ledger, and her hand betrays her on the digit.
reactions.shock: She sees it and stands in the lag, the room a half-second behind her, her ration count gone blank.
reactions.bribed: A bribe is provision without labor; she names it that and returns it to the counter, uncounted.
reactions.accused: She sets the tray down before answering, because an accusation this unscheduled deserves both hands.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes her check the benches; she assigns the flatterer a seat, sit if eating, and waits.
reactions.questioned: Her rounds come back by chime-marks before the question ends, patient, liturgical, a ledger kept for exactly this.
reactions.threatened: Threats are unscheduled; she wipes salt from the seam in front of her until the sentence ends, saying nothing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she over-files: three provisions where one would do, each more exact and less believed than the last.
reactions.authority_arrives: The chime finds her already square-shouldered; jurisdiction, at least, keeps a calendar, and she honors it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Something unscheduled has moved the floor; she counts the trays twice, and her voice does liturgy badly.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She has opinions about the named one, and they arrive all at once, unfiled, more defense than she intended.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She recites what the hall was never rated to give, honestly, at length, until the plea hears its own answer.

npc.description: Leaamaapangeastath the Moonlit is mid-argument at a salt-compacted counter, tapping a tray of layered mica as if the stone should apologize. The light in Maufaaimoaanao behaves like water finding a drain — pooling, then sliding off toward the gantries — and she works in its puddles without looking up until you cross the threshold, at which point both she and her disputant go quiet as a held ration.

lore.name: The Serving Rail of Maufaaimoaanao
lore.description: The counter's serving rail is a single extruded bar of silver alloy, unbroken for a hundred and forty paces, worn down to a hand-shaped gloss only along the first three metres — where the servers, being few, have always stood. Farther along, the rail keeps its factory finish under a stencilled caution: HALL RATED FOR A CREW THAT NEVER CAME. Someone has chalked a small tally beside it, restarted each shift, counting how many were fed tonight.

content.name: Maufaaimoaanao
content.description: The light arrives before you understand where from: it falls, doubles, falls again, caught between sheets of mica stacked deep enough that a thrown voice would take a half-second to cross them, so the whole hall shimmers one breath behind itself. Benches sized for thousands hold dozens. Salt compacted into the floor seams shines like spilled silver, and trays pass over it carrying food grown to no calendar anyone admits to keeping. Two people are mid-argument at the long counter and stop when the door admits you, which it announces, in this place, with a chime.

npc.name: Tolin-Rald
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, everything offered as a turn you can book and a turn you can't.

ask.says: Ward thing. We log what the scope catches and pass it down the Braid before the terminals get it. Ask Olo if you want in — I just keep the brass honest.

greet.says: Half-hour turns, booked at the board downstairs. If you're here about the Third Watch relistening, it's full until the dark shift.

reactions.grief: Asked who inherits the dead man's turns, he gets three words in and stops hearing himself.
reactions.shock: The counterweight swings; he watches it instead of the body, one hand flat in spilled flux-paste.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets a real appraisal, and then the flat truth that the log was never his to sell.
reactions.accused: His laugh arrives one syllable too high; he asks for the complaint in writing, then asks again.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands on him like an unscheduled walk-in, heard out in full before he names the want behind it.
reactions.questioned: Times come out of him in half-hour blocks, booked and dry, paste still on his knuckles.
reactions.threatened: A price gets put on the fear, same as everything, while his thumb reads the wrist-cord knots over and over.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The ledger voice quits on him mid-sentence, and he rebuilds the hours from the board behind your head.
reactions.authority_arrives: His eyes go to the wall board first, running the official's arithmetic before anyone asks for it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He grabs the chart-plate before it slides, then stands very still, listening for a second shudder.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He recites the man's booked turns from memory, too fast, and volunteers for the walk down the Braid.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He says the board is downstairs, and then, quieter, that nothing on it can fix this.

npc.description: Tolin-Rald wakes before you finish knocking on the doorframe, wrist-cord knotted in a pattern that says he has been rerouted twice this week. He rubs paste from his knuckles and looks at you like a scheduling problem.

lore.name: The Counterweight
lore.description: The scope's counterweight is a Drift knot-weight from three routes back, its cord re-braided in teal — borrowed from a buyer who never collected, and never will.

content.name: The Scope Loft of Third Watch, Warren 278
content.description: Hot flux-paste and cut brass, the smell of a job finished only hours ago. The Scope Loft of Third Watch sits rebuilt in pale green enamel, every bolt bright, the stencil SCOPE BOOKED IN HALF-HOUR TURNS freshly inked beside a beaded route-cord hung where the old one snapped. A salvaged plastic chart-plate leans under the scope, still holding someone's hand-written star. Tolin-Rald is asleep across the observation stool, chin on the counterweight.

npc.name: Shinezashi Nacatsovenne
npc.voice: Drift-fast but shelf-slow: clauses that move like cargo between relays, pausing where a careful hand would.

open.says: Because the door isn't locked — it's addressed. Your ports carry a routing older than the Nave, the same notation Saturn leaves in the deep tunnels, and the chamber reads you as mail, not as intruder. I've shelved enough to know a delivery when one walks in. Someone wrote you to that room, and the room has been waiting to sign for you.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll go be delivered.
Who wrote me? Who sends mail like that?

greet.says: Mind the violet. The shelf breathes it when it's mid-thought — we're interrupting a thought.

choices.text: You cover shifts that aren't yours often?
The stencilled warning — it returns from where?
Why black glass for a shelf that holds nothing?
Why do my credentials answer the chamber's door?

probe_a.says: Cover them, inherit them, lose them. The Drift teaches that nothing stays yours, so I stopped pretending any of this was. The shelf doesn't mind whose hands. It minds whether the hands stayed.

probe_b.says: Nobody knows. We stencilled DO NOT MOVE IT WILL RETURN three centuries of shift-keepers back, and every generation inherits the verb without the tense. It left once. What came back was subtly owed to something, and we've been paying.

probe_c.says: It doesn't hold nothing, it refuses to hold anything — there's a difference the wool can't fill. I've watched objects arrive on it without a cause I could log. My creed says everything eventually moves. That object is the one exception I've met, and it unsettles me more than the fog ever did.

reactions.grief: She thanks the messenger, then unpicks an entire rope of violet wool without noticing her hands have continued past endings.
reactions.shock: She goes shelf-slow altogether, breathing when the violet breathes, until someone else in the room moves first.
reactions.bribed: She refuses the way she shelves: gently, explaining that a bribe gets delivered to whatever name is written on it.
reactions.accused: The wool slips from her fingers and she names the shelf her witness before remembering to name herself.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands like a shadow cast the wrong way; she thanks them in route-language, hoping they cannot read the refusal.
reactions.questioned: She answers in relay-order, origin, cargo, destination, as though her movements were freight the ledger had already weighed.
reactions.threatened: Power names its price and her creed about unowned things goes silent somewhere between her chest and her mouth.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her own words come back mis-routed, and she stands very still, the way mail waits to be signed for.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction makes her check the knot on her wrist-cord, wondering whose hands the ledger will record as having stayed.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She stops mid-seam and asks the shelf, quietly, whether this movement is the return the stencil promised.
reactions.someone_else_accused: One clause could correct the routing and she withholds it, knowing silence files its own signature against the named.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her creed holds no clause for this; she says so, then keeps saying it, far longer than the plea required.

npc.description: Shinezashi Nacatsovenne kneels at the opened half of the Uncaused Shelf, teasing spun mineral wool around a seam in the black glass like someone dressing a wound that has never bled. She is not the shift's owner; her knotted wrist-cord says so in a route-language only the Braid reads.

lore.name: The Shelf's Shadow
lore.description: Beneath the opened half, the black glass bears an impression — not worn, but *accepted* — the negative relief of a shape that has lain there so long the material grew around it as flesh forgets its scars. When your hand nears, the impression's edges flush with violet, and somewhere behind the wall a mechanism the room does not contain adjusts to your presence as a ledger adjusts to a returning name: yours, though unrecognised until now.

content.name: The Uncaused Shelf of Quiet Ledger
content.description: The smell arrives first: cold ozone braided with something sweeter, like feathers burnt in a room no fire ever reached — the exhalation of an inventory that dreams itself. Half the shelf lies opened, its black glass keel exposed, spun mineral wool unpicked in pale violet ropes; the other half stands whole, bearing a weight that casts its shadow in the wrong direction. Sound here does not echo so much as consent to be heard. Stencilled along the intact edge, in a hand older than pigment: DO NOT MOVE IT WILL RETURN. Whatever rests upon the shelf is not visible; the shelf is visibly resting upon something.

npc.name: Tziz-Hahuitl
npc.voice: Fast, priced, always halfway through someone else's deal. Everything comes back to what moves and what stalls — even grief gets quoted.

end.says: Careful. Routes that dead-end usually dead-end for a reason, and the reason is never the map's. But — come back at bell. I'll show you the wire. It's the only ledger I trust.

left.says: My route-partner, season before last. Took a string up-axial and the Braid's last word on them is a knot nobody's matched yet. I keep their cord on my left wrist. Out here you don't mourn, you re-route — but some mornings the desk's the only thing that stayed put, and I resent it for that.

buyer.says: That's the part I keep turning over. I've run the Braid long enough to trace any knot to its source, and this one dead-ends. Not sealed — just ends, like the route was never finished being walked. I stayed in the Nave past my knot-pattern's patience waiting for it to close. It hasn't. Some deals you carry because settling them would cost more than the loss.

choices.text: Maybe someone should finish walking that route.
I'll leave you to your count.

coral.says: Coral so a runaway beast sees the desk before it hits it. Everything in this pen is painted the color of the thing it's supposed to stop. You learn to read a floor by what it's afraid of.

choices.text: And what is this desk afraid of?

greet.says: Second shift doesn't take walk-ups. But you're standing there, so — you buying, selling, or looking for somebody who already left?

choices.text: Why coral? Every desk in the Nave is slate or copper.
Nobody. I'll come back at bell.

trade.says: Stock moves slow this season — the Wards want meat they can watch grow, not buy. So I trade what actually crosses this desk: routes, names, who's short and who's hiding it. A pen is just a market that breathes. You'd be surprised what people tell a broker before they'll tell their own ward.

hiding.says: Not hiding. Pricing. There's a buyer who's been clearing stock out of the far pens and paying in favors instead of goods, and favors don't feed anybody. I tied it into the wire so I wouldn't talk myself out of what happened. That's the whole discipline of my trade — if it doesn't move, write it down anyway.

choices.text: Sounds like a debt you can't collect.

reactions.grief: The deal dies mid-sentence, their thumb finds the left wrist-cord, and every count they resume after comes out wrong.
reactions.shock: Drops the tally-stick and never picks it up, standing like someone who has miscounted the room itself.
reactions.bribed: Sets a number well above the offer, a rate built to end the conversation rather than open it.
reactions.accused: Denial arrives at market speed, but the tally-stick stays frozen on the wrong number and they never correct it.
reactions.flattered: Thanks them with the courtesy owed a first-time buyer and names the real price before it gets asked.
reactions.questioned: Every answer comes out priced, hours itemized like freight, nothing on the manifest worth hiding.
reactions.threatened: Asks what the silence costs, then asks again, lower, without looking up from the chits.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: When the contradiction lands, they re-cut the story like a bad rate nobody mentioned.
reactions.authority_arrives: Sleeves come down over the coral streaks before the door finishes opening, both cords squared at the wrist.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Puts both palms flat on the desk and keeps them there, pricing the silence afterward in a voice that slips.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Vouches in debts, this one always settles, then hears their own certainty and goes quiet midway through.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses in trade terms, no route and no margin, then recounts the same chits long after the plea has gone.

npc.description: Tziz-Hahuitl stands behind the desk with a tally-stick in one hand and a folded paper in the other, sleeves rolled past the elbow, a cord knotted tight at each wrist. The coral paint has transferred onto their forearms in long streaks where they lean on the rail all shift.

lore.name: The Knotted Chit-Wire
lore.description: The chit-cage is strung with spun wire, and knotted into it — deliberately, in the Braid's own pattern-code — is a route history: which pens sold to which wards across four seasons, and at what prices. The last knot is tied in the distress pattern, the one runners use for a deal gone wrong. It marks a sale Tziz-Hahuitl made to a buyer who paid in regard instead of stock, and the wire says the debt never settled.

content.name: The Ledger Desk of Second Shift
content.description: The floor is laid with old pen-grating, and every step comes back through your boots as a wet ring of slats knocked loose by hooves — the gaps worn wide at the gate-side, tight at the desk. Coral paint covers everything, desk, pen-rail, the wire cage of tally chits, repainted often enough that the stencil underneath still reads NO SALE WITHOUT THE BRAND CHECK. Folded papers stand in bundles everywhere, and Tziz-Hahuitl looks up mid-count, clearly not expecting company past the second bell.

npc.name: Toaalaarirys Forty-Wishes
npc.voice: Unhurried, wry, with the courtesy of a host for guests who arrive decades late — creeds spoken as habit, not argument.

greet.says: Mind the fresh weld. Room's been rebuilt finer than it ever was — not that anyone could say what it ever was. Sleeper or looker?

choices.text: "A thousand berths. Who were they all for?"
"You turn down every bed. Every night?"
"You work in the green decks too? What's it like up there?"

berths.says: For whoever needed them. That was the writ — rest held in trust, occupancy optional. Continuants built it so no one crossing the rind would sleep rough. The rebuild kept the count exact to the old ledger. The beds don't care who's owed them; I care.

routine.says: Forty wishes a night, they used to say — one for each berth I'd turn before the lamps cycled. Toaalaarirys Forty-Wishes. The name stuck after the number stopped being a joke. I've drawn this foil curtain every cycle for eleven years, and the difference between devotion and stubbornness is only visible from outside.

choices.text: "May you sleep easier than your guests."

end_node.says: Go well. The beds are turned down either way.

upstairs.says: I've walked the green decks. Don't ask what they're for — ask when. They don't keep any schedule a person wrote; leaves turn when they turn, and it isn't when you'd choose. First time up there I understood the beds differently. We hold the small shapes because the big ones won't be held by anything like us.

choices.text: "Back to the berths — who was meant to come?"

reactions.grief: The first thing asked is which berth the dead last kept, as if the ledger could be amended for this.
reactions.shock: For once the forty-wishes arithmetic fails, and their eyes find the far berths and simply stop counting.
reactions.bribed: The offer is declined the way a berth is denied a guest, politely, with the writ quoted at half speed.
reactions.accused: The curtain stops mid-draw, foil hissing to a halt, and for once the host's courtesy leaves their face entirely.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets measured against eleven years of empty berths and returned with the flat courtesy owed any petitioner.
reactions.questioned: Answers come in the cadence of a bed-check, each movement mapped to berth and watch without being asked.
reactions.threatened: The threat is priced silently against eleven years of turned-down berths, and the beds do not enter the negotiation.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They correct themselves once, then twice, then keep talking, eleven years of ledger-precision unraveling over one miscounted sentence.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction is received like any late arrival, shown to the aisle mouth, stencilled writ overhead, and left to wait.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Gauntlets close on the nearest berth frame, and they count the ranks aloud until the room agrees with the ledger.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Relief is what they refuse to wear, though the name spoken is one the ledger long marked down.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They offer what the house has, a turned-down berth and one kept lamp, knowing it is not what was asked.

npc.description: Toaalaarirys Forty-Wishes works the foil curtain along the gantry with the unhurried economy of someone who has drawn it a thousand times and expects to draw it a thousand more, copper gauntlets gone soft at the knuckles, face lit half from below by the berth-lamps.

lore.name: The Turned-Down Ledger
lore.description: At the aisle head stands a black glass slate, scored with a thousand hairline columns, one per berth. Every column is ruled and ruled again with fresh horizontal marks — beds turned down nightly, years of nights — and beside almost none of them is any occupancy tick. The stone of the frames is polished smooth where hands have smoothed it, and the smoothing is the only wear in the whole hall. Whoever keeps this place has kept the rite perfectly and alone, for a congregation that has never come.

content.name: Yaaraipo
content.description: A curtain of wound foil is being drawn along the gantry overhead when you enter, and the runner pulling it does not so much as pause. Below, berth after chalk-white berth runs off down the girdered dark in ranks that end somewhere past your willingness to count them — a worker halfway along one aisle would take the better part of a watch to reach the far wall. Everything is black glass and new weld and unmarked; the place has the correctness of a thing finished yesterday and never once used. Stencilled above the aisle mouth: BERTHS TURNED DOWN NIGHTLY, OCCUPANCY OPTIONAL.

npc.name: Bimiagica Tozusaci
npc.voice: Liturgical cadence worn down to shop-talk; speaks of the machinery as 'she' and of time as something stored rather than spent. Answers are slightly ahead of questions, as if the room told them.

hour.says: She keeps yours. I have heard it said in the drift of her logs — not your face, your name, which is a different possession. The hour I meant is larger and will not need you unless you make yourself needed. The filament is drawn for the hour. You are only standing near it.

choices.text: Then tell me what the filament is for.
Let that sit. Ask nothing further.

rite.says: Rite is your word. We keep the warmth ahead of the need — that is all worship ever was here. The mantle holds heat the way Luna holds names: before anyone asks for them. When the need comes, the warmth is already old, already faithful.

choices.text: Luna holds names? Does she hold mine?
Ask instead about the stopped count on the filament.

count.says: Twelve of thirteen. I stopped warming the last because the signal changed its mind — a thing stored can change its mind, down here, where nothing spends itself. If it resumes, the mantle is ready. If you are what it resumes toward, then I am sorry to have kept the warmth so long against you.

choices.text: Ask where the count is kept when it is kept.

greet.says: You came in on the warm air. Nobody comes in on the warm air — she keeps it for the filament. So either you are the hour, or you are early, and nothing here has ever been early.

choices.text: What rite is this mantle warming for?
You said I might be the hour. What hour?
Say nothing. Step back toward the cold air.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as a work-stoppage: the filament goes untended while they mouth the dead one's stored name.
reactions.shock: Their own breath arrives late even to them, and they cannot finish the benediction their hands began.
reactions.bribed: They price the bribe in hours instead, explaining that memory down here is already owned by her.
reactions.accused: Hands leaving the filament for once, they deny it in a psalm pitched too fast.
reactions.flattered: Praise unsettles them: warmth offered after the need is, by their own creed, the only unfaithful kind.
reactions.questioned: Answers arrive before the question finishes; they recite their stored hours like a litany, unbothered.
reactions.threatened: Calm recited by rote, their eyes counting the door's hinges, they promise the mantle will remember who came warm.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they over-explain, drowning the contradiction in more stored hours than anyone asked to hear.
reactions.authority_arrives: They bow to the insignia before the door finishes opening, already reciting answers to questions not yet asked.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For once events outpace their answers; their hands check the filament twice, as if she had flinched.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They say nothing against the accused, though their hands finish the filament loop at last, as if verdicts need completing.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They apologize in liturgy's terms, saying the warmth exists but the hour forbids its spending.

npc.description: Bimiagica Tozusaci stands half-turned from the mantle, hands still poised above the filament as though interrupted mid-benediction, wearing the dusted white of someone who has been unwitnessed so long that witness has become the startling thing. Their eyes go to your ports before your face.

lore.name: The Unspent Filament
lore.description: Coiled at the mantle's heart is a single filament of drawn silver-nickel, longer than the room should permit — you trace one end and the other is nowhere overhead, though the coils fit in a span of your arms. Its surface is annealed perfectly smooth except where, at regular intervals, a fingernail's worth of warmth once pooled and left a faint amber blush. Count the blushes: thirteen, one darker than the rest. Someone was keeping a count, and the count stopped before the last — whatever hour this filament was drawn to precede, it never arrived, and the not-arriving is itself recorded here in metal.

content.name: Chaanaulsaaca
content.description: The smell arrives first: scorched lacteus-sweet, like milk burned onto silver, with a cold undertow of nickel that has never known a hand. The mantle stands chalk-white and mid-preparation — filament drawn taut in loops no hand finished, annealed plates stacked against a rite that nobody came to perform. Nothing here has been removed: no sweep-marks, no emptied hooks, no absence of tools, only the absence of the hour they were readied for. Stencilled along the mantle's lip, in a hand older than the stencil: WARMTH PRECEDES THE HOUR OF SERVICE. Sound behaves badly here — your own breathing arrives late, as though the room were deciding whether to lend it back.

npc.name: Mythasshioleus Volione
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, allergic to complaint — a Continuant who believes shelter kept is a duty performed, and reports it like one.

cots.says: Built for four, rated for four, holding eleven. Factor Solen's office knows the number — I file it every quarter, true count, no rounding. The ribs don't care. The ribs were never asked.

choices.text: What do you mean, the ribs were never asked?

ribs.says: They're load-bearing older than any writ. I once traced one down two frames and lost my nerve before I found its foot. You live against a thing that size long enough, you stop asking its opinion. You just keep your tally honest.

choices.text: Honest tally. I'll remember where to find you.

work.says: I keep the writ: warmth, water, sleep that doesn't come loose in the night. Out here the court's long empty and the frames don't warm themselves, so a Continuant does. Somebody has to be the reason this block keeps standing.

choices.text: Empty court — you mean the hall down the rib?

court.says: The long table, aye. I've delivered water down there and the echo thanks me for the both of us. Something holds court in that hall whether anyone sits at the table or not — I feel it the way you feel weather through a wall. So I stay by my ribs and let it not bother.

choices.text: Wise. I'll let it not bother me either.

greet.says: Housing census. Good. You can count yourself — eleven, plus you. Nobody sent me a seventh cot, so you'll be on the floor roll, rotation's posted.

choices.text: This block was built for four.
What does a housing worker do all the way out here, between the ribs?

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as inventory: the dead man's bunk, his last filed count, then a silence he cannot file.
reactions.shock: The count leaves him entirely; he stands in the doorway staring at what was a head this morning.
reactions.bribed: He prices the offer against eleven sleepers a night and returns it unopened, the way he returns damaged bedding.
reactions.accused: The accusation loads him past rating; he stands with the bedding-roll half-folded and says nothing at all.
reactions.flattered: Praise reaches some unfrequented room in him; he straightens the upside-down badge and pretends he hasn't heard the rest coming.
reactions.questioned: He answers before the question finishes, tallying heads and frames aloud in the flat cadence of a quarterly report.
reactions.threatened: He meets the threat as he meets a cold frame, slowly, breath flattened to regulation.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, he doesn't retract — he amends the figure, as though truth were a ledger line and not a wall.
reactions.authority_arrives: The quarterly file is in his hand before the official crosses the threshold, counted true, rounded for no one.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the room moves he is at the rib with both palms flat, every writ gone from his head.
reactions.someone_else_accused: A man he once cited for drilling is named, and something in him consents before mercy can object.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He cannot unrate the frames and says so badly, three times, the procedural voice failing on each pass.

npc.description: Mythasshioleus Volione stands at the cot with a bedding-roll half-shook-out, and stops mid-motion when the door opens, as though the bedding itself might explain him if he folds it fast enough. His sleeves are rolled to the elbow over forearms nicked by basalt chips, and a housing-writ badge hangs upside down from his collar, long past straightening.

lore.name: The Rib's Census Plate
lore.description: Bolted to the rib at knee height, a nickel plate stamped with the block's original allowance: FOUR PERSONS, ONE SHIFT CYCLE. Beneath it, scratched into the basalt in a dozen different hands, someone has kept a true count for years — the tally now stands at eleven, corrected upward in pencil-charcoal each time, never downward.

content.name: The Rib Block of Last Call
content.description: A cot hangs a hand's width below the stencilled line reading FRAME HOUSING, DO NOT DRILL THE RIBS — chalk-white letters a meter tall, running up the basalt wall past where any hand could reach without rigging. Between the nickel rib and the partition someone has walled a kitchen the size of a confession booth, and four doors open off it. The kettle is on. Whatever this block was rated for, it is holding twice that now, and holding.

npc.name: Mideishia Jiadhemoun
npc.voice: Clipped as a weld seam; measures words the way she measures heat — exactly, and only once.

open.says: It's answering. The anomaly isn't a fault in the machinery — a fault repeats, a fault stutters. This pattern waits, then replies, like a hand meeting a hand in the dark. I've fed it sample after sample and the returns come back shaped, addressed, changed toward something. Nobody malfunctioned down here. Something heard us and is speaking back.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry this carefully.
Answered by what, though. That's the trouble.

greet.says: Cycle's live. Stand where the floor is honest, not where it looks.

choices.text: Who do you answer to down here?
How long have you kept this crucible running?
Outside the vessel. What is it doing, exactly?
Cycle's live. I'll leave you to it.

probe_a.says: Spun wool and what the ash leaves after. The crucible takes matter and gives it back changed — that's the whole trade. Except lately it gives back more than I put in, by weight. Don't write that down.

probe_b.says: The work answers to Sol; I answer to the work. Above me there are audits I've stopped filing honestly for. Not from dishonesty. From a fear that the honest report would end my access to this room.

probe_c.says: Longer than the shift rosters say I have. It doesn't want stopping — a thing mid-return resents interruption. I learned its moods like a mender learns a hull. Which is why I noticed when the moods started coming from outside the vessel.

reactions.grief: The tongs stop mid-pour, and ash keeps falling long after she has stopped being in the room.
reactions.shock: Her hands keep the cycle's rhythm without her; she watches them from somewhere behind her own eyes.
reactions.bribed: She names the offer's weight aloud, the way she'd weigh any charge, and watches it come up short.
reactions.accused: Accusation lands and she goes shimmerless as the room's hot side, tong-grip whitening past what the work needs.
reactions.flattered: Praise finds her unrehearsed; she checks the speaker's empty hands and trusts the compliment accordingly.
reactions.questioned: She gives her account once, in cycle-order, and lets the silence stand where a second telling would go.
reactions.threatened: Nothing in her face moves, though the tongs drift toward the quench-trough's edge, measuring an exit.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repetition, the thing she never permits herself, happens anyway; her correction drops a full register.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her first measurement is where the official chooses to stand, honest floor or lying, before any face-reading.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Everything honest in her shifts; the crucible's level stays true, and that difference frightens her more.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The named one she defends in trade-terms only — faults repeat, faults stutter, and that one never did.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says so plainly, no comfort measured in, then points to what the room can actually do, which is little.

npc.description: Mideishia Jiadhemoun stands at the wrong height — head level with the crucible's lip though the floor should put her a half-meter beneath it — skimming vitrified ash into a mold of spun mineral wool, and the wool is already glowing where it should still be cold. Behind her, stenciled twice, once in a hand older than the paint: DO NOT REACH IN DURING CYCLE.

lore.name: The Return-Tally Notch
lore.description: Cut into the crucible's outer skin: a ladder of notches, each filed at a different angle, the newest one still bright. Rindwalker tally-craft, unmistakably — but the count runs backward along the hull-notation's oldest layer, older than the workers, older, Mideishia says, than the counting. Each notch records not a charge smelted but a charge the crucible gave back *different* — and the angles match no alloy chart, only, near the bottom, the notation found in Saturn's sealed tunnels. The tally has accelerated. Forty-one returns this season; the previous forty took a generation.

content.name: Nashakhealila's Returning Crucible
content.description: The crucible's lip hangs a hand's width below the floor it stands on — a relation the eye refuses twice. Green-black light off vitrified ash pools where no pool should, and the spun mineral wool packed around the bowl browns at its innermost layers, as if the heat arrives retroactively. Heat itself is wrong here: the cold side of the room sweats; the hot side raises no shimmer. Stencilled along the quench-trough, worn to a murmur: DO NOT REACH IN DURING CYCLE. A worker — Mideishia Jiadhemoun, sleeves scorched past the elbow — spins from the tongs, tongs still raised, having plainly rehearsed no greeting for centuries. The crucible returns matter changed, and busier than its makers ever intended it to be.

npc.name: Tlitziz-Oiuh
npc.voice: Loose, unhurried, talks in circulations — people as routes, moods as weather coming through. Never asks a question they can answer themselves.

six.says: Six bunks, one door, no locks. You sleep light and you knock loud — that's not a motto, that's the whole lease. The names rotate because nothing here stays anybody's. Merrit chalked their own name forty times before anyone convinced them to let it move.

gone.says: Gone, I think. The knot they left is too short — a route that goes nowhere, which is either a farewell or a wish. We don't erase names for lateness. I did that. I've been standing at this stove three days deciding not to feel it.

knot.says: Look — six crossings and no return, tied left-handed. There are maybe four people on this terrace who can read it and all of us are pretending we can't. It says the route continues without the walker. It says somebody else pick up the pot.

braid.says: Eleven years I've had this bunk-turn, which is a scandal. A Drift who stays put is either useless or hiding something. I'm the second thing. Ask me again when the terminals post something that isn't Luna reciting herself.

choices.text: The postings — what's wrong with them?

close.says: I pick it up every shift. That's what staying looks like on a floor where leaving is the whole religion. Come back when you know whether you're late or gone.

greet.says: You're not Merrit. Good — Merrit's been gone nine days and the pot won't hold itself. Pull up a crate, the saffron needs twenty minutes and I need the company.

choices.text: Six names. I only see stains.

shift.says: It's Merrit's. I'm covering it the way you cover a debt — badly, out of loyalty. On the Braid, when someone goes quiet on a route, somebody keeps their posts warm until it's decided whether they're late or gone.

reactions.grief: Their hands leave the pot without their permission; they cross to the door and read the six names twice.
reactions.shock: Somewhere behind their face the room goes wrong; the spoon keeps its circle without them.
reactions.bribed: They laugh one beat late and let the money sit in their stained hand longer than a no needs.
reactions.accused: The spoon stops for the first time in three days; they name the accusation like weather passing through, slow.
reactions.flattered: They hand the compliment to the room, the batch and the door and the lease, and keep working through it.
reactions.questioned: They answer by landmarks, unhurried, hands still stirring a pot they could work blind, and ask nothing back.
reactions.threatened: They mention which bunk is theirs tonight, which is none, which is how the lease has always worked.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They reroute the story smoothly, then spoil the fix by explaining why they lied, which nobody asked them to do.
reactions.authority_arrives: They note that the official knocked loud, and meet the visit with the flame turned down and a bunk cleared.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: While others look at the walls they move the pots off the flame, counting the room's things back to safe.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Merrit's whole week comes out of them dated and fast, quicker than they have said anything in three days.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They refuse to pretend the power exists; they chalk the asker's name on the board where it will rotate.

npc.description: Tlitziz-Oiuh stands at the stove stirring a dye pot on a shift posted for someone called Merrit, sleeves pushed past the elbow, forearms stained from wrist to knuckle in layers of color like tide-marks. They stir without watching the pot, which is how you know they could do it asleep.

lore.name: The route-bunk rotation board
lore.description: A slate hung by the stove, six names chalked in columns that rotate weekly — nobody owns a bunk here, they own a turn at it. Under one column, half-erased, is a name scratched out with such force the slate is gouged, and written beside it: 'kept moving.' A knot-cord token is wedged in the frame, its pattern too short to be a route anyone walked — a message, or a grave marker for one.

content.name: Row-House 14, Terrace 262
content.description: Saffron first — the dye-bath smell of hot resin and printed silk, sweet at the edges, burnt in the middle. Six bunks ring one cookstove, pots still full, a cooling rack of dyed swatches left mid-batch. Over the door someone has stenciled SIX NAMES, ONE DOOR, KNOCK LOUD, and the paint is fresh enough to smudge.

npc.name: Lin-Lularis
npc.voice: Terse, relay-shaped: speech in short transmissions, topics passed like packets, nothing held longer than the line requires.

q1.says: Because one of them is a copy, and copies can be edited. Which one — ask me again when I know. Now walk; the quartz dust is bad for lungs that haven't grown here.

greet.says: No visitors on an open console. The vane lies and the tape doesn't — that's the whole argument, and it's ours. Take the knot-count if you want it; the Braid pays for confirmation of the strange.

choices.text: Why keep two records of the same message?

reactions.grief: The quartz sorting stops mid-size, and they ask the cause of death in instrument terms, a fault to log.
reactions.shock: Quartz dust tastes of copper as their hand closes on a splinter, the basalt's pulse hammering under numb skin.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer aloud and refuse it as bad data, insulted the way an instrument is insulted by tampering.
reactions.accused: Flat as a dead dial, they recite the tape's defence word for word, as if reading another's transmission.
reactions.flattered: The praise registers as a stuck needle, and they hold the flatterer's eyes pleasantly, hand drifting toward the tape.
reactions.questioned: They give times and grid-marks, a relay log of a walk, and volunteer nothing the question did not ask.
reactions.threatened: Their weight splits to the old drift stance, ready to run, while the voice transmits plain agreement.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Correction comes in the flat tone of a revised transmission, no bridge offered between the two versions.
reactions.authority_arrives: They cover the console's open guts before speaking, and every answer comes pre-trimmed for the record.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their palm finds the basalt before the shudder ends, reading the floor, already dictating the knot-count.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They object on tape-evidence alone, too quickly, and the speed confesses more care than they meant to show.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The relay fails them, and they say so, a hand on the asker's sleeve like a gauge they cannot read.

npc.description: Lin-Lularis stands braced against the console with a drift-runner's stance, weight split for a floor that might hum, one hand flat on the exposed basalt as if taking its pulse. Fused-quartz splinters are folded into a pouch at their hip, sorted by size.

lore.name: The Dead Vane's Log-Tape
lore.description: A punched paper tape feeds from the console's open flank, recording the vane's movement hour by hour, and the perforations continue in perfect rhythm — though the vane overhead has not moved since the last eclipse-tally. The tape's wax seal carries Mercury's transit-mark and a knot pattern Olo Vashti would read at a glance: same message, sent twice, once by instrument and once by hand. Someone chose which record to keep.

content.name: Masir
content.description: The signal-vane at the gantry's tip should be turning; every dial says it is, the needle swinging a slow arc across fused quartz, and yet the vane itself hangs dead in the iron-dark air. Below, two workers argue in low voices over a basalt console split open like a loaf, half its guts wound in copper. Stencilled above the horizon ports, where the axial light goes strange: GANTRY INSTRUMENTS CALIBRATED TO NO EYE'S SCALE. They stop when you cross the plate.

npc.name: Chotsudi Shadake
npc.voice: Quiet, procedural, with long pauses where a season would go.

loan.says: The green decks needed it more than I did. That's the answer I gave the auditor, and it's true, and I hate it. If the replacement doesn't come this cycle, I'll rebuild the bracket from what's in the scrap bin, and I'll water the top tray by hand until I do.

choices.text: Wish her a good first bell.

room.says: Nineteen years. My mother stacked these tiers, and before her, someone I never met. They were careful and I am careful, and the room is still failing, shelf by shelf. That's the part the audits don't cover. Care isn't a repair.

choices.text: When does the bracket come back?

tray.says: It is. The bracket cracked in the thaw season and the spare is out on loan to the green decks. So I lift the tray to the bowls for its light hour and set it back down after. It works. That's what I keep telling myself.

choices.text: When does the bracket come back?

cycle.says: There's no difference I can find. You water on the bell, the bell is rung by people, the people are fed by this. I stopped asking which end I'm on.

choices.text: How long have you kept this room?

greet.says: You're standing where the water comes. Step back, or don't, but the first bell hasn't rung yet and I don't water early.

choices.text: That top tray is set too low.

sleep.says: I sleep where I can hear the bell. If I sleep at the dormitory, I water late, and late water on these sprouts sets the whole cycle back a week. I've done it once. Once was enough.

choices.text: Whose cycle is it? Yours, or the sprouts'?
How long have you kept this room?

reactions.grief: She keeps watering until the pan runs clear, then says the name once and asks who found them.
reactions.shock: She recites the watering rule to no one twice, stops mid-word, and sits beneath the shelf where she sleeps.
reactions.bribed: The offer is a new bracket, and she takes one full season of a pause before refusing it.
reactions.accused: For once her voice carries past the trays, and she lists nineteen years of first bells until someone stops her.
reactions.flattered: Her thanks come out flat, and she names the favor she expects before the visitor can.
reactions.questioned: Her answers come in watering order, first bell to light hour, exact and complete.
reactions.threatened: She hears the threat through without moving, and her only question is whether the top tray is included.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Told the log says otherwise, she corrects the number without excuse and writes the true one in the day's box.
reactions.authority_arrives: The water log is open, and she has moved so her back is between the official and the top tray.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The tiers get both her hands before her fear does, and afterward she counts the spill on the drip pan.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The tone she saves for dead seedlings comes out while she lists three reasons the accusation can't hold.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She confesses nineteen years of small failures in place of the help, then stops, then starts again anyway.

npc.description: Chotsudi Shadake wakes before you speak, sitting up off the linen as if the trays had called her. She rubs the soil line at the edge of her palm and looks at the top tray first, not at you.

lore.name: The Raised Drip Pan
lore.description: The lowest tray rests on two enamel bowls turned upside down, their glaze worn through where the tray has been lifted off them, twice a day, for years.

content.name: Chinhado's Sprout Tray
content.description: The top tray sits lower than the wick above it — the sprouts will touch the light before they're ready. The rest of the trays climb in crooked enamel tiers, grey-green with damp. A stencil on the drip pan reads WATER AT FIRST BELL ONLY. Under the lowest shelf, Chotsudi Shadake sleeps on folded bleached linen.

npc.name: Nym Zialeakhethavael
npc.voice: Speaks in the diction of maintenance applied to things that cannot be maintained — exact, unhurried, occasionally using load-bearing words for the room itself. Asks questions as if checking a log.

time.says: A shift ends when the gauge blinks. It has blinked four times. I no longer convert that into the Nave's clock; the conversion wears the converter.

choices.text: Let them return to the sheeting.

gauge.says: It hasn't moved since first survey, and first survey is not a date. The needle isn't reading the draw — the draw is constant by definition, or we would not be constant. It reads the room's consent. While it holds there, the middle of everything holds.

greet.says: You came in on the concensus. Most do. The drum doesn't mind — it drew around sleepers before there were any. State your business with the draw.

choices.text: That gauge — the needle hasn't moved.
You were sleeping at the drum.

sleep.says: The drum winds whether I watch or not. So I rest inside the watching, and let it watch for both of us. You'd understand if you'd stood a shift. Some call it devotion. It's nearer to division of labour.

choices.text: How long is a shift, here?
Leave them to the drum's watching.

chamber.says: Follow the filament past the last marked junction and then trust the pull in your teeth. The Signal Chamber is not lost. It is merely unattended, which is a different condition — everything here is in some condition or other, and few of them are loss.

choices.text: Thank them, and follow the draw.

consent.says: Of the oldest tenant. I've stood in its consideration. It doesn't speak; it permits. You have credentials older than the Nave on you — I can smell them. Ask your next question of the deep, not of me. I only mind slack.

purpose.says: For is a word for finished goods. This is continuous. Sol draws it; the vault holds the drawing; what it's for is downstream of us, the way breath is downstream of the lung. I mind the slack. There is never any slack.

reactions.grief: Reports the dead one's draw-dates in detail far past usefulness, log-keeping become the only mourning available to them.
reactions.shock: Looks at the violence once, then at the needle, needing to know which of the two the room permitted.
reactions.bribed: Names the offer aloud once, flatly, to log it, then refuses as though the entry settled the matter.
reactions.accused: The word lands like a dropped tool; they keep flattening the silver sheet they already flattened.
reactions.flattered: Thanks them in gauge-diction while their rubbed eyes betray how long since anyone spoke to them unprompted.
reactions.questioned: Recites their movements as gauge-readings, timestamps unconverted, watching whether the question ends when the answer does.
reactions.threatened: Their diction tightens to tolerance-limits, exactness deployed as armor, eyes going to the gauge like an exit.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recalibrates rather than recants, offering a corrected figure as though the fault were the instrument's, never theirs.
reactions.authority_arrives: Does not stop winding; jurisdiction, they note quietly, holds no stencil anywhere on the vault wall.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Between needle holding and room moving they stand divided, the two readings disagreeing for the first time.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects on procedural grounds first, then keeps objecting long past procedure, revealing how much the named one matters.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Hears the plea fully, then files it like an out-of-range reading: noted, unactionable, forwarded to nothing.

npc.description: Nym Zialeakhethavael wakes without transition, the way machinery changes states — one moment curled in silver sheeting beneath the drum, the next standing, smoothing the sheet flat as if the sleeping were a shift-task like any other. The wear of this place is on them, not their surroundings: eyes rubbed to a shine that doesn't quite track, hands precise past the point where precision stops being a choice. They glance at the gauge, then at you, in the same motion — one reading among others.

lore.name: The Gauge Without a Zero
lore.description: Bolted to the drum's axial bearing hangs a draw-gauge whose needle has been pinned against its end-stop for longer than its dial's numerals remain legible — the scale was worn smooth not by weather but by being read, over and over, at the same value. Rindwalker notation, the oldest layer of it, is scratched beneath the pivot: a correction, dated in a calendar no Nave institution keeps. The needle does not measure the filament. It measures the room's willingness to permit the filament, and it has not wavered since first survey.

content.name: Vault 45 Fore
content.description: The light here declines to arrive; it is conceded, grudgingly, from somewhere the spool has already decided about. Chalk-white filaments leave the winding drum finer than thought and thicker than the eye can follow, each draw passing through black glass that behaves less like a window than like a membrane consenting. The vault exceeds its own walls — a step taken toward the far face arrives before the foot is set down, and the stencilled injunction DRAW CONTINUOUS SINCE FIRST SURVEY reads across a surface with no wear on it anywhere. Someone sleeps at the drum's base, curled in silver sheeting, and the machine winds around them.

npc.name: Gusatara Fucfura
npc.voice: Quiet, exact, prone to treating abstractions as objects with weight and grain. Uses the word 'listen' where others would use 'read'. Answers slightly after you finish speaking, as if waiting for the room to finish returning your voice.

keep.says: Everything spoken near it, but not the words — the words pass through like weather. It keeps what the words were carried on. The undertow of them. I have listened to three years of my own voice in there and could not once find myself saying anything.

choices.text: Has it ever kept something that wasn't spoken here?
Then perhaps the room keeps you, not the reverse.

luna.says: I speak toward her the way the skein speaks toward salt. She walks the dream-logs; I keep the wakeful ones. Twice she has come through this room and both times she paused at the opened half and touched it, and the salt remembering her touch is the closest thing I have to an order.

choices.text: And what do the dream-logs dream about?
I'll leave you to your pressing.

work.says: Repair is the wrong noun but the only one the manifests will accept. The salt relaxes — very slowly, the way a habit relaxes — and I press it back into tension. Luna's lading. I have been pressing the same four metres for eleven years and it has accepted maybe a hand's width of my effort.

choices.text: Luna's lading? You speak for her?
Eleven years of pressing. I won't keep you.

greet.says: You walk loud. It doesn't matter here — the skein takes only what it wants — but I flinched, so the fault is mine. This half is opened for re-tensioning. The other half is working. It is always working.

choices.text: What does a recording skein need repaired?

signal.says: Once. Before my time here a layer was cut — you can see the groove — and what came out of it was not any tongue, but the quartz tool's tip dissolved trying to hold it. They reseated the panel and stopped asking. It keeps something that was said down-axis, before anyone was near to say it. Speak carefully. The skein keeps.

reactions.grief: Asked who the dead one listened like, she cannot finish, never having needed that tense before today.
reactions.shock: She stares past the body to the skein's flank, knowing with sickness that the salt kept the whole of it.
reactions.bribed: Refusal comes easily, palms flat on the quartz, as though the offer had a taste the salt must not learn.
reactions.accused: The accusation she sets down like quartz, both hands, though her thumb keeps pressing long after.
reactions.flattered: Underneath the praise she listens for the want, finds it at once, and says nothing of having found it.
reactions.questioned: Her day's accounting comes only after the room has returned the question, itemised in the order manifests demand.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands; she waits for the room to return it as always, and this time flinches first.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she does not retract; she amends, quietly, as though the first sentence had been a mishearing of salt.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction enters and her half-beat pause doubles; she answers the rank, not the person, a beat later than ever.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder passes through salt as no voice ever has; she presses her four metres harder, certain of loss.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name is denied before the sentence ends, too quick, betraying which suspects she has privately weighed.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She cannot unkeep anything, and says so plainly, then stands beside the pleader through the long return of their voice.

npc.description: Gusatara Fucfura is seated against the skein's opened flank with her ear flat to the salt, eyes shut, one hand resting on the quartz panel she has clearly lifted and set down a thousand times. She startles upright — caught at a devotional act she would not name — and busies her hands with the tool-rest as if you had not seen.

lore.name: The Skein's Salt Body
lore.description: The compacted salt is not cladding but the mechanism: each stratum, viewed where the quartz panels are lifted away, holds a compressed interference pattern — generations of speech ground down into mineral, the oldest layers at the core so old their grain matches the notation on the deep tunnels' walls. A groove in the open half shows where someone began extracting a single year of talk and stopped, the quartz tool still seated in the cut, its tip dissolved. The skein has kept what was said in this room longer than there has been anyone to say it to.

content.name: Leebireashio's Recording Skein
content.description: Before the eye finds anything, the ear does: your footfall arrives back to you stripped of its strike, its scuff, its intent — a sound laundered down to syllable. The room does this to everything. Voices enter and return as weather, as the murmur a river keeps from stones. Only then the skein itself: a bulk of compacted salt veined with fused quartz, half of it panelled open like a wound that has agreed to be examined, chalk-white past whiteness into absence. Along its flank, cut where no hand should reach, letters: SPEAK CAREFULLY THE SKEIN KEEPS. The far walls refuse their distances. Somewhere the room is still finishing a sentence begun before the Nave had a name.

npc.name: Yardeishana the Twice-Unmade
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, given to counting; speaks of the room's pull the way sailors speak of tide — respectfully, without explaining it.

greet.says: You came in on the beat. Good. This isn't my shift, so say what you carry and go. The pull runs truer with fewer breathers in it.

answer.says: What the heart can't hold. Not poison — the word's too small. Place and withdraw. Never enter. You'd do well to keep that, since you're built half of elsewhere yourself.

reactions.grief: The tally in their head loses its place; they keep counting anyway, well past the true number.
reactions.shock: Healer's instinct fires before horror does: halfway to the wound, hands already moving, before they understand whose body this is.
reactions.bribed: They price it aloud, flatly, then decline on arithmetic: a third unmaking isn't in the count.
reactions.accused: 'Twice-unmade' stops being a title in their mouth; the count they keep goes wrong for the first time in years.
reactions.flattered: They clock the flattery like a change in the pull, noting the beat, adjusting nothing, giving the praise no purchase.
reactions.questioned: They name the hour, the tally, the beats between; the arithmetic of their own whereabouts bores them visibly.
reactions.threatened: They place the threat and withdraw from it, as taught, and their hands won't manage the never-entering.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They let the contradiction stand, unamended, and give the drain their whole attention, as though distance itself were on trial.
