reactions.authority_arrives: They yield the room as the room yields to the pull, and give their account in beats, not sentences.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Half a beat lost from the count; they re-measure the drain-to-sump distance three times and stop pretending it's routine.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They say nothing, which from them is testimony; the silence takes a shape, and it doesn't fit the accused.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They explain, too fully, what place-and-withdraw cannot reach, a whole doctrine spilling out where two words would have served.

npc.description: Yardeishana the Twice-Unmade works the foil-tension with too few movements, as though the gestures were borrowed from a longer sequence and clipped to fit a shift. Their eyes go to the far dark between touches, timing something the room is doing whether or not they attend it.

lore.name: The Withdrawn Cup
lore.description: At the drain's lip rests a cup of layered mica, its rim fretted with knot-work any Rindwalker would swear by. Inside, a residue of gold dust lies in thirteen exact strata — as if the same draw has been measured, placed, and withdrawn thirteen times, each layer older than the last by an interval nobody has words for. The fourteenth stratum has been started. Someone, or something, still expects a fourteenth.

content.name: Vozomala's Drawing Lung
content.description: The drain sits an arm's length from its sump, which is a distance the eye keeps re-measuring and losing — too near for any plumbing, too far for accident — and between them the gold floor is worn to a shine no foot made. Wound foil hangs in slow coils from a height that suggests a ceiling the room declines to confirm; layered mica admits the light in sheets, so the air itself seems gilded and counted. Stencilled along the sill: PLACE AND WITHDRAW DO NOT ENTER. Something pulls, patient and enormous, through the far dark; the room yields to it the way a lung yields, without complaint, without end.

npc.name: Olo Vashti
npc.voice: Measured, low, and laced with the quiet cadence of one accustomed to translating silence into currency.

greet.says: Welcome back, I suppose. Luna said I'd find you here, newly reconstructed, if a little worse for wear. Her transmission offered little more; only a riddle wrapped in static. She tells you: Before you can map your own seams, you must learn how the city wears its skin. Walk the Commons. Let the Continuants’ order, the Drift’s circulation, and the Rindwalkers’ devotion press against you. Observe how they trade their faith for legitimacy. The architecture of loyalty is built in plain sight; you need only learn to read the mortar.

choices.text: I cannot say no to an order from one of the Seven.
I have watched the three faces wear their masks, and the city’s quiet pulse is no longer a mystery to me.

turnin.says: You have let the Commons move through you. My time with you is at an end; my task was the simplest one. Go now to the wards, but know that they will demand more than sight: they will ask what you owe them. Seek out Factor Solen at the Slate Quorum. The path... already opens.

choices.text: I have seen the mask; I am ready to slip beneath it.

npc.description: Olo Vashti stands with the quiet gravity of one who has watched generations pass through her threshold without altering her course. Her fingers turn a loose coin with practiced economy, her gaze holding the patient stillness of a deep-water current.

lore.name: A Withered Spool of Route-Thread
lore.description: This knotted cord has not recorded anything for a very long time. Olo Vashti cannot translate the information it carries, if indeed it carries any at all. She seems unmoved by its antiquity.

content.name: Reconstruction Bay 14
content.description: Insectile machinery looms over the metal table you find yourself sitting on. Bright, sterile light comes from recessed diodes along one wall; those on the other wall have long died, leaving half the room in dim shadow. Against a column coiled with copper filament leans a figure with the patience of aeons. Beyond, through a threshold, the Commons thrums—a distant respiration, mechanical and biological.

npc.name: Babuchedd Trys
npc.voice: Slow, practical, speaks of repair work the way others speak of duty.

open.says: It means the ship is a body and the work is the prayer. Fix the wick, mend the wall, same act. We keep things running because that IS keeping faith. The city thinks we're tinkers with religion attached. It's the reverse. The mending came first and the prayers grew out of it.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll think about that.
That sounds like a hard life.

greet.says: I'm awake. Say what you need or pick a candle off the list.

choices.text: This room's stuffed past its seams.
What does maintenance actually mean to you?

probe_a.says: Candle bottoms. A candle that tips is a burned shrine. I set every one in pitch before it goes out the door. Slow work, but the shrines stay standing.

probe_b.says: The walkers with route-access. They tell me what the deep halls need and I supply them. Nobody ordered me to sleep here. The Commons dormitory is full and my counter is warm. That's the whole grievance.

probe_c.says: It is. The shrine-supply stops at this counter, and lately everything stops here. I store what comes and sort it when I can. A room holds what the faith needs it to hold, even past its size.

reactions.grief: He keeps setting candle bottoms in pitch through the whole telling, then gets the next one wrong twice.
reactions.shock: Three candles go over when he stands; he sets each one upright before he will look at what happened.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets handled like damaged stock — examined, priced aloud, refused — and his hands don't slow down once.
reactions.accused: The accusation gets an inventory in reply: where he stood, what he sold, who carried the pitch crates.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes his eyes drop to the order book, where the flatterer's name goes once the request comes.
reactions.questioned: The answer comes slow and complete, every delivery named, because he has given this account a hundred times.
reactions.threatened: His voice stays level; his thumb keeps pressing the same soft wick long after it needs pressing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: There is no good answer, so he over-supplies a bad one, explaining the substituted wax long past anyone's asking.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets a nod at a crate to sit on, and the trimming doesn't stop, which is answer enough.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He counts the leaning racks before anything else, and his damage count comes out thinner than he wants.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The list of that person's shoddy candles starts leaving his mouth before he hears how it sounds and quits mid-item.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He explains what he can mend and then what he cannot, and the second list takes longer to say.

npc.description: Babuchedd Trys has fallen asleep sitting up behind the counter, chin on a crate of pitch. Candles crowd every shelf and half the floor; the room is damp enough that the wicks have gone soft.

lore.name: The Pitch-Sealed Prayer Rack
lore.description: One rack under the counter holds candles unlike the stock above: grey solder run into the wick-ends, pitch smeared over the joins. Each candle has been mended, not replaced, and the mending is old and repeated. Someone counts these as too valuable to burn, which for a chandler is a strange kind of faith.

content.name: The Chandler Counter
content.description: Sound goes dull here, as if the walls were packed with something soft. Candle racks crowd the counter, crates stacked to the shelf edge, all of it oxblood with dripped wax. Babuchedd Trys sleeps face-down on the ledger, one extra arm folded under his head.

npc.name: Mett-Mukk
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, warm only by accident. Talks in what things are owed and where they're going.

move.says: Nothing stays, that's the whole trade. You hold a thing long enough to be trusted with the next one. Take the cord-knot trick if you want it: loop twice for return, once for kept. That's the only inheritance anyone here gets.

greet.says: If you're borrowing, the fine's posted and I'm not waiving it. If you're looking for what was in that bay — it moved, and no, I won't say where before it gets there.

reactions.grief: Three times they start the same sentence about a loan the dead one never settled, and finish none of them.
reactions.shock: The pipe goes into the canvas at their feet, and for a while their hands forget the knot.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer out loud against the fine for misremembering, and find the arithmetic insulting.
reactions.accused: The pipe comes down on the desk and they quote the fine for false accusation, neither figure raised.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets itemized with everything else that changes hands here, and their pipe tilts toward the exit.
reactions.questioned: The week comes out of them in loan-terms, item by item, a tally they keep faster than the question.
reactions.threatened: Their hands keep winding webbing, though the roll has stopped getting tighter for some time now.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: A second version of the story arrives, sturdier and no truer, priced like it was always on the books.
reactions.authority_arrives: They straighten the returns-desk stencil with a thumb and let the official state business first.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Smoke drifts the wrong way and they read it like a defect report before feeling anything themselves.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They recite the accused's borrowing record unprompted, which is as near to a defense as the trade allows.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The refusal comes out shaped like directions somewhere else, which is the only mercy they stock.

npc.description: Mett-Mukk stands ankle-deep in folded canvas, winding webbing into rolls the way other people count money, pipe clamped in one corner of their mouth. The last crate is sealed and stencilled; they are, visibly, the last thing in the room that hasn't left yet.

lore.name: The Pantry Ledger Rail
lore.description: A brass rail runs the length of the empty bay, drilled with hooks at spacing too narrow for books. Canvas webbing loops hang from every hook but one, each stitched with a route-code and a name, some names crossed through twice. The wide gap in the bay matches the one missing loop exactly — whatever left, it left on the rail's terms, logged and owed. The crossed-through names are the ones nobody collected the deposit on.

content.name: Range 37 Outboard
content.description: Light comes down the aisle in strips, dodging the smoke from someone's pipe and landing wherever the ceiling dips lowest. Teal lacquer coats the shelves to the height a hand reaches, bare wood above. One bay stands empty, floor scuffed in a rectangle the size of a grain press, and over the returns desk someone has stencilled: RETURN WITHIN THE FORTNIGHT OR PAY THE FINE.

npc.name: Shithgioleshiel Twelve-Winters
npc.voice: Circulation-born: she speaks in relays and transit-times, answers that arrive already moving, everything offered like goods passed hand to hand and nothing owned once spoken.

open.says: I filed the manifests, so I'll say it plainly, the way goods are said plainly. Bay 14 wasn't built and then forgotten—it was *finished*, recent, and its finishing is logged as preparation. You were made ready the way a knot is made ready: everything about you arranged so that when the signal came, something down here would have a hand to close around it. The ship dreamed you before you woke. I only catalogued the dream.

choices.text: Arranged by whom? Say that part.

greet.says: Log four hundred and nine is still running. Stand where the wool can read you, or come back when you've less shadow on you.

choices.text: Who do you answer to down here?
I'll come back when I'm legible.

probe_a.says: Wool holds what salt cannot—salt keeps the shape of a dream, wool keeps its *order*, the sequence of it. You spin them together or the log plays all its hours at once. Everything worth keeping is a braid, never a line.

probe_b.says: To the route, same as any Drift. Luna sets the waybill; I sign for what passes. Answer to *her*—no. You don't answer to weather. You dress for it.

probe_c.says: The logs shortened. Long stillness at the head of each one now, minutes of nothing before playback—like the ship clearing its throat. And something downstream has begun answering before I finish the question.

reactions.grief: From memory she recites the dead one's full itinerary, a catalogue that swells past bearing before she can stop it.
reactions.shock: Mid-feed she stops, salt halted above the rim, the body before her playing all its hours at once.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer aloud like freight, then declines on craft alone: misremembered logs braid badly and play all wrong.
reactions.accused: Accusation strikes her as a filing error; she corrects it with a sharpness that startles even the spindle's patience.
reactions.flattered: Praise finds the one shelf she never dusted; she keeps her eyes on the spindle and under-reacts with visible effort.
reactions.questioned: Her account arrives in relays, each hour delivered like signed freight and disowned the moment it lands.
reactions.threatened: Threat does what the ship never managed: her relays stall, salt spilling past the rim, an unscheduled silence in transit.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she routes the contradiction through three relays of reinterpretation, each arrival more owned than she intended.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction enters and she straightens into procedure, angling her shadow beyond the wool's reach before offering any account.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder she treats as an unscheduled entry, salt already stacked for playback, learning outrunning her fear by seconds.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name lands and her rebuttal arrives before her discretion does, routed through evidence she swore was sealed.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What she cannot give she relabels as cargo, routing the plea toward relays she will never confirm.

npc.description: Shithgioleshiel Twelve-Winters draws a filament of spun mineral wool through a silver comb, and the filament remembers—replaying some drowned hour of the ship's sleep in a shiver of light across compacted salt. She does not look up; the spindle turns whether witnessed or not, busier than any architect intended it to be.

lore.name: The Cradle-Notch
lore.description: Set into the spindle's housing is a recess shaped precisely like the port array in your own forearm — worn smooth at the edges, as if something with your exact modifications was seated here, long ago or long hence. Salt has accreted in the notch in annual rings; there are twelve. The thirteenth ring has begun.

content.name: Taawiothbaeewe's Dream Spindle
content.description: Something is already turning when you enter: a spindle of spun mineral wool and compacted salt, rotating without axle, replaying a dream no one here had. The silver of it is not shine but patience — light arrives late, as if consulting. The chamber's proportions decline to resolve; your ears insist the far wall is closer than your eyes allow. Across the spindle's base, stencilled in a hand that has been dead longer than the Nave: PLAYBACK BEGINS AFTER LONG STILLNESS. Shithgioleshiel Twelve-Winters works the rim without pausing, feeding salt to the turn like grain to a mouth.

npc.name: Atl-Hinqi
npc.voice: Short sentences. Counts things. Warms only when asked about the work itself.

full.says: Store room overflowed. Crates sleep in here now, and I step around them. The pot feeds what comes; the crates are somebody else's problem.

board.says: Some days. A long queue, a thin pot, and I stand there holding the ladle up like it's empty. It never is. The rule holds because I make it hold.

choices.text: How long have you stood at that pot?

greet.says: Pot's done for the day. If you're hungry, come back at first light and queue properly.

choices.text: The whole room seems fuller than usual.
You're packing up. Late for finishing?

years.says: Long enough to know every regular's hands before their faces. The pot outlasted three of my coats and one of my hips. It'll outlast you too.

choices.text: Let them close up in peace.

leaving.says: Late is normal. The last bowl out the door is the day done. Go on, I've rubber to fold.

choices.text: The whole room seems fuller than usual.

reactions.grief: One extra bowl goes out for someone who won't queue again, and it never enters the count.
reactions.shock: Stands still with the rubber sheet dripping, then asks how many, in the voice they keep for the queue.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced against a day of bowls and comes up short; they say so, flat, and stir.
reactions.accused: Stops wiping mid-fold, says no once, then recounts the whole day too fast, ladle knocking the pot rim.
reactions.flattered: Praise aimed at them slides off; praise of the pot pulls them out, and they talk broth too long.
reactions.questioned: Reels off the day's count unprompted — bowls served, benches wiped, hour by hour — the way they'd read a stock-take.
reactions.threatened: They answer the threat with the rule — one bowl per person — as if the stencil outranks the arm behind it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The wrong number holds a beat too long, then everything comes out, even the seconds nobody asked about.
reactions.authority_arrives: Badge first, face second; the stove is checked, and the official is pointed toward the stencilled board.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches the pot lid before it slides off the rim; the crates can go over, the pot cannot.
reactions.someone_else_accused: No verdict from them; only the queue — third in line, before the pot ran thin — fair to a disliked face.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What the rule allows is given, then words keep coming — shifts, weather, the thin pot — anything but what was asked.

npc.description: Atl-Hinqi wipes down the last bench with a sheet of rubber, folding it over and dragging it flat, over and over. Coat off, sleeves rolled, one crate already by the door.

lore.name: The ladle hook
lore.description: A hook of worked stone bolted beside the pot, worn to a shine on its underside. The ladle has hung from it so long the stone remembers the weight.

content.name: The Soup Pot of Last Call
content.description: Sunlight comes in slabs, cut off and restarted by whatever stands in the yard outside. The rest of the room holds a grey-green dim that draughts keep stirring. The pot takes up more floor than the benches do, and crates wait behind it where no crate should. Atl-Hinqi stacks bowls near a stencilled board: ONE BOWL PER PERSON, SECONDS AFTER.

npc.name: Butraca Ferch Rhudwys
npc.voice: Short, dry, allergic to thanks. Measures everything — cracks, patience, other people.

fan.says: Fan's off because the pot's resting. Resin sets sullen if you churn it while it cools. Everything here has a temperament, same as people, and you learn them or you ruin stock.

held.says: For owners who stopped coming down. You mend a thing twice and it tells you who it belongs to. When they come, they come. Until then it sits on my floor and I answer for it.

choices.text: That's a long way to keep faith.

kind.says: It's the only way anybody's found. Go on. Mind the pot on your way through.

books.says: Sent in from three decks over, spines gone the way paper goes when nobody believes in it anymore. People keep what they can carry. What they carry, I keep working. The riveted ones at the back — don't ask, and don't dust them either.

greet.says: Hold that. No — hold it like it matters. Cracked forty millimeters and somebody before me filled it with hide glue, which is a way of saying nobody before me. What do you want.

choices.text: These books aren't from this warren.

reactions.grief: Forgets the pot entirely, four hands open on the bench, and asks whether it was quick.
reactions.shock: Takes the wound in as damage first, person second, then has to sit down among the stacked spines.
reactions.bribed: Names what the thing on her floor belongs to and says that answer isn't hers to sell.
reactions.accused: Stops the press with all four hands and takes her time deciding whether this one is worth denying.
reactions.flattered: Lists the flaw in the praised seam before the compliment even finishes, then names her fee.
reactions.questioned: Gives her movements in exact hours, the way she'd read a crack, no offense taken and none invited.
reactions.threatened: Does not look up, though the resin feeds uneven for the rest of that pass.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recuts the story smaller instead of dropping it and adds a detail only a liar would need.
reactions.authority_arrives: Looks at the jurisdiction first, the face second, and keeps wiping hands that were already clean.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Gets two hands on the glue pot before the shelves settle; boards can fall, resin cannot.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Denies it faster than the facts allow, then covers with the exact state of that person's bench.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says the honest number of mends left in it, then stands in the doorway long after they've gone.

npc.description: Butraca Ferch Rhudwys works with four arms and a bench set up for six, pressing a new spine flat with one hand while another feeds resin thread, not once looking up. Their apron is stiff with dried ochre and burned through in a fan of small holes around the pot side.

lore.name: The spine ledger
lore.description: Under the workbench, a board ledger ruled in Butraca's own hand: every book repaired here, dated, with the crack length and the resin batch noted beside it. Three columns at the back are kept apart from the rest — books mended twice, then marked with a copper rivet and a word nobody uses in trade: 'held.' The oldest 'held' entry is forty years in ship-date and has no return date.

content.name: Warren 32 Low
content.description: The ceiling fan stands still and the glue pot with it, though both are plugged into a live line. Stacked spines and cracked boards fill every shelf and most of the floor, ochre with old sizing, all the way to a stencil worn to NO OPEN FLAME NEAR THE GLUE POT. Copper rods and resin blocks share a drawer with the good brushes. Warren 32 Low was built for less than this.

npc.name: Lainar-Meikavel
npc.voice: Brisk, transit-flavored — everything is routed, timed, or held; they speak of the loop the way a sailor speaks of tide, with respect and no romance.

loop.says: No engine. Never was one. The spin does the hauling and Mercury — the actual one, the tall hum in the walls — keeps the timing honest. I've coasted freight four hundred meters out on this gantry and felt nothing under my feet but certainty. That's rarer than it sounds.

choices.text: Why is the brake wrapped up?

brake.says: Because braking early is the one sin this line recognizes, and somebody decided we'd sin less by removing the opportunity. I think that's prayer, myself, dressed in plumbing. I tally the coast-cycles because tallying is how you stay on speaking terms with a thing this old.

choices.text: Nod, and step back over the chalk line.

greet.says: Mind the chalk line. This isn't my shift — it's nobody's, which is a different thing. You want the way down, or you want the loop?

shaft.says: Nobody comes back from down there, but nobody's confirmed gone, either, and I've learned to leave that arithmetic alone. What I'll tell you for free: the hum in the walls changes pitch past the third junction, like something down there clearing its throat to speak. Mercury speaks easy. That lower register isn't Mercury.

shift.says: Roster says Kelver-Osse. Kelver-Osse went down the shaft in the spring and the roster never learned. So I cover it, because freight that stops being moved stops being freight. The Drift would call that sentiment. I'd call it the route keeping itself.

choices.text: Down the shaft — did they come back?

reactions.grief: The count under their breath stops mid-number, and they find themselves standing past the chalk line they have never crossed.
reactions.shock: They go still as a braked sled — the one forbidden thing — eyes nailed to the plating, not the body.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer aloud like freight, then decline, because a misremembered count is cargo they won't haul.
reactions.accused: They offer their wrist for a timing check, voice flat with the insult of the question.
reactions.flattered: The praise coasts past them unanswered while they check what track it was laid on and where the hand-off comes.
reactions.questioned: They answer with a manifest's grammar, origin to hand-off, and the sled-count under their breath never stutters.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets filed like a schedule change, acknowledged and never once allowed near the count.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie dies mid-sentence and they re-tally aloud, correcting it like a bad log entry, apology nowhere in it.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction ends at the chalk line, and they say so by stepping over it slowly, wand stowed, every courtesy intact.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The count breaks in their throat, and they press a palm to the plating, asking the hum what moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their objection is all timing: the named party was coast-phase elsewhere, and they won't say if they'd mourn them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They refuse the plea without softness, then give the only thing they hold — the exact minute the next sled passes.

npc.description: Lainar-Meikavel walks the loop's inner rail with a quartz sampling wand, stepping over a chalk line drawn across the plating as if it were a threshold in a house. Their coat is a Continuant-issue cut recut in Drift cord-knots at the cuff, and they count sleds under their breath in a rhythm older than either faction's name for counting.

lore.name: The brake lever, bagged and tied
lore.description: At the gantry's head, the brake lever has been wrapped in fused quartz film and tied off with salt-cord, the way you'd bag a wound or a relic — not broken, not worn out, simply denied to itself. The tally beside it records two hundred coast-cycles since the last braking, each chalked, the most recent in a hand that pressed too hard. A sled on this loop needs no brake while the spin holds; whoever bagged the lever was saying that the spin holds, and has been proven right every cycle since, and keeps counting anyway.

content.name: Gantry 14 Outboard
content.description: Something is still moving when you step in: a freight sled, uncoupled, coasting the loop at walking speed and passing you twice before you understand it has no engine at all — it rides the spin, and the spin does not tire. The gantry reaches out maybe four hundred meters to meet the curve, chalk-white with compacted salt packed into every joint, and the work stopped mid-sentence: harnesses hung, a quartz plate half-set in its cradle, a mug with the tea still wet at the bottom. Stencilled along the rail: COAST PHASE SILENT, DO NOT BRAKE EARLY.

npc.name: Shilandra Treanmear
npc.voice: Measured, procedural, faintly liturgical — a Continuant who talks like a work order that has learned to breathe.

open.says: The board says updated by crew, not by hand, and I used to read that as a stamp of oversight. It isn't. It's a boundary marker — this was Jupiter's, and the crew only kept the ledger, never the verdicts. The desk in the closed half is sized for someone I cannot picture sitting down, and the dock for whatever sat opposite them is sized for a ship. Continuants govern rooms. Up here, governance means something that predates our writ and will outlast it, and I've stopped pretending the difference is small.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry this carefully.
A god holds court above the Nave. Right.

greet.says: Hall's half-closed for repair. You can stand there if you like, but the board doesn't answer questions and neither, quickly, do I.

choices.text: Who held judgment here, before crew stopped coming?
I'll come back when it's quieter.

probe_a.says: Salt takes a set when it's rammed — harder than the iron around it, and it doesn't shift. Whatever stood on this floor for however many centuries, the floor was meant to outlast the standing. That's the whole craft, if you want it in a sentence.

probe_b.says: Factor Solen's writ, through three hands down to me. Continuants sign their work so the next generation knows who to trust or blame — my mark goes in the channel cap when this dries. Nobody above me has seen this room. I've seen it. That's the arrangement.

probe_c.says: Old book frames, tally rails, a counter's desk the size of a granary. Machinery for dispute, all of it. Some of it still moves when I lean on it, which I don't recommend and can't explain.

reactions.grief: She rams salt into a channel already set, harder with every strike, and the work needs nothing — neither does she.
reactions.shock: Her eyes measure before she can stop them — span, depth, set — and the counting is what breaks her.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer aloud like a defect entry and asks whether they mean to bribe the board as well.
reactions.accused: The trowel stops — she asks which verdict they think a ledger-keeper could alter, sharper than liturgy allows.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands somewhere she keeps unlitigated, so she answers with the repair schedule and does not meet their eyes.
reactions.questioned: Her hours come back as tasks — salt to nine, cable to noon — a day that keeps its own ledger.
reactions.threatened: She names the threat's expiry like a maintenance date, and only her knuckles on the trowel admit she heard it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught between the wreck of her sentence and the need to file it true, she corrects tense instead of denying.
reactions.authority_arrives: She rises with funeral formality, and catches herself picturing the official, at last, seated at the impossible desk.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first motion is to the salt seam — reading for cracks, the way one reads scripture caught contradicting itself.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She offers no defense, and the silence where a defense should stand says her opinion of them held no mercy.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She recites the limits of her writ, and for once the procedure sounds like apology, not shield.

npc.description: Shilandra Treanmear is on her knees at the base of the odds board, troweling compacted salt into a floor channel that runs the whole length of the hall and then some — a gutter, apparently, for a floor. Behind her the opened half of the room stands in raw iron ribs, and the finished half is green-black to shoulder height, polished by decades of shoulders leaning on it to read the odds.

lore.name: The Underboard Rail
lore.description: Beneath the great odds-board runs a secondary rail of iron, inlaid with thirteen grooves and worn bright along only three. Pinned above it, a Continuant writ orders that verdict-lengths of play be logged here — every wager recorded as a measure of order kept, the hall licensed not for profit but as a sanctioned pressure-valve of the court. The grooves no one uses have oxidised green-black; the three that shine have been counted against in a hand that stopped, mid-column, three months ago.

content.name: Odds Hall
content.description: The tally-board hangs eight meters above the wagering floor, which would be sensible if the counter beneath it had not been built for a person of ordinary height — the clerk's stool stands at the board's foot like a chair set under a cliff. Half the hall is opened to its ribs, iron plates stacked in courses, compacted salt floor exposed like a struck vein, and the stencilled notice on the far pier still reads: BOARD UPDATED BY CREW, NOT BY HAND. Shilandra Treanmear is coiling cable by the one working shutter, coat already on.

npc.name: Sish-Kigharis
npc.voice: Fast, elliptical, counts things — loads, hours, lifters. Speaks of the cranes as colleagues and of Mercury the way a porter speaks of the timetable: present, impersonal, always running.

greet.says: You're standing in a cleared path, so either move or be moved. Forty years I've worked this yard and the lifts have never once waited on a sleeper — I'm not going to be the first.

choices.text: You were sleeping at the edge of a drop.
What's the plate with the scores in it?

sleep.says: You get to know where the loads don't go. That lip has taken naps off four generations of carters and never owed one a scratch. The yard knows its own, or I've decided it does, which comes to the same on a shift this long.

choices.text: Who checks the paths when you don't?

tally.says: The plate checks itself. Older than the yard, older than the ceramic under it, and it has never missed a lift. Don't ask me who set it — ask the rind, and the rind will tell you the same thing everything down here tells you: things were being kept before we arrived, and they have not stopped.

choices.text: You work Mercury's lines. Have you met it?

cranes.says: The clearances hold. That's the honest answer and the frightening one. Three months back the diagnostics started reading before I ran them — not wrong, mind, just early. I stopped asking whether the yard waits for me or I for it. The lifts happen. You learn to be grateful for that and file the rest.

choices.text: Does Mercury know you feel that?

mercury.says: Met it? I've stood inside its throat — the transit arteries run past this yard and once, in a stall, everything went quiet at once, all of it, cranes to corridors, one full breath of nothing. Then it took us back. I don't say that to people who haven't worked a lift. But you asked well, so: it knows the loads. Whether it knows me — that's a longer tally, and I'm not done cutting it.

reactions.grief: The count goes wrong twice before they ask how many hours the dead carter still had.
reactions.shock: Freezes at the lip with the gauge still in hand, and for the first time finds no numbers to read.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the offer back as tonnage and refuses in the same breath — a misremembered load is how lips get fed.
reactions.accused: The word lands like a dropped load, and forty years of clean tallies rise fast, loud, in dated entries.
reactions.flattered: Praise receives the scrutiny owed a strange load: inspected first, lifted never.
reactions.questioned: The last three hours are returned as numbers — lifts, carters, minutes — in the tone of a timetable being read.
reactions.threatened: They write the threat down where loads get logged, same hand, same speed, an entry among entries.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stops the tally mid-number, starts again from a different hour, and everyone present can hear the count go wrong.
reactions.authority_arrives: Stands without being told, hat off, reciting shift totals to a jurisdiction they outrank in hours if not paper.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their eyes go to the hanging load before the floor settles, checking whether the stopped swing has remembered itself.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Nine years of that carter's tallies come out of memory fast — dates, tonnage, nothing dropped — a defence of numbers.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No lift waits, they say, not even for mercy — then they take the lip watch themselves anyway.

npc.description: Sish-Kigharis sleeps under the winch with a knotted cord wound twice at the wrist, hands still curled around a shackle gauge, boots past the ceramic's lip where the yard drops away without rail or caution. Waking, they sit up already reading the tally plate, the way another person might check the weather.

lore.name: The Cleared-Path Ledger
lore.description: Bolted to the crane's foot is a plate of iron with a stylus arm that scores a mark into ceramic each time the load path is checked — a tally cut by the crane itself, not by any hand. The scores run back further than the ceramic's casting seam; the plate has outlived the cranes bolted over it, and holes from earlier mountings dot its margins like scars. Whoever reads it understands the checks never stopped, through every crane, every crew, every generation — the yard does not remember them, and does not need to.

content.name: Crane-Yard 53
content.description: Noise goes first: the yard swallows a footstep and returns it a half-beat late, from overhead, so you hear yourself after you have already moved. Cranes of iron stand in ranks across sintered ceramic, each one able to lift a house, and under the nearest hangs a load the length of a corridor, stopped mid-swing. Nothing moves. Stencilled along the crane's leg: LOAD PATH CLEARED BEFORE EVERY LIFT — the paint worn to ghosts. Lead-grey light lies over all of it, and beneath a winch housing someone sleeps, hat over face, boots hanging past the edge.

npc.name: Sham-Yash
npc.voice: Clipped, load-bearing sentences; measures time in relays missed, not hours.

open.says: Stopped? Sham-Yash laughs once, flat. I've worked this truss eleven years and never seen it empty — not the dead watch, not the dim hours, never. And it's not just this one; the runners say the whole web is the same, every artery, every junction, a circulation that has no memory of ever pausing. That's when I understood what my wrist-knot means at scale: nothing on the Tabard is ever still long enough to be owned, and the moving itself is older than any of us. We're not keeping a road open. We're keeping a heartbeat from noticing it's been beating since before there were ears.

choices.text: Thank you. Your work holds, and so do you.
A heartbeat that never rests. That's not comfort.

greet.says: Mind the slope — the floor takes the careless downhill. If you're standing, you're cargo; move or help.

choices.text: Has this artery ever actually stopped moving?
Don't let me keep you from the slope.

probe_a.says: Compacted salt, packed under the wool — it takes the vibration and gives it back slow. Cheap, heavy, honest. The wool holds the heat, the salt holds the shake, and between them the artery keeps its temper another season.

probe_b.says: Nobody's here. That's the stencil on the wall and the truth under it. The relay sets the work-window and the relay doesn't know this station exists — we sleep when the traffic thins, which it does less every cycle.

probe_c.says: It holds. That's the pride and the problem in one word. I can make any joint hold for now — but now is all I'm ever given. Nobody up here budgets for a fix that outlives the relay window.

reactions.grief: They keep walking the slope as the news lands, then overshare about a joint the dead one packed with them.
reactions.shock: For once they stand still on the sloping floor, trowel hanging loose, gone somewhere the crowd's rhythm cannot follow.
reactions.bribed: Their eyes do the arithmetic of the bribe, come back with cheap, and the answer is already no.
reactions.accused: A flat laugh escapes, then they name the shift-leaders who can swear to every relay of eleven years.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them name the truss's eleven years and ask, flat, what the flatterer actually needs moved.
reactions.questioned: Answers come in relays missed, not hours, and the eleven-year tally arrives without effort.
reactions.threatened: Words are refused; the wrist-knot comes up instead, held out as if knots could testify.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The trowel stops mid-stroke; they start correcting the relay count downward, then add a second lie to cover the first.
reactions.authority_arrives: The wrist-knot gets touched once, an old reflex, and they report the truss's temper unprompted, in case jurisdiction wants numbers.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Trade keeps their feet through the shudder; their eyes go upward, toward wherever the heartbeat felt itself.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The argument runs on tool-marks and salt grades — defending someone never much liked, because the evidence is wrong.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The refusal comes level, but they stay packing wool beside the asker — presence being the only answer they own.

npc.description: Sham-Yash is flat on their back under a relay cradle, feeding spun mineral wool into a gap in the conduit jacket with a salt-packed trowel, working the stuff in like mortar into a joint they know will open again. Around them the artery's foot-traffic parts and rejoins without slowing — a river being patched from inside.

lore.name: The Relay Nail
lore.description: Driven into the sloped floor at the artery's exact midpoint is a hand-width nail of grey metal that no porter will step on or over without touching it — a habit worn so deep the floor around it has compacted into a shallow bowl. The nail holds nothing; it predates the floor's current surface, the third such surface, and the salt itself was compacted around it rather than over it. Whoever drives the relay schedule drives everything else, and the nail is the only fixed point in a kilometre of motion — put there by someone who understood that a room like this doesn't need a heart, only a dot to swing around.

content.name: Truss 24 Antispin
content.description: The floor tells you first: spun mineral wool packed hard by ten thousand boots a shift, giving underfoot like old felt laid over iron, and sloping always to the right so that standing still means leaning without deciding to. A kilometre of artery stretches ahead under a gold haze of lamp-oil and saltsalt dust, the light burning the colour of the fusion-heart's postcards, and along its length the crowd moves at a pace no station clock set — carts, runners, stretchers of freight, all matching a rhythm that arrives from somewhere off the ship's spin entirely. The salt-compact walls take the noise and give nothing back, so a hundred people can pass you close enough to smell their work-clothes and leave no echo behind them. On the third stanchion, stencilled in a hand that has been re-inked more times than the stanchion has been replaced: SCHEDULE SET BY RELAY, NOT BY STATION.

npc.name: Larin-bin Tal
npc.voice: Brisk, route-minded, answers in schedules and line-names. Slow to say anything that doesn't circulate.

end.says: Come back when the junction's busier. Or when it's emptier. Either way, I'll still be here. Somebody has to be.

braid.says: The Braid knows the line stopped. What it doesn't know is why, and that's the part worth selling. I grease wheels. I hear what rolls through. Roll through and I'll tell you the rest.

choices.text: Before that — why keep the slate?

greet.says: If you're here for greasing, tools are elsewhere. If you're here for the Ninth Rung, you're the third to ask today and I still have nothing.

personal.says: My sister ran dispatch on the Ninth Rung before I took this bay. She taught me: a stopped line isn't quiet, it's holding its breath. Four days. She'd have walked the route herself by now. Maybe she did.

ninth_rung.says: Fastest line through this junction — forty years, never missed a slot. Four days now. A line that doesn't run is a rumor with a schedule. The Braid's carrying it before the council even logs it.

choices.text: You look like you knew the crew.

third_asker.says: Two carters and a woman asking for names I don't give. Drift business moves through me; it doesn't stop here. That's the whole trade.

choices.text: What line are they asking about?

reactions.grief: The bearing turns long past clean under their hands, work standing in for whatever the news unseated.
reactions.shock: The nearest line-name comes out of them again and again, the way other people say no.
reactions.bribed: The first question is which junction the money changes hands at, because a bribe still needs a route.
reactions.accused: Stops wiping the clean bearing and asks which line the accusation came in on, as if it were freight.
reactions.flattered: Accepts the praise in exactly the tone reserved for carters about to be overcharged.
reactions.questioned: The day's movements come out as junctions and shift-times, complete and unembellished, nothing volunteered past the timetable.
reactions.threatened: Glances at the door first, then offers nothing that doesn't already circulate the junction.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The schedule gets recounted slower this time, hunting for a minute where both versions could be true.
reactions.authority_arrives: Procedure comes out loud — inventory, schedules, the sign on the wall — anything but the bare tool rack.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their expertise runs three lines deep, and then the fourth possibility arrives and the naming stops.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The accused's last known route is out of their mouth before they remember to wonder what defending them costs.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Gives directions to somewhere better staffed, then can't look at the door it leaves through.

npc.description: Larin-bin Tal works the grease bay the way a relay runner works a leg — everything within reach, nothing owned. Sleeves rolled over forearms stained coral to the elbow, wiping down a hub bearing that is already clean. The carter left without a word when you came in.

lore.name: The tally slate behind the tallow pot
lore.description: A salvaged plastic slate hung on a nail, ruled in grease-pencil: arrival times for every cart-line through the junction, kept in Larin's cramped hand for three years. The last four days are blank except for one line — *Ninth Rung cart, due, not come.* Under it, in a different chalk: a knot-pattern copied badly, the kind worn at a Drift wrist. Someone recorded a route that stopped moving and kept the record anyway.

content.name: Lamuba's Greasing Bay
content.description: The cart-wheel cradle sits empty, chain slack, tallow pot cooling — nothing greased and nobody waiting. Larin-bin Tal and a carter stand half-turned from each other, coral grease-film on everything but their hands, which are clean. The wall sign says GREASE YOUR OWN AXLE, TOOLS PROVIDED; the tool rack is bare. No tin foil on the burn barrel, though the smoke says it burned recently.

npc.name: Runa of the Weightless Burn
npc.voice: Terse, timed, allergic to finished sentences. Everything is a version; nothing is final; she corrects herself mid-word and lets the correction stand.

greet.says: Don't cross-reference mid-run. You'll fold two decks together and I'll spend a shift unbraiding you. — Ask your thing. The pulse gaps in twelve counts.

choices.text: What is this place recasting, exactly?

recast.says: The libraries. Deck by deck, word by word — the old renderings are drifting out of match with what they describe, so we recast. Which means the old ones stop being true, which means we were never keeping truth. We were keeping the newest version of it. That's the whole creed. Now — pulse is back. Mind the rail.

reactions.grief: The forty-first knot goes tight around her finger and she keeps tightening it, saying the name once in the wrong tense, then refusing every version of comfort offered.
reactions.shock: She does not speak at all; her hands keep the recasting motion long after the mica is gone, buffing empty bench, timed to a pulse she can no longer hear.
reactions.bribed: She names the price out loud, exactly, the way she'd tally freight, so the offer becomes inventory and therefore something she can refuse without heat.
reactions.accused: The word lands mid-recast and she sets the mica down too hard, a hairline tick running through the sheet before she can say version one, withdrawn.
reactions.flattered: Praise runs against her creed like a stale rendering against fresh — she recasts the compliment into a defect report and hands it back, watching whether the flatterer keeps the newer version.
reactions.questioned: She answers to the pulse rhythm, not the questioner, forty knots under her thumb like a ledger she trusts more than her own account.
reactions.threatened: She counts the pulse gaps between his sentences and finds them shorter than the foundry's, which frightens her more than the words, though she'd recast this feeling twice before admitting it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her correction habit betrays her — she starts to amend the sentence and hears, too late, that the amendment is a confession, and lets it stand because that is the creed.
reactions.authority_arrives: She is at the rail before the seal finishes speaking, wrist behind her back where the knots can't be read, an old Drift posture she thought she'd outworn.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Every knot on her wrist goes still at once; then, low, to no one: the pulses never miss a count — and she starts walking the gantry to prove it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She starts to defend him, then folds the defense mid-word and asks instead which deck his last rendering touched — an answer she will spend a shift regretting.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She gives the plea eleven seconds of full silence — a pulse and a half — then says the honest thing too fast, and leaves before it can be argued into a promise.

npc.description: Runa of the Weightless Burn stands with a mica sheet held to the pulse-light, reading its layers by what the shine does inside them, one ear turned toward you before her eyes are. Her wrist carries forty knots and a fresh fraying forty-first; she has been here long past any Drift stay, and the room's rhythm has gotten into her speech — she talks in pulses, clipped, timed.

lore.name: The Ledger of Discarded Translations
lore.description: Bolted to the last gantry leg hangs a slate rack of failed recasts — every deck's rendering that didn't survive cross-check, kept anyway, corded in Drift knots by the deck they died on. The oldest cord carries a count in the hundreds; the newest, from this rebuilding, carries one. Whoever recast this library has thrown away more versions of it than the library itself now holds, and kept score of every loss.

content.name: Valsun's Translation Foundry
content.description: Light here refuses to settle: it arrives down the gantries in pulses, silver, timed to some artery no one sees, so that every deck of stacked mica catches its turn and passes the shine along like freight. The foundry is new enough that the sintered ceramic still shows tool-marks, each translation bench squared to its neighbors within a finger's width, nothing yet scuffed into habit. Two workers stand over a half-recast shelf, mid-argument, and stop when you cross the threshold. Stencilled beside the rail: RECASTING IN PROGRESS, DO NOT CROSS-REFERENCE MID-RUN.

npc.name: Hiashym Aaeroun
npc.voice: Slow, exact, devotional in the way of someone for whom every weld is a prayer properly filed. Says little; each word weighs like a placed plate.

open.says: Come here. Put your wrist by the panel — yes, that port, the one no standard chart admits to. When your apparatus opens, the gauges answer. Not mend, not simulate — answer, in the oldest notation, like a lock recognising the key cut for it. I have watched iron speak to men for forty years and it never once spoke first. Whatever you are, walker, you were wound for this room's question.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry what holds.
Wound for it. By whom, though?

greet.says: Press is full, filaments are talking, and I'm not taking stock. Say what you came to say or hold the seam.

choices.text: Where does your stock come from?
Who do you answer to down here?
The gauges read nothing. What reads for you?

probe_a.says: No one living drew this filament. It arrives fed, wound, warm from the takeup, as if the deck above remembered me and pre-delivered. My creed says maintenance is meaning — but who maintains the maintainer's supply, hm? I stopped asking. The iron doesn't care who sent it; it only cares that it holds.

probe_b.says: Sol, in the way you answer a fire — not conversationally. Once a season the notation on the walls changes a glyph, and we're told nothing and adjust everything. The oldest layer of marking is older than the Nave, older than any walker's grandmother's creed, and it has never once been wrong. That is who I answer to.

probe_c.says: The gauges. Three months back the lower decks went quiet on their instruments — stasis pressure, flux, the very heartbeat of the hold — all reading nothing, or reading madness, and the reporting crews stopped filing past that. Meanwhile my press runs full regardless, as if some ledger elsewhere insists the work continues. I stay because if I leave, who mends what holds?

reactions.grief: Something unfiled opens; they sink against the press the way they sleep, unguarded, and say the name once.
reactions.shock: Their hands keep welding while their eyes refuse the sight, the tiniest tremor entering a seam nobody else could measure.
reactions.bribed: Bribery offends them liturgically: to misremember is bad maintenance, and they decline as one declining a miswound spool.
reactions.accused: For once the plates drop: they deny it twice, too fast, words tumbling where forty years taught placement.
reactions.flattered: Forty unsung years make the flattery land anyway; they pretend to check a gauge until the warmth passes.
reactions.questioned: The accounting comes out of them like filed prayers, each answer weighed, and the supplier stays unmentioned.
reactions.threatened: The threat is received like weather against iron: they recite their forty years, slower, as if filing it somewhere permanent.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their thumb finds a filament they claim never passed their hand, and they answer the iron instead of the question.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction gets the only hospitality they keep: an honest accounting of stock that arrived from nowhere.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Something they stopped asking reopens behind their eyes while the filaments sway, and for once they look up.
reactions.someone_else_accused: That one they defend without heat, citing what the filaments fed and when, evidence no waking witness could hold.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The refusal comes placed like a plate, heavy with uselessness, their eyes held on the seam throughout.

npc.description: The ceiling rack hangs a hand's breadth above the press head — closer than any drawn filament should stand to a machine that breathes — and beneath that wrong margin Hiashym Aaeroun is asleep against the iron, one copper-browned hand still closed around a filament as if the hand, not the worker, had custody. The stencilled arc above the hopper reads STOCK ARRIVES SUPPLIER UNRECORDED, its letters silvered over so many times they sit atop one another like tide-lines, and nothing in the aphotic hush can say whether the room was built this full or merely forgot to stop.

lore.name: The Die With No Reverse
lore.description: The press's die is a single piece of iron, and it has no reverse stroke — the mechanism offers no way to open it, no seam, no hinge, only the one gesture: close. Yet the die's face is worn smooth in the shape of filament drawn through it ten thousand thousand times, and the wear runs backward, as if the stock had been pulled out through the closed jaws. Your translation apparatus, reading the die's vibration the way gauges cannot, answers with a single word it has never volunteered before: *awaiting*.

content.name: Blind-Press 6
content.description: The press stands a hand's breadth from the wall it was forged to leave a corridor from — or the wall has come to it; distance here behaves like a tide with no moon. Silver filament hangs in drawn ropes from ceiling to stock, and the stock is the wrong part: bales without origin, stacked past the press's throat, sedimented in strata like a riverbed that never learned to flow. No seam admits light. No light objects. Stencilled into the iron, half-buried under oxide the colour of old blood: STOCK ARRIVES SUPPLIER UNRECORDED. Beside the press, in a nest of filament as if it were straw, Hiashym Aaeroun sleeps — deeply, unguardedly, where no maker sleeps.

npc.name: Til-al-Tanz
npc.voice: Fast, transactional, prices before names. Thaws when a question shows the asker knows what weighing costs.

gap.says: So you can count. Standard says weekly. It's been twenty days and the factor's man hasn't come. I weigh what's true and mark what isn't. That's all any of us can do from a stall.

cord.says: Proof. One bead per weighing so nobody argues after. And the double knots are recalibrations. Look at the spacing yourself if you like — I'm not the one who let it drift.

greet.says: If you're buying, the yellow sacks are cumin and honest. If you're here about the scale, it was calibrated. It was.

choices.text: This isn't your usual shift, is it?

shift.says: Kesh's shift. Kesh's kid's sick, so I'm breathing smoke until dark. Cover a stall twice and it starts costing you your own routes. Say nothing to the Braid about it.

reactions.grief: Stops mid-weigh, leaves a bead uncounted on the pan, and asks what the body weighed when they found it.
reactions.shock: Drops a full bead-string; the scattering takes a long time to notice, and longer to matter.
reactions.bribed: The offered coin goes on the pan, is weighed aloud, and is refused at exactly its worth.
reactions.accused: Names a price out of habit, then forgets the weight in the pan; both wrist-cords get pulled tight.
reactions.flattered: The price of everything on the counter goes up a coin while they listen, flat-faced, to the praise.
reactions.questioned: Answers in inventory: sacks sold, weighings made, knots tied, the day priced out before any question lands.
reactions.threatened: Sets the pan down empty and names the exact sum a false seizure would cost the factor's office.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recites the calibration date a second time, identically, though their eyes have gone to the worn stencil instead of the questioner.
reactions.authority_arrives: Has the knot-record and bead-string laid out before the official finishes crossing the threshold.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches the hanging scale mid-swing, then checks the recalibration knots as though the shudder were their fault.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Gives the accused's last three weighings from memory, exact to the bead, like testimony they never meant to keep.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses the plea in three words, then talks instead about the factor, the twenty days, everything the stall can't fix.

npc.description: Til-al-Tanz stands at the counter weighing something that isn't spice — a folded paper packet, checked against the pan and rechecked. Their wrist wears two knotted cords, not one. They don't look up until the scale stops moving.

lore.name: The Proof Cord
lore.description: A beaded cord hangs from the scale's arm, one bead per weighing, knotted in Drift pattern. Every seventh knot is doubled — the recalibration marks. The double knots have been drifting further apart down the cord. The last gap is twice the length of any before it.

content.name: Weigher-Stall 30
content.description: The hanging scale swings as you duck in, its brass pan still rocking from the last weighing. Sacks crowd the counter, the floor, the hook-rack. Smoke from a brazier hangs pale green under the lamp. A stenciled line on the beam reads SCALE CALIBRATED WEEKLY, DISPUTES TO THE FACTOR, half worn away.

npc.name: Raleem Laisal
npc.voice: Short sentences. Trade terms without explanation. Answers questions about the work willingly and questions about anything else not at all.

work.says: Floor gave. I pulled the boards myself and found the joists soft underneath, so it all came up. It gets mended in order or not at all. Now let me work.

greet.says: Fitting days are over. If you need boots, I size you now and you collect Thursday. If you're not here for boots, say so, I've got two pairs to close before the strip dims.

choices.text: What happened to the other half of the shop?

reactions.grief: Says the dead person's boot size before their name, then says the name twice, quieter.
reactions.shock: The awl goes through the leather and into their thumb, and they don't feel it until the thread reddens.
reactions.bribed: Gives the offer a trade answer, not work they do and not leather they stock, and goes back to the seam.
reactions.accused: Puts the awl down flat and stands too straight, the posture of someone buying time to deny it.
reactions.flattered: Takes the praise as a fact about the boots, corrects one detail, and waits to hear what it costs.
reactions.questioned: Accounts for the day in stitches and lasts, then asks whether they need boots or not.
reactions.threatened: Keeps stitching evenly through the threat, then sews the same seam twice without noticing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Starts the denial over, fails past the first word, and leaves the truth on the bench between them.
reactions.authority_arrives: Answers the greeting in three words and stands squarely between the official and the sheeted half.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Drops to one knee, palm flat on the boards, and waits for whatever the floor does next.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says the named person's heels always failed, then hears, mid-sentence, how much that sounds like testimony.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Answers with the shop rule, mended in order or not at all, and hears for once how cruel it is.

npc.description: Raleem Laisal works standing, an awl in one hand and a last clamped at the hip. Their apron is pale with tallow down the front and black at the knuckles. Every few stitches they glance at the sheeted half of the shop, then back down.

lore.name: The stranded commission
lore.description: On the far bench sits a boot half-built, last still inside, thread waxed and knotted off mid-seam. A tag on the last reads a name and a date from two seasons back. The order was never collected. Raleem has kept the bench clear around it ever since, and re-waxes the thread so it will still take a stitch when its owner comes.

content.name: Bootmaking
content.description: The strap-wheel should be turning. It hangs stopped over the bench, and Raleem Laisal stands under it working by hand. Half the shop is sheeted off behind pitch-sealed planks, its light leaking at the seams. The room is one person wide. Bins of lasts line the wall under a stenciled board: LASTS SIZED, DO NOT MIX BINS.

npc.name: Rurun-Onyrugg
npc.voice: Terse, ledger-shaped, answering the question behind your question and none of the ones you asked aloud.

greet.says: If you're a request, it's in writing; if you're not, you're between the racks. Mind the trolley line — it doesn't mind you.

choices.text: Ask about the glossy new drum.

greet2.says: Came down the shaft already sealed. My job is to store it, not to open what Mars's welders sent — and I'd sooner keep it that way. Write your request like everyone else. Now stand off the line; I've forty counts left before dark.

reactions.grief: His hands tie a route-knot he has not tied since that man taught him, and he lets them finish.
reactions.shock: The slate hits his foot and he does not feel it, because his eyes are counting the wounds like drums.
reactions.bribed: He prices the offer against forty years of sealed drums and finds it weighs less than the graphite.
reactions.accused: The accusation goes into the slate margin, dated, because a lie survives better on paper than on his face.
reactions.flattered: He lets the praise finish, then asks what drum the flattery is trying to open.
reactions.questioned: His answers come as tally-strokes, one tap of chalk per year worked, and the count stands as his testimony.
reactions.threatened: He asks whether the threat is in writing, and the stack hears how badly he wants it to be.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: His voice goes flatter with each word until he is reciting drum weights forty years stale, and hears it himself.
reactions.authority_arrives: He steps between the official and the glossy new drum, one body's width, the way a man shields a ledger.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He counts the racks by eye before anything else, because forty-high stock falling is the only disaster he has rehearsed.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He says the named man's counts never ran light, then hears himself defending someone and stops with the name half-spoken.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He recites the request-in-writing rule and hears, too late, that the plea was never about drums.

npc.description: Rurun-Onyrugg works a windlass one-handed while tallying a chalked drum-count against a slate gone shiny from years of the same hand. Copper rings his wrists in the route-knots of someone who stopped moving long ago but never unlearned the knots. He logs the new drum last, and with a stroke lighter than the rest.

lore.name: Seal-Plug of the Newest Drum
lore.description: The glossy drum's graphite plug is unweathered, its stamped decade-mark a symbol nobody upstairs can read off the standard ledger-key — a notch-count older than any stencil paint on the walls. The plug has been fitted and sealed within the week, its graphite still dusting fingers fresh. Whatever decade it claims, it was cast somewhere that still remembers how.

content.name: Drum-Stack 17
content.description: A hoist trolley crosses overhead before you finish the doorway, hauling a drum the size of a grain-silo up through the green-black gloom of Drum-Stack 17, where basalt drums sit in stacks forty-high and the gantries vanish upward into dark that eats the second torch. Each drum is ringed with packed graphite, and the stencil on the nearest reads DRUMS SEALED BY DECADE, REQUEST IN WRITING. Racks built for one request a generation now turn stock weekly. One drum near the ladder is a wrong, glossy, unmistakably new thing.

npc.name: Nuna-Zetharis
npc.voice: Terse, relay-inflected — talks in manifests and counts, warms by way of facts volunteered.

pod.says: Left before light, no manifest, no runner's cord left in the box — which means whoever moved it didn't want the Braid counting them. Pods numbered, do not swap. Somebody swapped. I re-salt the pallets and I say nothing, because that's the job.

choices.text: And the mark under the paint?

greet.says: This isn't my shift and I'd thank you not to log it. Count's short one pod, and the cradle doesn't lie. You here about the count, or just walking?

choices.text: What happened to the missing pod?
Whose mark is that, sunk in the bed-plate?

notation.says: Deeper than the deep tunnels, that hand. Walkers find scraps of it and argue for years. I've run Mercury's arteries twenty seasons and I'll tell you what I know: that writing counts things before they've happened, and it has never once been wrong. It counted this pod gone a week before it went.

choices.text: That's more than I expected. Good counting, Nuna-Zetharis.

reactions.grief: They add a knot to the wrist cord, the first in years, and cannot make it sit straight.
reactions.shock: Something in them closes like a hatch, and they count aloud past sixty, past the whole of the nest.
reactions.bribed: They quote the offer back as a line item, refuse it as one, and log the hour exactly.
reactions.accused: Denial comes in manifest terms, then the whole night's custody pours out, voice cracking on the runner's cord.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them list their own errors unprompted, an accountant's modesty deployed like a locked door.
reactions.questioned: They recite their movements like a manifest, then volunteer one fact nobody asked for, which is how they warm.
reactions.threatened: They answer only what can be written down, and what can be written down is suddenly very little.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: For once they say nothing, then ask to see the figure in their own hand, as if penmanship could disagree.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the bare anchor-plates before the official's do, and they begin re-salting shelves already salted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Before the hooks stop swinging, a palm is already flat on the ceramic, asking what the girders won't say.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The accused's old manifests come back to them whole, and they defend the person with twenty seasons of volunteered fact.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea outruns their authority, so they give the only inventory left: what they saw, and at what hour.

npc.description: Nuna-Zetharis works the salt pallets with a tally-slate hooked to one wrist, stopping every fourth shelf to press a palm flat against the ceramic and listen, as if the pods kept time. They wear a knotted cord at the wrist with too few knots in it for someone this old.

lore.name: The Unswapped Pod's Cradle
lore.description: The missing pod sat in a cradle of girders built to hold exactly one shape, and its bed-plate still carries an impression — a maker's mark sunk through four layers of paint, older than the stencil above it. Beneath the mark, scratched into the silver with something harder than any tool sold in the Nave, runs a line of notation that matches the oldest carving on the rind tunnels' walls: a pod inventory, in a hand nobody here could copy. The count is current. It includes tonight.

content.name: Pod Housing
content.description: Something swings when you enter — a chain of signal-hooks strung between girders, still trembling from a departure that left the air moving. Sixty pods stack in welded tiers, each numbered in silver paint, and one whole face of the nest is bare: a pod the size of a grain silo was cut free here, its anchor-plates still bright where they tore. The stencilled warning runs along every ladder — PODS NUMBERED, DO NOT SWAP — though somebody swapped. A worker moves among the sleeping shelves, counting salt-compressed pallets into sintered ceramic cradles that were never meant to hold them.

npc.name: Thorimir of Odaeshograd
npc.voice: Dry, spare, hoarding words like spares — technically precise in the wrong grammar, speaking of the machinery as a flock one tends rather than a thing one fixes.

count.says: Of apertures. The ship is mostly aperture wearing the clothes of wall — doors that were never doors, cracks that vote daily to be cracks. Saturn tallies them. I turn the screw so the tally stays honest. That's mending, down here. Not less breaking. *Truer* breaking.

choices.text: Nod, and leave them to the liturgy.

crack.says: Closed is a kind of forgetting. Held is a kind of prayer. Saturn keeps the count of what stays — you don't hand the oldest layer a *done*, you hand it a *still*. The glass remembers the ash; the ash remembers the fire; I remember the quarter-turn. That's the whole suture.

greet.says: You stand in my light. Not that the seam minds — it has its own ideas of dark. This shift isn't mine; the one whose it is went toward the Chamber and hasn't come back to claim it. State what you want or turn the screw behind you on your way out.

choices.text: Why keep the crack open at all?
Where did the shift's owner go?

names.says: Mine, once. A long time ago, or last week — the bed doesn't keep those apart, and neither do I, anymore. It said a name it shouldn't have known, belonging to someone rebuilt in a bay that isn't on the drawings. If that someone is standing in my light: the Chamber already knows the way. It's only waiting for you to agree.

shift.says: Toward the Chamber. Everyone says *toward* — you'll notice the word does the walking so the feet don't have to confess. The ship signals; the ship was always signalling; lately the signal says names. If it says yours, come back and tell me. I collect those.

reactions.grief: They count apertures aloud and lose the number twice, then say too much about the shift no one will claim.
reactions.shock: Mid-quarter-turn they freeze, screw half-raised, and the tally behind their eyes adds one it cannot file.
reactions.bribed: Thorimir prices the offer like counterfeit glass: the ash remembers the fire, never the buyer.
reactions.accused: Thorimir looks at the accuser the way one looks at a hinge voting to crack, neither alarmed nor kind.
reactions.flattered: The compliment lands anyway, and Thorimir wipes at a wrist already clean, twice, before naming the want behind it.
reactions.questioned: Thorimir answers in flock-grammar — hinge-headcounts, seam-weather — until the asker's patience runs out before the inventory does.
reactions.threatened: Nothing in the hands changes, but something behind the tally does — a first aperture opening where they keep their fear.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The screw takes a full turn instead of a quarter; Thorimir lets the wrongness stand, buying themselves one sentence.
reactions.authority_arrives: Thorimir straightens without standing and offers a report of stills: everything held, nothing closed, the seam honest.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room lurches and Thorimir's hand goes first to the seam, reading it like a flock after wolves, breath held.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name gets answered with the room's own stencil — held, not closed — snapped out like a foreman's count.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: For once the liturgy fails: asked what they cannot mend, Thorimir keeps turning the screw and says nothing.

npc.description: Thorimir of Odaeshograd sits where the heat pools wrong, ankle-warm, hands grey to the wrist with basalt flour, turning the clamp's idle screw one quarter-turn and back again, a liturgy performed with the bored precision of long office. They do not look up until the player's shadow crosses the seam.

lore.name: The Unlatched Clamp
lore.description: Bolted to the splice-bed's flank is a clamp of no civilian pattern, its jaws open a finger's width around the sealed seam — and its drive screw is polished bright along the threads, as if turned daily. It has held nothing for decades; the tension it once carried now lives in the glass-over-ash, which hums faintly when the floor does not. Whatever mends this bed does not close the crack. It keeps the crack *choosing*, every day, to stay a crack.

content.name: Svimlislav's Splice Bed
content.description: Nothing here turns that ought to: a drive-spline the girth of a drowned bell hangs mid-correction, its shadow fixed on the basalt like a moth pinned mid-flutter, while somewhere beneath the floor a patience the width of continents holds its breath. Heat pools wrong — cold at the gloved hand, warm at the ankle — as if the room had misremembered which way fire falls. Vitrified ash has been poured into the hairline seam of the splice-bed and sealed under violet glass, glossier than anything new has a right to be. Along the sill, stencilled in a hand that pressed hard: CRACK HELD NOT CLOSED FOR DECADES.

npc.name: Hiyiha-Tozkan
npc.voice: Terse, counting always. Speaks in minutes and dosages.

greet.says: Twenty minutes a soak, no more. Bad knee, bad back, or bad sleep? Sit, and I'll fetch the mineral cups. Do not argue about the time, I will come get you.

choices.text: Where does the mineral water come from?

water.says: A pipe under the floor, older than this room. We test it twice a week and it has never once failed. That's all anyone needs to know. Take a cup on your way in.

reactions.grief: Keeps dosing the cups, but the counts come out wrong for the rest of the shift.
reactions.shock: Stands with a full cup until it overflows their hand, saying the soak limit to nobody.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer in soak-minutes, finds it short, and says the pool keeps its own records.
reactions.accused: Stops counting mid-number, then finishes it anyway, quieter, both eyes finally on the accuser.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit a second too long, then asks what the praise is meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Gives times and dosages flat, volunteering the pipe-test schedule before anyone asks for it.
reactions.threatened: Asks how many minutes the threat is worth, and moves the mineral cups a little further away.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Redoes the arithmetic aloud, arrives at the same wrong answer, and starts explaining the floor drain unprompted.
reactions.authority_arrives: Watches the official's boots cross the wet floor, tallying steps, before offering a mineral cup.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Fear arrives as arithmetic: they need the ripple timed, and their hands are steady only while counting.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends them in minutes, citing every soak they supervised, then stops and asks whose word counts more.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains what twenty warm minutes can and cannot fix, and holds the door open anyway.

npc.description: Hiyiha-Tozkan starts awake, checks the glass at the door before saying anything. Their hands smell of sulfur and soap. They keep one eye on the pool while drying the other on their apron.

lore.name: The Timing Glass
lore.description: A sand-glass hangs at the door on a wire, its bulb cracked and re-sealed with wax. Someone has scratched extra notches beside the twenty-minute mark.

content.name: The Soaking Room of Quiet Ledger
content.description: Nobody is walking along the pool edge, though the floor is wet with fresh footprints. Hiyiha-Tozkan has fallen asleep in the trickle-chair meant for sprained knees, boots off, clipboard on chest. The room is scrubbed past its paint: warm grey concrete, a square of cut turf by the door, and a stencil reading TWENTY MINUTES PER SOAK, TIMED AT THE DOOR.

npc.name: Snobar Ginagli
npc.voice: Terse, exact, proud of the count. Talks in measurements and dates.

work.says: Feed line for the west stall lights. Old run, forty years checked and never failed. Sign the log on your way out. That's the whole rule of this room.

greet.says: Door was latched. You here for a splice or a look? Because the look costs nothing but waiting, and I'm behind.

reactions.grief: She asks for the date, then the hour, and cannot produce either, the scraper forgotten in her bare hand.
reactions.shock: Her arm stays in the wall through three callings of her name, heat glove cooling on copper she stopped seeing.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against a forty-year run with no faults and calls it short by everything she owns.
reactions.accused: Her voice stays level while she demands the exact date, since dates can be checked and people cannot.
reactions.flattered: The compliment gets one nod, the same she gives a delivery of copper, and then she asks what needs splicing.
reactions.questioned: The day's count comes back with gauges and timestamps before the question finishes, delivered toward the wall, not the asker.
reactions.threatened: Word for word, the room's rule comes back at the threat, though her bare hand has whitened on the scraper.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The contradiction sends her reciting every splice from that week, faster and faster, as if volume were proof.
reactions.authority_arrives: She rises to full height for the first time all shift and has the log open before any request.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder gets logged to the minute, the only part of it she can hold, while the coils swing.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The named worker's inspection record is out of her mouth unprompted before she hears how partial she sounds and stops.
