reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her no takes four words, and only after the door closes does her bare hand begin to shake.

npc.description: She has a heat glove on one hand and the other bare, holding a scraper. Copper dust on her forearms, slate slivers at her feet. She was reaching into an opened wall when the door moved.

lore.name: The Third Splice Log
lore.description: Under the bench, bolted where a knee would kick it, hangs a leather-bound log. Each splice in this loft gets three entries: the date, the maker, and the date it was next checked. Columns run back forty years without a gap. The last pages are Snobar Ginagli's own hand, one line per day, even for splices already passed twice over.

content.name: Row 33 Outboard
content.description: The splice bench sits a hand's width below the window ledge, low enough that a worker here stoops all day. Half the loft is opened to the wall: copper runs exposed, coiled and tagged. The other half is swept, ordered, oxblood-painted. Stenciled above the bench: SPLICE LOG MUST BE SIGNED. A woman straightens up, startled.

npc.name: Vilkrazd Krich
npc.voice: Clipped, apologetic about nothing, precise about everything. Talks the way a person talks when they are filling in and want it over.

greet.says: Sit if you're bleeding, wait if you're not. I'm covering for Fenner, so the hand speed isn't what you'd get on a good day.

choices.text: I'll come back when Fenner's here.

pedal.says: It's rocked for four years. Before that there was a proper pedal, and before that there wasn't a chair at all, just a bench and two strong cousins. The drill's older than my name. It'll outlast the chair, and then the bolt, and then whoever's counting.

shift.says: It's mine as of this morning and nobody's by tonight. Fenner's boy is sick and the roster won't bend. Third time this month I've covered. I had a different trade once. Hard to remember which.

trade.says: I set bone, down the row. Cleaner work. A fracture closes or it doesn't. Teeth argue with you for years and then everyone acts surprised. Fenner knows this. That's partly why it's me here.

roster.says: Because bending it costs regard, and nobody who runs the floor wants to spend theirs on a drill room at the end of row 83. So they spend mine instead. I haven't decided if that's an insult or a compliment.

worried.says: It held yesterday. That's the whole ledger I keep. Come back tomorrow and I'll tell you if the ledger got longer.

reactions.grief: Twice the count comes out wrong before they set the tray down and say the name once.
reactions.shock: For a second the hands reach for the tray out of habit, then stop, because there is nothing to heal.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets a question back: what exactly would they be forgetting, and for how long.
reactions.accused: A short wrong-sounding laugh escapes, then they list every patient treated that day from memory.
reactions.flattered: Without looking up, they correct one detail of the praise, unable to let an error stand.
reactions.questioned: The answer is a list of instrument counts, precise to the minute, with no question back.
reactions.threatened: The roster goes unmentioned and the stitch gets finished before they look up.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted with the tally, they admit it flatly, then explain the lie in more detail than needed.
reactions.authority_arrives: They glance at the door the way they glance at the clock, then recite the waiting list like a defense.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The instruments slide and they keep a hand flat on the patient's shoulder until the room settles.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their first thought is the culprit's bandaged hands, and they say so, then wonder aloud why they noticed.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What they cannot do gets a precise answer, then they do the small part anyway, knowing it is not enough.

npc.description: Vilkrazd Krich works the tray with their back to the door, counting instruments by touch. The smock is too short in the arms and buttoned to the collar. They keep glancing at the wall clock as if it owes them something.

lore.name: The Borrowed Pedal
lore.description: The pedal is not original to the chair. Someone bolted it on with a bracket cut from an old bed rail, and the bolt holes don't line up, so it rocks a finger's width either way. A second pedal lies dismantled in the tray drawer, its cam stripped. The bracket is newer than the chair, older than the shift.

content.name: Row 83 Deep
content.description: The cold sits at ankle height, pooling off the floor seams, while the pipe overhead still carries heat to rooms that matter more. The chair creaks under anyone who sits in it. The foot pedal is worn glossy, and stencilled above it: PEDAL SLOW, THE DRILL DOES NOT FORGIVE HASTE. Sacking has been stuffed into the draught gap under the door.

npc.name: Baiqah Raidanawi
npc.voice: Terse, procedural. They name tools, not feelings.

greet.says: Shift isn't mine. Covering until Sevin sends someone. Don't light anything indoors.

stall.says: Babruck's maker left it as-is. We don't clear a shrine until the rite is closed. Somebody will come back to close it.

reactions.grief: The grinding stops mid-feed; they recite the dead one's open orders until the list loops and starts again.
reactions.shock: Resin skins over in the tray while they stand there, eyes on the body, hands forgotten around the pour.
reactions.bribed: They price it out loud — mold count, rite closure, Sevin's return — and the sum comes up worthless.
reactions.accused: Hears the accusation and answers with the whole borrowed shift in order, twice, flatter the second time.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands like a part cut to wrong size; they hold it, test the fit, and wait for the ask.
reactions.questioned: The borrowed shift answers for them: hours, absent owner, bench rules, no flame indoors.
reactions.threatened: The sleeves come down past the extra joints; they name the threat's terms back, level by effort.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They repeat the wrong detail once, hear it fail, then file the true one as a correction to the log.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the official's boots, then the hanging smoke, weighing which rule the visit intends to enforce.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their hands take the bracing stance before they agree anything happened; the molds get counted, twice.
reactions.someone_else_accused: A defense arrives faster than their rules allow, listing what the named one's hands could never manage at that bench.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They name every form that exists and who holds each, then keep naming, because the answer underneath is no.

npc.description: Baiqah Raidanawi stands at the workbench, feeding resin into a grinder that belongs to someone else. Their sleeves are rolled past additional joints that should not exist, and they do not mention them. They work quickly, like a person borrowing time.

lore.name: Split mold
lore.description: One clay mold has been pried apart and left mid-pour. The tallow inside hardened with a thumbprint in it, small enough to be a child's.

content.name: Babruck
content.description: The smoke from the censer should rise. It hangs instead, a grey rope above the tray, and the stall around it waits. Clay molds sit in rows where they were set down. Solder coils lie open. A stencil across the counter reads BURN OUTDOORS OR NOT AT ALL.

npc.name: Nemikirnar-Yaianui
npc.voice: Short sentences. Counts things out loud. Corrects the player's grip before correcting their questions.

dye.says: Whatever the market orders this week. Sand for the Continuant clerks, blue for the writ. The lead vats hold the color where iron would eat it. Next batch is yours if you wait an hour.

greet.says: Mind the line. Gloves past it or not at all. You buying dye or standing in my light?

reactions.grief: The dead owed them two coins and a stencil, and they list this aloud, then smaller things, unable to stop.
reactions.shock: They look at the body straight on, the way they never look at the vats, and their hands keep working.
reactions.bribed: The offered coin holds their eyes a beat too long before they price it against a season's wages and refuse.
reactions.accused: Hands stop mid-fold; the cloth goes down too carefully, and the question comes back twice as hard.
reactions.flattered: Nothing in their face moves at the praise, but the next bolt goes under the surface smoother than usual.
reactions.questioned: Routine questions get batch numbers and clock hours, counted out flat while the cloth keeps moving.
reactions.threatened: Their voice stays level while their eyes find the glove line, measuring exactly how far back they can stand.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The count in their mouth skips a number; they hear it themselves and start the batch over from one.
reactions.authority_arrives: Work does not stop for jurisdiction; they nod once at the stencil and keep both hands in the vat.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Both hands find the vat rim; they watch the color, not the ceiling, waiting to see what it does.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The named person gets defended through insult, crooked work and a bad grip, and they mean every word kindly.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No is all they have, delivered in the spoiled-batch voice, and the next three batches get checked twice.

npc.description: Nemikirnar-Yaianui stands over the second vat with sleeves bound at the elbow, feeding a bolt of cloth under the surface one hand-width at a time. They never look down while doing it.

lore.name: The count board
lore.description: A hammered lead slate hangs by the door, scored with tally cuts in iron. The oldest cuts have gone brown. Someone has been counting batches here longer than the current sign has hung.

content.name: Dye-House 8
content.description: The light never sits still here. It slides off wet dye in the vats and shivers across the low ceiling, sand-colored, doubled by steam. People pack the aisles shoulder to shoulder. The floor sticks at every step. On the second lead vat, stenciled in flaking red: VATS HOT, GLOVES PAST THIS LINE.

npc.name: Ziztilatl-Yitlhuitl
npc.voice: Counts before they speak. Talks in weights, dates, and short verdicts. Nothing offered twice.

greet.says: Mind the third stack. It leans. You here to draw stock or to stand in my light?

choices.text: The ledger says you're over capacity.

overflow.says: Three harvests, no new silo commissioned, no grain refused. The Factor's office knows. The chalk stays until somebody makes it a lie. Now — I have a wall to argue with.

reactions.grief: Keeps reciting the dead one's carrying loads, dates and all, long after anyone wants them.
reactions.shock: Eyes fixed on the body, mallet still raised from a strike they do not finish.
reactions.bribed: Says no before finishing the count and goes back to arguing with the wall.
reactions.accused: Puts the mallet down with both hands before answering, then talks longer than they have in seasons.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise finish, then asks flatly what is wanted in return.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day's movements sack by sack, dates and door-times included, plainly bored by the routine.
reactions.threatened: Their voice stays level while, inside, they tally everything the threat could actually reach.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stops mid-count, repeats the false figure once, and corrects it in a voice gone thin.
reactions.authority_arrives: Meets the official's eyes once, then answers in door counts and dates, no greeting offered.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Names the shudder's length in seconds before anyone else speaks, then walks the stacks, mallet up.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends the named person with three dated facts, then adds a fourth that sinks the defense.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Tells them who else to ask, which costs more to say than the refusal did.

npc.description: Up a ladder between the sacks, driving a timber brace into a bowing wall with short, hard strikes of a mallet. Chalk dust on both forearms. They finish the strike, look down at you, and wait.

lore.name: The Overflow Ledger
lore.description: A slate hangs by the hatch, chalked in two hands. One column counts what the silo was built to hold. The other counts what is actually in it, and the second number has been climbing for three seasons. Below both, someone wrote: 'We do not turn grain away. We do not promise the walls can take it.' The chalk on that last line has been gone over many times, so it will not fade.

content.name: The Grain Silo of Quiet Ledger
content.description: Sound arrives wrong here. Voices go in and come back flat, as if the grain ate the edges off them. Sacks climb the timber walls past the second shelf, and the weighted hatch behind you settles on its rubber seal with a thud. Stenciled on the frame: HATCH WEIGHTED, DO NOT PROP OPEN.

npc.name: Jaqy Vithia
npc.voice: Terse, murmured, as if the room were listening — which it may be. Words paired in ways that almost parse: the sleeper is 'mid-deposit,' the salt 'keeps its opinion.'

greet.says: Mind the floor. It's mid-deposit — don't give it a second shape to argue with. You've gold on you. Heartward, then? Everyone heartward eventually.

sleeper.says: Impression retained, occupant unknown. That's the whole of the doctrine, friend — we keep what the salt keeps and we don't audit it. Off-duty sleeping this close to the heart, though... the salt was already growing the shape before they lay down. Take this rod. It's read the floor longer than I have.

choices.text: Take the rod and go back to work.

reactions.grief: Hands keep feeding wool into a gap already closed, wool to nowhere, their face gone iron-dark on both sides.
reactions.shock: Something in them goes mid-deposit, a shape half-grown and abandoned; they do not finish the thought or the sentence.
reactions.bribed: They name the offered thing aloud to the room, once, so the salt holds its record of it.
reactions.accused: The no-audit doctrine collapses audibly; they invite the accusation into the record, voice losing its murmur entirely.
reactions.flattered: Praise reaches them where accusation cannot; they warm toward it a full breath before remembering to distrust the donor.
reactions.questioned: Their comings and goings emerge as litany, each hour a deposit, leaving the floor nothing to argue with.
reactions.threatened: Their eyes fix on the intruder's feet, reading the floor's opinion of them, saying nothing worth keeping.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Jargon arrives too fast and keeps arriving; they re-explain the first lie slower, as though the salt misheard.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction makes them smaller; they surrender a glass rod unasked, the way one hands over a tooth.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Everyone else steadies; Jaqy watches the wool, whispering that the room moved first, that rooms here never move first.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name lands and they defend it too quickly, citing impressions, and the speed itself becomes testimony.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea outlasts their doctrine; they repeat what the salt keeps, quieter each time, until it stops meaning anything.

npc.description: Jaqy Vithia crouches at the nook's threshold with a bristle of glass rods in one fist, feeding spun wool into a gap that closes before it is filled. Heat-shimmer plays across them though nothing here burns; gold light from the shaft beyond gilds one side of their face and leaves the other iron-dark. They work without looking at their hands.

lore.name: Salt Impression Block
lore.description: Where the sleeper lies, the compacted salt has not merely dented — it has recrystallized, grown a faceted negative of the body as though the floor were preserving an impression the way amber keeps an insect, down to the weave of the wool. Rindwalker practice salts a dwelling floor to record who treads it; this one has recorded more than treading. The facets are still growing. Whatever lay here was not the current sleeper, and the salt remembers them anyway.

content.name: The Occupant Nook
content.description: Underfoot the salt has been trodden to something like tile — granular, faintly warm, as if the floor itself were asleep and running a fever. The nook holds one occupant's shape pressed into spun mineral wool, iron-dark, a body's negative occupying more of the room than the room was cut to give; the walls meet it without seam, the way water meets a drowned stone. A stencil near the floor reads IMPRESSION RETAINED OCCUPANT UNKNOWN, half-absorbed by the wool, legible only if one already knew to look. Analogy offers itself — a nest, a reliquary, a root-cell — and each dies mid-thought. Somewhere beneath, the machinery breathes without lungs. The sleeper does not stir, and the room adjusts around them anyway, patient as geology.

npc.name: Morioshin Viabayono
npc.voice: Terse, precise, using index-words for things that have no index; corrections offered like settlements of debt.

greet.says: You're breathing my shift's air. Fine. Touch nothing with a shelf-mark — the stack remembers whose hands, and it files complaints. Ask, or step back.

reactions.grief: For once refuses index-words, using the dead person's name twice before their voice files the rest under nothing.
reactions.shock: Confirms what they are seeing the way they confirm plates, twice, and the second pass fails to make it true.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the bribe costs the record, not them, and names its price in shelf-marks before refusing.
reactions.accused: Stops confirming mid-plate, stylus frozen; says nothing, the first true rebuttal still unindexed.
reactions.flattered: Treats praise like an unindexed plate, confirming nothing, asking what entry it wants filed under.
reactions.questioned: Movements recited as shelf-marks, dates first, one correction offered unprompted like a small debt paid.
reactions.threatened: Names the threat like a misfiled plate, aloud and flat, while their other hand finds the nearest seam.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their shift-chord betrays the route they named; they re-knot it slowly, offering a new number instead of a confession.
reactions.authority_arrives: Finishes the current confirmation before looking up, then removes one glove, as if jurisdiction required bare hands.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Counts the stacks once, gets eight, refuses the second attempt, and writes the discrepancy where no one will read it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects by citation, three discrepancies between the claim and the stack's memory, faster than grief or mercy could arrive.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits the limits like a settled debt, then stays anyway, stylus down, learning the plea though it changes nothing.

npc.description: Morioshin Viabayono works the third stack with gloved hands and a stylus of packed graphite, tracing plates the way a person checks a sleeping animal's breathing — not reading, confirming. They wear a shift-chord knotted for a route that ends here, which no honest route does.

lore.name: A silver shelf-mark, hammered flat
lore.description: One plate bears a small badge of hammered silver — a catalogue mark from a system nothing else here uses — dented as if dropped from a height no ladder reaches.

content.name: The Unindexed Stack
content.description: The smell arrives first: graphite sweating under load, a heat that has never once been felt as warmth, sweetened faintly by silver oxidising where no air should bother it. Plates rise in stacks the eye declines to total — each seam where two faces meet is absent, as if the metal had been persuaded rather than joined. You count seven stacks and stop counting; the number disagrees with itself on a second attempt. Sound behaves like light in deep water, arriving from directions that have no geometry. Stencilled across one plate, in a hand older than the paint beneath it: ORDER CONSISTENT PRINCIPLE UNDETERMINED. Someone has underlined UNDETERMINED, twice, in a fingernail's worth of silver.

npc.name: Tliz-Nozkoatl
npc.voice: Clipped and transactional. Counts what you say back to you before answering. Warms a degree when a question is exact.

end.says: Mind the bamboo on the way down. It takes ankles.

busy.says: The floor is moving more than usual. Talk runs ahead of everything else these weeks — the terminals post strange, people trade on it, I keep the accounts. Sit if you can find a spot.

choices.text: Tell me about the ledger instead.

thaw.says: Hm. You ask like someone who'll be worth a cord someday. Come back when you have a name to trade, or news I can knot. The desk stays open.

greet.says: You climbed the stair, so you want something. Name it or go back down.

choices.text: You look busier than this room allows.

posts.says: Motifs that repeat where they shouldn't. Regulars argue over it like it's weather. I don't sell what I don't understand — I sell what I can verify. That's the whole trade.

choices.text: That's a rarer discipline than it sounds.

ledger.says: Names. One cord per name, one knot per favor owed. A rumor costs a cord, not coin. When I pull your cord, you answer, or the knot comes out and everyone learns why.

choices.text: And the sources? The stencil says you don't keep them.

longest.says: Not telling. Pulling a cord is my move, made when I choose it. Ask again when you own one.

choices.text: Then give me a cord. What do you want to know?
I'll come back with something worth a knot.

sources.says: Sources rot. Names hold. You keep what keeps, and you let the rest move through. Every Drift wrist knows that pattern before it can talk.

choices.text: Fair enough. I'll remember how you work.

reactions.grief: Says the name once, writes nothing down, and for the first time in weeks the queue just waits.
reactions.shock: First their eyes take in the door, then the body, then their own hands, knotting something they never started.
reactions.bribed: The offered sum gets counted aloud twice before it goes back across the desk, slower than any refusal should travel.
reactions.accused: Their denial comes flat and immediate, followed by a request to have the accusation entered verbatim.
reactions.flattered: They thank the flatterer the way a fee is receipted, then ask what the praise is meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Answers in the order asked, then waits, stylus ready, as if the question were a sum to check.
reactions.threatened: They repeat the threat word for word, and the next three knots come out wrong, which is their flinch.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie gets corrected in fewer words than it cost, the false cord untied by their own hands.
reactions.authority_arrives: Rises before being asked, turns the ledger face-down on the desk, and offers the correct title unprompted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The announcement that bamboo does this comes out steady, though their free hand has found the desk's edge.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Three dates the accused could not have kept come off the ledger flat, and they defend nothing past them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The door stays open after they explain, entry by entry, everything the desk has no power to undo.

npc.description: Tliz-Nozkoatl sits behind the desk with a stylus behind one ear and a cord loop around three fingers, knotting without looking down. The waiting benches are fuller than the room was built to hold, and they are working through names faster than the cords can be tied. They look up only when you reach the desk itself.

lore.name: The Cord Ledger
lore.description: The ledger's pages hold no writing. Each page is a panel of holes, and cords run through them, knotted in Drift patterns. Every cord ends in a name and a tally of notches. Rumors here are not bought with coin — a client pays by owing, and the desk decides when to call the debt in.

content.name: Ratra's Ledger Nook
content.description: Bamboo strips underfoot shift and squeak; mica dust sticks to your soles and follows you up. The stair climbs harder than a stair should, and at its top a ledger desk stands in a space meant for one person, now holding three benches of waiting clients. Above the doorframe, stenciled: NAMES KEPT, SOURCES NOT.

npc.name: Iagngrim-Renn
npc.voice: Blunt, ledger-precise, reverent about materials and impatient with questions that aren't about the work; talks of the hold the way a mender talks of a body — bays as ribs, cold as a pulse.

end.says: Mind the lip on your way out. And if you pass a tally down there deeper than mine — don't add to it. Just walk away.

choices.text: Leave Iagngrim-Renn to the cold and the count.

dark.says: I've gone down to tier nine, where the frost stops melting ever. Below that the bays are older than the tally, and the shelving isn't ours — older joins, older gods, whatever laid it out didn't need our ladders. I sealed the hatch behind me and I log the depth and that's all any of us should do. Mars holds that dark. It isn't ours to walk.

choices.text: You've felt Mars, then. Down here?

help.says: Then hold the far edge and don't fight the cold — it wants the sheet flat more than you do. Layer it with the grain, mica reads pressure like scripture. There. Seated. That's one more bay ready to receive whatever the ship decides it needs kept.

hers.says: Her last entry reads only: cold's deeper this year. It was. The cold has been moving up the tiers my whole time here, slow as a season nobody named. I don't dwell on it. I seat sheets, I keep the tally, I mind the lip.

choices.text: And when the course is done?

hold.says: For the emergency never declared — it says so on the wall, and the wall was here before anyone's grandmother. Four hundred years of rations sit in the dark tiers below, still sound, still counted, and no summons ever came for them. Some call that waste. I call it faith with a ledger.

choices.text: Has anyone walked the lowest tiers?

mars.says: Once. Tier seven, a weld the length of a county, still warm after nobody knows how long, and I understood I was standing inside someone's hand. Not a story. A hand. I bowed to it, because you do, and came back up, and I've seated sheets ever since like a person saying grace. Whatever sleeps below that, it keeps its own counsel and I keep mine.

choices.text: Then I'll let you keep it.

read.says: Every weight it has ever carried is written in its layering, pressed in like growth rings. The old builders knew it; we inherit the knowing. That's what we are, in the end — inheritors of a craft we didn't invent, maintaining a patience we didn't start.

choices.text: You've felt Mars, then. Down here?

work.says: A woman named Ossa, dead eleven years now, left this course three sheets from done. Her clamp is still where she set it; I won't move it until the work it held is finished, that's just manners. The rind keeps what we finish and forgets what we leave, and I'd rather be remembered by my welds than my name.

choices.text: And when the course is done?
Did she ever say why she stopped?

count.says: The tally is mine now, and before me it was three others, each chalked over the last. Two hundred and nine bays sealed. The count is the prayer, down here — you keep the number honest and the number keeps you.

choices.text: Has anyone walked the lowest tiers?

greet.says: Mind the lip. The floor ends where the last mender stopped believing in it. You've come down to see the cold, or to help me seat this sheet?

choices.text: What is all this kept for?

finish.says: Then the bay opens for storing, and the hold keeps its shape one course longer. That's the whole of it. The ship doesn't thank you; it just holds, because you held first. In my creed that's better than thanks.

choices.text: Has anyone walked the lowest tiers?

reactions.grief: The felt hands go still; afterward they press the copper smear twice, once for the tally, once for the name.
reactions.shock: Describes the wound as a failed join, too precisely, the way a mind goes when it refuses the sight.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offered thing far too high, a mender's contempt for bad material, and sets it among the rejects.
reactions.accused: Sets the sheet down harder than work requires and recites bay numbers like alibis, voice cracking on tier nine.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit unfinished the way a sheet sits when the grain runs wrong, and waits for the ask.
reactions.questioned: Answers in tally-depths and bay numbers, not looking up, as though the ledger already settled the matter.
reactions.threatened: Fear arrives as arithmetic: they count the steps to the hatch without meaning to, and log the count.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Says the tally is wrong before checking it, then checks it, then says nothing at all, which is answer enough.
reactions.authority_arrives: Looks up for once, measuring the official as they would a crack in a shelf lip, slow and silent.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Lays a bare palm against the shelving and counts, as if taking the pulse of something that should have none.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names the last three jobs that person botched, unasked, and only hears their own voice on the third.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses in the same tone they log depths, then reseats a finished sheet that was already seated, twice.

npc.description: A broad figure in rust-brown leathers gone stiff with cold, working with hands wrapped in felt against the chill, breathing through a scarf crusted at the edges. Iagngrim-Renn talks without looking up, voice pitched to carry across the open tiers, and marks each seated sheet with a smear of copper oxide like a signature of devotion.

lore.name: The Abandoned Course
lore.description: The half-done shelving ends in a mica sheet tacked on with one clamp, and beside it a chalked tally in a hand not Renn's, counting bays sealed — it stops at two hundred and nine, mid-stroke.

content.name: The Cold Hold
content.description: The cold comes off the opened half like a breath held for generations, and under it sits the work-smell of this place alone: flux-burnt copper, wet mica dust, and the faint green sweetness of frost dying on black glass. You stand on a lip of flooring that ends in nothing; the hold drops away in shelved dark, tier under tier, each bay broad enough to berth a harvest fleet that never came. A stencil on the shuttered half reads HOLD MAINTAINED FOR EMERGENCY NEVER DECLARED. In the working half, Iagngrim-Renn is setting sheet-mica into a shelf lip someone else abandoned mid-course, years ago by the look of the tooling.

npc.name: Lutuleth Lukishaipaaloa
npc.voice: Terse, unhurried, in the cadence of someone whose work will outlast the conversation by decades.

greet.says: Mind the mist line — it's not poison, but it will grow in you if you stand in it. You want something or you want to watch?

ask_room.says: An atrium that seeds on its own time, and its own time is longer than ours. Venus keeps it; we keep the beds. The pumps are older than the terraces and failing kinder than they should — so we stay ahead of them. Go on, I've forty beds before the light dims.

choices.text: Let me get out of your way.

reactions.grief: Sets the wand down with both hands and leaves a bed unmisted for the first time anyone here remembers.
reactions.shock: The filter fogs from breathing gone wrong, and for a moment they are the one standing inside the mist line.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer in seed-years, finds it small against a decade of beds, and keeps walking the terrace.
reactions.accused: The wand comes off their shoulders for the first time all shift, and their voice loses its measured pulse.
reactions.flattered: Takes praise like the room takes light, secondhand and slow, eyes already pricing what the flatterer wants back.
reactions.questioned: Answers in bed-counts and mist-times, wand still moving, as if forty beds were alibi enough.
reactions.threatened: Voice level as ever, but the bed-count runs one short, and they hear it too late to hide.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Holds the accuser's eyes a beat too long, then corrects the record in the flat tone kept for dead beds.
reactions.authority_arrives: Greets jurisdiction the way they greet a failing pump, as a scheduled fact, and keeps the wand moving past them.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Watches forty beds' worth of drifting light swing out of true, and does not resume misting until it settles.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks up unprompted, against their own rule about other people's names, and recites the nights that person stayed past dim.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: States plainly what they grow and what they cannot, then names who upslope might still owe them a favor.

npc.description: Lutuleth Lukishaipaaloa walks the upper terrace with a siphon-wand across both shoulders, breathing through a ceramic filter the color of old copper, releasing a measured pulse of spore-mist into each bed and marking the rod without breaking stride.

lore.name: The Seed-Tally Rod
lore.description: A basalt rod, notched edge to edge, leans where the walkway meets the first terrace — one notch per discharge of the upper spore-vats, and the notches run past the number anyone would bother carving for a single season.

content.name: Spore-Atrium 18
content.description: The light does not fall so much as drift, caught and slow-turning inside green-black clouds of spores that hang at every height the eye is willing to test, so that brightness arrives at the walkway already secondhand. The atrium runs downslope past the sight of anyone standing on it, terraced in cast basalt and sintered ceramic, half its beds still raw substrate where seeding was promised and postponed. A stenciled line rides the third terrace wall: ATRIUM SEEDS ON ITS OWN TIME. Somewhere upslope, a pump labors against a rhythm it was not built for.

npc.name: Zhubael Evavel
npc.voice: Clipped, liturgical; measures worth in load borne, not words spent.

open.says: Older. That is the word I have been circling since my first descent. The stasis gear, this lattice, the sealed chambers beyond — none of it was built by hands like ours; our civilization grew up in its working like moss in a gutter. You cannot mend what you did not make; you can only keep faith with it. Everything the Nave calls ancient is a young thing sunning itself on the back of this.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry that carefully.
Then nothing down here is ours at all.

greet.says: Mind the filament. It remembers tension longer than I remember names.

choices.text: The machine healed it before you touched it.
Why do you stay, if the work needs nothing?
Who do you answer to, down here?
This lattice — is it newer or older than us?
I'll come back when I'm worth the trouble.

probe_a.says: Aye. Basalt casts, filament draws — the lattice closes a break between one pulse and the next. What's left for me is witness. Somebody must stand here and see the ship forgive itself, or the forgiveness never happened.

probe_b.says: Grievance, if you want it plain: we were sent down to maintain, and maintenance is a courtesy between two parties who know each other. Whatever this is, it was never briefed to us. I stay because abandoning a post is a kind of lie.

probe_c.says: The writ says the Continuants; the copper on my wrist says my route; the deepest honest answer is the tally Saturn keeps. I file reports. Lately I file them knowing they vanish somewhere between here and the Nave, and I file them anyway. That is the whole of my obedience.

reactions.grief: She keeps winding filament round a strut the lattice closed long since, her hands outliving their reason.
reactions.shock: Her witness's habit fails outright: she sees the violence entire and files none of it, unable even to look away.
reactions.bribed: Her refusal comes fast and in the grammar of debts: a gift unearned is a weight she will not carry.
reactions.accused: Twice, and too precisely, she recites the mender's creed; the word breaker has cut deeper than she will admit.
reactions.flattered: She takes the praise the way she takes suspect strand — tested, not trusted — and concedes nothing in return.
reactions.questioned: She answers in loads and lengths, as though each question were a strain to be entered and borne.
reactions.threatened: Some inner tally weighs the threat, finds it light as spent filament; her calm is chosen, and the choosing shows.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she does not retract; she explains, then explains again, spending a month's worth of words in a single minute.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes reach the door before protocol reaches her spine; the day's tally is ready, and so is her stillness.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She waits a pulse for the lattice's answer; the silence that comes frightens her more than the shudder.
reactions.someone_else_accused: In ledger-terms she vouches for the named one — honest weight, years of it — then flinches at her own haste.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Owning no mending for this, she offers the last office left her: to witness it, and say it happened.

npc.description: Zhubael Evavel crouches in the lattice's amber aftershock, winding drawn filament around a shattered strut the machine has already made whole again — her hands finishing a repair that finished itself, so the record and the member agree. Around her, too many menders press close in the iron-dark gloom, each tending work that no longer needs them.

lore.name: A slack coil of drawn filament, unspooled mid-work
lore.description: One lattice-thread lies slack across a bench, cut clean, and beneath it a repaired arm-bone — not bone, not alloy — that carries the thread's weave inside itself as a scar. Whoever worked here pulled the thread mid-mend and left; the mend continues anyway, grain by grain, at a pace you could watch for a year and not catch. The work does not need the worker, and never did.

content.name: The Knitting Lattice of Quiet Ledger
content.description: Light behaves here like a rumour of light: it arrives already tired, pooling around the filament-strung lattice as though apologising for interrupting. The room is iron-dark and crowded past sense — folk stand shoulder to shoulder among cast basalt benches, mending things by pressing broken members to the woven threads, which close over fracture like water remembering its channel. No wall admits to being a wall; the ceiling may be a floor the room forgot. The cold is wrong-footed, warmer where it should bite and vice versa, and beneath everything a stencilled legend, half-oxidised: BREAKAGE REPAIRED BEFORE REPORT FILED.

npc.name: Desvodon Krazdvo
npc.voice: Counts portions while talking. Short sentences. Talks about feeding as a duty that does not pause for conversation.

fed.says: Hold it with both hands, it's hot. Come back tomorrow. There'll be a line and there'll be soup. That's the whole promise and I keep it.

room.says: Stores from three depots, sent here because we feed more than most. Nobody came to collect the surplus. So it sits. I ladle around it.

choices.text: Is there enough food for all of it?

wait.says: People leave this room every day and most come back tomorrow. You learn not to sort them too fast into gone and not gone. The soup keeps either way.

choices.text: That's a patient way to run a room.

work.says: A volunteer started mending the bench, left the pattern cut, never came back. Three weeks now. I keep it there. If she returns, the work should be where she left it. If she doesn't, I'll finish it myself. Either way the bench gets mended.

choices.text: Three weeks is a long wait.

board.says: That's mine. Count of second bowls. The rule is seconds after, and I keep the count so the rule stays honest.

choices.text: Some days look marked through early.

greet.says: One bowl now, seconds after. You'll wait if the line's long. State your business while I fill.

choices.text: Why is everything stacked to the ceiling?
Whose sewing is that on the bench?
What are all the marks on that board?

hands.says: I won't name names over soup. Ask the council if you want a report. Ask me and you get fed. That's the arrangement.

marks.says: Some days I serve seconds before everyone's had a first. Sick folk, small children, a Rindwalker fresh out of a long tunnel. The count records what I did. It doesn't excuse it.

choices.text: Sounds like good judgment to me.

enough.says: There is enough. There has always been enough. The problem is never the pot. It's the hands between the pot and the bowl.

reactions.grief: They serve the mourner seconds without being asked, breaking their own sign, and do not count the bowl.
reactions.shock: Four bowls get poured for an empty room before their eyes come back from the door.
reactions.bribed: The offer sits on the crate untouched, like a bowl nobody claimed, and they quote the sign instead.
reactions.accused: Their eyes stay on the pot through the whole accusation, and the ladle, for once, is not counting.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets the same answer as an order: a nod, a bowl, and a reminder there is a line.
reactions.questioned: Questions get numbers for answers, bowls served, bowls owed, and the ladle never pauses for the asking.
reactions.threatened: They finish filling the bowl in front of them before looking up, which takes longer than it should.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They do not deny it; the count comes out different the second time, and they hold to the new number.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door opens and they check the pot before the badge, deciding the soup is the one that cannot wait.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room moves and their hands are on the pot rim already, counting heads before the light returns.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They keep stirring and say nothing, which from them is a verdict, and they know it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Bigger than the pot, they say, and mean it; then they fill one bowl anyway, because one is theirs.

npc.description: Desvodon Krazdvo works the pot with a long ladle and does not look up until the bowl is filled. Slate apron, sleeves rolled, forearms scalded pink from years of steam. Behind them a half-mended bench holds a buckram pattern cut but never sewn.

lore.name: The Second-Bowl Board
lore.description: Under the ladle rack hangs a buckram board, stiff with grease, ruled into columns. Each column is a day; each mark is a second bowl given out. The rule says seconds come after everyone has eaten once, but the last six days are marked through before the pot is even empty. Someone has been counting and breaking the count at the same time.

content.name: Soup-Pot 46
content.description: The light dims whenever the pot steams, then comes back through it in a gray wash. The room is one step up from the landing and a ladder down to the stores. Crates of bowls stand against the hardwood wall, more than the sign above them allows for: ONE BOWL PER PERSON, SECONDS AFTER. The pot holds half the floor.

npc.name: Sajamila bin Nairal
npc.voice: Clipped, practical, spoken around the work. Sentences end where the thread does. Long enough in this stall to treat cloth as furniture and strangers as weather.

room.says: Live in it? I keep it. Someone cans fish upstairs all day, and the smell settles. A sheet changed weekly keeps it out of the bedding. That's half the creed, done small.

choices.text: Why store all this here, then?

count.says: Every person who slept in this stall. Knot when they came, cut when they went. Rindwalkers move by routes. This is my route, so this is my record.

choices.text: The last rows are all knots.

greet.says: Mind the sheets. They're the walls. You break a seam in here, you break my roof.

choices.text: What are you stitching on that hem?

store.says: Not mine. Half the stall holds other people's goods — out of season, out of work, waiting. I've the sheets and the dry corner, so I keep them. You hold things for people, they hold you.

uncut.says: They keep meaning to leave. Storage down here, work up top, and the stall fills faster than they can sew. So I stitch. When a hem runs out, you start a new sheet. That's how it's always gone.

choices.text: Say nothing and let the needle run.

reactions.grief: The needle goes through their thumb, and they finish the stitch bloody before asking who else knows.
reactions.shock: Somewhere inside them the count goes on, one stitch, two, while their eyes stay on the cot.
reactions.bribed: No is their first answer, though they ask, after a moment, what exactly the knot would need to show.
reactions.accused: 'Me' is repeated back once, then twice, then a third time, while the needle sits idle.
reactions.flattered: Praise for the stall gets one shrug; the want underneath it gets their full attention.
reactions.questioned: Dates come off the hem knot by knot, unprompted, in the tone they save for weather.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets priced out loud, then set aside, and the thread keeps moving.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They blame old wax for the slip in their story; a fresh cake sits on their palm.
reactions.authority_arrives: Hours of stitching stop when the official crosses the doorway, and they stand with cotton dust on their knees.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Both hands catch two sheets mid-swing, and they hold the walls together until the motion stops.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Three nights of that person's knots are out before they remember the record is not theirs to spend.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refusal comes in the words they use for torn seams, and afterward they cannot meet the asker's eyes.

npc.description: Sajamila bin Nairal sits on the floor with their back to a cargo net gone taut with stored goods, pushing waxed thread through a sheet edge with a horn needle. They do not look up. The needle goes in, the thread comes out, the count on the hem grows by one stitch.

lore.name: The Tally Cloth
lore.description: The sheet nearest the cot is the oldest, its waxed thread gone horn-brittle. Along one hem, in tiny stitches, someone has worked a count — one row per sleeper this stall has held, a new knot for each arrival, a snipped end for each departure. The last three rows are all knots. Nobody has snipped anything for years, and there is no room left on the hem.

content.name: Yafinila's Sheet Stall
content.description: Noise dies at the doorway. The hung sheets soak up every sound, so the loft holds a hush that presses on the ears. Past the first cloth, iron-dark shapes crowd the walls: crates, bundles, a cot, more sheets folded into stacks that reach the low smoke-stained ceiling.

npc.name: Kulf Bieldnagli
npc.voice: Quiet, literal, a little tired. Talks about the bell the way you'd talk about a patient. Uses we for the tower even though they're alone in it.

greet.says: Mind the fourth stair. It gives. You're not here for the dusk bell — it's hours off.

choices.text: What are all those marks on the wall?
The stencil says dawn and dusk only.

rules.says: The stencil is old and right. Dawn and dusk. The others are mine, off the count. If the tower falls it'll be because I broke a rule to keep it, and I've made peace with that arithmetic.

shift.says: Dagn's. Dagn's hands went bad in the tunnels and someone has to pull. So I pull. Nobody assigned me. It just turned out that way and stayed that way.

choices.text: How long has it stayed that way?

howlong.says: Two seasons. I keep thinking I'll hand it back and then I ring and it feels like mine. That's the trap of work, I think. It takes your name while your back is turned.

ownwork.says: Sealing. Below, in the shafts, when a passage has to close. Good work. Clean ends. There's no clean end to a bell — you just stop, and someone else starts, and the tower doesn't care whose hand it is.

tallies.says: Every ringing since before I was born. My grandmother started the slate, or someone did. I'd have to check the count to tell you. The bell doesn't count itself.

whyseal.says: Sometimes the reason gets written down. Mostly not. I sealed two I was never told the reason for, and I've stopped asking. It isn't doubt exactly. It's more like — you learn which doors the ship closes, and you learn to let them.

reactions.grief: The name lands, and they mend the same inch of rope three times, and the third pass is no better.
reactions.shock: Not one of their many arms moves, and they stay on the chapel side of the door.
reactions.bribed: What the coin would break gets named first: the dawn-and-dusk rule, word for word.
reactions.accused: They believe it for a second, honestly, because they break bell rules daily and know their own arithmetic.
reactions.flattered: They answer the want under the compliment and never once look up from the fray.
reactions.questioned: The account comes out in the same order every time, stairs and hours, plus which stairs give.
reactions.threatened: Moves the broth horn back from the rail's edge, which is the only answer they give.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Corrects the record once, then keeps correcting it, further back in time than anyone asked about.
reactions.authority_arrives: Stands, wipes the wax from each hand in turn, and answers only what the jurisdiction actually covers.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The rope is caught before it finishes swinging, and then every stair gets checked for new cracks.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Offers an alibi for a person they have argued with for years, then admits they don't know why.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say what they have no power over, item by item, until the quiet turns honest.

npc.description: Kulf Bieldnagli sits with the rope across their knees, mending a fray with waxed cord, working by the cold light from the arrow slit. More arms than a person should have, none of them idle. They don't look up when you enter.

lore.name: The Rung Count
lore.description: Besind the rope, a slate column of tally marks runs up the wall — one per ringing, dated in a small copper hand. The last hundred are all in the same hand, and the dates are wrong: midday ringings, midnight ones. Whoever has been covering this tower has stopped keeping the rule and started keeping the count instead, as if the counting itself were the duty now.

content.name: The Tower Chapel
content.description: Heat sits at the top of the room, around the bell, and never comes down the stairs. Below, the stone stays cold enough that Kulf keeps a horn of broth on the rail. The chapel holds three chairs, a cracked lead sheet patching the east wall, and no room left over. Stencilled above the door: BELL RUNG AT DAWN AND DUSK ONLY.

npc.name: Raibah Naiqoun
npc.voice: Short sentences. Talks about the shrine the way a mender talks about a pump: it has a job, and the job is being done.

back.says: Mind the tray on your way out.

help.says: Hm. Yes. Hold it flat, don't push. You'd be surprised how few ask. Everyone wants to look at a shrine. Nobody wants to hold a panel while it seals. There. Good.

choices.text: Why do you tend this alone?

take.says: Once. Man took a token off the old line, tried to erase a debt by carrying it off. Brought it back within the week, plus interest. The shrine doesn't chase anyone. It just stays where it is, and that's worse.

work.says: Damp got under the west panels. Wall sweats every cold season and the seam I laid last year didn't hold. So I'm doing it right this time. A shrine that leaks is a lie you tell with a building.

alone.says: Others come. Sevin sends menders when a job's past me. But a threshold is one person's promise most days. Mine, at present. The copper keeps me honest about that.

greet.says: Shrine's half-closed till the seam cures. If you came to leave something, the tray's by the sill. If you came to ask, ask.

choices.text: Leave what? What do people leave?

leave.says: Whatever they can spare. A bolt, a strip of cloth, an hour of labor. Nobody takes. That's the rule since before me and it'll hold after. Take nothing from a threshold and the threshold stays a threshold.

tokens.says: Accounts. You take passage, a favor, a tool — you hang a token, you owe the shrine a return. Most people pay in work. The long line is old families. They keep paying. That's the whole of it.

collect.says: Whoever's home first. That's the office. No title, no vote. You sweep, you seal, you read the tokens. I've held it eleven years because I keep showing up.

choices.text: Eleven years is a long stay.

reactions.grief: The iron stalls twice in one pass before she asks who settles the dead one's token line now.
reactions.shock: The sight grays her face, and she asks in her seal-checking voice whether anyone has touched the body.
reactions.bribed: No is out before the figure is finished; anything taken off this shrine comes back with interest.
reactions.accused: She sets the sealing iron down before she answers, and the denial comes out one register too high.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets the same nod she gives a panel that held, and then she waits for the favor.
reactions.questioned: She answers in work order, panel to seam to token line, the same list every time, unbothered.
reactions.threatened: Her voice stays level, but the third arm grips the loose panel hard enough to bow it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She does not argue the evidence; she re-does the account from the start and flags her own error out loud.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets a nod over her shoulder and one arm still holding the panel steady.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first act is counting the token lines; her second is a structural explanation nobody asked for, delivered too calmly.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She recites every job that person has held flat for her, then asks which of them the accuser watched.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea gets the only honest answer she has — her hands promise seals, nothing else — and she holds the door.

npc.description: Raibah Naiqoun kneels in the opened half with a sealing iron in hand, sleeves rolled past the elbow. One arm holds a panel steady while the other two dress a seam. She stops and looks at you without getting up.

lore.name: Horn token line
lore.description: Each token is scratched with a name and a debt count. The longest line holds names going back four generations; the shelf was never cut to hold them all.

content.name: The Threshold Shrine of Long Account
content.description: A copper pan swings on its nail as you come in, still rocking from the door. Half the shrine is open to its bones: panels lifted out, tools laid in a row on sailcloth. Sunlight lands on the finished half, where small horn tokens hang in strict lines. Stenciled under the sill: LEAVE WHAT YOU CAN, TAKE NOTHING. One of the token lines is twice the length of its shelf and droops past the edge; nobody has trimmed it.

npc.name: Nakym Reaa
npc.voice: Measured, liturgical about materials, wrong in small confident ways — she speaks of the mould and the absent casting in the same present tense, as though both were on shift.

you.says: I keep the mould. When it has finished correcting — when the salt stops holding a shape — my work is done or my work was never mine. Either way, that's a fine day to stop salting. Go. The floor likes you; it's warmer already where you stood.

cast.says: Cast? Nothing was cast. Something was *kept* — the mould doesn't make, it sustains the shape against the pressure of everything that wants the shape gone. What left, left intact. We're not permitted the word for what it was. The mould knows it; ask the floor, it answers warmer where you stand longest.

choices.text: Then what is it correcting now?

greet.says: Mind the seam. The floor takes salt best from a light hand — it's correcting for the weight that's gone, and it overdoes, like anything grieving. You'll have come down for the shape it's holding. Everyone does, eventually. Some of us just got here first.

choices.text: You said it's correcting. For what, exactly?
Is the Signal Chamber close to this?

signal.says: Close? You're standing in its anteroom and calling it a neighbour. The Chamber isn't a place the way the Nave is places. It's where the holding *answers*. It has started answering again — that's what the tallies are for. Your ports will hear it before your ears do. When they do, walk toward the warmth that isn't from the floor.

choices.text: Will you come with me when I go?
Then I'll walk toward the warmth.

correcting.says: For the absence. Salt remembers load — pack it under a weight for long enough and it holds the weight after the weight's gone. The whole deep is salt under the ceramic, under everything, holding up a shape nobody alive has seen. Three months back the holding changed. I salt the seams. That is my whole religion, and it is sufficient.

choices.text: The readings from down here — are they the holding, changing?

reactions.grief: The horn stops mid-tilt; she asks which floor the body warms now, and cannot hear her own answer.
reactions.shock: She stands salt running from the tipped horn, a white seam spreading at her boots, counting nothing.
reactions.bribed: She weighs the offer in her palm the way she weighs compact, then names its provenance worthless, refusing without heat.
reactions.accused: The salt stream wavers mid-pour; she stares past the accuser as though the charge were addressed to the mould.
reactions.flattered: Praise she treats like over-salting — the floor overdoes when grieving — and she answers with a correction about seam weight instead.
reactions.questioned: Her rounds come back as litany — seam, horn, seam — answered before the question finishes, entirely unbothered.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets named back in materials — horn, salt, weight — her steadiness a taxonomy, not courage.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she repeats her claim more slowly, as if slowness were a form of proof, then oversalts the seam twice.
reactions.authority_arrives: She angles her body between the official and the bare mould, salting steadily, deference rendered to the floor alone.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder sends her to the mould before thought, hands checking seams, whispering inventory to something that cannot answer.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Relief arrives before she can refuse it; she covers by cataloguing the accused's technique, every measurement suddenly generous.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her confession is narrow — the office keeps shapes, not people — and she offers warmth-readings from the floor instead.

npc.description: Nakym Reaa stands ankle-deep in the crowd, salting a fresh seam of ceramic with ground compact from a copper horn, blowing it evenly as a sower. Gold dust has settled into the creases of her gloves so thoroughly it reads as skin. She works without watching her hands, and her eyes keep returning — briefly, involuntarily — to the empty mould, the way one checks on a sleeping thing.

lore.name: The Corrections Ledger, scored into the floor
lore.description: Around the empty mould, scored into the ceramic itself in lines no tool could have cut so fine, runs a tally of adjustments — each one dated in a calendar older than the Nave's oldest writ, each one recording a change made to the castings *after* the thing cast had already been removed. The most recent entry is a single mark. You understand, dimly, that the mould has not stopped correcting: it is adjusting for an absence, holding the shape of what left the way a socket holds the memory of a tooth. The stasis you walked through to get here is not stillness. It is compensation — continuous, patient, and aimed at something no longer present.

content.name: Mould Floor
content.description: The floor is sintered ceramic fused over compacted salt, and it gives underfoot like a tongue testing a wound — granular, faintly brined, faintly warmer at each footprint than the one before, as if the ground were learning you. Gold saturates everything: not gilding but a colour the light itself has agreed upon. Crowds press shoulder to shoulder into a space that seems, wrongly, larger than its walls admit; the gap where something vast was casted out and drawn off stands bare, and every worker orbits it without looking. Above a scorched arch, stencilled: CASTINGS ADJUSTED AFTER REMOVAL.

npc.name: Shamoshii the Once-Remembered
npc.voice: Clipped, precedent-citing, allergic to wonder; she has heard every question this room provokes and answers only the ones with a procedure attached.

greet.says: You're standing where the record says nobody stands. Writ or observation — choose, I have forty-one judgments due before the dim.

throne.says: It seats an Officer who has not been down since the audits; the writ says unoccupied, so unoccupied it is, and what sits in it on the rare days is not my business to witness twice.

reactions.grief: No line on the death-form takes what she actually wants to write, and the pen stays capped through three attempts.
reactions.shock: She freezes mid-stamp above a finished order, the room's cold current suddenly the only thing she can feel moving.
reactions.bribed: She cites the statute against falsifying a record, voice flat as the stencil, and pushes the offer back unexamined.
reactions.accused: She names the statute that makes the accusation a filing, then hears her own voice arrive one tone too high.
reactions.flattered: Praise has no form to file, she observes, and asks which writ the compliment is meant to serve.
reactions.questioned: She answers by writ number alone, every movement already on record, and returns to judgment thirty-four before the asking finishes.
reactions.threatened: Her grip finds the stamp as if it were precedent, and the groove-touch comes twice where once is habit.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She rules the discrepancy a transcription error and re-inks the entry herself, slower than any correction requires.
reactions.authority_arrives: She rises before the doors finish opening, covers her stamp, and produces a deference she has plainly never practiced.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder gets logged as vibration, unexplained, source pending, its entry stamped while everyone else is still looking up.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her objection arrives by the book, yet she volunteers a detail of the accused's habits no filing ever required.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea has no form attached, and she says so twice, the second time quieter, already listening for one anyway.

npc.description: Shamoshii the Once-Remembered stands at the writ-table nearest the dais, stamping orders with a stamp older than her office, pausing between each to touch two fingers to the groove in the steps — a habit, not a rite, performed the way one taps a cup to settle its leaves.

lore.name: The Petition Groove
lore.description: A shallow trough worn hip-deep into the dais steps where every petitioner has stood in the exact same place for — the clerks will not say how long — and the stone has simply given up.

content.name: Span 54 Antispin
content.description: The heat pools at the foot of the dais steps where a hundred petitioners' bodies have warmed the basalt for generations, and the cold rules everything above head-height, where the air moves in a current nobody lit and nobody owns. Twelve clerks' desks orbit a throne built for something forty armspans through the shoulder, each desk sized to a person, each dwarfed past apology by the gold-chased architecture around it. Two processions — writ-bearers in slate, rind-clerks in copper — file past each other without acknowledgment, working the same floor as rivals share a river. A stencil the height of a child runs the dais face: THRONE UNOCCUPIED, DO NOT APPROACH.

npc.name: Hana Shawy
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical without knowing it. She uses words like sift and tenure and proof incorrectly, or correctly according to a grammar you were not taught. She does not explain the room. She has stopped being asked.

greet.says: You're early. The sill knows you before I do, so I'll take its word for it. Don't touch the filament — it remembers hands. If you're going further down, go before the wax sets; after that the floor grows choosy, and I'm not authorized to argue with it.

choices.text: Go before the wax sets. Understood.

leave.says: Then go.

ask_room.says: Not what. Whom. Same question down here, in the end. Sol keeps the tenancy rolls, and the rolls are older than the tenants — you're on them or you aren't. I only pour the wax. Take that with you: whoever's roll you're on, they've been expecting you longer than you've been expected by anyone else.

reactions.grief: Grief miscounts her: three times the sequence fails, then she sets the glass face-down and asks who found them.
reactions.shock: She is somewhere behind her own eyes, lips counting on without her, forearms cold against all the remembered heat.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against her tenure, finds the arithmetic insulting, and resumes her count at the same number.
reactions.accused: The count stops mid-number and she offers her palms for whatever proof they think they want.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands somewhere unguarded; she answers with a courtesy she doesn't feel, suddenly fascinated by her own sleeves.
reactions.questioned: Her accounting arrives verse-shaped, one movement per syllable, and her ear never leaves the glass.
reactions.threatened: She sifts the threat as she sifts the wire, listening for the flaw that will someday let it snap.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she does not retract — she repeats the wrong word more slowly, as though slowness could consecrate it.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction in the doorway makes a novice of her: she presents herself to be known, word-perfect, and despises how easily.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder passes through the nickel; she keeps counting, because if she stops, the floor will have to be real.
reactions.someone_else_accused: For once she explains, a whole liturgy of objection for someone she swears she never thinks about.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Not authorized, she says, in the room's own grammar — then breaks it to tell them where the wax runs thinnest.

npc.description: Hana Shawy sits cross-legged on the warm nickel with a tuning-glass pressed to the floor, listening through it the way a physician listens through a chest-piece — except her eyes are closed and her lips move, counting. Sleeves rolled past the elbow, forearms coppered with old sunburn that has no sun to blame. She does not startle when she notices you; she simply stops counting, which is worse.

lore.name: The Sill's Second Threshold
lore.description: The sill is not one threshold but two: the quartz filament, and beneath the nickel plate a second, buried lip of the same metal, worn mirror-smooth on its underside — worn, that is, from beneath. Whatever passes this sill passes through it downward, or the sill passes through them. Someone has drilled weep-holes along the buried lip, tiny and recent, Rindwalker work, and each hole is plugged with wax from the green decks. They are keeping something out. Or in. The wax is refreshed; the schedule of its refreshing is not written anywhere you can find.

content.name: Forioloud's Recognising Sill
content.description: A silver wire is trembling when you enter — one filament of fused quartz drawn taut across the sill, oscillating though nothing touches it, and it stills as if embarrassed to be seen. Beyond it the room opens the way a throat opens: nickel, annealed to a luster like held breath, folding back on itself farther than any room's right. Heat comes from the wrong quarter — from below the feet, faintly, as if the floor were remembering a furnace. Along the lintel, stencilled in a hand older than the paint beneath it: PRESENT YOURSELF AND WAIT TO BE KNOWN.

npc.name: Chathbesfuca Tsugozaris
npc.voice: Ledger-cadenced and elliptical; they speak of the room's contents as weights, never objects, and of themselves as an entry.

greet.says: You register light. Barely. The stricken weight went outboard three shifts back — took the turner with it, or the turner with it. Take the tally-slate from tier nine if you're counting; I'm not, anymore.

reactions.grief: For once no column fits, and they say the dead one's name like a weight nobody ever recorded.
reactions.shock: Counts under their breath, tiers, weights, anything, because arithmetic is the only thing holding their eyes open.
reactions.bribed: Names the offered thing's weight aloud, precisely, and declines to misremember on the grounds that memory is inventory.
reactions.accused: Offers no denial, only asks which column the charge belongs in, debited or stricken outright.
reactions.flattered: Weighs the praise like everything else, finds it light, and says so before the favor can be asked.
reactions.questioned: Recites their movements in ledger cadence, each hour a weight, unbothered as a column that balances.
reactions.threatened: Some old terror of being struck from the record surfaces, and they volunteer themselves as collateral too quickly.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Goes quiet mid-notation, and the correction they write is smaller than the truth they were caught withholding.
reactions.authority_arrives: Rises, the first time in anyone's memory, and stands at something like attention until the official's weight is entered.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The arrested indexer stirs beneath their palm and, for one unguarded breath, they want it to turn again.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Snaps that the named one never carried enough weight to move anything, then hears their own certainty and distrusts it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Does not pretend otherwise; enters the plea itself in the ledger as a weight the room cannot hold.

npc.description: Chathbesfuca Tsugozaris lies coiled in the gap between two ascending tiers, woken by your footfall but unhurried about admitting it, one hand resting on the indexer's rim the way a farmer rests a hand on a beast's flank. Their eyes adjust to you slowly, as if you are the thing arriving from a great depth.

lore.name: The Counterweight Manifest
lore.description: Etched into the arrested indexer's toothed rim, a manifest in notation older than the oldest hull-wall: every case logged by weight, and one entry struck through so deeply the ceramic is gouged. The stricken line corresponds to nothing in the room — its mass exceeds every case present, summed. Something was buffered here heavier than the room could hold, and the ledger admits it by refusing to.

content.name: Warpworks, Register 412
content.description: Nothing in Register 412 turns that ought to be turning: the warp of threaded cases hangs mid-cycle, its great indexer arrested between weights, and the hush where motion should live is louder than any clatter. Cases of sintered ceramic ascend in spirals toward a ceiling no eye finds, their glassy ash surfaces drinking the green-black dark whole. Where something vast has gone, the absence has edges — a case-shaped cavern, dust still arranging itself into the memory of what filled it. Stencilled along a spandrel, in glyphs worn to whispers: HEAVIEST INBOARD ALWAYS. One sleeper lies folded among the lowest tiers, breathing where no ledger admits a person.

npc.name: Netike-Meberide
npc.voice: Brief, proprietary, worn in like a favorite route. They count things when they talk.

cord.says: House cord. Six knots, six of us, burnt end where I got careless with a pan. We kept it off the old wall when they stripped it. A house can be rebuilt. Its counting shouldn't start over.

greet.says: Six of us on this door. One asleep, wrong shift, so make it five and a half. You knocking or drifting through?

relay.says: Word, mostly. Small word, fast word. The Braid pays in favors and Tefi collects them like buttons. She'll trade with you when she's up, if what you carry is worth a listen.

rebuild.says: Three weeks. Stove first, walls second, beds last. You can tell what a house loves by what it fixes first. White paint was Osen's idea. It'll yellow. Everything yellows.

choices.text: What's the cord by the stove?

sleeper.says: Tefi. Runs relays on the night leg, comes back smelling of corridor and sleeps through the morning meal. We stopped waking her. Knock loud at the door, not at her.

reactions.grief: They make it a count — years, favors, knots on the cord — and the count fails partway through.
reactions.shock: Their eyes run the room by habit, bunk to bunk to stove, and keep stopping on the body.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced aloud against six knots and a burnt end, and it comes up short.
reactions.accused: Told to their face, they lose their place in a number and make the accuser say it twice.
reactions.flattered: They take the praise without warming and answer with a list of what the rebuild got wrong.
reactions.questioned: The answers come in counts — hours, doors, knocks — a full ledger offered before anyone asks twice.
reactions.threatened: Inside, it is already arithmetic: what the threat costs them, what it costs the other five names on the door.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The false number stays out on the table, face stays still, because a count once spoken stands in this house.
reactions.authority_arrives: They stay at the stove with the boiled kettle and let the official wait out the silence.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The bunks go out of true and they start the count aloud — six knots, six names — before anyone else speaks.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They recite the accused's shifts and comings in exact numbers and stop one count short of vouching.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say no twice, then add the plea to what the house keeps, where at least it gets counted.

npc.description: Netike-Meberide sits at the stove doing nothing with great attention, a kettle that is already boiled in front of them. They are cataloging the room with their eyes — where each bunk went, what the rebuild got wrong.

lore.name: Beaded cord on the stove hook
lore.description: A beaded cord hangs by the stove, six knots worked into it. Whoever strung it counted routes — the old house, before the rebuild. The cord is scorched at one end. Someone pulled dinner off the flame too fast, more than once.

content.name: Row-House 7
content.description: The stove stands closer to the door than the sleeping mat does — someone rebuilt the room around the fire, not the beds. Bright white walls, still tacky with fresh seal. Bamboo bunks in two neat rows. On the door frame, stenciled: SIX NAMES, ONE DOOR, KNOCK LOUD. One bunk is occupied at the wrong hour.

npc.name: Rolara-Eimenne
npc.voice: Brisk, clipped, timing her sentences to the capsule interval; she says a thing once and lets the room hold it.

cargo.says: Sealed pallets, sealed letters, once — I'll say this once — a cradle padded like a bed, warmed, and empty when it landed. The Drift says everything moves and nothing is yours. I've started thinking the ship agrees too literally.

choices.text: Ask where the empty cradle went.

empty.says: Down. Sevin's people logged its arrival and sealed the chamber behind it, and that is the whole of what I know, which is more than most. I fire the capsules. I don't follow them. That's not piety — it's employment.

choices.text: Ask if she has met Mercury.

greet.says: Hour and a half. You can talk until the hum climbs, then clear the tube. Nobody rebuilt this hall to have an audience — so either you're lost, or you're the reason we rebuilt it.

choices.text: Ask why the hall is so new.
Ask if she has met Mercury.

height.says: Nobody's fixed it because fixing means re-surveying the floor, and the floor answers to no survey I've seen. The ship grows at both ends and apparently it doesn't consider the middle worth mentioning. I stand on a crate and call it seniority.

mercury.says: Met? You don't meet a schedule. But three times now the hum has climbed early, and once the whole hall smelled of rain though rain isn't a thing here. I think this domain knows I keep its hours, the way a dog knows the hand that feeds. It hasn't bitten.

rebuilt.says: Four capsules came through with tape on their seams — tape, on a hull fitting. So we pulled the whole line apart and put it back within a hair. Correct isn't the same as true yet. It takes years of firing before a tube believes in itself.

reactions.grief: She runs the calibration a second time it does not need, then sits on the loading floor without deciding to.
reactions.shock: Behind her steady face she is firing capsule after capsule into what she saw, and none of them land.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced against a wage paid in launch intervals, and the pricing takes one breath too long.
reactions.accused: Her denial comes once, then again before she can stop it, and the second telling costs more than the accusation.
reactions.flattered: Flattery she files with the stencil warnings — true, printed, and addressed to whoever needs it.
reactions.questioned: Launch times, not dates: she accounts for her movements the way she logs freight, offering nothing from the hours between.
reactions.threatened: Her grip shifts to the wrench's working end, and she counts minutes to the next launch instead of answering.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: One full interval of silence, then the same lie again in the same flat meter, word for word.
reactions.authority_arrives: She stands straighter and waits to learn whether this is inspection or employment, because the difference decides her answers.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder finds her hands on the manual seal before her head decides anything, which is what intervals are for.
reactions.someone_else_accused: An opinion about the name exists and stays put, filed with the empty-cradle story behind her teeth.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No is the whole answer, in her stencil voice, and then she stands too long inside the cleared tube's shadow.

npc.description: Rolara-Eimenne stands waist-deep in the tube's access cradle with a torque-wrench across both shoulders, motionless for exactly the length of time a person waits for a sound the room has not made yet. When she sees you she does not startle; she checks the tube mouth first, then you, in that order of threat.

lore.name: The Hour-Chart on the Loading Cradle
lore.description: The cradle's edge carries a strip of copper foil, pinned under a lug, scored with marks that repeat every hour and a half — the capsule cycle — but the marks start over eleven times, each restart offset a little earlier, as if something underground were dragging the schedule forward. The last mark is dated in a hand no one here would use, and it is tomorrow.

content.name: The Conduit Hall of Quiet Ledger
content.description: The launch tube's mouth stands a hand's width above the loading floor, as if the hall were built for a floor that has since grown taller. New black glass runs the tube's whole length without a single scuff to prove it has ever fired, and green-black mineral wool swallows the hum until it arrives more as pressure than sound. Along the near wall, stenciled twice at different heights and both correct: CAPSULE LAUNCH ON THE HOUR, CLEAR THE TUBE. Nothing here has had time to be anyone's.

npc.name: Sacharafu Tsusaki
