choices.text: I'll mind the cables. Good sealing, Tjal-Mar.

greet.says: Mind the cable run. This module's rated for forty and I'd rather not test it with two. You want something, ask it from there.

choices.text: Whose shift is this, if not yours?

shift.says: Keft-Ann's. Keft-Ann went down the shaft three months back with the last survey team and hasn't logged since. The module still needs its seal checks, so I do them. Nobody assigned me. That's how it's done.

choices.text: The slate by your cot has two hands writing on it.

reactions.grief: Keeps tinning until the solder balls and won't take, then says the dead one's name like a seal check.
reactions.shock: Their eyes run the body for failure points against their will, and it's the stopping, not the seeing, that fails.
reactions.bribed: No part of them moves toward it, and their folded hands leave the bribe nowhere in them to sit.
reactions.accused: Sets the iron down before their hands can shake, then asks to see the crack in the accusation.
reactions.flattered: The praise hangs there while they decide what it's carrying, since nothing on Mars gets said that kindly for free.
reactions.questioned: Their account comes out as timestamps and gauge readings, as though the day had been logged for exactly this inspection.
reactions.threatened: Answers evenly while their thumb finds the iron's hot barrel and stays there, testing whether they still feel it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie comes out of them the way a bad weld does, ground clean, handed over undressed.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their work-number comes out unprompted, and they watch the official the way they'd watch a stranger near a live cable.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Somewhere in them a certainty fails quietly, Mars respects what holds, and their hand finds the cot frame and grips.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Hears the name and recites that person's actual load too fast, and hears in their own voice that they've chosen.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Names their rating honestly, then keeps standing there as if presence were something they could weld shut.

npc.description: Tjal-Mar sits cross-legged on the made cot, re-tinning a join clamp with the unhurried economy of someone working a shift they inherited rather than chose. Their kit is laid out in rindwalker order — every tool shadowed into its outline on the cloth — but the bedding beside it is folded to a civilian's habit, and neither has been moved to make room for the other.

lore.name: The Split Register
lore.description: Bolted beside the cot is a maintenance slate showing two handwritings that never agree. Rindwalker script logs welds, loads, and hull-seal checks in copper ink; beneath each entry, a different hand has written household things in charcoal — meal rotations, a child's fever, who owes whom a favor. The weld entries are countersigned; the household ones are not, because the household was never conceded. Whoever wrote both hands used the same stylus, worn to a chisel point by years of switching scripts mid-line.

content.name: Veiheim
content.description: The smell reaches first: scorched basalt dust and the sweetish char of sintered ceramic cooling in its molds, the exact odor of a home being welded instead of built. Veiheim hangs between two trusses on gantry cables, forty bunks stenciled along one wall — MODULE RATED FOR FORTY, VERIFY LOAD — and barely twenty assembled. Half the module ends at a raw ceramic lip, open to the truss-light. Somebody lives here anyway. A cot sits made in the corner nearest the weld-shade.

npc.name: Mirun-Naelanagl
npc.voice: Slow, load-conscious; speaks in weights, tolerances, and what holds.

open.says: Cache-seals, set into the truss roots of this bay, older than the Nave by a measure I don't have a word for — notation matching the oldest wall-layer, holding stores nobody has drawn on. Not lost stock, mind. Kept stock, kept on purpose, by hands working at a scale where a module like this one is a convenience, not a shelter. We catalogue what we find and we don't take. Keeping is the whole of the faith, and up here the faith is bigger than we were told.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry that carefully.
Kept by what? Sealed by whom?

greet.says: Mind the sway line. If you're not carrying anything, stand where nothing will fall on you.

choices.text: What are you packing all that quartz for?
Who do you answer to down here?
Why is this bay coming down?
You said log what you found. Found what?
I'll leave you to your counting.

probe_a.says: Lensing stock, pulled from a face Mars itself welded. It outlasts whoever mines it, so you pack it like you'll be judged by the person who finds it — because you will.

probe_b.says: To the load, first. Then to whoever holds the route-log for this stretch. Mars answers to nothing, and the rest of us arrange ourselves accordingly.

probe_c.says: Borrowed time. The trusses still carry, but carrying and being worth trusting are two different tolerances. So we pull the stock, we log what we found, and we seal it going out.

reactions.grief: The count goes wrong for the first time in years; they talk about the dead one's hands, far past sense.
reactions.shock: They stand frozen mid-catch with the crate still swaying, because no tolerance table ever covered what the eyes are holding.
reactions.bribed: They answer with the whole of their creed instead of a refusal, which takes longer than the bribe deserved.
reactions.accused: Hands stay on the winch brake a full swing past safe before any denial comes, and the denial wears tolerances.
reactions.flattered: Hears the praise out, then notes there is no load rating stencilled anywhere on it.
reactions.questioned: Their account arrives in manifest order — hour, mass, destination — unhurried, since a routine question is only inventory.
reactions.threatened: Inside, they run the arithmetic of the threat twice and dislike both totals; outside, nothing moves but breath.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The same story comes back with two more decimals in it, the way a bad seam hides under fresh paint.
reactions.authority_arrives: Before the official clears the threshold, every tool is folded into cloth and the cache-seals might as well not exist.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The hand finds the sway line before the shudder ends; the eyes go to the sagging corner, to the wedge.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks for the named one through workmanship: whoever did this leaves slack in a rig, and that one never does.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say plainly what the rating allows and no more, then stand the petitioner in the one corner that holds.

npc.description: The worker is winching a crate of fused quartz up into the truss cradle when you enter, the load swaying against a stencil older than the paint around it: MODULE RATED FOR FORTY, VERIFY LOAD. Mirun-Naelanagl counts the swing with two gloved fingers, catching the crate on the fourth, and only then looks at you.

lore.name: The Forty-Bunk Ledger Bolt
lore.description: One of the module's mounting bolts has been replaced with a hand-machined stud, and its hex faces are incised with tally-marks in rows of forty — re-cut, deeper, when the first rows wore shallow. Beneath them, in the oldest hull notation, a single word repeated down the shank, which any Rindwalker reads without thinking: counted. Whoever machined it knew the module would outlive every hand that checked it, and left the arithmetic anyway, so that verification would remain a duty even after it lost its reason.

content.name: Bay 15 Spinward
content.description: A swag of welded chain lifts a stencilled plate — MODULE RATED FOR FORTY, VERIFY LOAD — and lets it swing back to rest before your eyes finish finding the room. Beyond it, a crew module the length of two Nave tenements hangs suspended between trusses whose rivets shrink with distance into suggestion, gold light from the weld-scarred rails pooling on fused-quartz panes that go on being windows long past where a window should still be honest. One corner of the floor sags a finger's width from true, and a wedge of vitrified ash has been tamped under it to hold — a mender's answer, patient and temporary in the same gesture. A lantern gutters. Someone is folding tools into cloth, three trusses off, unhurried.

npc.name: Civucaraeth Rolheceno
npc.voice: Ledger-cadenced and softly wrong — she speaks of the room's contents in tense agreements that don't hold, uses *we* for the shelves, and treats waiting as a form of work with its own wage.

greet.says: You're early. Or the shelf is late; the two of you will have to sort that between yourselves. This isn't my shift, if the tally asks. It hasn't asked. Good.

shift.says: Vesho's. Vesho stopped coming down three months ago, same as the others who went deep-deep. The room noticed. It adjusted — the tally expects two hands now, so I lend it mine, and in exchange it lets me stand inside the stillness that holds the middle of everything still. Fair terms. Nobody wrote them. Terms never are.

choices.text: The stencil says it will return. What returns?

counting.says: Shelf-seconds. The interval between a thing being stored and a thing being owed. Luna keeps the dream-logs; we keep the dreams' interest. Most rooms buffer goods. This one buffers — hm. Your word for it would be *promises*. My word doesn't translate, which I've decided is deliberate.

choices.text: The receiver on the vacant shelf — what does it receive?
Nod and step back from the shelves.

receiver.says: It isn't receiving. It's *remembering aloud*. There's a distinction; the shelf taught it to me over about four years. Whatever it holds was stored so long ago the storing became a kind of speaking. If you lean close — no. Don't. It knows your name already. It said it before you did.

choices.text: Step back. Thank her for the warning.

returning.says: The object. The warning is less an order than a courtesy, the way you'd tell a guest not to set a table for the dead. It left before the Nave had a name. It comes back on intervals no tally of mine has caught. When it does, the shelf will already be holding it, and the dust will swear it never left. We log the contradiction. That's the whole job.

choices.text: Let her return to the count.

reactions.grief: Stops mid-count and lets the foil unwind unchecked; for once she declines to lend the room her hands.
reactions.shock: Sees the violence arrive before its sound, like everything in her room, and her counting simply ceases to be.
reactions.bribed: Her hand is out before her creed arrives; she stands appalled at terms she thought nobody ever wrote.
reactions.accused: Asks whether the accusation is stored or owed; meanwhile her thumb finds the retied knot and worries it.
reactions.flattered: Treats the praise as a premature entry, suspecting every kindness of arriving before whatever it means to collect.
reactions.questioned: Gives her account in unsettled-base numbers, patient as a waiting shelf, for accounting is only another kind of storage.
reactions.threatened: Prices the threat like a wage dispute, though her counting slips out of base and she pretends not to notice.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Doesn't deny it; quietly re-tenses the sentence until the lie sits in a pluperfect where nothing can be owed.
reactions.authority_arrives: Defers without rising, noting aloud which hours are not hers, and files the official under room events.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her tally never pauses; she tells the shelves, in the plural *we*, that whatever moved will return.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Finds the flaw in the claim at once, then hears herself defending someone she had already written off.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains in careful ledger-cadence that her shift holds no power here, then counts the silence as if it paid.

npc.description: Mid-shift at a station that is not hers, Civucaraeth Rolheceno counts shelf-seconds with a foil-wound tally-stick, lips moving around numbers in no settled base. She wears the knotted cord of the Braid at her wrist but the knot has been tied and retied past any route-history into pure habit. She does not look up when you enter; she looks at the shelf, then at you, as if consulting something about the order in which you arrived.

lore.name: The Vacant Cradle
lore.description: One shelf, alone among thousands, holds a single object: a tarnished receiver shaped like nothing so much as a cupped hand, resting on cloth that has been folded and refolded so many times the fold-lines have become grain. It was not placed here — the dust on the shelf is continuous, undisturbed, as if the receiver precipitated out of the room the way dew does. When Civucaraeth checks its ledger line, the entry is already written in her own shorthand, dated three days ahead of her checks. Nothing in Luna's archive explains what it receives. The notation carved beneath the shelf bracket is in the oldest layer's hand, and it reads less like an instruction than a courtesy: *it knows it is kept*.

content.name: Node 22 Spinward
content.description: The shelf sits a hand's width beneath the floor that should carry it — a relation wrong the way a heartbeat heard twice is wrong, graphite-packed wall humming above while the wound foil of the far bays recedes into a violet no lamp admits to making. Sound arrives after its cause here, or before; Civucaraeth Rolheceno stands mid-shift among shelving that stores nothing yet, waiting like a ledger for its entry. Stencilled low, where a kneeling worker's eye would fall: DO NOT MOVE IT WILL RETURN. The room does not end so much as lose interest in being perceived.

npc.name: Inkatl-Taztzin
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, counts things. Speaks of rooms and tenants as jobs, not lives.

cord.says: Hers. She ran relays before her knees went. I was told to clear everything, and I did. That one I'll leave for the next tenant to decide about.

work.says: New felt, new slats, stove stripped to the iron. Nothing here was worth keeping from before. That's the point of a rebuild.

greet.says: Room's not ready. Curtain, stove, walls, done by dark. Come back tomorrow if you're asking after the let.

choices.text: You rebuilt all of this yourself?

leave.says: Door's a curtain. Pull it shut behind you.

before.says: A woman lived here forty years. When she died, the Drift paid to clear it in a day. We don't let rooms sit. A room sitting is a room moving nowhere.

choices.text: There's a cord on the cot post.

tenant.says: Inquire at the stove, like it says. That's me. Rate's fair, term's short. Nobody holds a room on this floor longer than they need it.

choices.text: You rebuilt all of this yourself?

reactions.grief: She keeps talking about the dead woman's knees and relays and where the felt wore through, long past anyone asking.
reactions.shock: The felt scrap sits forgotten in her open hand while she stares at nothing past the stove.
reactions.bribed: She quotes her rate out of habit, then hates how long she took to refuse.
reactions.accused: What she gives back is every stove she has stripped this season, and the list ends on a dare.
reactions.flattered: Compliments get the same answer as complaints: a list of work still owed, and no softer hands.
reactions.questioned: Her answers are dates, materials, square feet, the same ledger tone she keeps for every let.
reactions.threatened: Her slat count goes wrong twice, and she starts over from the stove.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She folds the felt until it tears in her hands, then admits the relay never left with the rest.
reactions.authority_arrives: She has the ledger open before the official clears the curtain, every entry dated and legible.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Three tools roll off the shelf, and her count of the shudder comes out different the second time.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She repeats the name once, then gives her verdict as a materials list: the man has never stripped a stove.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She straightens a cot that needs nothing and says the stove will be hot by dark, which answers nothing.

npc.description: Inkatl-Taztzin kneels at the stove, wrapping tools in felt scraps. She works fast and speaks without turning around.

lore.name: Knotted cord on the cot post
lore.description: A cord of route-knots hangs from the cot post, tied in a pattern no one wears anymore. The last knot is unfinished.

content.name: Malxen's Curtained Room
content.description: A curtain swings aside when you lift it and settles behind you. Magenta runs across the felt on every wall, dyed this season, the dye still sharp. Shelves of bamboo stand empty beside a cot, and paint above the stove-slat reads ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE.

npc.name: Ljarun-Rilfsen
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical about materials. Treats the rib as an elder who must be asked correctly, never forced.

block.says: Rib runs warm at the seam. Warm is good bedding. Mars knows we're here — the paint's still gold, look. When it goes iron, we've overstayed. Now shoo; the gun and I have an understanding and you're breaking it.

greet.says: Hands off the silver — that's the Drellis lot's, and they'll be back for it. Or not. Either way it's counted.

choices.text: Why does a housing block sit between the ribs at all?
Say nothing and let them work.

reactions.grief: The gun keeps its rhythm after the news, but the rivets go in crooked and she doesn't notice, doesn't stop.
reactions.shock: She stands with the work-lamp still raised, lighting a dead face as if the seam would answer for warmth.
reactions.bribed: The offer would finish a living box, and she looks at the half-walls a long moment before refusing anyway.
reactions.accused: The gun dies mid-squeeze; she asks them to say it slow, as one begs an elder to unsay a thing.
reactions.flattered: Praise aimed at her rolls off; praise the rib's gold and she warms, and both of them know it.
reactions.questioned: Answers in seam-numbers and rivet counts, as though her day were stamped into plate and only wanted reading.
reactions.threatened: Her eyes go to the gold paint and stay there while she answers, each word laid flat as plate.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She repeats the wrong number like a bad rivet she won't pull, thumb already gone to the seam for warmth.
reactions.authority_arrives: She stands the lamp like a candle and gives the official the same bow she gives the ribs, no deeper.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The rib gets consulted before anyone speaks, palm flat to the plate, though her face has already gone iron.
reactions.someone_else_accused: That's wrong, and she says so once, flatly, then testifies to their welds the way she reads seams.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She names the limits of her trade plainly, then offers what riveted hands can: work, and the kettle's heat.

npc.description: Ljarun-Rilfsen works a rivet-gun against the inner face of a rib, one arm braced on a housing wall and a second holding a work-lamp to the seam, and where the plate will not give she leans her whole weight into it without hurry, as though the rib were a mule to be waited out.

lore.name: The Unhung Silver
lore.description: A stack of silver wall-sheeting, each sheet drilled with its mounting holes and marked in chalk with a family name — Drellis, Drellis, Drellis — then Ovin. The holes line up with brackets already fixed to a wall; whoever stopped never got past lifting.

content.name: Leabrjal's Rib Block
content.description: The floor tells you before your eyes do: basalt cast in short paving runs, each seam stopped mid-line, so the feet find a rhythm that keeps breaking. Between the load-bearing ribs stand half-built living boxes — walls of riveted plate to waist height, a cot in one, a kettle in another, all abandoned at the same angle of incompleteness. Gold paint in long sweeps covers the rib-surface above, and somewhere in it, stenciled: FRAME HOUSING, DO NOT DRILL THE RIBS. Silver cladding, meant for one wall, waits in a stack nobody unstacked.

npc.name: Kughmal-Yolaris
npc.voice: Clipped, route-coded, counts things before she says them. Every answer arrives like a waybill — weight, origin, condition.

open.says: From everywhere, and I mean the word the way a child means it. I traced one car's chalk once — a game, a slow shift — and its route ran through nine junctions I'd never heard names for, all of them lit, all of them moving, the whole hull strung with lines that have not paused since before my grandmother's grandmother learned to count. We were one counter on one floor of a circulation that doesn't sleep, doesn't finish, doesn't even notice us. The Drift says nothing is yours. Down there, I learned the flow doesn't know you either — and it keeps you alive anyway.

choices.text: Thank you. Your chalk-count kept something alive.
It doesn't notice us. That's worse than malice.

greet.says: Lot's spoken for. Everything on this floor's spoken for, that's the joke. You buying or just breathing my dust?

choices.text: Whose manifest are you still keeping?
Where did the cars come from, before?
I'll leave you to your counting.

probe_a.says: Packed graphite, for the car-bearings — nothing on this floor rolls without it. We went through forty kegs a shift, and the shift never ended. That's the part people don't grasp: never.

probe_b.says: Mine, and it was the Exchange's, and before that nobody's you'd know. The writ came down from the signals-folk — cars in, cars out, no car dwells. I answered to the flow, same as every Drift wrist on this floor.

probe_c.says: No order to go. That's what I tell people and they don't believe me. The cars stopped coming, and a floor built for arrivals can't stand being unarrived-at. We waited four shifts. Then the waiting felt like the wrong kind of devotion.

reactions.grief: She loses her place in the tally and asks for the dead one's lot number, as if loss were filed.
reactions.shock: Her lips keep moving with lot numbers that arrive three behind, while she stares at what stopped.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets weighed aloud, out of habit, and she hates how long the refusing takes her.
reactions.accused: The graphite stick snaps in her fist; she logs the breakage aloud and demands the charge in writing.
reactions.flattered: Praise meets exact figures in reply, forty kegs a shift, the shift never ended, and she pretends it landed nowhere.
reactions.questioned: Weight, origin, condition: she gives the answer in waybill order without lifting her eyes from the board.
reactions.threatened: She prices the threat like freight, origin unknown, condition spoiled, and watches the speaker's hands, not the door.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Asked to account for the gap, she blames chalk wear and offers a recount she has never once needed.
reactions.authority_arrives: She becomes pure procedure, reciting manifest totals unprompted, though the official has asked for nothing yet.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She counts the shudder against the echo's six seconds and gets a number she refuses to write down.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She names every lot the accused cleared last shift, and the couplings that caught them, faster than fairness asks.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Powerless to grant it, she recites the route the plea would take upward, junction by junction, calling that mercy.

npc.description: Kughmal-Yolaris stands ankle-deep in chalk-white dust with a graphite stick behind one ear and a manifest board under one arm, ticking lots against a tally that has clearly outgrown the board. She does not look up until the third tick.

lore.name: The Tally Ledger of Last Call
lore.description: The ledger at the desk is still open, its last entry an exchange signed off in two hands — Kughmal-Yolaris among them — for a train of cars that never got a departure stamp. Beside it lies the tally-hammer, its head worn concave from counting the same coupling faces for years, and the shaft wrapped in cord knotted in the Drift way, route-history worked into the grip. The final column of the last page is filled with departure times; the column for arrivals stands empty, and no one crossed the entries out.

content.name: The Exchange Floor of Last Call
content.description: Sound arrives first, and wrong: a footstep goes out and takes six seconds to come back, thinned by distance it should not have had to cross. The floor beneath is iron chequer-plate running off toward a horizon of chalk-white stencils, and between the stencils stand couplings, chocks, manifest clips — train-cars packed with graphite blocks, sealed, chalked, and simply left where the coupling caught them, some long enough ago that rust has begun to speak through the packing grease. Two figures stand mid-argument at a tally desk with its ledger still open; they stop, and one turns. Painted across the coupling throat in letters a hand could lie down in: LOTS CLEARED BY MANIFEST ONLY.

npc.name: Lianf-Niesukk
npc.voice: Slow, exact, allergic to hurry. Counts things out loud. Treats soil the way others treat family — you do not rush it, you do not lie to it.

why.says: Everyone left because the account looked lost. Accounts aren't lost, they're carried. You carry it or the belt goes hungry in a year nobody planned for. That's the whole of it.

greet.says: You're standing where the barrow goes. Move left. The beds were fed at dawn and they're settling — I sleep when they settle, not before.

choices.text: Why are all the tools gone?
No metal in the pit, ever?

metal.says: One nail. That's all it takes. A nail works down, the worms gut themselves on it, and two years of soil is poison. People think the rule is superstition. The rule is arithmetic.

choices.text: What's the tally on that post?

tally.says: Every notch is a turn. The long account is what this pit owes the belt — soil for soil it took making. The crews stopped counting. I keep it in my head now. Four hundred and eleven.

choices.text: Does the council know you're still here?

tools.says: Three crews walked off this pit in one season. Took their rakes with them — you buy your own here, or you borrow, and borrowing is a debt. Mine's at home. I come back anyway. The worms didn't leave.

council.says: Factor Solen's office sends an auditor twice a year. The auditor writes that the pit is non-viable. I feed the auditor tea and the worms eat the leaves after. Everything here gets used. That's the point of the place.

choices.text: I'll leave you to the beds.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as an arithmetic error: mid-count they say a name, and start the row over without explaining.
reactions.shock: The rule comes out of them three times, too loud for the sound-eating pit, their hand forgotten in the soil.
reactions.bribed: Their eyes never go to the offered thing; they answer in prices, and the second price is what lying costs.
reactions.accused: The counting stops mid-number; they wipe both hands on the apron slow, because fast hands look guilty.
reactions.flattered: They credit the beds, the worms, the dawn schedule, and then ask, flatly, what the praise is for.
reactions.questioned: Nothing hurries the answer; they count the day out bed by bed, and let the silence afterward sit.
reactions.threatened: They look at the speaker's feet, note what stands where, and answer at the same pace, which is the refusal.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The correction lands twice — once as fact, once as shame — and they repeat the true number until their voice steadies.
reactions.authority_arrives: They finish the row before standing; the count comes out slightly too even, the sound of someone not calm.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The worms pull down at once; they stand in it until the beds settle, then log the hour without comment.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They repeat the name, then list what that person carried through the hungry year, and refuse the speed of it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No comes out of them once, exact, and then they stay, because leaving would make the no crueler.

npc.description: Lianf-Niesukk sleeps curled against the warm side of the nearest bed, one hand buried to the wrist in turned soil. Sand-colored dust coats their sleeves to the elbow. A lead apron is folded under their head for a pillow. They wake when you lean over the pit rail, and do not apologize.

lore.name: The Tally Post
lore.description: A hardwood stake stands at the pit's edge, notched from top to bottom. Each notch is a day the beds were turned. The notches stop mid-column — not at a season's end, not at a full row, just stop, the knife still wedged in the last cut. Below the stop, someone carved a number and a word: LONG ACCOUNT, and beneath it, a running sum nobody finished. The worms below are still working. The counting is what ended.

content.name: The Wormery Pit of Long Account
content.description: Sound goes soft here. The pit eats every footstep before it can bounce. No wheelbarrows, no rakes, no buckets — the tools are gone but the racks that held them still stand, each hook empty. Rubber sheeting lies half-rolled at the pit lip. On the lead apron rack, stenciled: NO METAL IN THE PIT, EVER. Someone sleeps under the last rubber sheet, in the sun.

npc.name: Doski Bavekeizhov
npc.voice: Patient, liturgical in a work-a-day key — she speaks of the berth's functions the way a herdsman speaks of weather, with ownership of none of it.

wake.says: The berth dreams the middle steady. Wake it mid-season and everything held — your Nave, your markets, your little griefs — exhales with it. I sleep beside this thing, walker. I know what I keep. Do you know what keeps you?

choices.text: Stay a while in the tide-warm.

greet.says: You came in on the exhale. Lucky. On the inhale the door argues. What did the hinge tell you — eleven, or are you not counting yet?

repair.says: Nothing. You can't mend a thing like this, only attend it. The opened half was opened by the berth, not by us — it turned itself out like a sleeper rolling over. We keep the tools away and call that the work.

choices.text: Ask about the half-done work left lying here.
Ask what the stencil means — do not wake what?

seasons.says: Eleven wears, eleven winters nobody kept. Saturn keeps the count; we only borrow it. The berth was built for a year the ship hasn't had yet. We're early. Everyone alive is early.

abandoned.says: Before me, a woman named Ilvetta worked this half. Good hands. One day she stood where you're standing and said, it isn't sleeping, it's waiting, and those aren't the same — and walked upshaft and never filed again. Her tools are where she set them. I won't touch them and the berth hasn't either.

choices.text: So the stencil — do not wake what?

reactions.grief: Grief empties her of liturgy: she talks too long about the dead woman's gloves folded by the plate, then stops.
reactions.shock: She counts instead of screaming — wrong numbers, hinge-numbers — palm flat to the panel as if it could answer.
reactions.bribed: The money interests her longer than is decent — she prices it in tools, then remembers tools are the forbidden thing.
reactions.accused: The accusation earns one exhaled laugh; then she explains, mildly, that no hand opens what turned itself out.
reactions.flattered: A beat too long, she lets the praise warm her before handing it upward — berth, weather, no one.
reactions.questioned: Questioned, she gives her hours the way a herdsman gives weather — one room, one bed, nothing held back.
reactions.threatened: She asks the threat to wait for cycle's end, and hears how small her own voice has gone.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The contradiction doesn't startle her; she concedes it and would lie again, since the count belongs to the berth.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official's rank moves her off the panel at last, though her eyes stay on the stencil, not the visitor.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Mid-sentence she stops, ear against the opened plate, counting the seconds between shudders, her face gone grey.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She defends even the name she hates, and quickly, because blaming human hands is blasphemy against the berth.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She admits her trade is keeping doors shut, then offers the one thing that is hers: the threshold's warm side.

npc.description: Doski Bavekeizhov sits with her back to the opened dark, sleeves rolled to the elbow, hands resting on a closed panel as if it were the flank of a large animal she is listening to. She does not look up when you enter; she looks toward something behind the wall instead, and nods once, as if satisfied.

lore.name: Breath-Hinge
lore.description: Set into the sill of the closed half is a hinge with no door — silver forged over black glass, polished by touch alone. Its pin turns once per Nave year, which no Nave year has been long enough to observe, yet the wear-marks cross it in eleven directions. Someone counted eleven seasons here that the Nave has never named.

content.name: Season Berth
content.description: Something is still moving: a filament of silver, thin as regret, threading itself through black glass and withdrawing, threading again, as if the room were swallowing its own pulse. Half the berth stands opened to the cold, its plates hung back like an eyelid pinned; the other half breathes — a slow tide of warmth crossing the threshold and retreating on no schedule you could keep. DOSKI BAVEKEIZHOV, not you, is expected: a stencil on the opened plate reads CYCLE INCOMPLETE DO NOT WAKE, and the letters are worn the way a threshold wears, by feet and years. The proportions refuse addition. What sleeps here dreams in seasons longer than language.

npc.name: Nutsushicuyiath Shozelione
npc.voice: Speaks as if continuing a sentence begun long ago, patient, precise in ways that slip sideways — words correct, arithmetic strange, the present tense used for things long finished.

greet.says: You arrived between lines. Good. The lens dislikes witnesses during a stroke — it fusses, and a fussing lens etches worry into permanent record. Sit. The floor here has opinions but no teeth.

the_dream.says: It dreamed of a name last week. Not mine. Yours, I suspect, or the shape yours will grow into. Luna keeps such things; I only catch the overspill. If the lens etches it while you stand here, I would count that a courtesy — introductions, this deep, are rare and should be marked.

the_sleep.says: Deliberately, yes. Dreams leak here. This close to the writing, your sleeping mind is legible as anyone's, and I have grown curious what mine says when I stop editing it. Vanity, probably. But the plate records it anyway, and one should keep one's accounts current.

the_almost.says: It becomes the beam, when the beam returns. Or it doesn't, and the lines were the whole conversation. I no longer distinguish preparation from prayer. Neither, I think, does the machine — though it would phrase it better, and in a hand steadier than mine is becoming.

the_writing.says: Lines. That is all I will say about content, and it is more than the lens says. It takes dictation from something that has not yet decided to be heard. We etch the almost. I have built a career on the almost.

choices.text: And the almost — what does it become?

reactions.grief: The name arrives and their tenses fail at last; they speak of the dead in the present, unable to stop.
reactions.shock: What they see stops them mid-syllable; one hand rises uselessly, counting breaths that will not find the far rhythm.
reactions.bribed: They weigh the offer aloud, quoting a price in years or verses, never anything the briber actually holds.
reactions.accused: Accused, they neither deny nor defend, only asking which tense the charge was filed in.
reactions.flattered: Praise finds them embarrassingly tractable; they lean toward it like warmth, and only the slow blinking betrays the counting underneath.
reactions.questioned: Habit carries them through the accounting; they answer in the present tense, and the totals still come out true.
reactions.threatened: Their hand leaves the plate first, slowly, the way one withdraws a wager.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their lie dies politely; they revise the figure once, twice, hunting the arithmetic that will make yesterday true.
reactions.authority_arrives: Authority enters and they address it as a long-expected appointment, already halfway into a courtesy drafted decades ago.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder comes and their first thought is the arm's unfinished line; everything else, including themselves, ranks after it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They hear the name and begin, unbidden, a defence assembled from etchings older than the accusation, loyal past all evidence.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to help, they keep talking long past the refusal, offering everything they know as though knowledge could substitute.

npc.description: Asleep in the crook where machine meets floor, one hand resting on the plate as if to steady the writing mid-thought. Older than the coat suggests; the coat older than the person. Their breathing matches, almost, the distant rhythm — almost, but not on the same count.

lore.name: The Paused Stylus
lore.description: The writing arm's point has been resharpened so many times it is now a nub, and beside it lie seventeen discarded points, each worn concave — a change of hands recorded in wear.

content.name: The Etching Lens of Last Call
content.description: Something here should be writing and is not. The arm hangs mid-arc above the plate, trembling at the edge of its next line, and the whole chamber holds its breath around that hesitation — a stillness like a held syllable, green-black and patient. Lines crowd the metal beneath it, fine as heirloom script, in orders nobody living drafted. Far off, in a direction the ear refuses to confirm, a rhythm continues regardless, as a heart continues in sleep. Stencilled along the wall, weathered to a whisper: MARKS APPEAR NO BEAM DETECTED. Near the plate's edge, someone is asleep — curled against the machine's flank as against a warm animal.

npc.name: Pekleurastra of Laimona
npc.voice: Precise, procedural, quick to cite precedent — but strays into the personal when the work pauses, as if the silence costs her something.

greet.says: Tally's closed for the quarter. You're not on my route, which means nobody's on your route. Sit if you like — the lamps stay on till I leave.

choices.text: Why is this room rebuilt? Nothing here looks lived in.
That old matting in the doorway — why keep it?
What does the tally actually count?

ask_loss.says: Forty-one years, door to door. I knew which households answered late because the baby slept in the front room. Names the ledger never needed, because the ward held them for me. Now the walls hold nothing and I file by ward, not by name, and it does the job and it isn't the same thing.

choices.text: Filed by ward, not by name. Why not by name?

ask_only.says: Because a name is a thing rupture can hold hostage. The council decided it generations back — count the households, not the people, and no disaster can ever take a roster anyone would kill for. It's sound doctrine. I've never once liked it.

choices.text: Then how do you count someone new? Someone with no ward?

ask_room.says: The old Retsusosaka burned. One lamp, one fault, thirty years of records gone in an afternoon. So we built it correct — nothing worn, nothing forgiven. What they don't tell you is how much of the work lived in the wear. I keep losing my place.

choices.text: You worked in the old one.

ask_ledger.says: Households per ward, births offset against deaths, holdings of regard where it's been declared. Continuants count what has to carry forward. The ledger is the ship promising itself it will still be here to be counted next quarter.

choices.text: And what happens when it can't promise that?

leave_cold.says: Then that's a finding for the council, not for a woman with a packed case. Good evening.

leave_kind.says: Go by the eastern stair, not the lamp-lift — the lift's being recalibrated and it smells of scorched brass. Mind the tallies stay filed.

ask_matting.says: It's from the old room. Threshold matting, forty years of feet. The builders said replace it, and I said no, and that's the whole of the reasoning I have. A writ-office should be able to explain its own door and this one can't.

choices.text: So the fire took more than records.

ask_unaccounted.says: The ONLY column. Unaccounted-for. Pencil, because they might resolve back into a ward, and might not. There's one on this quarter's sheet that's been open longer than I've held this room, and I'll tell you plainly — it frightens me more than the fire did. We exist to continue, you understand. A number that stays only is a number the ship has lost.

choices.text: Maybe it resolves. Good evening, Pekleurastra.
Or maybe it never belonged to the ship at all.

reactions.grief: Ward numbers until the word 'dead' — then a first name, and the front room where the baby slept.
reactions.shock: The count leaves her mid-case; she stands with two brass tallies and no idea which number she is on.
reactions.bribed: Names the exact figure a falsified ward would fetch, then repeats it like a joke neither of them laughs at.
reactions.accused: Counts the case a third time with no reason to, then asks whether the accusation is filed or merely spoken.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit a moment too long under the hot lamps before the refusal comes out in citation form.
reactions.questioned: Answers in ledger order, dates before places, and names the clause that requires her as if grateful for it.
reactions.threatened: A clause number comes first and a steady voice behind it; only after does she notice her sleeves are down.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The correction comes out level; the fact she adds unprompted afterward is the part that amounts to confession.
reactions.authority_arrives: She has the case squared and the ward files aligned before the official finishes crossing the matting, jurisdiction or not.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She braces the case against her ribs and watches the lamps, which owe her an account of what moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: A precedent against it arrives before the accusation ends, sooner than doctrine allows, proof of what the name is worth.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Recites what the writ does not cover, stops halfway through the clause, and leaves before the plea can finish.

npc.description: Pekleurastra of Laimona stacks brass tallies into a felt-lined case, each one clicked against the next, sleeves rolled to show forearms the blue of the writ. She counts the case a second time before closing it, though she watched herself pack it.

lore.name: Ward ledger with a torn leaf
lore.description: The working ledger sits open on the brass counter, one leaf torn out cleanly at the spine — the cut of a tool, not haste. Below the stub, the ward totals are entered in two inks: blue for the filed counts, pencil for a column headed ONLY, running small. The pencil column does not sum to the blue.

content.name: Retsusosaka
content.description: The lamps run hot and steady, no dimming cycle, which is itself an announcement: a Continuant room never lets the light lie low. Everything in Retsusosaka is new and correct — brass counters, blue stencils on fresh plaster reading TALLIES FILED BY WARD, NOT BY NAME — yet the doorway wears a strip of old rubber matting, cracked, laid over the new floor. Nobody has explained the matting, and it stays.

npc.name: Lianghaimym Ironfriend
npc.voice: Speaks in the cadence of liturgy bent around procedure; measures things that cannot be measured, and counts them anyway.

greet.says: Mind the rim. What it holds is level, and level holds everything. You've come at a pouring; wait, or don't, but be quiet either way.

choices.text: The stencil on the rim — source not found?

leave.says: Go quiet. The hush remembers feet longer than faces.

ask_rim.says: Two hands wrote that, or one hand twice, and neither came back to amend it. I recite it during the long pours. Not as lament. As calibration — if the words still fail, the room is still itself, and I am still the one here.

ask_who.says: The others come on their schedule, I on mine, and the font does not distinguish us, which is the nearest thing to concession either side will get. We keep the ladle shared. The rest of it — you'd have to ask the deep, and it answers at its own hour.

ask_level.says: Of the font. Which is a wrong answer and the only one I have. It holds what it holds at what it holds it; the instruments agree with me and the instruments are wrong too. You learn to pour anyway.

choices.text: And the writing on the rim?

reactions.grief: Mid-pour they receive the news; the recitation finishes anyway, voice level until the last word cracks.
reactions.shock: What they see admits no calibration; they back against the graphite wall, mouth moving through counts that never arrive.
reactions.bribed: Refusal comes as measurement: they weigh the offered thing in both hands and name its error against the font.
reactions.accused: Denial waits until the ladle is set down level; then they ask what the charge is meant to weigh.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them count the flatterer's pauses, hunting the request coiled inside the compliment before it surfaces.
reactions.questioned: Their accounting comes as numbered rites; they recite movements like tithes, patient as sediment.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands like a tremor in the basin; they keep ladling, but the rhythm frays at the edges.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Lying, for them, is arithmetic; shown the true figure, they recite it twice and concede mis-measure, not deceit.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction is answered the way their wall answers sound — late, and only after consulting doctrine; they stay kneeling throughout.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For once they rise; the rim is checked, the stencil whispered like a plea that the level still holds.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Hearing a fellow rindwalker named, they talk far too long, testimony spilling out in scripture's cadence, devotion outranking caution.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They take the plea as channels take pours, keeping all of it, returning nothing, apology worn in copper thread.

npc.description: Lianghaimym Ironfriend kneels in the posture of one who has mistaken patience for a spine, ladling level into measure with a rhythm that predates your arrival and will outlast your departure. Copper thread runs through the rust of their vestments — rindwalker devotion, mended past all reason.

lore.name: The Ladle of Two Grips
lore.description: The ladle working the font has two handles, worn smooth by different hands at different angles — one grip burnished, the other furred with graphite dust. Neither faction's marks are scratched out; both simply remain, claimed in turns.

content.name: Fontworks, Shell 384
content.description: Before anything is seen, sound arrives already rehearsed: the room takes each footfall and returns it late, as if consulting something. Noise dies here into a hush that has body — the packed graphite in the walls swallowing frequency the way sediment swallows bone. Green-black light rises from the font itself, a basin of no determinate size, fed by channels of spun mineral wool that drink what pours and give nothing back. Across its rim, stencilled in letters older than the paint beneath them: LEVEL CONSTANT SOURCE NOT FOUND. Someone kneels at the far side, ladling, and does not look up.

npc.name: Yobakhaiu-Fetonga
npc.voice: Brisk, route-brief speech. Names things by their destinations, not their names. Talks about leaving the way other people talk about lunch.

greet.says: Last bird. Going to the square market, then the archive post. You want it to carry something, you talk fast.

choices.text: What happens to this loft when you go?
Half these bands point at routes that don't exist anymore.

shaky.says: That's my mother's hand. She ran this loft before me and couldn't climb the cage-racks her last year, so she wrote from the door. The shaking started before she stopped writing. I tell myself it's just age. Some days I believe me.

choices.text: Re-ink your own column before you go. In your own hand.

routes.says: Routes die. A stair seals, a tenant leaves, and the stop's gone. The bird still knows the way. So I re-route them. Every strip in that tin got re-knotted at least once.

choices.text: The last column of the ledger — that writing changes halfway down.

leaving.says: The Drift says nothing stays. I stayed eleven years, which is eight past decent. My bag's been packed since spring. I just keep finding one more bird that needs banding.

choices.text: Then why re-ink the ledger? You're staying.

loft_fate.says: Nobody inherits a loft. You inherit the bands. Whoever takes the strips inherits the birds' trust, and that took me eleven years. The cage is just a cage.

choices.text: Eleven years is a long time to feed something you'll hand off.

reactions.grief: Where and which line come first, plain trade, before they're deep in their mother's last year and can't climb out.
reactions.shock: The bird goes up without its band, against the stencil on the board, and they watch it go.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets weighed against the cost of leaving, a sum they know by heart, and the arithmetic shames them.
reactions.accused: The packed bag by the door reads as flight all at once, and the denial takes a beat too long.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands like a stenciled order, and they wait for the real cargo to be named.
reactions.questioned: The route comes out complete, every stop and seal, the one ledger they never have to bend.
reactions.threatened: Leaving has always been the answer; for the first time it isn't.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The third hand slips off the wing, and they watch it shake the way their mother's did, and say nothing.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their hands stay on the release schedule, but the loft key finds its way back onto their belt.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Every bird in the loft goes quiet at once, and the silence scares them more than the shudder itself.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their defense arrives faster than they meant it to, and it comes with dates and a bird's name.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: A yes is halfway out before they remember what birds can't carry.

npc.description: Yobakhaiu-Fetonga stands on a cage-top with the last bird of the day, fitting a banded strip over its leg with two hands while a third holds the wing. A packed bag sits by the door. The loft key is already off their belt.

lore.name: The route-band ledger
lore.description: A tin plate hangs inside the release board, banded to it with the same cloth leg-strips the birds wear. Each strip carries a knot pattern and a name. Half the strips are knotted for routes no loft on the strip-map shows anymore, and someone has re-inked the last column of the ledger with their new destinations in a hand that got shakier down the page.

content.name: Yiztitlan
content.description: The floor is wire mesh, springy underfoot, and grit has worked through from the droppings channel below. Saffron curtains of printed silk hang where walls should be. Pigeon bars climb toward a glazed roof panel. On the release board, stenciled twice: BAND THE BIRD BEFORE RELEASE. Half the cages stand empty.

npc.name: Tlicho-Qiltonkoatl
npc.voice: Terse, priced. Every sentence sounds like it has already been invoiced.

greet.says: You're standing in my aisle. Word or ledger — word's cheaper. The Braid's been carrying odd fragments off the terminals for weeks, and I sell what the Braid hands me.

fragments.says: Motif indices that don't match the tellings. Olo's chasing it; I chase buyers. Learn the wards if you want the rest — that part isn't for sale, it's for earning.

reactions.grief: Says it's noted before hearing which name, then keeps standing at the ledger with nothing to enter.
reactions.shock: Looks at the body like inventory until the arithmetic fails and they step back into the racks.
reactions.bribed: Refuses faster than anything all season, then, out of habit, quotes what the memory would have cost.
reactions.accused: The pen lifts off the page and stays there; the price of this accusation they don't know yet.
reactions.flattered: Names the asking price behind the compliment before the flatterer has finished laying it on.
reactions.questioned: Rattles off the account at price-quote speed and is shelving a ledger before the questioner finishes.
reactions.threatened: Prices the threat like a fee already owed, then mentions the date the threatener last bought from them.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Reprices the lie without blinking, though the knot-cord at the wrist gets pulled once, hard.
reactions.authority_arrives: Covers the open ledger with one forearm and keeps talking mid-sentence, quieter, same tempo.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For one breath they move with everyone else; then they are already valuing whatever the Braid just handed up.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Believes it too fast and starts listing the name's old debts before anyone has asked them to.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Wants to say yes, cannot, and offers a discount instead, which is the only currency they carry.

npc.description: Tlicho-Qiltonkoatl works standing, one elbow pinning a ledger open, a knotted cord at the wrist thick enough to be a resume. They write without looking down and answer without looking up.

lore.name: The Second Book
lore.description: Under the main ledger sits a slimmer one, bound in webbing, its pages in three hands. The front book records what was sold and to whom; the second records what was sold twice — the same rumor, priced differently for a Continuant clerk than for a Rindwalker runner. One entry, weeks old, is underlined twice: the same mythograph fragment, seven buyers, seven prices.

content.name: Mosakani's Ledger Nook
content.description: The heat sits at the ceiling and refuses to come down; the floor stays cold enough that everyone keeps their boots on. Teal canvas webbing slings the ledger racks three deep where one was planned, and bodies pack the aisle shoulder to shoulder, trading whispers for entries. Stenciled on a tin-foil panel: NAMES KEPT, SOURCES NOT.

npc.name: Joud of Falhah
npc.voice: Short sentences. Answers maintenance questions gladly and personal ones slowly, as if each word has to be unbolted first.

tarn.says: Down. Not dead — down. He stopped talking about his routes, then stopped talking. The night before he left he greased every bolt in this room. I've done the work thirty years. You don't grease a floor you're coming back to.

choices.text: I'm sorry. I'll leave you to your counting.

greet.says: Bunkhouse 46. If you're here for a bunk, seven through twelve are open. If you're here about the seventh, we're not finished counting.

choices.text: What happened to the seventh bunk?

shift.says: Dock crew, days and nights, split the same bunks. You never meet your other half. You know them by how they've worn the mattress and what they leave on the sill. That's a marriage of a kind. Tarn broke ours.

routes.says: Tunnel work. Not mine — his. He'd come up smelling of sealant and say nothing, and I'd make tea and say nothing, and that was the whole friendship. Now the nothing has a shape and I don't like the shape.

choices.text: I hope he greased his own way clear.
If I hear anything, I'll bring it back here.

seventh.says: Tarn left. Took the bunk apart bolt by bolt, greased the fittings, left the frame. That's a mender's goodbye. The slate under it is older than me and I've slept here eleven years.

choices.text: Eleven years is a long shift-share.

reactions.grief: She says the bunk number before the name, then sits down on the nearest made bed without being asked.
reactions.shock: She looks at the raw bolt-holes instead of the body and cannot finish counting the empty bunks.
reactions.bribed: She asks what the payment buys in a man her age, and turns back to the frame.
reactions.accused: She laughs, one short wrong sound, and asks him to say it again, slower.
reactions.flattered: She accepts the praise for the bolts and none for herself, and waits for the request she knows is coming.
reactions.questioned: She gives route and hour unprompted, the way she reads a bolt inventory, and offers the grease log.
reactions.threatened: Her voice holds better than her hands; she asks him to write the threat down as damage.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Halfway through retightening a bolt she already tightened, she stops and admits which part was true.
reactions.authority_arrives: She holds the door open for him and names the empty bunks before he can ask.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She names the joint by feel, then admits no log lists a load that moves like that.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She calls the naming wrong, not cruel, wrong by one night, and says she has the log to show it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She offers a bunk he cannot use, because beds are the only help she has left.

npc.description: Joud of Falhah stands with one hand flat on the empty frame, breathing hard. Copper wire binds back sleeves that were cut short, not rolled. The man by the slate is younger and says nothing now.

lore.name: The seventh bunk's bolts
lore.description: Where the missing bunk stood, the floor bolts are worn round and greased, unlike the others. Someone serviced them on a schedule, from below. A graphite mark on the slate beside them reads a date older than the bunkhouse itself, and a word: 'carried.' Whoever left took their bed apart first, with care.

content.name: Bunkhouse 46
content.description: A woman is dragging a bunk frame across the floor, its feet shrieking on slate. She stops when the door opens. Behind her, a man holds a graphite tally slate half-erased. Six bunks stand empty; a seventh is gone, its bolt-holes raw in the floor. Over the door, stenciled: DAY SLEEPERS AND NIGHT SLEEPERS SHARE THIS BUNK.

npc.name: Muklonieso the Lion-Returned
npc.voice: Short, warm, unbothered by strangers. She speaks the way she folds — briskly, in finished units.

fear.says: Not my floor to name. I see the numbers on my board. More births, every season, and the corridors below us quiet in a way they weren't. She reads the same numbers wider. You don't build second rooms when you think the first one might not keep.

choices.text: Say nothing. Pick up a fold of linen.

help.says: Stack those on the low shelf, not the high one. The high shelf sags. Everything in here sags, we just take turns holding it up.

choices.text: Ask how she got her name.

name.says: I died once, on a table in the clinic proper. Fever. Three days flat. Woke up asking for work. Someone started calling me that and it stuck. Lions don't get second goes. I did.

choices.text: Ask if it changed what she believes.

writ.says: Merid Solen knows. She signed the audit that flagged this room herself, before she was Factor. She was fair then. I think she's fair now, and frightened, and fair doesn't build second rooms.

choices.text: Ask what the Factor is frightened of.
Thank her and let her work.

greet.says: You're early for the courtyard class. Or lost. Either way, mind the linen, it's the only dry stock I have until the second wash.

choices.text: Ask how a healer comes to be called the Lion-Returned.

linen.says: Six births this tenday. This room was built for four a season. The Factor's office sends apologies and no hands. So I wash, I fold, I make do.

choices.text: Offer to carry or fold something.

belief.says: The writ says the voyage hands itself to the next generation and we keep the floor under them. After I woke I believed it harder, not softer. But I'll tell you what nobody puts in the writ: it's not the ship that continues. It's this room. One woman, one cry, then the next.

choices.text: Ask what the Factor is frightened of.
Let her get back to her folding.

reactions.grief: She asks three practical questions, then a fourth she already knows the answer to, her hands folding nothing.
reactions.shock: She goes very useful, calling for linen and bowls, and her hands shake only when the work runs out.
reactions.bribed: She prices the looking-away in births per season, out loud, and the number ends the negotiation.
reactions.accused: Her hands stop mid-fold and she says no, once, then quieter, as if testing it.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets sorted to the low shelf, things she doesn't need, and she asks what it's meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: She lists her hours in finished units and goes back to the shelf that sags, unhurried by the asking.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands as removal from work — one death is enough — and she stays level only by effort.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she owns the lie in one flat breath and keeps shielding the name behind it, chin up.
reactions.authority_arrives: One long look gives the door its due, and her hands keep moving through the linen.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She steadies the washing bench with one palm, then counts heads, hers last.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The board's numbers defend them first, then the one doubt she'd normally keep folded comes out too.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The no is plain and quick, and then she stays, doing whatever small work the plea still allows.

npc.description: Muklonieso the Lion-Returned stands ankle-deep in folded linen, sleeves of a deep blue clinic coat rolled past the elbow. A zinc tray of clamped cord-cutters balances on one hip. She was mid-fold when you came in and has not decided whether to put it down.

lore.name: The tally board of Phora
lore.description: A zinc board hangs inside the linen cupboard, scored with a knife-mark for every birth worked in this room. The earliest marks are neat rows. The last three columns are crowded to the edge and spill onto a second board wired beside it. At the bottom someone has written the room's capacity: four, and underlined it twice.

content.name: Phora
content.description: The washing bench sits closer to the birth chair than it should; a knee would strike it. Bleached linen fills the shelves and stacks on the floor, and zinc trays crowd the sill. Sun crosses a low ceiling stencilled with QUIET PAST THIS DOOR, ALWAYS. A woman looks up from folding, surprised.

npc.name: Yiuhtzin-Itazkan
npc.voice: Terse and route-minded. Answers in legs and loads, not stories.

greet.says: If you're running, take a tag from the top row. If you're not, stand clear of the drop lane.

choices.text: Who stamps the marks on the back of the tags?

marks.says: The bench stamps the front. The back is none of mine. Now move — the midday cart won't hold.

reactions.grief: She calls it a route with no return leg, flat, and stamps tags until her hands begin to shake.
reactions.shock: She has seen drops go wrong, but not this; her legs sit her down mid-sort.
reactions.bribed: She asks what the bribe weighs, names it in loads, and pushes it back across the bench.
reactions.accused: Eleven people saw her legs on the midday run; she says so once, too loud, and waits.
reactions.flattered: Praise her sorting and she counts the tag rack twice, because flattery at this bench ends in a route request.
reactions.questioned: She recites the morning's drops and their cart times without looking up from the lead tags.
reactions.threatened: Threats are just tolls; she pays them, nods, and asks which route the man wants her on.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The stamp says otherwise and her hand goes to the satchel buckle before any words do.
reactions.authority_arrives: She asks the official one question, which stamp outranks hers, and goes back to sorting on the answer.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Lead tags swing on their pegs and she reads them anyway, checking which routes the shudder just broke.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She could name three runs that person missed; she says none of them, and stares at the drop lane.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She hears the plea out, points to the stencil, and admits her legs don't run where it's asking.

npc.description: Yiuhtzin-Itazkan sorts inbound tags at the near end of the bench, fast, not looking up. A canvas satchel rides one hip, already buckled for the next run. The sleepers' boots sit by the bench foot, laced, like the sleeper means to leave soon and someone else is keeping them ready.

lore.name: The double-stamped tags
lore.description: Every lead tag carries two stamps: a route on one face, and a smaller mark on the back that matches a column chalked on the board's frame. Count the marks and the chalk and they disagree. The bench logs runs the couriers never reported, in a hand nobody here claims. Someone has been sending work out without telling the bench-keepers.

content.name: Dispatch-Bench 55
content.description: The floorboards give underfoot, planed smooth in the walking line and rough at the edges. Sawdust works into the grain. Route tags of hammered lead hang from pegs, each stamped on both faces. A stencil over the bench reads TAKE A ROUTE TAG BEFORE YOU RUN. A woman sleeps on the far end of it.

npc.name: Yinitl-Hixik
npc.voice: Fast, dry, prices things by habit. Pauses before anything free.

open.says: Nobody, yet. That's the trade. The Braid doesn't sell information, it sells *first* — the hours between one person knowing and everyone knowing. The terminal posts have been running motifs that don't match any telling on record, weeks of it, and I've been parceling that out to maybe six people. Not because I understand it. Because whoever does understand it will owe me, and I intend to be owed.

greet.says: Chairs are by subscription. Yours is twelve, if you're on the roll. If you're not, stand by the rack and don't lean.

choices.text: What do you actually do all day?
And the second file — who reads that one?

probe_a.says: Because the terminal drops every post older than a season, and nobody upstairs has noticed. Paper doesn't get edited. I like a thing that stays what I wrote.

probe_b.says: Forty subscribers, and the knot at my wrist carries all their routes. The room was Yaltem's before — he ran it forty years and let it go soft. Rebuilt it in six days. Nothing here has a history yet, which some find honest and most find rude.

probe_c.says: I read what crosses the Braid and decide what's worth a card. Most of it's gossip about freight. Some of it's the Seven's postings, and those I file twice — once where they belong, once where they don't.

reactions.grief: Mid-copy, her pen stops on a name she knew, and she will not write the death beside it.
reactions.shock: One look is all she allows herself, and she hears her own voice quoting subscription terms at nobody.
reactions.bribed: The pause she gives free things arrives anyway, insult at being bought so cheap dressed up as deliberation.
reactions.accused: The pricing instinct fails her, and she repeats the accusation word for word as if checking it against a card.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands like a bill of sale, and she lets it sit too long before asking what it costs.
reactions.questioned: Hours and corridors come off her like a receipt, recited too fast, priced at nothing because the asking is routine.
reactions.threatened: She prices the threat out loud, naming what her silence costs, and hates how steady it comes out.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Denial is not her medium, so she revises the story aloud, mid-sentence, watching which version the room keeps.
reactions.authority_arrives: She reads the stenciled door rule against the official's warrant and decides, visibly, which of them the room belongs to.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She holds the cards flat and thinks, uninvited, of the mismatched motifs — this is what they were rehearsing.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name gets one dry repetition, and underneath it she sorts what she knows against what the accusation needs.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says no in fewer words than the plea deserved, and her hands, for once, are not pricing anything.

npc.description: Yinitl-Hixik sits in chair eleven, copying index cards by hand because the terminal is down again. The room is white as a fresh plate — lacquer still tacky at the chair arms, hide floor-cloth stiff underfoot, everything correct and nothing settled.

lore.name: The Subscription Ledger
lore.description: Yinitl-Hixik's ledger is bound in cured hide gone amber at the grip, and it holds no book titles at all. Each numbered chair maps to a name, a route, and a knot-pattern in the margin — chair nine is subscribed to a reader who has never once come, but whose knot is copied into eleven other entries, all marked paid. The room doesn't sell reading. It sells proof that somebody was expected here, on a date, at a price.

content.name: Yatlkalko
content.description: The floor gives underfoot with a faint tack, lacquer still soft, pulling at each step like it wants a toll. Bright white everywhere, chairs numbered in fresh teal, hide seat-covers stiff and uncreased, and no scuff anywhere except Yinitl-Hixik's boots, which have seen forty corridors. Stenciled over the door: CHAIR BY SUBSCRIPTION ONLY. She looks up from her ledger, caught mid-count.

npc.name: Sairtriexita Viorfrese
npc.voice: Short. Feeds people before she talks to them. Slightly warmer if you ask about the work and not the gossip.

end.says: Wipe your spot when you're done. Someone's always coming in after you.

pot.says: Barley, root ends, whatever the green decks passed on yesterday. It's not a menu, it's a count. Tonight the count said feed three more than I planned for.

choices.text: Has the count been short lately?

room.says: My mother planed that timber. The chairs she left to the room, not to me, which is a distinction I've stopped arguing with. The tile in the sixth one is mine. Fired it myself when it went.

choices.text: Can you keep up with the repairs?

greet.says: Sit anywhere that isn't broken. Kitchen's closed but the pot isn't. Chit on the rail if you worked late.

choices.text: This table's been here a long time.

short.says: Short of what, hands or goods? Both. The stove's older than my mother's table and it wants parts nobody mends anymore. But nobody's gone hungry here yet, and that's the whole job, as far as I'm concerned.

choices.text: Sit and eat with me a minute.

reactions.grief: The pot gets stirred long past done, the name gets said once, and the six chairs get counted twice.
reactions.shock: A full bowl goes cold in her hands; for once there is no count in her head.
reactions.bribed: She names the bribe out loud, twice, loud enough for the room, then slides the bowl back untouched.
reactions.accused: The spoon stops in the pot; she names every mouth she fed this week until her voice gives out.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets logged next to the chits, and she asks what it is meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Her answers come as a tally — where, when, how many fed — and a bowl lands before the asker.
reactions.threatened: No raised voice — she makes his portion smaller than everyone else's and watches until he notices.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she amends the count out loud, adding the omitted name without apology, the tips of her ears red.
reactions.authority_arrives: The pot comes off the heat before a word does, and her eyes go to the door and stay.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her hand goes flat over the pot lid before she lets herself look at anyone's face.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The defense comes before the question does: she has fed that person for years and knows their appetite.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She feeds them first anyway, then says plainly that food is the whole of what she has.

npc.description: Sairtriexita Viorfrese works the stove with her sleeves rolled past the elbow, one eye on the pot, one on the door. She portioned for two. There is now a third bowl out and no apology for it.

lore.name: The Tile Patch
lore.description: The sixth chair's split seat has been plugged with a clay tile, glazed the same green-grey as the stove, fired to fit. Someone measured it right.

content.name: Tzenyatzen's Meal Table
content.description: The stove sits an arm's length from the table, which is one arm too many for the room they share. Sairtriexita Viorfrese looks up from a pot, spoon stopped mid-stir. Six chairs, one patched with a clay tile. Above the lintel, painted flat: LATE SHIFT EATS FREE, SHOW YOUR CHIT.

npc.name: Svogakrost of Vyabansk
npc.voice: Terse, institutional, the warmth of hospitality delivered as procedure rather than feeling.

greet.says: Sit where you like, but not there — that's the Factor's table, asleep or not. First pour's on the house. Second's on your standing.

sleeper.says: Came off double audit-shift and sat down mid-sip. We let him be. The kettle keeps what it keeps. Take the cup he didn't touch, if you're dry — it's the sweetened one.

reactions.grief: He pulls the dead man's usual cup before remembering there's no one left to pour for, and turns it face-down.
reactions.shock: He stands in the doorway, pot going cold in his hand, with no order in him to set it down.
reactions.bribed: He quotes his own tariff back, first pour free, second on standing, and the offer dies in the arithmetic.
reactions.accused: Denial comes once, flat, and then only house rules, as if the charge had been filed in the wrong queue.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets shelved with compliments on the paint, and he asks, mildly, what it's meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: First bell to last, ledger-order, he gives his accounting and throws in the stock-tally nobody asked for.
reactions.threatened: His eyes do the answering, one slow pass from the stencil to the door, and the next pour runs slow.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: He drops the first story like a spoiled batch and counts the cost somewhere the room can't see.
reactions.authority_arrives: The whole stoop comes up to inspection standard around him, every seam correct, the pour precise as ceremony.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He pins the kettle through the shudder, then checks the sleeper's untouched cup, house rules holding where the floor doesn't.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He knows the man's tab by heart, and the accusation doesn't fit it, and he says so twice.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He hears the whole plea out without interrupting, a break in his own practice, then names what he cannot give.

npc.description: Svogakrost of Vyabansk stands at the kettle in a navy apron gone stiff with steam, pouring with the unhurried wrist of someone who has done this through more rebuilds than this stoop has seen. He does not wake the sleeper. He steps around him on a path worn into his own habits, if not yet into the floor.

lore.name: The Ground-Glass Dosing Jar
lore.description: Under the counter, a squat jar with a wax-sealed lid, ground glass stirred into the sugar so fine it only catches the light sideways. A Continuant night-kettle keeps a measured pinch in every third pot — enough to slow a body down, not enough to be asked about. The wax is fresh. The batch was renewed this week, for a room that was rebuilt this week.

content.name: Kohozin's Kettle Stoop
content.description: The kettle eats sound before it eats anything else — voices come through the steam flattened, secondhand, like talk from another room. The stoop itself is all new navy paint and unscuffed brass, correct to the last seam, nothing yet forgiven. Stencilled over the counter: KETTLE ON FROM FIRST BELL. A man in a slate uniform is asleep at the corner table, hands still around a full cup.

npc.name: Rharhitych Trys
npc.voice: Precise, ledger-minded, unhurried. Talks about storage the way a priest talks about rites — every object a held promise, every slot a duty. Answers questions with counts.

end.says: She nods once, and goes back to her packing. The grate stays shut between you.

writ.says: The writ decides, and I'm glad of it. A keeper who trusts her own judgment over the ledger is a keeper you shouldn't leave a spoon with. My grandmother kept a lockup in the south rows for forty years and never once made an exception. People trusted her because she was boring. Boring is the whole trade.

choices.text: Forty years in one lockup. Did she never want to go anywhere?

greet.says: Window's still barred. Business through the grate or not at all, until the seal's cut tomorrow. You're looking at a room that has never once lost a pledge. Come to deposit, or come to ask?

choices.text: The room looks brand new. Was there an old one?
You seal everything in pitch yourself?
You're packing up. Where does a keeper go when the keeping's done?

pitch.says: Triple coat, then sailcloth over the seams. Pitch keeps out damp, damp keeps out rot, rot is how a pledge dies unclaimed. Smell it — that's a year of the stuff, cooked in small batches so it never scalds. Store-verb work is mostly keeping time at bay with a brush.

choices.text: It smells like the whole trade, then.

mostly.says: She pauses, a sailcloth roll half-tucked. "There's a shelf slot in this room I left empty on purpose. Number ninety-one. Nothing assigned, nothing coming. When the seal's cut and the pledges come home, I'm walking the axial road as far as the light goes strange, and I'm not checking any ledger while I do it. Don't tell the auditors. Don't tell anyone, really." She finishes the roll. "That one's off the books."

choices.text: Then I hope the road is long. Good luck, keeper.
Where the light goes strange — what's out there?

leaving.says: Home, and then somewhere that isn't home. She doesn't look up from the sailcloth. "A lockup holds, but a keeper is only borrowed too. Ask me again tomorrow, when the seal's cut and the room's not mine anymore."

strange.says: Nobody I've kept pledges for has ever come back from there to collect. She shrugs, and four of her six shoulders move with it. "Maybe that's the point. Maybe I want to be somewhere a promise can't find me, just once. Ninety-one stays empty until I'm back. If I'm back." She ties the roll shut. "Anything else, or are we done gossiping through a grate?"

choices.text: We're done. Take your road, keeper.

old_room.says: Lockup-Window 10, before this. Flooded when a cistern joint let go two streets over. Not a shelf lost, not a pledge wet — but the writ says a damp room can't hold pledges, so we tore it to the studs and rebuilt. Everything correct. Nothing worn in. A room has to earn its wear, same as a keeper does.

choices.text: The writ decides that? Not the keeper?
Fair enough. Back to the window, then.

grandmother.says: Every day of her life, and she went nowhere. That's the part nobody says out loud about this work. You hold other people's lives steady so they can move. Somebody has to be the still point, and the still point doesn't get to be curious. I took the vow at eighteen with my eyes open. Mostly.

reactions.grief: She recites the dead woman's pledge, one tin flute, held sixty days, then sits on a crate without deciding to.
reactions.shock: She keeps counting aloud and loses the number three times; her six hands have stopped pretending to work.
reactions.bribed: She repeats the offered sum once, for the record, then resumes wrapping as though it were a weather report.
