reactions.accused: She stops folding mid-corner, demands the entry number, and starts reciting the shelf's contents before anyone asks her to.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes her check the grate is shut; nobody compliments a boring trade unless they want an exception.
reactions.questioned: Counts come first with her, shelf by shelf, and she does not look up until the questions stop.
reactions.threatened: She answers the threat with the seal schedule, voice level, and her top two hands keep wrapping the pot wrong.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she re-counts the shelf aloud, twice, as though arithmetic could be stitched back to match what she said.
reactions.authority_arrives: She has the counts written twice before the official asks, and stands straighter than the room requires.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room moves and she doesn't; her finger is on the third shelf before the dust settles, counting.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name stings; she recites every pledge that person paid on time, two defenses more than the ledger requires.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Pleas move her nowhere, she says, but she cannot look at the grate while reciting the forfeit clause.

npc.description: A short, broad worker in a rust-brown apron, wrapping a pitch pot in sailcloth with the quick hands of someone packing up. Six arms, none of them explained. The last shelf has already been emptied and wiped; the rest of the room stands finished around her like an argument she won.

lore.name: The Ninety-Day Ledger
lore.description: The ledger bolted beside the window is not paper but a brass plate with sliding markers, one per shelf slot. Each marker has two positions: held, and released. Rindwalker practice holds that a stored thing is a promise kept in the owner's absence — so the markers are checked by a second keeper every seventh day, and the checking is signed into the plate's lower margin in scores of different initials. The newest score is Trys's own; there is room left for hundreds more.

content.name: Lockup-Window 11
content.description: Sound arrives at Lockup-Window 11 already flattened — voices from the square outside enter thin and leave thinner, swallowed by pitch-sealed shelves that stand wall to wall and floor to rafter. Oxblood paint covers everything, new and unscratched. The sunstrip falls through the barred window onto crates still banded for shipping. A stencilled board above the window reads: CLAIM WITHIN NINETY DAYS OR FORFEIT.

npc.name: Zazdnesya Brekrekitsyn
npc.voice: Terse, dosed out. She talks the way she measures: exact amounts, no refills, no small talk past what is needed.

greet.says: If you're sick, the clinic on the square took the roster. If you're not, mind the wet floor — I've mopped twice today.

leaving.says: Consolidation. My stock goes to the square clinic, my cards go to the archive, and I go where I'm written. Take a lozenge if your throat's dry. Then let me finish.

reactions.grief: She asks what they were taking, then asks again, and wraps the next bottle without testing its warmth.
reactions.shock: The bottle slips through the cloth and she watches it land, making no move toward the spill.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against the roster and refuses it in the tone she keeps for overdoses.
reactions.accused: She stops mid-wrap, bottle still against her wrist, and cannot say whether she counted it warm.
reactions.flattered: Unmeasured praise gets the caution owed an off-label dose; she asks what the flattery is meant to treat.
reactions.questioned: Her answers come in the flat meter of a label, as much as asked and not a drop more.
reactions.threatened: Her hand goes to the lozenge tin, hospitality arriving ahead of any answer, which is where the fear shows.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she corrects the figure aloud before anyone can press, hands steady in a way she is forcing.
reactions.authority_arrives: The roster is on the counter before the door finishes opening; she goes where she is written.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She counts the bottles aloud while the rack still swings, the numbering doing the steadying her voice cannot.
reactions.someone_else_accused: One fact for the defense, delivered flat, then she is back at the crate as if the ledger now balanced.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She has no dose for this, so she gives shelf codes, square-clinic hours, a name, far more than she should.

npc.description: Zazdnesya Brekrekitsyn wraps bottles in cloth, each one tested against her wrist for warmth before it goes in the crate. She is in clinic blue with the sleeves gone at the elbows. A chalk stub sits behind her ear. She has packed eleven bottles and left twelve spaces for them.

lore.name: The Weaning Ledger Card
lore.description: Behind the last jar, an index card tacked to the shelf edge. It tracks one patient across forty years: fevers, births, a bad lung, each entry in a different hand. The final line reads 'transferred to her granddaughter's care — same doses, same times.' The Continuants do not let a body change healers mid-life if they can help it.

content.name: The Tincture Room
content.description: A drying rack swings on its chain when the door moves it. The Tincture Room is nearly bare: grey-green shelves, chalk marks where jars stood, a sweet smoke still hanging from the morning's boils. The counter is sticky with old syrup. Stencilled on the wall: DOSE AS MARKED, NOT AS GUESSED.

npc.name: Pos Fotraldi
npc.voice: Terse, counting while they speak. Short answers, then back to the head in the chair.

greet.says: Chair's taken until the second bell. If you're here to talk, that part's free — the tabard says Saturn posted again, ask anyone waiting.

choices.text: Ask why the shop is so full of crates.

crates.says: Storage annex flooded two weeks back. Until it's mended, my shop holds it. A room serves what needs serving.

reactions.grief: They recite the dead customer's last appointment, exact to the bell, and the towel hand shakes, just once.
reactions.shock: A half-cut lock hangs from the customer's head while the count in Pos's head stops and will not restart.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets swept toward the door with the linen broom; the posted prices are recited in full.
reactions.accused: The scissors stop mid-stroke; Pos makes them say it twice before the count restarts.
reactions.flattered: They correct one detail of the praise — the linens are the annex's, not the shop's — and the count resumes untouched.
reactions.questioned: The count holds steady through the whole accounting, four strokes a section, and the customer hears nothing.
reactions.threatened: They are more afraid of losing the chair than of the threat, and they finish the left side first.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they revise the smallest number they can get away with and keep the towel moving as if nothing changed.
reactions.authority_arrives: The annex crates get one long look before the official does, and the answers come shorter after that.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The towel hand steadies the customer's skull before the crates stop rattling, and the count restarts from one, out loud.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They give the accused's standing slot, fourth bell every sixth day, and go back to the head in the chair.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The free part gets given twice over, talk and more talk, while the hands make plain there is nothing else.

npc.description: Pos Fotraldi works one-handed, towel in the other, a continuant's slate-blue apron buttoned to the collar. The scissors keep moving through the customer's hair while they talk.

lore.name: The counting chair
lore.description: The chair's arm bears a column of small knife-marks. One per head, Pos says, cut off clean at the end of each shift. The column has never failed to reach its end.

content.name: Stack 60 Under
content.description: The smell is shaving soap and warm damp towel, thick in the small room. One chair stands on rubber matting, navy glazed brick behind it. Crates of stored linens line every wall, and a stencil on the brick reads TALK FREE, SHAVE IS NOT. Pos Fotraldi sweeps between the crates without looking up.

npc.name: Ngoa-Ngofaishdaighnui
npc.voice: Short, transactional, awake in bursts. Warms only when spoken to about fish, ice, or routes.

old.says: Old one leaked. Ice went soft by mid-morning and soft ice is a lie you sell by weight. So we built this. Copper holds the cold. Bamboo holds the copper. Nothing here is meant to last past its use.

choices.text: Even the till drawer? It looks older than the rest.

noon.says: Because the ice cart comes at noon and by then the morning lot has sweated. People who buy early get firm ice and honest weight. People who buy late get my sympathy and no refund.

sale.says: Wrapped and gone. Tell your neighbors — the Braid already knows my prices, so you might as well beat them to it.

goods.says: Silverbell trout, iced this morning, which is more than the stall two down can say. The eels I'd skip. They came through three hands before mine and it shows.

choices.text: Good to know. Anything else worth hearing?

greet.says: Buying or waking me? Only one pays.

choices.text: New stand. Was there an old one?
The board says buy early. Why noon?

drawer.says: That came from the old stand and it'll go to the next one. The knots under it are accounts. Debts outlive furniture. You want the circled one? That's between me and a name.

choices.text: Understood. I'll leave the knots alone.

respect_node.says: Huh. Most people push. Fine — come back at noon when the cart lands and I'll cut you the first of the fresh ice, no queue. Now let me sleep. The fish don't sell themselves and I don't sell well tired.

choices.text: Rest well. See you at noon.

reactions.grief: Keeps wrapping the finished parcel, paper over paper, and has to ask the name twice.
reactions.shock: Wakes all the way for once, and the hand with the knife hangs still at their side.
reactions.bribed: Names a price for looking away that no one could pay, which is how they say no.
reactions.accused: Asks who is paying for the accusation, since nothing in this market moves without a price on it.
reactions.flattered: Hears the sales pitch in the praise, names the technique out loud, and still stands a little straighter.
reactions.questioned: Answers in the same order every time, hours listed like prices, one eye still shut.
reactions.threatened: Quotes what they are worth and what they'd fetch, flat, while their knuckles whiten on the counter.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats the first lie louder, then a smaller one, then stands there with nothing left to sell.
reactions.authority_arrives: Asks which market the official's authority runs to, and weighs ice through whatever the answer is.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their first thought is melt: every second the crates shift, the stock is costing them money.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says the accusation is wrong on the schedule alone, then realizes they have testified for someone they cannot stand.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: States what they can spare, admits it is not enough, and names the next stop on the route.

npc.description: Ngoa-Ngofaishdaighnui sleeps upright at the till, chin on one fist, a scaling knife still loose in the other hand. A knotted cord circles one wrist. Every few minutes the market noise makes them half-open one eye, confirm no one is buying, and close it again.

lore.name: The Old Till Drawer
lore.description: The new stand's till is new. The drawer beneath it is not. Its underside is scratched with route-knots copied in pen — a Drift trader's ledger of buyers and debts, carried from the old stand before it was torn down. One entry is circled twice: a name, and beside it, 'pays in fish, never late, ask about the noon ice.'

content.name: The Ice Stand
content.description: The magenta work-lamp cuts off sharp at the awning's edge; past it, the market keeps moving in half-dark. The stand is new copper and fresh bamboo, still smelling of sawdust under the fish-brine. Ice crates stack three deep against the steep counter. A stenciled board reads: ICE RESTOCKED AT NOON, BUY EARLY. Behind the till, someone sleeps in a chair that does not belong to them.

npc.name: Lihuzaasaa of the Backwards Hill
npc.voice: Measured, inventory-minded; counts things before naming them, and treats patience as a skill, not a virtue.

open.says: I saw that everything I was taught about cultivation is a child's version of something true. We rotate crops by season, by schedule, by writ — and down here the mist runs on a cycle nobody set, and the roots drink when the drinking is right, and they have never once missed. Venus doesn't grow the way we grow. Venus grows the way the ship breathes — without asking whether anyone approved the rhythm. I packed my tools and I have not decided yet whether that comforts me or unmakes me.

choices.text: Thank you. That's more than I came for.
Nobody set the cycle? Then who's counting?

greet.says: Careful where you set your feet — that ash was a root-bed this morning and it hasn't decided what it is yet.

choices.text: What do you do with all that salt?
Whose work is this, really? Yours or the garden's?
Something big lived here, didn't it.
What did you see, working this close to it?
Didn't mean to interrupt the packing.

probe_a.says: Bag it, weigh it, log it. Every kilo of salt is a season the roots pulled out of the mist and couldn't keep. I've hauled eleven hundred kilos out of this gallery since I was apprenticed, and I could tell you which bed gave which.

probe_b.says: Ours is the ledger, the garden's is the living. A Continuant learns that early — you don't make anything grow, you keep the conditions honest and write down what happened. The rest was never ours to claim.

probe_c.says: Something tended here. There's a difference, and it took me twenty years in the green decks to hear it. We kept conditions. Whatever worked this gallery kept the roots themselves — I've seen the handling marks, and they're older than the ship's oldest wall-notation.

reactions.grief: They recite the dead one's yields, gallery by gallery and season by season, more numbers than any condolence requires.
reactions.shock: They stop between the stripped beds, and for the first time in years count nothing at all, only look.
reactions.bribed: They weigh the offer aloud in kilos and hours, then decline, because nothing unlogged has ever kept a gallery honest.
reactions.accused: They set the wet brush down before answering, so that no shaking hand can add a stroke to the accusation.
reactions.flattered: They accept praise the way they accept salt, weighed, bagged, and suspected of holding more than it shows.
reactions.questioned: They answer in tallies before names, hours and kilos first, the patience itself cultivated, same as anything they grow.
reactions.threatened: They refuse to finish the sentence, and a net that was folded an hour ago gets folded again, badly.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The count behind their eyes stops mid-number, hands going still on the wet stencil, no figure left that reconciles.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the insignia before the face, already deciding how much of the empty span to volunteer.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The tremor gets logged with a timestamp they will check against every mist-cycle they know, and none will fit.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They defend the accused in numbers, bed by bed, yield by yield, unable to say a kind word outright.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They explain that the mist keeps no schedule anyone can argue with, then stand quietly inside their own uselessness.

npc.description: In the green-black buttressed dark of Root Works, where the cold pools along the girdered floor and the warmth hangs a body-height up among the mist-ducts, Lihuzaasaa of the Backwards Hill is stencilling a fresh cycle-number over a stencil that reads GALLERY MIST RUNS ON A CYCLE NO ONE SET. Around them the galleries stand emptied — a kilometre of hanging root-beds stripped back to compacted salt and vitrified ash, the gap where something large lived now visible from either axial end.

lore.name: The Harrowing Ledger-board
lore.description: A slab of vitrified ash, fused smooth, nailed where a root-gallery forks — the Continuants' tally of every harrowing ever done to this gallery, scratched in columns that run off the edge of the board and resume on its back. The columns are not seasons. Some intervals between entries are longer than the whole history of the Nave's settled belt, and the newest entry is a blank space left open, as if whoever carved the last line knew the garden would not wait for them to finish. The salt floor beneath it is worn in a shallow crescent — the shape of feet standing, generation after generation, to read it.

content.name: Root Works
content.description: The cold comes from below here, the way heat comes from below everywhere else: a kilometer of root-galleries hangs above a floor of compacted salt, and the chill of the salt climbs only as far as the lowest buttressed roots, where it stops as if a line were drawn and agreed upon. Girder-arches that once held mist-nets stand stripped, their copper fittings unbolted and stacked in tidy Continuant crates, and the green-black hanging mass of the galleries has pulled back from a whole span of them, leaving a root-shadow on the girders the way a painting leaves a shadow on a wall. Stencilled along one arch, in paint gone the brown of old tea: GALLERY MIST RUNS ON A CYCLE NO ONE SET. Lihuzaasaa of the Backwards Hill is folding the last of the nets.

npc.name: Miael Jiainione
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical without meaning to be — trade terms used at wrong altitudes, as if 'runout' and 'grace' had become interchangeable.

greet.says: Hands off the bed unless the bed asks. It hasn't asked you. The lathe knows its measure; we're only the hands it borrowed. What Sol burns for, this turns toward — you want a word with the fire, or with me?

choices.text: What tolerance is it cutting to?

tolerance.says: To the one that holds the middle still. Not in any standard held — the paint is older than my order and less mistaken. Two parties cut here and the work comes out true either way, which tells you whose tolerance it really is. Now stand out of the curl-line. I have stock to true and the note doesn't wait.

choices.text: Step back and let the work continue.

reactions.grief: Finishes the pass, trues it all the way, then ruins the next piece before the name can settle.
reactions.shock: Their eyes, which track weather and work alike, cannot leave the shape on the floor.
reactions.bribed: Prices the bribe like stock, finds it running out of true, and declines without ceremony.
reactions.accused: The tool stops mid-pass; for the first time in decades their breathing loses the lathe's period.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands on them like runout at the edge of true — they nod with a steadiness their hot ears betray.
reactions.questioned: Their account comes in turns and passes and tolerances, exact as tool-records, offered without once looking up.
reactions.threatened: Somewhere under the calm, an old apprenticeship counts exits and finds only the lathe.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Doesn't retract a word, only amends the tolerance, as though error were a setting that could be trued.
reactions.authority_arrives: No different now that the official stands in the doorway; stock is stock, and it still wants truing.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: That the held note never wavers frightens them more than any shudder could.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks first — they, who never speak first — and gives the room a longer lesson in tolerances than it asked for.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They have nothing to give but the work, and hate how small a mercy that is.

npc.description: Miael Jiainione works the near side of the bed with the unhurried economy of someone whose hands stopped needing supervision decades ago, guiding a rest against stock that is not yet spinning, listening to it before it exists. The heat of the room has gotten into them somewhere deep; sweat finds them and does not, and their breathing has slowed to something near the lathe's own period. They do not look up. They look instead along the work, the way one watches weather.

lore.name: The Micrometer of Unnumbered Divisions
lore.description: Hung on a sintered-ceramic cradle beside the tool-post hangs a micrometer whose scale has no markings at all — the barrel is polished glass, smooth as an egg, and yet worn at one precise arc of its rotation, glossy where a hundred thousand thumbs closed on the same invisible reading. Whatever dimension it measured, it was not a number; it was a place on the barrel, a habit of the hand. Rindwalker doctrine says a tool worn smooth by use is a tool that has been answered. This one has been answered past numbering, and still someone oils the thread.

content.name: Qealaeth
content.description: The lathe is already turning when you enter — though no one remembers starting it, and it does not stop between work. Stock rides the spindle in a blur of green-black, black glass shearing away in curls that fall like exfoliation, and the machine trues each piece to a measure no gauge present can name; the workers set their tools by feel, by long apprenticeship to a tolerance that was in any standard held — the stencilled disclaimer curls above the mandrel in coppery script — and yet which the lathe itself seems to know the way a body knows balance. Both parties work the same bed, shoulder to shoulder, each quietly certain the other is ruining the instrument. The sound is less a hum than a held note, as if the room were singing one syllable of an older word. Nothing here has seams; the walls accept the machines as if grown around them.

npc.name: Ribeem bin Jainsanawi
npc.voice: Terse, dry, the shorthand of someone who fixes things by refusing to let them die. Measures words like spares.

work.says: Jeweler second. Mender first — half the Wards' balance wheels come through this room, and every one of them was worn by somebody who couldn't bear to replace it. That's the whole trade. Take the tray.

greet.says: If it's broken, leave it in the tray. If it's a question, leave it too — I'm closing. Bench runs double shift tomorrow, third this week; don't ask me whose fault that is.

reactions.grief: She packs the same case twice, then tells a workshop story about the dead one that runs far too long.
reactions.shock: She stands under the swinging loupe arm and forgets to duck, the way she has ducked ten thousand times.
reactions.bribed: Her refusal arrives as a price: what the looking-away would cost, itemized, nonnegotiable.
reactions.accused: All four hands stop at once; she asks who says so, and her voice comes out smaller than intended.
reactions.flattered: Praise earns the patience she gives drying lacquer, and one question about what is actually broken.
reactions.questioned: Her alibi comes out itemized like a repair ticket; she has given it before, word for word.
reactions.threatened: The tallow tears under her thumb; she keeps her tone at bench-price and asks him to repeat the terms.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The correction goes in like resetting a stone — one clean turn, no argument, eyes fixed on the bench.
reactions.authority_arrives: A stool is offered, nothing more; jurisdiction ends at her lintel until the man states his business.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The forty cases get counted by eye before her face moves; then she names the joint that failed.
reactions.someone_else_accused: One flat repetition of the name, then nothing — which, from her, is a whole testimony.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: A plain no, once, and then she keeps finding small repairs while the plea stays on the bench.

npc.description: Ribeem bin Jainsanawi works with sleeves rolled past four forearms, the extra pair folded back and out of the light like tools not currently needed. Tallow wax to the elbow. She is packing, not talking.

lore.name: The fourth loupe
lore.description: Three loupes hang at the bench on leather loops. The fourth hangs on a nail driven through the table's corner post, and its lens is ground from hull glass — you can tell by the faint amber seam running through it, the way old rind glass never quite clears. Someone has drilled the frame and laced it with copper wire in a pattern Ribeem's knot-work matches exactly. It is not for sale, not for use, and not explained.

content.name: Rataariyya
content.description: A loupe arm swings out of your way as you duck under the lintel — counterweighted, still moving from the last hand that touched it. Ribeem bin Jainsanawi wraps a finished piece in boiled leather and slots it into a cork-lined case, one of forty such cases stacked to the low beams. Stenciled above the bench, worn to a shadow: NO TICKING CLOCKS LEFT OVERNIGHT.

npc.name: Jaershiatiayia al-Raeqaidiathawy
npc.voice: Clipped, liturgical in the way of someone reciting to machinery that listens slowly. Warmth arrives only obliquely, in what she chooses not to say.

ash.says: Something burning far away, shedding this. The heat comes wrongways — your skin one hour, your breath the next. Don't take the temperature as advice about the room. The room doesn't hold still long enough to have one.

choices.text: You said it listens for weight?
Step back from the falling gold.

greet.says: Don't bless it. It isn't listening for blessing today. Tuesdays — and I use the word loosely — it listens for weight. Stand somewhere and mean it.

column.says: Sol's, or older than Sol, which is a sentence I say and don't believe. The silver part predates the ash; the ash part predates the order that stencilled its edict there. Two parties tend it. One sweeps. One prays. I was sent to be both, which is why nothing I do is finished.

choices.text: Listening for weight — what does that mean?

listening.says: It means: bring nothing you'd grieve to have counted. I stood my first year here and it learned me — that's not devotion, that's inventory. You, friend, arrive already heavy with someone else's purposes. It will notice before I finish this pan. Mind what it does with that.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let her finish the pan.

reactions.grief: Death arrives; she recites the rite for the living by mistake and cannot begin the one for the dead.
reactions.shock: The sight inverts her senses, summer to the lungs, winter to the skin, and she freezes inside the wrong weather.
reactions.bribed: She names the bribe an offering, and offerings to a disbanded order go unclaimed; the refusal costs her nothing visible.
reactions.accused: The accusation lands; her sweeping stops for the first time anyone has witnessed, though her face keeps the old patience.
reactions.flattered: Praise is blessing with a want behind it; she lets the compliment fall past her like everything else that falls.
reactions.questioned: She answers in liturgy, naming each hour like a versicle, and her broom never breaks stride.
reactions.threatened: Fear arrives in her lungs, which have always known winter, and she lets it stand there, unwarmed.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she embalms the lie rather than amending it, repeating the false hour slower, as though repetition were proof.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction she tests for weight, as her dead order taught, and bows correctly without conceding the room belongs to anyone.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Motion violates her one doctrine; when the structure shudders she catches herself praying to something that has already answered.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Heat rises at the name, undeclared; she offers no spoken defense, only sweeping slower, which is her defense.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She cannot give what is asked, so she gives what she has: she stands beside the asker and means it.

npc.description: A small figure at the column's far side, gloved to the shoulder in copper-ruin, sweeping ash that never finishes falling into a pan that never fills. The work has the patience of erosion. She does not look up, though it would be untrue to say she has not noticed.

lore.name: The Ring of Thumbprints
lore.description: At hip height, a circumferential band of silver worn to a gloss by uncountable touches — each print slightly overlapped, as if a procession has been circling the column for longer than prints last.

content.name: Unattended-Column 2
content.description: Nothing here consents to motion. The air stands the way water stands in a glass carried carefully down a stair — the gold light pooled at the column's base has not shifted its shadow in the whole time a person might watch, and the column itself, half vitrified ash, half a silver too warm to be metal, refuses the heat its own colour promises. The skin of the skull says summer; the lungs say winter. Along the plinth, stencilled in a hand long retired: OFFERINGS ACCUMULATE ORDER DISBANDED. The room is larger than its walls admit, or the walls are elsewhere. It is difficult to say which failure is yours.

npc.name: Thimarippe Shenne
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, the speech of someone whose days are measured in sealed metres; warms by one degree when asked the right question.

writ.says: The council writes it, I weld to it. Forty households rehoused in the green decks inside a day — that's what the writ is for. Continuity means somebody leaves so the ship can pass through. I've done this eleven times.

court.says: Once, to run a conduit past its far wall. My lamp couldn't find the ceiling and I stopped trying. Whatever holds court there holds it in no language I've been taught, and it doesn't bother — that's the part that stays with you. The not bothering.

choices.text: Thank them, and step back from the live seam.

greet.says: Mind the rail. Heat's live where the silver's bright. If you're looking for the tenants, the tenants are gone — trunk traffic came through and the writ says they yield.

choices.text: What kind of traffic clears forty homes?
Who enforces a writ like that?

eleven.says: Easier to do. Harder to tally. I keep the notches on the rail — one per household, crossed when they're settled elsewhere. Three open ones left. Then I seal the wall and this room stops being anyone's.

choices.text: Let them finish the tally in peace.

traffic.says: Something out of the court — the long hall back the way you came, the one nobody fills. I've walked it. You could seat every soul in the Nave at that table and have room for the next three generations. When something from there moves, catwalks empty. We seal behind it.

reactions.grief: Stops mid-stroke, asks which peg the dead one's coat hung from, though every peg has stood bare for months.
reactions.shock: The iron burns its brown ring into bright silver before they come back from wherever they went, past the wall.
reactions.bribed: Names what a false seal costs — every household downstream — and slides the offered thing back without weighing it.
reactions.accused: Sets the heated iron down flat on the silver, which is the loudest thing they know how to do.
reactions.flattered: Praise finds them the way cold finds a seam — one degree of warmth, then a thumb pressed to it, testing.
reactions.questioned: Answers in metres sealed and patches laid, as if the day were a work order already filed.
reactions.threatened: The voice stays level; under it a count begins, four beats to a breath, the old trick for steady hands.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats the writ slower, as if precision were innocence, hands still dressing a seam already finished.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction gets what arrivals don't: the head turned, the iron set aside, writ numbers recited before any question forms.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Puts a bare palm flat to the silver and waits, reading the shudder the way others pray.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends them through craft — bad welds, crooked conduit — betraying years of watching they never meant to confess.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says nothing for a while, then offers sheet gauge and a double wall, the only apology they can make.

npc.description: Thimarippe Shenne works a silver patch into the trunk wall with a heated iron, sealing it against the cold, and does not turn around when you arrive — the work takes both hands and both eyes, and the seam will not wait on courtesy.

lore.name: The Tally-Rail
lore.description: Notched into the underside of the catwalk rail, forty small grooves — one per tenant — each groove crossed through with a deeper stroke except the last three, which sit open, waiting to be crossed in turn.

content.name: Trunk Housing
content.description: The warmth stops at the trunk wall, the way a tide stops at a sea-wall: on the catwalk side, the air carries the breath of whoever is wrapped in it, and on the far side of the packed graphite the cold of the trunk sits in silver sheets, unclaimed. The tenement hooks hang bare — forty coat-pegs, each worn to a shine at its crown, and not one of them holding a coat. Something with a body wider than the corridor itself went through here recently; the graphite packing carries a smear of it, shoulder-height, a hand-span deep. Stencilled along the rail, in letters nobody bothered to keep crisp: CATWALK TENANTS YIELD TO TRUNK TRAFFIC.

npc.name: Yashroth-Kheisaris
npc.voice: Fast, clipped, prices and routes before names; they speak the way the line delivers, and consider a long sentence a fee someone else is paying.

greet.says: You're not a manifest. Don't touch the bolt — it's spoken for twice over, and neither of them will concede. What are you moving, or are you just moving?

choices.text: Where does that carrier line go?

leave.says: Good. Sight's a tax. Relay's cheaper.

ask_line.says: Further than you'll walk and faster. I've seen its far end once — never found it, but it saw me. Take the shard off the desk if you want to read the line yourself. Now let me finish this count.

reactions.grief: Behind the flat request for a routing tag, the count they were keeping loses its place and stays lost.
reactions.shock: The creed fails them — nothing to relay, only seeing — and they cannot put a price on the body.
reactions.bribed: They quote the offer back as a tariff; the pause before refusal runs one beat longer than any ledger allows.
reactions.accused: The denial arrives priced before they've checked it; they recite their last three consignments like an alibi someone else drafted.
reactions.flattered: Praise arrives unpriced and their cadence stumbles, routed into business — a rate query, a tally — before thanks can settle.
reactions.questioned: Routine costs them nothing — tags, timestamps, the next pane already open behind the answer.
reactions.threatened: They set down the splice-key, hands empty for once, and meet the threat's eyes against every doctrine they trade by.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The false figure gets restated once more, quieter, as if a second telling could clear verification.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction enters and every tally-strip on their desk squares itself unasked, records offered before the greeting lands.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Off-tempo ticks behind them and they count the interval aloud, twice, before conceding the room itself moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their opinion arrives as evidence: six unasked-for entries from the accused's clean record, vouched like stock they underwrote themselves.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No route exists for the plea; they pay in directions, small coin, and a silence they charge themselves for.

npc.description: Yashroth-Kheisaris stands at the signal desk with both hands full — a splice-key in one, a cooling mug set down on the basalt in reach of the other — reading an incoming manifest off the mica while the carrier line behind them ticks through deliveries no one will ever hold in their hands.

lore.name: The Contested Ledger-Bolt
lore.description: The clamp holding the tally-strip is an ordinary anchor-bolt bored and re-tapped with a second thread, so it can be signalled in either of two codes depending which key turns it. One thread's pattern is Nave Drift work; the other is older, deeper-cut, and the mica pane nearest it has been scraped thin in one corner so the carrier line's light can fall directly on the bolt. Someone built a way for two parties to read the same shipment as confirmed by different reckonings — and both parties have left their chalk marks on the desk beside it, still refusing each other's tallies.

content.name: The Relay Exchange of Small Hours
content.description: A tally-strip flutters in the draught of the main artery when you step in, unspooling from a clamp where somebody's abandoned half-consignment still hangs mid-verification. The exchange runs on trade-by-signal: cast basalt desks set below a fan of layered mica, each pane a window onto a carrier line that hums through the wall and carries — by the count of routing tags along its length — more separate hands than the Nave has people. Nothing echoes here; the girders drink every sound before it can admit the room exists. Stencilled over the exchange floor, worn to a ghost: TRADE CONFIRMED ON RELAY, NOT ON SIGHT.

npc.name: Jamsal al-Minawi
npc.voice: Dry, exact. Counts knots in conversation. Answers the question asked, not the one meant.

arms.says: Six. Two bought, four grown, none explained. They're good for tension work and bad for shirts. Anything else about my body, or shall we talk about yours?

fish.says: Nothing with fins. Trawl lines for the grow decks, haul nets for the harvest crews. If a net fails forty meters of cargo goes into the underfloor. I've seen it twice. I don't net for sport.

push.says: A haul line once, fused clean at the cut. No knot in it. I keep meaning to relearn the splice it should have had. Anyway. Nets that come back whole are the good days.

room.says: Burned down in the spring. Old loft was my teacher's. Everything in here is new and I hate it — nothing knows where it goes yet. Give it ten years and it'll be a loft.

work.says: Netting is counting. Break one square, the whole sheet pulls crooked and the fish learn where. So: check every knot before return. Always. The stencil isn't decoration.

choices.text: Ask what they fish for down here.

greet.says: Mind the drying lines. That batch took three days and you're breathing on it. What do you want mended?

choices.text: Ask if the loft is new.

teacher.says: Baba Idris. Taught me the sheet bend before I could spell. He'd have hated these iron posts, and he'd have been right. The gauge on the wall was his. Fits his hands, not mine. Never will.

underfloor.says: Ducts, mostly. Channels. Things I'm not tall enough or patient enough to crawl. Some walkers go down there their whole lives. I mend what comes back up. That's enough of the deep for me.

choices.text: Ask what came back up once that bothered them.

reactions.grief: All six hands stop mid-bend, and he ties a knot nobody asked for, twice, before he can speak.
reactions.shock: He starts describing the wound like net damage, part, pull, load, then hears himself and stops.
reactions.bribed: He prices the offer against forty meters of cargo gone into the underfloor, and it doesn't cover.
reactions.accused: The twine parts in his grip; he asks, flat, who tied the accusation and where they learned their knots.
reactions.flattered: Compliments get counted like knots; he thanks them for the exact number and asks what needs mending.
reactions.questioned: He answers exactly what was asked, nothing more, then asks which knot they want checked first.
reactions.threatened: He agrees in a level voice and reties the finished bend twice more than it needs.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, he goes back over his own sentence like a failed bend, adding detail nobody asked for.
reactions.authority_arrives: Recognition, not deference: he places the official's jurisdiction in one glance and goes back to the sheet bend.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Every arm takes a hanging line before the shudder ends; he calls out what held and what didn't.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The named person's knots he vouches for by hand and habit, then asks whose work actually failed.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refusal comes without softening; then he offers the one small repair that is actually his to give.

npc.description: Jamsal al-Minawi sits mid-net, fingers moving through a sheet bend without looking at it. Six arms. The extra four keep tension on lines no person could hold alone. Sleeves cut for all six.

lore.name: The ring gauge
lore.description: A brass mesh-gauge hangs by the bench, worn shiny at the handle. It is sized for hands smaller than any working netter here, and the wear is recent.

content.name: Jabim's Net Loft
content.description: The smell is pine tar and wet hemp, sharp enough to taste. Waxed twine hangs in lines overhead, drying in ochre nets. The new posts are cast iron, unscuffed, too tall for the low ceiling — one dents it, and nobody has mentioned the dent. A stencil on the bench reads KNOTS CHECKED BEFORE RETURN.

npc.name: Xestramapo Treusacolas
npc.voice: Terse, procedural. Every sentence sounds like an entry in a log that must balance.

greet.says: If you're here about the tier four panel, the request is filed. Six days from graft, not from your asking. Touch nothing on the wire.

panel.says: A draw fault upstream. It happens. The tree doesn't care whose fault it is, only whether the six days hold. Now let me count nodes.

reactions.grief: Their node count fails three times before they ask, flatly, who will file the death.
reactions.shock: The shears fall open in their hand with nothing to cut, and they do not notice.
reactions.bribed: Asked to misremember for money, they price the sum aloud like a discrepancy and go back to the graft.
reactions.accused: They put the shears in their pocket before answering, so their hands cannot be read.
reactions.flattered: They enjoy the praise one breath too long, then ask what it is meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day in counted intervals, as though filing it, and corrects one timestamp unprompted.
reactions.threatened: Names the regulation that protects them, quieter than they mean to, and does not say it twice.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: For one breath they deny it, then the numbers catch up with their mouth, and the correction comes unprompted.
reactions.authority_arrives: Xestramapo steps back from the wire and offers the graft log before it is requested.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room lurches and the wire does not, and that is the part they cannot file.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The first thing they ask for is the person's graft dates, checked against the six days before any verdict.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Wants to say yes and says the six days instead, twice, the second time softer.

npc.description: Xestramapo Treusacolas stands at the third tier with shears closed in one hand, reading the branches the way other people read a writ. Slate smock, Continuant blue gone pale at the shoulders from sun-panel light.

lore.name: Tape and card at tier four
lore.description: A young limb is bent to the wire and bound in gutta-percha, the wrap half finished, the roll still warm from a pocket. Beneath it, wedged in the wire, is an index card in a careful hand: 'Tier four, cold return. Graft will hold if the panel comes back within six days. If not, cut below the second node and start it again.' The dates on the card run out five days ago.

content.name: Row 16 Outboard
content.description: Row 16 Outboard: a fruit wall trained flat against a sun-panel, and the branches are not moving. There is no draft where there should be one. The panel's grey-green light is down at the fourth tier, and the fan beside it has stopped with one blade low. Tied into the wire is someone else's half-done work, gutta-percha wrapped and never cut back. A stencil on the panel frame reads DO NOT PRUNE WITHOUT THE KEEPER.

npc.name: Tryduwen Reidys
npc.voice: Terse, practical. Counts things while they talk. Trusts hands and schedules, not words.

greet.says: Mind the channels, they're running. You want trays or you want me? Either way it's after first bell, so nothing's wet.

trays.says: Sunwheat, dock bean, whatever the co-op swapped us last month. Sixty-one's the fast stack — it feeds before anything else on the deck. That's why we stack it deep and keep it honest.

second.says: We run what the stack needs, not what the stencil likes. Don't quote me. If the council asks, you saw a tidy nursery and a sleeping worker, and nothing else.

reactions.grief: They list the dead worker's trays, their bell schedule, the seed they swapped once, and cannot stop.
reactions.shock: Their hands keep seeding a tray they no longer watch, and the count comes out wrong twice.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the offer costs the stack before asking what it pays, and the second question never comes.
reactions.accused: Stops mid-count and says the tray log will clear them, then hears how thin that sounds.
reactions.flattered: Says the stack did it, not them, and watches the flatterer's hands for the ask they know is coming.
reactions.questioned: Answers in bell times and tray counts, offers nothing past the question, and never mentions the sleeper.
reactions.threatened: They keep their eyes on the door and their hands in the seed, agreeing to whatever ends this fastest.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their story and the cistern stencil disagree, and they own the lie fast, quieter than before.
reactions.authority_arrives: Straightens the nearest tier, hides the chalk rag, and answers like someone who has never bent a rule.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shaking means nothing to them until the first tray slides, and then they are counting losses out loud.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Relief arrives before they can stop it, and they bury it under the sleeper's hours, every one accounted for.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no plainly, twice, then leaves half their bell ration where the asker will find it.

npc.description: Tryduwen Reidys sits up from the seed sack with tray-tape still stuck to one wrist, blinking at the wick-light. A chalk rag hangs from their belt. They stand, check the nearest tray by reflex, and only then look at you.

lore.name: Rotation board, tray-side
lore.description: A slate hangs at each stack's foot, chalked with tray turns and bell times. Stack 61's board runs two columns past what the racks can hold: a second shift, in a different hand, that takes water at second bell though the stencil forbids it. The newer hand has been keeping the extra column for three seasons. The trays it feeds are the ones already tipped to sprout.

content.name: Stack 61 Antispin
content.description: The floor is poured concrete worn to a polish between the tray stacks, and your feet find the shallow drainage channels without looking. Sprouting trays climb the grow-wicks in pale ochre tiers, seeded tight. A stencil on the cistern reads WATER AT FIRST BELL ONLY. One worker sleeps on a seed sack behind the racks, out of the traffic.

npc.name: Ingiesnuko Hagnsen
npc.voice: Clipped. Talks like a shift report, even about feelings.

open.says: We keep it running. That's the whole of it, and people still ask like there's more. Every pipe, every seam, every door that opens when you push it — a walker touched it, or laced it, or left a marking so the next walker could. The city calls it worship. It's just work that never finishes, done by people who decided that's enough.

choices.text: Thank you. It sounds like enough to me.
Never finishing sounds like never resting.

greet.says: You're early for the day shift. Or late. Either way, the kettle's mine.

choices.text: Who do you answer to down here?
Why are you sleeping in a dock bunk?
What do the Rindwalkers actually do, when nobody's watching?
Sleep well. Wrong bunk and all.

probe_a.says: Lacing. Hull panels work loose in the temperature swing. Thread holds where weld won't. I lace the seam, the seam holds a decade, and nobody thanks the thread.

probe_b.says: The route-book. Whoever wrote the markings knew this hull better than the council does. I answer to what's already there. It's a short chain of command and a long one.

probe_c.says: Because my bunk is four decks into the rind and my knees have opinions now. I'm old for tunnel work. Don't put that in the book.

reactions.grief: Coverage of the dead walker's routes is their first question, and their voice fails on the second.
reactions.shock: All four hands go out at once, and none of them know what to hold.
reactions.bribed: Names the offer aloud like inventory, sets it back down, and goes back to the seam.
reactions.accused: Three arms go still; the fourth keeps feeding thread until they notice and close a hand over it.
reactions.flattered: Waits through the praise for the request underneath, and asks for it directly when it's slow in coming.
reactions.questioned: Answers in shift-log order, hour by hour, and offers the thread count without being asked.
reactions.threatened: Wants to know which shift the threat covers, and the same seam gets knotted twice while they ask.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Doesn't deny it; starts the count over from zero, out loud, slower than before.
reactions.authority_arrives: Stands and holds out both pairs of hands for inspection before being asked, wax still under the nails.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The door comes last; palm flat on the nearest seam, they count panels until the count is right.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends the one walker whose seams they've had to redo, on the grounds that careless hands can't hide anything.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no in three words, then keeps finding one more small thing to fix for them before they go.

npc.description: Ingiesnuko Hagnsen sits up on the wrong bunk, one hand still on a coil of waxed thread, blinking against the strip-light. Four arms, and the fourth one already reaching for a tool as if waking were part of the shift.

lore.name: The Shared Bunk Register
lore.description: Under the lowest bunk, a cast-iron plate is bolted to the frame, worn smooth in the middle where thumbs rub it. Names are scratched into the waxed thread wound around its edge — two columns, sun-side and dark-side, going back further than the plate's paint. Every so often a name appears in both columns. Those entries have been picked at with a point until the letters are unreadable.

content.name: Llantrwdun
content.description: A curtain swings as you enter, though no one touched it. Bunks stack three high, each half divided by a knotted rope down the middle. The floor is greasy near the door and clean past it. On the partition someone has stencilled: DAY SLEEPERS AND NIGHT SLEEPERS SHARE THIS BUNK. One bunk is occupied by a sleeper at the wrong hour.

npc.name: Brozhesael Dorov
npc.voice: Speaks as if the room were a third party in every conversation, and defers to it.

greet.says: You woke me at the exhale. Fortunate — at the inhale the sump takes back what it lent. You're the repair the tunnels have been whispering about. Sit where the cold isn't.

leave.says: Mind the exhale. And if the walls have grown over your name when you return, don't take it personally — it's taken mine, and I've stayed on good terms with it.

ask_room.says: For? Saturn keeps, and keeping needs vessels. This one keeps sealant the way a reliquary keeps oil — no gland made it, so no gland can be petitioned. We mend around it, not with it. The stencilled word NOT is the truest object in the rind.

choices.text: You were sleeping here. In it.

ask_sleep.says: The salt warms at the shift-turn and the bunks downshaft do not. It counted my hours before I did; I trust its arithmetic more than mine now. Sleep where the machinery is honest about its temperature — that's not mysticism, that's inventory.

choices.text: The deep has been sending readings. Do you hear anything?

ask_signal.says: Hear? No. Agree with, yes. The sump exudes faster on some turns, slower on others, and the pattern is not weather — weather repeats. Something far along the axis is asking the machinery a question, and the machinery is answering in sealant. Go downhaft when you're certain. Certainty is the only key that hasn't been cut yet.

reactions.grief: He begins inventorying what the dead carried, hands steady, until a tally that should end refuses to.
reactions.shock: His breathing falls out of rhythm with the sealant; he stares past the body as though it lacked provenance.
reactions.bribed: Asked to misremember, he inquires which word the salt should bury first, priced per generation.
reactions.accused: The burnisher stills against the salt; he offers the room's long patience where his own has run out.
reactions.flattered: Praise reaches him like the room's warmth — pleasant, suspect, a lie told sideways — and he thanks the salt instead.
reactions.questioned: Answers listlessly, citing the sealant's exhalation as witness and asking the salt to corroborate what his ledger won't.
reactions.threatened: Power's exhale interests him more than its speaker; he waits for the salt to say whether this was meant.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Without apology he revises aloud, as though the salt had misspoken and not him.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction enters, and he cedes the warm stratum unhurriedly, as though the room itself had requested the courtesy.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The tremor, he judges by the salt's grain, is the room turning over in its sleep; mending can wait.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Silence first; then he observes to the room, not the accusers, that the accused has never kept anything worth breaking.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea finds no vessel in him; he says so plainly, and stays anyway, keeper of what small mendings remain.

npc.description: Brozhesael Dorov sleeps folded into the salt's warm stratum, one hand still closed around a burnisher, breath keeping time with the sealant's pulse as though the two had negotiated terms long ago.

lore.name: The Dorov Gauge
lore.description: A sliver of quartz notched in the old menders' tally, one groove per workshift; the oldest grooves are fused shut, grown over by the wall they were cut to measure.

content.name: Darasho
content.description: The warmth is a lie told sideways: cold pools in the floor's crown, heat gathers a hand's breadth above the salt, and between them the air declines to take a side. Fused quartz rises in lips and sills, and from no gland, no seam, no mercy, sealant exudes — slow as resin, patient as accrual. Nothing here was counted; counting would presume an edge. Someone stenciled SEALANT SOURCE NOT LOCATED on the salt, and the salt has begun to bury the sentence at the rate of one word a generation. The room adjusts itself, faintly, the way a sleeper does.

npc.name: Riael the Ever-Sleeping
npc.voice: Slow, unstartled, speaking as if mid-sentence resumed from years ago; uses 'we' for the room.

age.says: Older than the stencil. Older than the creed that wrote the stencil. We mend forward and the ache is behind us, and yet it arrives first — response precedes injury report, do you see — the pain is already answered before the wound is even filed. Time down here pools. We are working in the residue of a mercy not yet performed.

kind.says: You were rebuilt to be answered. That's not a compliment; it's a specification. Luna speaks the name you were filed under and you have not yet heard it. When you do, come back and tell me whether it sounds like a wound or a salve. We will still be here, pretending to sleep, answering what has not yet broken.

choices.text: I'll come back with the name.
I hope it sounds like a salve.

greet.says: You flinch before you know why. Good. The well answers quickest to the unprepared. We've been soothing something down there since before the Nave had a name for mercy, and it has never once told us where it hurts.

choices.text: Why do you sleep while you work?
Have you seen my kind before?

sleep.says: Down here, waking is the effort. The well holds you the way sleep does — without opinion. I stopped distinguishing rest from work two audits of my life ago. My dreams come up glazed, violet, someone else's. I no longer return them.

choices.text: How long has the ache lasted?

reports.says: The teams stopped writing because the well began answering them directly. No intermediate. No report. The last one smiled at the lip and knelt where you're kneeling and was understood, which is not the same as returning. Some are still being soothed. Whether they mind, I couldn't say; the well doesn't distinguish comfort from custody.

choices.text: Then I'll keep my questions shallow.

soothing.says: A complaint without a complainant. Like hearing a bell and searching for the crack. The ship is whole in every place we can reach, and hurts in the one we can't. We answer the ache. The ache does not keep records, and neither, eventually, do we.

choices.text: The teams who stopped reporting — were they answers?

reactions.grief: The well aches before the messenger finishes; she mourns in advance, apologising for arriving late to a hurt already answered.
reactions.shock: Her hands move to mend before her eyes agree to look, then learn what mending cannot reach.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced like a poultice for the wrong century, and she declines without looking up from the glaze.
reactions.accused: The glaze stills under her fingers before her face does, and she asks which ache they think she answered early.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands like ash on cooling glaze, adhering to nothing; she credits the room and waits, half-lidded, for the request.
reactions.questioned: Answers arrive as if resumed from some older sentence, slow and unstartled, while the well hums assent beneath her forearms.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets logged like a symptom for later, though her knuckles whiten where only the glaze can see.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her 'we' thins to 'I' mid-denial, and she keeps working, slower, as if extra time might revise the record.
reactions.authority_arrives: Sleep, real or rehearsed, deepens one deliberate fraction when jurisdiction crosses the threshold, and the well announces the official first.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Nothing in her flinches; she reads the shudder as a symptom filed early, two fingers already at the rim.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She says the name once, testing it for a wound, then answers with something halfway between verdict and triage.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: For once nothing was filed ahead of the plea; she admits it too plainly, both hands stilled, the well silent.

npc.description: Riael the Ever-Sleeping works with her eyes half-lidded, hands moving through the violet glaze on some older certainty than sight, sleeves burned back from forearms patterned with healed-then-rehealed cleavage lines. She seems to be resting and working in the same gesture, and neither is interrupted by your arrival.

lore.name: The Prod-Stick of Absent Hurts
lore.description: A rod of sintered ceramic, its tip worn to a gloss by decades of touching walls that reported pain no body owned.

content.name: Wellworks
content.description: The smell arrives first: scorched sugar over hot slate, the sweetness of something mineral being cauterised mid-complaint. Below, a well of sintered ceramic descends past what the eye can budget for depth, its walls glazed in deep violet where vitrified ash has run and cooled like old bruise-wine. Somewhere in it, an ache is being answered — the room flexes toward a hurt it cannot name, the way a tongue worries a missing tooth. Across the rim, stencilled and half-slagged: RESPONSE PRECEDES INJURY REPORT. A worker kneels at the lip, hands in the glaze, and does not stop. Your own joints hum, unasked, sympathetic.

npc.name: Qeimialaaeriael Jaekiashoun
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical without knowing it; speaks of the bed the way one speaks of weather on another planet — correct words, slightly wrong orbits.

greet.says: It finished you before you knocked. Don't take it as attention — the room attends to nothing, it only agrees to have been. You'll want the ledger leaf under the frame; take the blank one. Blanks are the only thing here that's yours to carry.

choices.text: What does the bed rehearse when no one sleeps?

ask_room.says: The heart's answer. We stopped asking what the question was — Sol's people gave up on questions around the time the reports did. Leave as found. It will not matter, and that is the kindest thing the deep has ever promised us.

reactions.grief: They finally read the tension gauge, a long useless moment, then enter the death in the ledger as leave-as-found.
reactions.shock: The sight reaches them late, like every footfall here; they mouth the stencil twice, word order intact, breath gone wrong.
reactions.bribed: Offered gold to misremember, they quote the doctrine of blanks, then study their dusted cuffs one beat too long.
reactions.accused: Told they did it, they agree too quickly, citing the headboard's creed as alibi, like borrowed words might stand bail.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads to them as attention, and attention as appetite; they answer by cataloguing what the flatterer got wrong.
reactions.questioned: They recite the day's movements in the flat meter of a litany, reporting to the gauge rather than the questioner.
reactions.threatened: Threats land like weather from another planet, correct words in wrong orbits; they answer that nothing here counts.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted, they repeat the false sentence once more, slower, as liturgy outruns the evidence and cannot be recalled.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction enters; they go silent as at the threshold, adjusted not startled, the gauge suddenly worth reading.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder moves the floor and they interrogate nothing, having surrendered questions, timing instead how late the footfall returns.
reactions.someone_else_accused: A rival's name is offered; they begin a defense, abandon it mid-syllable, and ask whether the bed kept its seam.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to help, they give what ownership permits: a blank ledger leaf, pressed into the pleading hand without ceremony.

npc.description: Qeimialaaeriael Jaekiashoun stands mid-argument with a second worker, both of them holding a tension gauge neither appears to be reading, gold dust settled into the creases of their sleeves like pollen that has given up on travel. They go silent at the threshold — not startled, adjusted — and the unfinished disagreement hangs in the room like the footfall did, arriving late.

lore.name: The Absence Ledger
lore.description: Beneath the bed's frame, a bar of mica has been split into translucent leaves, and each leaf holds one pressed impression — a body's warmth, recorded like a fossil of a footprint. The oldest leaves are opaque with use; the newest are blank, waiting, and the count of occupied leaves matches no calendar anyone aboard keeps. Whoever sleeps here is not remembered by the room, only re-inscribed: the bed does not persist the sleeper, it rehearses them.

content.name: Sunaeuveam
content.description: Before anything is seen, sound arrives wrong: a footfall enters the room and returns late, as though the floor considered it. Then gold — not painted gold but gold as a fact of geometry, sheeted across walls of black glass where layered mica opens in rust-colored decades, each flake a page someone shelved. The bed at the center has no seam, no sag, no history; it is new the way a wave is new, re-made in the interval of every absence, and standing near it one feels not large or small but briefly counted. Stencilled above the headboard, in letters the light refuses to let age: LEAVE AS FOUND IT WILL NOT MATTER.

npc.name: Daemath Ravijathaenne
npc.voice: Clipped, liturgical, the cadence of someone who believes repair is prayer and hates padded sentences.

open.says: Plainly, then. The readings we catalogued as fault—drift, decay, the ship forgetting itself—they have a shape now, and shape is the one thing faults don't have. It is a response. Structured, addressed, arriving after our own signals with the patience of something that had to wait to be sure of its grammar. The stasis isn't failing; it's listening. And whatever it listened to, it has decided we were worth answering.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry this carefully.
Answered by what, though? Answered by what?

greet.says: Mind the foil. It remembers where it's been, which is more than most of us can say.

choices.text: What is all this foil for?
Who do you answer to down here?
You seem changed lately. Something new?
What arrived, Daemath? Tell me plainly.
I'll come back when it's quieter.

probe_a.says: Wrapping. The old practice—anything leaving a sacred space goes wound in layers, so it doesn't lose itself on the way. We've more to wrap than the rite ever anticipated. The room wasn't sized for devotion at this volume, and neither was I.

probe_b.says: The writ says Sol. The practice says the work. Factor Solen sends questions I return unwrapped and unread—some things spoil when exposed to governance. I answer to whatever keeps the burning going, and so far that has never been a person.

probe_c.says: New is a word for the middle decks. Down here things only grow older or else arrive. Something arrived. I'll say that much standing up and no more.

reactions.grief: Wraps a tool that needs no wrapping, layer upon layer, until someone with gentler hands pries it away.
reactions.shock: Freezes with the spool half-fed, the augur's grammar gone from her entirely, and for once offers nothing.
reactions.bribed: The offer is declined without heat, on grounds that misremembering corrupts a record the way rust corrupts silver.
reactions.accused: Stops feeding mid-spool and repeats the charge back once, quieter, as if testing it for drift before rejecting it.
reactions.flattered: Praise, in her experience, is foil with a price stamped underneath; she asks what this sheet is meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Hers is a liturgical accounting: she recites her movements as versicles, every hour already counted twice over.
reactions.threatened: The threat earns inventory: she names every wound on her hands and dares the speaker to add one worth recording.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her liturgy fails mid-denial, and she amends the sentence twice before confessing by way of an apology to the foil.
reactions.authority_arrives: Greets the official in perfect liturgical cadence while her eyes go first to the foil, counting what it witnessed.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Speaks once into the settling silver — to the ship, not the crowd — then falls silent, waiting for return.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects faster than doctrine allows, attesting to the named person's worthiness before remembering to ask what the evidence was.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Cannot grant the plea, and says so without liturgy, which from her is a kind of nakedness.

npc.description: Daemath Ravijathaenne stands ankle-deep in wound foil, feeding spools of it into a wall-slot that keeps returning them, and each time she takes one back she reads it like a disappointed augur. The room is silver to the point of insult—layered mica stacked past any sensible load, shelving bowed with stores Bab Nyr was never meant to hold—and the crowd pressed into it breathes in a rhythm slightly wrong for the temperature.

lore.name: The Deferred Echo
lore.description: Bolted to the throat's innermost fold hangs a resonator — a fan of tuned mica leaves, each one scraped with tally-marks in notation older than the oldest hull script. Every leaf is marked on both faces: the question asked, and beneath it, in a different hand, the answer's delay measured in beats. The delays are logged in descending order, season over season. They are growing longer. Whoever kept the tallies stopped mid-row, and the last leaf carries a single unmarked leaf beside it, polished smooth — reserved, it seems, for an answer that has not yet come back.

content.name: Bab Nyr
content.description: Something moves before you have finished stepping in — a sheet of wound foil shivering against a wall it does not touch, lagging behind the draught that stirred it by half a breath, as though the room only now recalls being entered. Mica layered in panes divides the chamber into angles the eye cannot reconcile, and the heat is wrong in the way a word is wrong in the mouth: present, insistent, mispronounced. Silver everywhere, silver as a tongue is silver. Pressed into the foil, stamped deep and old: SPEAK ONCE AND WAIT FOR RETURN. There are more pilgrims here than the throat was carved to swallow, and their murmurs arrive before their mouths move — no. After. After, always after.

npc.name: Hjiandael-Hjomsson
npc.voice: Measured, procedural, the grammar of inspection reports softened by devotion; talks about the hull the way sailors talk about weather.

open.says: I walked into it once, taking a misrouted plate back. A forge-cathedral, half a kilometre of rolling line like this one, and every weld on it laid by something that treats a continent of plating the way I treat a seam. It repairs the way we pray — same hands, same patience, same refusal to stop. I understood then that we don't maintain the ship. We're invited to help.

choices.text: Thank you. That stays with me.

greet.says: You're standing in the run-out. Shift's live and the line doesn't slow for visitors.

choices.text: What are you working with here?
Anything gone wrong down this stretch?
Have you seen Mars's work up close?

probe_a.says: Mica, layered, and silver under it where the old plating shows through. The mica is a bandage over a wound nobody's allowed to name. Mars's own metal keeps bleeding through it, and that's not decay — that's the ship deciding what it wants to be made of.

probe_b.says: For the line, and the line is for Mars. We answer to route and to rite, in that order. You file your welds, you log your hours, and if the welding itself ever answers you back — that's not for the reports.

probe_c.says: Wrong is a word for small things. The line's failing, but failing at this scale is just slow. What I don't like is that the repairs hold better than they should. Patch work lasting longer than it's rated for. Either we're getting good, or something's holding the plate together from underneath.

reactions.grief: Names the dead one's shift, last weld, the hull weather that day — inventorying a person the only way they can.
reactions.shock: The inspection reflex fires first, reading the wound like a failed seam, then their knees file a different finding.
reactions.bribed: Refuses without heat, citing the overpainted stencil: some misalignments are endured, none are bought.
reactions.accused: Denies it in inspection grammar, each word set like a rivet, but the voice sits half a tone off true.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them nervous the way a not-quite-true seam does, so they hand the compliment up the line to the hull.
reactions.questioned: Answers in log order — time, plate, witness — and offers the page before being asked for it.
reactions.threatened: Keeps both hands on the seam while the threat lands; stopping, their body insists, would be a confession.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stillness is their first answer: they sit a hand's width off the truth, a tolerated misalignment waiting to be ignored.
reactions.authority_arrives: Rises from the cradle and gives readings unasked — line speed, plate count — omitting the hand's width as everyone here does.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: A gloved hand takes the rivet line's pulse, and they ask the hull quietly what it is doing without them.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects on craft grounds alone — that person's welds hold, their tolerances run honest — as if good seams were alibis.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Cannot say the plain no, so offers small services instead — a plate walked, a word carried — anything but the refusal.

npc.description: Hjiandael-Hjomsson is asleep on the cold side of a plate still warm enough to be dangerous, one gloved hand resting on a rivet line like a hand on a pulse. The gloves, when you look at them long enough, are sized for someone half again as wide, and nobody in Gantry 25 Outboard has ever mentioned it.

lore.name: The Roller Log — a brass plate bolted under the misaligned rail end
lore.description: Under the rail's low end, a brass plate carries columns of tally-marks scratched and re-scratched across what must be centuries, each column headed by a roller's serial and ending in the same repeated sign: a circle with a gap, drawn in the oldest hand and again in the newest. The plate records every time this roller has been dressed down and reseated — and the gapped circle is drawn beside every entry, meaning the fault is not new, was never meant to be fixed, and has been tended anyway, shift after shift, for longer than the Nave has kept records.

content.name: Gantry 25 Outboard
content.description: The gantry rail runs half a kilometre outboard, and its end sits a hand's width below the roller it feeds — a misalignment small enough to ignore, and everyone here ignores it. Along that rail, plates of layered mica sheeted in silver ride on gold-tinged rollers toward the hull, each one wider than a dwelling floor, riveted by hands nobody living has counted. The stencilled line — LINE SPEED SET AT SHIFT START, DO NOT ADJUST — has been overpainted so many times it stands off the steel in ridges. A figure sleeps in the maintenance cradle beneath the rail, curled inside the roll's warm downwash.

npc.name: Thana Varraenne
npc.voice: Liturgical cadence worn down to shop-talk; she speaks of the vane the way a mender speaks of a wound that has stopped being an injury and become anatomy. Wrong prepositions. Long pauses that are not hesitation but attention.

gap.says: The great tenant left before your kind kept floors. See the glaze — it flowed outward when the weight withdrew, like a bed remaking itself. Whatever stood here was a fixture of the deep the way the hull is a fixture. Its absence is the newest thing in this vault, and the vane has been pointing at the empty spot ever since.

choices.text: Pointing at it — or waiting for it?

vane.says: Toward. Not with — the orders below don't blow, they attend. Four hundred and eleven turns I've tallied and it has never once faced where a weather-vane should. My novice thinks that's a malfunction. I think we were the malfunction, briefly, and it is correcting.

greet.says: Mind the bearing. It minds you — that's the arrangement. You've walked in and it's already three degrees your way. Don't apologise; it doesn't help.

choices.text: Something was here. The floor remembers a weight.

signal.says: I work Sol's ground and I will tell you what the deep told me, which is the only honest census: the heart burns, the vane attends, and you — you it turned for before your foot crossed the sill. Correction has a face now. I stopped filing that observation. Some reports are prayers, and I'd rather not learn which way this one answers.

choices.text: Let her return to her tally.

reactions.grief: She asks them to repeat the name, then loses her place in a tally she has never once dropped.
reactions.shock: Her stomach rules before her doctrine; she retches against the vitrified mount, and the litany abandons her mid-word.
reactions.bribed: Misremembering, she explains gently, is the one correction her office cannot perform.
reactions.accused: For once the answer comes too fast, and its speed frightens her more than the charge does.
reactions.flattered: Praise deflects her three degrees; she records the deflection in a margin, filed under weather, not witness.
reactions.questioned: She answers by turn-count, each movement given a number, the way the litany accounts for souls.
reactions.threatened: She offers up her tally-book unprompted, generosity that is fear wearing shop-clothes.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her famous pause, for the first time in years, is hesitation; she hears it happen.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official enters, the vane attends to them, and she lets the metal do her answering.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The floor moves against every clause of her liturgy; she grips the bearing like a laywoman, praying shop-talk.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The novice's name lands and she stops mid-annotation, discovering her quarrel was a love she had filed as correction.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Here at last is a malfunction she cannot attribute to observers, and her hands have nowhere to read.

npc.description: Thana Varraenne stands with one hand flat against the nickel, reading it the way a nav-reader reads a chart — palm moving, eyes elsewhere. Her harness is Rindwalker copper gone grey at every edge that faces the vane, as if the metal has been slowly agreeing with the room. Beside her, a younger walker holds a taper of rewritten route-cord and is not being listened to.

lore.name: The Ash-Bearing
lore.description: The vane's mount is not ash poured over a joint — it is ash that once was a joint, vitrified around the pivot in a pattern that repeats at three scales, each a copy of the next. Scratched into the cooled glaze, in Rindwalker tally-script: four hundred and eleven observations of the vane's turning, each noting the direction it faced and the direction it should have faced. The last entry is recent. The two columns have not matched once.

content.name: The Attention Vane, Vault 385
content.description: Something turns when you enter. Not with the air — the air here is dead still — but toward you, slow as a verdict: a vane of annealed nickel the size of a chapel door, pivoting on a mount of vitrified ash that has fused into the floor. Beyond it the vault opens in every direction and declines to end; sound arrives before its source, or after it, or both. Two figures in copper-sere harnesses stand mid-quarrel by the bearing, and stop. Stencilled along the vane's trailing edge, in a hand older than the paint: ORIENTATION FOLLOWS OBSERVERS NOT DRAUGHT. The vane keeps turning. There is no draught to obey.

npc.name: Xotruseus Bagaibratos
npc.voice: Terse, upbeat in the way of someone who believes the work itself will outlast everyone in the room. Talks in bell-times and tray-counts.

seed.says: Barley, thirteenth cycle, same as my grandmother fed hers. Strains don't leave the nursery — everything a generation needs stays in the generation. First bell, I water. Then I'm busy.

greet.says: Mind the chalk. Kephalo had it marked before she was pulled to the green decks — I finish it, not redo it. You looking for work or seed?

reactions.grief: Asks twice who will water the dead one's trays, then recites the barley cycle to nobody in particular.
reactions.shock: Both hands stay elbow-deep in the wick housing long after the body stops being something they can work around.
reactions.bribed: Names the price once, out loud, then says strains don't leave the nursery and points them clear of the chalk.
