reactions.accused: Stops with the filament halfway home and repeats the tray-count, louder the second time, as though volume were proof.
reactions.flattered: Goes pink at the praise, then covers it by asking whether the visitor has ever seen wick grease set.
reactions.questioned: Answers in bell-times, first bell to last, then goes back to the filament without waiting to be dismissed.
reactions.threatened: Recites the watering hour and the barley strain, voice even, though their thumb leaves prints in the wick grease.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The corrected bell comes out before the question ends, ears going red above the rag as they recant twice.
reactions.authority_arrives: Sets the rag aside and has the day's tray-count ready before the official crosses the threshold.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They count the cups twice before trusting the number, then stand listening for a bell that doesn't come.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Chalk still under the nails, they say the named one's hands were never strong enough to pull that frame.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no with the door still open and the plea standing in it, then waters the seedlings early, just once.

npc.description: Xotruseus Bagaibratos crouches in the opened half of the rack, elbow-deep in the wick housing, sliding a new filament into its porcelain seat by feel. A rag is tied over one ear against the wick grease. The abandoned half-finished frame belongs to somebody else — the chalk hand isn't theirs — and they work around it without touching it.

lore.name: The Tray Ledger Frame
lore.description: The rack's side panel is a repurposed ledger board, its printed rows half-sanded and overwritten in chalk, generation under generation. The oldest legible entry, three hands back, records a barley strain by a name nobody uses anymore — and a note: 'gave half to Drift stall, got it back next season, thinner.' Continuants don't loan seed. Someone did, once, and kept the proof.

content.name: Xyldeipeiso's Sprout Tray
content.description: The smell hits first: wet split-pea mash and the green tang of new barley, sweetened by whatever the wicks burn. Half the tray rack lies opened, trays pulled and stacked like dishes, a spill of chalk lines marking where the frame is supposed to go back together. Stenciled on the stand: WATER AT FIRST BELL ONLY. Porcelain cups — nursery issue, navy-rimmed — hold seedlings nobody has watered since before last bell.

npc.name: Zeeheaapael Raarileathloa
npc.voice: Terse, hospitable in the way of duty rather than welcome; talks about the hearth as a patient under care.

greet.says: You'll want warmth, then. Take the near bench — the far side is spoken for by the corridor, and we keep our bargains with it. Mind the gauge; it lies by a hair, but only ever downward.

ask_hearth.says: For the deck beyond, as it's been for nobody's lifetime. Venus keeps her gardens warm; we just keep the promise. Draw it down and the beds go cold by increments so slow nobody's blamed for it — that's the whole trick of failing. Now sit, or don't, but let me finish my rounds.

reactions.grief: A long silence, then far too much detail about how the dead always ran cold, the rounds abandoned mid-list.
reactions.shock: Hands go to the body's wrist out of trade habit — temperature first, identity later, the way rounds always run.
reactions.bribed: Refuses by reciting the stencil's own words back across the offer, as if painted letters outranked money.
reactions.accused: Goes still as banked coals, then offers the accuser a bench, hospitality arriving too late to convince anyone.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets tonight's readings in return, as though the fire earned the compliment and they only wrote it down.
reactions.questioned: Their account comes in gauge readings, each hour recited like a duty roster, offense finding no purchase.
reactions.threatened: The threat finds nothing to grip until it touches the hearth; everything else in them was surrendered long ago.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Does not deny it — amends the ledger entry in front of them as if the figure, not they, had lied.
reactions.authority_arrives: Wakes fully for the first time and stands, ledger squared, glancing at the stencil as if checking its testimony.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Somewhere below, the fire has shifted in its bed; the room's movement reads to them as a patient turning over.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Snaps that nobody who sleeps against a cold seam would waste warmth, and hears, too late, how much that admits.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Warmth beyond the bargain is not theirs to give, so they offer the near bench and cannot watch it accepted.

npc.description: Zeeheaapael Raarileathloa sleeps seated, back against the warm pier, a ledger of temperature readings open on their chest and rising with each breath. They wake without surprise, check the gauge first, and only then look at you — someone who has learned that in this room the fire outranks the visitors.

lore.name: The Draw-Down Gauge
lore.description: Beside the hearth stands a silver column with a dial whose scale runs to figures no corridor should need — the lowest marking counts warmth enough for ten thousand seats, the needle resting a hair above zero. Someone has scratched a new mark below the zero and dated it in three different hands, each later than the last: the floor of acceptable warmth, lowered and lowered again. Whatever this hearth was built to hold, they are now rationing its leftovers and calling that enough.

content.name: Warming Service
content.description: The floor is cast basalt laid in slabs a hand-span thick, and it carries warmth unevenly — hot as a kiln sill over the fire-trench, cold enough to feel the seams by three strides out, so your feet map the failing heart of the room before your eyes do. Silver ducting, untarnished after nobody knows how long, runs the gantries overhead toward a hearth you hear rather than see, banked low behind screens. A stencil across the nearest pier: HEARTH BANKED FOR CORRIDOR, DO NOT DRAW DOWN. Someone sleeps against its warmth anyway.

npc.name: Hotzatlatl-Qontzin
npc.voice: Fast, dry, allergic to ceremony. Talks in odds and route-talk; warms only when you ask the right question instead of the obvious one.

game.says: Kites off the rail, wagers on clearance, side-bets on tangle and fall. Everything moves — wire, cane, coin, reputations. A kite that never flies is just a debt with a tail.

choices.text: And the board takes its cut?

push.says: Mine. Every knot on this cord is a route I ran, and I'm unwinding them one bad payout at a time. When the cord's straight, the loft goes to whoever's next. Nothing holds. That's the whole creed, friend — you just have to choose what you spend it on.

choices.text: I'll leave you to the wire.

stay.says: Olo stayed longer. Ask him why sometime — he'll give you an answer and it won't be the one he gave me. Me, I've got a rail to clear before this loft comes down.

board.says: Sharp eyes. The board says what keeps the floor alive; the rail says what happened. Some nights those are different stories, and I decide which one gets told. That's not cheating. That's keeping the game breathing.

greet.says: Loft's closed. Not to you, obviously, since you're in it. State your business before the wire slips.

choices.text: The board and the rail notches don't agree.
You've been up here a long time for a Drifter.

reactions.grief: They start naming the dead one's routes and payout odds, twice through, before their voice runs out of numbers.
reactions.shock: The kite-frame slides off their knees to the floor, and they watch it lie there.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer like a side-bet, names it higher, and leaves the coin untouched on the betting board.
reactions.accused: They ask which knot on the wrist-cord the accusation hangs from, and the wire stops mid-loop.
reactions.flattered: They let the praise finish, wind one loose loop, then ask what it's meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Gives odds before the question finishes — two runs since dusk, both clean — and never looks up from the wire.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets a shrug; their thumb finds the wrist-cord and stays there.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The story gets rerun aloud with the corrected fact worked in, faster, like a losing hand shown early.
reactions.authority_arrives: Doesn't stand for the official; they angle the betting board's flaked face away and keep winding wire.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The sway puts them off the rail boards first, habit older than any question of why.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Olo, once, flat — then they defend the man's routes harder than his character, as if the odds were slandered.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They have nothing that answers the plea, so they untie one knot from the wrist-cord and give that.

npc.description: Hotzatlatl-Qontzin sits cross-legged by the stove, cane kite-frame across their knees, wire spooled around two fingers and threaded blind while they watch you instead of the work. Their wrist carries a knotted cord gone soft with handling, and they keep their weight off the rail side of the loft like they've learned which boards owe them nothing.

lore.name: The Rail Tally
lore.description: The rail itself is grooved with notches, hundreds of them, cut at the exact point each kite cleared — or didn't. The last forty notches stop matching the board's payouts: kites recorded as cleared that the notches say never made it. Someone has been paying out on losses, quietly, out of their own standing. The notches don't lie. The board does.

content.name: Kite-Loft 38
content.description: The cold sits at the rail where the wind comes through and nowhere else; the loft's little stove owns the rest. Pale green paint flakes off the betting board, and a stenciled strip above it reads BETS CLOSE WHEN THE KITE CLEARS THE RAIL. A man with wire in his lap turns around like he's been caught counting.

npc.name: Haaleiisuraatean Lingeartonga
npc.voice: Clipped and procedural at first, with the ward's habit of speaking in tallies; warms into something almost tender when the talk turns to who the beds are actually for.

decks.says: Once, to carry a requisition, and I'll tell you what nobody upstairs believes: the garden is not a place we keep. It let me walk a causeway the length of the Nave with green on both sides and no floor beneath it that I could see, and something down there noticed me the way weather notices you. The Seven are real. I heal their district and try not to be a rounding error.

greet.says: You're not on my roster, and neither am I, so we'll call it even. Mind the third rack — the mist runs colder there than the gauge says, and I'd rather not log a second scald today.

choices.text: This isn't your shift, is it.
Why does the hall fog itself? Who told it to?

shift.says: Orrin's shift. Orrin went down a shaft three months back with a maintenance team and the roster never came back either. I cover it because the fog doesn't know the difference, and if nobody logs the density, the green decks read this district as empty and throttle the air besides.

choices.text: The whole team? No word since?

missing.says: Factor Solen read what came up and filed it, which tells you what came up was worse than nothing. I've stopped expecting reports. I expect this hall to still be here in the morning, and so far the hall has been the reliable one.

choices.text: You've been down into Venus's actual decks, then.

reactions.grief: Stops mid-reading with the wand still lit over the bed and cannot remember what number her hand was keeping.
reactions.shock: Drops the gauge wand without hearing it land and counts breaths anyway over a chest that has stopped.
reactions.bribed: Refuses in the cadence of a density reading, as though remembrance were oxygen she had personally logged.
reactions.accused: Asks which rack the accusation was logged at, because in this ward nothing counts unless the gauge recorded it.
reactions.flattered: Hears the praise the way she hears a gauge run dry, and asks what the flatterer wants healed, and where.
reactions.questioned: Her account comes in rack numbers and mist readings, calm as a shift-board, before the question is even finished.
reactions.threatened: Stands very still under the threat, one thumb finding a scald-line on her forearm like an old tally.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Does not deny it, only re-reads the roster as if two borrowed names were a clerical matter.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes follow the official the way her gauge follows fog: from the edges, where authority gathers first.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The gauge never lies about a shudder, so she reads it twice and only then lets her shoulders come down.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says the name back once, flat, then asks whether the accuser has ever logged a single bed here.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers what the ward has: a name kept on the roster, a density logged, and hates how small that is.

npc.description: A stocky worker in a slate Continuant wrap moves down the overstacked beds with a gauge wand, logging mist density at each rack, and does not look up until the third bed. Their sleeves are rolled over forearms mapped with the pale scald-lines of someone who has misjudged the fog many times and stopped bothering with gloves. A ward roster hangs from their belt with two names clipped to it that belong, by the shift-board outside, to other people.

lore.name: The Census Drum
lore.description: Set into the cistern's base is a rotary counter of fused quartz, its silver digits worn shallow by contact with the counting wheel. It tallies the mist cycles against the number of bodies registered in the district, and the two figures have not matched in years — the cycle counter has run on ahead, as if fogging a population that stopped being counted. Someone has scribed a running correction table on the cistern's flank in Continuant blue, one line per quarter, each line shorter than the last.

content.name: Bulkhead 38 Outboard
content.description: The light arrives before anything else, bent through a fog that hangs where no pipe feeds it, refracting off a cistern of silver the width of a farm field and giving the whole hall the glow of a dimmed sun-strip seen from underwater. Fused quartz ribs arch overhead in spans no foundry on the floor could pour today, and beneath them the ward's beds, gurneys, and mist-trunks have been stacked three-deep past every marking the floor was stencilled with. Somewhere behind the cistern, painted over an older stencil: MIST CYCLE RUNS REGARDLESS OF CENSUS.

npc.name: Sunme Hamereda
npc.voice: Terse, exact, used to being obeyed about figures. Dues are not a topic, they are a fact.

wall.says: Seep came through the back seam. Council sent nobody, so I opened it myself. The dues still count the same with a wall missing. Everything here counts the same. That's the point of it.

greet.says: Office is half-closed. If you're paying, pay. If you're not, the stencil tells you when.

choices.text: Ask what happened to the wall.

reactions.grief: She recites the dead man's outstanding balance before she can stop herself, then says his name once, wrong.
reactions.shock: No numbers come; she counts the lamp's blinks instead, because the body will not resolve into figures.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer aloud before she can help it, then refuses it for being short, not for being wrong.
reactions.accused: She demands the exact sum they think she took, and her voice climbs a half-step on the number.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes her check the tally twice; she assumes an error before she assumes goodwill.
reactions.questioned: She finishes the figure before answering, then gives the count and nothing past it.
reactions.threatened: She writes the threat down like a debt, date and amount, and her hand is steady until the last stroke.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her chalk stops mid-stroke; she restates the false number slower, as if repetition were evidence.
reactions.authority_arrives: She watches the official cross the felt and does not stand; jurisdiction covers the room, not her column.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The lamp skips a blink; she holds the slate flat until the shaking stops, then checks whether her totals survived.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The delinquency roll is out before anyone asks; she has kept that man's failures to the day.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She has no line for mercy in the book; she says so, and writes the plea into the margin anyway.

npc.description: Sunme Hamereda sits behind the felt half with a tally slate, sleeves pinned back. A mug of something gone cold stands within reach. She does not look up until she has finished the number she is on.

lore.name: The Split Ledger
lore.description: The dues ledger lies open under the felt corner. The page records every household of Row 23 Low for six generations in the same hand-widths, column after column of paid. The current page stops at the second month ago. Beneath the desk, a second book holds the unpaid — more names than the paid column has left, and all of them on this row.

content.name: Row 23 Low
content.description: The lamp gives two blinks for every steady stretch, and where the wall panels are gone it stops reaching altogether. No counter sits at the counter. Slate felt covers the good half of the floor; bleached linen sheets the torn half. A stencil reads DUES DUE BY THE NEW MOON, cut off mid-word by the opening.

npc.name: Tsemutsanion Arshizamenne
npc.voice: Terse, domestic, idioms slightly misfiled — she speaks of the fold the way one speaks of weather in a house.

greet.says: Mind the pleats. The fold remembers where you slept last; best not to disappoint it. Take this — it knotted itself into the wool and I've no use for what volunteers.

water.says: Stopped? It's nesting. Everything down here densifies eventually — even falling. Go on, I've four bunks to re-tuck before the fold turns.

reactions.grief: Stops mid-pleat and leaves the wool gaping — first unfinished fold in years — then walks toward the dead one's bunk.
reactions.shock: Covers the body with the first armful of chalk wool, tucking it in before her mind arrives.
reactions.bribed: Looks at the offered payment as at wool that volunteers itself, and the refusal comes out almost gentle.
reactions.accused: Spreads both silvered hands flat on the unfinished pleat and holds them there, as if the wool might testify.
reactions.flattered: Corrects the compliment's facts, crediting the fold, while her ears go pink beneath the silver dust.
reactions.questioned: Recites her movements as bunk-counts and fold-times, idioms misfiled enough that the question loses its shape.
reactions.threatened: Her creases come out crooked, and she calls it the wool's doing, never the fear.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Admits it sideways, blaming the fold for turning mid-sentence, and her voice loses its weather for a moment.
reactions.authority_arrives: Marks the official by the draft on the wool, back turned one breath longer than respect allows.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Bunk by bunk she counts aloud before the shudder finishes, panic reserved only for whoever the fold took.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Volunteers every crooked tuck the accused ever made, catalogue running long past useful, betraying years of watching.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Hears the plea to its end, then gives the only thing in reach: a knot from the wool, and silence.

npc.description: Tsemutsanion Arshizamenne folds mineral wool with the tenderness of a mason squaring stone, silver dust silvering her forearms to the elbow, and pauses — the whole room seems to pause with her — before tucking the pleat home.

lore.name: The Paused Fountain
lore.description: Its silver water hangs mid-fall, each drop a little mirror; a child's chalk marks on the basin tally days, and the tally ends years ago, mid-number.

content.name: The Nesting Fold, Vault 420
content.description: A fountain stands in the fold's heart, silver water that has stopped mid-arc and stayed — nobody here remarks on it, which is worse than remarking. The chalk-white mineral wool has been woven, unwoven, rewoven into cells within cells, a dwell that outgrew its own arithmetic and kept counting anyway, families nesting in the pleats of a thing that repositions between visits like a sleeper turning. Bunks crowd the gilt inspection gantries; laundry dries on stencilled plating reading POSITION LAST CONFIRMED SIX YEARS AGO. However far one walks inward, one's shoulders meet no wall — only further chalk, further wool, further held breath of a place not witnessed even by itself.

npc.name: Bandajai Shisa
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical shorthand. Speaks of the grain the way a mender speaks of load-bearing members — with respect and no romance.

corks.says: Some readings belong to the person. Some belong to the ward. The ones that belong to neither get plugged in the wood, and I don't unplug them. Ask Sevin, if you must — though she'll only tell you to leave them be, and she's right.

choices.text: Leave the corks where they are.

grain.says: The ship grows the barley, the barley falls where it falls, and what falls was never random. That's the whole of the craft. Everything else is knowing when to keep your mouth shut about what you read.

choices.text: Ask what she keeps her mouth shut about.

greet.says: You'll wait your turn. A reading wakes me, not the reverse. And it's one each — the grain hates being asked twice in a day.

choices.text: Ask how spilled barley tells anyone anything.
Ask about the corks in the counter.

reactions.grief: She finishes the stranger's reading in silence, then casts a forbidden second and plugs it in the wood.
reactions.shock: She stands so long at the counter that the tallow drowns its own wick before she moves.
reactions.bribed: The offer dies mid-air; she counters with one condition, that the briber never ask her for anything again.
reactions.accused: No defense comes; she asks instead who read the accusation and whether that reader squared the grain.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands like counterfeit grain, and her only answer is to ask what the flatterer wants read.
reactions.questioned: She recites her movements like a stencilled rule, no more words than the frame above her demands.
reactions.threatened: The threat makes her quiet the wrong way, and the grain she squares drifts crooked for once.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she says the reading belonged to the ward, which is her word for nothing anyone can check.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets the one courtesy she never gives visitors: she stands, and the grain stays where it fell.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder ruins every cast in the ward, and she reads the new scatter anyway, because it fell.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name draws one flat fact from her readings of the person, and after that, the craft's own silence.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea falls outside what the grain carries, and she says so plainly, then fills the visitor's tallow cup anyway.

npc.description: Bandajai Shisa sleeps sitting up, chin on fist, more arms folded on the counter than a person should have. A lamp of tallow burns at her elbow. When she wakes she does not apologize; she squares the grain with one finger and looks up.

lore.name: The Plugged Counter
lore.description: The counter's edge is studded with corks, each one sealing a split in the wood. Beneath every cork, scratched small: a date and a word — 'thin', 'east', 'salt', 'third-child'. Bandajai Shisa has been driving a plug into the table for every omen she could not say aloud, and the table is running out of edge.

content.name: Oracle Stand, Ward 230
content.description: The smell arrives first: barley steeped in tallow, cork, sailcloth gone sour with years of readings. A booth of sailcloth stretched over cork, swept and squared, everything in its place except the reader asleep across the counter, one hand still resting in a cast of spilled grain. Stencilled along the frame: ONE READING PER VISITOR, NO REPEATS SAME DAY.

npc.name: Strivaronos of Eunpolis
npc.voice: Measured, liturgical about the roster, allergic to hurry; thaws when asked about the work itself rather than the place.

cut.says: Teams from below — quiet ones, three months back, with instruments I didn't know and manners I didn't like. They looked at my joists like a physician looks at a pulse. Never filed a closing report either, and nobody up here will say the word for that. So I cook. The roster holds whether the floor does or not.

gap.says: With a tray and a wrist, the way it was done before the cutting. The rail takes the weight if your wrist takes the rail. I slid four hundred trays across that gap before the repairs opened, and I'll slide four hundred after. The floor is a convenience. The service is not.

choices.text: Who ordered the floor cut open?

food.says: Barley water, seed-cake, salt broth — what the roster says and what the roster has always said. The kitchen below the decks feeds a generation; this galley feeds whoever the decks send up hungry. Same meal. Same roster. That is the whole of the creed that matters in a kitchen.

hall.says: The one this galley serves. Follow the steam-plume fore and you'll see the table before you see anything else — seats like hills, all of them empty, and the air up there has the habit of being listened to. I cook for an audience that stopped attending before my line began. The meal goes up anyway. That's the service.

greet.says: Mind the plank. Third service is at the turn of the strip and I'll not be delayed by a guest in the vats. You'll be wanting feeding or wanting asking — they're different bowls.

choices.text: How do you serve across that gap?
How long have you cooked here?

years.says: I fed the audit trains in my mother's shift and she fed the survey trains in hers. My hands learned this gantry before my feet learned the ground. Eunpolis sent kitchen-blood up the rind for nine generations running — someone must serve at height, or the height goes unfed, and an unfed hall is a hall that starts deciding things.

roster.says: The roster wrote itself, the way sediment writes a riverbed. Somebody cooked once and it was right, and enough somebodies repeated it that being right stopped being a choice. You don't amend that. You keep it. Everything in this ship that lasts was kept by somebody too stubborn to improve it.

reactions.grief: Without a word she portions a second helping, sets it where a tray would reach, and resumes the count.
reactions.shock: For once her eyes go down past her boots and stay there while the vat behind her runs over.
reactions.bribed: The offer sits untouched beside the seed-cake, and she names it a tip left after bad service.
reactions.accused: The count under her breath stops, and she turns her whole body from the vats for the first time.
reactions.flattered: She warms at praise of her wrist and talks freely of the rail until she hears what the praise wants.
reactions.questioned: The questioning gets the roster, name by station by hour, as though it were a list recited for years.
reactions.threatened: Her answer is a request that the threat be entered in writing, since so little else here ever has been.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The same answer comes back word for word, slower, as though precision could close the gap inside it.
reactions.authority_arrives: She does not stop decanting, since jurisdiction in her experience has always come and gone between services.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first glance goes to the plank over the gap, and the count resumes half a beat late.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Too fast for her own tempo, she testifies to every tray the accused served on time since the repairs opened.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea gets the only power she holds, a full tray and the promise that the roster will hold tomorrow.

npc.description: Strivaronos of Eunpolis works the gantry in a slate apron gone gold with years of steam-scald, decanting barley water vat to vat without once looking down past her boots. She counts under her breath in a serving-rhythm older than her.

lore.name: The Tray Rail
lore.description: A bronze rail runs counter to kettle at exactly tray-height, polished bright along its whole forty-pace length — generations of laden trays slid it across the gap where the floor used to be. It is still kept polished, though the floor is gone.

content.name: Bulkhead 30 Fore
content.description: A serving counter stands forty paces from the kettles it serves, and the floor between them has been cut away for repair — the distance a tray must cross is a plank over open girderwork, down and down into gold-lit structure. Fused quartz vats steam in ranks tall enough that the cook works from a gantry. One worker moves along it, unhurried. Stencilled above the idle spigots: GALLEY RUNS ON THE OLD ROSTER.

npc.name: Deronshomi the Silent
npc.voice: Says nothing. Writes short, clipped lines on a slate — declarative, unadorned, the grammar of someone who has decided what the room needs before you have.

room.says: [The slate:] Fire took the old counter. Wards council had it standing again in nine days. What feeds the ward doesn't wait on ceremony.

choices.text: Ask if the council feeds the wards, or watches them.

creed.says: [The chalk hesitates, then:] Stock runs short by spring, every spring. Nobody outside this room learns that. Remember whose table told you.

greet.says: [Deronshomi writes on the slate:] Sit. The sixth bowl is spoken for — he pays Tuesdays. You'll take the fifth.

choices.text: Ask why the room was rebuilt.

slate.says: [The slate stays blank a long moment. Then, in small letters:] Voice went with the fire. Counter came back. Fair trade.

council.says: [A pause before the chalk moves.] Both. Merid Solen audits everything she keeps. You'd be warmer if you stopped asking which half you're standing in.

sleeper.says: [The slate:] Green-deck shift. He sleeps here because home is four doors past where his feet stop working. We feed him anyway. That's the whole creed, if you want it short.

choices.text: Ask what it costs them, feeding everyone.

reactions.grief: The sixth bowl is portioned anyway, full measure, set at his stool as if Tuesday were still owed.
reactions.shock: Broth overruns the bowl, the ladle pouring past full, past stopping, their eyes fixed nowhere in the room.
reactions.bribed: The offering sits untouched while the briber's bowl comes up a ladle short.
reactions.accused: Hands keep portioning, but the fifth bowl fills past its mark — the measure telling what the slate won't.
reactions.flattered: The ladle tilts once, the only question flattery gets: what is wanted, and from whom.
reactions.questioned: The slate needs only turning; its answer was chalked that morning against exactly this question.
reactions.threatened: The ladle is set down for the first time anyone can remember, and nothing is written at all.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The slate goes face-down under a forearm, its last line smeared past reading twice over.
reactions.authority_arrives: A bowl is portioned before the official's foot clears the mat — exact measure, nothing generous in it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The lamp rig swings; both arms lock around the stockpot before the sixth bowl can slide.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The slate fills — names, dates, who owed what on which Tuesday — a silent person shouting the room down.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The chalk goes back to its rail empty, and the ladle turns over — a signal the room has never seen.

npc.description: Deronshomi the Silent works the counter in slate apron and deep-blue cuffs, portioning noodles into six bowls before anyone has ordered them. They do not speak; they tilt the ladle, and that is the question.

lore.name: The counter's corner-brace
lore.description: A brass brace under the counter's far corner, salvaged from something older — the screw holes don't match, and someone has filled the old ones with wax the color of the wood.

content.name: Lalikon
content.description: The rubber matting is new enough to grip your soles, tacky where the seams overlap, laid over stone that gives nothing back. Six stools in bleached linen, ivory counters, a lamp rig hung too high and too white — everything correct, nothing broken in. A stencil on the counter's flank reads SIX STOOLS, NO STANDING SERVICE, and one stool is occupied: someone asleep, chin on chest, coat still buttoned.

npc.name: Kronana the Twice-Returned
npc.voice: Brisk, counting everything. She talks the way a carter loads: one thing at a time, nothing set down twice.

who.says: Above my reach, friend. I crank the signal, I load the turf, I keep the board. Twice-Returned means I left this line twice and came back twice, and both times the rail was still here waiting. Rail's patient. People are what move.

choices.text: Let her get back to the turf.

name.says: Left for the green decks once, left for the market row twice. Both times I came back inside a season. The line gets in you. Kronana the Twice-Returned — the third name was earned, not chosen.

flood.says: A seam let go two rows down. Rindwalkers patched it in a day — good people, that. But the sheds stayed wet a week, and the Continuants wrote it up as handled. Paper says one thing. Sacking says another.

choices.text: Ask who decides what gets written up.

greet.says: Car's not due. You walked here, or you're early. Either way, mind the turf — that's winter feed and it doesn't forgive boots. What brings someone down the aft line at this hour?

choices.text: Ask why so much is stored here.

notice.says: That the aft line runs lighter every year. Fewer cars, same rail. Somebody upstream is choosing to send less, and nobody's said so out loud. I count cars. That's my whole job. The count is going down.

choices.text: Ask who could be choosing that.
Say the count might pick back up.

signal.says: Crank it twice, the arm drops upstream, next car knows to stop. Once means nothing. That's the whole trick of it. Thirty years and it's never once failed to be that simple.

storage.says: Because the aft sheds flooded and nobody upstream will take the load. So it lives here, and I live with it. Row 16 was built for a trolley and a bench. It's holding a harvest now.

written.says: The council decides. I move what they tell me moved. I've done it thirty years and I don't grudge the work. But when the writing and the weight stop matching, you notice. You can't help noticing.

choices.text: Thank her for the work she does.

reactions.grief: She keeps stacking turf until the stack leans wrong, then stops, sits on the bales, and talks about the dead man's cranking rhythm for too long.
reactions.shock: Her hands keep loading while her eyes stay fixed on the body, and she loses the count she has kept since morning without noticing.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer out loud like freight — so much turf, so many seasons — and then says the board already knows what the sheds are worth.
reactions.accused: The sacking block hangs in her grip a beat too long before she sets it down, and her count of the day's loads falters at four.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them for the praise in four words, then points at the seam two rows down and asks whether their thanks covers wet sheds.
reactions.questioned: She answers with a count — loads shifted, cranks turned, turf accounted — then waits, hands still, for the next question.
reactions.threatened: She names what the rail pays, what the sheds cost, and what she has already lost twice, in a voice that shakes only on the last item.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She does not reach for a second story; she stands at the platform edge, recites the true numbers, and lets the mistake sit there.
reactions.authority_arrives: She straightens the stack she was going to fix anyway, wipes her hands again though they are clean, and lets the official speak first.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She grabs the signal post, checks the crank clicks true, and starts a count of the platform blocks that have shifted out of line.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She says the name twice, flat, then starts defending a person she has openly called lazy every season, faster than the accusation deserves.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says no in one breath, then stays by the stove an hour after, explaining every route off this line and why each one fails.

npc.description: Kronana the Twice-Returned stands hip-deep in baled sacking, hauling a turf block onto a stack taller than she is. She stops mid-lift when she hears you, sets the block down with care, and wipes her hands on her thighs without looking away from the platform edge.

lore.name: The Counting Board
lore.description: A slate rail-side, chalked with car tallies going back months. One column, headed TWICE, is scratched out and restarted four times.

content.name: Row 16 Aft
content.description: The trolley rail swallows sound first. Footsteps go flat, the way they do over packed earth, and the crank on its post clicks in the quiet it makes. Then the platform: turf stacked in cut blocks, sacking baled past the ceiling line, a smoke-blackened stove wedged where a bench should be. Stencilled on the signal post: CRANK THE SIGNAL TWICE FOR NEXT CAR.

npc.name: Kicha-Hatzin
npc.voice: Quick, deal-shaped sentences that loosen when the queue is empty; treats information like inventory — priced, but always moving.

kell.says: Kell doesn't wear the cord anymore. Walked a route nobody sanctioned and came back knowing things about the spinward shafts. Now he fixes walls instead of running past them. Some of us thought he'd die out there. He thought so too, I think.

left.says: Down the axial line, they said. People say that when they mean they stopped saying where. I keep the apron because a route history's no good with a gap in it, and she's my gap. Now — buying or selling?

braid.says: The Braid knows everything and believes none of it. Somebody three wards over noticed the terminal posts reading strange — motif indices repeating where they shouldn't. Could be a teller with a broken generator. Could be nothing. I've already made two trades off it, so it's something to me.

choices.text: I'll keep an eye on the terminals.

greet.says: Buying or selling? Rates are whatever I say until the sheet's up, so speak quick or speak cheap.

choices.text: What happened to the other half of the shop?
Why is today's sheet still blank?
This isn't your apron, is it.

rates.says: Because the Braid says scrip's about to wobble and I'd rather post once, right, than twice, wrong. You hold goods through a wobble, you come out ahead. That's not rumor, that's arithmetic. Don't repeat it.

shift.says: It's Vess's apron. Vess left. That's the whole story I tell, and the one I believe on good days. Sit down if you're not trading — the stool's the only thing in here not for sale.

repair.says: Load-bearing wall went soft. Kell's crew opened it up and found the old till-rail behind it, from before the window was a window. We're deciding whether to keep it or trade it. Everything's stock eventually.

reactions.grief: She writes the name on today's blank rate sheet, then scrubs it off with her thumb until the paper tears.
reactions.shock: She hears herself quote a price to the body before her hands stop moving.
reactions.bribed: The offer sits on the sticky counter while she decides which memory moves at that price.
reactions.accused: The deal-math runs wrong for once, and she asks who authorized the count in a voice that doesn't hold.
reactions.flattered: Flattery gets the same appraisal as salvage, though she lets it sit longer than she should before naming the markup.
reactions.questioned: The answers come priced and unhesitating, small change she keeps counted out beside the till.
reactions.threatened: Knot by knot her thumb works the wrist-cord while she talks the threat down to freight rates.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The story gets repriced on the spot, spoiled stock at a discount, and she watches them decide whether to buy.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her voice flattens to posted rates while her free hand draws the magenta sheeting a little wider.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The plastic rattles, the sheeting billows, and she's already repricing, faster than the tally needs, everything the shudder just devalued.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Kell's name lands on the counter and she defends him with route history, then hears the defense sound like testimony.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She thinks of a gap down the axial line and gives away, for once, information for free.

npc.description: Kicha-Hatzin works the till in a shift-apron too wide in the shoulders, knotted cord at the wrist, pricing salvage plastic by thumb and eye while the opened-up half of the shop ticks behind the sheeting.

lore.name: The Rate Board's Back Plate
lore.description: Behind the daily scrip sheet, the board's back plate is scored with older rates, scratched out and re-scratched, decades deep. The bottom row never changes: a barter column where goods swap for goods, no scrip at all, kept current in a different hand. Whatever Kicha-Hatzin posts out front, the window has always run two markets — one for the ward, one for whoever the other column is for.

content.name: Ward 50 Spinward
content.description: Scrip ink and hot plastic — the smell of rates being rewritten in a hurry. Half the pawn-window is sheeted off behind magenta canvas webbing, and the counter that remains is sticky with resin someone never sanded off. A stenciled SCRIP RATES POSTED DAILY hangs crooked over the till, today's sheet still blank.

npc.name: Sorudur Mibovocurom
npc.voice: Terse, threaded with Luna's domain — talks about the room as though it keeps records of them, not the reverse. Uses 'found' as a verb for things that happened to people.

count.says: It doesn't count. We counted. It was already more than the number before the first of us got found by it. Look, I sealed Halzec's side last week — it healed a crease he'd left. His crease. It remembers what it should forget and forgets what we remember. That's the whole of it. Now leave the foil where it lies; the bed will finish what I started.

greet.says: Take the far side if you're lying down. I'm covering Halzec's shift and I'd rather not be talked at while I do it. Ask one thing, then let me finish the seam.

choices.text: Why does the bed count its own re-formings?

reactions.grief: Presses a palm flat against the healed stratification and stays that way too long, mourning the way you mourn something that might yet remember him.
reactions.shock: Sits down hard on the chamber floor, footfall arriving before its echo, and cannot finish the seam they have sealed a hundred times.
reactions.bribed: Names a price absurd and specific, having decided to be bribeable only in currency the offerer cannot pay.
reactions.accused: Sets the stylus down before their hands can betray them, then says nothing at all, letting the seam wait and the silence confess nothing.
reactions.flattered: Waves the praise at the stencilled frame — leave as found, it will not matter — though their hands slow, pleased despite the creed.
reactions.questioned: Answers the accounting without lifting eyes from the stylus, as though the bed itself might amend the record if they get a digit wrong.
reactions.threatened: Shrugs toward the frame, bare feet planted, telling the powerful voice that everything down here is already found — them included.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Does not look at the evidence; looks instead at the foil, as if hoping the bed will swallow the discrepancy the way it swallowed Halzec's crease.
reactions.authority_arrives: Keeps sealing, deliberately, the hot stylus steady, granting jurisdiction nothing but the smell of silverleaf and scorched foil.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Lays both hands on the grey frame and listens, needing to know whether the bed moved with the room or was moved by it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Snaps that the bed has never found anyone by name, then softens, because their opinion of the named one is not simple.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says plainly they cannot, then stays anyway, sealing the stranger's side while pretending it is only the shift.

npc.description: Sorudur Mibovocurom works barefoot on the frame's underside, sealing a seam of wound-foil with a hot stylus, taking the shift of someone who, they mention later, has not come back down in some weeks. They speak to the seam more than to you, and pause — long, unhurried pauses — as though listening to the bed answer.

lore.name: The Bed's Own Counter
lore.description: Beneath the foot of the frame, a sliver of wound foil has been peeled back to expose a row of notches scored into silver — one per re-formation, someone began counting once. The count stops at 341, mid-tally, and beneath it a different hand has written: it was 341 before we started. The bed has been re-forming more times than anyone has been here to sleep in it.

content.name: Tonomka's Reforming Bed
content.description: The smell arrives first: crushed silverleaf and scorched wound-foil, a scent like a bell breathed on — like something ringing at a frequency the nose answers before the ear. The bed stands mid-chamber, lead-grey, and where sleepers have lain it has healed itself between absences, sheet over sheet, so that it has grown stratified, geological; two claimants sleep in shifts and neither has ever finished a night. Sound behaves wrongly here — a footfall arrives before its echo, or after it, or not at all. Stencilled along the frame, in letters the foil has half-swallowed: LEAVE AS FOUND IT WILL NOT MATTER. The scale is intimate; the time is not.

npc.name: Saqfasam al-Kafaiqani
npc.voice: Terse, ledger-bred. Counts in half-thoughts, answers in allotments. Doesn't waste breath on welcome — breath is measured too.

greet.says: Sixty measures over and the shaft won't take more. You want grain or you want the reason. Only one's free today.

choices.text: Why is this close so full?

surplus.says: Belt rations run light, and the council's ledgers don't count what I count. What's set aside on the second shelf is owed — not to you. Mark it and go.

reactions.grief: A number nobody asked for comes out of her — the whole second shelf, all of it owed — and more follow.
reactions.shock: The tally in her head goes blank; her extra arms keep folding and unfolding, looking for work.
reactions.bribed: The offer is weighed like grain, found light, and handed back with the scoop still in her fist.
reactions.accused: Her scoop stops in the grain; she demands the missing measure, because the number will name the liar.
reactions.flattered: She says the tally speaks for itself; a spare arm curls toward the stranger before she catches it.
reactions.questioned: Hours, route, purpose — she deals them out in allotments, a tally she has given before.
reactions.threatened: For three breaths the ledger leaves her entirely; what comes back is flatter than she intends.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The figure gets revised twice before it settles, and it settles wrong, and she knows it.
reactions.authority_arrives: She's up the ladder before the boots clear the hatch, reshelving what was never there, back turned to be busy.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first count is the second shelf; her second, the hatch weight; her third, the warm breathing under the ladder.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The accused's counts for three seasons come off her tongue in order; defense or verdict, she won't say.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No allotment covers this; her hands leave the work and hang open, and she hates them for it.

npc.description: Saqfasam al-Kafaiqani wakes on the second shove of your boot — or was already awake — and is up the ladder with a scoop before any question forms. Extra arms fold out of the way without comment. She moves through the leaning sacks without touching them, a route worn into her feet.

lore.name: The tally stick on the doorpost
lore.description: A copper rod nailed beside the hatch, notched on every face — the room's ledger, kept the old way. Counts run long for six rotations back: intake notched faster than outflow, the surplus rising into the second shelf that wasn't part of Close 40's original volume. The last notch is doubled-deep, the way a keeper marks something set aside that isn't grain. Beside the final notch, a small loop-and-slash in notation older than any guild stencil. The rod has been rubbed smooth at the handle end, where a thumb worries it.

content.name: Close 40 Outboard
content.description: Light falls wrong here — bent through the seam where the weighted hatch never quite seats, striping ochre across sacks that stand stacked past the second shelf and lean into the walkway. Everything has a tacky sheen; resin was spilled and never scraped. Beneath the ladder, one body curled in the warm, breathing. Stencilled on the clay wall: HATCH WEIGHTED, DO NOT PROP OPEN.

npc.name: Fokofainogh-Fukloa
npc.voice: Short, load-counted sentences. Speaks like inventory: what came, what stayed, what broke.

both.says: Both. That's the joke of this landing. The ship says a room sleeps one. The ship never counts what people carry up the stairs.

stay.says: You stack a life long enough, it gets heavy to lift again. I chalk every one that stays. Somebody should keep the count. Me, I stopped unpacking years ago. Easier that way.

cargo.says: Mine, some. The others belong to people who meant to move on. The rope knows better than they did. Everything that comes up these steps slows down.

greet.says: Mind the rope. Mind the crates. If you're not here to haul, say so quick.

choices.text: Do you live here, or work here?

reactions.grief: Halfway into counting the dead one's crates that will never be claimed, the voice gives out on the number.
reactions.shock: Their hands go on crimping nothing, and it takes three askings before the eyes come up from the floor.
reactions.bribed: The bribe gets counted out loud, twice, and refused on the grounds that some things don't tally.
reactions.accused: The crimper comes down hard enough to dent, and the denial arrives as a count of what they never touched.
reactions.flattered: Praise weighs like an empty crate to them, and they say so, and keep working.
reactions.questioned: They read the day out like a manifest, what came and what stayed, and volunteer nothing past the ledger.
reactions.threatened: Nothing in the face moves; inside, they are already pricing what obedience costs against what defiance weighs.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The recount comes up with the same number both times, and they give the lie again anyway, quieter.
reactions.authority_arrives: Name, shift, load: they give the official all three and stop, eyes down, hands loose and visible.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They count heads before crates for the first time in years and pretend the order was always so.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They laugh once, wrong-sounding, and list everything that person carries, because nobody that loaded could move fast enough.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They confess the limit in inventory terms, room one bed deep, no keys, no rope, and stay put anyway.

npc.description: Fokofainogh-Fukloa stands ankle-deep in crates, re-binding a split seam with iron banding and a hand crimper. Their gloves are worn through at the palm. They do not look up until the crimper bites.

lore.name: The Landed Manifest
lore.description: A slate hangs behind the crates, chalked in a stevedore's hand. It lists every load that has passed through this landing in eleven years — crate counts, weights, whose hands took them. The last column is titled STAYED, and it is longer than the one titled MOVED ON. This room keeps what the docks forget: half the cargo never leaves.

content.name: The Stair Landing of Second Shift
content.description: A crate swings down past your head on a rope and settles among forty others. The room is one bed deep, and the bed has crates on it. Pale ochre limewash goes dull with smoke above a stencil on the stair door: NO COOKING PAST THE THIRD STEP.

npc.name: Tsaerya Narentso
npc.voice: Exact. Short sentences about the work first. Warming takes time and shows up as longer sentences, not softer ones.

you.says: I've been asking myself that for six weeks. The new pours ring clean. That's the problem — clean like arithmetic. Denna heard something in the old ones worth leaving a life over. Some nights I think the fourth notch on that frame should have been mine.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let the silence stand.
"The fourth pour is yours. Finish it."

back.says: Slowly, and with an apology in every pass of the file. A bell holds the hand that tuned it. Hers had a light touch. I don't. By the third one I'll have overwritten her entirely and I keep doing the first two over instead.

end4.says: Maybe. Come back when the third one rings and we'll see what my hand sounds like. If it's wrong, at least it'll be wrong as me.

greet.says: Mind the channel. It's clay, not stone, and it doesn't forgive a boot. You're the second visitor today, which is one more than usual.

tally.says: My predecessor started that. I kept it going because stopping felt like an insult. Four hundred and eleven, then the last stroke never got finished. That was the day Denna left, actually. Funny what you notice later.

whyquit.says: She said the bells sounded wrong. Not cracked — wrong. Same alloy, same process, and she swore the tone had moved. Nobody here heard it. She went to ask somebody who might. Nobody asks that kind of question and stays a founder.

whosework.says: Denna's. She started three bells for the market hall and quit at the third wax. Left the molds set like they'd keep. Clay doesn't keep. I've been finishing them at half speed between my own orders.

choices.text: "How do you finish someone else's bell?"

reactions.grief: Says the name once and keeps filing the same pass until the rim shines through.
reactions.shock: Drops the hook where she stands and stays in the ankle-height heat, not hearing the metal cool.
reactions.bribed: Wipes clay dust from her palms before answering, wanting clean hands for the refusal.
reactions.accused: Snaps that her hands are counted at every pour, then hears how loud she got and stops.
reactions.flattered: She hears the praise the way she hears the new pours, too clean, and waits for the ask.
reactions.questioned: She answers in pour times and mold counts, then asks if the third bell counts as evidence.
reactions.threatened: Decides the threat can wait until the metal is out, and pours on through it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Goes quiet a beat longer than any denial takes, then corrects herself down to the minute.
reactions.authority_arrives: Points at the rope-marks and the other workers' molds, making the room's neglect official before anyone asks.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first look goes to the crucible, not the ceiling, counting seconds until the surface steadies.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She names the pour that puts them elsewhere, faster than she has spoken all shift.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits the limit flat out, then offers to stand the night pour with them anyway.

npc.description: Tsaerya Narentso works a crucible hook with both hands, sleeves rolled, forearms patched with clay dust that has dried into a second skin. She pours without looking up, then sets the hook down on the exact spot the handle-wear says it always goes.

lore.name: the lone-pour tally
lore.description: Notches cut into the doorframe, one per pour done in this room. Someone kept count past four hundred and then stopped, mid-stroke.

content.name: Sarah
content.description: The heat sits low, ankle-height, rolling off the clay drainage channel; the air above your head stays cold. The pour floor is meant for one worker and has three jobs' worth of molds on it. Half of them are someone else's, abandoned at the rope-marks. Green-grey clay tiles cover the walls to the ceiling. A stencil reads MOLDS SET, DO NOT POUR ALONE.

npc.name: Neth the Outer
npc.voice: Dry, exact, allergic to comfort — measures everything in loads and intervals, and treats praise as a misreading of the work.

gap.says: A spool carriage. The big one, the one they wound the mast-thick runs on. Hauled out a month back and nothing has come in its place, which tells you the schedule up here matters less than whatever needed the carriage more. Things get reassigned. Rooms don't get refilled.

choices.text: And the log in the frame?
Have you worked this hall long?

log.says: The haul log. Every line is a re-tensioning, and the spacing between lines is the only true story this room tells. Read it and you'll find the cables going slack at longer and longer intervals — the load growing lighter. Then the last line: woke to slack. A cable under tension doesn't go slack unless what it holds changes its mind about being held.

choices.text: The ship moved? The hull can move?
How do you keep working, knowing that?

work.says: Thirty-one years on this bench, and the room hasn't changed and the work hasn't changed, which is the reward and the whole wage. You tension the cable, the cable holds, and next interval you tension it again. Anything that holds is holy. Anything that holds quietly, without asking to be thanked — that's the good work, and there's more of it under this floor than anyone up top will ever need to know.

choices.text: What was taken out of here?

greet.says: Mind the sag line. It wants that dip — take the dip out and you take the give out, and a cable without give is a blade waiting for a reason. You're off the marked path by some forty strides, so say what you're here for or hold something.

choices.text: What left that clean rectangle in the dust?
How long have you worked this hall?

moved.says: Everything moves. That's the oldest thing the rind teaches you before it teaches you anything else — the hull grows, the ends grow away from us, and whatever kept this cable loaded kept it loaded the way a hand holds a line, with intent, and now the hand has shifted its grip. We retension what we can measure and we keep faith with the rest.

choices.text: Why do they call you the Outer?
Years of this, though. How many?

outer.says: Because I walk the outer runs — the cable paths that follow the hull past the last marked gallery, where there's no bench, no crew, and nothing but the curve going on. I've seen the weld-beads down there laid in patterns no crew of ours made, and I catalogued them and came back, which is more than my good sense wanted. Neth the Outer. It's not a title. It's a warning the others give me by using it.

choices.text: The beads — whose work was it?

patterns.says: Old. Old the way the oldest wall-notation is old, and laid like someone welding who had all the time there ever was. I don't say a name for them. Down there, saying names is how you start expecting answers. I'm a tensioner. I keep the give in the line. That's the whole of my devotion and I recommend finding one the same size for yourself.

reactions.grief: Names the dead once, then inventories everything they held, line by line, far past any answer.
reactions.shock: They cross to the frame without deciding to, hand flat on the burned log, and stay through two hauls.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against thirty-one years of holding, finds it weighs nothing, and says so without insult.
reactions.accused: Stops the windlass mid-haul to face the charge square, then corrects it like a misread gauge, level and slow.
reactions.flattered: Calls the praise a misreading, flat as a log entry, and keeps cranking through the compliment.
reactions.questioned: Answers in intervals and loads, unhurried, as if the question were a tension reading needing only confirmation.
reactions.threatened: Threats carry no load they can measure; their hands stay right on the crank while the interval count goes wrong.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Lets the lie stand a count too long, then overloads the correction with schedule-talk where one fact would do.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes find the scuffed stencil first, and the official is granted exactly the line's authority, nothing beyond it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Checks the needles before anything else, then says the word slack aloud as if it were a diagnosis.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends the named one in load terms, tensions held, lines tended, and hears too late the loyalty in it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no in the tone of a failed line, then presses a spare shackle into the pleading hands anyway.

npc.description: Neth the Outer works the windlass with the unhurried economy of someone who has stopped needing to watch their own hands. They wear copper-Brown wraps gone iron-dark at every gripping surface, and they stand with a slight forward lean into the bench, braced against the room's slope as a habit of decades. Their right hand rests on the frame's burned log the way another person might rest a hand on a sleeping animal.

lore.name: The Haul Log Burned into the Windlass Frame
lore.description: Into the windlass's chalk-white frame someone has torch-burned a working log, one line per re-tensioning, running back further than paint would survive. The early lines are short: hall 40, hall 40, hall 40. Then the spacing changes — the same cables, re-tensioned at longer and longer intervals, because whatever load they carry keeps growing lighter rather than heavier. The last line is dated a month ago and reads: woke to slack. Slack in a tensioning hall is not wear. Slack means the ship itself moved off the cable, and the menders have no verb for that.

content.name: Tensioning-Hall 40
content.description: The tensioning bench stands two body-lengths from the anchor it serves, and every cable crossing the room must sag to reach it, dipping like rope that has given up before the windlass hauls it taut again. Chalk-white gussets buttress the sloped floor; a stencilled line reads TENSION CREW ONLY PAST THIS MARK, half scuffed by boot-traffic. Spools of annealed nickel and wound foil sit racked in sizes no hand spool matches. Something mast-heavy stood here until recently; the clean rectangle in the cable-dust says what size.

npc.name: Dusnja Ingensson
npc.voice: Counts things before she says them. Talks in amounts, dates, conditions.

busy.says: Busier than the room likes. Thirty-two out today, fourteen in. Every crate gets limewashed before it shelves — the smoke stains otherwise. Bab Zar takes everything the squares won't hold.

choices.text: How long have you worked here?
Sounds like enough for one day.

hers.says: Nineteen years. I know every wobble in every shelf leg. That's the whole trade — keeping what other people set down, long enough that setting it down wasn't a loss.

keep.says: Maybe. Or maybe whoever paid the freight on it is gone past claiming anything. Either way it stays on my slate until I'm not here to write it.

board.says: Nine years, that top line. A bed, turned posts, good joints. Nobody's claimed it and nobody's sold it. Rules are rules, but I rewrite it every wash. Don't ask me why.

choices.text: Maybe someone's coming back for it.

greet.says: We close at the bell. If you're claiming, have the chit. If you're browsing, browse quiet — that stack by the stair leans.

choices.text: That slate's full of old dates.

reactions.grief: She crosses a name off the crate list before hearing the rest, then stands there, crayon still raised.
reactions.shock: Her eyes stay on the body while she counts under her breath, wrong numbers, twice.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer out loud against nineteen years of a clean slate, and the arithmetic comes out no.
reactions.accused: Her hands stop on the rubber mid-tuck; she asks which day and which crate, twice.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them in the flat tone she uses for damaged goods, and asks what needs moving.
reactions.questioned: She answers in dates and counts, unhurried, a slate read aloud, and asks nothing back.
reactions.threatened: She names the exact penalty her contract carries, then asks whether he means it today or on record.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She recalculates out loud, catches her own wrong date, and corrects it flat, offering no excuse.
reactions.authority_arrives: She watches the official's boots for which path they take, rubber or bare floor, before she speaks.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She names each shelf leg that did not wobble, voice steady until the list runs out.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She offers exact claim dates and old misses, faster than fairness needs, then hears herself and stops.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says the ninety days are spent, then writes the refusal down so her hands have work.

npc.description: Dusnja Ingensson is wrapping a lamp base in sheet rubber, tucking the edges the way you tuck a bandage. A packing crate beside her is marked and re-marked with crossed-out names.

lore.name: The ninety-day chalk board
lore.description: A slate by the counter with dates rubbed into it in columns. Most lines are struck through — claimed. The oldest unclaimed line is nine years old, kept and rewritten each time the board gets washed.

content.name: Bab Zar
content.description: The pulley over the door hangs still, and nothing swings from it. Beyond, shelves of chairs and cabinets rise past the lamplight, all limewashed off-white. A stencil on the stair riser reads CLAIM WITHIN NINETY DAYS OR IT IS SOLD. The air is smoky; sheet rubber has been laid over the busiest path.

npc.name: Dako the Marble-Remembered
npc.voice: Terse, ledger-minded. Counts things before answering. Talks about stock, not about anything else.

gap.says: One crate, one entry, gone before I got here this morning. Bigger than anything that fits down those stairs, and I've carried everything that fits down those stairs. That's all I'll say. Rag's mine, work's mine.

greet.says: You're not on the winter list. Cellar's counted, so touch nothing. If you want the trapdoor after dark, key's at the desk, like the stencil says.

choices.text: What was in the empty bay?

reactions.grief: They wipe one lid long past clean, then ask who signs for the dead the way stock gets signed.
reactions.shock: The jar in their hands goes down hard and cracks; they stand there naming shelf numbers to nobody.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced aloud against a winter of clean entries and handed back as bad stock.
reactions.accused: The rag stops mid-wipe; they say, flat, that the crate left before their shift and the ledger proves it.
reactions.flattered: They thank them in four words, then wait, rag paused, until the asker says what the praise is for.
reactions.questioned: Recites yesterday's jar count without looking up, then asks if the ledger itself will do instead.
reactions.threatened: Stock worth gets recited in a level voice while their thumb wears at the rubber square.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their count doesn't hold and they know it; they start recounting aloud, faster, and lose the number twice.
reactions.authority_arrives: The count is ready before the official asks for it; the key's location gets stated, stencil-cited, without being requested.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their first question is whether anything fell; the second, quieter, is whether it will happen again.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They object on carrying-weight grounds — the named one couldn't move that crate alone — then hear how it sounds and stop.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say what they actually hold — jars, gaskets, a locked trapdoor — and refuse to dress the shortage as kindness.

npc.description: Dako the Marble-Remembered kneels among the jars, wiping each lid with a rag before it goes back on the shelf. A coil of sheet rubber sits at their knee, cut into squares for lid gaskets. They do not look up until you speak.

lore.name: Brass tally-hook
lore.description: A brass hook by the empty bay, worn smooth on the underside. Its ledger strip lists forty winters of crate weights, all in the same hand until the last entry, which is different and unsigned.

content.name: Root-Cellar 16
content.description: The smell reaches you first: cold dirt, old turnip tops, and burnt lamp oil. Shelves of off-white jars stand in tidy rows, and one whole bay is empty, the floor pale where a crate sat for years. A stencil by the trapdoor reads TRAPDOOR LOCKED AT NIGHT, KEY AT THE DESK. Sheet rubber hangs over the empty bay's corner, tacked up to keep the draft off the jars next to it.

npc.name: Triothedea the Marble-Returned
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, softened only at the edges. She states facts and lets the player do the work.

why.says: Because her daughter's upstairs and shouldn't see the room go blank in one visit. We do it in strips. Two more days and the wall is bare. That's the whole of it.

choices.text: I'll leave you to the packing.

card.says: I know. It stays until the last day. Continuants don't paint over a count that isn't finished. Then it goes in the crate with the rest.

greet.says: Room's turning over. If you want it, ask at the stove, not at me.

leave.says: Mind the enamel on the step. It isn't dry.

whose.says: A widow's. Thirty-one years on this cot. I'm clearing it because the rent stopped and the council won't carry an empty dwell past the quarter.

choices.text: There's a card on the wall.

reactions.grief: She wipes a piece that was already clean, folds the cloth wrong, and starts again without naming the dead.
reactions.shock: Nothing in her moves toward the body, and the wrapping takes her whole attention, too evenly to be real.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer out loud, an honest number, before the rule takes it back.
reactions.accused: Told to her face, she says no in ledger terms, and the second no lands slower than the first.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes her hand credit to the room's last tenant, and she waits flatly for the request.
reactions.questioned: Her answers come as dates and room numbers, nothing extra, and the wrapping never pauses.
reactions.threatened: Under threat she gets more procedural, not less, and recites the rules until her own voice steadies.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: When the evidence lands, she drops her denial and starts the count over from one, out loud, wrong.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets her by-the-book answers, and her hand keeps returning to the marked wall.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She puts the basin down with both hands and checks the curtain rod's lean before believing anything.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The one they name counted true when she packed them out, and she says so before deciding to.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What she cannot do comes first, said plainly, then the stove, which is all she has to give.

npc.description: A continuant in a slate work coat, wrapping an enamel basin in cloth and setting it into a crate. She wipes each piece before it goes in. The stencil over the doorframe, ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE, is partly behind her crate.

lore.name: The Widow's Card
lore.description: An index card is pasted low on the wall, at the height of someone sitting on the cot. Written around its border are the days of a month, and each day is crossed off twice — once in pencil, once later in ink, by a shakier hand. The ink stops eleven days before the pencil does. Whoever made the second set of marks was already gone from the room, and someone kept counting for her.

content.name: Curtained-Room 53
content.description: The room smells of warmed enamel and last night's stove smoke. One cot, one stool, and a curtain rod bolted into stone that leans with the floor. Sunlight from the slit window falls across the cot and stops there; everything else is already packed.

npc.name: Ioshearas Straxunogenes
npc.voice: Measured, precedent-haunting; speaks as if every sentence might be entered into a record.

greet.says: Stand off the rail line, please. This ruling cools as a unit or not at all — hold, and hold quietly.

choices.text: What is this place, that rulings are welded?
You share this gantry with someone, from the look of the clamps.

ask_room.says: A court. The oldest kind — where judgment becomes matter. Ink can be argued with; a weld in basalt has only one reading. The Writ's whole craft is deciding what deserves to outlast the people it binds.

choices.text: Who does the judging now? The hall seems empty of everyone but you.
I won't keep you from your bead.

ask_judge.says: The bench above holds court the way the tide holds a harbor — rarely, and at its own hour. I have laid rulings for years and met no judgment I could address. But the hall is not abandoned, whatever the runners say. Things this size are never abandoned. They are merely not presently attending.

choices.text: Then I'll leave you to work in its silence.

ask_dispute.says: The Continuants file here. Others come and weld their own gloss to the same rail — Drift glosses, mostly, knots and shortcuts where law should sit. Neither side concedes the gantry. So the record carries both hands, and only the basalt knows which line was first.

reactions.grief: Asks that the death not be entered anywhere, the first thing in forty years they have wanted unwritten.
reactions.shock: The visor drops over a face that has nothing to do with sparks, and they stand absolutely still.
reactions.bribed: Declines without naming the offer, saying only that a weld allows one reading and they intend to keep it.
reactions.accused: The answer comes out level, but the bead they lay afterward wanders for the first time in years.
reactions.flattered: Praise reaches something no one ever addresses, and for a moment they forget to ask its price.
reactions.questioned: Answers with times to the minute, as though the movements were already entered in some record.
reactions.threatened: Notes aloud that threats carry no weight until welded, though a hand has already closed on the rail.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stops mid-clause like a torch lifted off metal, and for once has no second pass.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the door and hold there until the official speaks first, an instrument awaiting its hand.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The first thing they check is the nearest ruling, thumb along the bead, reading for fracture before fear.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects that a name spoken is not a name proven, and the voice thins on this particular name.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains that they may only seal what has been decided, and the explanation takes far too long.

npc.description: Ioshearas Straxunogenes works bent against a rail clamp, visor down, laying a bead along a ruling's final clause with the unhurried hand of someone who has sealed thousands of decisions and reopened none. Sparks fall and are gone before they land.

lore.name: The Strike Gauge
lore.description: A hand tool hooked at the worker's belt: a tungsten stylus with a worn thumb-groove and eleven notches filed into the handle, one per judge who has held the office, the twelfth notch left uncut.

content.name: Kenaska
content.description: Before anything is seen, sound is taken up and pressed flat: the gantry eats a voice at arm's length, returns it as a hiss along iron-dark railings that run out past counting, a span the eye gives up measuring after the third buttress. Wind from the open gallery scours the deck clean of anything loose. On black glass panels set into the basalt rail, stencilled in bands, RULING WELDED AT TIME OF ISSUE — and beneath the stencil, row over row, actual welds, each one a sentence no one will ever grind out.

npc.name: Laameasshearluea Reathione
npc.voice: Measured, kind, unflinching — triage grammar. Nothing is greeted; everything is assessed, then released.

ask.says: Someone who earned a view of the outward dark, by old reckoning, though the old order that said so doesn't file reports anymore. Venus keeps this gallery breathing and asks nothing of us but that we keep it breathing after. Now let me finish this seam — it won't wait and neither, soon, will the wall.

greet.says: You'll want to keep your voice down past bay nine — that one's slept here three days and I've stopped arguing with the sleeping. If you're walking the gallery, walk it on the warm side; the cold edge takes the ankles first and I don't have beds to spare.

choices.text: Who sleeps out past the last bay?

leave.says: Walk warm.

reactions.grief: Says the name back once, correctly, and the chalk dust on their fingers will not settle.
reactions.shock: Their hands start triage on a body past triage before their eyes agree it's over.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer like a symptom, names what it indicates, and declines before the number finishes.
reactions.accused: The accusation lands somewhere they'll examine later; the seam under their hands gets sealed a half-beat too hard.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise finish, diagnoses where it's routed from, and asks what actually hurts.
reactions.questioned: Sorts the questions by severity, worst first, and answers each exactly once.
reactions.threatened: Names the threat's prognosis out loud, calmly, and only then notices their own hands have gone cold.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Admits it in four words and no more; whatever the lie was protecting gets moved tonight.
reactions.authority_arrives: One glance goes to the last bay; the rest of their courtesy goes to the official, rationed.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Steadies the nearest bed on its shims first, their own footing second, and never the wall seams.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects at once and on craft grounds: those hands, watched for years, don't shake.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Promises warmth, not safety, and hates the distinction more than the asker will ever know.

npc.description: Laameasshearluea Reathione stands hip-deep in the warm stratum of air, changing a sintered panel with the ease of someone who knows exactly which seam will fail next quarter. Sleeves bound at the elbow, chalk dust to the wrist, a stylus of graphite behind one ear and another behind the other, in case.

lore.name: The Graphite Pointer
lore.description: The tallest bay's shim is a length of packed graphite, tooled square, worn glossy on one face — an old survey marker from the outer structure, salvaged because it held, and re-used so long that a bed now leans its whole recovery upon it.

content.name: Heesaawaahotia's Convalescent Gallery
content.description: The warmth sits low and long, banked along the floor like a stoked flue, and does not rise — overhead the air thins toward the chill of the outer structure, so that a patient's feet are warm while the ceiling above them sweats condensation in a cold no one maintains. The gallery runs outward-facing, a kilometre of chalk-white ceramic bays where sintered panels have been patched with packed graphite wherever the wall gave up, each repair a dull black seam in all that white.
