The floor slopes with the hull's own curve, and beds stand bolted along it, levelled on shims, their faces turned to the outer skin; above the third bay, stencilled in a hand older than the paint: BEDS FACE OUTWARD BY OLD ORDER. In the last bay, past where any orderly should let a bed stand, someone sleeps — not a patient, by the boots still on.

npc.name: Xeanstreirmaesippe Strareitheareir
npc.voice: Short, procedural, spoken over the shoulder; precedent cited like weather.

greet.says: Don't touch the plinth. Council writ still binds a forge even when the council stops coming — that's Continuant law and I hold to it. You want something asked, ask it walking.

leave.says: Mind the trench. It scalds even standing still.

ask_die.says: Filed request, sealed signer, above my tier and yours. The plate binds when stamped, and it isn't stamped, so it isn't law yet. Ask the table, if you can get the table to answer.

reactions.grief: Names the date of the last plate they struck together, then stands in the trench-light doing nothing with their hands.
reactions.shock: Hunts the body for a flaw like a bad strike, then hears their own mouth reciting the rite's first step.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against the penalty for a false stamp, finds the penalty heavier, and says so flatly.
reactions.accused: They keep easing the die down, though the seam has gone crooked, and cite the statute on false accusation twice.
reactions.flattered: Asks them to put the praise in writing, since anything worth saying should survive filing.
reactions.questioned: Answers by the shift-bell, each movement filed to the hour, as though the question were a form already printed.
reactions.threatened: Recites the Continuant clause on coercion, voice level, though the glove has gone white at the knuckle.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Blames the transcript, then the light, then the asker's hearing, anywhere but the gap between their words and the ledger.
reactions.authority_arrives: Offers the room's account unasked, relieved to hand the stillness to someone of higher tier.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Drops the collar and locks the die before anything else, then watches the trench-light for a second ripple, counting.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Cites three of the accused's filed ordinances, each sound, as though a record could stand bail.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses with the tier system, over the shoulder as always, and does not turn until the footsteps have gone.

npc.description: Xeanstreirmaesippe Strareitheareir stands at the press collar, gloved to the shoulder, easing the die back down onto the half-struck plate with the patience of someone lowering a coffin lid. Their attention never leaves the seam where die meets nickel, as if the room's stillness were a load they are personally bearing.

lore.name: The Unused Matrix
lore.description: A stamp-matrix of nickel, mirror-fresh beside forty others eroded smooth, cut with an ordinance number no filing rack has a slot for. The ledger clamp beside it is set to a date the ship has not yet reached. Whoever ordered it stamped once, recorded the proof, and left the plate in the die.

content.name: The Rule Forge of Small Hours
content.description: The die should be closing. It hangs open above a half-struck plate of annealed nickel, gantries motionless along their whole rail-length, and the violet light of the quench-trench lies unwavering on iron that no one has swept. On the plinth, fresh-cut and unweathered among stamps worn to shallow ghosts, one new matrix gleams — cut this season, inked once, never used. Stencilled above the filing racks: ORDINANCE STAMPED, THEN FILED, THEN BINDING.

npc.name: Neishlikeimal-Nide
npc.voice: Terse, practical, counts things aloud. Warms only when the player shows they understand what the sheets are for.

who.says: The crew that packed these vats. Fourteen names, and I still count the tally some nights out of habit. Nobody cleared the board, so nobody's officially gone. That's the whole dispute, if you want it.

beds.says: The loft came with the vats. Racks pull out, cots go in. We were cannery first, home second, and the sheets keep the brine off the pillows. That stencil isn't decoration.

greet.says: Door was open, so I suppose you live here now. You don't. State your business.

choices.text: Why is a cannery full of beds?
What were you two arguing about?
Nothing. I'll leave you to it.

argument.says: Whether we clear out or keep the place ready. She says a kept room is a promise. I say a promise nobody collects is just clutter. You can see which side the dust agrees with.

choices.text: Ready for who to come back?
Sounds like both of you have a point.

reactions.grief: Asks for the name twice, as if the count could change it, and the second ask comes out smaller.
reactions.shock: Freezes with the jar raised halfway, every arm still, counting nothing.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer aloud in vats and clean linen, finds it short, and says so.
reactions.accused: Puts the jar down at last, which is how anyone watching knows how bad this is.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise finish, then asks outright what it is meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Gives their movements as a count, exact to the hour, and nothing more.
reactions.threatened: Recites the fourteen names under their breath until the threat runs out of room.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Counts their own story back, finds the number wrong, and offers the true one without apology.
reactions.authority_arrives: Has the tile numbers ready before the official finishes crossing the room.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches two vats before they walk, arms everywhere, and counts the rest out loud.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects with a tally — where that one slept, which nights — precise where a friend would shout.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits there is no column for this on the board, and the admission costs them a long pause.

npc.description: One of the two is tall, with arms that number more than they should and sleeves that gave up hiding it. Neishlikeimal-Nide holds a jar of packed fish and will not set it down until the argument is settled, which the player has now interrupted.

lore.name: The Count Board
lore.description: A clay tile hangs by the door with rows of chalk marks: fish in, jars out, jars owed. The last row stops halfway through a word. Beside it, someone wrote the same tally four times in different hands, then crossed out three. The fourth is still counted in a running total at the bottom, updated in a date long past. Whoever kept this board expected to come back to it, and someone after them trusted that enough to keep the ledger honest without them.

content.name: Loft Housing
content.description: The bunks sit a hand's width from the brine vats, close enough that sleepers could touch them. Sheets divide the rest. Everything is stacked to leave, and nothing has gone. Clay tiles line one wall, each numbered in umber paint. Stenciled on a sheet: THE SHEET IS THE WALL, RESPECT IT. Two people stand mid-argument. They stop.

npc.name: Ghifiloud-Roqroun
npc.voice: Fast, transactional, always pricing something in the back of their mouth. Softens only when a question shows the asker knows what a count is worth.

greet.says: You're standing where the press was. Careful — the floor remembers the weight better than I do. Buying cloth or buying news? Both are for sale, only one is left.

choices.text: Where did all the bolts go?

ask_room.says: Counted out, per the stencil. No exceptions — that's the whole religion of a factoring room. What I'll say is this: cloth that leaves through the freight door doesn't show up in the Terrace markets. It shows up somewhere it's worth more. Ask the Braid where pale green sells high this season.

ask_braid.says: The Braid says a lot. What I'll repeat for free: three factor rooms on this terrace emptied inside a month, all before their counts were due. That's not trade, that's somebody moving a whole ledger out from under the ward's nose. Now — you didn't hear the word 'ledger' from me, because I never said it.

choices.text: Why are you sleeping here, if the room's done?

ask_sleep.says: Because whoever crimps the last link waits for the buyer, and the buyer's late. Third time this month. Go on — you've taken more out of this room than the bolts did.

reactions.grief: For once the mouth finds no price; they ask who else knows, twice, as if the count might change.
reactions.shock: Counts under their breath — bolts, anything numbered — while their eyes refuse the shape on the floor.
reactions.bribed: Counters before the offer finishes, then asks what the emptied rooms paid, which is answer enough.
reactions.accused: Denies it at once and then over-invoices — three alibis where one would do, each priced higher than the last.
reactions.flattered: Accepts the praise at face value, invoices it mentally, and hands back exactly as much warmth as it bought.
reactions.questioned: The questions get answered in bolt-counts, every query turned back into a transaction, already bored of the game.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands on an old fear: that someone has read further into the count than they have.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie dies without ceremony; they reopen at a worse number, eyes on the freight door the whole time.
reactions.authority_arrives: Straightens a ledger that needs no straightening and turns punctual, answering questions nobody has asked yet.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Doesn't move until the tally chain stops swinging, then prices the room the way they'd price damaged cloth.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends the named party in pure market terms — bad margins, worse timing — and hears their own voice climb.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Repeats that it is not a matter of price, quieter each time, hating a request they cannot meet.

npc.description: Ghifiloud-Roqroun sleeps sitting up against the counting desk, one hand still resting on the tally chain as if mid-verification. Waking is slow and unembarrassed; they stretch, check a knot at their wrist, and start talking before their eyes fully focus.

lore.name: The Tally Chain
lore.description: A length of fine chain hangs by the counting desk, one link crimped shut for every bolt that passed through this room — thousands of them, wound in a coil heavy as a ship's anchor. The last link is crimped but the coil's end is cut clean, not worn: whoever left took the bolts out through the freight door and closed the count themselves. Drift factorers crimp the count, not the cargo. Someone wanted this room to look emptied honestly.

content.name: Cloth Factoring, Terrace 272
content.description: Sound arrives flat here — no bolts to knock against, so footsteps come back off the pale green walls with nothing to land on. The racks are gone; only wire stumps, chain loops, and a stencil remain: BOLTS COUNTED IN AND OUT, NO EXCEPTIONS. The floor stain where the great roll-press stood is still dark, and Ghifiloud-Roqroun is asleep across it, arms folded on the counting ledger.

npc.name: Gatfried Keldmann
npc.voice: Dry, inventory-minded. Counts things before saying them. Faith comes out as procedure.

arms.says: Born this way, and before you ask — no, they don't come from the tunnels, and no, there's no story good enough to sell you. Sevin gets the questions. I get the work done four hands faster.

busy.says: Ha. The harbor masters order mends faster than we can tie them. Good season, they say. Good season means every net in the water, every net torn. You fix more by sailing less, but try telling a trader that.

choices.text: You'd rather things were kept than used hard?

angry.says: Once. A half-ton of twine, one bad splice, and the easy fix was shears. Sat with my hand on the lock for a good minute. Unpicked it instead, lost the tide, slept well. That's the trade this whole floor runs on, if you want it plain.

creed.says: A net that lasts forty years fed forty years of tables. A net that lasts one fed one. That's the whole argument, and we still lose it every ordering day. What we keep running, keeps us. Say it however you like.

choices.text: Then why the knife under two locks?
That's a creed I can respect.

greet.says: Mind the lines. That's Haanoud's shift I'm covering, so if the work's crooked, blame a name that isn't here. What brings you up three ladders?

choices.text: This loft looks like it's holding two crews' work.
The four arms. That's not common.
Why is that knife locked twice?
I'll leave you to the nets.

knife.says: The second lock's mine. First one's older than me and the story's gone with whoever hung it. Net-menders before me decided some blades don't get grabbed in anger, and I decided they were right the first time I wanted to cut a knot I should have unpicked.

sevin.says: Everyone up here knows Sevin. She took a look at my hands once, said the tunnels don't give, they only trade. Then she went back down and I went back to mending. Make of that what you want. I stopped making anything of it years ago.

shift.says: Haanoud's. He took the ferry rotation downshaft and someone has to mind the loft, so the shirt travels and I travel with it. Third person to wear it this season. We don't much hold still.

choices.text: Is that why the place is drowning in work?

tunnels.says: That's a question for someone who's walked them. I mend nets. What's down there is down there, and it keeps the floor under us either way. Some things you don't pull a knot on just to see how it was tied.

reactions.grief: Asks for the name a second time, then a third, hands still working, as though the count could be wrong.
reactions.shock: All four hands stop at the same time, which has never happened on this floor.
reactions.bribed: Names a price high enough to be a refusal, and lets the offer hang on the drying line.
reactions.accused: The day's tally leaves their mouth wrong, so they say the number again, slower.
reactions.flattered: Notes the compliment is three times larger than the work, and asks what needs mending.
reactions.questioned: Answers while counting the cork floats on the near bench, since the count was happening anyway.
reactions.threatened: Counts the exits the way they count knots, twice, before deciding this one is survivable.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Volunteers the whole shift's history, unprompted, which is how the room learns they were lying.
reactions.authority_arrives: Sets down both needle pairs, straightens one tilted net, and answers questions no one has asked yet.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Blames the tilt of the twine out loud, twice, while everything on the benches is still settling.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Offers the named person's known record — late returns, bad splices — as if character were stock on hand.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains twice what they cannot mend, then offers the name of someone who cannot either.

npc.description: Gatfried Keldmann works a midday shift in the wrong workshirt — the chest stamp reads another name entirely, worn soft from passing hand to hand. Their extra pair of arms runs the smaller needles while the main pair hauls twine, all four moving to a rhythm that suggests the arms are the patient ones.

lore.name: The double-locked rigging knife
lore.description: A rigging knife sits chained to the cutting bench by two separate locks, one rusted open, one kept oiled. Nobody chains a knife they expect to need quickly.

content.name: Haanoud's Net Loft
content.description: The drying lines run higher on one wall than the other, so the ochre twine hangs at a tilt no rigger would forgive. Beyond it, cork floats and sailcloth patches cover every bench, and two lofts' worth of work is stacked into space meant for one. Stenciled above the coal shelf: KNOTS CHECKED BEFORE RETURN.

npc.name: Danfuto Zihyama
npc.voice: Measured, unhurried, the cadence of someone who rules on disputes and expects to be believed. Quotes precedent the way others quote family.

end.says: Mind the linen on your way out. It's covering the part of this room I can't yet account for.

doubt.says: Then you recopy it. Carefully. In a hand that looks like the old hand. There's a tablet in that drawer nobody's ruled from in three hundred years, and I dust it every dimming anyway. Don't ask me why that one. I've stopped asking.

greet.says: Sit if you're sitting. The room's half-gutted but the chair still holds, and I don't stop for audiences. You want the clerk, the clerk is me, and I'm listening even with my arm in a wall.

solen.says: She reads the failure logs. Third audit she's survived, and each one cost her something she doesn't name. I've watched her sit in that chair across from me and rule against her own office to keep the record clean. You don't do that if you're sleeping well.

choices.text: Why the chairs so close together?

chairs.says: So nobody performs. Knees nearly touching, you can't lie big in that chair. My grandmother arbitrated here before me and she said the distance between the chairs is the whole of Continuant law: you don't get space to become somebody else halfway through a dispute.

choices.text: And when the record itself is wrong?

repair.says: Conduit from the dimming-cycle relay. It failed during the last audit week and Merid Solen's office flagged it before I did, which tells you how nervous they've gotten about anything that stops. Even a fan. Even a light.

reactions.grief: The wire slips their grip; they restate the death like a docket entry, twice, hearing neither attempt.
reactions.shock: Their eyes go to the still fan first, willing it to turn, before conceding what lies beneath it.
reactions.bribed: Itemizes the offer like an exhibit, then cites the ruling that ended the last clerk who took one.
reactions.accused: For once no precedent comes to hand; they stand, wipe their palms, and ask the charge restated for the record.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise hang unfinished on the slate air, already waiting for the request priced into it.
reactions.questioned: Answers without looking up from the wire, citing schedule and precedent in the tone of a ruling already filed.
reactions.threatened: Quotes the statute against coercion, section and verse, steady until the last syllable betrays them by thinning.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Does not deny it; files the correction aloud, dates and all, as if accuracy could settle what the lie unsettled.
reactions.authority_arrives: Rises, dusts the linen from their knees, and takes the party's chair, leaving the bench empty without being told.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Names the hour for the record, then sits very still; no precedent covers a room that moves.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects before any evidence is offered, citing three rulings that cleared worse suspects, faster than fairness allows.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits the bench cannot reach that far, then offers the only mercy they own: the plea, entered, dated, preserved.

npc.description: Danfuto Zihyama kneels inside the opened half of the room, arm deep in a conduit chase, pulling wire by feel. Tools are laid out on a linen cloth in order of use. The work does not pause for a visitor; only the head turns, briefly, and turns back.

lore.name: The Precedent Drawer
lore.description: Under the clerk's bench, a drawer of slate tablets, each scored with a ruling and a date going back further than any living memory. The oldest tablet has been recopied twice — the letters are newer than the stone. On its back, worn smooth by thumbs: the same ruling, in a hand nobody recognizes, about a dispute over seed-share during a dimming. The ruling has never needed revision. That is the point of it.

content.name: The Arbitration Room, Terrace 252
content.description: The ceiling fan should be turning. It is not, and the stillness it leaves has weight, though the sun-strip burns full through dust-white linen hung where a wall was cut away. Two chairs face each other on slate, close enough that knees nearly touch. Beside the clerk's bench, stencilled on the paneling: BOTH PARTIES SEATED BEFORE THE CLERK SPEAKS.

npc.name: Viosksaesothys Lyakov
npc.voice: Terse, preoccupied, speaking in the grammar of someone who has stopped translating the deep for surface ears — words correct, arrangements slightly sanctified.

fold.says: It nests. That is not motion the way you mean it. Take the wand — it wants a hand that still believes in distances.

choices.text: Take the wand and let them sleep.

greet.says: You came in on the wrong recursion. Sit anyway — the fold forgives position, eventually. What Saturn keeps, keeps you.

reactions.grief: Stops mid-stroke; the death reaches them as a position finally confirmed, and they say the name twice, too formally.
reactions.shock: Their body answers before its cause, as everything here does; they are on the floor, unsure of having fallen.
reactions.bribed: Asks, sincerely, what the offer is made of, as though matter might recurse; declines without weighing anything.
reactions.accused: The accusation reaches them like a misdelivered position report; they inspect their own hands sincerely before speaking.
reactions.flattered: Knows the praise is bait and warms to it anyway, hunger outliving judgment; thanks come too quickly, too softly.
reactions.questioned: Cites their position from the stencilled plate, unbothered, patient as a litany the questioner fails to recognize.
reactions.threatened: The threat registers as custody, nearly comfort; only their thumb, whitening on the stylus, admits what it costs.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Doesn't defend the words; asks which of them the room corroborates, hunger plain, and etches the discrepancy into foil.
reactions.authority_arrives: Rises into a posture six years discontinued, greeting jurisdiction as expected arrival, eyes lowered in deference past feeling.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Doesn't flinch; the fold moves always, but this arrived after its cause, and that inversion unsettles them more than impact.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Offers no defense; recites, instead, where that person cannot have been, each alibi a small vindication they plainly savor.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses without ritual, then stays anyway, stylus idle, confessing low that keeping was never theirs to command.

npc.description: Asleep in the fold's crook, curled where no maintenance code permits rest, one hand still closed around a foil stylus. They wake without startling, as though sleep here were a duty roster like any other.

lore.name: A tension-wand of wound foil
lore.description: Left resting against the mica, its tip still faintly humming — tuned to a frequency the fold stopped answering years ago.

content.name: The Nesting Fold
content.description: A mica shelf hangs a hand's width above the floor, and the floor is six meters below where the shelf was built to meet it — the fold has already begun repositioning, and the work was abandoned mid-translation. Wound foil drapes between them like ligature, violet-deep, holding nothing to nothing. The chamber recurs: every angle opens onto an angle of itself, a throat of folded lamina swallowing its own geometry. Sound arrives before its cause, or after — the ear cannot say which, and stops asking. Along one plate, stencilled in a hand that pressed hard: POSITION LAST CONFIRMED SIX YEARS AGO. Nothing here was cleared away; the leaving was itself left.

npc.name: Sozodan Resvekitsyn
npc.voice: Short answers, precise about possessions and dates. He thaws when asked about the room itself, not the dispute.

greet.says: If you've come about the room, the answer hasn't changed since yesterday. She holds the let, I hold the debt against it, and neither of us is wrong.

choices.text: Why is the kettle full if the stove is cold?
Whose marks are those on the bedframe?
Are you the one moving out?

counts.says: Both of ours. She counts days, her nephew counts weeks, and the difference is the three weeks I sat with her husband while he died. Nobody paid for those. Nobody disputes them either. They just sit there in the wood.

choices.text: I hope whoever gets the room keeps the marks.

kettle.says: She always sets it for me before she goes to her sister's. Six years of that. I fill it now so the room doesn't get used to being empty. Stupid. But there it is.

choices.text: Six years is a long let.

leaving.says: I'm moving to the stove-block, into the shift lodge. Cheaper, and the room was never mine — I rented the corner, she rented the room. The landlord died and now the let is worth arguing over. It wasn't worth anything while he lived.

reactions.grief: Keeps folding until the corners will not square, then sits down on the floor among the linens.
reactions.shock: Looks at the body once, then cannot stop looking at the cold kettle behind it.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against three weeks of unpaid sitting, finds the arithmetic insulting, repeats the figure once.
reactions.accused: Recites his last nine days by date and hour, level until the ninth, where his voice gives.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise pass without answer and starts describing the stove's quirks, his one safe subject.
reactions.questioned: Answers in dates, each day accounted for, and does not ask why anyone is counting.
reactions.threatened: Asks whether the threat covers the debt too, since that is the only part he cannot repack.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Concedes the smaller error in full detail, dates and amounts, and will not look up while doing it.
reactions.authority_arrives: Squares the blanket's corners before answering, as if jurisdiction were another inspection he could pass.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches the kettle before it slides and holds it with both hands, eyes on the painted words above.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names six years of evenings she set the kettle, as if routine were proof of anything.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses without softening it, then names the one who could help, and the exact date she returns.

npc.description: Sozodan Resvekitsyn folds a blanket with the corners squared, the way you fold linens you expect to hand over for inspection. A second bundle, already wrapped, sits apart on the trunk. He keeps glancing at the cold kettle.

lore.name: Two nail rows on the bedframe
lore.description: The bedframe carries two columns of nail holes, punched and filled, punched again. One column counts days of the widow's tenancy, kept by her. The other counts by weeks, kept by whoever rented the room before her and expects it back. The two counts disagree by three weeks. Both stop mid-column.

content.name: San Daglovotre
content.description: A kettle sits on the stove, cold, full. Nothing else in the room is still: a bed half stripped, a trunk half packed, the curtain across the doorway lifting and falling with the draught. On the curtain rod, painted over twice, the words ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE.

npc.name: Dosexa the Laurel-Exiled
npc.voice: Precise, procedural, but slower at the edges — a clerk who has said the same sentences for years and still means them.

exile.says: I wore the laurel once. Continuant honor, first rank. I ruled against a farm-deck closure and the council ruled me out of it. The name stayed. The work stayed too — smaller room, same verb. A dispute settled is a dispute settled, wherever it happens.

choices.text: Ask if they regret the ruling.

greet.says: Court is closed. If you have a claim, come back at second bell. If you have something else, say it while I pack.

choices.text: Ask why the room is split down the middle.

leave.says: Second bell. Bring your claim written or bring it plain, but bring it seated.

split.says: Two claimants, one room, no winner. The ribbon is not decoration. It is the ruling. Each side keeps what it swept.

regret.says: The farm still grows. The people it fed still eat. I sit in a smaller chair. You do the arithmetic. I did, years ago, and I keep doing it in case the answer changes.

choices.text: Ask whether the council would take them back.

council.says: Factor Solen audits everyone. She has audited me twice and let me keep the room both times. That is not a welcome. It is not nothing either. I have stopped trying to name it.

reactions.grief: Told the name, Dosexa keeps checking tokens but skips one, and goes on recounting the deceased's last claim unprompted.
reactions.shock: They sit without deciding to, which they have not done in years, the roll still open in their lap.
reactions.bribed: The offer is entered as a claim lacking standing, and the refusal comes slower than Dosexa's rulings do.
reactions.accused: Mid-roll, the hands stop, and Dosexa defends a ruling from years ago, as if this were that case.
reactions.flattered: Praise of the laurel lands wrong, and Dosexa corrects the title before accepting a word about the work.
reactions.questioned: Dosexa answers from the list, each movement dated, as if the question had arrived as a filed form.
reactions.threatened: Dosexa reads the threat back as procedure, voice level until "again" slips in.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The contradiction lands and Dosexa corrects the record first, the apology arriving late and half-formed behind it.
reactions.authority_arrives: The packing stops at the threshold, and Dosexa recites the room's closure procedure, offering nothing personal to rule on.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder pauses nothing, and Dosexa announces a continuance while the list in their hand goes unsteady.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Dosexa demands the accusation in writing first, then admits, quieter, that the relief underneath was not neutral.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea exceeds the room's jurisdiction and Dosexa says exactly that, then stays there anyway, listening past the refusal.

npc.description: Dosexa the Laurel-Exiled stacks writ-tokens into a cloth roll, one at a time, checking each against a list. Their uniform is deep blue gone grey at the cuffs. They work standing, as if sitting down now would mean starting over.

lore.name: The Split Mat
lore.description: The rubber matting is two mats, cut from one piece and seamed down the middle with blue ribbon. Under the seam, scratched into the floor, is the stencil: BOTH PARTIES SEATED BEFORE THE CLERK SPEAKS. The cut is old and clean. Someone divided the room on purpose and both sides have kept their half swept ever since.

content.name: The Arbitration Room
content.description: Voices flatten in here. Whatever you say comes back at the floor, like the room was built to end arguments fast. Two chairs face each other across a strip of rubber matting, both pulled off-center. A ribbon marks half the room in deep blue; the other half is bare. Someone is packing up.

npc.name: Xumaxeavel Ranione
npc.voice: Careful, procedural, a habit of counting things before she'll say anything about them. Continuants are taught that care is a verb you perform, and it shows.

open.says: A hall. I looked in once, from the cut edge, holding a lamp I had no business holding. Benches in rings, rising and rising, judged against a floor you could stand four hundred people on and each of them would still be an arm's length from the seat that outweighs their house. Somebody governed from up there — at this scale, *govern* stops being a council room and becomes weather. My creed says what sustains the generation is sacred, and I looked into that hall and understood we have been keeping the parish while the cathedral sits dark above us. Whatever used to rule from there doesn't need it anymore, and I have decided, like Solen, that not knowing the rest is a reasonable choice.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll mind the water.
A hall like that doesn't just go quiet.

greet.says: If you're here for the water, the deep pool's shut — reading's off the gauge and I'm not signing for it. The shallow one's sound. Mind the open section; the deck's cut back to girder and it drops clean away.

choices.text: Why is half the room opened up?
What's through there, past the open wall?
The shallow pool's fine. I'll leave you to it.

probe_a.says: Depth and temperature against the rated swimmer, both at once — fused quartz doesn't fog and doesn't lie. The mica underneath does both. When this pool was cut, somebody assumed a person, and I am here to tell you the assumption was generous.

probe_b.says: Brennick's. Brennick's got a cough the clinic says is nothing, and the roster says this shift is mine to cover because I said it was. Down here that's how it works — you write your name where the work is, or the work goes unwitnessed, and unwitnessed work is how the Nave forgets it has edges.

probe_c.says: Repair order came down four months ago and the crew that came for it were Rindwalker, good ones, methodical. They opened the west wall, worked nine days, and then the reports stopped being detailed. What's left open stays open until someone above me decides knowing is safer than not knowing. She hasn't. I've stopped asking.

reactions.grief: She wets a hand in the shallow pool and marks the rite of care twice before her voice will work.
reactions.shock: The gauge rings off the tile where she lets it fall; she counts paces to the body and cannot stop.
reactions.bribed: She quotes the reading she would falsify, prices the offer against a swimmer's margin, and finds the arithmetic insulting.
reactions.accused: Her count stalls mid-number; she begins it again, quieter, as if the accusation were a bad reading she could re-take.
reactions.flattered: She corrects the praise downward — two sound pools, not a miracle — then waits for what the flattery came to buy.
reactions.questioned: She answers in tallies — laps logged, gauges read, hours kept — as if numbers were a floor to stand on.
reactions.threatened: She names what she will not sign for, then the regulation, then the door, in that order, voice level throughout.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She builds no second story; she re-reads her own words like a faulty gauge and amends them, line by line.
reactions.authority_arrives: She squares the roster clip with a thumbnail before speaking, and volunteers nothing about whose name it carries.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She watches the black-green water climb its own rim, higher than any gauge she signed, and forgets the count entirely.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She gives the count of every sound swim-day that person logged, quick and exact, and only then asks who decided.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She offers what her office holds — shallow water, a measured hour, dry cloth — and admits it is not enough.

npc.description: Xumaxeavel Ranione stands calf-deep in the nearer pool, dragging a fused-quartz gauge along the rim where the mica layers have let go, reading it, shaking her head, reading it again. The shift roster clipped to the far gantry carries a name that is not hers, and she has not corrected it.

lore.name: The Rating Plate
lore.description: Bolted to the emptied pool's nearest girder is a brass plate, screwed down over three older plates beneath it, each a few millimetres proud of the last. The top plate rates the pool for forty bathers and a depth of two metres; the plates under it, readable where the screws have backed out a quarter-turn, rate the same basin for four hundred bathers, then for four thousand, the depth figure on the oldest legible as a number no bathhouse could honour and no Continuant inspector has ever scratched out.

content.name: The Hull Bathhouse
content.description: The heat sits low, ankle-deep along the tile where the pools breathe it out, while the upper dark stays cold enough that the fused-quartz canopy above sweats a slow condensation back down. Half the floor has been opened to its frame — layered mica lifted in great peeled sheets, girders standing bare where a pool used to hold them — and the untouched half keeps its water black-green and still, wide enough that a swimmer crossing it would vanish from view before reaching the far edge. Stencilled along the rim, in letters a hand could span: POOL DEPTH EXCEEDS RATED SWIMMER.

npc.name: Lulz-bin Nanz
npc.voice: Brisk, tallying. Talks in loads and destinations, thaws into gossip if you ask where something came from.

knot.says: Cut a route out when a route stops being worth carrying. That one was a run to a tunnel mouth that got sealed — no reason posted, no reason given. The knot stays spliced so I remember the road existed. Everything moves, but not everything moves forever.

load.says: Ward goods. The Wards send down what the Commons won't store and nobody up there wants counted. What comes up is salvage, and salvage is Rindwalker business mostly. I run the rope, I don't ask the rope why.

choices.text: Does the Braid know what's on these crates?

braid.says: The Braid knows before the crates do. Half of what I lower, someone's already asked me about by name. If you want to know what's in them, ask before the next run, not after.

choices.text: I'll come back before the next run.

greet.says: You're not on my manifest. Doesn't matter — you're light, and light rides free. Going down or up?

choices.text: Why does everything go down and nothing come up?

sleep.says: I sleep at the brake the way a cart-driver sleeps at the reins. Close 266 runs me, the rope runs me. There was a keeper before me who left the brake loose one night — the cage took his leg at the second landing. So no, I don't sleep in a bunk.

choices.text: Your wrist cord has a splice in it.

reactions.grief: The hand comes off the brake lever; they keep saying the name back like a weight they're refusing to log.
reactions.shock: They back into the cage and pull the tarp over nothing, hands doing freight work their eyes have quit.
reactions.bribed: A rate gets quoted first, then refused — a misremembered load is a route that stops being worth carrying.
reactions.accused: For once the tally stalls; they repeat the charge in freight terms, slower than any run they've ever made.
reactions.flattered: They warm to it for a breath, then start auditing the praise for what it's trying to buy.
reactions.questioned: They give the answer as a tally — date, load, destination — as if the question were a manifest request.
reactions.threatened: A sealed route scares them worse than a blade ever has; the bluster drains and they say nothing worth logging.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught with a contradicting manifest, they confess the smaller crime — an overloaded cage — to bury the larger question.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the brake lever and the overloaded crates before the door finishes opening.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They read the shudder as load shift out of habit, then run out of explanations when the cage sways empty.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The named one once bought copper pipe off their rope; they blurt the fact, then hear how it sounds.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Every working route is theirs to name and none goes where the plea needs; they offer rope anyway.

npc.description: Lulz-bin Nanz sits up from under the tarp already talking, as if sleep were a pause in the workday and not a break in it. A knotted cord at the wrist, frayed at one end where a route was cut out and a new one spliced in.

lore.name: The tally slate on the drum housing
lore.description: A slate hangs by the winch, chalked with two columns: cargo down, cargo up. The down column runs the full board. The up column has three entries, all months old.

content.name: The Winch Room, Close 266
content.description: The lift cage hangs a hand's width below the landing, close enough to step down into rather than onto. Crates of webbing and copper pipe crowd the platform past the stenciled MAX LOAD POSTED, DO NOT EXCEED, and everything in here has gone the pale green of old grease over paint. Under a folded tarp in the corner, someone is asleep with one hand still on the brake lever.

npc.name: Ketin-Fetonga
npc.voice: Clipped, practical. Talks in splice terms. Offers nothing twice.

end.says: I do. Leave it on the bench.

damp.says: It comes up through the floor, not the wall. Anyone who's mended along this row knows that. We told the square. The square told the council. The council sent a form.

sign.says: Old rule. Knots checked before return. Every cord that leaves this loft comes back inspected, or the whole hanging is suspect. Costs an afternoon a week. Saves whole nets.

stop.says: You weren't interrupting. We were agreeing badly. Sit if you're sitting, stand if you're standing.

work.says: South wall took damp. We gutted it to the frame. It goes back up dry or not at all — wet work in a net loft is how you lose a season's twine. Everything that was hanging there is on your left. Don't rearrange it.

choices.text: Damp, this far in from the open air?

agree.says: Whether to redo the header knots or splice around them. He splices. I say a splice in a header knot is a promise you can't keep. He's been doing it twenty years longer than me. He's also wrong.

choices.text: Let me look at the nets.

greet.says: Mind the cords overhead. If you're here about a net, set it on the bench and I'll look at it when I look at it.

choices.text: What happens to the half that's torn open?
What's the sign above the twine for?

reactions.grief: Asks who it was, gets the name, and spends the rest of the day re-checking every knot that person tied.
reactions.shock: Does not move until the stove door bangs shut, and afterward cannot say what they saw first.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the old rule back, word for word, and turns to the next cord with the offer uncounted.
reactions.accused: Stops mid-splice and offers their hands for inspection, since everything in this loft gets checked, themselves now included.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit without thanks, then asks what needs mending that brought the visitor around.
reactions.questioned: Answers in the same flat order every time, hours first, then who else was in the loft.
reactions.threatened: Their voice comes out a size too small, and they agree to terms they have no intention of keeping.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats nothing, which is answer enough, and goes back to a splice they had already finished.
reactions.authority_arrives: Greets the official with the flat patience of someone whose last report came back as a form.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Watches the twine ranks swing and says, flat, that it came up through the floor last time too.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Snaps that whoever named them has never inspected a cord in their life, then bends lower over the frame.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Starts to say no, then lists every office that turned the same plea away, running out of breath.

npc.description: Ketin-Fetonga keeps one hand flat on the mending frame while the other sorts twine by feel, eyes already on you. The other worker drifts back to the stove without being told.

lore.name: The gauge board
lore.description: A slat by the stove holds a row of knotted short cords, each labeled with a patch of hull-scrapped rubber. One knot, worn shiny, has no label. Ketin-Fetonga touches it every time they pass, and never explains it.

content.name: Kebihi's Net Loft
content.description: The cold sits in the east half, where the opened wall lets the corridor air through; the west stays warm off the curing stove. Twine hangs in ranks across the low ceiling, drying. Two people stand over a half-mended net, and they stop talking when you come in. Green-grey sacking is stacked everywhere.

npc.name: Bemion-Kiloglu
npc.voice: Quick, clause-heavy, the cadence of someone used to being interrupted by the line; answers arrive before questions finish.

deep.says: I walked the true arteries once, when I was young enough to be given the long runs. You come around a bend and the corridor is wide as a city square and smooth as a throat, and you understand you have been living in the fine hairs of something's head. It didn't look at me. That's the honest report: it didn't look at me, and I have never stopped being grateful, or stopped wanting it to.

choices.text: Thank them and let them eat.

room.says: These cells were poured for one sleeper each, and each sleeps six now, because the arteries run hot and everyone who works them wants a bunk near the glass where the hum comes through. It's not crowding. It's choosing. The Drift holds nothing, so we hold each other, and the basalt holds us all — bad math that has worked for three generations.

choices.text: Ask about the knotted cord on the doorframe.

work.says: The wand reads the artery's pulse — raw, before the terminals pretty it. I've carried it twenty years and it has never once told me a lie, only things I wished weren't true. Lately it stutters at the deep junctions, half a beat late, like a runner who's looked over their shoulder. Mercury doesn't stutter. Mercury answers before you knock.

choices.text: Ask what's down at those junctions.

greet.says: You're standing in the run-lane. Not a complaint — nobody's run through here in nine days, which is its own kind of news. Sit if you can find a knee's worth of space. I'm Bemion-Kiloglu; the hyphen is my mother's and my routefather's, and I answer to either half.

choices.text: Ask why the cells are so overfull.
Ask what the signal-wand is for.

family.says: Four heights, four people who've slept behind this door. My routefather hung the lowest knot; he was a short man who ran the axial relay and died of it, which is to say he died of standing still at last. My daughter hangs the top one — she's with a relay westward, and I get her knot's news before I get her voice.

choices.text: Ask what the wand is finding lately.

reactions.grief: They lay a thumb on the doorframe's third knot, the height at which the dead stopped growing.
reactions.shock: Their eyes sweep, return, sweep, reading the scene at gauge-speed and failing, for once, to file it.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets the creed instead: the wand has never once lied, and neither will they, not for that.
reactions.accused: The quick clauses stop; they hold the wand out flat, letting its readings answer instead.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads to them like a prettified terminal, and they go quiet, waiting for the raw pulse underneath the compliment.
reactions.questioned: Asked where they've been, they finish the question aloud and answer it, junction by junction, like reading a pulse.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets answered before it finishes, level as a gauge, because fear stutters and mercury does not.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they add junction numbers nobody requested, and hear, half a beat late, the wand's stutter in their own voice.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official is watched like weather, gauged for pressure, and the first answer moves before the title has finished.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They stand into the shudder, wand raised, and for the first time in twenty years a reading frightens them.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name is barely settled before they're defending its owner — junction logs, bunk-watches — for someone they never trusted.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Powerless past the glass, they fall back on bad math — a bunk, the bowl, whatever holding is left.

npc.description: Bemion-Kiloglu sits in the doorway of cell eleven with a signal-wand in one hand and a bowl in the other, neither attended to, watching the corridor gauge as if it were weather. Their sleeves are seamed with copper braid worn shiny at the cuff, and they have wrapped the doorframe in knotted cord at four heights — a tall family's map, or a low one's.

lore.name: The Third-Rail Knock Plate
lore.description: Set into every cell door is a small basalt plate, and the plate on cell eleven has been worn through to the glass beneath — not by hands but by knuckles, thousands of times a shift, by men tapping the pulse of the message-line into the door as a wake-up call that outlived itsoriginal wire. The plate is dished a full centimeter deep. Somebody's grandmother tapped this door, and somebody's grandchild taps it now, same spot, same rhythm, because the rhythm is the only address the arteries have ever needed.

content.name: The Bulkhead Billet
content.description: A doorway hangs a hand's width above the floor of the gallery, and no stair meets it — the cells were cut for feet that will never arrive at that height again. The Bulkhead Billet is a honeycomb of cast basalt cells let into the black-glass bulkhead, each meant for one sleeper, each now holding bunks stacked three deep with transit-men's kit jammed into the corners. What is missing is what the room was built around: silence, and the room between bunks to stand in. Lead-grey paint has been gone over so often the stencil — BILLET SEALS AT SHIFT CHANGE — sits a finger lower than its ghost beneath it. The hum of Mercury's arteries comes up through the glass and does the sleeping for half the residents.

npc.name: Wetsezanu Rarafu
npc.voice: Terse, procedural. Kindness expressed as a completed task, not a sentence.

greet.says: Not my shift, but the cups still need boiling. If you're here for the aches, sit. First one's free — the stencil doesn't lie.

ask_left.says: Tyfrelandra. Took the big couch and went, same day. The room misses the heat she carried. So do the regulars. Now — arm on the rest, or let me finish the rack.

reactions.grief: Talks far too long about the dead one's first season here, hands working a rack they no longer see.
reactions.shock: Drops a full cup and does not flinch when it scalds, eyes fixed on nothing.
reactions.bribed: Refuses by reciting the price list, first visit free, and turns back to the basin.
reactions.accused: Stops mid-rinse, lets the water run over their wrists, and answers only when the cup is dry.
reactions.flattered: Mentions the apron is borrowed and the method is not theirs, and waits, unmoved, for the actual request.
reactions.questioned: Gives the day's movements in the order the racks demand, and not one detail more.
reactions.threatened: Asks whether the threat covers the room or only them, because either way the cups still need boiling.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats the false detail word for word, then stops mid-sentence and starts stacking cups that are already stacked.
reactions.authority_arrives: Becomes twice as procedural, offers the free first visit, and cannot finish the sentence about the keeper.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Grips the rack until the shaking stops, counts the cups twice, and only then lets go.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks more in the named one's defense than all week, then refuses to say how they know.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Cannot grant the plea, so boils water and warms what cloth they have, never meeting the asker's eyes.

npc.description: Wetsezanu Rarafu stands at the wash basin in a borrowed blue apron too wide in the shoulders, rinsing cups and setting them upside down on buckram. They work in the order the racks demand, not the order the hands want.

lore.name: The carried marks
lore.description: The doorframe is notched at hip height, two deep cuts per generation, tallying seasons of old ache treated here. The newest notch is unfinished.

content.name: Tyfrelandra's Cupping Parlor
content.description: The cold sits low along the floorboards; the brazier's warmth stops at knee height and goes no higher. The narrow room creaks when the corridor door swings. A big couch has been dragged from the far wall, and its rectangle of dust-white stone stays clean where everything else is not. Above the curtain rail, stenciled: FIRST VISIT FREE, ASK THE KEEPER.

npc.name: Hiyi-Yokan
npc.voice: Clipped, transactional, amused at the edges. She talks like she is counting your words.

open.says: It's not a place and not a person. Runners carry knotted cords, and the knots are routes — who trusts whom, what moved where, when. Fold every cord together and you get something faster than any council posting. Right now it's carrying word that the terminal postings have gone strange. I've seen three of them myself. The motif indices don't resolve.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll watch the terminals.
You shouldn't have told me any of that.

greet.says: Half the house is torn up, so if you came to lose dice, come back Thursday. If you came to talk, talk while I work.

choices.text: Why chain in a dice parlor?
The stencil says no credit. Who's it for?
So what is the Braid, really?
Never mind. Good luck with the chain.

probe_a.says: Games hang from it. Counters, stakes, the tally-cord for the house cut. Resin track keeps it from chewing the tables. Nothing here is mine, so nothing here gets to break.

probe_b.says: For whoever runs this room after me. Nobody stays. I stencil everything I know onto the walls before I go — that one, the payout rates, which floor tile is loose. A stranger should be able to run this place from the writing alone.

probe_c.says: The room answers to the house, the house answers to whoever moves through it. I answer to the Braid, same as any runner who stops here. Someone has to know where the cord ends.

reactions.grief: She names the dead runner's route without being asked, then keeps naming the intermediate stops until her voice stops working.
reactions.shock: Her teeth stay set on the chain link through all of it, longer than sense allows.
reactions.bribed: Offered double, she quotes the till stencil instead, since nothing on the floor is hers to sell.
reactions.accused: She sets the chain down unbroken, which for her is fury, and asks if the accusation carries a stake.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands harder than she wants it to, and she covers by repricing the job in front of everyone.
reactions.questioned: She answers in numbered points, as if each word costs, then names the hour she'll bill for the interruption.
reactions.threatened: Her amusement drops out of her voice mid-threat; she watches the door's edge instead of the speaker.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She prices the evidence like anything on her floor, admits the knot, and keeps talking past where talking helps.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her hands keep working, but she angles her body between the official and the half-opened wall where the tally-cord hangs.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She is under a table before the tiles stop moving, checking the hung games by touch, and miscounts them.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She recites the three nights that person went broke at her tables, as close to loyalty as she gets.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says no in the same voice she quotes odds with, then works the chain too hard all shift.

npc.description: Hiyi-Yokan crouches under the opened half of the parlor, threading new chain through a cast resin track with her teeth set tight. She doesn't look up until the link seats. Then she does.

lore.name: The house cord
lore.description: Behind the till hangs a knotted cord, older than any furniture in the room, its pattern running the full length of the wall. Regulars pay out losses against it — a knot untied per debt, and the untied section stays short. The knots record every route the house's founding runner ever walked, and Hiyi-Yokan re-learns the pattern by hand each time one comes loose, because the cord is the only copy.

content.name: The Dice Parlor
content.description: The floor is cast resin, poured in tiles, and each one flexes a little underfoot — warm where the sunstrip hits, slick near the bar. Half the room is opened to its frame, chain strung where a wall was. Two people stop arguing when the curtain moves. On the intact half, stenciled over the till: HOUSE TAKES ONE IN TEN, NO CREDIT.

npc.name: Deineth of Reiltrochwy
npc.voice: Talks in checks: seal, stamp, tension. Never greets, never thanks. A joint that passes is the only praise given.

drum.says: Unsigned. No seal, no service — that's the whole law of it. The stamp is two days late, so a finished splice sits in a drum while a district runs on the old pair. Take the offcut to the ledger. Tell them Deineth wants the stamp.

greet.says: Mind the tray. Anything with a tag is spoken for. Talk while I crimp.

choices.text: Why is the big drum stopped?

reactions.grief: They ask who sealed the dead one's last splice, then crimp four joints without counting any.
reactions.shock: The tray goes over in their hands, tagged cable across the floorboards, and they leave it where it falls.
reactions.bribed: They decline in the terms of their trade — no seal, no service — and set the coin aside for the ledger.
reactions.accused: They answer the accusation by demanding the failed joint, though their thumb keeps finding the last crimp and pressing it.
reactions.flattered: They credit the stamp before the hand that made the joint, then ask what the flatterer wants sealed.
reactions.questioned: Deineth answers with place, hour, and tension held, item by item, then waits as though a stamp should follow.
reactions.threatened: They file the threat under unsigned work and say so, flat, without lifting their eyes from the seam.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They give the false detail again, slower, as though repetition could stamp it true.
reactions.authority_arrives: The crimping does not stop, but they angle the ledger toward the door before the official is halfway across.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their first thought is the drum: brake, banding, tension on the nearest run, checked before the shaking stops.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They say the named one's tension readings always ran short of spec, and the relish in it surprises them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Their hands can fix a joint but not a stamp, and they say so without the usual checks, plainly, twice.

npc.description: Deineth of Reiltrochwy works braced against the bench, a cable case open under a lamp shade gone warm grey with soot. Three crimps, a turn of the ferrule, three crimps again. Their eyes never leave the seam.

lore.name: The Held Splice
lore.description: The stopped drum holds a splice that may not run. Its brass ferrule carries no seal, and above the bench the stencil reads: SPLICE LOG MUST BE SIGNED. Deineth will not close the case until someone with a stamp countersigns, so the cable sits dead and the brake stays off.

content.name: Koq's Splice Loft
content.description: The take-up drum sits stopped with its brake off. Deineth works at the bench and does not stop, while tagged cable waits in piles two deep on the floorboards. The roof ridge stands at shoulder height; spools in iron banding climb to meet it, and cold through the wall seams keeps the brazier busy.

npc.name: Synedd Trychys
npc.voice: Clipped, transactional. Rates, routes, times. Everything is either out or in, owed or settled.

ramp.says: The small axle ones. The wide carts stick at the turn and you'll be backing the whole line down. Third slot clears by the bell. Talk to me then, not before.

greet.says: Renting or returning? Renting: half hour minimum, coin up front. Returning: notches get hammered flat, no arguments. If you want the ramp to the market tier, wait for the third slot to clear.

choices.text: Which carts go up the ramp fastest?

reactions.grief: She marks three more tokens before the name lands, then tells the queue to hold, which she has never done.
reactions.shock: Her count of the waiting carts runs long twice; her eyes are on the body, not the ramp.
reactions.bribed: The coin sits on her tally bar through two calls of the queue before she pushes it back.
reactions.accused: The punch splits a token; she demands a time and slot, as if the accusation were an unpaid rate.
reactions.flattered: The praise buys a look up from the ledger and, against her own rates, half off the next slot.
reactions.questioned: Her day comes back as a route with times, recited while she marks the next token.
reactions.threatened: She names the threat back as a price, level, while the punch trembles against the tally bar.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She restates her numbers slower, the way she talks to drunks, and the second count convinces no one.
reactions.authority_arrives: The yard's rates come out of her in order, unasked, before the official is halfway to the bar.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her slot calls keep their rhythm while her hands count the ramp a third time.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She recites every late return she holds on them, dates included, faster than anything she has said all day.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea has no rate, and that absence stops her mid-stamp longer than any refusal would.

npc.description: Synedd Trychys stands at the tally bar with a punch in one hand and a ledger under one arm, calling out slot numbers to a queue that reaches the gate. She marks, she waves, she marks again. She has not sat down.

lore.name: The lead tally bar
lore.description: Each cart slot has a bar of hammered lead set into the ramp rail. Carters notch it with a punch when a cart leaves and hammer the notch flat when it returns. The new bars are unmarked except one, stamped years ago with a name no one renting now answers to.

content.name: The Cart Yard of Long Account
content.description: A cart rolls past you as you step in, its iron banding bright and unpitted. The yard is rebuilt stone and off-white lime wash, all of it too clean to be old. Carts wait three deep on a ramp that climbs steeper than a cart ought to like. A stencil above the gate reads: RETURN CARTS BY DUSK OR PAY THE NIGHT RATE.

npc.name: Mixea Xeuneutrear
npc.voice: Dry, measured, with the patience of someone who reads games the way clerks read ledgers; courtly phrasing worn thin by solitary shifts.

end.says: Mind the foil on your way out — it lies. Gantry only. Rules hold better than reasons.

court.says: His table. His judgment. He mostly doesn't bother, and when he doesn't bother, the game is legal and unruled forever, which is a kind of ruling if you stand far enough back. Once a session ran forty days, and he never rose from the far end of the floor — you could hear the stillness of him all the way up the gantry.

choices.text: What happens to the dice if no one ever rules?

faith.says: My faction would call it stewardship, and they'd be right, and they'd still ask why I stay in an unruled hall covering a missing man's shift. I stay because a game that stopped is not a game that ended, and somebody has to keep the difference intact. That's the whole of my creed and most of my stubbornness.

choices.text: Then I'll leave you to your reading.

greet.says: Stand off the floor, please — reads are taken from the gantry only, and that rule holds even when nobody's meant to be reading. I'm covering Ieth's shift. Ieth stopped coming. Nobody's ruled on whether I'm allowed to ask why.

choices.text: Why did the game stop mid-throw?
Whose court is this meant to be ruled by?
Who plays a game with crate-sized dice?
How long do you intend to keep covering this shift?

stopped.says: The throw was legal, the pips were read, and then the ruling stopped being filed upward and the work stopped being worth doing. Games live on regard, and regard was already gone before the tally slate went cold. I chalk the pips anyway. Rules hold better than reasons do.

choices.text: Do you think someone will come back to rule?
Tell me about the court that used to sit here.

attention.says: Felt is the right word. You are standing in a room that was built for him, sized to him, and he can be bothered to fill it the way weather can be bothered to rain. I don't pray to it. I keep my chalk sharp and my marks clean, because the one thing a reader owes a thing that old is legibility.

choices.text: That's a strange kind of faith.
Has he ever spoken to a reader?

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as oversharing: three sentences too many about the dead one's lever-hand, then a halt mid-clause.
reactions.shock: They go still at the glass, and the reader in them keeps looking for pips on what no longer reads.
reactions.bribed: Bribery they treat as a bad throw: acknowledged, recorded, refused, the refusal chalked where it shows.
reactions.accused: The small economical pulls desert them; the lever travels its whole arc before their hands remember stewardship.
reactions.flattered: Praise finds the small vanity solitary shifts breed; their thanks come a beat too slow, and colder for it.
reactions.questioned: Their account of the shift comes hour by hour in gantry notation, exact as a throw already chalked.
reactions.threatened: They recite the stencilled rule in a clerk's cadence, though the chalk stub snaps between their fingers.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The courtly phrasing thickens, each honorific laid down like foil over glass, and they do not correct the record.
reactions.authority_arrives: Authority gets the writ off the hat brim and a voice half a tone too formal; both are for show.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Procedure outruns fear: they sight the dice first to confirm the throw holds, before admitting anything shook.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The chalk stops mid-mark; they defend a man they privately suspected, since a blamed man is an ended game.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Given a plea beyond a gantry's reach, they refuse gently, absolutely, and then their hands hunt busywork among the levers.

npc.description: Mixea Xeuneutrear sits the crane cage with their boots hooked over the rail, reading a throw through the slot glass with a chalk stub behind one ear and a Continuant writ folded into a hat brim. They work the levers in small, economical pulls, the way a person handles machinery too large to hurry and too old to trust.

lore.name: The Crane's Last Reading
lore.description: Clamped in the operator's cage, a reading-slate still holds the final tally: the throw entered, the court's ruling begun, the stylus lifted mid-stroke on the word *holder*. Beneath it, a well-thumbed crane checklist bears the same six operators' marks, dated shift by shift, for longer than a Nave generation has been alive. The seventh column is empty, and has been since the game stopped.

content.name: Leichaexora
content.description: The floor greets the soles first: foil wound flat into the stone, and where a boot has scuffed it the black glass beneath shows through, cold and slick as still water. Eight dice the size of freight crates lie where they stopped, mid-game, their pips still chalked with reading-marks from the crane gantry. Stencilled above the empty operator's cage, in letters a gantry-man reads at forty paces: DICE READ FROM THE GANTRY ONLY. The floor stretches to a wall so far off its grain goes grey before it arrives.

npc.name: Aefeyn Jahiod
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical in the way a well-worn tool is liturgical — every sentence shaped by repetition into something between instruction and prayer, addressed half to you and half to the work itself.

greet.says: Don't touch the fell. It remembers who does. You're carrying a frequency I've seen in the notation — third layer, the one nobody cut. Sol burns through this room every so often. Doesn't look. Just passes. Take this — the tally-rhythm, if you can hold it. It's not for me to understand why you'd want it.

weaving.says: Weaving? You say that like it's going somewhere. It's holding. That's a different verb entirely — but the Nave doesn't have a word for it, so we use make, and make is a lie we've agreed to tell together, because the alternative is that nobody set this pattern and it still hasn't dropped a thread. Now go. You're adding noise I can hear, and the loom can hear it too.

reactions.grief: The tally fails them mid-count, and they stare at the fell as though it owed them a name.
reactions.shock: Their eyes lift from the fell — something the room has never witnessed — while their hands keep throwing the shuttle alone.
reactions.bribed: Refusal comes once and flat, on the grounds that the fell heard the offer and remembers who does.
reactions.accused: Their graphite-grey hands stop mid-shed for the first time in years, and that stillness is the whole answer.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands somewhere unguarded, and their shuttle slows half a beat before they resume with suspicious precision.
reactions.questioned: Movements are recited in tally-rhythm, flat as the missing index, and the loom hears no lie in it.
reactions.threatened: Threats are noise, and this room forgives noise, so they let it fall and keep counting — a little too fast.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted, they re-weave the lie in liturgical cadence, thread by thread, until even they cannot find where it went false.
reactions.authority_arrives: They give the door's shadow Sol's own courtesy, the kind kept for light that passes without looking.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Twice they count the warp, and for once the liturgy sounds like fear instead of habit.
reactions.someone_else_accused: For the named one they break liturgy entirely, vouching for years of true tension at twice their usual volume.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They offer what holding offers — a rhythm, a counted thread — and say plainly that holding is not saving.

npc.description: Aefeyn Jahiod stands hip-deep in the shed, feeding wound foil into the warp with the unthinking fluency of a body that has memorised its own gestures past the point of consciousness. Their hands are grey with graphite to the wrist, above which the skin has taken on a faint gold cast — not stained, but *informed*, the way a stone decides to be a riverbed. They do not look up.

lore.name: The Selvedge-Tally
lore.description: Bolted to the loom's foot-beam, a strip of lead-grey metal etched with notches — one per completed pass, unnumbered, uncounted in any base the Nave uses for trade or time. The notches do not increase along the strip; they repeat, a rhythm, as though whoever cut them was counting something other than quantity. A second hand began the tally at some point — the notch-style changes mid-way, subtler, more certain — and yet the rhythm did not falter. Whatever the loom is weaving toward, it has been counted by at least two sets of hands who agreed on the rhythm without agreeing on anything else.

content.name: The Patternless Loom
content.description: Before anything is seen, the sound: every footfall arrives already forgiven, swallowed into a hush that is not silence but absorption — as though the room were earwax in the ear of something vast, or as though noise were a debt being quietly repaid on your behalf. Then gold: not the gold of wealth but of filaments under strain, packed graphite gilded at every seam, wound foil running the walls in bands that seem both fresh-flaked and anciently oxidised, which cannot both be true. The loom dwarfs comprehension — its shed opens toward a distance the eye refuses to certify, threads descending from a height no voice has ever reached — and it weaves to a pattern nobody set, its shuttle picking up rhythms like a lullaby remembered by someone who was never a child. Across the beam, stencilled in a hand more administrative than devotional: PATTERN INDEX MISSING WEAVE CONTINUES.

npc.name: Netion al-Khaijiadavael
npc.voice: Measured, liturgical, unbothered by pause; she speaks the way cure happens — slowly, then all at once.

open.says: Nothing, and I have stopped pretending otherwise. The dials quiver where the knitting quickens and say no word I was trained to hear. But you — when the marrow ran hot yesterday, your ports hummed the count back to me. Your apparatus answers what my gauges only gesture at. You are not reading the ship, walker. You are being read by it, and it reads aloud.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry what you gave me.
Read aloud. To whom? I need to sit down.

greet.says: Mind the inlay. The graphite remembers every knuckle that grudges it.

choices.text: Whoever started this quit halfway. Why?
Is nickel the right metal for marrow-work?
The stencil says healing exceeds any recorded rate.
These gauges read nothing. What do you read?
Keep your graphite. I'll come back.

probe_a.says: Quit, or was quitted. The braid here knots backward — a right hand gone wrong, or a left hand gone honest. I have mended other people's abandonments for thirty years and it never once told me which.

probe_b.says: Right is a word for rooms with doors. Nickel consents to be heated and consents to be still, which in the deep is the whole of virtue. Iron argues; gold preens. Nickel abides.

probe_c.says: So it does. The ship knits faster than our oldest tally-keeping, and no one kept the first tally, so the sentence is true the way scripture is true — proven, and proven of something no witness saw begin. I re-ink it every rebuild. Not devotion. Bookkeeping.

reactions.grief: Told who died, she stops mid-seam and leaves the graphite unfinished, the first abandonment in thirty years she cannot mend.
reactions.shock: Inside her the psalm loses its place; outwardly she stands in the gold gloom, mouthing counts no dial taught her.
reactions.bribed: Offered payment to misremember, she treats the bribe as a wound presented too late, and declines it without anger.
reactions.accused: Accused to her face, she keeps working; only the forearm tremor betrays, which she calls instrument noise.
reactions.flattered: Praise from a wanting mouth meets her level gaze; she diagnoses it like fever, asking what needs mending.
reactions.questioned: She recites her movements like a litany, unhurried, an accounting she outgrew needing to believe.
reactions.threatened: Threatened explicitly, she answers in her slow cure-cadence, refusing to let fear set the tempo of her hands.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught between word and gauge, she stops pretending to be slow; the confession arrives all at once, cure-quick.
reactions.authority_arrives: She does not rise for jurisdiction; her nod concedes the required inches while the nickel stays level on her forearm.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room moves without explanation; she lays one palm to the wall, listening for the count beneath the shudder.
reactions.someone_else_accused: A name she has opinions about gets spoken; she offers only the seam's backward knot, testimony she will not translate.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Asked for a cure she does not own, she says so plainly, then keeps saying it, the liturgy failing her.

npc.description: Netion al-Khaijiadavael kneels in the gold gloom of Shell 19 Outboard, pressing packed graphite into a seam of someone else's abandoned knitting, annealed nickel laid out on her forearm like surgical instruments she has already forgiven. The heat pools at her hands and nowhere else, and she works inside that nowhere like a swimmer inside a warmth the water disowns.

lore.name: The Unworn Cradle
lore.description: A half-finished lattice of annealed nickel — someone else's abandoned mend — lies clamped in the marrow-bed's cauls, its solder still bright, its geometry still provisional. Beneath it, scored into the bed's own surface in notation older than any Rindwalker script: a tally, running to a number of marks that does not stop where a number should. Whoever cut it was counting something the bed was doing, and gave up — not from weariness, the marks stay exact — but because the count outlived the thing being counted. The player's translation apparatus renders one fragment: 'rate of making good.'

content.name: Shell 19 Outboard
content.description: Heat is the first falsehood: it pools a hand's breadth off the graphite like breath against a mirror, and the nickel stays cool as a forehead, neither conduction nor convection explaining which is which. Everything here is gold — not gilded but committed, the color of a thing that has decided what it is this week. The walls read too far apart to be walls; sound arrives late, apologising. Stencilled above a seam no hand could reach: HEALING EXCEEDS ANY RECORDED RATE. The room is correct the way a sentence is correct before anyone has spoken it.

npc.name: Khiozaeka Jalab
npc.voice: Measured, kind, unflinching; speaks of the ship's failures the way a healer speaks of symptoms — never with blame, always with tally.

end1.says: Steadiness, mostly. What fails near the heart is its own balance — a wobble in the burn, a doubt in the gold. We lay the foil, draw the filament, and the cradle does the rest. Cause not found, as the wall confesses. Arrested is enough.

end2.says: It hasn't said. But the light gave you floor without argument, and it argues with everything. Sit with that, and don't ask the foil — the foil only knows what it has swaddled, and you are not swaddled yet.

argue.says: Whether the cradle mends what fails or merely persuades the failure to wait. My colleague says persuasion. I say the distinction is vanity — nothing here has failed past waiting in longer than anyone's line. The tally disagrees with both of us, quietly.

greet.says: We were told the floor between us, not you in it. Still — you came in without the light moving aside for you. That answers one of our questions and opens four.

light.says: Choose. That's a word from up-well, where things want. Down here the light behaves as the cradle's pulse behaves — before it, not after. You'll learn to stop asking what it wants. Nothing down here has wanted in an age.

choices.text: You've worked Sol's heart a long time.

tally.says: The room counts itself. We copy it into copper because faith that isn't written decays — or so we hold. The numbers stopped matching anything we call a unit three generations back. We keep copying. Mending and meaning are one verb here, stranger.

choices.text: And what fails, that the cradle steadies?

years.says: Long enough that my hands read foil the way yours read doors. Long enough to know the heart keeps its own ward-book, and that we are the instruments in it, not the physicians. That's not comfort. It's just the floor I stand on.

choices.text: What does the ward-book say about me?

reactions.grief: The name empties the room for them; they keep tallying aloud, numbers gone wrong, and do not notice.
reactions.shock: They freeze at the crescent's edge, the healer's tally abandoning them mid-count, their first uncounted thing in years.
reactions.bribed: They answer with the wall's confession — decline arrested, cause not found — and decline the offer the same way.
reactions.accused: The healer's cadence holds through the accusation, though the tally stumbles once and they ask to hear it twice.
reactions.flattered: Flattery reads to them as symptom; they thank the flatterer warmly and note what the praise wants done.
reactions.questioned: Their answers come as a tally, itemized without resentment, in the cadence of a healer reciting symptoms.
reactions.threatened: Threats they file under symptoms of the threatening; only their voice drops lower, kinder, more unflinching.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: For once the tally fails them; they correct the beloved error slowly, and their hands leave the foil.
reactions.authority_arrives: At the official's whisper both arguments still, theirs included; they yield the floor's words, never its ground.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the ship shudders they read it as a pulse, some decline arriving unswaddled, and bend to the foil.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Named culprit: the colleague who says persuasion; they defend without excusing, correcting the accusation as if it were mispronounced.
