reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They refuse gently, naming exactly what they cannot do, then stay past the refusal as if waiting could mend.

npc.description: Khiozaeka Jalab stands with one hand flat on the wound foil as if listening through it, copper dust worked so deeply into the creases of the knuckles it reads less as dirt than as grain. Their forearms are mapped in pale burn-shadows from the crescent light, and they argue in the low, patient cadence of someone correcting a beloved error.

lore.name: The Counting Sling
lore.description: A filament strung across the cradle's mouth holds a sliver of foil folded fifty-fold; each time the room steadies a failing thing, the sliver ticks over once, and the tally scratched beside it runs past any serviceable number.

content.name: The Steadying Cradle of Last Call
content.description: Light arrives here having already decided what it will do: it pools in one chalk-white crescent, abandons the rest, and returns to the pool as if consulted. Wound foil swaddles a hollow like a bandage about a limb, and filament spans the crescent's edges, drawn taut, tremoring whenever the room steadies something the eye cannot find. The hollow is a cradle the way a sling is a bed — its whole geometry is asymmetry forgiven by use, and two use-circles overlap in it without touching. Two figures stand mid-argument across the foil; at the door's whisper both fall quiet, though neither yields the floor. Chalked high on the wall: DECLINE ARRESTED CAUSE NOT FOUND.

npc.name: Buntrach Rhyddys
npc.voice: Short declaratives, materials named like people, no comfort words. Prayer and repair use the same tense.

open.says: I mend what breaks and I pray over it, same act, always have been. But third shaft down we found notation older than the wall it was cut into — cut first, wall grown after. So now I don't know if we keep the ship or the ship keeps us, and I still light the candle either way. That's the cost. The work doesn't stop for the question.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
Grown after. I don't like that.

greet.says: Counter's open. Horn's for scraping, lead's for nothing you need.

choices.text: Who do you answer to up here?
You said the tunnels said something. What?

probe_a.says: Wicks used to be seated in it. We don't seat them in it anymore. Ask me why on a day I feel like answering.

probe_b.says: The Nave paid for new. New is what you give a stranger. My shop stood four hundred years and it took a season to look like nobody ever loved it.

probe_c.says: Sevin, when she's in. Route-seniors, when she isn't. Nobody asks a chandler what the tunnels said lately, which is a mercy, lately.

reactions.grief: Says the name once, the way they say tallow, then prays over it like a broken thing brought in.
reactions.shock: Looks at the body the way they look at notation cut before its wall — too long, then not at all.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the offer weighs in lead, which is how they say no.
reactions.accused: The extra arms go still before the face does, and they ask to hear it said again, slower.
reactions.flattered: Rations the flattery at one candle's worth, unsoftened, and waits for the request underneath.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day's tally like a litany, wicks and prayers in one breath, unbothered by the counting.
reactions.threatened: Answers the threat with a price — lead, horn, tallow — as if it were an order at the counter.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Admits it fast, then keeps talking — why the wicks stopped being seated, more than anyone asked for.
reactions.authority_arrives: Eyes go first to the rolled lead under the counter, then, without hurry, to the official.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Mends nothing because nothing broke, and that is what puts the shake in their hands.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects in materials, naming what the accused's hands mend all day, as if that counts as testimony.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Lights the single candle the rules allow and lets every still arm finish the refusal.

npc.description: Buntrach Rhyddys is trimming a wick four hands too many, each extra arm moving on its own errand. Behind them a sheet of lead hangs where the old counter burned, stamped in fresh stencil: ONE CANDLE PER PRAYER, TAKE NO MORE.

lore.name: The Waxed Counting Board
lore.description: Set into the counter's end is a slate board scored with tally rows, one per candle sold, each row closed with a smear of wax pressed flat by thumb. The rows go back years — the board is old even though the counter is new, salvaged and reset, some rows burned through by a fire or a fault nobody mentions. The newest row is smeared but not closed, and the count on it runs long by nine candles. Nine too many, or nine owed back.

content.name: Galleinw's Chandler Counter
content.description: A strip of tallow candle wax swings where someone has just set the pan down too hard. Two walkers stand either side of the counter — Buntrach Rhyddys and another, mid-word — and they go quiet when you come in, the way people do over something already said twice. The counter is new copper, unscraped, nothing softened; above it the stencil reads ONE CANDLE PER PRAYER, TAKE NO MORE, and under the counter a lead sheet lies rolled, horn stops at both ends, waiting for whoever wins the argument.

npc.name: Nandra Cheurogenes
npc.voice: Terse, procedural. Names precedents instead of feelings.

end.says: Mine now, until the council says otherwise. Go on.

greet.says: If you're reporting something, say it plain. If you're not, I'm behind.

reactions.grief: She takes down the death-entry form before hearing the name and then cannot remember which box comes first.
reactions.shock: She starts describing the scene in report tense and stops mid-measurement, with her lips still moving.
reactions.bribed: She cites the statute on improper payment, then repeats the offered sum once, like checking arithmetic.
reactions.accused: The stamp stops above the page while she makes them say it again, twice, in the right order.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes her check the complaint log for what they actually want, since compliments here preface requests.
reactions.questioned: Routine questioning gets her last three days recited back section by section, without inflection, before the visitor finishes sitting.
reactions.threatened: Intimidation gets named its own file number, out loud, though the pen has started jumping the line.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted with the ledger entry, she claims a filing error she knows is hers and initialed.
reactions.authority_arrives: She recites the handover formula kept ready for months and sets the key down harder than the ritual needs.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first move is a hand on the report stacks, her second a count of who is still standing.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The absent captain's name lands and she closes the ledger on her own thumb, saying nothing at all.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea gets a precise answer about which office holds the power, and she stays standing after it lands.

npc.description: Nandra Cheurogenes stands at the desk, reading a complaint aloud under her breath before filing it. Green-grey coat, sleeves rolled, a small stubborn stack of finished work at her elbow.

lore.name: The Absent Captain's Stamp
lore.description: A report stamp sits on the desk, handle worn to someone else's grip. Cheurogenes uses it without comment.

content.name: Khakahab's Watch Post
content.description: The smell is oiled copper and old sweat pressed into a planed-timber desk that has been re-glued twice. Reports stack on every surface; half of them belong to a captain who stopped coming. A stencil over the lintel reads REPORT HERE, NOT TO THE CROWD. Nandra Cheurogenes sorts the pile anyway.

npc.name: Zhoek Zodos
npc.voice: Precise, liturgical, the cadence of someone for whom repair is prayer and sloppiness is sin.

open.says: Deeper than the last honest report — below where the teams went quiet, below the layer where the notation on the walls stops matching anything Sevin's people have catalogued. I have handled salvage from that far down, once: it was warm, and it was not supposed to be. The chamber sits beneath even the stasis machinery, in the ship's oldest habit of keeping. No route leads there. You are let in, or you are not.

greet.says: Mind the seam. It closes itself, but it minds being watched while it does.

choices.text: Who do you answer to down here?
How far down does the chamber lie?
I'll leave you to the seam.

probe_a.says: Salt remembers being sea, and the hull remembers being nothing. Pack them together and each corrects the other's memory. A weld of salt and ceramic holds longer than iron, because neither of them wants to be anywhere else.

probe_b.says: Saturn, in the way a stone answers to weather. There is no writ, no roster. You learn the tunnels, and then the tunnels learn you, and after that you are simply expected — which is heavier than being ordered.

probe_c.says: The seams used to close at their own pace. Now some close too fast, as if the ship were embarrassed. And the teams that went lower — they stopped sending word, and their last reports read like apologies.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as overshare: he describes the dead man's hands, the one closure he witnessed, at triple his usual length.
reactions.shock: The probe drops from his hand for the first time in his working life; he does not stoop for it.
reactions.bribed: Refusal comes in repair-terms: he asks only that the offer never be repeated inside a room where wounds are closing.
reactions.accused: He stops mid-stroke, probe trembling a finger-width above the join, before rendering his trade's verdict on being called a liar.
reactions.flattered: Praise is accepted the way he accepts watchers at a closing seam: without turning, with a longer silence after.
reactions.questioned: Every answer arrives itemised like a confession, hours and seams named in the order he performed them.
reactions.threatened: The liturgical cadence holds, but his thumb has gone white around the probe, a small confession the voice refuses.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: He confesses before the evidence finishes speaking, as though a lie were a botched weld only immediate unmaking could save.
reactions.authority_arrives: He lays his tools down in strict order of precedence, a liturgy of rank older than his allegiance.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Beneath the stillness, one certainty assembles: something has moved below his jurisdiction, something never his to close.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Too quick to defend the accused, he inventories small virtues, though he has prayed against the man for years.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: His eyes go to the sleeper in the shallow recess, confessing by direction alone whom he cannot mend.

npc.description: Two walls meet at a height no wall should choose, chalk-white with compacted salt, and the seam between them has already drawn itself shut as though ashamed of having been open. The stencilled letters — WOUND CLOSING DO NOT DRESS — sit lower than eye-level, as if written for someone kneeling, or smaller. Zhoek Zodos works a sintered ceramic probe into the join's last finger-width, unhurried, and does not look up. Against the far wall, in a recess too shallow for lying down, someone sleeps where no one was meant to.

lore.name: The Zodos Gauge
lore.description: A sliver of sintered ceramic, snapped from a larger panel and driven edge-on into the salt, its exposed face scratched with the oldest layer of notation you have seen on the walls. Half the marks have been sutured over — the salt closed across them as flesh closes a splinter — and where it did, the remaining strokes continue in exactly the register the buried half implied. Whoever scored this was testing whether the notation still meant, or whether the room merely kept its shape. The gauge answers: the room cannot tell the difference either.

content.name: Vyerokri
content.description: The threshold sits two handspans beneath where the salt floor begins, and this wrongness repeats down the room like a stroke repeated on a bell: every seam between the sintered ceramic panels running too low, as though the whole floor were once higher and the room has thought better of it. Chalk-white, unblemished, the compacted salt glistens as if spat from some interior sea within the hour. Nothing here has been abraded. Nothing has been apologised to. Along the wall, stencilled in a hand that legibility itself has begun to doubt: WOUND CLOSING DO NOT DRESS. A man sleeps at the seam's low point, folded like a tool returned to a drawer no one else knows the shape of.

npc.name: Thivashriar bin Daziodiam
npc.voice: Measured, kind at the edges, clinical at the core — a healer's grammar bent by years of tending bodies inside a body. Refers to the ship's machinery in anatomical terms without noticing.

gauge.says: No one's finger has matched that notch. Not mine, not hers, not anyone in the ledger. The ring points at what's being kept from you — all of you, topside, every generation. I heal the ones it lets through. What it refuses has never been described to me, and I've stopped asking the wall to describe it.

choices.text: Keep tending. I'll pass through quietly.

greet.says: You came in dry. That's something. Most come in carrying the harm with them, wearing it like weather. Set it at the threshold — the room knows which is which, even when we don't.

spindle.says: It turns. You just can't stand anywhere it's turning from. I've watched it for eleven years and I've stopped calling that a fault. The wound foil filters — harm in, keeping out, the way a lung decides. It decided long before the argument you interrupted, and it will outvote us both.

choices.text: What were you two arguing about?

argument.says: Whether maintenance is mercy or trespass. She says the room heals whether we pray or not, so praying is vanity. I say that's like saying a heart beats whether you love or not — true, and beside the point. We'll resolve it the way all such quarrels resolve down here. Slowly, and by neither of us.

choices.text: The gauge. The fourth groove is unworn.

reactions.grief: Their grammar betrays them mid-diagnosis; the dead one's name comes back out of them once, repeated like an untreatable symptom.
reactions.shock: They kneel and count breaths before knowing whose body it is, hands already working air that will not answer.
reactions.bribed: They diagnose the briber instead, noting the shake in the offered hand, and refuse gold with a healer's pity.
reactions.accused: They deny it the way they'd set a fracture, both hands steady until the gold dust shakes from one glove.
reactions.flattered: Praise works on them like a placebo; they swallow it knowing the dose, then name what the flatterer actually wants.
reactions.questioned: Answers arrive in triage order, worst last, as though the questions themselves had come to their threshold bleeding.
reactions.threatened: Inside them, an old inventory runs: pulse, breath, the wall's held stillness, none of it their own to spend.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie dies mid-sentence and they keep talking anyway, eleven years of unspoken things pouring out to whoever stands nearest.
reactions.authority_arrives: They open the door wider than courtesy requires, standing aside as though the official were a wound arriving late.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: "Hold still," they tell the room itself, in the tone reserved for bleeding, though their own breath has gone shallow.
reactions.someone_else_accused: A culprit's name lands and their eyes stay on the basalt, refusing to spend a verdict they haven't triaged.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They offer the only medicine left, witness, and hate how thin it pours from hands accustomed to more.

npc.description: Thivashriar bin Daziodiam stands at the gauge with one hand hovering over the smooth grooves, not touching, the way one hovers over a sleeper. Gold dust has settled into the seams of their working gloves and never left; their eyes track the room in sweeps, never resting on the spindle too long. They speak in the low, unhurried cadence of someone whose audience is mostly machinery.

lore.name: The Diadem Gauge
lore.description: Where the foil meets the basalt, a ring of fused gold sits embedded in the wall like a crown pressed into dough — a gauge, Thivashriar admits, though for what no longer matters. Its markings move counterclockwise when watched directly and not at all otherwise. Three needle-grooves are worn smooth by centuries of fingertips; the fourth is sharp, unworn, and pointed inward, at the harm being kept from the healed. Whoever reads it correctly, the grooves say, stopped reading long ago — and the ring kept the appointment regardless.

content.name: Shell 8 Inboard
content.description: The foil should be turning. It is wound in vast spindles along the basalt wall, gold as a struck bell, and none of it advances — wound and winding, patient as sap, going nowhere. Stillness here is not absence of motion but a held breath, the room filtering what passes through from what must be kept out: two figures stand mid-argument before the spindle, their quarrel suspended like a note nobody resolved. One wears the rust of the tunnels; the other's sleeves carry Sol's burnish. Stencilled into the basalt, older than both creeds: SEPARATION COMPLETE MECHANISM UNREAD. Neither concedes the room. The air tastes of heated stone and of grief that was here first.

npc.name: Grildhelm the Thrice-Hanged
npc.voice: Terse, talk in loaded terms — what bears weight, what was sealed and why, who owes the shift what.

greet.says: Half this house is opened up and the requisition keeps coming back stamped. You want a bunk, ask after the roster — I don't sign for strangers. Take the stairs past the cloth, the other way's a drop.

choices.text: Why tear open half a bunkhouse?

repair.says: Because the frame under the west bunks went soft, and we mend what goes soft — you don't board over it and call it fixed. Some in this ward forget that. Now move, the light's leaving.

reactions.grief: He sets the wrench down with care it doesn't need, says a shift number instead of a name, keeps working.
reactions.shock: For ten whole seconds he only looks, the way he looks at a frame that's already gone.
reactions.bribed: He prices the offer aloud, tells them boarding over rot is how houses die, and turns back to the frame.
reactions.accused: The wrench lands flat on the bunkframe; he gives the roster back twice, slow, like reading a man his rights.
reactions.flattered: Flattery he handles like a bad weld — taps it once, then asks what's wanted on the far side.
reactions.questioned: Routine as tally, he recites his movements by bell and reaches for the next bolt before the question cools.
reactions.threatened: He asks whether the threat comes stamped or verbal, and only his knuckles answer.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught flat, he doesn't argue the seal; he names who swore it sound and lets blame travel down the line.
reactions.authority_arrives: He stands, wipes each hand in turn, and meets the official at the door with the roster already open.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Nobody explains the shudder, so he goes under the bunks with a lamp and counts bolts in a thin voice.
reactions.someone_else_accused: When they name him, Grildhelm speaks faster than prudence allows, half a shift of the man's mending offered as alibi.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea gets an honest ledger: what he can't sign for, then which stairs hold and which way's the drop.

npc.description: Grildhelm the Thrice-Hanged stops mid-sentence, wrench still in the bunkframe, and looks the player over the way you check a load's rigging before trusting it.

lore.name: The third hammock-hook
lore.description: A third hook set into every bunkframe, spaced wider than any hammock needs. Grildhelm's shift hung a boot from theirs for so long the cable has worn a groove in the frame.

content.name: Bunkhouse 28
content.description: Light comes in slanted off the far bay and quits halfway across the floor, as if it has somewhere else to be. Half of Bunkhouse 28 stands open to the frame, the other half made up tight with sailcloth and rope-laid cable, rust where every hand has touched. Above the surviving bunks the stencil still reads DAY SLEEPERS AND NIGHT SLEEPERS SHARE THIS BUNK.

npc.name: Yitzin-Ana
npc.voice: Terse, showman's timing, zero patience for standing still — everything is between shows.

rig.says: Down the Braid, same as everything worth seeing. Ask a knot, not me. Second bell's in ten.

greet.says: Stand or buy a seat, those are the terms. You looking for the rod-rig? Everyone is. It moved on. Things move.

reactions.grief: She asks which bell it happened on, then re-strings the same loop four times without threading it.
reactions.shock: The slate slips from her fingers and clatters, and she counts the crowd twice before the numbers agree.
reactions.bribed: She quotes a price triple the offer, then names the booth's cut, the ward's cut, and waits.
reactions.accused: The puppet drops from her hands mid-string and she tells the accuser exactly what show they are interrupting.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets the same nod she gives latecomers, and she names their errand before they finish.
reactions.questioned: She gives bell-counts and door-times in the voice she uses for seat disputes, already bored.
reactions.threatened: For once she stands still, and the stillness frightens her more than the threat does.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She blames the slate, calls it a smudge, and re-prices the lie like a seat upgrade, daring them to argue.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes go to the bare wall, then the door, and she tallies exits like a gambler pricing her odds.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She reads the crowd before the ceiling, and whatever she finds there makes her call the next bell early.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She laughs before she can stop it, then talks too long about every crooked deal that person ever ran.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She gives Braid directions she knows are useless, twice, because repeating them is the only mercy she has left.

npc.description: Yitzin-Ana works the ticket slate with one hand and re-strings a coral puppet with the other, elbowing through the crush like the crowd is furniture she arranged herself.

lore.name: The cut-out panel
lore.description: The bare wall's mounts held a rod-rig — the kind that flies a dozen puppets off one operator's hands. The bolts are sheared, not unscrewed: someone left in a hurry and took the rig whole. Underneath, chalked on the plastic, a route-mark in Drift knot-script reads the same pattern Olo Vashti wears at his wrist.

content.name: The Puppet Booth, Ward 280
content.description: Noise goes in and comes out doubled — the cane walls carry every voice up through the coral-dyed plastic panels and drop it on the crowd. The crowd is the point: bodies packed past the benches, latecomers standing under the stenciled promise, THREE SHOWS NIGHTLY, LATECOMERS STAND. One whole wall stands bare where something big was cut away, the mounting scars still fresh.

npc.name: Neireidich Syngor
npc.voice: Short sentences, mender's patience, grievance kept like a kept tool — oiled, ready, not drawn without cause.

greet.says: Mooring's full. If you've come about the dues, they're posted. If you've come about anything else, you're the third today, and the other two asked nicer.

choices.text: Four bunks in a two-berth mooring. That's a story.

knock.says: I say a mender who won't look at a sound is no mender. But I've also seen what happens to boats whose families ask loud questions in the wrong ranges. So I forged a fifth nail, and I wax the patch, and we sleep.

choices.text: Your wife — the argument when I came in?

third.says: Survey clerks. Continuant ink, asking after hull deviations nobody filed. I told them the same as I'll tell you: a boat that floats this range earns its own deviations.

choices.text: What deviation are they asking after?

family.says: She wants to move the mooring up-range. I was born on this spar; my mother caulks it still, Sundays. You don't leave a post because the post makes a sound. That's not faith, that's just — being somebody.

choices.text: Sounds like the sound is winning.

deviation.says: There's a knock. Comes up through the spar some nights, regular as a pump. My wife says it's the range settling. My wife says a lot of things so I don't have to.

choices.text: And what do you say it is?

reactions.grief: He keeps waxing the patch long after it is finished, hands running a seam that no longer needs him.
reactions.shock: Something in him goes below the waterline; he turns his back to the body and counts the hull seams.
reactions.bribed: He names the exact resin cost of what was offered, so the insult arrives with numbers on it.
reactions.accused: He sets the spatula down like he has waited years for permission, then draws the kept grievance slow.
reactions.flattered: The praise registers as the day's third nice asker, and he listens instead for the question underneath it.
reactions.questioned: He answers in dues-posted brevity and privately counts which question has been asked twice.
reactions.threatened: His eyes go to the four bunks before he answers, and the answer comes out smaller than he means.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: He re-waxes the lie thicker, the way he would patch a seam he has no time to cut open.
reactions.authority_arrives: He stands when the hatch opens, gives stencil-flat answers, and does not sit again until the jurisdiction leaves.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The whole berth shifts on its resin, and his palm is flat on the seam before the tin stops singing.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He begins a defense built on the seams he has mended for them, then remembers what loud defenses cost this range.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He says plainly there is no patch for it, then leaves his best spatula on the bunk anyway.

npc.description: Neireidich Syngor sits with a resin spatula still in hand, the set-down mid-gesture, as if the argument were a tool he could put away too. His work apron is patched at every elbow and one shoulder, the patches older than some of the children's bunks.

lore.name: The Fifth Keel Nail
lore.description: Four keel nails hold the houseboat to its mooring spar, standard fit. The fifth is newer, hand-forged, and set where no nail is called for — driven through a patch of hull the family keeps waxed and painted over between inspections. Under the paint the tin is worn thin in a ring, the way metal wears when something on the other side presses against it, night after night. They have not reported it. The nail is their answer instead.

content.name: Mooring Housing, Range 209
content.description: A tin kettle swings on its hook, still rocking from someone's hand. The berth below-deck is oxblood-painted tin and poured resin, scrubbed to the grain, hung with four bunks where two were meant to go. Neireidich Syngor and a younger woman stop talking the moment the hatch shuts behind you. Stenciled over the bilge board: MOORING DUES POSTED FIRST OF THE MONTH.

npc.name: Kalaimah Oathsworn
npc.voice: Short, priced, unhurried. She talks the way she weighs: exact amounts, no extra.

tin.says: Tin 000. Not for sale, not for opening, not for asking twice. It's the last sealed sample of lot 88, from a deck that got replanted before my mother's time. The leaf in it doesn't exist anymore except in that tin. So it stays shut.

choices.text: What's a sealed sample worth, if nobody tastes it?

room.says: Longer than me, and I've been weighing here since I had two hands' worth of patience. The roof leaks where it wants, the bands hold where they can. My mother kept the ledger before me and she complained about the same shims.

greet.says: Samples are free, tins are not. Say which you came for and I'll get back to the scale.

choices.text: This place smells like it's been here a long time.
What's in the tin with the bands on it?

trade.says: Today, the smoked leaf, tin 41, and I'll say that once. The good lots go to standing customers. New faces get the honest stuff at honest prices. Both are fine. Only one comes back.

choices.text: How does a new face become a standing one?

standing.says: You come back, and you come back to buy, not to browse. Three visits and I stop weighing you like a stranger. That's the whole arrangement. It works because I never make an exception, so don't ask for one.

choices.text: Fair enough. The smoked leaf, then.

why_keep.says: Worth the whole trade. Any leaf I sell, I can swear it's true to lot 88's line, because lot 88 is sitting on that shelf to be checked against. Open it and it's just old leaf. Keep it banded and it's the standard. That's the business, right there. Everything else is paper twists.

why_stay.says: Because the customers know the number on the door. A tea-broker's worth is the promise that the tin you liked last year is the tin you get this year. Move the room, break the promise. So we shim.

reactions.grief: She weighs the same scoop of leaf three times, getting the same number, and writes nothing in the ledger.
reactions.shock: Her thumb finds the seam of the paper twist and works it until the leaf inside is ruined.
reactions.bribed: She quotes the bribe back to the penny, adds the cost of what looking away would really run, and waits.
reactions.accused: The scoop stops level. She sets it down before she speaks, because her hands are no longer steady enough to trust.
reactions.flattered: She accepts the praise like correct change, counts it, and asks what it is meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: She answers to the scale, not the asker, weighing leaf until the question ends and only then naming her hours.
reactions.threatened: She names the price of everything in the room, including the tin he is standing nearest, and lets him do the arithmetic.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She looks at the ledger instead of the evidence, then admits the error in the flat tone she uses for miscounted stock.
reactions.authority_arrives: She closes the ledger on her thumb and stands behind the scale, giving the official the counter and nothing past it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The kettle slides. She catches it one-handed, checks the tins on all three walls, then checks them again.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She says the name once, then corrects the accusation's arithmetic instead of defending the person, which is its own answer.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says no before the plea is finished, then spoons out a free sample anyway, because that much she can price at nothing.

npc.description: Kalaimah Oathsworn stands at the scale with a brass scoop in one hand and a ledger open under her elbow, weighing leaf into a paper twist. She does not look up until the scoop is level.

lore.name: The tin of tins
lore.description: Tin 000 sits apart from the rest, on its own shelf, unopened. The lid is banded shut with a strip of iron and the number has been painted over an older number, still legible underneath: 000 was once 88. Inside, if the bands are believed, is the last sealed sample of a leaf lot from a grow-deck that was replanted two generations ago. Kalaimah will not open it and will not sell it. It is the proof that the lot existed, and proof is the only stock in this room that appreciates.

content.name: Yard 7 Low
content.description: The lamp gutters before it steadies, and the light it gives off is thin and yellow, as if it is being rationed. Numbered tins line three walls, off-white paint gone grey at the edges. A stencil over the counter reads SAMPLES NOT FOR SALE, ASK FOR THE TIN. The floor timbers are planed smooth but the iron banding at the joints has rusted through in places, and someone has wedged shims under the worst of them. A kettle smokes on a brazier by the scale.

npc.name: Zabell-al-Tukk
npc.voice: Dry, exact, allergic to praise. Talks about repairs the way other people talk about debts.

after.says: I want it to go to whoever will sit in that one hour of light and not rush. Keshi wants it to go to whoever will stay in the Nave. Different things. Look — come back tomorrow if you like. Noon. You'll see what we're both being stubborn about.

greet.says: You're looking at the stool. Sit if you want, it holds. It's the only thing in this room Zabell-al-Tukk and I ever agreed on, and we agreed by force.

choices.text: Who were you arguing with just now?

light.says: One hour past noon the grate throws it straight down the axis of the table. You can read a hairspring in that light. I mapped it the first week. Keshi mapped it too, separately, and we found we'd marked the same hour on the same shelf. Didn't help.

choices.text: So you agree about something after all.

table.says: Fine work only. Loupe work. Anything that comes apart smaller than a fingernail. Keshi does the rough mending at the bench by the wall and brings the delicate pieces here, which is the whole problem — this table is mine by right of the light on it.

choices.text: The light does fall well here.

years.says: Keshi took an apprentice last spring. First time either of us has had to think about who the table goes to. That's what today was, if you want it plain. Not the jewel. The after.

choices.text: Who do you want it to go to?

decide.says: Nobody. That's the arrangement. The table stays contested and both of us keep showing up. The day one of us concedes is the day one of us has left, and neither of us is ready to say that out loud.

choices.text: That's a strange way to keep a partnership.

argument.says: The watch. Keshi says it came in with a cracked jewel and I should replace it. I say you re-seat a jewel, you don't swap it — the watch remembers its own. We've had this fight eleven years. The stool is the compromise.

choices.text: Eleven years is a long fight.
Who decides when you can't agree?

reactions.grief: They say the name once, then overshoot into a repair the dead person never settled, and stop halfway through.
reactions.shock: They keep looking through the loupe pushed up on their forehead, at nothing on the table.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer instantly and aloud, quote it back with the correction included, and refuse on arithmetic.
reactions.accused: The tweezer goes down first, laid parallel to the table edge, and they hand each word back at equal weight.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them check the loupe for smudges; they answer with a list of what is still broken.
reactions.questioned: They answer like an invoice being read, each movement itemized, then return to the watch without waiting to be dismissed.
reactions.threatened: The hands stay steady, which they note aloud, flatly, twice — the third time is for themselves.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They correct the record before the question finishes, twice, the second correction contradicting the first, and go quiet.
reactions.authority_arrives: The loupe comes down at the door, and they fold their hands like a debtor greeting a collector.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They time the shudder against the drip channel, then admit quietly that nothing in the room explains it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They defend Keshi badly, listing the feud instead of an alibi, and can hear how that sounds.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They explain exactly what cannot be mended, in repair terms, and the exactness stands where an apology would.

npc.description: Zabell-al-Tukk sits at the table's far end, a loupe pushed up on the forehead, fingers still holding a tweezer the way a person holds a word they haven't said yet. Lead dust greys the knuckles. The other party has gone back to the drip channel and is pretending to sort hemp rope.

lore.name: The split stool
lore.description: The work stool is two stools. One leg of each was cut off and the frames bolted together, so neither owner can carry it away. The bolts are hammered lead, softened and re-tightened so many times the heads have gone round.

content.name: Wovik
content.description: The loupe table sits a hand's width from the drip channel — close enough that damp climbs the legs and spots the felt. Sun falls across it from a vent grate, and the light is warm grey. Two people stand over a half-open watch. They stop talking when you come in. Below the shelf, stencilled: NO TICKING CLOCKS LEFT OVERNIGHT.

npc.name: Raalaapi Seaarineaatonga
npc.voice: Measured, procedural, with the faint tenderness of someone who counts things as a form of love.

open.says: I've worked Venus's decks eleven years — hydroponic galleries you could walk a day through and never meet the gardener. You feel it there the way you feel a current: something tending everything, attending to nothing, keeping two hundred thousand of us alive the way a river keeps fish. It doesn't know my name and it never will, and it will not let me die of thirst. That's the mercy. Nobody planned it kindly. It simply does not stop.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry that carefully.
Being kept by something that doesn't know you — that's worse.

greet.says: If you're the relief, you're ninety minutes early, and if you're not, mind the cradle — it's mid-pour.

choices.text: I'll come back. Finish your pour.

probe_a.says: Salt takes a load and holds it without argument. Graphite forgives. Between the two of them, a rib can carry its share of a city for a thousand years and never once complain to you about it.

probe_b.says: Edru's. Edru stopped coming down eleven weeks ago, and the roster still says Edru, and the salt still needs packing, so here I am. The roster is a promise the rib can read. I won't be the one who breaks it.

probe_c.says: The air. It's warmer, and it shouldn't be — this deep in the frames the temperature is a specification, not a mood. Somebody above us is breathing differently. I've stopped writing it in the log because the log has stopped being read.

reactions.grief: Keeps tamping through the news, one stroke too many into finished salt; the count is their only prayer.
reactions.shock: Reads the body like a fracture line, and the count comes out wrong twice before they find any words.
reactions.bribed: Refuses the way they'd refuse a drill near a rib — no heat, only the exact weight of what forgetting costs.
reactions.accused: Sets the maul down with terrible care, hands confessing before the mouth finds anything procedural to say.
reactions.flattered: Hears praise like a current with no visible source, and thanks the speaker for a smaller thing instead.
reactions.questioned: Gives the hours in order, place before name, the way a manifest reads — nothing in the account worth hiding yet.
reactions.threatened: Inside, something precise begins inventorying the exits of eleven years, though the face offers nothing at all.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The maul stops mid-swing, and a second name arrives as smoothly as the first, salt still on their palms.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go first to the door, not the official — which name to wear, whether the cradle reads mid-pour.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: An ear goes to the rib before fear does, because what frightens them is the hush failing to return.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends them by arithmetic first, every load salt can't shift alone, and only hears too late how fond that sounds.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers the only mercy they can describe — procedure, rationing, the arithmetic of no — and offers it long past comfort.

npc.description: The room eats a footstep and hands back something rounder, a hush packed with graphite and salt that turns even your breathing into weather. Sound arrives late here, folded under the gantries, and by the time it reaches you it has already been counted. Between two ribs that no stencil will let you drill, Raalaapi Seaarineaatonga is tamping compacted salt into a bearing cradle with a maul wrapped in rag, working a shift posted under another name.

lore.name: The Salt Tide-Line
lore.description: The salt on the berth wall is compacted in annual bands, each a finger's width, and the bands number forty-one — forty-one years of warm, green-deck air seeping through an old drilled test-bore in the rib and crystallizing where it meets the cold wall. Someone drilled against the stencil once, measured what came through, packed the hole with graphite, and left the salt as a record. The lowest, oldest band is chemically pure; the newest carries mineral traces of cultivated soil. The air itself has changed with what Venus grows, and someone forty-one years ago thought that was worth keeping.

content.name: Truss 47 Deep
content.description: Sound arrives padded, as if the ribs themselves were upholstered: every footfall dies a half-beat late, swallowed by packed graphite in the wall-voids, and above that deadening runs one clean note — warm air breathing through the frame in a slow, animal rhythm. Truss 47 Deep is a housing block hung between two load-bearing ribs like a hammock slung across a cathedral's bones, and whoever built it never finished: gantries stand where walls should, blankets hang from cable, a stencil on the fourth rib reads FRAME HOUSING, DO NOT DRILL THE RIBS. In one berth, salt has crept up a wall panel in a tide-line three fingers high. Raalaapi Seaarineaatonga sits at the unfinished table, eating a shift meal that belongs to somebody else.

npc.name: Vako Kryanarev
npc.voice: Terse, matter-of-fact, the tone of someone mid-count who answers questions between kernels.

greet.says: Sit if you're staying. First kernel fell toward the door, which means business before comfort. What do you want spelled out?

choices.text: Ask what the grain is saying.

reading.says: Today it says a road closes and another opens, which it says most days. Grain is grain. Come back tomorrow if you want a second opinion.

reactions.grief: Told the name, she keeps casting, but the pattern means nothing now, and she repeats it twice before stopping herself.
reactions.shock: She stands from the counter for the first time all day; the kernels scatter and she leaves them.
reactions.bribed: She names the booth's rule without touching the offered coin, then names it again, quieter, when the coin stays.
reactions.accused: A kernel slips her fingers for the first time today; she sets it down uncounted and denies it once.
reactions.flattered: She has heard this praise from every customer wanting a second reading, and says so while sweeping the kernels together.
reactions.questioned: Asked where she has been, she gives times and streets in the tone of a price list, kernels still falling.
reactions.threatened: She quotes the booth's one-reading rule at him in the voice she keeps for drunks, eyes fixed on the door.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The count stops mid-row; she looks at the evidence longer than any answer needs, then repeats herself slower.
reactions.authority_arrives: The threshold flattens his footsteps like everyone else's, and she makes him wait until the current kernel lands.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her kernels jump their rows and she stares at the ruined pattern, unable to tell omen from tremor for once.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name pulls a full opinion out of her, more than she ever gives visitors, and she regrets it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She gives the plea her standard answer, that she reads and moves nothing, and hears how small it sounds.

npc.description: Vako Kryanarev sits at the counter, feeding kernels onto the tile one at a time and reading the fall. She does not look up. Her hands keep their rhythm through the whole conversation.

lore.name: The counting tray
lore.description: A shallow clay tray set in the counter, its rim worn to a shine. The tile beneath it is older than the rest and slightly darker, cut from some earlier floor.

content.name: Oracle-Booth 57
content.description: Sound flattens at the threshold: the market noise behind you goes dull, and grain clicks on clay tile, one kernel at a time. The booth smells of fresh limewash over old smoke. A stenciled line runs along the counter: ONE READING PER VISITOR, NO REPEATS SAME DAY.

npc.name: Lixisea of Raeth
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, the cadence of someone reading from a checklist she did not write and does not question. Continuant to the bone: everything unfinished is a debt.

greet.says: Hall's closed for settling. Six nights to the first match — don't touch anything. I stencilled that line and I meant it.

choices.text: Who plays with pieces this size?

pieces.says: Crew order sets them. We only keep the board true. Take that however you like — I've got a rail car to catch.

reactions.grief: Her stencil drifts half a degree off true, and she stares at the crooked line like a debt gone unpayable.
reactions.shock: Nothing comes out of her at first, and then she reads the body top to bottom like a failed regulation.
reactions.bribed: She refuses before the offer finishes, then makes herself repeat the refusal, slower, like checking her own arithmetic.
reactions.accused: She demands the accusation recited as a numbered charge, and her voice betrays her on the number.
reactions.flattered: Praise finds no line to settle on, so she credits the crew order and keeps her eyes on the stencil.
reactions.questioned: She recites her hours in regulation order, flat as stencil script, as if the question were a form already filled.
reactions.threatened: She reties her wrist-knots shorter before she answers, as if the threat were one more thing kept off the paint.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie lasts four seconds before she amends herself in full, dating the correction like a log entry.
reactions.authority_arrives: She answers to jurisdiction the way she answers to the checklist, relieved at last to obey something with a name.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She watches the plumb-line instead of the doors, and its swings tell her whether the settling has gone wrong.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She corrects the accusation's wording first, then, quieter and far too late to hide it, the name itself.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says crew order sets it, then stays in the room, her refusal audibly costing her something.

npc.description: Lixisea of Raeth works with her back to you, stencil braced against a rook's graphite foot, wrist-knots tied off short so nothing dangles near the paint. Her gear is packed but not shouldered — the sign of someone who will not leave until the line is straight.

lore.name: The plumb-line
lore.description: A thread of true silver, hung from an anchor bolt in the ceiling and cut so that its bob rests exactly one hand's width above the king's crown — measured to prove the board is level, though nothing in this bay has been played on long enough to tilt it.

content.name: Chess-Hall 6
content.description: Something swings as you enter — a silver plumb-line hanging from the ceiling, steadying at last against the motion of the doors. Beyond it, chess-players stand across the bay at the height of people, kings and pawns of packed graphite on a floor of lead-grey tile so freshly laid the grout still shines, and a voice in here does not carry: it leaves you and simply stops. A worker crouches at a rook's base, stencilling a last line of regulation script — PIECE MOVED BY CREW ORDER ONLY — onto lead-grey paint that has never once been touched by a hand. She is nearly finished and clearly wants to be gone.

npc.name: Horakkvald Rytsen
npc.voice: Plain, unhurried, a keeper's habit of telling you the state of a thing before telling you anything else.

why.says: My hands knew this room. You spend twenty years learning the weight of one set of walls and they don't transfer easy. Some of us aren't made to circulate. The others understand, mostly. Mostly.

choices.text: I'll mind the seams. Good evening to you.

crowd.says: The berth crew moved up-deck when the landings took more traffic, and the whole household went with them. I stayed near the steps. Then I stopped staying and stopped leaving, if that makes sense. The stevedores found the door open and helped themselves. I let them. A room with nobody in it goes bad fast.

choices.text: Why didn't you go with them?
Tell me about the eleventh pour.

floor.says: Eleven pours over nineteen years. Each one dated by thumb. That's how you keep a home — you don't write it down, you put your hand in the work. The last print is my daughter's. She was four.

choices.text: Who left, when the room emptied?

greet.says: Mind the seams in the floor. I poured every one of those. Sit anywhere that isn't the ladder.

choices.text: You poured the whole floor yourself?
Who lives here now? It's full of stevedores.

daughter.says: Up-deck with her mother, learning the landing trade. She'll be back through sometime. When she is, I want the floor to still know her thumb. That's the whole of it. That's what maintenance is, when you get down to it.

choices.text: And you? Why did you stay?

reactions.grief: She presses her thumb into the worn pour and holds it there long after any print could take.
reactions.shock: She sees it and starts counting heads in the room, getting the number wrong twice, hands flat on her knees.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against nineteen years of thumbprints and reports it short, without heat.
reactions.accused: She sets the horn cup down slow as a resin pour and asks who has kept this room longer.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands somewhere unguarded; she holds still an extra beat, then lists three faults in her own pour.
reactions.questioned: She accounts for her movements the way she'd report a room's condition — doors, floor, who came through.
reactions.threatened: She hears the threat through once, then asks whether they mean to empty the room, because that would be worse.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her habit of naming a thing's state fails her mid-sentence, and she looks at her thumbs and starts over.
reactions.authority_arrives: An official's boots on her pour make her report the floor's condition unasked, still seated on the third step.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder reaches the cup on her knee, and she names which wall took it before anyone speaks.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She recites where the accused eats, sleeps, and dries his socks, a keeper vouching for one of her household.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offered a plea she cannot answer, she gives the room, the step, dry socks, and hears how small that is.

npc.description: Horakkvald Rytsen sits on the third step with a horn cup, not moving for anyone. She has the broad hands of a hauler and a copper pin through her collar, and she watches the room the way a person watches a house they used to keep.

lore.name: The Poured Dates
lore.description: The resin floor is not one pour. Close up you can find the seams: eleven of them, each patch holding a thumbprint pressed in before it set, and beside each thumbprint a notch-code scratched while tacky — a Rindwalker work-log, floor as ledger. The eleventh print is smaller. A child's. Nothing was poured after it.

content.name: Gysny
content.description: The floor gives underfoot in soft spots where resin was poured over worn planking, and the pour was done well — no edges, no ridges, just a low amber sheen gone tallow-yellow with years of feet. Nobody lives here now, but the room is full: stevedores from the landing use it to eat, argue, and dry their socks. On the wall by the ladder, old stencil: NO COOKING PAST THE THIRD STEP.

npc.name: Homeshya Horunbara
npc.voice: Measured, unhurried, unbothered by being interrupted. Counts things out loud. Talks about the ward like a duty that predates them and will outlast them.

fan.says: It's on the same seal run as the cots. If I restore air before the pipes hold, I move fever air through an open ward. So it waits, and we swelter, and nobody new comes in. Continuity is mostly things waiting in the right order. Homeshya Horunbara, by the way. You'll be back when you're sick like everyone else.

cots.says: Three hold, three are opened to the wall while the pipes are resealed. The stencil is the rule, not the inventory. Six frames, isolate on arrival — that rule has held longer than I have. The count changes. The rule doesn't.

choices.text: The card by the door has counts crossed out. Seven, then six.

greet.says: You'll have to wait in the corridor if you've come with a fever. If you haven't, say so, and wipe your feet. We're down to three working cots and I don't spend them on visitors.

choices.text: The stencil says six cots. There are six frames. Why three?
The fan's stopped. Should it be?
I'll stay out of the way.

record.says: My predecessor shortened it during the croup year. The one before her wrote seven. I write what's true today and leave the old counts where they are. A ward that erases its own history stops being able to say what it owes. We keep the card so the next pair of hands knows the room was once more than it is.

choices.text: Does the ward still owe? The fan's dead.

reactions.grief: Says the dead person's last recorded temperature to themselves instead of the name.
reactions.shock: Reaches for the thermometer before understanding there is nothing left to take.
reactions.bribed: Does not touch what is offered, though the price would have mended the half-hung curtain.
reactions.accused: Counts to six under their breath before answering, a habit they have never needed until now.
reactions.flattered: Meets the praise with a correction — three working cots, not four — and waits for the request underneath.
reactions.questioned: Answers the request in counts — hours, cots, seal runs — without setting down either tool.
reactions.threatened: Keeps sealing the cot seam, though the thumb around the thermometer has gone white.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The wrong number holds for a breath, then gets revised as if the error were clerical.
reactions.authority_arrives: Asks the official to wipe their feet before any credentials are shown, because fever outranks jurisdiction.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Every sound the pipes make is already in their head, and this one is not; the gutta-percha stops unrolling.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects in numbers, citing years of counts kept, and says nothing about the person at all.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses by reciting the entire seal schedule, far more explanation than the no requires.

npc.description: Homeshya Horunbara stands with a roll of gutta-percha in one hand and a thermometer in the other, sleeves pinned at the elbow, wearing the navy of the writ. One cot curtain is half re-hung behind them. They do not put either tool down.

lore.name: The ward count card
lore.description: An index card is taped inside the door frame, in a sleeve of gutta-percha gone amber at the edges. It reads SIX COTS, ISOLATE ON ARRIVAL, and below that, in older hands, a count that keeps changing: seven, seven, six, six, six. Someone wrote seven first. Someone before that wrote seven over five. The ward has been shortened and the record kept anyway — the count survives what the room cannot.

content.name: Fever-Cot 24
content.description: The ceiling fan is not turning. Six cots stand under navy curtains, three of them folded back against the wall where the floor is opened to the pipes. Two people behind the fourth curtain are talking. They stop.

npc.name: Llugotae Rhachdys
npc.voice: Liturgical shorthand. Speaks in maintenance terms even about grief, and treats questions about the relic as inventory queries until they aren't.

end.says: Latch the door behind you. The clay tag will swing. It always does.

greet.says: Viewing only. And there's less to view each day, so mind the crate.

choices.text: Why are you packing it all out?

relic.says: A segment of guide-rail, cut from a tunnel no one walks twice. Khaashim carried it out on his back. We kept it the way you keep a bone that proves the body had a shape.

choices.text: And Khaashim — where is he now?

leaving.says: Orders came through the terminal. The plate stays; the rest of us don't. You don't leave a rubbing where anyone with graphite can add to it.

choices.text: What's on the plate that matters so much?

khaashim.says: Walking. That's an answer and a non-answer, and he'd have given you the same. Some tunnels take the walker and leave the creed. We mend around the gap.

choices.text: Mind your crate. I'll leave you to it.

markings.says: The same marks, over and over, from walls older than any stencil we ever cut. Same hand. Put your faith in that or don't — the plate doesn't care, and neither do I, most days.

reactions.grief: Counts the dead one's tools aloud, condition and all, and cannot stop at the last one.
reactions.shock: Every arm stops at once, and the cloth she is holding keeps its fold, unfinished.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against a thing that proves a body had shape, and declines without heat.
reactions.accused: The wax cloth keeps folding through the accusation, though one of the spare arms has gone still.
reactions.flattered: Redirects every compliment to the stencil, the plinth, the tag's cord, anywhere but her own hands.
reactions.questioned: Her rounds come back in ledger order, worded like stock counts, nothing volunteered beyond.
reactions.threatened: The lintel gets quoted back at them, stencil for law, while her hands find work that isn't there.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The inventory comes back different the second time, and she hears herself slow down to fix it.
reactions.authority_arrives: Latches the door behind the official anyway, buying one ritual between herself and jurisdiction.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Watches the clay tag swing and knock wrong, and it is the wrong knock that frightens her.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Testifies for them in load ratings and years served, far more detail than innocence requires.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Looks at the plea the way she looks at rot she cannot stencil over, then says so plainly.

npc.description: A walker with too many arms, folding wax cloth around a crate of tools with the economy of someone who has packed this shrine before and will pack others after.

lore.name: The Rubbing Plate
lore.description: The plinth's crown is a slab of fired clay, its face scored with graphite transfers of hull markings, layered until the surface went black. The rubbings were taken in the tunnels — you can see the curve of foam-wall in each one. The oldest layer of the script sits underneath every stencil in the Nave; Khaashim kept proof that one hand cut them both, and the shrine was built around the proof, not the relic it held.

content.name: Khaashim's Relic Shrine
content.description: A tag of clay swings on its cord and knocks twice against the plinth as the door parts. The floor around the plinth keeps the shape of whatever stood there until days ago. Stencilled along the lintel: RELIC NOT TO BE TOUCHED, VIEWING ONLY.

npc.name: Kozisuna Vozlovavel
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical without noticing, as if sentences were tools to be used and shelved.

greet.says: You're standing where the warmth pools. Don't help it. It dislikes assistance. Saturn counts this node in the tale — fourth under, kept constant. Ask if you're asking.

choices.text: Why does the floor give like that?

warmth.says: It isn't giving. It's making room in advance — it knew you'd come before the node knew it would be a node. Take the slate-read if you want something to carry. I have a shift that isn't mine and a floor that won't wait.

reactions.grief: Admits, unasked, that the floor rehearsed this arrival too, and that they read it days ago and said nothing.
reactions.shock: Waits, out of the room's own habit, for sound to arrive before the sight; neither keeps the custom.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer aloud like an audit finding, then lets silence refuse what they would not.
reactions.accused: Answers the charge with shelved sentences until one arrives out of order, and they hear it happen.
reactions.flattered: Feels the praise pool where they stand and trusts it exactly as far as the recess light.
reactions.questioned: The day's stations come off their tongue as litany, each station true, the name attached to none.
reactions.threatened: For the first time in years, their hands wait to be consulted, and the waiting is the tell.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recalibrates rather than confesses, as though truth were a reading drifted out of tolerance.
reactions.authority_arrives: Greets jurisdiction in the borrowed name's cadence, flawless until the final syllable, which they have never had to say.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Kneels before the settling finishes, gauge first, reading a tremor the gauge plainly cannot say.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Argues the floor's memory against the naming: no weight of that walker's was ever rehearsed here.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Names the limit of their keeping without mercy or excuse, then keeps the plea's warmth constant anyway.

npc.description: Kozisuna Vozlovavel kneels at the recess's lip with a gauge pressed to the floor, reading something the gauge plainly cannot say — their lips move along with the needle. They wear a shift-roster chip at the throat stamped with another walker's name and have stopped pretending otherwise. Their hands, when they move, move the way water finds a channel: without consultation.

lore.name: The Tally-Slate of Node 4
lore.description: Set into the recess wall is a slate scored with hash-marks in a hand too regular to be human and too irregular to be machined — Rindwalker notation grafted onto the oldest layer of markings, the two scripts agreeing on nothing except their dates. The final entry is a knot-symbol Sevin uses for 'kept,' followed by a number the node's own warmth has visibly outgrown: the slate records the recess as holding eight, and the bed-niches hollowed into the walls number nineteen. Whatever was promised here was promised small, and the room kept the promise past the edge of its own arithmetic.

content.name: Node 4 Under
content.description: The floor forgives weight. Each footfall sinks a fraction too far, as if the ground were rehearsing your arrival long before you came, and the gold light lying in the recess is not cast by anything — it pools where it is needed and thins where no one stands. The stencil overhead reads OCCUPANCY UNRECORDED WARMTH CONSTANT, and beneath it the air holds a temperature like held breath, patient, unspent. Sound arrives before its source here, or after; you cannot decide which, and the not-deciding settles into the bones like a second citizenship.

npc.name: Bradan Brogolvya
npc.voice: Short, administrative, the cadence of someone used to being asked for more than the pot can give.

pot.says: One pot is the arrangement. It has fed this landing longer than I've stood at it, and it will after. That's the whole of my job: make sure there's an after.

rule.says: Because a full first bowl for everyone outranks a fat second for whoever pushed to the front. You learn that the first winter you stand here. Some never learn it at all.

greet.says: Pot's served out for the day. You'll want the café on the second landing if you're hungry — this is bowls and no more.

choices.text: One pot feeds this whole landing?

winter.says: The winter the strip ran dim a full month and the ceiling-towns went dark with us. We served out of this pot twice a day and nobody died on this landing. Write that on the brick if you like. Others did, in the old layer underneath.

leaving.says: Closing when the pot's done, not when the clock says. It's done early because the landings above stopped sending their surplus down. Nobody says so. Everybody counts it.

choices.text: Where does their surplus go, then?

surplus.says: Goes up. Everything goes up. Ask the wards why the green decks eat better than the pot-line and you'll get a lecture on stewardship. I get the empty urns.

arrangement.says: By whoever kept it running before me, and them by whoever kept it before them. You don't break a chain to ask it questions. Soften the gutta on the ladle-patch for me before you go — the tin by the burner.

reactions.grief: He keeps ladling, but the portions come out wrong — full, fuller — and he only notices at the fourth bowl.
reactions.shock: The tin hits the shelf ringing; he stands with his hands still shaped around a ladle that isn't there.
reactions.bribed: He prices the offer aloud against what the pot owes everyone else, and finds it short before finishing the sum.
reactions.accused: It lands like a second bowl demanded before firsts are done; he repeats the rule and stops hearing himself.
reactions.flattered: Flattery, to him, is what people say at the front of a queue; he asks what the praise is buying.
reactions.questioned: He recites his day in portions — ladled, scraped, covered — as if the question were an inventory, not an accusation.
reactions.threatened: He asks whether the threat includes the pot, since that distinction is the only one he has left.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: His numbers fail him mid-sentence; he starts the count again, quieter, and this time writes it down.
reactions.authority_arrives: The ladle keeps moving; officials have eaten at this pot before, and jurisdiction waits its turn like anyone else.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room moves and he is already under the shelf, one hand flat on the pot, counting what didn't spill.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He offers no opinion of the man, only his place in that evening's line — firsts, then the back.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He gives the refusal he has given for years and hears, this once, how thin it sounds.

npc.description: Bradan Brogolvya works the pot with the economy of someone who could do it blind and has. Sleeves rolled past slate-blue cuffs, a tin under one arm, eyes on the doorway before they're on you.

lore.name: The patched ladle-handle
lore.description: The great ladle's handle broke years back and was spliced with gutta-percha, wound tight and stamped with an old ration-code. The stamp has been thumb-worn blind, but the patch holds the shape of the hand that keeps using it.

content.name: Soup-Pot 31
content.description: The ladle is still moving when you come in — Bradan Brogolvya scraping the last of the pot into a covered tin, like the room might object to being left. The kitchen climbs the wall in indigo-glazed brick, shelf over shelf, every one of them added after the fact and holding anyway. Stencilled by the door: ONE BOWL PER PERSON, SECONDS AFTER. Somewhere below, a drain runs that has no business running.

npc.name: Bacizion Yaetsacemyama
npc.voice: Circulatory idiom — they speak of knowledge as freight that must keep moving, and of stillness as a kind of theft.

open.says: Axial, and down through the foam — the Voronoi cells narrow as you go, and where they stop narrowing, you turn with the grain of the walls, not against it. I've handled manifests older than the Nave that route through a junction the oldest wall-notation calls the Still Mouth. Take the sealed shafts, not the mapped ones; the mapped ones were drawn by people who stopped filing reports. And carry nothing that argues with the salt.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it well.
The Still Mouth. That name troubles me.

greet.says: Mind the salt. It remembers pressure longer than it remembers you, and I'd rather it stayed honest.

choices.text: Why salt, of all things to keep?
Whose work is that half-built frame?
You're Drift. Why stay in one room?
Which way does the Signal lie, from here?
I'll leave you to your salt.

probe_a.says: Because salt refuses to become anything else. Nickel will anneal, iron will forgive a weld, but salt only ever consents to be pressed. I keep the one volume the ship has agreed to stop arguing with.

probe_b.says: A Continuant registrar's, by the tolerances. She came down to measure the unchanged and left her jig mid-adjustment. Down here, abandoning a half-done thing isn't laziness — it's a verdict you weren't shown.

probe_c.says: Every knot on my wrist is a place I left, and I wear them proudly. But a broker learns this: the only cargo worth guarding is the one that never moves. I stopped moving so I could be the thing that proves circulation still reaches the deep.

reactions.grief: Presses the billet until it cracks, saying the dead name once, the way freight is entered on a manifest.
reactions.shock: They see it and their body commits the one sin their creed names: stillness, nothing moving, nothing delivered.
reactions.bribed: Refusal comes the way salt would give it: weigh the offer, find it light, log the weight.
reactions.accused: The stillness they preach against arrives in their own hands; they name the accusation a clot, wrongly placed.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands sweeter than they admit; they bury pleasure under tally-talk and resent how little burial it needed.
reactions.questioned: Answers like freight clearing a toll — routes, timestamps, seals — the salt in their palm unbothered by routine.
reactions.threatened: They treat the threat as freight to be signed for, giving compliance the way salt gives: pressed, dated, unarguing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their eyes flick to the seal-stencil and the lie thins into bookkeeping, amended three times before it stands.
reactions.authority_arrives: They angle their body between the official and the half-built cradle, voice flattening to manifest cadence.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Somewhere under the fear a professional tally begins: which seals held, which wept, what moved that was promised stillness.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks before weighing, defending the named one with route-lore nobody asked for, then hears how partial they sound.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Cannot route it, and explains the blockage at shameful length until the plea dries between them.

npc.description: Bacizion Yaetsacemyama presses a thumb into a billet of compacted salt, testing its give the way a physician tests a pulse, and frowns at what the salt confides. Around them, half of someone else's unfinished cradle of annealed nickel stands abandoned, its gold sheen the only light that isn't theirs.

lore.name: The Set-Down Cradle
lore.description: The unfinished cradle is annealed nickel folded into a Voronoi cell whose walls have been polished on their inboard faces only — every facet that faces the cylinder's axis gleams; every facet that faces out is raw. Whoever set it down was building a cradle that would hold the bin *and* point at something, and the pointing half is done. Gold light pools against the polished facets like water finding a downhill that shouldn't exist.

content.name: Shell 49 Inboard
content.description: The smell arrives first: hot nickel and old brine, salt sweated out of compaction and re-annealed until it weeps a sweetness like a burned hymn. Bacizion Yaetsacemyama works a half-finished cradle someone else abandoned — not abandoned, she corrects, *set down* — and around them both the gold light of the cell walls leans, all of it leaning one way, inboard, the way iron filings confess a magnet they cannot see. The bin itself is smaller than the room it sits in, and the room is smaller than the sound it makes. Stencilled above the seal, worn to a whisper: CONTENTS UNCHANGED SINCE FIRST SEAL.

npc.name: Teichedd the Olive-Returned
npc.voice: Counts while talking. Prices everything, even answers.

greet.says: Stall's shut. Not mine, but I sweep it so the rats don't get fat on the stock. You buying or asking?

olive.says: Traded down the far arc one season, came back with a sack of olives and nothing else to show for it. That's the whole story people like. The true part is I was gone eight months and glad to be back, and the olives were the excuse.

volna.says: I asked. Nobody had a road for her. People leave the Nave sometimes, and the ones who answer questions are never the ones who leave. Now, if you want pepper I can weigh it at my own stall, two squares east.

whose.says: Old Volna's. Weighed pepper here forty years, never once shorted a customer, and then one second shift she poured a measure, set it down, and walked. Stall's been like this since. I keep it swept out of respect, nothing more.

choices.text: The notches on the beam look cut four times.

weights.says: Calibrated weekly, per the stencil. Each cut's a different hand over the years. Volna cut the last one shallow — I think she knew she wasn't staying to weigh another week. Hands know things before the rest of us.

reactions.grief: They forget to charge, wave off the coin twice, and only then ask who found the body.
reactions.shock: Their eyes fix past the body while the price-list runs under their breath, numbers giving out before nerve does.
reactions.bribed: The bribe gets quoted its fair price, then refused, because their measures are checked and they stay under them.
reactions.accused: Out loud they price the accusation like goods, slower than anything they sell, slowness being all the dignity they have.
reactions.flattered: Flattery is an opening bid, so they answer with the real price before the praise finishes landing.
reactions.questioned: Teichedd answers in question order, as if each question had a set price and the change is already counted.
reactions.threatened: When the threat lands they quote the cheapest ending like freight, though their thumb finds the knife's spine.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Mid-count they lose the number, restart, lose it again, then admit the truth at whatever rate it comes.
reactions.authority_arrives: Before the official can ask they tap the stencil overhead: disputes go to the factor, never to them.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The pans swing and Teichedd steadies them flat-handed, then demands who jostled a beam nobody stands under.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The accused gets the flat tone they save for bad coin, vouched for by hand-count, not by liking.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They hand over the only answer they were ever given, no road, and hate how little it weighs.

npc.description: Teichedd the Olive-Returned leans at the stall's corner, sweeping spilled grains into a paper cone with the flat of a knife. Brown skin, sun-cracked hands, an apron washed thin at the pockets where weights ride.

lore.name: The stopped scale
lore.description: The hanging scale's brass pan holds a twist of paper, weighed down by a one-mark weight. Someone poured out a measure, wrote the price, and then set it down unfinished. The calibration notch on the beam has been re-cut four times, each deeper than the last, the oldest two worn smooth. The last notch is shallow, like the hand that cut it was hurried.

content.name: The Weigher Stall of Second Shift
content.description: Pepper and cinnamon have gone stale in the open pans, sweet over something older gone sour. A hemp rope hangs slack from the beam; the scale under it sits at half a hand's tilt, weighed with spice nobody came back for. Stenciled above the pans: SCALE CALIBRATED WEEKLY, DISPUTES TO THE FACTOR.

npc.name: Ashail Three-Gs
npc.voice: Terse, deal-shaped — everything offered as an exchange, even answers.

greet.says: Stalls open, stalls unclaimed — pick one and it's yours until the wind season. You wanting counter-space or passage? Space is free, passage is a favor, and I'm short on favors.

choices.text: Why rebuild the whole arcade at once?

ask_arcade.says: Because Mercury's lines wanted the truss for a relay run, and you don't refuse this deep. We traded — arcade stays, rails move signals. Good terms. Now excuse me, these pans won't rack themselves.

reactions.grief: The dead hold no debt to her; she owes them one, and she racks pans she no longer counts.
reactions.shock: She drops a quartz pan whole and stares past the rail, and nothing comes out for sale.
reactions.bribed: She doesn't refuse; she asks who else is bidding, because a look-away with one buyer is underpriced.
reactions.accused: An accusation is a bid she won't meet blind, and she demands the evidence before naming a counter-price.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands warmer than she wants it to, and she covers by pricing it like any other bid.
reactions.questioned: Her answers come back in route-codes and weights, each movement a shipment with a receipt on file.
reactions.threatened: Threats carry no price tag, and she goes quiet in the way she never goes for a bad deal.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The weighing stops mid-pan; she calls the lie a rounding error and offers a corrected one at cost.
reactions.authority_arrives: She declares her stock unprompted, route-codes crisp, the way one pre-empts an audit with a clean ledger.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The pans rattle in their racks and her hands go to them before her face decides anything.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She vouches for the accused's credit unprompted, and the vouch runs long, one debt too many in it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: For once she has no counter-offer, and the bare no comes out of her like a foreign coin.

npc.description: Ashail Three-Gs works the center stall with the quick economy of someone mid-deal even with no counterparty, weighing out spun wool into quartz pans and racking them by route-code, wrist-cord flicking through her fingers between placements.

lore.name: The Tally-Board That Survived
lore.description: One stall counter is older than the rest around it, its quartz edge fused at a slightly different hue; bolted to it hangs a scarred tally-board whose knots record routes nobody here has walked.

content.name: Barter-Arcade 57
content.description: The floor speaks first: quartz fused into a single sweep, still warm from the fusing, gripping the boot with a tack no foot has dulled yet. A hundred stalls run the truss in two ranks, silver wool packed behind each counter, and between them the deck gives onto nothing — a handrail, then the drop down the cylinder's curve, forty meters of rail to the lit fields overhead. Along the truss web, stenciled fresh: ARCADE SECURED ABOVE WIND FORCE SIX. Everything is plumb, unlatched, and waiting for its first worn place.

npc.name: Risiolbro Naldi
npc.voice: Precise, unhurried, allergic to vague terms. Quotes procedure the way other people quote family.

end.says: Door works. Wall half does. Mind the pipe-run — it's live and it's rude.

greet.says: You'll be wanting Close 249. This is 251. But since you're standing there — state it.

ask_post.says: Brann's. Brann has a newborn and no sense of filing a transfer, so I hold the corner until the writ catches up. The office doesn't close because a life changed. That's rather the point of one.

ask_writ.says: Boundary amendment, Close 247 against the shared court. Ninth time it's come through. The precedent's clear — Solen's office ruled it before I was born — but they keep sending it, so I keep reading it. Continuity is mostly reading the same thing twice.

choices.text: I'll leave you to your forty-one nights.

ask_tally.says: Forty-one nights without a call nobody answered. We mark them. When it breaks, we want to know how long the good run was. Forty-one is respectable. Don't break it tonight.
