reactions.grief: Gives the dead man's close number before his name, says the name twice, and writes nothing down.
reactions.shock: Their eyes go to the body once and return to the writ, which they have stopped reading.
reactions.bribed: Names the exact section of code the offer violates, and prices the offer out loud, insultingly low.
reactions.accused: Asks for the accusation in writing, and the pen in their hand is steadier than their voice.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit on the desk unfiled, and asks what the flatterer actually wants.
reactions.questioned: Answers to the minute without looking up, as though the question were a form already filed.
reactions.threatened: Recites the threat back verbatim, slower, as though filing it made it survivable.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stops mid-sentence for the first time in anyone's memory, then blames the transcript.
reactions.authority_arrives: Stands, gives jurisdiction its titles in order, and does not sit again until invited.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Writes the time of the shudder in the margin first, and only then admits their hands are shaking.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects on procedure first, and only the pause before it suggests the objection is personal.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Quotes the clause that binds their hands, and for once the precision sounds like an apology.

npc.description: Risiolbro Naldi sits behind a desk too large for the room, sleeves rolled, reading a writ with the patience of someone who expects it to argue back. The coverall is watch-blue and fits like it was issued to somebody broader.

lore.name: The shift board
lore.description: A slate by the desk with the watch rotation chalked a month deep. Every name is in a different hand except one column — the night watches, all in the same slanted script, going back further than the slate should allow.

content.name: Watch Office, Close 251
content.description: The heat has pooled by the opened wall where the pipe-work lies exposed; the desk end still holds last night's cold. The room is one wide stride across, floorboards announcing every step. Deep blue paint runs up the wall in a hand-height band, and above it, stenciled twice where the plaster's been cut away: REPORT HERE, NOT TO THE CROWD. A rubber mat curls under the desk. A chalk tally stands at forty-one on the shutter, reason unlisted.

npc.name: Bode Nozdova
npc.voice: Short. Fair-minded in a bookkeeping way — every kindness comes with a note of what it costs.

tubs.says: Valve seals went. Old ones. This isn't even my shift — Nozdova's on a delivery — so mind what you touch. Chalk's on the shelf.

greet.says: Back of the line unless your name's on the board. It isn't. You want a slot, you wait like everyone else.

choices.text: What happened to the other two?

reactions.grief: The hand-valve drifts open under their fingers, scalding water rising, while they ask twice who will cover the shift.
reactions.shock: Stands in the doorway with chalk already out, then writes nothing, because the board has no column for this.
reactions.bribed: The cost of looking away gets itemized aloud — tab, board, room's name — then declined, politely, at no charge.
reactions.accused: The accusation comes back flat, then quieter, then quieter still, and it never balances.
reactions.flattered: Whatever the praise is selling, they let it finish, then ask the price — flat, unembarrassed, twice if needed.
reactions.questioned: The day comes out of them in ledger order — delivery, hour, borrowed tab — then they ask who else answered.
reactions.threatened: Their voice stays level through rule, fine, and appeal, but the loose ribbon goes untied the whole time.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: One breath too long on the denial, then the correction pours out all at once, reasons itemized.
reactions.authority_arrives: The borrowed tab, still inside-out, gets straightened twice before the official finishes crossing the room.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Tub, valve, list — they call the count before anyone asks, because counting is what they do instead of fear.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They give Nozdova's delivery to the minute, then hear how fast it came out and stop.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No comes first, reasons second, and still the plea gets chalked on the board's edge for whoever holds power.

npc.description: Bode Nozdova sits on an upturned pail, rationing heat to the one working tub by a hand-valve they open and close without looking at it. Their shift-tab is clipped inside-out, borrowed from someone smaller. A length of ribbon ties back hair that keeps coming loose.

lore.name: The Long Account Board
lore.description: The wait-list is not paper. It is a slab of slate by the third tub, and the names on it are chalked over decades of chalk, the board never washed. Rub a thumb across it and you feel the grooves of names from generations back, scrubbed thin but not erased. Continuants add to it in the order they arrived, and nobody has ever moved a name up.

content.name: The Bathhouse Tub of Long Account
content.description: The floor is gritted with dried soap; bare feet read every step of it. One tub still steams. Two lie open, pipes coiled on the tiles, and a stencilled sign overhead says THREE TUBS, SIGN THE LIST. Sunlight sits in a strip across dust-white linen. Wait-list work.

npc.name: Perbita Derteraldi
npc.voice: Brisk, short answers, over-practiced calm. She names prices before you ask. If you ask about the kettle she tells you it comes on when it comes on, and her hands stop moving while she says it.

lit.says: There. Steam in a minute. Sit anywhere, the good bench is the one that wobbles — Doss never let anyone plane it flat.

host.says: The thin row is Doss. She kept this stoop thirty years and poured slower at the end, I don't know why. She went down a tunnel with the Rindwalker cousins last month and hasn't come back up. I lit the kettle that night. Today I couldn't.

greet.says: Tea's four. Six with the plum cake. The kettle's slow today, so cake if you're in a hurry.

choices.text: Point at the tallies pressed into the lead.
Take the tea and step aside.

shift.says: This isn't my shift. I cover Frame 82 Over on the last bell, mornings I'm at the green decks. The host didn't come today. That's all I know, and I've told the council the same.

choices.text: When did you notice the kettle hadn't been lit?

tally.says: A hundred pours, a nick. That's the counter itself, not mine. The deep ones are the first host's. Mine start where they go thin.

reactions.grief: She tells them how Doss poured slower at the end, far more than anyone asked, and keeps wiping.
reactions.shock: She stands in the doorway with a cup in each hand and does not come in, or move, or speak.
reactions.bribed: She quotes the sum back like a menu price and asks what memory they think they are buying.
reactions.accused: Her hands stop on the cup and she asks, too loud, who told them that.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them in the same voice she uses for prices and waits for the ask she knows is coming.
reactions.questioned: She lists her morning like prices, brisk, and only her eyes flick to the cold kettle.
reactions.threatened: She names the price of tea again, flat and pointless, and her eyes stay on their hands.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She stares at the cold flue, then says the kettle line again slower, as if they misheard her.
reactions.authority_arrives: She straightens Doss's apron before the official reaches the counter and greets them like any customer, prices first.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room moves and she looks at the cold kettle, first time all day, then back to her cups.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She says no before the sentence finishes, because if the cousins did it, Doss is not coming back.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says she pours tea, that is the whole of it, and her hands stop while she says it.

npc.description: Perbita Derteraldi stands where the host should, wiping cups that are already clean, in an apron rolled at the waist to fit someone taller. She has not lit the kettle and does not look at it.

lore.name: The Pour Ledger
lore.description: The lead counter is soft metal, and the kettle stand is set into a shallow dish of it. In that dish someone has pressed a tally: one nick per hundred pours, in rows, some of them darkened with tea. The rows stop abruptly two-thirds across. A second hand began the last row, and its nicks are shallower and farther apart than the first.

content.name: Frame 82 Over
content.description: The kettle sits silent. Steam should be rising from it by now, and is not. Behind it the counter of hammered lead carries a stenciled line, KETTLE ON FROM FIRST BELL, half worn to shadow. Sun falls through the doorway onto customers waiting without complaint.

npc.name: Shana Venov
npc.voice: Ledger-calm, terms worn smooth from private use; she speaks of the sump the way a person speaks of a coworker, accurately and without affection, and occasionally answers questions the player has not asked.

greet.says: You came in on the warm floor. Everyone does, first time. Sit if you like — the cold up there doesn't want you, but it'll take you anyway, given an hour. I'm finishing here. The sump's past its keep, and I'd rather be gone before it decides anything.

choices.text: Past its keep — what does it keep?
Where does all the salt come from?
You said 'before it decides.' Decides what?

ask_salt.says: That's the wrong question, but a good one. It doesn't come from anywhere. It accretes — the room pulls it out of nothing, or out of time, I've stopped distinguishing. Weigh a dike Monday, weigh it Friday, and the mass is more than the air could have owed. Saturn keeps a ledger we can't see the other column of.

ask_sump.says: Everything that settles out of the deep air. Rust-breath,shed prayer, whatever the hull exhales when Saturn turns over in its sleep. My order says retain, not analyse. I used to think that was humility. Lately I think it's mercy — the ones who analysed are the ones who stopped filing, and I'd like to keep my filing hand.

choices.text: The maintenance teams. You knew them?

ask_player.says: I know. I could tell before you spoke — the air settled differently around you, like it had already made room. Whatever you were rebuilt for, the deep has been expecting the shape of you. Mind the warm floor going down. It's the last honest thing you'll stand on.

ask_filings.says: Rindwalkers, like me. Good hands, better than mine. They went past the third seal with instruments that still worked and came back without the part of a person that writes reports. One of them told me the sump isn't a sump. She said it's a wound that forgot whose. Then she smiled at the floor for a long while.

choices.text: I'm going deeper. Past the third seal.

ask_leaving.says: Nothing I have words for. The sump is overfull, and overfull things get opinions. I store what it refuses, I mark what it keeps, and I go home while the going is a choice. That's the whole of my theology.

reactions.grief: Answers the death with a file number, then winds one loop of filament four times over.
reactions.shock: Stands one-booted, unable to remember which foot comes first, watching the violence the way the sump watches sound.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the gift would cost the ledger, and refuses on arithmetic before morality gets a word.
reactions.accused: Corrects the charge like a misfiled entry, though her hands have gone still on the filament.
reactions.flattered: Weighs the praise like sump-fall, finds it lighter than the air could owe, and files it under suspicion.
reactions.questioned: Recites her movements like a filed entry, then supplies tomorrow's route before anyone asks.
reactions.threatened: Names exactly what is threatened, in the tone she keeps for the sump's deeper figures, eyes never lifting.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats the claim once, quieter, then logs the discrepancy against herself in a hand less steady than usual.
reactions.authority_arrives: Extends her ledger before any greeting, one boot still off, jurisdiction outranking dignity in her arithmetic.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Waits for the sump to hesitate, then records the hour anyway, her hand steadier than her breathing.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Offers an alibi for the named culprit unprompted, then hears her own loyalty in it and stops mid-sentence.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains precisely why she cannot, then stays anyway, winding filament that no longer needs winding.

npc.description: Shana Venov coils the last of the drawn filament with the tenderness of someone binding a wound that is not hers, working by a rhythm that ignores the room's wrongness the way sailors ignore weather. Her pack sits already buckled. She has one boot off.

lore.name: A sounding-weight stamped with an older tally
lore.description: A filament plumb-bob rests on the sump's lip, its face incised with tally-marks in Saturn's oldest notation — more marks than the room's years could earn, scratched in a hand that gave up somewhere past counting and began again smaller.

content.name: The Settling Sump
content.description: The cold is not here. That is the first thing the body reports, and the first thing it cannot mean: warmth pools at ankle-height as if the floor were breathing upward, while the vault above stays iron-dark and temperatureless, a sky that has opted out of weather. Salt, compacted into pale dikes, rims a sump deeper than its mouth admits — sound goes in and does not so much echo as hesitate. Drawn filament hangs in curtains, catching no light yet being visible anyway. Stencilled above the drop: ACCRETION RETAINED NOT ANALYSED. More has settled here than the room was made to keep, and the room, if rooms keep, has not complained.

npc.name: Yedichiama Toadmothered
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical, wrong in the combinations — she speaks of the smoke the way a nurse speaks of a pulse: as a thing monitored, not caused.

greet.says: You're breathing my smoke secondhand. Nobody lights it. Nobody ever lit it. Don't ask me who tends it — I tend the flue, and the flue tends the smoke, and past that the chain goes somewhere I've stopped following.

choices.text: Where does the smoke come from, then?

smoke.says: From below. From where the dreams are filed. The ship exhales what it remembers, and we built a chimney to it centuries after the fact — like drilling a well into a river. Take the tally-stylus if you're going down there. She'll know you've been counted.

reactions.grief: She goes down the flue in her mind, to where the dead are filed, and stays there a while.
reactions.shock: She kneels ankle-deep in the seam and reads the dead like a pulse, finding stillness where a pulse should be.
reactions.bribed: Her eyes go to the stencil — SMOKE PRESENT, NO COMBUSTION LOGGED — as if it were the bribe's rebuttal.
reactions.accused: The stylus skips its tally for the first time in years; she resumes before anyone can call it a confession.
reactions.flattered: Praise unsettles her like still smoke; she checks the flue for what is being drawn out of her.
reactions.questioned: Asked to account for herself, she gives her watch in liturgical order and omits nothing because nothing has ever happened.
reactions.threatened: Threatened, she overshares the whole chain — flue, smoke, whatever files the dreams — as if volume were a place to hide.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She denies nothing, only corrects the record as though truth were a transcription error in someone else's ledger.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official receives the deference owed a censer, not a person — acknowledged, unaddressed, kept at stylus-length.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder she logs like any reading; the smoke's hesitation is what makes her set the stylus down.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Relief crosses her face and is instantly repented; she has wanted that name said aloud for longer than she admits.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She refuses in liturgical form, which is her only shape for helplessness, and cannot meet the asker's eyes after.

npc.description: Yedichiama Toadmothered stands ankle-deep in the seam between wall and floor, running a stylus of drawn filament along a joint that has no depth to measure. She does not startle at your entrance; she simply pauses, the way water pauses, and looks at you with the flat patience of someone who has outlived the need to explain a room to anyone.

lore.name: The Unkindled Censer
lore.description: The censer is capped, cold, and bolted against refilling — yet a hairline feed of smoke threads from beneath its seal, drawn upward through the filament like water finding a level that does not exist. Scratched into its base in an older, deeper hand: a tally of watches, each mark struck through. Whoever kept count stopped counting the day the smoke began.

content.name: The Incense Flue of Third Watch
content.description: The censer hangs a hand's breadth below the flue's mouth, which means the smoke must climb a distance it cannot cross — and climbs it anyway, unhurried, as if height were a suggestion. Walls of vitrified ash, chalk-white, recoil from the drawn filament overhead in seams no fingernail could find. Stencilled at knee height, absurdly legible: SMOKE PRESENT NO COMBUSTION LOGGED. The air tastes of myrrh that never burned, correct and unearned, like a confession rehearsed for an audience of no one.

npc.name: Vosvoto Nestkridryazd
npc.voice: Plain, unhurried. Counts things out loud even in conversation. Talks about the flock as a line of birds reaching past her, and any break in that line as a debt.

wax.says: Clinic porcelain. The blue glaze holds warmth through a cold night better than anything the makers sell now. Crack it, plug it, keep using it. My grandmother plugged these same cups. Mine will outlast me, plugged or whole.

cage.says: That was Toma's frame. Toma built fast and finished slow. Weeks gone now, no word down the stairs, and the hens lay in it anyway like it was done. I finish what's left in this room, whoever left it. That's the whole job, near enough.

coop.says: Forty-one years of eggs and feathers, and the roof under it older than the ledger. The slats go every third winter. The wax goes every season. You don't ask if a thing like this lasts. You ask what it needs next.

next.says: The west wind finds every gap now. I want real sheeting, and the requisition says spring. My knees say autumn. One of us is wrong and it isn't the knees. But the hens lay, the line holds, and tomorrow I count again. Sixteen, if the roof is kind.

toma.says: The council logged it. Logged, filed, done. I asked Vey in the hall office to keep the file open another month. He said files don't work that way. I said neither do birds, if you stop feeding them. He didn't laugh.

greet.says: Hold on. Fourteen, fifteen... sixteen. Good. Sixteen hens, close count, as the wall says. What brings you up two hundred steps to my birds?

choices.text: Ask how long the coop has stood here.
Ask about the wax on the feed cups.

reactions.grief: She stops at thirty-nine and starts over three times before she asks who else was on the stairs with them.
reactions.shock: She looks, then describes the wire gauge of the nearest cage, voice level, hands gone still around the feeder.
reactions.bribed: She asks what the offer buys in feed and slats, then says no in the same ledger voice.
reactions.accused: The hen goes down first; she gives the day's count twice, slow, as if the number might argue for her.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them in three words and asks twice what it is they actually want fixed.
reactions.questioned: She answers in exact numbers, hens by cage, and treats the questions as one more tally at close.
reactions.threatened: Under the counting her mind is doing subtraction: what she owes, what gets taken, which cages go empty first.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Mid-count she loses her place, starts over at one, and does not look up while she lies about the rest.
reactions.authority_arrives: She counts the escorts before the official, then places herself where the stencil on the wall sits visible behind her.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first words are numbers; she counts every bird aloud before admitting the shudder has no place in her ledger.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She lists the accused's small paid debts — mended slats, loaned feed — saying far more than a witness should.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She cannot mend what's asked and says so plain, then puts six eggs in the pleading hands anyway.

npc.description: Vosvoto Nestkridryazd kneels at the third cage down, indigo coat open, holding a hen against her forearm the way you hold a thing you have held ten thousand times. Beside her sits a half-built cage frame that is not hers, abandoned weeks ago by someone who never came back for it.

lore.name: Porcelain feed cups
lore.description: The feeders are porcelain, blue-glazed, older than any cage here. Each has a hairline crack stopped with a plug of sealed wax. Vosvoto melts a new plug every season. The cups came from a clinic storeroom forty years back, and nobody has found better since.

content.name: Coop Farm
content.description: The roof smells of feather dust, warm grain, and the sharp ammonia tang of quail droppings baking in the sun-strip. Wire cages stand in crooked rows along the parapet, half of them patched with wax-sealed cloth. Wind comes straight through the gaps. A stencil on the coop wall reads: COUNT THE BIRDS AT CLOSE.

npc.name: Tziktzin-Yolkoatl
npc.voice: Terse, transactional. Talks in totals and counts. Regards conversation as a fee being paid out, and pays the minimum.

desk.says: Every animal through this pen gets a brand check before coin moves, that's the rule and I keep it. More herds coming through this season than the desk was built for. If you're buying, the ledger's the truth of what's for sale. The sellers will tell you the rest.

choices.text: Understood. I'll leave you to the queue.

greet.says: Buyer, seller, or looker? Say it quick. The pen queue doesn't shorten itself.

reactions.grief: Talks for a full minute about the dead seller's dog, the longest anyone has heard from them.
reactions.shock: Looks once, then looks at the wall with the rule on it, and does not look back.
reactions.bribed: Names a price high enough that no one could pay it, and calls that honesty.
reactions.accused: The mallet comes down once on the counter, hard, and they demand the accuser's figures in writing.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands somewhere unguarded; they go red to the ears and raise their fee for talking.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day's movements by count and hour, then names the fee for another minute of it.
reactions.threatened: Promises whatever is asked, keeps counting entries aloud through the whole threat, and misses a number for the first time.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Gives a number, is shown the ledger says otherwise, and gives the same number again, slower.
reactions.authority_arrives: Reaches for the ledger jurisdiction always asks for before the official is through the sacking.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches two ledgers off the leaning stack before they fall, and waits for a second shudder that does not come.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Has kept the accused's unreconciled tallies in their head for years and empties the whole hoard now, unprompted.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says the stamp is the stamp, means it, and hates how easily they mean it.

npc.description: Tziktzin-Yolkoatl sits wedged behind the ledger stacks, sleeves rolled, one hand flat on an open page as if holding it down against the draught. The other gestures at the person across the counter to wait. A sacking apron, ink to the second knuckle, a stamping-mallet hung at the hip like a tool that has settled there.

lore.name: The Brand-Check Gauge
lore.description: Bolted to the counter's edge is a copper yoke with three notches, sized to fit against a beast's ear-stamp. The middle notch is worn bright; the other two are clogged with ink. Below them, scratched into the counter: a fourth notch, added later, deeper than the rest, and a column in the ledger beside it headed DOUBTFUL. Half that column is filled in.

content.name: The Ledger Desk
content.description: The pen noise comes through flat, like voices under cloth; sacking hangs over the doorway and eats every sound at a yard. Inside, ledgers stack to the ceiling on a copper counter, spilling onto stools. Two people stop talking when you duck in. Off-white plaster above the counter reads NO SALE WITHOUT THE BRAND CHECK.

npc.name: Ryepyazeim Dozdov
npc.voice: Clipped, liturgical, the grammar of maintenance-as-prayer; measures before metaphors, but cannot resist the metaphor.

open.says: No one you could name, and I have read the oldest layer on these walls with my own hands. It predates the Nave, predates the wards, predates the word 'aboard.' Whatever civilization is, it grew here like moss on something that was already thinking. We are not maintaining the ship. We are guests maintaining the host's nervous system and calling it ours.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry what you said.
Guests. Then who is the host?

greet.says: Mind the floor seam. It moves when we are not looking, which is most of the time.

choices.text: What is this room made of?
Who do you answer to down here?
This machinery—who laid the first stone of it?

probe_a.says: Salt pressed until it forgot the sea it never saw, and wool spun from stone that never was a lamb. We build with substances that mime origins they never had. So does the ship, if you press your ear low enough.

probe_b.says: Answer to? The doctrine says Saturn, but Saturn has never once corrected me, and correction is the only conversation I trust. My answers run uphill to people who stopped filing. I keep working. That is the whole of my obedience.

probe_c.says: Borrowed time is still time, and a mender does not ask whose loan. What I hate is that the machinery forgives my failures before I make them. It anticipates. A thing that anticipates a mender needs no mender, and yet here I stand, salaried by habit.

reactions.grief: The name reaches him and his liturgy arrives late, hands already moving through a rite the dead cannot use.
reactions.shock: Shock empties him of scripture; he speaks to the corpse familiarly, as to furniture that has stopped working.
reactions.bribed: Offered payment to misremember, he refuses on property grounds: the walls belong to something older than either of them.
reactions.accused: He sets the gauge to the nearest wall first, needing one true reading before trusting his own voice.
reactions.flattered: Praise from a wanting mouth, he prices like any ledger entry, and finds himself pleased anyway, which shames him.
reactions.questioned: He recites his movements like a breviary, giving the routine inquiry the complete liturgy it never requested.
reactions.threatened: Under explicit threat he answers in the grammar of inspection, voice level, thumb whitening where it grips the gauge.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The evidence contradicts him and he blames the seam — walls move, testimony moves — then falls silent at his own glibness.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction enters and Dozdov gives it stencilled deference while his eyes audit the seams the official never reads.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The stillness of six years breaks and he laughs once, awful with relief, a sound no register holds.
reactions.someone_else_accused: When his quarrel-partner is named culprit, the quarrel dies at once, and he notices its dying with alarm.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to grant the plea, he offers a dweller's only asset: attention, and a vow to keep measuring.

npc.description: In the chalk-white fold of Register 54 Under, where compacted salt sweats against spun mineral wool and a stencilled line swears POSITION LAST CONFIRMED SIX YEARS AGO, Ryepyazeim Dozdov stands with a gauge pressed to the wall—and the gauge is still, though nothing here should be. The air is thermally wrong, warm at the floor, cold at the hand's height, a recursion of climates arguing with themselves.

lore.name: The Gnomon Weight
lore.description: The suspended counterweight is scored with a helical groove worn by something plumb and patient — a cord of Rindwalker braid, generations of it, used to take its reading. The groove's turns outnumber any braid's knot-pattern a walker could wear in a lifetime. Someone has been asking this room where it is, over and over, far longer than the Nave has had a name for asking.

content.name: Register 54 Under
content.description: Nothing moves. That is the first fact: a pendulous counterweight the size of a coffin hangs mid-swing it plainly began years ago, and the dust settling on its upper face lies in drifts, undisturbed. Chalk-white folds of compacted salt and spun mineral wool interlock like the gizzards of some preterlucent god, each fold seating into the next along seams too regular for hands and too worn for machines. Stencilled across one wall: POSITION LAST CONFIRMED SIX YEARS AGO. The air is warm where cold should pool. Ryepyazeim Dozdov and a companion stand mid-quarrel, salt dust on their sleeves, and go silent as one.

npc.name: Tzitlil the Twice-Burned
npc.voice: Short, dry, quick to answer a question with a question. Words chosen like goods being weighed for trade.

open.says: The Braid is us. Runners, brokers, anyone who carries word for pay. No head, no hall — a cord knot, a promise, a route. It moves news faster than the council can print it, which is why the council pretends it's a rumor. A room like this is a knot in it: subscribers come, they read, they talk, and by evening the whole belt knows. I burn twice and still the words get through. That's the work.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll subscribe if I pass again.
So nothing said here is only said here.

greet.says: Chairs are by subscription. If you're not subscribed, stand or leave.

choices.text: You said the Braid notices things. Who are the Braid?
I'll come back when you're done.

probe_a.says: Fire took the old room twice, and me with it, mostly. Third time we built in glass so the next fire has to work for it. Everything correct, nothing worn in. Give it ten years and it'll feel like a room.

probe_b.says: Subscribers pay. Traders mostly, readers between runs. I keep the list, and the list keeps me. Nobody reads free, and I don't argue with that anymore.

probe_c.says: Routes, prices, gossip off the terminals. Lately they compare the mythograph postings like race results. Someone changed something in those posts. Readers notice before officials do. That's the whole trade, right there.

reactions.grief: The name lands; she finishes the crate anyway, then sits in chair number one without a subscription.
reactions.shock: She sees it and goes elsewhere, counting chairs under her breath until the room is only a room again.
reactions.bribed: She asks what the silence costs wholesale, then quotes a number nobody in the room can pay.
reactions.accused: She stops mid-fold on a ledger page and says the accusation back once, flat, as if checking the exchange rate.
reactions.flattered: She hears the praise, prices it like stolen goods, and thanks the flatterer for the opening bid.
reactions.questioned: She answers with a question of her own, pricing the asker like a subscriber she hasn't quoted yet.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands somewhere old and burned; her hand finds the cracked glass pane and stays there.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she re-weighs the words aloud and adjusts the lie like a bad quote, without apology.
reactions.authority_arrives: She keeps packing the crate and gestures at the subscription sign, letting jurisdiction wait its turn.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder hits and she is under the table before she decides anything, hands over her head.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She names the accused's route and standing before anyone asks, faster than she has ever quoted a price.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She takes the plea like a message she cannot deliver, and says so twice, the second time quieter.

npc.description: Tzitlil stands a numbered chair on the tabletop, unscrewing a cracked glass pane from its back. The room smells of hot glue and cut plastic, sharp and sweet, the smell of a rebuild with no years on it yet.

lore.name: The subscription board
lore.description: Beside the door hangs a slate board with forty numbered hooks. Each hook holds a cord knotted in a different pattern, and under each a strip of paper with a name and a date range. The knots are Drift route-marks: subscribers leave their wrist-cords here while they read, so anyone checking the board can see who is in the room, who is due back, and who has knotted a detour into their return route. Three cords hang on hooks with no paper at all.

content.name: Reading Room
content.description: The room smells of fresh-cut plastic and hot glue, the sharpness of it still in the air. Numbered chairs sit in rows under the sun-strip, all magenta, none scuffed. A stenciled sign says CHAIR BY SUBSCRIPTION ONLY. Tzitlil the Twice-Burned is packing ledgers into a crate, nearly done.

npc.name: Hesoto Yidinbara
npc.voice: Terse, institutional, tired. Counts things before speaking.

ask.says: Not mine. That was Brenner's work, and Brenner walked out of here three days ago without undoing a single knot. Take the bundle if you want it. Wrap something. Somebody should.

greet.says: We're down to nine cots. If you're here about the leaving, ask the registry, not me. I clean. I don't file.

choices.text: Ask who wrapped that bundle on the cot.

reactions.grief: The name lands and they recount the cots, twice, getting twelve both times, and start over anyway.
reactions.shock: They note the mess before the body, then scrub one clean tile until someone takes the rag away.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets counted twice, aloud, then refused in the same flat tone they use for inventory.
reactions.accused: Their denial comes too fast and runs too long, dragging in every name that walked out without undoing a knot.
reactions.flattered: They hear the want behind the praise, weigh it like inventory, and answer in two dry words without looking up.
reactions.questioned: Already counting before the question ends, they recite hours and destinations and go back to a tile that needs nothing.
reactions.threatened: They ask whether the threat comes with paperwork, eyes on the grout the entire time.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Halfway through their count the number goes wrong, and they stop, rag slack in one hand, saying nothing after.
reactions.authority_arrives: Numbers arrive before the official asks — cots, names, days without incident — in the voice of every inspection they have survived.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They steady the basins first, then stand very still in the clean square as if it might explain the sound.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They say the name is wrong and then list, unprompted, every fault the accused doesn't have.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say the registry handles it, then say it again slower, and keep wringing the rag like it owes them an exception.

npc.description: Hesoto Yidinbara works a rag along the big square of clean floor, going over tiles that are already clean. A half-wrapped bundle of gutta-percha sits on the cot beside them, started by another hand, abandoned mid-fold. They don't look up when the smoke from the little brazier drifts between you.

lore.name: Cot Frame with Two Names
lore.description: One cot is bolted differently from the rest: its gutta-percha wraps have been cut and re-laced, and the name plate carries two names, one filed down. Under the plate, scratched into the frame, is a third name in a child's hand, misspelled. Somebody counted this child twice and couldn't decide which listing was true.

content.name: Foundling Home
content.description: Something skitters along the top shelf and stops. The silo rises six floors, dust-white, ringed with cots and enamel basins. A stencilled line on the stair wall reads TWELVE COTS, TWELVE NAMES ON THE WALL. Where a big thing stood near the center, the floor tiles are a cleaner square.

npc.name: Adaska Gringer
npc.voice: Ledger-precise, short on patience, longer on what the ship is owed. Talks in weights, counts, and dates.

end.says: Mind the third rung on your way up. It's worn.

gap.says: A turnstone cradle holds what it's poured to hold, and that one's empty by order, not by theft. The count is right. The count is always right — ask the desk, not me.

choices.text: Fair enough. What do you store down here, normally?

who.says: Walkers with route-access, and the desk. My partner thinks fewer. I think fewer is the problem, not the answer. That's the whole of the argument you interrupted, and you've had it for free.

choices.text: I'll leave you to your count.

greet.says: Nobody comes down that ladder without business. Yours, or the one we were having?

order.says: Written, sealed, and above my pay in regard. What I'll say is this: when a thing is kept, it's kept for the generation coming after. When it's moved, somebody decided they won't need it. I don't have to like the arithmetic to keep the ledger honest.

choices.text: Who else knew it was here?

normal.says: Turnips, seed-cord, brine-kegs for the winter deck, and whatever the tunnels send up that needs a cool dark place and no questions. Mostly turnips. The ship feeds us first; that's the covenant.

disagreement.says: We disagree the way family does — about whether to report a discrepancy or sit on it until we understand it. One of us is wrong and it's not me, which is what everyone says.

reactions.grief: She keeps counting the resin layers on the wall until the number stops meaning anything, then asks when.
reactions.shock: The slate slips from under her arm; she lets it lie, reading the scene as a miscount she can't locate.
reactions.bribed: Whatever is offered gets quoted back at desk price, twice, so the offer knows it has been appraised and refused.
reactions.accused: The brush stops mid-stroke; she demands the accusation dated and in writing, as if ink makes it deniable.
reactions.flattered: Real figures, lower ones, stand in for her thanks; afterward she waits to hear the compliment's price.
reactions.questioned: The date, the hour, the tally — she supplies all three and returns to the resin before the question ends.
reactions.threatened: She assigns the threat a weight and a date, aloud, as though a filed number could keep it from landing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Cornered by her own numbers, she recounts them aloud, slower each time, the flush darkening past what the argument left.
reactions.authority_arrives: The stencil over the trapdoor comes out of her word for word, rehearsed, as if jurisdiction were a password.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the shudder passes she recounts the resin layers, finds one more than the ledger allows, and stops there.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The defense arrives before the accusation finishes — dates, crates, who signed — more complete than anyone asked her for.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She answers with the desk, the hours, the key — while one folded hand comes open at her side.

npc.description: Adaska Gringer stands with a ledger slate under one arm and a resin brush going dry in hand, the other hands folded out of habit. Copper thread at the collar, gone brown with cellar damp. The argument has left a flush that doesn't fade when the talking stops.

lore.name: The Turnstone Cradle
lore.description: Set into the slate where the gap opens, a resin-cast cradle shaped to hold something long and jointed, padded with braided cord worn glossy at the contact points. The cast is keyed — notched to fit only one object, the way a seal fits a hand — and someone has re-poured it twice; older casts' ghost-lines show under the newest layer. Whatever rested here was checked on often, and by more than one pair of hands.

content.name: Adefried's Root Cellar
content.description: The cold sits low here, ankle-deep, while the last of the day's heat pools at the ladder's mouth and goes no further. Two people stand over a swept gap in the slate floor, big enough for something you'd need help carrying, and they stop talking when your boot finds the third rung. Bone-pale resin coats the walls in layers, and over the trapdoor's frame, stenciled: TRAPDOOR LOCKED AT NIGHT, KEY AT THE DESK.

npc.name: Leaamaapangeastath the Moonlit
npc.voice: Measured, kind, unflinching — a healer's cadence applied to metal, never hurrying, never softening what the work does.

bones.says: When the ship mends a section, we mend whoever it was carrying through that section, same pour, same alloy. She doesn't distinguish. Neither do we. It's the only honest surgery there is.

greet.says: Mind the walk — it carries what the forge doesn't. You're standing in Venus's other clinic. Bones are bones, whatever they're made of.

scale.says: Once a year, down the green decks at their true size. She grows things on no schedule I can find, and she is *there* — not watching, just present, the way heat is present. After that the forge feels like a kitchen.

abandoned.says: Ranila's. They stopped filing mid-repair three months ago and haven't come up, and I keep their pour warm anyway. What Venus grows, she doesn't like to see torn out — and I don't like to ask the question that warm pour is really asking.

reactions.grief: Procedure reaches their mouth before sorrow does, and afterward they keep counting names that were never on the list.
reactions.shock: Reaches for a pulse before remembering to look at what made the wound, and the look is what stops them.
reactions.bribed: Prices the bribe like scrap nickel, finds it short of an oath's weight, and goes back to work.
reactions.accused: Points at the stencil above them both, then regrets the gesture's theater and lowers the hand.
reactions.flattered: Their eyes tap-test the flatterer first, and they thank the alloy that taught them to listen for hollow rings.
reactions.questioned: Answers in pour-log order, times and batches, the same cadence they use asking where it hurts.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands on hands that have reached into melt; they note its depth and ask when it takes effect.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They amend the statement like correcting a chart, flatly, and only their hands stop moving.
reactions.authority_arrives: From the gantry's worn center-line, they greet the official and do not step down to meet them.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Bare-handed, they check the nearest poured seam for new hairlines before checking the people.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says nothing about character, only what their hands have witnessed of the accused's work, which is worse.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Names the honest limit of their craft, kindly and without softening it, then stays in the room past the answer.

npc.description: Leaamaapangeastath the Moonlit stands braced against the melt-glow with the flat patience of someone whose shifts are measured against a forge's schedule and not a human one. Their forearms carry the shine of a hundred pours, nickel-bright at the crease of the elbow, and they move along the gantry without looking down, feet finding the walk's worn center-line by habit older than attention.

lore.name: The Queue Ledger, Cast in Place
lore.description: Bolted to the forge's living half is a plate of annealed nickel, and stamped into it, entry after entry, are paired names — one of a machine, one of a person — with the same date beside each. It is not a memorial list. It is a casting schedule: when the ship recasts a section of itself, it recasts the crew assigned to that section in the same pour, same alloy, same heat, and the ledger has kept that pairing for longer than the forge has kept any other part. The queue does not discriminate, and nobody here has ever written down why that is a comfort or a threat.

content.name: The Bone Forge
content.description: Something is turning when you enter: a mould of drawn filament, three hand-spans across, that Leaamaapangeastath is easing out of annealed nickel still warm enough to sting. The forge runs the length of a gantry walk that carries load from somewhere overhead to somewhere below, and half of it stands opened up, its ribs folded back like a chest on the table. Deep violet light off the melt pools up into a stencil on the framing: MACHINE AND CREW QUEUE SEPARATELY, TREATED THE SAME. Everything here is new or being made new; the only worn thing in the room is the worker.

npc.name: Skuras-Asen
npc.voice: Ledger-cadence, precise to the unit, courteous in the way of someone measuring out a scarce resource. Devotion expressed as tolerances.

draw.says: The tanks fill themselves, at their own valves' pleasure — the seals open on pressure we don't set. Filling is the ship's grace; drawing was ours, and the authority for it lapsed before my grandmother held a wrench. So we keep. Keeping is the whole of the vow when taking is closed.

choices.text: The pressure you don't set — has it ever opened a valve early?

early.says: Once. Tank nine, in a lean year — opened at full dark, vented clean, sealed again by morning, no mark on the drum but warmth. I logged it. Mars logged back, in the notation on the third weld-ring, and I have read that ring every shift since. You learn to be content with being answered at all.

choices.text: Keep your tanks. I'll mind the ash.

greet.says: Mind the ash on the walk — it slicks after a shift's footfall. You've come to the Skiolagn, where we hold what the hull gives back. State what you're after and I'll tell you whether it's stored here or merely kept.

choices.text: What do the cisterns actually hold?

leave.says: Walk center-of-bead. It holds best.

tanks.says: Ash, fused. What Mars's welding burns off comes down as fall-out and we vitrify it into drums — nothing the hull sheds goes back into the air unwon. Four hundred and twelve tanks, and the farm was drawn for half that. The ship burns hotter than the ledger allowed for. Note that I said hotter, not worse.

choices.text: The stencil says drawing requires authority no longer issued. So who fills them?

reactions.grief: The next seal gets torqued past spec, and once more, because hands refusing a name will still obey a number.
reactions.shock: The wrench stays half-turned in their grip; their eyes do the scripture-reading without them, and find no line for this.
reactions.bribed: The offer is measured like a gauge reading, acknowledged with perfect courtesy, and declined without once being named.
reactions.accused: Something old and unrepentant lifts its head, and their denial takes one calibration too long to leave the mouth.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands like the answer on tank nine's weld-ring — wanted, unwelcome — and their thanks run one degree too warm.
reactions.questioned: They account for each hour in quarter-shift increments, courteous as a ration, volunteering nothing the question never asked.
reactions.threatened: No fear gets named; they answer in tolerances, thumb finding the warm weld of the nearest cistern for ballast.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The figure gets corrected in three words; the account of tank nine follows unasked, hands gone still on the wrench.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction makes them straighten like a seal reseating, half-hoping to be read, half-afraid of what the reading finds.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They stand still as others stumble, lips moving through the count of four hundred drums; the count will not close.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Relief arrives before grief does, and they hate its arithmetic, and they say only that the timings do not balance.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Pleaded with for what the tanks hold, they recite inventories instead, and their voice slips only on the units.

npc.description: Skuras-Asen works the valve-gallery with a wrench longer than their leg, torquing seals in a rhythm that suggests the wrench, the arm, and the drum have agreed on a tempo. Chalk dust and ash-grey powder grind into the creases of their gloves; when they step back to read a pressure gauge they read it the way other people read scripture — once, close, without moving their lips.

lore.name: The Tally-Bar
lore.description: A copper rod hangs at the first cistern's valve, notched edge to edge with hatch-marks, and where the notches ran out the rod was extended — spliced, soldered, and notched again. Somebody has been counting draws on this tank for longer than the rod's original length allowed.

content.name: Skiolagn
content.description: Underfoot the floor gives first: sintered ceramic worn to a glassy polish along the tank-walks, gritty where spillage of vitrified ash has been swept but never fully lifted, and every few paces a weld bead rises through the tread like a healed scar. Beyond the walkways stand the cisterns — sealed drums of ash-fused material, each tall enough that a person on the catwalk reads them as architecture rather than vessels, so many that counting them past four hundred becomes an act of faith. Iron-dark and sweating faint warmth, they fill a chamber their girders were sized for a smaller traffic than crowds it now carries; queues braid between the tanks, and the stencilled warning — DRAW REQUIRES AUTHORITY NO LONGER ISSUED — has been trodden nearly blank.

npc.name: Khaimoth-Minavel
npc.voice: Fast, clipped, questions answered with what you need and not a syllable more — but a good question buys you an extra sentence.

deep.says: Below this there's shafts nobody upstairs has walked, and I've walked the ones I have. You're asking how deep the drain goes. So did I, once. The drum turned a full year before I stopped asking out loud.

greet.says: Walk, don't stand — the drum logs loiterers. You want something, ask it while we move.

choices.text: What used to sit in that cradle?

cradle.says: A core. Walked out under its own crating, if you believe the manifest, and I've stopped disbelieving manifests down here. It'll surface where it surfaces. Everything moves; that's the whole religion.

mercury.says: This is Mercury's artery, friend, not Mercury's parlor. The quick one answers — you'll have noticed — but answers on their own clock. I log the turns; the turns get read. That's the whole of my part in it.

choices.text: Could it have gone down? Below the rind?

reactions.grief: One full rotation of silence; then a new knot goes into the route-cord, as if the dead could be routed.
reactions.shock: The walk fails them mid-ring — the body that learned the drum's timing forgets which foot comes next.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the offer costs the record, then declines with the flatness of someone quoting a stencilled plate.
reactions.accused: One flat denial, then the rotation log offered up as witness, voice steady in the way of rehearsed things.
reactions.flattered: One extra sentence — exactly one — is all the flattery buys, priced like a question that wants something.
reactions.questioned: Answers in rivet-counts and ring numbers, already three steps along the second gantry before the question finishes.
reactions.threatened: The answers shrink to a single syllable apiece, and the graphite rod goes untouched though the pace holds.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Goes back to touch a rivet already counted, the closest they come to admitting the route was misstated.
reactions.authority_arrives: Watches the official the way they watch the drum's rim — counting the turn, waiting for it to pass.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For once they stand still, one hand flat on the rivets, listening for whether the rotation log caught it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The clipped economy cracks; they speak for the accused at double length, citing shaft-runs and manifests nobody requested.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers the only currency they hold — a route, recited twice — then counts rivets they no longer see.

npc.description: Khaimoth-Minavel walks the second ring with a graphite rod in one hand, touching it to each rivet in passing, lips counting. Wrist wrapped in a knotted cord worked dense with route-history; the walk is automatic, a body that has learned the drum's timing the way other bodies learn stairs.

lore.name: The Withdrawal Cradle
lore.description: The empty cradle was not built empty: its packing is spun mineral wool, combed and compressed to the shape of a drum-core that stood here until recently, a cylinder within the cylinder tall as three people and dense as packed graphite — which is partly what it was. Where the wool was lifted away you can read the pressure marks, and under them, scratched into the silver, a single tally notation matching nothing in the current log protocol. Whatever slept in this drum left inside a month, and the drum has been turning for it ever since, logging an absence.

content.name: Archive-Drum 13
content.description: Ozone and chilled graphite greet you first — the smell of messages long sped elsewhere — then the drum: a silver archive-cylinder riveted from rim to rim, wide enough that a full turn of it takes a minute you can stand inside and feel. Gantries ring it at three heights. Something large has lately gone from the central cradle, and the clean oval where it sat is paler than everything around it. The drum spins, echoless, past a stencilled plate: DRUM ROTATION LOGGED, DO NOT HALT MID-TURN. One worker moves along the rings, not stopping.

npc.name: Sher-Doranz
npc.voice: Quick, transactional, allergic to sentiment. Answers questions with better questions unless you pay in kind.

open.says: Esteem, that's the honest ledger — who's trusted, who's owed, who's worth knowing. But lately? The terminal posts. The tellers' blueprints have gone strange, and the Braid's been copying them and selling access to the strangeness, careful, to anyone who might read them. I've handled three copies myself. I can't read them. The buyers can, or think they can, and that's enough to set a price.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll knock loud somewhere else.
You're selling something you don't understand.

greet.says: Door was open because we're moving. If you're buying, buy. If you're staring, the stove's the only thing here that needs looking at.

choices.text: What is the Braid actually selling?

probe_a.says: Route banners. Every knot-pattern on the Braid gets printed before the runner leaves, so if they don't come back, the cloth does. Cyan for long hauls. This batch is for routes nobody's run in a season, which tells you what you want to know.

probe_b.says: The sixth name on the door. And before you ask — no, we don't scratch them off. The Drift doesn't own its people, so it doesn't get to erase them either. Everything moves. That's not the same as everything's gone.

probe_c.says: The knot I wear. My route history's in it — every relay I've ever run. Answer to that, mostly. Olo Vashti when the Braid needs a face, and lately the Braid needs a face more than it used to.

reactions.grief: They keep printing the route-banner for a runner who won't be carrying it, and only notice at the fourth strip.
reactions.shock: Nothing in the ledger covers this; the strip runs off the press uncut until the tray overflows.
reactions.bribed: A number comes back high enough to mean no, and the bare bunk gets swept again that night.
reactions.accused: Sher-Doranz stops mid-strip and asks who paid for the story to travel this far.
reactions.flattered: They let the praise finish, once, then ask what it's supposed to cost them.
reactions.questioned: No answer comes without a counter-question about who's paying for the asking, eyes never leaving the strip.
reactions.threatened: A price gets named for the threat, no higher, and the press starts up before their hands can shake.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The revision happens fast and out loud, the story repriced to fit the evidence mid-sentence.
reactions.authority_arrives: A stool crosses the floor to the official before any greeting does; deference doesn't come with it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The hanging banners sway before anyone speaks; they read the knots and don't like the answer.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Half a defense comes out and turns into the accused's own debts recited from memory, which is worse.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say plainly no route runs there, then cut a strip of cyan anyway, unasked.

npc.description: Sher-Doranz is feeding cyan-dyed silk through a press by the stove, one long strip after another, and doesn't stop until the strip is done. The row-house is narrow and low, cluttered with lacquer trays, and the gap where a sixth bed used to be is still swept clean around.

lore.name: The Cord Board
lore.description: By the stove hangs a lacquer board studded with hooks, one knotted cord per resident — wrist-length, each knot a leg of a route, the Drift way of keeping a history you can hold. Five cords are thick with knots, some worn shiny from handling. The sixth hook holds a cord pulled straight, no knots at all, its end freshly cut: someone left this house by unmaking their route, every leg of it, rather than carry where they'd been.

content.name: Row-House 14
content.description: A silk banner is still swaying from the ceiling when you duck in — six bunks, one lacquered cookstove, cyan everywhere the silk hasn't faded to white. Two people at the stove stop talking, the sentence cut clean in half. Over the door, stenciled: SIX NAMES, ONE DOOR, KNOCK LOUD. A seventh bunk space stands bare to the wall, scrubbed lighter than the rest.

npc.name: Shealyneus Veshogenes
npc.voice: Measured, unhurried, treating every question as a load to be sorted — but warmer once she decides you are not interrupting, only adding to the wash.

ask.says: Full count. Same count as when the stencil was cut, and the stencil's older than my grandmother's grandmother. Say a name into the feed and the drum knows it — that's all I know, and it's more than most.

choices.text: Ask about the fresh holes in the drum.

her.says: Twenty-six years folding, and my mother ran this line before me, and hers before the writ reorganized the crews. There is a sheet in every third load — I know its darn by heart — that comes back washed no matter how it wears, and it was darned for someone whose name I've never found on any roll. I keep folding it. I expect you'd call that faith. I call it the work.

choices.text: Say nothing. Help her fold the next one.

hall.says: The repair writ came through the council chain three seasons back, sealed and prioritized, and no crew ever arrived. So we serve out of half a cathedral and call it efficiency. Solen's office says the schedule holds. The schedule has never once held.

choices.text: Ask about the hall's true master.

drill.says: I know about those. I've chosen not to know who cut them. The wash comes out whiter for the new names — you can smell it in the rinse — and I have decided that's a blessing rather than a question.

final.says: There. Crease against the stone, never the hand — it outlasts you that way. Go on down when you're done. The steam's no climate for a visitor.

greet.says: Mind the wet floor past the third basin — the drained half's been open since spring and we've stopped pretending it'll close this year. You've come up from below, by the grit on your boots. Nobody comes up here from below for the laundry.

choices.text: Ask who all these sheets are for.
Ask about the opened-up half of the hall.
Ask how long she has worked here.

jupiter.says: This hall sits in the domain of the long table — you can feel it in the proportions, how the ceiling keeps its distance no matter how high you stack the drying racks. I walked further in once, to the bench itself. It is set for more souls than have ever lived in the Nave, and every place is laid. He doesn't trouble us, and we fold his sheets. That's the arrangement.

choices.text: Ask how long she has been here.

reactions.grief: Her hands keep folding after the news arrives, but both creases come out wrong, and she refolds them without comment.
reactions.shock: The body reads like a miscount, and she stares as if the number could be said back into order.
reactions.bribed: The offer sits between them like a stain she cannot treat, and she refuses it without raising her voice.
reactions.accused: She sets the half-folded sheet down unfinished, which from her hands is a confession of how badly the word landed.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets sorted like everything else, received in the tone kept for anyone pushing ahead in the queue.
reactions.questioned: She answers in load-counts and shift-times, reads her movements back like a manifest, and asks if that closes the tally.
reactions.threatened: Not a muscle of hers moves through the threat; when it ends she asks whether it goes in the record.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The count was wrong and she knows it; she starts the tally over from the top, slower this time.
reactions.authority_arrives: She straightens the way her mother taught her, gives the writ its full deference, and keeps folding through the introduction.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The hall moves and she stops mid-fold, looking up at steam that has never once given an answer.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Twenty years of small grievances about the one named come out of her at once, and she stops mid-sentence, appalled.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She promises what the work promises, which is nothing, and hates the honesty of it, and says it anyway, gently.

npc.description: Shealyneus Veshogenes works the folding line with the flat economy of someone who has folded these same sheets for twenty years, creasing each one against a basalt edge worn to a polish by hands that came before. She does not look up to take your measure; she finishes the fold first.

lore.name: The Census Ledger Wheel
lore.description: Set into the master boiler's feed-gear: an annealed nickel drum, ringed with punch-holes, one per name, turned by the load counter itself. Each cycle advances it one full revolution of names, so the wash is rationed to a population by the drum's own count. Someone has drilled fresh holes along the last arc — a few dozen, hand-cut, ragged — adding names to a census nobody living claims to have written.

content.name: Phiathsoklinth
content.description: The smell arrives first: lye cut with tallow and something older beneath it, the sour-sweet ghost of a thousand sleep-sweats baked into cast basalt drying-floors that have never once cooled. Steam climbs the sloped nickel in sheets you could walk on, and half the hall stands opened to its ribs, basins gutted, work rerouted through the working half where more bodies crowd than the aisles were measured for. On the drywall a stencil, re-inked in living hands: WASH LOAD SET TO OLD CENSUS. The wash-boilers run at full count anyway.

npc.name: Raqah bin Jaqaloun
npc.voice: Terse, work-first. Speaks in splice terms; treats questions as faults to be traced.

log.says: Then the splice isn't done. That's how it works — two names or it's just wire. Take the ferrule if you want; we've got a dozen more than the count says.

greet.says: Mind the flux. If you're here about the tray, it's signed off. If you're here about the other thing, so is the log.

reactions.grief: The news lands mid-splice; all four hands keep moving, and none of it is splicing.
reactions.shock: Their eyes run the wound for a pull point; only then do four hands start shaking.
reactions.bribed: A number gets quoted first, pure habit; then they remember the second name and slide it back uncounted.
reactions.accused: The ferrule stops mid-feed; they set both upper hands flat on the bench and ask which run they supposedly cut.
reactions.flattered: The compliment cools while the iron heats, and they wait it out, then ask what needs signing.
reactions.questioned: They answer in splice-log order, date, run, witness, as though the question were just another fault to trace.
reactions.threatened: Fear arrives as inventory: hands counted, exits counted, which walker owes them a favor.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They do not look up from the tray; the second lie comes slower than the first, solder-tempered and badly cooled.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets the stool, the good light, and their slowest hands; the unsigned log stays where it stays.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Even their four hands go still on the copper, and they listen for which way the shudder ran.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They recite the run that walker kept, junction and date, too fast, then hear how much they knew.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea outranks them; they say so once, flat, then busy a spare pair of hands with anything.

npc.description: Raqah bin Jaqaloun works with four hands and no hurry, feeding graphite into a brass ferrule while the argument cools behind them. The extra pair moves like it's always been there.

lore.name: The aft splice log
lore.description: The log is a brass plate hinged over the bench, its face scribed with years of signatures in graphite — two columns, one for the splice and one for the witness. The last entry is dated and unsigned in the witness column, though a signature was started and rubbed out. Beneath the plate, someone has drilled a second, smaller hinge for a plate that isn't there.

content.name: Warren 30 Aft
content.description: Rosin and scorched brass — the smell of a splice half-finished and left to think. Two walkers stand over an open cable tray, arguing in low voices, and stop when your boot hits the sticky patch of flux near the door. The loft is cheerful with rust: copper runs polished along every beam, and above the bench a stencil reads SPLICE LOG MUST BE SIGNED, unsigned.

npc.name: Veth-Brioraris
npc.voice: Flat, inventory-cadenced; measures things instead of describing them. Warmth arrives only as an admission of pride.

open.says: This vault. The one I'm emptying. The stencil on the inner frame says the seal predates current inventory, and current inventory goes back past the Nave's charter by a margin nobody at the terminals will publish. I ran my palm along the old weld-bead and the bead was laid by a hand larger than any hand I've met, in a rhythm I've seen since on Mars's own plating up the spar. What I packed today is nothing. What I unpacked this morning was already ancient when the city above it was agreed upon.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry what you told me.
A hand larger than any hand. Goodbye.

greet.says: Mind the basalt sill — it's cast, not cut, and it's older than your boots. Say what you're storing or move through.

choices.text: Whose work is this vault, really?
Is it true the vaults are failing?
What's the oldest thing you've ever sealed in?
I'll come back when you're finished.

probe_a.says: It breathes slower than the metal does. A crate sealed in graphite holds its contents at the pace of the steel around it, and the steel here is old enough to be patient. Everything I pack is meant to outlast me twice.

probe_b.says: Mine, and I answer to the route-walkers, and above that nobody signs anything. That's the trouble with the deep postings — Mars's stamps come without a name, like the work does itself. Down here you learn to respect a seal you can't trace.

probe_c.says: Borrowed time, all sixteen of them, and I'll not pretend otherwise. The girders hold; the seams sweat. I pack faster than I used to, which is its own kind of report.

reactions.grief: They ask when, then how, then nothing at all; the half-sealed crate stays half-sealed for a long minute.
reactions.shock: Their walls' hush fails them; the blood in their ears is suddenly loud, and their hands forget the seam.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer against the crates' contents and find it the lighter weight, and refuse at that exchange rate.
reactions.accused: They set down the sealer mid-crate and ask for the ledger that named them, the flat cadence losing its floor.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands twice, like a rivet-tap in this vault, and they take a half-beat too long to refuse.
reactions.questioned: They answer in manifest cadence, item and count, and the question gets no more weight than a tally.
reactions.threatened: They give the threat the silence a load-bearing beam gets, and start memorizing the speaker's insignia for the record.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The recount takes too long and they hear it happening, a number offered twice where once had been clean.
reactions.authority_arrives: They step between the official and the failing jamb first, manifest in hand, and only then acknowledge jurisdiction.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They take inventory aloud, twice, because a second count that matches is the nearest thing they have to prayer.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They defend the accused in counts and hours and weld-rhythms, warmth entering the record sideways and against their habit.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They refuse without softening it, then stand a moment longer than refusal requires, hands already looking for something to seal.

npc.description: The vault takes the sound of the spar and holds it a half-beat, so every rivet-tap of packing arrives twice, the second one smaller, like an echo that has thought better of itself. Veth-Brioraris is sealing the last graphite crate, thumb pressed to the seam, working the way a person works when the work is nearly done and the door is behind them.

lore.name: The Tally-Spar of Cache-Vault 16
lore.description: Set into the vault's threshold is a bar of cast basalt a forearm long, worn concave where a century of thumbs has pressed it, and notched along its length in the oldest layer of hull notation — the same strokes Sevin catalogs, cut here before the vault was stocked. Beside each notch, in copper inlay that could not be older than the Nave, someone has struck a tally: a running count of the cache's openings, the newest mark still bright against the black. The two records do not agree. The old notches outnumber the tallies by more than the vault has been opened in living memory, and no one has chiseled away the surplus.

content.name: Cache-Vault 16
content.description: Before anything shows itself, the room swallows your footfall — the packed graphite lining the walls takes the ring out of metal the way cloth takes the ring out of a bell, and what returns is a hush so total you hear your own blood in it. Then the spar's interior opens along a girdered throat of cast basalt, green-black in the work-lamp's cone, riveted in courses that run far back past where the light gives up. The vault's own seal is failing at the jamb, a hairline of daylight-thin glow where four generations of graphite have shifted, and the stencil over it still holds its full complement of paint: SEAL PREDATES CURRENT INVENTORY, DO NOT BREAK.

npc.name: Vjareth-Soleisen
npc.voice: Dry, inventory-minded, prone to answering questions with counts. Speaks of the patch the way a parent speaks of a child who has outlived them.

mars.says: Seen? Once, far down the weld-line — a darkness that was not darkness, working. It passed over a breach I had just dressed and I felt the weld set harder under my gauntlet, like a hand pressing mine flat. It has never spoken to me. It amended my work. That was enough, and it was forty years ago and I have not stopped thinking about it.

choices.text: Ask about the second congregation instead.
Let them keep the rest of their hour.

tear.says: Eleven metres of split plate, and I have dressed it forty years, and it holds because it is held. The seam has three signatures. I copied the oldest one when I took the work — not the name, the stroke. The stroke is what carries the load. Mars does not care whose hand; Mars cares that it holds.

choices.text: Ask if they have seen Mars itself.
Return to the matter of the room.

greet.says: Nobody comes down the mica stair. That is why I chose the hour. You are standing on my patch, by the way — both of us are — so mind your weight and your opinions equally.

choices.text: Ask who else uses this cathedral.

reports.says: Solen reads what comes up and decides the rest is a reasonable thing not to know. I have done the same with this tear forty times — dressed the outer bandage, declined to lift it. We are more alike than either ward would admit, she and I. The difference is that my not-knowing holds eleven metres of plate and hers holds people. Stay out of the lower tunnels, newcomer. My reasons are better written down than hers.

choices.text: Leave them with the hour they stole.

stencil.says: Blessed and logged, in that order. It is a rebuke. The Continuants want the log first — the record, the countersign, the paper — and we hold that a patch unprayed is a patch unkeyed. My predecessor wrote the stencil. I have renewed it every year, and every year someone from the wards paints a ledger-column under it, and every year I burnish it off. That is my liturgy now, I suppose.

choices.text: Ask who keeps painting over it.

contested.says: The Continuants audit this tear every quarter. It sits on their load charts, so they claim its paperwork, and they file their reports, and the reports stopped being detailed three months ago — you did not hear the doubt in my voice, because there was none, because I choose to have none. They come, I let them log, then I pray after they leave. Neither of us concedes. The patch does not mind. It holds for both of us, which is more than I manage.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as inventory — trade, age, last good weld — until the voice gives at the year.
reactions.shock: Their eyes go to the wound's edge and read the stroke there; the burnisher hangs unfinished, forgotten.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer aloud, correctly, then says Mars pays in holds, not coin, and turns back to the mica.
reactions.accused: The count collapses mid-number; one gauntleted fist closes, and they ask what exactly they are meant to have broken.
reactions.flattered: Takes the praise like plated nickel — they'd bite it, given leave — and answers with the patch's defect list.
reactions.questioned: Answers in counts — hours, strokes, buttons fastened — and asks whether the ledger wants the count or the truth.
reactions.threatened: Weighs the threat like stock, answers with a count of threats the patch has outlived, and stays on the seam.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recounts aloud, slower, and when the number comes out the same, sets the burnisher down like a confession.
reactions.authority_arrives: Finishes the stroke before looking up, because Mars ranks the seam above the badge, then offers the log for countersignature.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The count stops dead; they press a palm to the strap-work and wait, lips moving, for the patch to answer.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Snaps that the named one's welds are ugly but true, and offers to prove it seam by seam.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Lists what they can mend, item by item; the plea fits none of it, and they say so, and stay.

npc.description: Vjareth-Soleisen stands with a burnisher still raised, mid-stroke on the mica's edge, and does not finish the stroke — which, for someone of this trade, is the closest thing to alarm. Their apron carries more spare-pockets than a body has uses for, each one buttoned, and their gauntlets are worn through at the knuckles in the exact pattern mica wear produces.

lore.name: The Load-Bearing Patch
lore.description: The bandaged tear is not decoration; pull back the outer dressing and you find the patch itself is structural — nickel poured in situ, keyed into the strap-work below, so that the column, the floor and the patch are one continuous load path. Whoever patched it signed the pour in mirror-script along the seam, and beneath their signature, in older notation worn nearly flat, someone signed the same patch twice before. The tear has been mended, blessed and re-mended across three handwritings no one living matches, and the newest hands copied the oldest strokes exactly.

content.name: Zjabrand's Patch Cathedral
content.description: A sheet of mica the size of a barn door swings down on annealed nickel hinges as you enter, its chalk-white face catching what little light the slit-windows admit and giving back twice as much. Beneath it the floor is ribbed with nickel strap-work, every strap stamped and countersigned, holding up a column of layered mica that goes on past the second reading. A tear in the hull plating above has been dressed like a wound, bandage over bandage, and the air is warm where it leaks. Stencilled along the lowest strap: PATCH BLESSED AND LOGGED, IN THAT ORDER. Nothing you say carries; the room eats it.

npc.name: Yilitl-Tizha
npc.voice: Quick, dealer's cadence, prices and names in the same breath; warms when the talk turns to routes and goes flat when it turns to staying.

pan.says: Salt tray under it. You saw. Every weigher on this floor has a trick; mine happens to cost me money. Don't make it a story — it's just a habit I picked up from the woman who taught me, and she never said whose favor she was shorting.

stay.says: Because a stall is a route with the walking taken out, and I got old for walking. Olo Vashti stays too, and nobody asks them twice. Look — Drift says nothing is yours. Fine. This scale isn't mine either. I'm just the current hand on it.

braid.says: Says the terminal postings have gone strange — motifs nobody can index, tellers repeating themselves. Says it like gossip, which is how you know it's serious. The Factor's office says nothing, which is worse.

choices.text: Do you have a favorite teller?

greet.says: You're not buying saffron, nobody who stands that still is. Ask, then. The scale's honest even when I'm not.

choices.text: Why is the second pan drilled through?
You're Drift. Why has this stall been here so long?
What's the Braid saying this week?

vashti.says: Everyone on this floor knows Olo. Buys saffron here when they want to be seen buying saffron. Whatever they're actually trading, it doesn't come across my scale — and I'd know. My scale knows things I don't tell it to.

teacher.says: Called herself Meren. Weighed here before me, before the stall was even this stall — moved it three times down the row as rents shifted. Last thing she told me: keep the pan tilted to the buyer and the row will keep you. She left before the next calibration. Didn't say where. Drift doesn't owe you a destination.

choices.text: Then I'll let you weigh in peace.

tellers.says: Mercury, always. Clean structures, no tricks. But the last posting — I've weighed goods twenty years, I know when something's been measured wrong on purpose. That one was measured wrong on purpose. Whoever wrote it wanted us counting what doesn't add up.

reactions.grief: Weighs the same pinch three times, getting different numbers, and asks which route the death happened on, not how.
reactions.shock: Mid-deal they stop entirely, saffron loose in an open palm, staring past the body at the salt tray.
reactions.bribed: Asks the offer's worth in saffron first, and that is the refusal: nothing on this counter was ever theirs.
