reactions.accused: Sets the weights down harder than weighing needs and repeats the accusation once, exactly, like checking a measure.
reactions.flattered: Hears the praise, prices it like everything else, and lets the silence name what they actually want.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day's movements like a price list, thumb already moving to the next pan before the question ends.
reactions.threatened: Goes to the flat voice they save for talk of staying, hands still, agreeing faster than belief would allow.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Keeps talking past the point the lie dies, stacking explanations like small weights, watching the evidence instead of the accuser.
reactions.authority_arrives: Looks up mid-transaction for the first time all day, which on this floor counts as a raised alarm.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Watches the pans swing without a hand on them and, for once, says nothing to the scale at all.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says Olo Vashti's name once, then argues pan calibration with sudden volume, loyalty arriving sideways.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits the limit plainly, then starts naming who owes them favors down the line, cord already off the wrist.

npc.description: Yilitl-Tizha weighs saffron threads against cut-coin, one wrist knotted with a cord dense with route-work, and never looks up until the deal is done. Their apron is coral gone rust at the hem. They talk while they work, to the scale as much as to you.

lore.name: The Second Pan
lore.description: The great scale hangs from a chain, but its second pan is a replacement — a different weave of cane, lighter, and drilled through with small holes. Weighed goods sit in it over a shallow tray of salt, and the tray is nearly full. A weigher who salts the pan first can shave a little off every measure in the buyer's favor, or the seller's, depending which way the tray is tilted. It is tilted toward the buyer. Someone has been quietly shorting their own side for months.

content.name: Weigher-Stall 13
content.description: The sun-strip light arrives in slices, broken by the hanging scale's chain so that the coral-dyed cane baskets flash on and off as the pans sway. Every shelf is borrowed — a plank across crates, a door as a counter — and scrubbed down to bare grain. Under the counter lip, stenciled: SCALE CALIBRATED WEEKLY, DISPUTES TO THE FACTOR. The paint is older than the plank it sits on.

npc.name: Rudumake Kohiwesaki
npc.voice: Terse. Answers in the fewest words that still count as service.

greet.says: Kettle's cold until the pressure line's bled. Sit or come back at second bell.

kettle.says: New build, new pipes. Everything has to be done right once so it holds. That's the whole job.

reactions.grief: The stack gets finished first because half a job is half a job, and the count comes out wrong.
reactions.shock: A cup hits the boards, their first in years, and they stare at it, waiting for the flaw to show.
reactions.bribed: They repeat the offered sum exactly, the way a wrong order gets repeated, and wait for it to be corrected.
reactions.accused: Rudumake stops mid-wipe and decides, out where the accuser can watch, whether this counts as a customer.
reactions.flattered: They hear the praise as pressure and go check a valve that checked clean an hour ago.
reactions.questioned: They answer in bells and pour counts, the ledger they keep for every inspector, suspicion or none.
reactions.threatened: Under the slate apron their hands go cold, the exact temperature of the line they promised to bleed.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The story about the bled line comes out a second time, softer, and then stops being maintained.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets greeted by title and offered the best stool, while Rudumake's eyes go once to the cold kettle.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Rudumake catches two cups without deciding to, then kneels at the firebox with a thumb against the ground-glass seams.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defense arrives in sentences longer than any order ever taken: three winters of sound joints, itemized.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They explain why the answer is no, in more words than the stoop has heard from them all year.

npc.description: Rudumake Kohiwesaki stands behind the counter in a slate apron, testing the kettle valve with one hand and stacking cups with the other. Neither task finishes.

lore.name: The glass-sealed firebox
lore.description: Ground glass pressed into every joint of the firebox, still sharp-edged. The old box leaked steam for years; this one has never held a flame.

content.name: Roga's Kettle Stoop
content.description: The kettle on the corner stoop should be steaming. It is not. Everything else is: scrubbed hardwood, a dust-white counter, ground glass packed into the seams of the firebox. Stencilled on the stoop rail: KETTLE ON FROM FIRST BELL. Rudumake Kohiwesaki wipes the same clean cup and does not look up.

npc.name: Jafaqana Jawi
npc.voice: Dry. Counts things. Talks about worn goods the way other people talk about people they owe.

work.says: Nothing gets thrown out. Horn, thread, wax — we hoard spares because the day we don't is the day something stays broken. Unclaimed books wait on that shelf until someone comes. Some have waited my whole life.

choices.text: Ask about the shift board instead.

board.says: Half the bindery walked to other work. Spines crack whether or not anyone stays, so I stay. It's not devotion. It's arithmetic.

choices.text: Ask if they believe the work matters.

greet.says: Mind the glue pot. This shift isn't mine, but the books don't know that. What do you want mended?

choices.text: Ask what happens to the books nobody claims.

believe.says: A mended spine outlives the mender. That's the whole creed, if you want it small. Hold a crack closed long enough and it forgets it was ever open.

choices.text: Let them get back to it.

reactions.grief: Goes silent mid-stitch, then starts counting the dead person's outstanding repairs instead of answering, voice flat until it isn't.
reactions.shock: Every arm stops at once, and they stand holding the wax horn, staring past the body, past the room.
reactions.bribed: Refuses by quoting what the offer would cost later, already writing the number somewhere the visitor can see.
reactions.accused: Sets the horn knife down flat before speaking, insulted less by the charge than by its sloppy wording.
reactions.flattered: Ignores the praise until it names a favor, then nods, having heard the real sentence underneath.
reactions.questioned: Answers in ledger order, hour by hour, an extra arm folding away with each item accounted for.
reactions.threatened: Quotes the threat back as a repair cost, then keeps working, which is not the same as being calm.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recounts the night twice and gets two different totals, and the second number scares them visibly.
reactions.authority_arrives: Looks the official over the way they look at a worn spine, judging where it will split first.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches the glue pot before it slides, then keeps holding it, the only steady thing in a room gone wrong.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says the named person's stitching is too careful for the damage, which is as close to loyal as they get.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains twice that some things are past mending, and their voice keeps restarting on the word mending.

npc.description: Jafaqana Jawi works at the third bench with sleeves rolled past the elbow, paring a spine with a horn knife. More arms than a person should have. They do not explain it and do not look up until the second bench creaks under you.

lore.name: The Shift Board
lore.description: A board by the door lists workers in chalk, one name per shift, weeks deep. Every column past the last month is blank except one — Jafaqana Jawi, covering shift after shift that belongs to others. The last ordinary name on the board was scrubbed out, not erased cleanly. Someone left in a hurry and someone else kept the room alive anyway.

content.name: Yard 10 Outboard
content.description: Sound flattens in here. The ceiling sits low enough to touch, benches stand bare, and a cold glue pot waits beside a stencil: NO OPEN FLAME NEAR THE GLUE POT. Nobody cleared up when the work stopped. Spines, thread, a horn of wax — all of it mid-repair, all of it waiting.

npc.name: Yichi-Hiyitzitl
npc.voice: Counts before talking. Sells nothing they can't verify. Talks around what they owe people.

why.says: I sold here eleven years. I know every brand on this floor by the scar it leaves, not the paper. When Rasa comes back I'll hand her a ledger that's clean, and then maybe I go find what a floor without me looks like. I've been afraid to look for a while now.

choices.text: Before that — what's moving through the pens?
I hope the floor without you is kind.

desk.says: Cabinet came off a stall frame on the Third gallery when that whole row moved out. We never closed the back half. Drift logic — nothing stays finished, so why pretend. It holds books on one side and air on the other, and both work.

greet.says: Hold on. Six head, brand-checked, sold. Fine. Now — you buying, selling, or just warm?

choices.text: This isn't your shift, is it.
What's moving through the pens lately?

shift.says: Rasa's shift. Her mother's worse and she went to sit with her. I said I'd cover two watches and it's been eleven days. The animals don't care who counts them. I care more than I should.

choices.text: Eleven days is a long favor.

trade.says: Slow. Two shipments held at the junction for a brand dispute nobody will settle. The Braid says grain prices up the axial way, but I sell animals, not talk. If you hear what's holding the junction, come tell me. I'd owe you one count of honest business.

mother.says: She walked pens her whole life. Now her hands won't hold a brand-iron and she knows it. Rasa sits with her so she isn't alone when she stops being a broker. Somebody should be there for that. It isn't the counting that keeps me here, if that's what you're asking.

choices.text: That's fair. Back to the desk.

reactions.grief: They finish the tally line in hand before looking up, then ask for the name again.
reactions.shock: They walk to the pen gate, stand facing it, and see none of it.
reactions.bribed: A number higher than the offer is their whole answer, priced like stock they cannot verify.
reactions.accused: They try to start the count, lose the number twice, and answer with eleven years of clean tallies.
reactions.flattered: They credit the ledger, not themselves, and start calculating what the praise will cost.
reactions.questioned: Their eyes go to the pen gate mid-answer, a habit they offer no excuse for.
reactions.threatened: The cold at the ankles climbs while they keep writing, and the tallies stop meaning anything.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Paper does the answering now: they read the entry aloud that they claimed to know by scar.
reactions.authority_arrives: They offer the felt book open to today's page before anyone asks, stylus still behind the ear.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: No count comes; they log the hour once the pens settle and nothing about the cause.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They name every debt that person ever paid, too loudly, and stop mid-list when the room looks over.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They list their own debts before saying the plain no, because owing is the only answer they have.

npc.description: Yichi-Hiyitzitl stands at the working half of the desk, thumbing tallies into a felt-bound book, a cane stylus behind one ear. They cover a shift that is not theirs and check the pen gate every few minutes out of habit rather than duty.

lore.name: Half a ledger cabinet
lore.description: The opened half shows cane backing where drawers were never meant to be — the desk was rebuilt once from a stall frame and never finished.

content.name: The Ledger Desk of Third Watch
content.description: The cold sits low, at the ankles, where the pen floor drains. Warmth gathers at the desk's open side, where half the cabinet is gutted for repair and its missing drawers leave a gap you could put an arm through. Smoke pools under the slope of the roof. A teal felt banner reads NO SALE WITHOUT THE BRAND CHECK.

npc.name: Lisoud Vacuumrunner
npc.voice: Clipped, counted in cart-lengths. She talks the way freight moves.

chalk.says: The one that keeps the line running. Now duck — axle.

greet.says: Hold the rail or step off. You want the junction schedules, the Braid posted them an hour ago. Terminal by the market, teal post, third knot down.

choices.text: Whose chalk is the third column?

reactions.grief: The count in her head loses its place; she asks which junction, then which body, then which junction again.
reactions.shock: She watches the next three carts through without greasing a single axle, hands working the rag on nothing.
reactions.bribed: She quotes them a price high enough to end the conversation, eyes already back on the channel.
reactions.accused: The nozzle keeps spraying past her boot while she asks them to say the charge again, slower.
reactions.flattered: She lets the praise run to its end, the way she lets carts pass, and asks what it costs.
reactions.questioned: Her account comes in cart-lengths: the hour, the station, the number of carts, nothing a posted schedule lacks.
reactions.threatened: She names the threat back in fewer words than they used and shifts her grip on the rail.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She offers a second version of the story, then a third, each one shorter than the last.
reactions.authority_arrives: She points them to the stenciled board and the teal post, the same answer she gives everyone with questions.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder costs her a cart; she watches it run the slope ungreased, still holding the rail.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She repeats the name once, flat, then starts listing carts that cleared the junction faster than that person moves.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She gives them the junction and the knot number, then turns back to a cart she cannot finish anyway.

npc.description: Lisoud Vacuumrunner works the channel with a silk rag in one hand and a pressure nozzle in the other, feet braced against the slope's drop. Carts pass through her station faster than she can finish them, and she lets them.

lore.name: The Double Ledger Board
lore.description: A slate beside the tool wall carries two grease schedules in chalk, one in blue, one in teal, neither crossed out. They name the same twelve carts at different hours. Someone has drawn a third column between them and filled it with times that match neither, and that column is the one with the freshest chalk.

content.name: Tlanteyetl's Greasing Bay
content.description: Sound comes in from four corridors and the bay swallows half of it. Wagon axles clatter over a greased channel that runs down a slope too steep to stand on without holding something. Tools hang in marked rows over benches of teal-painted plastic, and every surface carries a second person's work beside the first. A stenciled board reads GREASE YOUR OWN AXLE, TOOLS PROVIDED; two hands have painted over the last word twice.

npc.name: Straisa Panogenes
npc.voice: Precise, procedural, allergic to rounding. Thaws when spoken to in the language of the ledger.

fan.says: Counts the room's own dues first, before anyone else's. We don't assess what we haven't paid. Third Factor's rule, and older than her.

slug.says: Precedent. When a ruling is made twice the same way, it stops being a ruling and becomes weight. That slug is the oldest one we kept through the rebuild. The rest you'd have to ask the sitting for.

choices.text: Rebuild? This room was torn down?

greet.says: Dues are by the new moon. If you're here about the range reassessment, that's sealed until the sitting. Which is it?

choices.text: What gets weighed in that drawer?

rebuild.says: Range 21 stood on the old footings since before the rolls begin. We raised it again on the same lines, same desks, same drawer. What continues, continues correctly. Don't read more into it than that.

reactions.grief: Her questions come in proper entry form, hour and cause, but she cannot find where the account closes.
reactions.shock: Counts the room under her breath, loses the count, and keeps clicking the stylus against nothing.
reactions.bribed: She asks the amount twice, not because she misheard but to give them time to be ashamed.
reactions.accused: The accusation itself doesn't frighten her; the possibility that the figures support it does.
reactions.flattered: The flattery lands only in ledger terms, and she warms to it anyway, hating the warmth.
reactions.questioned: Each answer comes numbered against the question, entered as she would enter it in the roll.
reactions.threatened: She names the rule that protects her twice, and the second time quieter.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: When she checks the roll to disprove the charge, the error sits where she left it, and two more besides.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction she honors instantly, standing, keys out, but the sealed drawer stays sealed until the sitting.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The roll goes under her hand before anything else; afterward she stands listening for a number the room won't give.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Three rulings deep, she cites precedent against the naming, and the relief in her voice is unmistakable.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: There is a rule and she gives it twice, unsoftened, then waives the late fee out of her own column.

npc.description: Straisa Panogenes stands at the far desk, entering figures into a bound roll with a stylus that clicks at the end of each line. She does not look up until the third click.

lore.name: The Precedent Drawer
lore.description: Under the middle desk, a shallow drawer lined in felt, empty except for one brass slug stamped with a date no ledger in the room matches. The slot above it is worn smooth; the rest of the drawer is factory-crisp. Whatever gets weighed here has been weighed before, and the answer is kept where only the sitter can reach it.

content.name: Range 21 Spinward
content.description: A tally-fan clatters through its arc as you enter, brass leaves flipping to zero and settling. Range 21 Spinward is new brick under indigo glaze, grout still pale, a stencil on the lintel reading DUES DUE BY THE NEW MOON. The room holds three desks, one worker, and no chair for you.

npc.name: Chutalgul-Raris
npc.voice: Sparse and transactional at first, each answer priced; warms into the restless patter of someone used to trading small talk for small truths.

open.says: You think the market is goods? I thought that too, four years in the corridors. Down here the Drift runs deeper than spools and route-history — Mercury's arteries carry estimations, regard, the weight of who trusts whom, metered and routed like freight. I watched a transfer go through this tank that had no object in it at all: a standing, a reputation, passed hand to hand at the speed of signal. Somebody up the line defaulted on one, and the water stopped moving to think about it.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
A market in people's standing. I need air.

greet.says: Cord's down. If you've come to move something, it isn't moving today.

choices.text: Why hasn't anyone cleared this out?
Who do you answer to, down here?
What are they trading down here, if nothing moves?
Never mind. Sorry to break the quiet.

probe_a.says: Wound foil, three hundred layers a band — Mercury's own spool-stock, or near enough. I was sealing sensor leads down the tank wall so the signal wouldn't bleed into the water. Now the signal sits in the water like a coin in a well, and the foil sits with it.

probe_b.says: Cleared for what? The order came to stop, not to finish. Down here a stopped job is a message — you leave the tools where they lie so the next pair of hands knows exactly where the hand before it lifted off. Somebody wanted that message legible.

probe_c.says: My knot says the grain route, the archive relays, four years in the corridors — you can read it if you know cord. I answer to whoever holds the next knot in the run, and lately the next knot keeps being held by nobody I've met. That's not how the Braid works. That's how something older than the Braid works.

reactions.grief: She keeps feeding foil through the dead jig, three hundred layers into a band no one will ever order.
reactions.shock: The scene files itself under the thing she has feared since the water stopped, and her hands stop with it.
reactions.bribed: She quotes the offer back at double before refusing, since anything worth bribing is worth pricing honestly.
reactions.accused: She offers the accusation back for weighing, twice, though her thumb has gone white on the jig's handle.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes her patter run warm before she catches herself metering what the flatterer must want in return.
reactions.questioned: She answers by weight, paying out exactly what the question cost and not one measure more.
reactions.threatened: She prices the threat out loud, decides it is overquoted, and tells the room so in a level voice.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she does not apologize; she reprices the lie downward and waits to see if it clears.
reactions.authority_arrives: The moment jurisdiction crosses her threshold she turns the lamp low, and every answer after is metered to the drop.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She watches the tank, not the walls; a shudder the water won't ripple frightens her worse than motion.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She knows exactly what that name is worth and says so at length, warmer than she has been all shift.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea outruns her jurisdiction and she says the cord is down twice, the second time softer, already apologizing.

npc.description: Chutalgul-Raris crouches at the sloped lip of the standing water, feeding wound foil into a splicing jig that has clearly not turned in a long while, and turns their head the way you'd turn toward a draft. The tank's surface holds still as poured glass — no ripple, no skim-drift, though the room breathes.

lore.name: The Racked Glass Ledger
lore.description: Each sheet of black glass carries lines of knots and notches pressed into it while hot — routes, prices, agreements — and the rack holds three hundred of them, the oldest gone cloudy from years underwater. This is the Braid's exchange floor: not a market of goods but of passages, favors and word-of-route, every transaction cut into glass and sunk past the water line where only the occupied level's tenants can retrieve them. The newest sheet is still warm.

content.name: Bughsun's Tank Housing
content.description: The stillness comes first: a rope of wound foil stretches from the sloped wall into the black water and hangs there without a tremor, though the artery beyond the housing hums hard enough to blur the stencil on the plating — WATER LINE MARKS THE OCCUPIED LEVEL. Sheet of black glass lie racked against the curve, each etched with routed marks, none packed. Four hundred strides of shoreline and not one footprint but yours. Then a scrape behind the intake baffles, and Chutalgul-Raris stands up with a light still burning in her hand.

npc.name: Mor Six-Hulls
npc.voice: Terse, metronomic, talking the way a runner talks between strides — nouns and directions, no ceremony.

greet.says: Twelve decks empty and you pick mine to breathe loud in. You want the count: last post moved through forty minutes ago, splice schedule holds till next dim. That's everything I have that's free.

choices.text: How long have you slept down here?

reactions.grief: Nothing in them keeps time; the arm that sways with the artery hangs still over the berth's empty half.
reactions.shock: They start counting pulses that aren't there, reach four, and step back on a decision the body made without them.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced like any cargo, comes back honest, and that honesty is exactly why they refuse it.
reactions.accused: Mor loses the beat mid-number for the first time in years and won't speak until three artery-pulses pass uncounted.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads like a mislabeled weight; nothing comes back heavier than the work, so none of it lands.
reactions.questioned: Their answer is a timetable: post moved at the last dim, splice holds till the next, nothing free beyond that.
reactions.threatened: Voice level, count steady, but both hands have gone to the rib's stencil and read it like scripture.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The recount happens out loud, arrives at their own wrong number, and gets handed over like a bad weight.
reactions.authority_arrives: Meets the official at the threshold with the spar tally already recited, as if numbers were the toll.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Mor logs the shudder three pulses off rhythm and keeps saying the number, because counted things can't be the end.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Three posts that person couldn't have made come out fast, and they don't hear their own speed rising.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Gives the only thing they own, a bearing and a count of safe dims, and it doesn't answer the plea.

npc.description: Mor Six-Hulls sleeps folded into a berth built for two, one arm hanging out and swaying slightly with the artery's rhythm, as if even unconscious they are keeping time with the passage below.

lore.name: Spar ladder, rung four
lore.description: The ladder between the third and fourth tiers has been rung-welded and un-welded so many times that its fourth rung is a palimpsest of beads — a decade of arrivals, each household re-climbing it to suit someone shorter, older, gone.

content.name: Saikjam
content.description: The cold lives at the floor and the heat has climbed to the eleventh spar, leaving the middle berths wearing a temperature nobody chose. Twelve decks of stacked sleeping cells rise against a far wall that leans inward as it climbs, each tier propped by columnar ribs, and the whole of it sits raw and unfinished — the work of settling it stopped mid-stride, hammocks still slung, bowls still crusted, everything left as if the leaving were temporary. Stencilled along the rib at eye height: BERTH ASSIGNMENTS POSTED BY SPAR NUMBER. The only sound is the artery's hum through the far wall, and one person's slow breathing.

npc.name: Yihel-Hiziki
npc.voice: Counts everything. Speaks in seat numbers, show numbers, minutes to curtain. Thaws into shop talk if you ask about the puppets themselves.

turf.says: Mine. Cut it myself, laid it over the old boards. People stand quieter on grass. They take their boots off, some of them. You don't get that on timber, and timber's all this district grows otherwise.

crowd.says: Everywhere there's regard to be had. Games, terminals, the squares. A body's got an hour of attention and spends it where it's counted loudest. I count heads out loud, every night. It's the only ledger I keep and I keep it well.

greet.says: Forty-one seats, forty-one backsides. You're the odd one out, so it's standing for you. First show starts in six minutes. Pick a wall.

choices.text: Why three shows? Why not two, or four?
The puppet with the torn sleeve — is it broken?

shows.says: Three because three fits between the market bell and the last tram. Four used to fit. Then the crowd got thinner and the smoke got thicker, and I filed the fourth notch off the crank myself. A show you play to nobody is just rehearsal.

puppets.says: Torn? That's the Traveler. The sleeve went three years back and I never sewed it. The audience decided it means something, so now it does. Half my job is the puppets. The other half is not fixing what people have started to love.

choices.text: This turf underfoot — whose idea was that?

reactions.grief: Asks what seat the dead one held, then stands at the top of the benches with nothing left to count.
reactions.shock: The cupped flame goes out in their hand and they do not remember it going out.
reactions.bribed: Puts a price on the offer against forty-one nightly heads and says the sum where the benches can hear.
reactions.accused: The spool keeps turning past its last wire, and the seat count comes out wrong twice before it rights itself.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands warm and they hate that it lands, counting the flatterer's pauses like latecomers.
reactions.questioned: Recites the night's ledger unprompted — forty-one in, forty-one out, no gaps — and waits for the next question.
reactions.threatened: Names the minutes to curtain as though the schedule could shield them, and their thumb whitens on the spool.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recalculates out loud to buy time, arrives at the accuser's own figure, and stops with no story behind it.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the door, tallying exits the official does not know are there.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Counts the shudder aloud — one — and the second number takes too long coming because their room has never moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their objection is all craft — what that person's hands can and cannot do — and it runs long past useful.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits the plea outranks them, then offers what a counter can: which show ran, who stood, when.

npc.description: Yihel-Hiziki works two stages at once, walking the catwalk behind the booth with a wire spool in one hand and a cupped flame in the other, melting resin onto a joint. Between shows they stand at the top of the benches counting heads before the doors open.

lore.name: The Rewind Crank
lore.description: Bolted to the side of the stage is a hand crank marked with three notches, one per show. The wood around the middle notch is worn pale — that show runs the fullest and the mechanism gets reset most. A fourth notch has been filed flat. Yihel-Hiziki says they cut a show when the hall stopped selling out, not when the puppets wore out.

content.name: Seinsun's Puppet Booth
content.description: A puppet with a torn sleeve crosses the stage on wires and is yanked back mid-stride. The booth is steep — benches cut from planed timber rise in tight rows, and turf squares carpet the aisles. Smoke from a heater curls past a stenciled board: THREE SHOWS NIGHTLY, LATECOMERS STAND. Every seat is taken.

npc.name: Bim-al-Zosar
npc.voice: Terse, transactional. Trades answers for gossip and says so plainly.

greet.says: You're not on the list. One riddle per visit, answer or leave. Riddle, or do you have gossip worth more?

choices.text: Here's gossip: the terminals posted twice this week.
I'll come back when it's quieter.

gossip.says: Twice. I heard. Take this instead of a riddle: the salons in the north square have started paying better. That should interest somebody.

reactions.grief: The queue goes through uncharged that day, and no one has ever seen them do that before.
reactions.shock: Their mouth keeps quoting the entry price while their eyes stay fixed on the body across the room.
reactions.bribed: A figure gets named before the offer even finishes, then doubled, since witnesses cost more than answers.
reactions.accused: Their cloth stops mid-wipe and they tell the accuser to take a number like everyone else, voice gone thin.
reactions.flattered: A compliment is a mark-up; they answer the praise with their actual rates and a shorter wait.
reactions.questioned: Routine questions get list-rate answers and a note of who asked, entered in the ledger before they leave.
reactions.threatened: They keep their eyes on the queue slates and recite the one-riddle rule as if the rule could protect them.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they skip apology and ask what the correction costs, whether it can be paid in gossip.
reactions.authority_arrives: They check the door first, then the queue, then turn the gossip ledger face down without hurrying.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Both hands pin the sliding slates flat; the queue resumes as though the shudder were bad weather.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They know too much about where the accused was that night, and hear it only after saying it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Nothing on any slate covers this, and they admit it without naming a price, which costs them.

npc.description: Bim-al-Zosar stands behind the answer desk with three riddle slates stacked and no time for any of them, holding a cloth and a queue.

lore.name: The Answer Bowl
lore.description: An iron-banded stone bowl by the door holds coins paid for failed guesses. A notch worn into its rim marks where one winner, years back, tried to take her winnings out again.

content.name: Baqabir's Riddle Salon
content.description: The noise arrives first: guesses, groans, coins on stone. The room swallows none of it. Low ceilings of worked stone hold every voice close. Benches made for forty hold sixty. A stenciled line over the door reads ONE RIDDLE PER VISIT, ANSWER OR LEAVE.

npc.name: Zaemeltaeca Recibicawa
npc.voice: Precise, unhurried, speaking in the cadence of dictation — as if conversation were a record being kept and her sentences were already filed. Uses words correctly in combinations that will not quite resolve.

count.says: It is not counting forward, if that is your next question. It is counting down to a word it already knows. I was sent to catch the word. Instead it learned my name, and I left it that — a fair trade, and cheaper than the reverse.

choices.text: Whose name did it learn — yours, or mine?

greet.says: You arrived during an early seventh. Noted. I am finishing — the work was concluded some years ago and I am only now catching up to it.

choices.text: Concluded? The transcription plate is barely half done.

plate.says: The plate records my failure to finish, which is itself the finding. Luna keeps the logs; the log kept me. One does not transcribe what one has become part of hearing.

choices.text: You heard yourself into the archive?

reactions.grief: Mid-wind, her hands stop; she grieves the way the bore holds a vowel, long, without releasing anything.
reactions.shock: The scene overwrites her, and for one full early seventh she cannot render it into any register at all.
reactions.bribed: In pure filing language she declines, since she already forgets professionally and cannot be paid to mishear.
reactions.accused: She corrects the accusation's tense before its content, as if error in time were the greater insult.
reactions.flattered: Praise rings a false interval to her ear, met with silence and the slow unwinding of glassy filament.
reactions.questioned: Questions get answered in her dictation cadence, each reply dated, filed under sounds she claims to have heard already.
reactions.threatened: She names the threat aloud as though entering it into the log, which steadies her not at all.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her dictation cadence collapses mid-clause, and she amends the record aloud twice without either version holding.
reactions.authority_arrives: The plate recording her failure comes out unprompted; jurisdiction enters her ledger the moment boots cross the threshold.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder she logs against the hum's held vowel, alarmed only that the sound did not change first.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Whoever stands accused, she testifies first to what the bore itself heard, creed outrunning whatever she privately believes.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: That the plea exceeds her she admits at once; the work concluded years ago, and she is only catching up.

npc.description: Zaemeltaeca Recibicawa winds the last of the mineral wool with the unhurried economy of someone packing a life into a case, pausing at intervals to tilt her head toward the bore as though confirming an appointment. Her sleeves are stiff with drawn filament gone glassy with age. She does not look up when you enter; she looks up when the hum changes, which happens to coincide.

lore.name: The Half-Transcribed Fact
lore.description: Beside the lamp lies a transcription plate, three-quarters scribed and then abandoned mid-line. What is legible reads: the bore's hum is not a tone but a count — the ship numbering its own dreams at intervals no watch can hold, and every seventh interval arrives slightly early, as if the deep were leaning toward something. The scribe's hand grows larger toward the break, as though the fact were getting heavier to carry.

content.name: Boreworks
content.description: The light here does not fall; it hesitates — arriving at the filament as if obliged, dimming where attention wanders, brightening over the spun wool only when someone looks twice. The bore runs further than the eye's arithmetic, its curve contradicting the floor's insistence, and the hum that comes up from it is less a sound than a vowel the ship has been holding since before there were listeners. Spools of mineral wool sit abandoned mid-wind, filament drawn out and left to sag like something interrupted mid-thought. Stencilled across the bore-mouth in flaked green-black: LISTEN LONG TRANSCRIBE NOTHING. A single lamp still burns, packed around, nearly surrendered.

npc.name: Kildgo Hjabrauhart
npc.voice: Short answers, priced by the word. Quotes repair times the way other people quote weather. Softens, a little, for anyone who asks about the work instead of the argument.

glue.says: Turf resin, ship render, and patience. Too many makers buy glue that sets fast and dies fast. Mine holds a boot together through two generations of the same family. That's the whole trade, if you want it in one pot.

bench.says: Me and Reval. Reval says it's theirs because they found it. I say it's mine because I keep it working. Row 161 has room for one of us and we've both stayed.

choices.text: How do you split the work?

greet.says: Resoles are four days. Heels are by appointment, and the book is full. Say what you came to say.

choices.text: What's in the glue that makes it grab like that?

shift.says: Not mine. Dalla called in wet and the bench doesn't wait. The soles don't care whose hands hold them down.

choices.text: Who does it usually wait for?

reactions.grief: Somewhere under the patched-over name, something gives, but the pot still needs stirring, so they stir.
reactions.shock: The brush drips for a full minute before they notice they are still holding it.
reactions.bribed: Their refusal is quick, but their hands slow while making it, and they notice, and hate that.
reactions.accused: The denial costs more words than they usually spend, and they pay it, slowly and out loud.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands somewhere soft, and they let it sit too long before pricing the favor behind it.
reactions.questioned: Answers each question with a repair time, as if the appointment book were the only record kept.
reactions.threatened: Looks at the stencil on the beam instead of the face making threats, as if the beam outranks them.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stops mid-stroke and lets the wet sole curl, which no customer has ever watched them do.
reactions.authority_arrives: Keeps both hands in the pot, since an official's visit has never once finished inside an hour.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Steadies the glue pot before their own footing, then names the last time the row moved like this.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Could say a hundred things about Reval and says none of them, which is its own answer.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Gives the honest no, then keeps working past dark, which is how they say the rest of it.

npc.description: Kildgo Hjabrauhart works standing, both hands in a glue pot, forearms green to the elbow. They wear a shift apron with another worker's name stitched at the chest and their own patched over it from the inside, so the old name shows through in the right light.

lore.name: The Two-Ledger Sole Rack
lore.description: The rack over the bench has two columns of hooks, each column chalked with a different tally mark. Left column counts soles done under one name, right column under another. Neither column has been erased in what the chalk dust suggests is years. Both stop at the same count, thirty-one, and both resume the next day as if the other never paused.

content.name: The Resole Bench, Row 161
content.description: Kildgo Hjabrauhart slaps a wet sole flat before you finish the last stair. The bench is bolted to the slope, and glue pots cling to everything you touch. Iron banding holds the cut turf that lines the floor. Green-grey wool hangs over the bench back. A stencil on the beam: HEELS BY APPOINTMENT ONLY.

npc.name: Ram-Sausen
npc.voice: Clipped, practical, mender's cadence — diagnoses before opinions, speaks of the ship like a patient he is fond of.

open.says: I walked into the upper weld-halls once, to see the work everyone tends but nobody does. There is a mending going on in there at a scale I can't put a number to — plate after plate, league after league, held whole by something that never sleeps and never asks thanks. I stopped signing my patches proud after that. It's not menders keeping this ship together. It's menders keeping it company while something vast keeps it together for us.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll look up, from now on.
Then what are we even for?

greet.says: Mind the walkway. Fourteen souls are stored past what this deck was drawn to carry, and I'll not have you adding a fifteenth under the salt.

choices.text: What do you work with, mostly?
Who closes the seams above your head?

probe_a.says: Whatever the deck gives me. Today it's spun wool packing and salt set hard as brick. Salt remembers pressure, if you ask it right — I set a berth on it thirty years back and it hasn't shifted a finger's width since.

probe_b.says: The spar numbers, first, and the tally board second. Above that there's a schedule nobody admits to writing. My work gets inspected before I finish it, some weeks, and I've stopped wondering how.

probe_c.says: The welds. I shim and patch these frames, and above my head the hull does its own mending — seams I sealed last quarter came back this quarter closed, and not by my hand. Good work, too. Better than good.

reactions.grief: He gives the dead one's berth number before the name, then recounts the deck's souls and loses the count.
reactions.shock: The spirit level slips from his hand; he leaves it where it falls, which from a mender is a confession.
reactions.bribed: He examines the offered thing as he examines rust — no temptation, only a fitter's sorrow that it grew there.
reactions.accused: The accusation gets diagnosed before denied: he asks what evidence it rests on, as he would ask a slat.
reactions.flattered: He gives the credit to salt and weld-halls, having sworn off pride in patches, and watches the flatterer's hands instead.
reactions.questioned: He recites his rounds like a repair manifest, berth by berth, and taps the slat twice when done.
reactions.threatened: He will not give the threat a flinch, though his thumb finds the level's bubble and holds it dead centered.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: His knuckle taps four times, then five — a frame that will not sit true, and he knows which frame.
reactions.authority_arrives: He rises to give a mender's report unasked — fault found, fault mended, fault outstanding — diagnosis before anyone demands opinion.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For once the diagnosis fails — he holds the frame, listens through his palm, and cannot name this tremor.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He objects on grounds of workmanship, naming what the accused's hands could never have managed, evidence before loyalty as always.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He says plainly he cannot, then does not leave, because keeping company is a mending he still has hands for.

npc.description: Ram-Sausen is crouched at a berth-frame with a spirit level, shimming a salt-pressed bunk slat by eye and tapping it twice with a knuckle to hear whether it holds. Every few seconds he glances at a gold-painted tally board as if daring it to disagree.

lore.name: The Salt-Packed Splice
lore.description: Where the lowest spar meets the hull proper, a seam has been packed with compacted salt and bound in spun mineral wool, renewed so many times the layers read like a core sample: grey wool over grey wool, and beneath them, deep in the packing, salt gone glassy with age — a mend begun so long ago the hand that started it belongs to no lineage anyone here can name. Each layer is signed with a mender's knot tied into the binding cord, and there are more knots than the cord has room for, the oldest pushed flat and worn to suggestion. The seal has never failed; it has only ever been continued.

content.name: Reivuhild's Berth Warren
content.description: The floor gives under the heel like muscle, then cracks faintly with dried crystal — the body reads warmth first, and the residue of many washings, before the eye reads anything at all. Berths rise in stacked galleries, twelve tiers of them, each hammock and curtain and private lamp multiplying upward until the gold light from the hull-side glows is swallowed halfway and the topmost bunks hang in a dim that looks almost like dusk. On the lowest spar, stenciled in a hand gone blunt with repainting: BERTH ASSIGNMENTS POSTED BY SPAR NUMBER. Two figures stand mid-argument near the third gallery; they fall silent together, the way people do when a stranger's tread has just told them something.

npc.name: Makur-Raljam
npc.voice: Measured, route-minded; speaks in loads, intervals, and what moves versus what waits. A Drift worker's habit of asking what anything is *in transit to*.

open.says: It's kept. All of it — every car, every manifest, every knotted cord and chalked interval that ever passed through Mercury's arteries — read and filed somewhere below us, in a chamber I've heard named and never seen. I used to think the Drift's Braid was the fastest record-keeping on the ship; then I worked a shaft in Mercury's domain and understood we are the slow copy. Nothing in motion is unrecorded. Including, I'd wager, this conversation — so I say it plainly once and never again: the manifests that stopped reconciling didn't stop. They were withdrawn from the copy we're allowed to see.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it quietly.
Withdrawn by whom? That answer frightens me.

greet.says: Careful on the ladder rungs — third from the top is iron gone chalk-brittle. This isn't my shift and I've no authority to wave you through, so whatever you're carrying, carry it quietly.

choices.text: Whose shift were you meant to work?
What happens to everything that moves through here?
Didn't mean to interrupt your counting.

probe_a.says: Telltale glass. It flickers when the shaft breathes, and the breathing tells you whether the transit arteries above are running hot or asleep. Iron takes the load; quartz takes the truth. A car lashed with iron alone is just weight — with a quartz telltale mounted, it's a reading.

probe_b.says: Bay-side relay, third bell, a good route with a good knot in it. I traded onto this dead shaft because the Braid said freight manifests here stopped reconciling six weeks back — cars logged as moving that never arrived anywhere. That's not a clerical error. That's circulation stopping, and circulation stopping is the one heresy I keep.

probe_c.says: Marks the wind. Every flicker interval I chalk onto the slate, and the intervals have been shortening — the shaft is pulling harder toward the deep than anything up here should make it pull. And there's the other thing: that junction housing, the one with no rust and no tool-marks and no dust. Everything in this shaft is old except that. It wasn't here when the work stopped. Somebody, or something, fitted it after.

reactions.grief: Told the name, they begin re-lashing a car that will never leave, knots too tight to be anything but prayer.
reactions.shock: Nine flickers into the count they stop, chalk raised, reading the body like a car fallen off every manifest.
reactions.bribed: They hold the offered payment a breath too long, set it down, and name the copy below as their witness.
reactions.accused: Accusation lands like a misweighed load; they stand very still and ask which waybill the charge travels under.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands and their eyes go over the speaker like a doubtful waybill, checking what the words are carrying.
reactions.questioned: Asked to account, they recite the last three intervals from the slate unprompted, nothing in the numbers hurried.
reactions.threatened: The threat is filed like a schedule change; only the telltale count betrays them, threes sliding into fours.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Shown the contradiction, they correct the entry rather than defend it, muttering of withdrawn copies, clerk to the last.
reactions.authority_arrives: The seal shows and they surrender the slate unasked, relieved someone finally holds authority over a shaft they kept alone.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder registers as traffic above, not catastrophe; only when the telltale stays dark does their voice lose its intervals.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They cite the accused's clean intervals before the charge finishes, a defense assembled from pure habit, not certainty.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refusal comes in route-talk, though they aim the lantern at the ladder and name the rung that will not bear.

npc.description: Makur-Raljam stands on the freight-car's roof with a fused-quartz telltale held to the shaft wind, counting its flickers against a chalk-marked slate. The car beneath them is loaded, lashed, and going nowhere; the work stopped around it weeks ago and they are the only thing in Cargo-Shaft 3 still pretending otherwise.

lore.name: The Car's Transit Ledger
lore.description: Bolted inside the gate is a slate frame holding a quartz pane scored with thousands of tally-marks, one per descent, each tagged with a route-knot in cord beneath — a count of everything this shaft ever moved, kept in glass because paper dies and iron forgets. The tallies stop mid-column, mid-stroke, the groove of the last mark trailing off unfinished. Beneath the frame, screwed in recently enough that the iron around it shows bright tool-marks, is a second, empty pane, waiting to be begun.

content.name: Cargo-Shaft 3
content.description: The smell is cold flux and scorched quartz — the sharp, sweetish burn of glass being married to iron at heat — though no heat has run here in a long while. The shaft drops past a car the size of a granary barn, its chalk-white plating wind-scoured to the grain, and a stencilled line across the gate still reads SHAFT TRANSIT ONE HOUR, DO NOT SIGNAL EARLY. Nothing echoes; the depth simply takes the sound. A lantern burns at the gate's lip, new wick, new oil — Makur-Raljam's, and the only thing in this place not old.

npc.name: Aleanthichaes of Leasheia
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, precedent-minded; answers in the grammar of writ and clause.

greet.says: Vault's mid-inventory. Whatever writ you want, it's either sealed, gone, or both. I can give you the zone charter — that one doesn't leave the racks, but you may read it here.

charter.says: Mind the tenth line. It's older than the office and we don't amend what we can't source. Now — I have nine hundred permits to reconcile against a chest that isn't here.

reactions.grief: Asks after the date, the seals, the disposition of record — then cannot say the name.
reactions.shock: Looks from the body to the chalk outline on his floor as though the two might reconcile.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the corrective statute on inducements without looking up, then re-inks a line he had entered correctly the first time.
reactions.accused: Denies it in statute — vault opened by double seal only, neither seal his — and the denial comes out too loud.
reactions.flattered: Waits, longer than courtesy allows, for the exception — no one commends a clerk unless a writ needs unwriting.
reactions.questioned: Gives his whereabouts in clause and timestamp, door by door, already reconciled to being doubted.
reactions.threatened: Recites his writ of appointment from memory, each clause slower than the last, the way a man grips a rope.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stops mid-line in the ledger, pen lifted, and reaches for a clause he knows does not exist.
reactions.authority_arrives: Rises off the stool with the ledger already open to the vault-status page, reciting inventory like a defence.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Steadies the foil spindles one by one, unwilling to admit nothing in the vault caused that.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Produces, unasked, three precedents proving the named party could not have broken the seal — too fast, too ready.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Names, precisely, the writ that would grant it, then confesses he holds no seal for any of its lines.

npc.description: Aleanthichaes of Leasheia wakes before you finish crossing the room, sits up, and begins straightening the seal-ledger without quite looking at you — the practiced economy of someone who has filed permits under a ceiling that has never once acknowledged him.

lore.name: The Chalk Outline
lore.description: Whoever emptied the vault traced the chest's footprint before it went, and wrote the tally of its seals beside it — nine, then a tenth added in a different hand, uncounted in the register.

content.name: Writ-Vault 19
content.description: A clerk's stool and lap-desk sit three paces from the door, close enough to trip over, while the racks they serve run sheer to a ceiling no ladder in the Nave would reach — six meters of emptied shelving, silver foil wound on spindles, mineral wool packed behind riveted sheet. The gap where one writ-chest stood is swept clean and outlined in chalk, the way you mark a grave. Over the empty brackets: VAULT OPENED BY DOUBLE SEAL ONLY. In the chalk outline's shadow, someone sleeps, coat for a pillow.

npc.name: Lleinadych Seabane
npc.voice: Short, amused, always mid-arithmetic. They talk in odds.

why.says: Off the market decks, mostly. People want somewhere to shout that isn't about work. My uncle ran this circle when shouting was cheaper. I think about that more than I should.

choices.text: Your uncle — is he still around?

them.says: Nineteen years raking and notching. I know every winner's weight by the sound they make hitting timber. Ask me anything except who's favored tonight — I sell those odds and I'm not giving them free.

crowd.says: Busier than the benches. We built for forty and get ninety. I rake between every fall now, which I never used to. The sand doesn't get a rest and neither do I.

choices.text: Where are they all coming from?

glass.says: Stone cracked in the frost years back and nobody quarries anymore. Glass holds a shoulder fine. Watch the edge, though — it's claimed two collarbones.

greet.says: Stand off the chalk or stand in the ring. Those are the only two places at Grildal. Which is it?

choices.text: Why the glass in the wall?
It's crowded today. Busier than usual?
How long have you kept this yard?

uncle.says: He walked into the tunnels with the Rindwalker crowd one spring and didn't come back. They still notch his name here when a Seabane wins. It's mine now, most falls. Raking keeps my hands busy on the days it doesn't sit right.

choices.text: I'll leave you to the sand.
Maybe I'll take a turn in the ring.

reactions.grief: They rake a stretch of sand already clean, then give the dead one's landing weight, unasked, to nobody.
reactions.shock: The running count in their head loses its place; they stand in the sand without raking.
reactions.bribed: No is the first answer, on principle, since a fixed book is worthless; then they name the real price anyway.
reactions.accused: The rake stops mid-stroke for the first time in nineteen years; they laugh wrongly and ask who laid it.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands warmer than they admit; they let it sit three beats too long before pricing the favor.
reactions.questioned: They answer each question with a number first, then the reason, amused that anyone wants it in order.
reactions.threatened: Fair odds on the threat, spoken level, while the knotted cord winds tight enough to bite their palm.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they recompute aloud, offer the corrected figure, and pretend the first number was always the second.
reactions.authority_arrives: They go back to raking with exaggerated care, making themselves furniture until the official says their name.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The roar thins and they listen to it go, counting who fell before anyone says what moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They snap that they have notched this person's every fall for years, and the numbers don't run to this.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea gets a silence, then the only free number they have given in years, eyes on the sand.

npc.description: Lleinadych Seabane rakes the sand inside the circle between bouts, dragging the chalk line back true with a length of knotted cord. They do not stop for you. The rake keeps its count.

lore.name: The scored rail
lore.description: The timber rail carries a notch for every fall ever won here, cut small, one per winner. The oldest notches are worn shallow from sleeves.

content.name: Grildal
content.description: You hear Grildal before you see it: shouted counts, bodies hitting planed timber, the crowd noise funneled by the stone ring into one flat roar. Inside, the chalk circle is packed ring-side with more spectators than the benches hold. Stenciled on the timber rail: FIRST FALL WINS, NO GRIPS BELOW THE BELT. A pane of plain glass has been set into the ring wall where a stone was missing.

npc.name: Maidfinah al-Rione
npc.voice: Measured, kind, unflinching — she speaks of the ship's body with the gentleness owed to a patient and the gravity owed to a god, never distinguishing between the two.

deep.says: Below us the ship keeps its oldest promise, and promises, when kept long enough, begin to want things. I was sent down once. I came back changed in my accounting of what counts as alive. You will go too. I think you were written into the ledger before I was.

choices.text: Ask her what she means by ledger.

greet.says: You came in on the cold side. Most do, now. The heat has opinions about who it receives, and lately it receives fewer.

ledger.says: I mean only that Sol has never sent for me by name, and I have worked here thirty years — and you, an hour old to this floor, and the doors open for you like a hand. Ask yourself who was wounded first, and who was built to close it.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the silence answer.

nickel.says: It dreams of the shape it held. Feel — there, where the grain leans. Absence has a texture, if you stand in Sol's light long enough to lose your own.

choices.text: Ask what the deep sends up, that needs a ward like this.

departure.says: Something large came through and was mended on its way, and the mending outlasted it. We do not say its name. Names are for things that stay.

practitionoitioner.says: Practitioner? Read the stencil. The wounds close regardless. We are permitted to watch — that is the whole of our vocation, and less than half of it.

choices.text: Ask what she reads in the nickel.

reactions.grief: Her hands begin, absurdly, the gestures of triage on empty air before the name finishes, then fall.
reactions.shock: For once the ship's body means nothing to her; she forgets the room, the gold, the god, everything but blood.
reactions.bribed: She holds the offered payment at scar's length, the way forceps hold what must be cut away.
reactions.accused: Accusation meets her as a symptom would: she asks where it hurts, and whether her accuser has eaten.
reactions.flattered: Praise of her standing finds the thirty-year wound beneath it, and she answers too warmly, too quickly, undone.
reactions.questioned: She answers each question in the cadence of a chart read aloud, unhurried, kind, long accustomed to accounting.
reactions.threatened: A threat is, to her, a prognosis; she receives it with the stillness of someone who has read worse.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her palm leaves the nickel for the first time, and the silence where her alibi should stand says enough.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door opens for an official of Sol as it never opened for her, and she watches, counting.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: While others grab the rails, she closes her eyes toward whatever vast thing below has rolled over in its sleep.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She could believe it, and that eagerness shames her; the objection arrives half a heartbeat late.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her voice takes the register kept for families outside the theatre; she stays anyway beside what she cannot close.

npc.description: Maidfinah al-Rione stands with one hand flat against the nickel, reading it the way the blind read a face, her gold-dusted sleeves tucked back from forearms mapped with old furnace-cicatrices. Her companion has already turned away, dispute unfinished, as though the argument were a thing to be stored and returned to on a schedule you are not party to.

lore.name: The Nickel Splint
lore.description: The great splint is annealed nickel, closed around a wound in a bulkhead the size of a fell thing's ribcage — and its lattice is still tightening, grain by grain, though nothing has lain beneath it for days. Someone has packed the fracture with graphite, dark as confession, so the metal may slip without shrieking. You understood mending to require a mender; the splint has not been told, and keeps closing anyway, the way a mouth keeps shaping a name after the person is gone.

content.name: Closing-Splint 6
content.description: The heat is not in the room; it is elsewhere, held off by something patient — the gold lattice splinting the air stands cold as a bone in January, and the cold stands nowhere you can put a hand. What is missing is enormous: a body-shaped absence the lattice still leans toward, wounds closing over a thing no longer there. Two figures mid-quarrel go quiet at your entry, the way a river pauses around a new stone. Stencilled above the fold of the wall, in gold gone dull: WOUNDS CLOSED PRACTITIONER ABSENT.

npc.name: Kotrearemos Phione
npc.voice: Slow, exact, hospitality worn like a uniform that no longer fits — offers comfort the way Continuants file reports, and means it more than the form suggests.

end.says: Go warm. And if you pass the mender who left this half-done, tell them the water's still honest.

deep.says: I think it was for washing something bigger than a swimmer, and I think it held. You can stand at its rim and feel the water-line cut into the stone at your chest height, and know the water used to come to your forehead. Perhaps someone will come down that hall someday and need the depth again. That's who I'm keeping it warm for. Not you. Not me.

fear.says: This is the court's own ground, do you understand? The long hall further in — benches cut for people nobody has ever brought me a measurement of. He holds it and he doesn't bother. The pools were built to serve whatever sat at that table, and whatever sat there was not swimming. I keep the salt, I mind the warm water, and I do not walk further in. That's my whole theology and I've held it thirty years.

choices.text: Ask what she thinks the deepest pool was for.

chain.says: You found the ledger. Good — it deserves eyes. The last auditor stamped every link and then kept going into the floor, which means the water was deeper than her chain, and she reported it anyway, which means she was braver than her chain too. They don't audit down here anymore. I check her notches every season. They're all still correct.

choices.text: Ask why the auditor measured at all.

greet.says: Mind the far pools — water's live on that side and I've not the hands to warn anyone twice. You're the first guest since the cut-open half stopped being mine to finish. Sit where it's warm; there's a reason the heat only sits low, and it's not the heating.

choices.text: Ask why half the bathhouse is opened up.
Ask about the depth-chain in the bench.

repair.says: The writ came down that the baths were to be rated for the present population, and the present population couldn't fill a tenth of them. So we're making a smaller thing out of a bigger thing, which is the only kind of repair anyone does up here. I keep the salt packed because salt keeps the water honest. Nothing else here is honest.

inherited.says: A mender's, not one of mine — a Rindwalker who capped the pipes, cut the wall, and left before the report. No name filed. You don't leave a job half-done unless the job told you something. I've been finishing it anyway, because the water shouldn't cool because someone got frightened.

reactions.grief: Names the dead once, then starts talking about the water-line in the deep pool, chest height, and cannot stop.
reactions.shock: The lamp goes down on the rim with a click they will not remember making; nothing in them follows.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the payment would buy, because if it is a mender for the capped pipes the answer changes.
reactions.accused: For the first time in thirty years the handful falls unmeasured; they ask the accuser to repeat it, twice.
reactions.flattered: The thanks lands harder than any threat; they answer twice, and the second answer forgets the filing cadence entirely.
reactions.questioned: Recites each hour since the last lamplighting in report cadence, as though the salt kept its own ledger.
reactions.threatened: Somewhere under the crust the forearms go cold, and the pour continues on thirty years' momentum alone.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Holds to the wrong hour a breath too long, then corrects it in a voice quieter than the lamp allows.
reactions.authority_arrives: Sets the lamp for the visitor like a place at table and turns the light from the far hall.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Thirty years of decided pace ends mid-handful; they watch the drained pool as though it might fill again.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Repeats the name once, in the tone reserved for salt of a grade they were never taught to pack.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers everything the room owns, the warm pool and a dry bench, then admits plainly it will not be enough.

npc.description: Kotrearemos Phione works alone at the seam where repair meets ruin, packing compacted salt into a cavity in the pool wall by lamplight, one measured handful at a time. Salt crusts the forearms to the elbow and the top of the head where a hood would sit; the work has the tempo of someone who has decided the pace years ago and sees no cause to revise it.

lore.name: The Long Bench Ledger
lore.description: Under the coping of the drained pool, a sintered ceramic bench has been split and hollowed, and inside sits a brass depth-chain, its links stamped with measurements no swimmer could survive — the lowest link alone runs the length of an arm. The stamps continue past the chain's end into notches cut directly into the pool floor. Whoever certified this water for use had been measuring, in increments, how deep it was still getting.

content.name: The Hull Bathhouse of Last Call
content.description: The heat sits at knee height and refuses to climb: warm brine lapping the near pools, and four body-lengths up, where the girdered ceiling opens to the cut, air cold enough to ache. Half the bathhouse is gone — a wall of sintered ceramic peeled back to bare hull, its plumbing sawn and capped, its benches removed without trace, so the emptiness has edges and the edges are where your eye keeps returning. The whole chamber is green-black, wind-scoured down to the grain, buttressed against a curvature of floor no bathhouse should own; a stencil across the deepest pool's rim reads POOL DEPTH EXCEEDS RATED SWIMMER, and the pool beneath it was drained a long time ago.

npc.name: Damaaereem the Twice-Returned
npc.voice: Speaks in the flat cadence of someone reciting to machinery that might be listening; uses temperature as others use time.

live.says: I sleep in the fourth warm seam and eat what the walk-in brings, and my dreams get inventoried somewhere I've never seen, by something that's very polite about it. That's a dwelling. Ask the Nave for more than that and they'll give you a lease and a lock, which is just a cell with the humility sanded off.

choices.text: Does anything here ever speak — a signal, a voice?

cells.says: For? You're asking a spoon what soup is for. They hold. That's the whole liturgy — they hold, and the middle of the ship holds because they hold, and I hold them, and Sol holds me, allegedly. Warm on the near side, warm on the far side, never at the seam. You live where the seam is.

choices.text: You live here? In the cells' shadow?

count.says: Because the room keeps its own tally and it resents the competition. Say a number in here and the cells go quiet for a shift, all of them, together — like a congregation that heard a cough during the elevation. I counted once. Twice, if you believe the name. I don't recommend believing the name.

greet.says: You walked in warm. That's a thing I can hear now, did you know. Nobody warns you what the ears do down here. This cell is mid-shiver — stand back from the mouth, or don't, it's your heat.

choices.text: Why shouldn't the cells be counted aloud?

twice.says: From the deep walk and back, both times, which the ledger calls remarkable and I call misfiled. What came back the second time was mostly me. The rest stayed down there, keeping something company. It seemed to want the company. That's not a thing I say to the warm.

choices.text: Let them return to the glass.

signal.says: The cells hum, the seam holds, and sometimes — at the violet hour, if the light's wrong — the whole rank answers a question nobody asked yet. I put my hand on the glass and I wait. I've stopped deciding whether it's Sol or the chamber or the ship dreaming in its own direction. Waiting is the work. Waiting is the worship.

reactions.grief: Names the dead in seam-units, how warm they ran, which cell favored them, and only afterward does the hand shake.
reactions.shock: Counts once under their breath before horror reminds them aloud is forbidden, the unfinished number a swallowed coal.
reactions.bribed: Asked to misremember, they quote no refusal but the sum converted into hours of unrationed warmth.
reactions.accused: The accusation lands on no one, since the room accuses them nightly and its testimony always ran longer.
reactions.flattered: The flattery is permitted to pool around their ankles like the cold, familiar, already factored into the tally.
reactions.questioned: Their answers come in heat rather than hours, as though the cold were a witness still to be satisfied.
reactions.threatened: Goes terribly polite, in the manner of the thing that inventories their dreams — the only fear they own.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recants by degree, cooler by a few warmth-units, on the wager that no one else reads temperature as time.
reactions.authority_arrives: Withdraws the palm from the glass a beat too late, squares the gold seams, and recites their station unprompted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Watches the cells rather than the ceiling, because only the hollows' grip matters when the room itself moves.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Testifies to the accused's heat, their hours, their seam, then hears how guilty that intimacy makes them sound.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains with unbearable gentleness that holding is not saving, and keeps their eyes on the glass while saying it.

npc.description: Damaaereem the Twice-Returned crouches at the rank's foot with a hand flat against the glass of the lowest cell, listening to it through the palm the way one listens to a door through a wall. Gold thread runs through their coverall at every seam — Sol's livery, kept immaculate in a room that forgives nothing — and they have drawn their feet up out of the cold pool without appearing to notice they did it.

lore.name: A silver dipper, worn concave
lore.description: Hung on a hook between two cells: a small silver scoop, its bowl rubbed thin on one side, as if someone has carried heat out of these cells a measured mouthful at a time for longer than a handle's worth of years.

content.name: Node 82 Over
content.description: The cold arrives first, and it is local — pooled at ankle height like water finding a grade, while the air above the cells burns faintly violet and warms nothing. A rank of body-sized hollows hums down the wall, black glass mouths rimmed in silver, each one exhaling a heat that never crosses its own threshold. Someone has stencilled along the lintel, in a hand gone careful with repetition: DO NOT COUNT THE CELLS ALOUD. The room does not end so much as decline to continue; the far rank sits at a distance the eye accepts and the feet distrust.

npc.name: Rold Two-Hulls
npc.voice: Blunt, measurement-haunted; speaks in tolerances and holds, gives credit to the metal before the hand.

deep.says: Further than my routes and further than I'm curious. Down past the shafts the markings stop being ours — older hand, older script, and no ladder back. A walker who goes past the last marked ring isn't mending anymore. She's visiting. And visitors come home or they don't.

choices.text: Thank her and step back from the trough.

mars.says: Seen it. Walked a weld seam during a pressure call, three days of my life, and the whole time I understood I was standing on something that noticed me the way you notice a splinter. It let me work. That's not welcome. That's tolerance, and tolerance is a wage you earn every shift.

choices.text: Ask how far down the tunnels go.

work.says: Spine. Six kilometres of it, pushed out at a finger's width an hour, and every metre has to hold a continent's weight for longer than your line has held a name. Salt goes in the mix for the grain. Mars welds the hull; we feed it. That's the whole of the arrangement.

choices.text: Ask whether she has seen Mars herself.

greet.says: Stand off the trough line. New hall, new spine, and the metal hasn't decided yet whether it trusts the dies. You want something, say it flat.

choices.text: Ask what the hall is making.

leave.says: Mind the vibration when the run cycles. It's expected. Everything worth keeping shakes before it sets.

reactions.grief: Twice she mis-times the draw after the name lands, and blames the filament, never her hands.
reactions.shock: Her eyes measure the body first, length and breadth, before the hook drops from a hand gone stupid.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against the spine's age, finds it short, hands it back like a mis-stamped plate.
reactions.accused: The insult lands nowhere; she asks which tolerance she exceeded and waits, hook steady, for the number.
reactions.flattered: Flattery aimed at her hands gets credited straight back to metal and dies while she watches for the ask.
reactions.questioned: She recites her movements as die timings, hook to trough, and treats the question as a gauge reading.
reactions.threatened: The threat measures smaller than a pressure call, and she says so in the flat voice that survived one.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Cornered by her own numbers, she recants like scrapping a bad batch, flatly, and names what she hid.
reactions.authority_arrives: She squares to the official like fresh paint on new gantries, offering numbers nobody has asked for yet.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder runs off-pattern and she knows it, hook frozen over the die, listening for a number that won't come.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She objects the way she rejects bad stock, on evidence, listing what the accused's hands do too well to waste.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She names her limits in tolerances, offers no hope she hasn't measured, and stays anyway, which is all she has.

npc.description: Rold Two-Hulls works the die-seat with a long hook of copper, fishing the filament's leading edge as it comes off the draw, and steers it with a touch so light it looks like courtesy. She wears a harness with two back-plates riveted over one another, the outer one cut down and polished from use, and she does not look up until the run is steady.

lore.name: The Gauge Spine
lore.description: At the hall's head stands the first length ever extruded here, kept as a gauge: a rib of grey metal three hands thick and, by its own stamped tally, forty-one metres long, with a second stamp beneath the first reading simply HOLDS. Every new run is measured against it before release. The metal is older than the rebuilt hall around it — salvaged, someone says, from a spine that failed, kept because it did not.

content.name: Girder Extrusion
content.description: The smell reaches you first: hot salt and drawn metal, a sweetness like scorched bread under it, the filament's sizing burning off as it passes the dies. The hall is new enough that the lead-grey paint still smells of itself, and every gantry stands square, unscarred, waiting to earn its dents. A stencilled line runs the length of the feed trough — EXTRUSION RUN IN PROGRESS, VIBRATION EXPECTED — and under it, forty people crowd a spine that will not be finished for a generation.

npc.name: Siotengaupimael Taapuneetath
npc.voice: Triage cadence — clipped triage shorthand softening into liturgy when Continuant matters come up; measures everything in patients and hours.

open.says: Three weeks ago the decks went green-rim at the wrong hour — Venus's hour, we call it, though she keeps no hour we've ever charted. I walked the supply corridor to the garden-gate and the growth had advanced like a full season overnight, fruit set, canopy closed, root-mat lifting seam-plate I couldn't dent with a mallet. Our cultivation is generation by generation, hand by hand, and we brag on our patience. Hers doesn't run on patience. It runs on something we haven't been asked to understand, and everything we grew to triage here was sized against a casualty list I now suspect was a garden's, not ours.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry this carefully.
Sized for a garden's casualties. That's unsettling.

greet.says: If you're bleeding, sit. If you're not, mind the cot lanes — they're numbered for stretchers, not visitors.

choices.text: What are you proud of here?
Something big left this room. What was it?

probe_a.says: Mass casualty reception. Six hundred cots, filament lines for ninety seconds of intake per body. It was built against a day the ship promised would come and never has, which we count as the working of grace.

probe_b.says: Paelozhen's. She logged out of the ward rotation eleven days back and the rota never filled her slot, so the sheets get me. I stopped asking the council where people go. The answer is always continuity, which is a way of saying wait.

probe_c.says: That we could take six hundred wounded and not lose the count of one. Rating a thing is easy; being ready for it, cot by cot, spool by spool — that's the whole of our creed made physical. Solen audits us for it. I pass.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives and they assign it a cot number by rote, then stand in the lane with nothing to receive.
reactions.shock: The first real casualty undoes them politely — hands perfect at intake, voice trying twice to log the hour and failing.
