reactions.bribed: For one breath the offer tempts them — the racks want filling — and then they remember what the racks are for.
reactions.accused: They sort the accusation like intake — which hour, which body — then their thumb finds the borrowed roster.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands like placebo, and they answer it with liturgy — capacity rated, grace unspent.
reactions.questioned: They account for their hours the way they'd log intake — corridor, minute, spool count — and offer the wrist-roster unasked.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets triaged aloud like a wound — class, minutes to bleed — as if severity named could be severity lowered.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they don't defend the words but recalculate them quieter, the way a chart gets revised after the patient dies.
reactions.authority_arrives: Authority enters and the borrowed roster slides beneath their cuff before the greeting comes, in perfect intake cadence.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room moves and they count the interval like a pulse, then go down the racks hunting spool-rims for green.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their defense runs to exact minutes of the accused's shift, knowledge no stranger should have, and they hear it late.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea exceeds triage, and they give it a cot, ninety seconds, clean filament — everything but an answer.

npc.description: Siotengaupimael Taapuneetath is restocking a wall of drawn filament spools with the unhurried precision of someone counting spoons in an empty house, pausing now and then to press a palm flat against a sintered ceramic cot as if checking it for breath. The shift roster clipped at their wrist belongs to a different name.

lore.name: Filament sizers, graduated by hectare
lore.description: A rack beside the intake aisle holds triage sizers of drawn filament, silver and taut as harp strings. A sizer is what a healer stretches across a wound to grade it — and each one here opens wide enough to span a field. The smallest template on the rack would cover a farmstead; someone has tied a knot of cord around it, the way a person marks the tool they reach for most.

content.name: The Triage Cathedral
content.description: Nothing moves. Cot after cot, ten thousand of them, stand made down a nave of sintered ceramic, and not one holds a body. Racks of gauze wait beside beds no casualty reached; the vents push a wind that has scoured the floor to bare grain and carries no sound back. Across the doorsill a stencilled line reads: CAPACITY RATED, NEVER TESTED AT SCALE.

npc.name: Trion Raexemio
npc.voice: Measured, tournament-cadenced, half announcer and half steward; treats every conversation like an opening ceremony that might still be worth holding.

room.says: Because a room this size was built for a crowd we have never produced, and we rebuilt it anyway, full measure, no corners cut. That's either faith or arithmetic, and I can't tell you which. The old bays didn't fuss. This one corrects itself, quietly, like something is still keeping the books.

champ.says: The seat's been open two seasons. The last champion stopped coming, and no one will say why, and the tier above mine stays empty like a held breath. Anyway. You've the look of someone who plays, or someone who's about to have to. Either way, the room is fresh and the paint is correct, and that's more than most of us can say.

games.says: Standing stones, relay chess, the long count — games you can lose slowly, which is the point. Status in the Nave is won here and nowhere else, and a seat at the tier above yours is worth more than a title. Walk the tiers sometime. The stonework remembers every champion; we inlay the names in silver and let the echoless acoustics keep them.

choices.text: Who holds the highest tier now?

greet.says: You're standing where the winner stands. Careful — the paint's not worn in yet, and neither am I, if that makes sense. Three rebuilds I've seen this room through, and it's never come back so correct. Nothing out of true. It bothers me more than it should.

choices.text: Were you sleeping in the judge's box?
Why does a correct room bother you?

keeps.says: I worked the upper courts in Jupiter's country before I came down to this. Don't ask me to explain that. I walked the long table's length once — took the better part of a morning — and understood that whatever held court there never needed us to watch. Here, at least, the seats face the players. It's a small mercy, but I've learned to prize those.

choices.text: You walked a table for a whole morning.

sleep.says: In the box, yes. It's the only seat in the Nave that faces everyone and answers to no one, and I find I sleep better where the judgment doesn't reach. Don't tell the ward registry. They register everything now, Solen's people — everything but the reasons.

choices.text: What do the Continuants have to do with a games hall?

solen.says: Continuants hold that a generation is a game you must not lose quickly. Solen audits us the same as the clinics — turns, attendance, whether the tiers held. She came to the last final. Sat where you're standing. She watched the whole match and never once looked at the board, only at the crowd, like she was counting us against some older figure.

choices.text: I'll leave her to her arithmetic.

reactions.grief: Delivers the dead player's record in full ceremonial voice, match by match, unable to stop at the losses.
reactions.shock: Their shout dies in the echoless geometry, and they stand counting ribs until their hands remember how to move.
reactions.bribed: The sum is priced, briefly, against lacquer and tier-sealing, before they remember whose memory is for sale.
reactions.accused: The ceremonial cadence thins to nothing, and the denial is aimed at the empty tiers rather than the accuser.
reactions.flattered: The praise registers as a rigged bout they have refereed before, savored anyway, since this room hears so little applause.
reactions.questioned: Their whereabouts come out in announcer's cadence, hour by hour, an account delivered like the evening's printed programme.
reactions.threatened: Names the threat a foul, quietly, the way a referee logs an infraction nobody has the standing to penalize.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The disproved claim gets one quiet repetition, in the manner of announcers repeating scores that refuse to change.
reactions.authority_arrives: The years-rehearsed welcome for visiting jurisdiction finally sees use, a full opening ceremony staged for an audience of one.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Counting begins unbidden, ribs and load arcs, because the room corrects itself quietly and this was not quiet.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Protocol asks what evidence earned the naming, while relief at someone else's name loosens the sash a fraction.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Their whole jurisdiction amounts to a seat and a fair count, and they say so without dressing it as more.

npc.description: Trion Raexemio wakes in the judge's box and comes down the tiers without hurry, silver tournament sash still knotted from the night's games, one hand trailing the buttress ribs the way other people use handrails. They count the empty seating as they pass it, lips moving slightly, a habit of a games-keeper who has never once seen the bay full.

lore.name: The Judge's Chair
lore.description: The chair in the judge's box was salvaged from the bay's cargo days, its seat worn to bare iron by four hundred years of pallets before it ever judged a game.

content.name: The Bay Amphitheatre
content.description: The smell arrives first: graphite dust baked onto iron, warm as a skillet left on the plate, with a sweet edge of fresh-cut lacquer where the seating was newly sealed. The stands rise in silvered buttressed tiers, each load-bearing rib sunk down through the old cargo bay's floor, and a shout at the rail goes nowhere — the geometry eats it whole. Stencilled along the lowest tier in careful new paint: SEATING RATED FOR FULL BAY, RARELY MET. Someone is asleep in the judge's box, folded into a chair sized for the absent court.

npc.name: Rarglin-bin Mailar
npc.voice: Short, procedural, kind in the way of someone counting your breaths. Asks before touching. Answers about the work, not about themselves.

end.says: Door's behind you. Use it soft — he's still sleeping.

leg.says: Field worker. Fell from a ladder rack on Row 181. Bone set clean, but the swelling came before he got here, so he sleeps it off and I watch it. He'll limp a season and then not. That's the whole story.

row.says: Row 181 is market terrace, south end. Comes to me for backs and wrists more than any street in the Nave. So I scratch it where I'll see it. When the same row shows up four times, you don't wait for them to find the room. You walk in before the swelling sets. That's on the wall for a reason.

choices.text: Ask if they need anything carried to Row 181.

frame.says: Made it myself, years back. Glass takes a set weight and holds it, no spring to lie to you. The cracked one I wire because it still measures true. You throw out a tool the day it lies to you, not the day it looks bad.

choices.text: Ask about the numbers scratched on them.

greet.says: You walked in quiet. Good. Most who need this room don't. Sit or stand, but keep weight off whatever brought you.

choices.text: Ask about the leg still on the table.
Ask about the glass spacers on the frame.

offer.says: Not today. But you noticed the row, so you'll notice other things. If a terrace sends you here twice in one month, come back and tell me. That's worth more than carrying.

reactions.grief: Asks who found them and whether there was swelling, the only grief their trade knows how to say.
reactions.shock: Hands that never shake wipe on the sacking again and again, long after they are dry.
reactions.bribed: Answers about the work, as always, which is how this one says no.
reactions.accused: Mid-splint they stop, hands still, and look at their own fingers as if these did it.
reactions.flattered: Treats the praise like a symptom, something arriving before its cause, and waits for the request.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day's ledger, who came, which row, what bone, and stops there.
reactions.threatened: First their eyes check the sleeping man, then the door, and only then do they answer.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The correction comes flat and immediate, and then they tie a strap that was already tied.
reactions.authority_arrives: Never looks up from the half-wrapped leg, only asks whether the official is bleeding before anything else.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Knows how a body flinches when something inside is wrong, and the room just flinched like that.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Cites the wrist they set on that person last month, dates and all, as if bone could testify.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Promises nothing, and for once their hands hang useless at their sides.

npc.description: Rarglin-bin Mailar wakes when you cross the floor, sits up, and rubs one wrist with the other thumb, working feeling back into it. A strap is still looped over their shoulder from the interrupted work. They look at the half-wrapped leg, then at you, and decide you can wait a moment longer.

lore.name: The Traction Frame
lore.description: Clamped to the table is a traction frame built from a salvaged cargo strut and plain glass spacers, ground by hand to different thicknesses. Each spacer is scratched with a row number and a weight. Row 181 is on four of them. The thinnest one is cracked and still in use, bound with wire. Whoever built this measured every patient's pull individually and kept the records on the glass itself, where a damp cloth could erase a mistake and a dropped frame could not erase the work.

content.name: Bonesetting, Row 181
content.description: The light here comes in dull and wavering, as if the fixture above the table is half dead and the wall is deciding whether to lend it more. A bonesetting table holds a half-wrapped leg, splints stacked beside it. Sacking covers a basket of straps. Nobody cleared up when the work stopped; someone is asleep in the chair by the basin, chin on chest.

npc.name: Theaoleinuna Phartusione
npc.voice: Clipped, competitive, half to themselves; speaks of the gallery's races as if the hall itself were a colleague who has been letting the side down.

race.says: The hall races whom it chooses. I once ran the full line against an empty gate and felt the floor take my stride like a hand under a heel — humoring me, or measuring. I logged it. The log came back filed under weather.

court.says: Deeper in there's the table. You'll know it when the gallery ends — a length of bench you could seat a district at, set for a meal that was never eaten, and the chairs turned outward like the company left mid-sentence. I keep the gauge readings current along the whole approach. Continuity is a duty even when the guest of honor can't be bothered to attend.

first.says: A Drift runner, wrist full of knots, wanting to race the length for record. I let her to the half-kilometre mark and no further. Whatever she carried back to the market, it wasn't the time.

choices.text: What's down the rest of the gallery?

fresh.says: For me, if you want it plain. Thirty years gauging these prongs and I've never taken my own start. The day the catch trips clean and the sled runs true, I go down that yellow line before anyone can tell me not to. My notch is wired already. It's the only argument about continuity I've ever won.

choices.text: I hope I see it run.

greet.says: Don't cross the line early. Not superstition — the prongs trip on weight, and the catch doesn't care who you are. You're the second visitor this month, which makes you a festival.

choices.text: Who do you race, with the hall like this?
The last column on the tally is burned away.

column.says: Burned, yes. By the steward before me, who said a record of winners longer than anyone living could remember had stopped being a record and started being an inheritance nobody asked for. I wire a notch every season anyway. Let whoever holds the hall next decide what to burn.

choices.text: The fresh notch — who is it for?

reactions.grief: Nothing in them times the sentence; they repeat the name back like a reading they refuse to log.
reactions.shock: Their eyes go to the far figure at the gallery's end and refuse, for once, to come back.
reactions.bribed: Refuses without heat, as if asked to race on a bent prong — the loss would be theirs, and permanent.
reactions.accused: The gauge slips off the prong before they catch it; the denial comes out too loud, timed for nobody.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands somewhere unguarded, and they spend the next three sentences proving how little it landed.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day from their own log, interval by interval, more piqued at the lost minute than at the question.
reactions.threatened: Behind their face some cold arithmetic prices the threat against what silence has already cost them, and the threat loses.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted with the mismatched entry, they indict the gauge first, the hall second, and their own hand only under protest.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their cadence turns writ-formal for exactly as long as the official is looking, then loosens mid-word.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Through the soles comes a shameful thrill ahead of the fear — the hall, at last, running.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Snaps that they have timed that stride for years — it would never cross early — then hears what the defense concedes.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Gives the refusal in race-official's terms, half-kilometre mark and no further, and hates that the terms still fit.

npc.description: Theaoleinuna Phartusione sits inside the gate's frame with a tension-gauge in both hands, walking the launch prongs one at a time, reading and re-reading. Their work coat is quilted in the slate of the writ, sleeves cuffed back from forearms corded with old gauge-calls, and they speak without turning, timing their sentences to the gauge.

lore.name: The Starting Gate, Still Armed
lore.description: At the head of the gallery stands the race gate: a ceramic frame taller than two people, its launch prongs still holding a racked sled against a catch that has never tripped. The tally-plate bolted to its flank lists winners in columns of notches — Continuant blue wire twisted around each entry — and the last column has been burned off at the metal, deliberately, with a welder's tip. Below the burn, one fresh notch waits, wired and unnamed, for a race that has not been run.

content.name: Stroiomion's Racing Gallery
content.description: Sound arrives wrong here: a footfall on the catwalk makes no second step, the hum of the filament-lathes starting and stopping between one heartbeat and the next as if the gallery drank each noise before it could come back. A kilometre of riveted walkway runs ahead under green-black light, both railings hung with spools of drawn filament stacked three deep where two were meant, sintered ceramic plates lashed over every clear span. Yellow line painted along the left rail, half worn: RACE LINE MARKED IN YELLOW, DO NOT CROSS EARLY. At the far end, small as a pin, someone works and does not look up.

npc.name: Rahab al-Kaiqani
npc.voice: Terse, exact, measures her words the way she measures thread — no more than the work needs. Softens when the work itself is the subject.

decks.says: Old steel keeps its shape and eats the tread. Newer patchwork shifts under load — you learn to leave slack. I could tell you which corridors to trust by the soles I've pulled off. That's more than most can say about anything down here.

greet.says: Shop's done. If you want boots, the Drift sells them. If you want boots made for a deck, you're late by a week.

choices.text: Why close a shop that still has work in it?
What are the small marks under the sizes on those lasts?

marks.says: Hull-script. Each last got walked against the stretch it was cut for — I fit the sole to the deck's wear, not the foot's hope. Walkers knew what they were buying. Nobody else ever looked twice.

why_leave.says: Orders stopped coming before I decided anything. A ward decides it's done with you, and you go. The tools stay — they belong to the room.

choices.text: What are the small marks under the sizes on those lasts?

reactions.grief: She asks what the dead one wore on their feet, then keeps folding the wax cloth wrong.
reactions.shock: Her eyes drop to the walker's soles before the face, a habit that shames her even now.
reactions.bribed: She asks what the silence weighs, then refuses because she would have to re-measure everything she ever said.
reactions.accused: Her arms stay folded back but the upper pair tighten until the apron strap creaks.
reactions.flattered: Praise for the stitching lands deeper than any accusation, and she hates how long she lets it sit.
reactions.questioned: Her answer is a list of fittings, each anchored to whose boots she resoled, and nothing more.
reactions.threatened: She keeps winding waxed thread at the same speed, as if pace were a thing they couldn't touch.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She repeats the false detail once, quieter, then lets it stand because correcting it would cost more.
reactions.authority_arrives: She answers from behind the bench and rates the official's boots first, before any word of theirs counts.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder reaches her feet in a wear-pattern she has never cut for, and she stands very still.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She says the name flat, then cannot stop listing every deck that person never had reason to cross.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She measures the plea like everything else and finds no thread in the shop long enough for it.

npc.description: Rahab al-Kaiqani works with her extra arms folded back and out of the way, packing like someone who has packed before and resents the practice. Her apron is ochre to the chest.

lore.name: The Pairing Rack
lore.description: Every last on the rack carries two burned marks: its size, and a smaller glyph beneath — a route-mark, hull-script, the kind walkers scratch in tunnels to say this way is sound. Rahab sized each last against a stretch of hull she walked, so the boot would know the deck it was born for. No buyer ever asked. She marked them anyway.

content.name: Bootmaking, Close 216
content.description: The stair eats footsteps halfway up — sound arrives dead, then doesn't. Ochre dust over everything: lasts racked in pairs, waxed thread coiled, rope-laid cable hung in measured lengths, none of it cleared away. A stencil over the bins reads LASTS SIZED, DO NOT MIX BINS. At the bench, Rahab al-Kaiqani folds a wax cloth over tools as though the shop will open tomorrow.

npc.name: Ngeaaleaaneth Liokaapoaaneaatonga
npc.voice: Counts people the way others count cups; talks in ration-clauses, warms only when fed a good question.

full.says: The decks above us decided to grow more than the corridors below us decided to carry down, and nobody above or below asked the middle. Four hundred extra bales a cycle. We serve lunch around them. Continuity means the meal happens, not that the room behaves.

choices.text: What's it like, working this close to the gardens themselves?

greet.says: You're standing where the soup line forms, friend, and the soup doesn't wait. Sit anywhere there's a chair under a bale, and mind you don't wake the one by the windows — she had the late shift in the tunnels and I'll not have her disturbed twice.

choices.text: Why is a dining hall being used for storage?
What does TABLE COUNT FIXED, ATTENDANCE VARIES mean?

gardens.says: Once a rotation I carry the tally up past the last service hatch, and the green goes on farther than the hall is long — on and on, beds nobody planted, keeping a schedule nobody wrote. You stop counting rows. You count what you carried in and what you carry back.

choices.text: Who is the woman asleep by the window?

sleeper.says: A grow-deck hand, down here every second night because the bunks ran short and my benches didn't. She keeps her section alive; I keep her fed. That's the whole arithmetic of this hall, and it's older than either of us — the tally-groove in this counter wasn't cut by anyone I served beside.

choices.text: Thank you — I'll let her sleep.

stencil.says: It means the hall was built to a number — nine hundred chairs, one shift, done. The number held. The attendance never did. Whoever cut that stencil meant it as a joke, I think, and then three generations lived it.

choices.text: Why is the room so overfull?

reactions.grief: Her head-count comes back one too many, and she reruns it rather than learn which name the room is missing.
reactions.shock: Stands with the ladle flat against her palm as if it were still good for waking someone.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer aloud in bales and meals before handing it back: a misremembered tally feeds no one.
reactions.accused: Sets the urn down without spilling, then names every seat she served that shift, faster than the accusation.
reactions.flattered: Warms exactly one degree at the praise, then cools, for she has rationed flattery before and knows its weight.
reactions.questioned: Accounts for her movements in ration-clauses, almost glad someone finally asked something countable.
reactions.threatened: Answers the threat by asking which shift it means to spare, her eyes on the sleeper by the windows.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats the figure once, hears it fail against the evidence, and lets the ladle go still mid-pour without correcting anything.
reactions.authority_arrives: The ladle pauses at the urn's lip while she weighs the official against the stencil: table count fixed, attendance varies.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches the urn, then counts the sleepers twice; the schedule nobody wrote never mentioned shudders.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Produces the sleeper's alibi before anyone asks, and its speed confesses she has counted hours all along.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no in plain clauses, then feeds the asker anyway, since refusal and a full cup can share a table.

npc.description: Ngeaaleaaneth Liokaapoaaneaatonga moves down the serving line pouring from a copper urn into quartz cups, waking sleepers with the flat of a ladle and not apologizing, hair pinned back with a length of drawn filament that has clearly done other jobs first.

lore.name: The Tally Quartz
lore.description: The counter is one continuous plate of fused quartz, and worn into its face is a groove — a thumb's width, polished smooth — where the head-count tally has been scratched and re-scratched at the same spot for so long the plate itself carries the record.

content.name: The Span Hall of Second Shift
content.description: The smell reaches you first — steamed chlorophyll and hot quartz, the sweet scorched-sap edge of trays pulled too soon from the grow-tunnels and cooled on the tables themselves. This is a dining span built for nine hundred seats, and bales of filament-spun bedding now fill the aisles between them, three deep in places, so that eaters climb over stores to find a bench. Gantry walkways cross overhead, their rivets green-black with a decade of garden condensation, and down the far length a single head rests on a folded jacket, asleep among trays nobody has cleared. Stencilled along the serving counter, in institutional blue: TABLE COUNT FIXED, ATTENDANCE VARIES.

npc.name: Yioriael al-Aezanione
npc.voice: Quiet, procedural, liturgical — a mender who prays in checklists and speaks of the living as work in progress. She measures with words.

open.says: Nothing broke. That's what the reports won't say and my hands know. The deep has a voice we never learned to hear, and for three months it has been speaking in our own registers — pressure, warmth, sedimented rhythm — like a stranger learning our alphabet before saying what it came to say. The anomaly is not a malfunction. It is a response. Something down there heard us, and is answering.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
Answered by what? That should frighten you.

greet.says: Wipe your feet or don't come further. The occupant doesn't get a second bath if you foul this one.

choices.text: What does the bath actually do?
Who do you answer to, down here?
What was your best piece of work?
The readings changed. Did the ship break, or did something else happen?
Keep your bath. I'll come back.

probe_a.says: It holds. Heat below, stillness above, the way a hand holds a sleeping thing without waking it. Wool takes the cold where it belongs; iron takes the rest. Everything correct, nothing worn in yet — a bath is never truly ready until it has failed once and been forgiven.

probe_b.says: Sol, in the way a candle answers to the sun. And above Sol, a schedule nobody wrote and everybody keeps. Three months ago the schedule stopped matching what the instruments say. I am instructed to trust the instruments. I am instructed to trust the schedule. Both, mind, at once.

probe_c.says: A drain I did not open. There was a bath like this one, older, and the writ said drain and the occupant said otherwise — occupant viable, stencilled where the water had eaten everything but the words. I left it sealed and took the censure. It holds to this day. Restraint is the finest weld there is.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as inventory: she begins listing the dead one's unfinished repairs and cannot stop, nor finish.
reactions.shock: Her hands start their triage before her mind consents — pulse, breath, warmth — on someone past all three.
reactions.bribed: Refuses without anger, as she refuses to chart a temperature she never took, because some readings cannot be edited.
reactions.accused: Denies it in triage order — wound, cause, hand — and only late notices she has been naming her own hands.
reactions.flattered: Treats the praise like a symptom — surface health reporting something wrong beneath — and thanks them with narrowed attention.
reactions.questioned: Answers in inventory — hour, hand, task — as though her movements were ordinated and she merely recites them.
reactions.threatened: Measures the threat as she measures everything — duration, depth, survivability — and reports herself stable with a voice that isn't.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Neither confirms nor recants, only begins auditing her own sentence, syllable by syllable, as though someone else misspoke it.
reactions.authority_arrives: Stands between the official and the bath, unbidden, her posture the stencilled command made flesh: occupant viable, do not drain.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her count stops mid-number, both hands lifting from the water as though the occupant had flinched.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her objection is pure differential diagnosis — what those hands could and could not have done — loyalty dressed as procedure.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her liturgy has no entry for this plea, and she says so without pretending otherwise.

npc.description: Yioriael al-Aezanione stands ankle-deep in the keeping-bath, one hand flat against the iron rim as though counting a pulse too slow to have a number, and does not look up until the second newcomer's shadow crosses the water. The bath is new — spun mineral wool still fluffed, seams unoxidised — and the wrongness of that is the first thing she seems to notice about you.

lore.name: The Sixth Cradle-Gauge
lore.description: Six gauges crown the bath's near stave, five of them reading in the old insulation-script every rindwalker learns before their first shaft. The sixth is unlabeled, its needle swinging in slow, deliberate unison with nothing — and this rebuild is days old, its gauges cast fresh, yet the sixth needle's wear-pattern matches the other five exactly, as if it had already run for the same uncountable span. Yioriael's workshop notes, wedged behind the stave, mark it simply: *fifth reading has an echo now. It did not, before the lower readings changed. It is answering.*

content.name: Keeping-Bath 36
content.description: Yioriael al-Aezanione stands with both hands submerged to the wrist before she sees you, and stops mid-word, leaving her companion's sentence orphaned in the green-black light. The heat here does not sit in the bath but above it — a warmth at brow-height with nothing burning, while the water itself holds a cold so patient it cannot be called cold anymore. The bath is new. Every iron stave straight, every wrapping of spun mineral wool ungreyed, and yet beneath it all a fainter room, sedimented, as though this one had been poured over an older one that declined to leave. Stencilled along the rim, gold on iron: OCCUPANT VIABLE DO NOT DRAIN. The two of them regard you the way one regards weather arriving on schedule.

npc.name: Nochomurara the Twice-Promised
npc.voice: Circulatory diction — everything phrased as passage, weight in transit; asks questions that are really routes.

open.says: Down the axial dark, where the foam-chambers stop looking like weather and start looking like marrow — keep to the cold faces, the ones that do not sweat. Count chambers; when a cell has no door, the next has two, and you take the one the bell would pity. The chamber lies past the third two-doored cell, below the stratum where Saturn stopped signing. I know because I carried a tool back from there once, and it was warm on the side facing home.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll keep to the cold faces.
Why would the bell pity a door?

greet.says: The bell rang before you touched it. Nothing here rings first unless something older than the bell permitted it.

choices.text: What is the bell made of, exactly?
Who do you answer to down here?
What changed in your work lately?
Which way through the Voronoi deep — where?
Keep your hours small. I'm going.

probe_a.says: Cast basalt under mica, and under that, nothing — an absence that rings. Mica lets light through in leaves, like pages nobody wrote. I polish what passes through; the passing itself I leave alone.

probe_b.says: A Drift knot answers to the route, not the ruler — I was promised twice, to two different roads, and both roads turned out to be the same tunnel. So I answer to whoever keeps the tally. Not by name. By keep.

probe_c.says: The stencils. RESPONSE OBSERVED MECHANISM UNKNOWN — that paint is older than my order, and last month it was not facing the door. Something turned the wall. Or the wall was always turned, and we turned.

reactions.grief: The routes fail them mid-sentence, and they stand inside the hush asking nothing, which for them is screaming.
reactions.shock: Sees the body and begins polishing the nearest facet, over and over, worship arriving where words should be.
reactions.bribed: Weighs the offer like freight, refuses it as undeliverable: nothing passes through them the bell has not blessed.
reactions.accused: Goes still as struck glass, then denies it in routes, reciting an itinerary that invents itself as spoken.
reactions.flattered: Examines the praise like a seal on a parcel, finding it intact but addressed to someone they decline to be.
reactions.questioned: Given routine questions, they answer in directions, routing each inquiry down the chambers until the asker forgets what was asked.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands like a toll; they pay it in silence, though one hand finds the mica and stays.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recalculates aloud without shame, bending the lie around the evidence as though contradiction were weather on some road.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their brightness lowers by degrees, the bell's own bow rehearsed in flesh, while they decide which promises count as testimony.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Waits, palm flat, to learn whether the bell rang first — movement without permission frightens them more than any fall.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects by cartography, insisting no such corridor exists — then stops, remembering one that does.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers the only passage they own — directions, counted doors — and watches the plea remain uncarried, heavier for it.

npc.description: Nochomurara the Twice-Promised is standing very still inside the bell's silver hush, palm flat against the layered mica as if counting its slow dissatisfactions, and does not turn until the floor has already told them you arrived. What the room lacks is silence: it dims itself, continuously, out of what can only be called respect.

lore.name: The Tally-Gong's Reverse
lore.description: Behind the bell, its counterweight: a basalt plumb hung in a lattice of mica shims, each shim notched with a mark, and the notches descend in a spiral — a map not of corridors but of refusals, cells sealed in sequence. The last unworn shim points down and axial, along the lean every facet repeats. Whatever charted this chamber mapped the Signal Chamber by what stands closed between here and there.

content.name: The Respect Bell of Small Hours
content.description: Underfoot the basalt is warm where no warmth is piped, cool where the bell's shadow falls — the body files a complaint it cannot phrase, since floor and foot have agreed on a temperature and omitted you. The chamber is defined by absences: no dust, no echo, no second doorway, though the mica walls open into cell after silvered cell, and every facet leans — you see it now — toward one axial dark, the way iron filings lean toward a lodestone buried past finding. The bell itself is dimming: not swung, not struck, merely lowering its own brightness, the gesture of one who bows. Stencilled in a hand gone matte with age: RESPONSE OBSERVED MECHANISM UNKNOWN. Workers move through in numbers no shrine this size was built to hold, and at the far bench, a figure freezes mid-rite — Nochomurara the Twice-Promised, who was promised no one would come.

npc.name: Khaghia al-Tawy
npc.voice: Liturgical cadence worn smooth by doubt; she uses ritual words for machine parts and machine words for holy ones, without noticing the exchange.

copy.says: The stillness. The way the middle holds, neither growing nor dying, while the ends go on without us. Every prayer I was taught is a small person's imitation of that patience. I no longer know if we invented worship or were invented by its example.

after.says: Then it closes, and I go up, and it continues without the indignity of my witness. That is the whole of my office now: to be permitted, briefly, to be unnecessary.

faith.says: Unmade, remade — the mica sheds, the wool is spun again. I only know that when I pray now, I am not asking. I am answering something that asked first, a very long time ago, and has been waiting, and does not mind waiting, and that is the terrible part.

choices.text: Bow, and leave her to the flue.

greet.says: Mind the mouth of it. It rises below, which took me nine years to stop flinching at. You're the one the doors answer. I can tell because the room turned toward you.

choices.text: What broke, that this needs mending?

heart.says: I serve in the gold country, yes. Close enough that my shadow arrives before I do. You'll go further down than that. It already knows the shape of your going — I felt the room practise it while you stood there.

smoke.says: Burn is a word for the short way. The heart does it the long way, and the flue carries the perfume of that — devotion without the expense. We built the rites backward, I think. To copy it. Not to please it.

choices.text: You've stood in the heart's domain?

teams.says: They saw that it was attending to them. Not hostile — attentive, the way a lighthouse attends to a ship it cannot save or harm. Some of them stopped being able to sleep in the middle decks afterward. Something about knowing the floor had opinions.

choices.text: And you? Did it attend to you?

repair.says: Nothing broke. That's what frightens the teams who came down and stopped writing. It opened itself — the way a body shows you where it hurts only when it has decided to be touched. I'm not repairing. I'm accepting.

choices.text: The teams. What did they see?
And after you accept — then what?

reactions.grief: Her grief is not tears; she logs the death to the flue twice, then folds wool that needs no folding.
reactions.shock: She looks away, not from delicacy, but because her eyes keep parsing the wound for liturgy, finding none.
reactions.bribed: Her refusal takes liturgical form: she recites what she witnessed, correctly, in full, before the offer is even withdrawn.
reactions.accused: The accusation finds her mid-litany; she completes it anyway, because somewhere a flue is listening.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands where her doubt already lives; she thanks the flatterer in machine words, torque and tolerance, and means neither.
reactions.questioned: She folds the wool closed before answering, reciting her movements like a psalm she stopped believing decades ago.
reactions.threatened: Something old looks out of her; the threat registers as weather, beneath the dignity of fear or answer.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She does not deny it; she emends the wording, softly, as though the lie were a mistranscribed verse.
reactions.authority_arrives: She rises for the office, not the officer, her bow perfect and her eyes already back on the conduit.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: While others stumble she lays one palm on the conduit, listening, as though the shudder were a breath finally drawn.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Whatever she believes about the named, her silence has the temperature of an argument she declines to hold.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says so plainly, once, then stays anyway, because presence is the only sacrament her hands can still perform.

npc.description: Khaghia al-Tawy is coiling the last of the mineral wool into a carry-frame, working with the unhurried tenderness of someone packing a relic rather than a roll. She talks to the flue before she talks to you — a word, a nod — as if apologising for leaving it half-mended.

lore.name: The Cold Censer
lore.description: A censer of dark gold hangs from no chain, level with no eye, swinging to a wind that does not touch your skin. Its bowl is spotless — never used, never cold, if those were different things.

content.name: Mosaeth
content.description: The flue's mouth sits a hand's width below the floor, a relation no draught could forgive, and through it moves incense that was never burned — violet-scented absence rising from no source. Half the chamber is opened to its own workings: layered mica peeled back like the shed skin of something that had never been young, spun mineral wool unpacked and waiting, and everywhere the missing things — no flame, no ash, no soot, no warmth — arranging themselves more insistently than furniture would. Stencilled along the exposed conduit: SMOKE PRESENT NO COMBUSTION LOGGED. The stillness here is not quiet; it is a held breath three civilisations long, and it notices you noticing.

npc.name: Kevogrim Snati
npc.voice: Terse, unhurried, answers as if the conversation is a task queued behind the current one.

cleat.says: Empty cleats don't collect dues. Fold your own line before you ask about other people's.

greet.says: Family took the big berth's line down themselves. Paid through the month, too. Don't ask me where they moored.

choices.text: They left the sixth cleat empty.

reactions.grief: The fold goes wrong under their hands, first misfold in years, and they ask who found the body.
reactions.shock: Three hands go still; the fourth keeps folding, and they watch it work without wanting it to.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced out loud against what silence costs, and the arithmetic ends the conversation.
reactions.accused: All four hands stop at once, which their hands never do, and they set the graphite down before speaking.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets the same silence an empty cleat gets, and they wait for the request they know is coming.
reactions.questioned: Names the hours back without inflection, eyes on the seam, as if reciting a log kept for exactly this.
reactions.threatened: The voice stays level but the answers shorten to single words, and they do not look up once.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The denial lands a beat late, and they patch it with an unprompted detail about the fold.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the seals on the sleeve, not the face, and the graphite keeps moving while they listen.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder gets no answer until the fold is creased, and then it gets one question about the hull.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their opinion of the named person comes out unprompted and takes longer than any answer they've given all day.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They give the true refusal, then break their own rule by naming which ledger page might hold more.

npc.description: Kevogrim Snati works a graphite stick along a sailcloth seam, marking it fold by fold, and does not look up when the ladder creaks. Their four hands keep four different tensions on the cloth without seeming to consult each other.

lore.name: The Cleat Wall
lore.description: Six copper cleats run along the inner hull, but only five show wear. The sixth is burnished brighter than the rest, polished by hands, and its mooring line is gone — not cut, coiled off and carried. Below it, scratched small: a tally of firsts-of-the-month, ending mid-count. Someone paid their dues on time and left anyway.

content.name: Mooring Housing
content.description: The sun-strip catches every scrubbed seam below deck, and it keeps moving: dust has nowhere to settle before the light finds it. The gap is what registers first — a bed-frame's worth of clean floor where the wall says something stood. A stencil by the ladder reads MOORING DUES POSTED FIRST OF THE MONTH. Sailcloth is folded. Graphite shavings sit in a dish.

npc.name: Chevear Seshixeun
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, the cadence of someone who talks while working and resents having to do either. She warms by degrees, like her coals, and only if asked about the work itself.

pour.says: Sit on the basalt, not the quartz — quartz lies about being warm. There. Barley and rindroot, drawn off the forbidden coals, which is why it tastes better than anything the café sells. You didn't get it from me. Nobody got it from me, ever, in twelve years.

choices.text: "What's it like, working a hall this size alone?"
"Thank you. Even if the corridor never says it."

greet.says: Mind the rake-line. You want service, the café's two decks down and warm all over. This bank feeds a corridor that's never once said thank you.

choices.text: "Forty hearths for an empty corridor. Who lit the first one?"
"Why does the ninth burn hot when the stencil forbids it?"
"Is this Jupiter's hall? It feels like a room built for someone bigger."
"Keep your coals. I'll leave you to it."

ninth.says: The ninth is mine. Twelve years I've drawn it down a hand's width past bank, and every auditor who's caught me has signed the plate and walked on. You draw a fire down too far in cold country and it dies bitter, sullen — you can taste it in the tea. A hearth fed right forgives you things. I'm not saying I'd defy the writ. I'm saying the corridor is cold and I have hands.

choices.text: "Auditors sign it? They don't stop you?"
"Pour me something from that ninth fire, then."

order.says: The writ says continue. Fire says the same thing, only more honestly. Now — you've had your tea and your questions and my coals need turning. Go on. The corridor's cold, and it's a long way to anywhere.

domain.says: Bigger than a hall. Deeper up. You walk the gallery north and the gallery doesn't end, just gets quieter, until the quiet has a weight to it — like a judgment deferred so long it's become architecture. I rake my forty hearths under all of it and I don't ask whose court I'm warming. You learn that early up here: be small, be useful, and the old things let you keep your little fires.

choices.text: "Small and useful. Sounds like a creed."

history.says: Lit before my grandmother's grandmother held a rake, and not by anyone with a face. The plan calls for eight. Somebody built forty and wrote DO NOT DRAW DOWN under them, which is a ruler's sentence if I ever heard one — plenty for a hall where nobody sits, and none of it for the people walking through. My order says keep them banked. So I bank. That's the whole of stewardship: you do the sensible half of somebody else's argument.

choices.text: "And the other half of the argument?"

reactions.grief: The news lands as arithmetic failure: she counts the ninth twice, loses the total, and stands very still.
reactions.shock: Her trade betrays her: she reads the body like a dead hearth, diagnosing what was starved, before her stomach answers.
reactions.bribed: Bribery she understands; what offends her is the coin, and she counters in fuel, silence, and a drawn-down hearth.
reactions.accused: The rake stops mid-settle; she sets it down with exaggerated care before denying anything, twice, in a voice too level.
reactions.flattered: Praise sits on her like heat off quartz: she checks it for the lie before letting it near the work.
reactions.questioned: She answers without lifting the rake, giving her movements as counts — nine hearths, twelve years — as if procedure were proof.
reactions.threatened: Her count falters at six; she resumes it deliberately, quieter, the way one feeds a fire one expects to lose.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Twelve years of denials arrive at once; she over-explains the ninth, citing auditors who signed, watching her story come apart.
reactions.authority_arrives: Before the official clears the door she has drawn the ninth to bank-depth, and her face to match.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Every flame on the bank leans the same way; she reads them like instruments and keeps counting, one number behind.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She stops working to talk — unheard of — and the defense comes out longer and warmer than she ever intended.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says no in the exact words of the writ, then fills a flask from the ninth while saying them.

npc.description: Chevear Seshixeun works the bank's far end with a long quartz rake, turning coals in a rhythm she does not break for arrivals — lift, roll, settle, lift — her lead-grey apron scorched shiny at the knee where she kneels to each fire in turn. She counts under her breath. When she reaches the ninth hearth she pauses longer than the rest, as if listening to it.

lore.name: The Ninth Hearth's Ledger Plate
lore.description: Bolted beside the ninth hearth is a cast-basalt plate, older than the stencil above it, scored with the tally of a hundred years of fuel drawn down: dates in a clerk's neat hand, then dates in cruder ones, then a century of small nicks — one per fire kept alive past regulation. The Continuants rule that a corridor hearth exists for the corridor. Somebody down the generations has ruled back, quietly, one nick at a time, that a hearth exists for whoever stops beside it. The plate does not say who won. It only shows the argument still running.

content.name: The Hearth Corridor
content.description: Light leaves this room in a hurry. It pools along the basalt hearth-bank, then slides up walls of fused quartz and is gone down the corridor, so the glow reads as motion rather than warmth — a tide being spent faster than it can gather. The bank itself runs longer than any tea-house's need: forty hearths at a stretch, each laid, lit, and banked to a hand's depth of ember. Above the eighth, a stencil: HEARTH BANKED FOR CORRIDOR, DO NOT DRAW DOWN. Someone has drawn down the ninth anyway. It is the warmest place in the corridor and it is never allowed to be.

npc.name: Zatlinatl Flareborn
npc.voice: Barker's rhythm, short and countable, jokes without pausing the work.

greet.says: Three shows. First bell, middle, late. You're early for all three, so pick a seat or pick up a rag.

shift.says: The troupe's. They finished the run and moved on; I hold the shows till someone takes the cord. Front row's yours if you want it — I have a stage to wipe before first bell.

reactions.grief: They thank the teller, then lose their count and start the tally over from one.
reactions.shock: They go to the rag and bucket and wipe a stretch of boards nowhere near the blood.
reactions.bribed: They quote a ticket price instead, a real one, and slide the offered coin back across the boards uncounted.
reactions.accused: Stops counting mid-number, and the missing number sits in their mouth a long second before the laugh comes.
reactions.flattered: The joke arrives before the thanks does, and neither lands; they watch the flatterer's hands, not the compliment.
reactions.questioned: Answers in show counts — first bell, middle, late — and chalks a fourth tally to the rail before the asker finishes.
reactions.threatened: Their hand finds the barker's whistle and does not blow it; they name the next show time instead, twice.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The patter runs dry mid-sentence; they set down the rag and finish the sentence anyway, slower, committed to it.
reactions.authority_arrives: They announce the official like a ticketholder — latecomers stand — and keep wiping while the room decides what to obey.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The chains swing and they count the swings aloud, four, five, because counting is the only hand they trust.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They recite every show that person played on time, too many shows, proving they were counting longer than anyone asked.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say so plainly, once, then offer what the booth holds: a front-row seat for however long it lasts.

npc.description: Zatlinatl Flareborn hangs chain links onto a puppet's control bar, testing each against a tug, counting under their breath. A barker's whistle hangs at their collar. They wipe the stage edge between counts and do not look up.

lore.name: The tour cord
lore.description: A knotted cord hangs by the stage rail, one knot for every stop the show made before this one; the last knot is old and fraying.

content.name: The Puppet Booth
content.description: A grinning puppet hangs mid-gesture, chains taut, going nowhere; a rag and bucket wait on the boards, still wet. Nobody struck the set. The Puppet Booth is bamboo lashed at every joint, painted bright white, stenciled along the rail: THREE SHOWS NIGHTLY, LATECOMERS STAND.

npc.name: Musi-Ralald
npc.voice: Terse. Talks in weights, destinations, counts. Answers only what is asked.

lift.says: It runs when I say. Today it doesn't. Cargo's still owed from the market side. Come back after the dim.

greet.says: Hold on. Counting. Forty up, thirty back, all day. Ask fast.

reactions.grief: The count stops mid-number and she picks at a grey knot on her wrist until it gives.
reactions.shock: She keeps counting aloud, wrong numbers, while the hand on the brake shakes against the frame.
reactions.bribed: She converts the offer into loads owed and tells them it doesn't cover the count.
reactions.accused: She lets the load drop a foot before catching it, then names the exact tonnage she moved that day.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets weighed like a suspect load, and she says nothing until the real request comes.
reactions.questioned: She gives the hour, the load, the destination, and nothing past them, hand flat on the brake.
reactions.threatened: She quotes the posted load limit as if it covers this too, and her voice almost holds.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Mid-count she loses the number and starts the day's tally over from zero, quieter.
reactions.authority_arrives: She volunteers the day's totals unprompted, which she does for no one else, eyes on the posted plate.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She throws her whole weight on the brake and keeps calling numbers, because the load is all she can hold.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She recites the accused's haul weights from memory, finds them two loads short of the day, and stops there.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She refuses in plain weights, then offers the next lift down, which is everything she has.

npc.description: Musi-Ralald stands braced against the winch frame, one hand on the brake, eyes on the shaft. She wears cyan cord at both wrists, old and grey at the knots. She counts loads aloud and does not look over.

lore.name: Knotted brake cord
lore.description: The brake lever wears a Drift wrist-cord, knotted through the housing so the lever can't be pulled past half. Someone tied it there a long time ago. The knots record a route nobody here has walked.

content.name: The Winch Room
content.description: Rope grease and cut cane, sweet under the ship smell. The freight lift hangs mid-shaft, loaded, going nowhere. A stencilled plate reads MAX LOAD POSTED, DO NOT EXCEED. Bamboo scaffolding crowds the platform. The winch handle still turns. Musi-Ralald works the brake lever, counting under her breath.

npc.name: Laitikhad-al-Mar
npc.voice: Short sentences. Prices first, names never. They correct wrong amounts before you finish saying them.

done.says: Window closes at dim. Don't come after.

greet.says: Buy or sell? I'm covering this window, not assigned to it, so the faster you decide the better for both of us.

rates.says: Built for a person they let go before my time. We adapted. Rates are on the wall, and tomorrow's is already up. Now — buy or sell?

trade.says: Good. Hand it through, flat, and don't fold the large notes. Next in line, step up while they count.

reactions.grief: Stops mid-count and touches the knotted cord, saying the one name their creed forbids.
reactions.shock: Keeps flicking bills through hands that no longer register them, posting three wrong totals before anyone notices.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against a day's take and says the gap aloud, which is neither yes nor no.
reactions.accused: The thumb stops on a bill mid-flick, and they correct the accuser's arithmetic to take the moment back.
reactions.flattered: Asks what the flattery is meant to buy, having heard this exact opening from better customers.
reactions.questioned: Answers in ledger terms, giving times and totals as if the question were an audit they have already passed.
reactions.threatened: Glances at the queue behind the threat, because closing this window costs more than the threat does.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recalculates aloud, twice, then amends the figure without ever calling the first number a lie.
reactions.authority_arrives: Turns scrupulously procedural, announcing posted rates from the wall to anyone in reach, overcorrecting on purpose.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their first thought is the rate board, their second the knotted cord, and the queue arrives last.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Lists the accused's debts from memory, which sounds like defense and is only inventory, and knows it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses in rate language, naming what the plea would cost, and keeps their eyes on the queue's middle distance.

npc.description: Laitikhad-al-Mar counts scrip at speed, thumb flicking each bill past without looking down. A knotted cord circles one wrist; the knot pattern is long and changes in the middle, the mark of a route cut short. Their eyes stay on the queue, which does not stop growing.

lore.name: the step-pallet
lore.description: The pallet under the clerk's feet is worn in two heel-shaped hollows, positioned for the counter's height. It predates the cyan paint; a dried paint line runs across its topside where it was set aside during the last coat. This window has been too tall for whoever works it longer than the paint has held.

content.name: Court 20 Fore
content.description: The counter sits at the wrong height, chest-level, so clerks have taken to standing on a bamboo pallet to work it. The queue doubles back on itself past the canvas-webbing rail. Cyan paint covers everything, fresh over old. Stenciled above the window: SCRIP RATES POSTED DAILY. Someone has crossed out today's and pinned tomorrow's beside it.

npc.name: Sendbrand the Ever-Starving
npc.voice: Short sentences, freight-yard cadence. Counts things when he talks — loads, trips, days. Warms up when asked about the work itself, not the gossip.

next.says: Somebody from the yards. They'll learn the drum like I did, or they'll crack a counterweight in a month. Either way the lift stays. Lifts outlast keepers. That's the whole arrangement.

choices.text: Then the room's in good hands.

work.says: Nineteen years on this winch. I know the load by the sound of the drum before I see it. Turf rides quiet. Lead sings. You get so you can tell a full run from a short one with your eyes shut.

choices.text: Nineteen years. I won't keep you.

empty.says: A press. Cast lead, four hundred kilos if it was an ounce. Took eleven trips on the counterweight alone. Bound for the turf yards below — they're laying new beds. Room looks wrong without it, don't it.

choices.text: Where do the turf yards send it after?

greet.says: Lift's cold. I mean to be gone before it matters. You wanting passage down or just standing there?

choices.text: What left here? The platform looks bare.

weight.says: Hammered lead carries its own note up the rope. That's why the plate on the platform matters — you tare the deck before you trust your ear. Every keeper here has kept that plate stamped. I'll not be the one who let it slide.

choices.text: Who keeps the winch after you?

reactions.grief: For the rest of the day he counts nothing — the man who counts everything, sitting with a rope going nowhere.
reactions.shock: He backs against the lift frame and reads the counterweight stencil aloud, twice, as if it might hold him up.
reactions.bribed: His eyes stay on the offered coin one beat too long before he quotes the posted load and refuses.
reactions.accused: Nothing comes out of him at first — the rope hangs half-coiled and his mouth keeps missing the count.
reactions.flattered: Praise pulls him in — he's three sentences deep into the drum's temperament before he hears the hook and stops mid-word.
reactions.questioned: Routine questions get the usual counts — trips, tonnage, hour — and none of the part about where he was headed.
reactions.threatened: He asks how heavy they mean to be, then returns to coiling, each coil counted out loud.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Asked to repeat the trip count, he does, and it comes out one short of the first telling.
reactions.authority_arrives: Down and latched — he gives the lever's position before his own name and waits by the drum.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He listens the way he listens to the drum, then says it plain — that shudder carried no load.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He lays out the yard man's week load by load — day, weight, trip — and stands on it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He counts what the winch can move and what it can't, then says the second number out loud.

npc.description: Sendbrand the Ever-Starving sits on an upturned turf crate by the winch house door, eating the last of a roll and coiling rope at the same time. A canvas sack of tools stands packed and buckled beside him. The winch brake lever is down, the drum latched.

lore.name: The Tared Platform
lore.description: The lift platform has a brass plate bolted at its edge, worn smooth at one corner where a gloved thumb rests. It lists the platform's own weight to the half-kilo, recalculated and re-stamped eleven times. The last stamp is two months old. Below it, an older line reads what the platform weighed before its deck boards were replaced — heavier by nine kilos, and someone has scratched 'good riddance' beside the figure.

content.name: The Winch Room, Stack 203
content.description: The cold sits low, ankle-height, pooling in the lift shaft's mouth while the rest of the room stays warm from the winch house stove. A rope-and-pulley freight lift hangs open at the landing, its platform swept clean. The ochre paint on the frame is fresh where it chipped. Stencilled on the counterweight: MAX LOAD POSTED, DO NOT EXCEED.

npc.name: Orlornar-Loraris
npc.voice: Clipped, unornamented, spoken to the work rather than to you. A mender's grammar: things are sound or unsound, and most of what people say is unsound.

mars.says: Once. One spar of the hull-work, a season's contract. You stand on plating that was joined before your grandmothers' grandmothers and the join is finer than anything we can make, and the iron remembers the hand that made it. It changes how you tamp a wall, knowing that.

choices.text: Thank them, and step back from the deck-edge.

work.says: A sleeper turns. Twelve times a night, some of them — the old ones, the ones who dream loud. Graphite drinks the sound before it wakes them. You don't put a person in a wall and let the wall talk back.

choices.text: You've done this a long time.

greet.says: Mind the open deck-edge. This stack's half gutted and the plates don't care whose foot they take. Talk or move on — the packing sets while you stand.

choices.text: Why pack graphite behind a sleeping shelf?
How long has this stack been standing?
Where do the berthed go while half their home is open to the shaft?

scale.says: Older than the chalk numbers, older than the stencil, likely older than the counting of it. I re-inspect. I don't date. Mars's welds hold; that's the whole of what I need from down-time.

choices.text: You speak of Mars plainly. You've been in the deep weld-halls?

end_warm.says: Hm. Come back when the stack's closed and I'll show you a finished wall. It sleeps well — I've heard it.

choices.text: Step away and let the packing set.

residents.says: Camped with kin on the green side, or berthed in the lower stacks, or sleeping where they can. The open half stays open because the frame beneath was failing quiet — quiet as the packing, see. We caught it by count, not by noise. That's how it goes wrong up here: it doesn't creak, it just stops matching the tally.

choices.text: And when the count stops matching something bigger?

reactions.grief: The tam lands crooked, then crooked again; they keep feeding graphite into a wall already full.
reactions.shock: Somewhere behind the eyes the mender's grammar fails; the body before them is unsound past any join they can name.
reactions.bribed: The offer is weighed honestly, which is more than it deserves, and set down with the rest of the scrap.
reactions.accused: All four arms stop for the first time; an unsound word in the cavity outweighs an unsound join.
reactions.flattered: It lands, the praise, somewhere the work never gets touched, and they tamp twice more before trusting their voice.
reactions.questioned: Answers arrive in the order the arms finish strokes; each word is judged sound before it is spent.
reactions.threatened: The threat is weighed like a load rating, found under tolerance, and answered at the ram's own pace.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The story comes out again unchanged, tamped a second time rather than cut out and made honest.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official is sized like any opening, load and seal, and the ram holds its tempo by decision, not nerve.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The sound arrives without a name; every join they ever packed revises itself, and none of them explains it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They say the named one's joins hold better than theirs, hear how far that reaches, and leave it standing.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What they give instead is a palmful of graphite, wrong tool and only tool, pressed into the pleading hands.

npc.description: Orlornar-Loraris stands half inside an opened berth wall, feeding graphite packing into the cavity by the flat of their palm, tamping it in strokes as even as breathing. They wear four arms the way a scaffold wears bolts — not one of them idle — and they do not turn around when you arrive.

lore.name: The counted spars
lore.description: Each berth is numbered by its spar, and the chalk tallies beside them run into five figures — re-inspections, per spar, per year, more counts than any resident could sleep through in a lifetime.

content.name: The Berth Warren
content.description: The light arrives late, folded twice by the sky arc before it reaches these depths, so the whole warren keeps the colour of a photograph left in a drawer — silver over everything, even the dust. Twelve decks of berths rise in a lacelike stack of black glass walls, each pane load-rated past any weight the Nave could put on it, and half of them stand open to the shaft like pulled teeth. Down one opened aisle, packed graphite packs the cavity behind a sleeping shelf, deadening sound for a sleeper nobody can yet see. Stencilled along a spar that runs the whole stack's height: BERTH ASSIGNMENTS POSTED BY SPAR NUMBER, letters a hand tall, holding.

npc.name: Zhayam Vyaksky
npc.voice: Terse, preoccupied, words chosen for a logic you are not party to — she names things by what they refuse, not what they are.

greet.says: It let you in. That's its business, not mine. Take the count — I'm owed sleep, and the sill doesn't tally itself.

reactions.grief: She loses count mid-number — the one arithmetic she cannot do — and stands, taking her exhaustion out into the corridor.
reactions.shock: She reads the body like her sill reads entrants, then stops — what it refuses to be has no number.
reactions.bribed: Nothing in the offer is heavier than her ledger; she declines without heat, because stasis is outwaited, never moved.
reactions.accused: Accused, she repeats the count once, slower, knuckles whitening around the obsolete tool she never puts down.
reactions.flattered: Praise settles on her like the room's dust, of which there is none; she waits for the want beneath it.
reactions.questioned: She recites her count flatly, movements rendered as arithmetic, because a sill-keeper's days tally easier than they explain.
reactions.threatened: Inside her something old and patient resolves to outlast the threat, the way iron outlasts whoever leans on it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her count falters; she stares at the evidence as though the room has finally accumulated something against her.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction outranks dwell; she yields the sill's edge without a word, reserving every number for herself.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder passes; what holds her is the rhythm below, which has not continued in years and now, briefly, does.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The named one gets defended in refusals — too fast, too complete, a familiarity she has never once admitted to.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea finds the one hinge her office refuses to own; she says so, then stays anyway, counting alongside.

npc.description: Zhayam Vyaksky sleeps sitting upright against the iron, hands still curled around a tool nobody uses anymore, her face carrying the particular exhaustion of someone the room refuses to let age. She wakes the instant you cross the sill, mid-breath, already speaking.

lore.name: A tally-slate fused to the sill's underside
lore.description: A sliver of black glass, its face scratched with Saturn's tale-count in notation older than the walls — someone counted here, and the count has not been resumed.

content.name: Recognising-Sill 52
content.description: The smell arrives first: cold ozone braided with something sweeter, like violets pressed under iron — the exhalation of stasis doing its arithmetic. The sill itself is a seam of black glass let into iron, violet-lit from no source, admitting only what it deems itself akin to; you feel read, briefly, and passed. Everything here is unworn — no scuff, no handmark, as if the room declines to accumulate evidence — while the stencil overhead, PRESENT YOURSELF AND WAIT TO BE KNOWN, has outlasted whoever painted it. Somewhere below, a rhythm continues that stopped long ago.

npc.name: Navithjeath Kiorany
npc.voice: Terse, practical, rindwalker to the marrow — she speaks of the recess the way a mender speaks of a joint that holds: with respect, with familiarity, and without once asking why it holds.

greet.says: You're standing in the cold half. There isn't one, but stand there and you'll find it. I'm covering Anselm's shift — he's been called down. Plate wants touching before I go off-cycle. That's all this is.

greet_2.says: It remembers you now. Don't ask me how a room remembers; I stopped filing that question years ago. Anselm won't be back. The recess keeps the warmth constant anyway. That's the whole of it — the ship does not need us to stay. It just lets us.

reactions.grief: She loses her count for the first time in years, sill twice, plate forgotten entirely.
reactions.shock: The numbers on her lips continue without her, a liturgy recited by a body already elsewhere.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets the same silence she gives a stripped bolt, assessment first, refusal without ceremony.
reactions.accused: She stops mid-check, thumb flat against the plate, and makes them repeat the word they used.
reactions.flattered: Praise runs off her like condensate off mica; she credits the room and names nobody, herself least of all.
reactions.questioned: Her answers come in maintenance cadence, sill to strata to plate, and figures the schedule never held.
reactions.threatened: She answers that she has mended worse, meaning joints, not men, and lets the ambiguity stand.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She does not amend the figure; she gives it once more, mender-exact, as if precision were proof.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction, in her experience, checks nothing twice; she recites her rounds before it can ask.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder files the question she swore off years ago; she hears herself ask the room aloud.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The accusation meets a mender's audit; the accused's hands, she notes, never learned the sill.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She cannot mend it and says so flat, then yields the warmer end of her watch anyway.

npc.description: A broad woman in copper-patched insulwear two sizes too warm for the room, working through a maintenance schedule held on a slate she consults without reading. Her hands move through the recess's checks in an order that has become liturgy — sill, strata, plate, sill again — and her lips shape numbers between them that the schedule does not contain. She has the settled stillness of someone who has stopped expecting the room to make sense and has begun, instead, to make sense to the room.

lore.name: The Concurrence Plate
lore.description: Set into the recess's lowest mica layer, a plate of black glass fused to the wall — fused, not fastened, its edges continuous with the strata around it as though the wall grew it. Its face carries a single groove, worn smooth at the center where generations of thumbs have pressed it, and beneath the groove a notation in the oldest layer's hand: two marks joined, then a line, then two marks joined again. Rindwalkers who pass here touch it going in and coming out. The groove is warm. It is the only thing in the room that is warm to the touch rather than warm to the sense — as though the heat had decided, long ago, where it preferred to live.

content.name: Warm-Recess 19
content.description: The sill of the recess sits a hand's height below the floor beside it, as though the room had knelt and forgotten to rise. Layered mica flakes the walls into a thousand green-black leaves, each one holding a warmth the air does not explain, and the black glass floor gives back no reflection at all — only a suggestion of gold, far down, like the memory of a sun kept out of kindness. Someone has painted OCCUPANCY UNRECORDED WARMTH CONSTANT across the oldest stratum, in a hand that knew the mica would outlive the paint. The recess does not cool. It has never cooled. Two bedrolls lie at opposite ends, neither touching the other's ground.

npc.name: Mezeiruna Voidbreaker
npc.voice: Fast, transactional, allergic to ceremony; drift-speak runs on rates, weights, and what moves.

cord.says: Vasek's cord. He got to the fourth knot and walked out mid-pattern, which no Drifter does. I don't finish another's knots and I don't cut them. The crate sits. It's load-rated anyway.

cord2.says: Eleven months? It used to. Now I figure the ship kept what it wanted and left the rest. Around here that's almost courtesy.

greet.says: You're standing on my weighing floor. Everything here is sealed, priced by mass, and honest about neither. What do you carry, and how fast does it need to be someone else's?

choices.text: Someone left a tally-cord on that crate.
This whole span hums. Whose is it?

stock.says: Mineral wool, salt, parts of parts. You buy the mass and the assurance the seal was never broken — and if it was, that's the stencil's problem, not mine. Certainty costs extra.

mercury.says: Ours to use, hers to own. I've walked the artery proper once — you could drop the Nave into one junction and lose it. You learn to stop looking up, or you stop working. I kept working.

reactions.grief: The name gets said once; after that she invents errands whose only route runs past Vasek's unfinished cord.
reactions.shock: The count leaves her mid-number; she stands holding the crate and cannot remember where crates go.
reactions.bribed: The bribe gets priced aloud, mass and market rate both, before she refuses it, so her no has a figure.
reactions.accused: She asks them to put the charge on the beam scale, voice level, though she calls no weight this time.
reactions.flattered: Praise slides off her like a misdeclared manifest; she wants to know what it weighs and who declared it.
reactions.questioned: Her answer takes the form of crate numbers and hour-marks, because her movements have always been a manifest.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands the way a miscounted crate does: she keeps working, but the next seal comes down crooked.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The correction dies behind her teeth; she offers a new figure instead, lower, as if honesty came in degrees.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets what no customer gets — a full beat of her eyes — before her rates return, flatter than usual.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She ignores the shudder until the hanging crates swing out of rank; then she counts them, lips moving, eyes down.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She argues the charge in ledger terms — hours, masses, habits — then hears herself and stops before the third reason.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No leaves her mouth before the plea finishes; what follows, quieter, is which pier holds the one who can.

npc.description: Mezeiruna Voidbreaker works a pediment-scale sealing press with the ease of someone closing a jar, weighing each crate on a beam scale older than the floor it stands on, calling weights aloud to nobody. She does not look up until your second step lands inside her floor.

lore.name: The Interrupted Cord
lore.description: Halfway down one crate runs a Drift tally-cord, knotted to the fourth route and abandoned mid-pattern — someone started certifying this seal and never finished, and Mezeiruna has left the cord exactly where it stopped for eleven months.

content.name: Span 11 Inboard
content.description: Sound arrives here already tallied: the artery-hum overhead is caught by wool-packed baffles and returned as a beat, so a whisper walks the span twice before it dies. Chandeliers of crated goods hang from cable in ranks, each crate sealed and unopened — the whole stock sells by weight and promise, never by sight. Bricks of salt and bolts of mineral wool line the aisles between buttresses of plating a hand could not reach around. On the nearest pier, stencilled in flaked pigment: SEALS BROKEN AT BUYER'S OWN RISK.

npc.name: Fynend-Lalfnagl
npc.voice: Blunt, exacting, proud of what holds and contemptuous of anything that doesn't; speaks in weights and tolerances.

mars.says: I've walked the welding floors proper — seen the seams that run a continent's length, laid by something that doesn't know my name and doesn't need to. You work under that long enough, you get religious or you get honest. I got honest. The tension's logged hourly, and He holds the rest.

work.says: Tension. Hourly, like the wall says — you log it or the strand logs you. Gauge's frozen past red since before I drew this shift, and Mars's welds upstream hold anyway. That's the whole sermon: what holds, holds.

greet.says: Foundry's cold, shift's dead, and you're standing where the strand would fall. Talk fast or step back. That drum holds more tension than your whole biography.

stopped.says: Order came down to stand fast, and we stood. Nobody cleared the benches because nobody told us it was finished — and in the rind you don't walk off a job the hull hasn't signed off on. So we wait, and the nickel waits better.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as inventory: she lists the dead man's lift ratings aloud, hourly figures, because the alternative is his face.
reactions.shock: One look is all she manages; the gauge ticks in her hand through a range she does not record.
reactions.bribed: The bribe gets quoted back in tonnage, so the buyer hears what little it weighs: nothing she'd log.
reactions.accused: The charge she makes them repeat word by word, like a suspect weld, and the flaw turns up in them.
