reactions.flattered: Oil off annealed nickel, the praise slides from her; she waits, unsurprised, for the weight the compliment exists to shift.
reactions.questioned: She recites her movements like a tension log, hourly entries, and dares the questioner to find a gap.
reactions.threatened: Threats weigh less than she does; having stood beneath falling loads, she names, flatly, what his hold is rated to.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she does the one honest thing left and restates the true figure, quieter, hating that her voice reads light.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets her eyes and her log and nothing warmer, jurisdiction being just another gauge with a worse record.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder reaches her first; her thumb finds the strand's hum and reads doubt where her creed promised none.
reactions.someone_else_accused: His welds she vouches for before thinking, and the vouch becomes a load she must stand under.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea exceeds her tolerances and she says so plainly, then stays anyway, since leaving would be a failure too.

npc.description: She stands dwarfed at the drum's base with a hand-lens on a chain around her neck, and she has dressed for the scale of the place: goggles worn up like a crown, boots with soles rebuilt twice, a harness slung loose because she no longer trusts it to matter.

lore.name: The Tension Gauge
lore.description: A brass gauge fused to the base of the last spool, its needle frozen past the red, its dial scratched with hundreds of tiny tally-marks in a hand that stopped mid-stroke.

content.name: The Cable Foundry of Second Shift
content.description: Fynend-Lalfnagl does not startle; she sets down her gauge with the care of someone who has learned that everything here outweighs her opinion, and turns. The light finds her first — gold off the annealed nickel, thrown upward in bars that climb a spool the height of a town's church and keep climbing, each drum wound with rigging thick as a torso, a single strand of which took, she will tell you, eleven men and a winch to bend. No one cleared the benches when the work stopped; the stencil overhead, SPOOL TENSION LOGGED HOURLY, has outlived its loggers.

npc.name: Zeka Zezhyavsky
npc.voice: Measured, exact, the cadence of inventory — devotion expressed as precise counts and honest tallies.

open.says: I have handled the sealing surface. Ran a thumb along it, catalogued its wear, matched its corrosion against the oldest layer on the walls. Here is what no one who made that seal could have known: the layer beneath it is older. Whatever closed that chamber did not seal it first — it sealed something already sealed, and badly, the way you patch over a crack you do not understand. The true closure predates the seal-makers entire. They were not locking a door. They were forgetting one that had been locked before there was anyone on this ship to lock it.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry that carefully.
Sealed twice. That means something got out.

greet.says: Stand off the rim. The floor takes impressions and I am the one who has to read them.

choices.text: Your counts don't settle — does anyone care?
What sealed the chamber — and how old is the seal?

probe_a.says: Accrual. The basin gathers grains no source admits to sending. My creed says storage is testimony — what a room keeps, it says. This room has been saying something for years and the number will not settle.

probe_b.says: A route-walker who came down on a seal-check and sat against the glass and did not get up. Thermally wrong in here — cold in the wrong places, warm in others. I let him be. Saturn's deep keeps stranger guests, and none of them explain themselves either.

probe_c.says: The Continuants want a report they can file. The walkers want a route. I answer to the room itself, or I try to. Good work is keeping faith with what holds, and lately the room has been holding more than it was built to. Busier than its spec. Nothing down here gets busier without a reason.

reactions.grief: She begins cataloguing what the dead one stored — habits, debts, small keepsakes — and cannot make herself stop.
reactions.shock: The floor is taking her impression right now, and for once she is the entry she cannot read.
reactions.bribed: She quotes the bribe back as a figure, entered nowhere, and asks what testimony it is meant to overwrite.
reactions.accused: Both hands go to the balance as if it might testify for her; her creed forbids false denials too.
reactions.flattered: Praise arrives like the basin's grains, from no source she can verify, and she trusts it exactly as much.
reactions.questioned: Her hours come out as ledger entries, exact to the grain, and she volunteers a count nobody requested.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets entered verbatim, word for word, filed where her creed keeps everything a room has said.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she corrects the figure aloud instead of the lie, as if accuracy could retroactively sanctify what she said.
reactions.authority_arrives: She angles the lamp a degree further from the sleeper before turning to render the official her full inventory.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Grains shift in the basin and she counts the new arrivals before permitting herself to breathe.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her objection arrives as evidence — a corrosion date, a wear-pattern — and sounds, to her own ears, like begging.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says plainly what she cannot do, then stays anyway, because honest insufficiency is still a tally owed.

npc.description: Zeka Zezhyavsky is stooped over the basin's violet rim, weighing grains of accrual on a silver balance whose pans are black glass, and refusing to write down the number. Beside her, on the seamless floor, a man sleeps where no one is meant to sleep — and she has angled her lamp so its light does not reach him.

lore.name: The Counter-Ring Beneath the Hoard
lore.description: Part the grains and the basin's floor is a fused ring of black glass, its face engraved with tally-marks in the oldest wall-notation—and beneath that notation, half-erased as if the glass itself tried to digest it, a second script no rindwalker has catalogued. The ring was meant as a seal: someone countable, someone with names, closed this chamber and notched the tally to prove a date. But the under-script passes beneath the ring and continues into the basin's wall uninterrupted, meaning the chamber was already sealed when the seal-makers came, and they built their lock over a door that had been shut for longer than their word for 'shut' had existed.

content.name: Accumulating-Basin 49
content.description: The grain-fall has stopped. Not paused—stopped, mid-air above Accumulating-Basin 49, a sparse constellation of dust hanging as if the room forgot to finish a sentence it began before the Nave had a name. The silver lip of the basin runs violet under light that arrives without a source, and the black glass floor gives back a cold the skin reads as depth rather than temperature. Where the wall should meet the floor there is only a continuous turning, like the inside of a closed mouth. In the basin's shallow hoard lies Zeka Zezhyavsky, asleep on Saturn's account-books, breathing in a rhythm too slow to belong to the living.

npc.name: Nichatl-Qikoatl
npc.voice: Terse, work-focused. Sentences come between tasks, not during them.

room.says: Home. Six of us behind these sheets, and the crates hold what the last three crews left. It stretches when it has to. Don't touch the stencil sheet, that's load-bearing, in a manner of speaking.

greet.says: Mind the cord on the floor. That's the stall count, not scrap. You want something or you want to watch me work?

reactions.grief: Twice, out loud, she counts the stalls behind her before the knife moves again.
reactions.shock: One look is enough, and she plants herself between it and the nearest stall, bare feet finding the beaded cord.
reactions.bribed: No glance at the goods: she says her remembering is load-bearing too and asks them to step around her.
reactions.accused: She stands, which she never does, and the cord slips off her wrist.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets nothing out of her, but the request folded inside it takes her eyes off the knot.
reactions.questioned: She accounts for her day in joints tied, not hours, and ties through the whole answer.
reactions.threatened: She hears the threat out, eyes on the knot, then asks whether it covers the six behind the sheets.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she doesn't retract but adds a second story with more detail than the first, hands still tying the whole time.
reactions.authority_arrives: The pole goes down flat when the official enters, which is as much standing as she gives anyone with papers.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Bare feet read it first, and she has a hand flat on the load-bearing sheet before anyone speaks.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her testimony is that the accused can't tie a knot that holds, delivered without looking up.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The refusal takes fewer words than the plea did, and a finished pole turns up later where the asker sleeps.

npc.description: Nichatl-Qikoatl works barefoot, cord wrapped twice around one wrist, the knot pattern dense with years. She cuts a bamboo joint, fits it, ties it, and starts the next one without standing.

lore.name: The Tally Cord
lore.description: A knotted cord strung along one sheet-edge, a knot for each person who has slept in this stall. The oldest knots are stiff and dark with handling.

content.name: The Sheet Stall
content.description: Nichatl-Qikoatl kneels in the aisle with a bamboo pole across her knees, and you have to step around her. The floor is layered: woven mat, then cardboard, then a strip of beaded cord she pushes aside with her foot without looking. Sheets hang everywhere, teal, dividing the loft into stalls no wider than a bed. Painted on the nearest sheet, in flaking stencil: THE SHEET IS THE WALL, RESPECT IT.

npc.name: Dyavryezes Dasvosok
npc.voice: Sparse, liturgical, the cadence of someone who counts by touch and distrusts the spoken number.

open.says: The chamber sealed itself, and before there were seal-makers — I have handled the closure, laid my palm flat against it, and the material is younger than the wall it sits in and older than the ship's oldest notation, which is impossible, and I have stopped expecting the impossible to apologise. The seal-makers who came after carved their glyphs into it like men signing another's testament and calling it authorship. What shut it was not a keeping-out. It was a keeping-quiet — the way a mouth closes around a word it has decided, finally, not to say. The stencilled warning on our own sill, DO NOT COUNT THE CELLS ALOUD, is a child's copy of that older discretion.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry this carefully.
A seal older than its makers. That shouldn't be.

greet.says: Mind the third sill. It remembers being stepped on and resents new feet.

choices.text: What is the foil wound around?
Half your cells are opened. Who ordered that?
Do you ever resent working unseen?
The sealed chamber in the deep — what shut it, and when?
I'll leave you to the quiet.

probe_a.says: Nothing, if you ask the foil. It winds itself around a tendency — a habit of the current, older than any spool we stock. We merely keep the wound from unravelling in the wrong direction.

probe_b.says: No one. The openings arrive like weather. Saturn's domain does not take orders; it sheds its casing the way you shed sleep, and my task is to be present when it does, and to say nothing.

probe_c.says: Resentment is a counting-word. Down here we are counted by what persists, not by who applauds. The Foolighter — the machine, not the god; I am careful with that distinction — has outlasted every name I could give it, and it has never once praised me. That is the only honesty I have ever been shown.

reactions.grief: They finish the seam before letting the name in, then say it once, quietly, like a number they regret.
reactions.shock: Shock walks them backwards into an open cell, where they stand kept quiet, in the oldest sense of kept.
reactions.bribed: They weigh the offered thing in one palm and give it back, having found it younger than its story.
reactions.accused: The pane slips under palms that have never let it slip, and the denial comes out of them already counting.
reactions.flattered: Praise counts too high; they hear the arithmetic of want in it and keep both palms on the quartz.
reactions.questioned: Their account comes in the order the hands remember, each hour pressed flat, never once counted aloud.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets no argument; they set one palm flat on the third sill, which remembers worse feet.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they do not retract but re-bless the lie, smoothing foil over it as though winding could reverse.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction is met the way they meet withholding light — bowed head, lowered eyes, hands that never stop.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the room moves, they read the shudder through their palms and find it honest, if unexplained.
reactions.someone_else_accused: That particular name draws an answer too fast for their creed, a certainty touch has never once earned.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What is asked exceeds every seal they tend, a fact they confess plainly before staying, palm flat on the plea.

npc.description: Light behaves strangely in Sink 20 Fore — it declines to fall on the opened cells, pooling instead where the wound foil still runs, as if shyness were a property of silver. Dyavryezes Dasvosok is coaxing a fused-quartz pane into a socket with the flats of both palms, no tools, the way one settles a sleeping animal, and does not look up.

lore.name: The Seal-Scar in Cell 31
lore.description: Where the foil is peeled back, cell thirty-one bears a fusion-seal across its mouth — applied, by the tooling-marks, with rindwalker irons, in the manner of the sect's oldest mending-rite. Yet beneath the seal, older notation continues uninterrupted: the same lead-grey script that crowds the deep tunnels, running through the wound as though the sealing were a contour it declined to notice. Whoever closed this cell believed they were ending something. The something predates the iron, the rite, and possibly the sealers' species of certainty — it was already ancient when it was buried, and it did not stop being said.

content.name: Sink 20 Fore
content.description: Light arrives here as rumour. It declines to fall; it pools in some cells and withholds from others, swapping its attentions at intervals no pulse can predict, so the rank of body-sized cavities hums half-silvered, half-swife, like a shoal deciding. Along the opened flank, wound foil has been peeled back from fused quartz in long silver labia, exposing chambers whose interiors give back a darkness with opinions. Stencilled above the thirty-first cell, in a hand gone rusty with devotion: DO NOT COUNT THE CELLS ALOUD. Dyavryezes Dasvosok works the exposed seam and does not stop, and does not look up, though the room looks at you both. The hum is a dwell. The quartz is warm where nothing has ever touched it.

npc.name: Zyeskion Abrenko
npc.voice: Terse, declarative, using room-words as if the plate were listening and preferred brevity.

greet.says: Stand off the standing metal. It is deciding. I will give you this much and no more: the comb was drawn by something that never came back to see if it worked. It worked.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives without paperwork; they sit down on the standing metal their creed forbids, and stay there.
reactions.shock: The violence puts them somewhere behind their own eyes; wool keeps feeding through their hands, untucked, wasted.
reactions.bribed: Offered payment to misremember, they quote the stencil instead, as though the plate had already been consulted and refused.
reactions.accused: The wool drops from their fingers; they say the accusation back once, flatly, as if testing a crack for depth.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them suspicious the way weather makes sailors suspicious; they answer by holding up the mended seam.
reactions.questioned: Their answers to questions come measured in channels filled, exact, never more words than the groove requires.
reactions.threatened: Threat lands on them like pressure finding equilibrium; their breathing adjusts one degree, the only tell they own.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: A third telling comes out shorter than the second, and they know it, and the plate knows it.
reactions.authority_arrives: They watch the official as they watch standing metal: at a distance, waiting to learn what it decides.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the shudder passes they press a palm to the comb and report, quietly, whether the cracks held.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They defend the accused with the brevity they give everything, then keep defending after the room has stopped listening.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They hold the door wide on the plea as though the room might answer it, then concede their mending cannot.

npc.description: Zyeskion Abrenko works the foil with hands that pause at intervals no clock would choose, feeding mineral wool into channels as if tucking something in. They do not look up. Their breathing has the patience of pressure equalising.

lore.name: A tally notched into the comb's root
lore.description: Cut into the plate where comb meets standing metal: small notches, one per repair, ending — not faded, simply stopped — at the exact place the new grooving begins.

content.name: Fracture-Comb 41
content.description: Light here does not fall; it declines to arrive, eddying back from the comb like a word withheld. Fracture-Comb 41 is freshly rebuilt — the plate grooved with a vast dental recursion, each channel drawing the next crack out of the iron-dark and setting it in order — and so it lacks everything a room accretes: no dust, no echo, no smell of prior occupancy, only wound foil and spun mineral wool laid out with a devotion that has not yet learned to fray. Stencilled along the comb's spine: PLATE IMPROVES ON STANDING DO NOT REMOVE. The scale refuses summation, as a prayer refuses arithmetic.

npc.name: Kunya Byama
npc.voice: Measured, unhurried, the cadence of someone who counts what she does before she does it.

open.says: Not my ledgers, that's the joke of it. The last auditor asked which rooms had stood empty past a season, and wrote the answers down and took them, and I've not seen the report since. Rooms going dark in the belt, one street at a time, and the council files it where filing goes to stop being read. I keep my panes frosted and my mouth shut. But I count the empty windows on my rounds now. Anyone would.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll keep what you said.
Maybe I'll count those windows myself.

greet.says: Mind the matting. The glass bites through boots faster than you'd think.

choices.text: What do the audits actually look for?

probe_a.says: Frosting the inner panes. A dwell room wants light you can live in, not light you can see through. The council sets the grade. I set the depth.

probe_b.says: It is. The old one came down in a week. Rebuilt to writ, every joint, every seal. Correct isn't the same as worn-in, but correct is what I can give.

probe_c.says: The ward auditor, on her rounds. Third one this year, and each wants more paper than the last. I keep my ledgers clean. Clean ledgers are how a widow stays left alone.

reactions.grief: Her count stumbles for the first time in years; she starts the pane from the edge twice, finishing neither.
reactions.shock: The tray of ground glass goes over under her hand, and she stands in it, not moving, not sweeping.
reactions.bribed: A price comes to mind high enough to be refusal; she quotes it and returns to leveling the glass.
reactions.accused: She lays the spatula across the tray with exaggerated care before turning, needing the extra second more than she'd admit.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them for the grade of the compliment and the depth of it, evenly, and waits.
reactions.questioned: Her rounds come back in walking order, pane by pane, and she asks whether they want it written down.
reactions.threatened: The frosting knife stays level in her grip while she works out, window by window, what they already know.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She says the number again, slower, as though the wrongness lives in the tempo and not in her.
reactions.authority_arrives: The welcome she gives the official is flawless and slightly too slow, each gesture rehearsed against this exact morning.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The glass shifts in the tray by a hair's width; she checks it, then the windows, counting what's still lit.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her mouth opens on a correction she has counted twice, and she weighs which silence costs less.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: There is nothing in her ledger for this; she offers the stove, the matting, and admits it isn't the ask.

npc.description: Kunya Byama kneels on rubber matting, grinding glass fine as salt and brushing it level into a tray, over and over, until the layer is exact. The room is scrubbed to a shine nothing has lived in yet; a slate panel by the stove still says ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE, though the stove is hers now.

lore.name: The Widow's Audit Ledger
lore.description: Under the cot, a slate board ruled in Continuant blue, filled in a steady clerk's hand. Page after page of the same entry, dated nightly: K. BYAMA, IN RESIDENCE, STATUS: HOLDING. The last column, headed CONTINUANCE, has a number for every night since her husband's death — and the number has gone up twice, both times corrected, the old figures scraped but legible. Nobody audits a single rented room. Somebody audits grief.

content.name: The Curtained Room
content.description: Warm wax and ground glass — someone's been cutting a fresh lens sill for the room's one window. Everything is slate-grey and new: the curtain rod still bright, the rubber matting uncreased, a stencil on the doorpost reading ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE. Kunya Byama kneels at the frame, packing the setting with a spatula, and does not look up.

npc.name: Factor Solen
npc.voice: Measured, precise, and laced with the quiet cadence of one weighing every syllable against the cost of error.

greet.says: Greetings. I presume you were sent by Olo--by Luna? Welcome to the wards. You've seen the city's skin by walking the plaza; now, I'm told, it's time for you to meet the flesh beneath. Know that identity here is not born, but bargained for in the wards’ quiet chambers. Slip past the public faces of our communities. Learn how they hoard their loyalties, what they bury beneath their own floorboards, and the shape of their silence. Return when their hidden architectures are legible to you.

choices.text: I will walk the halls and return wiser.
I have walked the inner wards and tasted the quiet weight of loyalty.

turnin.says: You carry their secrets like stones in your pockets. Loyalty is not a vow, but a calculated surrender to the mechanisms that keep us breathing. Step forward; the deeper currents await. It is time for you to see my... colleague... Factor Solen. I believe she is at The Confluence of Gears.

choices.text: Their quiet architectures are mapped within me. I step forward, bearing the weight of what I have learned.

npc.description: She moves with the measured gravity of a magistrate who has memorized every fracture in the hull. Her face is a cool mask of competence, though her eyes betray the sibilant tremor of a woman who knows how thin the ice truly is.

lore.name: The Palimpsest of Stasis
lore.description: Its polymer folios bear the scar-maps of marginalia, where survival metrics bled into theological confession. Reading it reveals that order is not decreed, but slowly suffocated by the quiet terror of the unmeasured.

content.name: The Slate Quorum
content.description: The chamber exhales the dry, metallic sigh of recycled centuries, thick with the effluvium of archived decrees. Slate-blue alloy walls absorb the axial luminescence, casting judicial shadows over a floor of polished grating where silence is treated as a structural load.

npc.name: Vostana the Merciless
npc.voice: Short, exact, numbers first. Warms a degree when asked about the trees themselves, not the work.

wall.says: Root rot, eight trees, down to the gravel. We took it out and started over. Better a clean wall than a sick one carrying fruit nobody should eat.

choices.text: How long until it fruits again?

greet.says: Mind the turf. New cut, still soft. If you're here about the wall, it's done and I'm not.

choices.text: Who is the keeper on that stencil?

years.says: Two seasons to first fruit, four to a real crop. I'll be old for the good years. That's the trade, and I signed it. The slate remembers everyone who did.

keeper.says: Whoever kept the counts before me. The stencil goes back further than the trees do. I re-chalk it every rebuild. It saves arguments.

reactions.grief: The name stops her hands mid-coil; she repeats it once, exactly right, and offers nothing after.
reactions.shock: She counts the wire anchors between herself and the body, twice, because her mind refuses anything else.
reactions.bribed: She repeats the offer as a figure and refuses it on slate terms, hands open at her sides.
reactions.accused: The knot goes wrong in her fingers; she unpicks it slowly and asks for the count against her.
reactions.flattered: Praise of the ties lands well for a moment; then she hears the request underneath and her face closes.
reactions.questioned: Gives hour, task, and tie count, then returns to the wire without waiting to be dismissed.
reactions.threatened: Her voice holds while she asks whether the threat outlasts four seasons, because the trees will.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She corrects the number without excuse and then waits, jaw working, for the correction to cost her.
reactions.authority_arrives: Finishes the tie before looking up, then recites her tag numbers unprompted, thumb pressing the finished wire flat.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The trees get checked before the people, tie by tie down the wall, and she doesn't apologize for the order.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her defense comes a beat too late, long enough for the room to hear the doubt in it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What she controls is water, wire, and light, and none of it is what they are asking for.

npc.description: A broad woman coiling drip line into a crate, sleeves rolled, forearms chalked white at the knuckles from tying. She works without looking up until the last coil is in.

lore.name: The counting ledger
lore.description: A slate hangs by the last tree, chalked with bud counts in four different hands. The oldest line is smudged but kept: the tally from the wall that stood here before.

content.name: Orchard Wall
content.description: A paper tag flutters on a young branch as the door opens. A fruit-wall stands trained flat against the sun-panel, every tie new, every wire still bright. Cut turf squares wait at the base where the old roots were pulled. A stencil on the glass reads: DO NOT PRUNE WITHOUT THE KEEPER.

npc.name: Rimibeem Bimaraib
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, with the flat patience of someone covering a shift they didn't sign up for.

greet.says: This isn't my counter, so I only know the rules, not the gossip. One candle per prayer. Take what you need, no more.

candle.says: Third shelf, they're sorted wrong but they're all there. Dip your own wick if you're staying long; the ready ones cost regard. Now excuse me, I have two hundred to restack.

reactions.grief: They keep counting, wrong now, and mention a debt the dead one never collected, quieter than they mean to.
reactions.shock: Wax runs over their fingers while they watch; they don't set the dipping frame down until someone takes it.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer out loud before refusing it, and the pricing takes longer than the refusal.
reactions.accused: The count stops mid-number; they list whose counter this isn't and how long they've covered it for nothing.
reactions.flattered: Praise sits on them like bad wax; they thank the visitor flatly and ask what the visit costs.
reactions.questioned: They answer in stock terms, times and tray counts, as though the day were inventory someone else will check.
reactions.threatened: They ask whether the threat applies on this shift or the next one, as if scheduling were the issue.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They restate the number as if a miscount explains it, then move a candle to make the shelf agree.
reactions.authority_arrives: Before anyone asks, they recite the stock count, the hour they took over, and the rule about ready candles.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They watch the candles instead of the walls and count the fallen twice, as though the shudder were a shortage.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They break the no-gossip rule by one sentence — the accused never dips their own wick — and hear how it sounds.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They give the rule instead of help, twice, and stand in the doorway afterward instead of restacking.

npc.description: Rimibeem Bimaraib stands at the back shelf, stacking candles by height instead of by wick type. They stop, count the tray twice, and look up only partway.

lore.name: The counting tray
lore.description: An iron tray scored with tally marks, older than the rest of the counter. It survived the rebuild; everything else was replaced.

content.name: Tsurozaki
content.description: The counter smells of hot wax and cut wick cord, sharp over the raw concrete. Everything here is pale ochre and days old: the shelving sits square, the iron banding has no rust, and the floor has no path worn across it yet. A stencil on the counter's edge reads ONE CANDLE PER PRAYER, TAKE NO MORE. Rimibeem Bimaraib is behind it, counting stock into the wrong arrangement.

npc.name: Threirnulf-Hjernagl
npc.voice: Dry, spare, hoarding of words the way they hoard spares; measures everything in what holds and what fails, and warms only toward those who ask about the work rather than the leaving.

work.says: New caps in the race — black glass, ground true, better than anything we could cast. Twelve of them, seated in a day. Then the thirteenth wouldn't go, and I stopped forcing things a long time ago. The race beneath is cold as a river bottom and the metal above still remembers the torch. You learn to read that difference or you don't last here.

choices.text: Where does black glass come from?

glass.says: Found stock. Old layer, older hands. We keep it, we catalog it, we argue about it — that's the whole of what I'll say. What I know is it takes a torque no forge of ours could match and doesn't wear. Everything I mend wears. That stuff just waits.

choices.text: So why walk away from it?

greet.says: Nobody comes down the span to Truss 47. So either you're lost, or you were sent, and I don't like either. The joint's locked. It stays locked. That's all the story there is.

choices.text: What was the work meant to be?

locked.says: Because the joint turned a half-degree while my back was turned, and nothing on this span turns itself. I stencilled the warning myself and I left the thirteenth cap sitting proud. Mars keeps the hull. I keep my hands. Some nights I think the hull doesn't need either of us — and some nights I think that's exactly the wrong thing to believe. Go up. Ask your questions where the light is.

choices.text: Leave them to the cold and the waiting.

reactions.grief: Names the dead the way they'd name a part that will never be restocked, then keeps talking about torque long past the point anyone's listening.
reactions.shock: The wrench drops from their hand and they let it lie — first thing they have ever left where it fell.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the piece a price in hours and labor, honest arithmetic, then refuses on the grounds that it doesn't hold.
reactions.accused: Goes still the way a bearing seizes, then asks which joint they think failed, voice flat with the effort of it.
reactions.flattered: Warms a degree, asks what they actually want mended, and lets the flattery sit like stock nobody catalogued.
reactions.questioned: Answers in torque values and shift-hours, precise as a ledger, offering nothing beyond what the log already shows.
reactions.threatened: Tells them plainly that threats cost nothing to make and everything to enforce, and keeps winding the cord braid through their fingers.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Holds the contradiction up like cracked stock, examines it, and admits nothing except that they misspoke — once, carefully.
reactions.authority_arrives: Stands at the collar of the pit with the wrench in hand and recites the stencil above them as though it were jurisdiction enough.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Puts a palm flat to the cold floor, reads the shudder through it, and the color leaves them before any answer does.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says nothing in the moment, but afterward walks the span to Truss 47 and checks whether that person's last knot is bright.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains exactly what fails, exactly when, in hoarded words — then admits they have no part for that and never did.

npc.description: Threirnulf-Hjernagl stands at the joint's collar with a torque wrench still in hand, copper gauntlets gone green-black at the knuckles, and does not move for a long moment — the stillness of someone counting exits. A braid of salvage cord hangs from their belt, each knot a route walked, and the newest knot is still bright.

lore.name: The Half-Seated Cap
lore.description: One black glass bearing cap sits in its collar but a finger's width shy of home, its seating face dusted with copper powder — the rite of fitting begun and never finished. A hairline of old grease, still tacky at the center, records exactly where the last hand pressed.

content.name: Truss 47 Deep, Span 291
content.description: The cold lives in the floor here, and nowhere else: the bearing race below holds a reservoir of chill that has outlasted the work, while the buttresses overhead still carry the ghost-warmth of welding done years ago. The pit slopes toward a joint the size of a granary, half-girded in silver sheathing, its black glass bearing caps stacked and waiting. Nothing was cleared away. Tools lie where hands set them down. Stencilled across the truss, in rust-brown that has bled into the metal: JOINT LOCKED FOR SERVICE, DO NOT ROTATE.

npc.name: Lleidnor Dylys
npc.voice: Terse, dry, talks in work-order: what it needs, how long, what it costs.

work.says: Longer than the stencil outside. Things come in broken, they leave whole. That's the whole trade and nobody needs it explained past that.

greet.says: You're not here for heels, so don't ask. Wait your turn or hand me something worn.

choices.text: How long has this bench been going?

reactions.grief: Names every repair they ever ran for the dead, boot by boot, until a customer leaves.
reactions.shock: Four hands stop at once, tacks scattering, and they watch the door instead of the body.
reactions.bribed: Quotes a price for looking away that no one alive could pay, then goes back to the boot.
reactions.accused: Quotes the hour, the tacks, the witnesses, all too fast, and only then hears the speed.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise pass unanswered and taps the stencil near the door — queue, wait, appointment.
reactions.questioned: Answers in shop terms — bench, hours, output — eyes never leaving the tack line.
reactions.threatened: The upper hands keep working; the lower pair has stopped, and the apprentice notices first.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Says nothing for three tacks, then corrects the record in the flattest work-order voice they own.
reactions.authority_arrives: Eyes the official's boot soles first, jurisdiction second, and asks how long before they need mending.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches the solder before it slides and, for once, offers no estimate of the repair.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Keeps tacking through the naming and calls the accusation wrong, once, in the voice kept for bad leather.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Measures the plea against everything stacked on the shelves and finds nothing there sized to it.

npc.description: Lleidnor Dylys works two benches at once, arms crossing over each other at the vice. One hand drives tacks, another trims cable ends to length, a third holds the boot steady. The fourth rests on the pile of finished pairs, counting.

lore.name: The Last Awl
lore.description: Lleidnor's awl has been rehandled four times; the oldest grip is a stub of rope-laid cable wound with solder wire. The blade itself has never been replaced.

content.name: The Resole Bench
content.description: The resoling wheel stands still. Four cobbles of tallow-waxed leather wait on it, half-tacked, and the bench around them is stacked chest-high with salvaged cable and grey solder sticks. The room climbs in shelves to a low ceiling. A stencil near the door: HEELS BY APPOINTMENT ONLY. Two customers, one apprentice, Lleidnor Dylys.

npc.name: Khaimiolin-Qinanz
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, answers measured like change from a till.

greet.says: You're standing in my curing lane. If you're Braid, the word is saffron runs short next cycle — tell it forward. If you're not, still tell it forward.

leave.says: Good. The Braid moves, everything moves.

ask_room.says: Mine and ours, depending which sheet you're behind. You don't want the whole ledger. Tell it forward.

reactions.grief: Holds the till-voice through the news, then asks, off ledger, who's going to take the cot down.
reactions.shock: The cane frame goes over in their hands; they stand in the wreck of their own work and count nothing.
reactions.bribed: Quotes a counterprice out of habit, then refuses it anyway, because the Braid's word isn't theirs to sell.
reactions.accused: The row of knots stops mid-hitch; they ask who benefits, not who's guilty.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit a beat too long before discounting it, the way they never let a price sit.
reactions.questioned: Gives the week in till order, no rounding, and the knot never stops under their fingers.
reactions.threatened: Drags the hung sheet shut between them and the threat; the voice comes out steady on the second try.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Reprices the lie without apology, though the knot in their fingers slips for the first time in years.
reactions.authority_arrives: Marks the official's ward-badge before their face, and moves the saffron talk one sheet further from the door.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The hung sheets swing and settle; they count the seconds out loud, twice, and don't like either number.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names the accused's outstanding debts unprompted, then hears, too late, how much they wanted it to be them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses flat, then gives a name in Range 260 who still owes them, and won't meet the eyes.

npc.description: Khaimiolin-Qinanz strings cane lattice without looking up, knots going in at a speed that says this hand has done it through worse. A knotted cord at the wrist, work-worn past color.

lore.name: The Split Cot
lore.description: One cot, sawn in half lengthwise, both halves kept — one on each side of the sheet line, neither slept in.

content.name: The Sheet Stall, Range 259
content.description: The heat pools at the ceiling where the cannery boilers still run; the floor stays cold, and the hung sheets do nothing about either. Cane frames and copper fittings divide the loft into claims that overlap but do not agree. Stenciled on a sheet at shoulder height: THE SHEET IS THE WALL, RESPECT IT. Nobody has taken the other side's cot down.

npc.name: Yachiarelnavom Thistlemothered
npc.voice: Terse, doubled — as if each sentence were being read aloud from a draft written slightly earlier by someone else.

ask.says: It remembers being read. Luna keeps the logs, but the logs are only the residue — the reading is the thing. You'll understand at the chamber, or you won't, and both outcomes are on record.

greet.says: You cast two shadows here. Don't apologise; the floor prefers it. Take the leaf you were going to ask about and go — the shift isn't mine and the room knows it.

choices.text: Ask what the floor prefers about it.
Take the mica leaf and go.

leave.says: Good. It was already yours.

leave2.says: Mind the shadow on your way out. It's ahead of you.

reactions.grief: Says the name once, draft only, then cannot summon the reading — mica shearing from their grip unregarded.
reactions.shock: Drops the sort entirely; their shadow keeps working across the floor without them.
reactions.bribed: Somewhere inside, the offer is already priced against their name in the logs, and found insultingly short.
reactions.accused: Halts mid-sort, leaf suspended, repeats the charge as though proofing someone else's draft, and declines to correct it.
reactions.flattered: Hears the praise as a transcription error and corrects the flatterer line by line.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day's traffic without hesitation, as if the gnomon has already testified and they merely concur.
reactions.threatened: Meets the threat as they read the gnomon's shadow, marking where it falls and declining to stand there.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Corrects the sentence, then the correction, volunteering a third version nobody requested.
reactions.authority_arrives: Doesn't look up from the sort, a courtesy reserved for whatever outranks the room.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches the mica mid-scatter, then watches not the ceiling but the gnomon, whose shadow has moved upstream.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects before the charge is finished, then pretends the objection was procedural.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Answers with the silence they file between verdicts, and logs the plea as received, unanswered.

npc.description: Yachiarelnavom Thistlemothered stands at the reading-ledge covering a shift that belongs to someone three rotations younger, sorting mica leaves by an order invisible until you notice the gnomon's shadow doing the sorting with them.

lore.name: The Gnomon's Second Shadow
lore.description: Beneath the gnomon's base, where mica has been pried back and replaced, the floor holds a second, fainter shadow burned into the ceramic — the same shape, cast at an angle the room's single light-source cannot produce. It has been re-burned eleven times, each trace identical, each a fraction deeper, as if someone has been checking for centuries whether the discrepancy persists. It does.

content.name: Voiiaasa
content.description: Underfoot the floor reads you first: sintered ceramic gone glassy along the walking lines, mica flaking elsewhere in laminae thin as the pages of a book no one bound — the body learns the room's traffic before the eyes learn anything. A gnomon rises from the reading-floor, iron-cold, and where its shadow falls the stencilled figures on the wall have changed since any record: one bears six fingers now, another weeps in the wrong direction. The inscription READING DIFFERS BY OBSERVER runs beneath them like an apology or a warning, and the shadow crosses it a hand's width to the left of where geometry insists it must.

npc.name: Gliqand Orbitborn
npc.voice: Brisk, tallying even in conversation. Counts things aloud. Answers questions with routes and times, not opinions.

keep.says: Because one day somebody official will ask where that crate went, and I'd rather show them a slate than my memory. Memory gets you audited. Iron strap and a good hand gets you a drink and a dismissal. Now move along — bell's due.

load.says: A crate, sealed, taller than me, and cold on the outside in a warm corridor. Six of us carried it and two of us quit after. It went down the axial stair, the long way. I don't take loads that direction anymore.

quit.says: They said the weight shifted wrong. Like carrying something that was walking. I said nothing, took my pay, and marked no return time. My mother portered this landing forty years and she always said: the ship moves what it moves, and you don't argue with the freight.

choices.text: I'll leave you to your counts.

bench.says: Older than the stairs, or the stairs are younger than the bench. Porters say the floor was raised twice and nobody thought to raise the resting place. Sit if you like. You'll be at knee height to everyone passing, which is about right for the job.

greet.says: Nineteen stone, going down, paid in advance — that's all I know and all I'll say free. You hiring or waiting?

choices.text: What was the load that just left?
Why is the bench lower than the floor?
That slate behind the bench — no return time on the last line.

ledger.says: You read it? Good eye. Most don't look behind the bench. That line stays blank on purpose. A load with no return is a promise the ship hasn't kept yet, and I write what's true, not what's tidy.

choices.text: Ask about the load that left.

mother.says: Born on this landing, near enough. She kept that slate before I did. She told me once that some loads go down and the ship keeps the difference — that a landing gets lighter when it should be heavier. I thought it was porter's talk. Now I keep the slate.

choices.text: Why keep the slate at all?

reactions.grief: Nobody is told to move along for a long while; then the dead porter's best lift comes out of them.
reactions.shock: They stop mid-count at the body, and the number they were on hangs unfinished in the stairwell.
reactions.bribed: They quote the fine for a false entry, then write the offer itself on the slate and initial it.
reactions.accused: They lay both sticks flat on the post and recite every hand that touched the crate, their own last.
reactions.flattered: They answer the praise with the crew's names and shift counts and watch the door the whole time.
reactions.questioned: They give the stair, the load, the hour, in that order, and wait for the next question.
reactions.threatened: They meet the threat with a pay rate, a shift end, and the nearest door, nothing about fear.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Told the slate shows the axial stair, they repeat third landing twice and quit tallying mid-load.
reactions.authority_arrives: The slate is squared and chalk fresh before the official finishes crossing, and they volunteer the day's numbers unprompted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Twice, quietly, they say the ship moves what it moves, then check the freight straps before the people.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They recite the accused porter's routes for a year, fast, and stop one route short of the axial stair.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They cannot lift it, so they give the only route they know and the hour the foreman drinks.

npc.description: Gliqand Orbitborn stands at the bell post with a tally stick in each hand, calling weights down the stairwell to someone below. They do not stop working to talk; they simply slow, and make room at the post without looking.

lore.name: The tally slate behind the bench
lore.description: A slate hangs on the iron banding, half-hidden where the bench meets the wall. It is a freight ledger: columns of loads, weights, and destinations in a porter's cramped hand. The last entry is recent and heavy — one line, one destination, no return time recorded. Every other entry has a return time. The slate's hook has been reinforced twice with iron strap, meaning someone expects it to hold records worth keeping for years.

content.name: Portering, Court 202
content.description: The bench sits a full step below the landing floor, as if the stairs were cut after it was placed. The space behind it is swept clean and wide — something large stood there, and its outline shows in the scuffed paint. Crowds pack the landing. A stencil on the iron banding reads PORTERS REST HERE, HIRE AT THE BELL.

npc.name: Vlyadan Vorev
npc.voice: Plain, procedural. She answers with rosters and schedules. Order is how she comforts herself.

open.says: It keeps this yard existing. Tam gets a clinic bed, the racks get a fifth worker, and next month the logs rotate on schedule whether she's back or not. That's the whole creed, if you want it. Nobody hands the next generation an empty rack. I've buried two registrars and the rotation hasn't missed a week in thirty years.

choices.text: Thank you. I understand better now.
Thirty years of the same week.

greet.says: Shift doesn't start for an hour. If you're here for logs, they're not marked yet.

choices.text: Who do you answer to here?
What does the council actually do for a yard like this?
I'll come back when the shift starts.

probe_a.says: It's Tam's. She's on the sick list, third one this month. I cover until the council finds a fifth body for the yard. They will. They always do.

probe_b.says: Tam didn't finish, so yes. A row that isn't marked is a log that rots without anyone noticing. The stencil says it plain enough. Mark your row, or the week means nothing.

probe_c.says: The green deck registrar, and above her Factor Solen. People complain the writ is cold. I've read it. It's the only thing on this ship that says someone will be here after you.

reactions.grief: She asks after the row, the shift, the cover, and sits down on an empty rack between questions.
reactions.shock: Her wand stays at full pressure and pointed at nothing until someone else takes it from her.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against a month of covering two racks and is ashamed the arithmetic takes so long.
reactions.accused: The wand comes down on the rack edge hard enough to chip, and her voice climbs past shift-talk for once.
reactions.flattered: She answers with the tally — weeks covered, names buried — and refuses to be warmed by any of it.
reactions.questioned: She gives her hour, her row, and the wand's pressure without being asked twice, plain as a log line.
reactions.threatened: She tells them the yard replaces people every month and watches to see whether they believe her.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She corrects the detail, then the correction, and stops speaking before the schedule fails her in front of witnesses.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes find the fresh chalk before they find the official, and she decides which of them to answer.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She logs the time to the minute, then reads the entry back twice, as if repetition could explain the room.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She recites the accused's logged hours before anyone asks, then hears how that sounds and goes quiet.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says the council finds a fifth worker every time, and hears, for the first time, how that answer sounds.

npc.description: Vlyadan Vorev stands at the third rack and does not move. The spray wand hangs in her hand, full pressure, pointed at nothing. Chalk marks on every row are fresh, in someone else's hand.

lore.name: The Chalk That Would Not Wash
lore.description: Under the fresh blue enamel of the third rack, one rail was never repainted. Someone scrubbed it and gave up: old chalk rows still read beneath the haze, the same name marked in the same slot for years past any rotation. The rebuilders built around it. In a yard where logs move weekly and rows are marked so the rotation never fails, a name that stayed put for that long means the yard itself broke the rule to keep a place open.

content.name: Yard 9 Antispin
content.description: A misting line hangs over the top rack and is not turning. Yard 9 Antispin holds its water and waits. New enamel racks stand tiered against the shade cloth, deep blue, each row chalked and stenciled: LOGS ROTATE WEEKLY, MARK YOUR ROW. Nothing here smells of mushrooms yet.

npc.name: Laameasshearluea Reathione
npc.voice: Ration-book diction: measured, procedural, with a caretaker's habit of counting before he speaks.

open.says: I was sent to query a shortfall and walked into the gardens themselves — not the farm belt, the true decks — rows going out past where my lamp mattered, tended by something copper-warm that moved like weather and did not once look at me. It was keeping eleven thousand souls alive the way frost keeps a field: totally, and without a thought to spare for any single seed. I came back up and cooked my tally. Mercy that large doesn't need you to believe in it. It needs you to set the table anyway.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll remember the tally.
Frost keeps a field. God help the seed.

greet.says: Service stopped at third bell, a season back if it's a day. So you'll state what you need, or state what you brought.

choices.text: What is all this foil in the vats?
Who do you answer to for this galley?
Do you ever resent cooking like this?
You said the green decks answer upward. What did you walk into?

probe_a.says: Wound foil, pan-liner grade, third-life at best. It came up from Venus's decks stamped for eleven thousand portions, and I cooked down to none. I don't clear a table I expect to set again — that's not sentiment, that's the writ.

probe_b.says: The roster answers to the green decks, and the green decks answer upward, and past that my writ goes quiet. I file my tallies to a slot in the council archive and the slot has never once written back. But the foil keeps arriving. Somebody is still counting portions.

probe_c.says: Resent it? I take pride in scale. Any man can feed a room. It takes a Continuant to keep a rota for mouths he'll never see, on a schedule no one set, because stopping is the one thing we're not permitted to do well.

reactions.grief: He names the dead one's ration number, then keeps naming portions he once served them, far too many, voice gone flat.
reactions.shock: He drops the ladle upright in the kettle and stands ankle-deep in ash, making no move toward the body at all.
reactions.bribed: He quotes the writ on remembrance and misremembering, word for word, then asks how many portions the offer is worth.
reactions.accused: The rake stops mid-stroke; he sets it down with care, then counts aloud to four before he trusts his own voice.
reactions.flattered: He accepts the praise like a ration slip, checks it for a signature, and finds none.
reactions.questioned: He recites his movements by bell and portion-count, raking still, as if the tally were proof of something.
reactions.threatened: He keeps portioning, hands steady, but his eyes go to the serving counter and stay there, counting nothing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: He does not deny the ledger; he recounts portions until the numbers agree with him, slower each pass.
reactions.authority_arrives: He straightens the foil on the nearest pallet twice, then announces the galley has been dark since third bell, unprompted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He holds the vat's rim until the rattle settles, then resumes portioning, saying the old roster never accounted for weather.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He says the accused cleared three thousand portions without a single shortfall, then hears how much that sounds like a defense.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He counts what he actually has — foil, stock, steam — and offers all of it, which is none of what was asked.

npc.description: Laameasshearluea Reathione stands ankle-deep in chalk-white vitrified ash, raking wound foil from a cook-vat the size of a threshing floor, and turns before the rattle of your boots has finished reaching him across it. Behind him, stencilled along a buttress, the words GALLEY RUNS ON THE OLD ROSTER survive where everything else has been left to set.

lore.name: The Roster Drum
lore.description: At the head counter stands a brass drum the height of a standing person, pegged around its circumference with meal-tokens — one row per feeding, the rows running so far around that a walker at its rim cannot see the start from the finish. The tokens are stamped with ward-counts, and the current day's row is pegged but the counts stop at roughly half: the drum shows a galley that set its tables for a population and then fed half of one. Someone chalked a correction on the drum's base, in a Continuant's careful hand: HOLD THE COUNT. THE DECKS STILL BREATHE.

content.name: Steam-Galley 7
content.description: The floor gives first: grit of vitrified ash underfoot, then a slick of cooled drippings that the boots of ten thousand cooks wore into a shine, and the body reads it before the eye does — this room fed people the way weather feeds a coast. Chalk-white steam-lines run the walls in runs so long the eye gives up counting; the galley floor alone would hold the Nave's whole market square with room for the queue behind it. Wound foil still swaddles pallets of ration stock, mid-unwrapping, ladles upright in their kettles, as if the crew stepped out between two beats of a service that has not resumed. Above the serving counters, stenciled in letters a hand could sleep inside: GALLEY RUNS ON THE OLD ROSTER.

npc.name: Lloddeidd Sadys
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, names things by their price. Loosens a little when asked a precise question.

fire.says: Ledgers don't burn from a lamp alone. Someone wanted a particular page gone and took the room with it. Nobody died, which I count as luck and also as a message. So: new walls, new rule.

rate.says: How fast it moves and who it burns. A rumor that scorches nobody is worth bread. One that scorches a Factor is worth a coat. This desk takes a cut of both — the lead sees to that.

wear.says: A year, maybe two, before the desk fits my elbows. Until then everything squeaks and I trust none of it. Ask me something worth recording and I'll stay awake.

choices.text: I'll come back with a good question.

greet.says: If you're buying a rumor, the rate's on the slate. If you're selling, I decide the rate. Wake me again for anything less than both and I'll add a fool's surcharge.

choices.text: You were asleep at the ledger.
I'll come back when I have something worth selling.

paint.says: I did. Two weeks ago, before the rebuild. The old nook kept names with the sources attached, and the old nook burned. Names kept, sources not — it's a rule now, and paint makes it harder to forget.

choices.text: What happened to the old nook?

sleep.says: The smoke did it. Dead lamp left the air thick and I sat down for a minute in a room that's been correct for two weeks and nothing in it argues with you yet. New rooms are honest. Honest rooms are tiring.

choices.text: How long until it wears in?

reactions.grief: Somewhere behind the tally a debt cancels itself, and they keep adding figures that no longer come out.
reactions.shock: Stands in the doorway with the day's entries still in their mouth and cannot price what is on the floor.
reactions.bribed: Prices the risk aloud, refuses, then enters the offer itself in the ledger while the offerer watches.
reactions.accused: The pen stops mid-entry; they name the accusation's price aloud and dare anyone to dispute the figure.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands warmer than they want it to, so the answer comes a beat slow and over-precise.
reactions.questioned: Answers every question about their movements with its cost in hours, and waits to be told the sum balances.
reactions.threatened: Asks what the threat is backed by — a stamp, a rope, or the man's own debts — before weighing it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Starts denying it on reflex, then stops, because the lie costs more than the truth and they say so.
reactions.authority_arrives: Turns the ledger to a clean page before the official crosses the threshold, nothing hidden, everything ready to be read.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Beneath the flinch there is already arithmetic: a building does not move unless someone is paying for the movement.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects on arithmetic alone: the person named had no stake in that page, and the figures prove it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no in one flat line, then, quieter, explains what the refusal protects and hates the echo in it.

npc.description: Lloddeidd Sadys lifts their head off the ledger before their eyes open. Ink on the heel of one hand. They straighten the top page without looking at it.

lore.name: The split ledger spine
lore.description: The desk's center spine is lead sheeting, folded and hammered flat. A slot runs down its length; rumor pages go in one side and come out the other, and the fold is already bright where hands keep touching it. The rest of the desk has never been touched enough to wear.

content.name: The Ledger Nook of Quiet Ledger
content.description: Lloddeidd Sadys sleeps face-down on the ledger desk, arms folded under a coat. The lead-lined stove corner holds the room's only warmth; the concrete behind the shelves stays cold and pulls at your ankles. Smoke from a dead lamp still hangs near the ceiling. Fresh paint, stenciled above the desk: NAMES KEPT, SOURCES NOT.

npc.name: Rioniru Babaluci
npc.voice: Slow, tidal — she speaks between the room's breaths, as if interrupting them would cost something. Drift-nomad grammar softened by long dwelling; she measures time in cycles, not days.

open.says: Because the chamber doesn't lock — it recognises. I've heard it try names into the dark, and yours is one it already knows, though you don't carry it, it carries you. You were written into the deep the way I write into mica: pressed in while still soft, before anyone thought to ask. The door doesn't open for your credentials, dear. It opens for its own handwriting.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll listen before I knock.
Written into it. Then who held the pen?

greet.says: Tread where you like, but speak after the exhale. She's mid-sentence, the room is.

choices.text: Whose berths do you tend, anyway?
Anything changed in the deep lately?
Why would doors down there answer me?
The room can finish breathing first.

probe_a.says: Mica forgets slower than people do. Layer it deep enough and a room keeps its own memory — every breath ever taken here, pressed flat like flowers. I don't record anything. I just keep what the walls remember legible.

probe_b.says: Nobody's and everyone's. The Drift taught me nothing stays — so they gave me the one job where staying is the whole work. I answer to Luna's ledger, which answers to nothing I've ever seen. Strange trade: the restless girl, made keeper of the still.

probe_c.says: The breathing shortened. Cycles that took a season now take less, like something far below counting faster. And three of the sleepers I tend have begun dreaming in unison — I know because their breathing synchronised. Rooms don't do that. Rooms don't agree.

reactions.grief: The chalk stops mid-tick; she keeps listening for a name the walls have not yet been told to forget.
reactions.shock: She holds her breath past the room's own, unwilling to let an exhale certify what she is seeing.
reactions.bribed: She lets the offer sit through a full cycle of the room before declining it in half a word.
reactions.accused: For the first time in years she answers on the inhale, and hates how easily her voice forgets its tides.
reactions.flattered: Praise settles on her like chalk on mica, nothing to grip, and she says so kindly.
reactions.questioned: Her answer comes only on the exhale, as if interruption were the one crime the room still punishes.
reactions.threatened: Inside her, something old and nomad lifts its head; dwelling has not unmade the part that leaves.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She reaches for a chalk-tick that isn't due, buying three breaths while she rebuilds the sentence she already spoke.
reactions.authority_arrives: She stands for the stencil over the lintel before she stands for the official, which the official notices.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder lands mid-inhale and, for once, she cannot tell whether the room flinched or something struck it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She repeats the name wrong on purpose, then takes six breaths arguing the room would never choose that one.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What she can give is memory — the walls will hold this — and she hears how poor that sounds.

npc.description: Rioniru Babaluci lies along the graphite sill with one ear against it, listening the way others read, and every few breaths she chalks a tick onto the mica that will not accept chalk. She is waiting for the room to finish an inhale it began before she was born.

lore.name: The Berth's Second Keyway
lore.description: Set into the berth's rim, beside the sleeper's hand, is a keyway cut in graphite and backed with mica — and its internal profile is not a lock's geometry but a negative cast of a hand, ports and all, a hand like yours. The mica behind it is layered in growth-bands, one per cycle, and the bands stop mid-thickness: whatever was being counted here was interrupted, and the berth has been breathing toward completion ever since. Whoever casts into this keyway does not open the berth; the berth answers them, as a door answers a door.

content.name: The Breathing Berth
content.description: Sound goes strange first: footsteps enter and are paid back late, a half-beat behind, as though the graphite-packed walls must be consulted before they are permitted to happen. Then the berth resolves — a sleeping cavity asymmetrical in the way a heart is, its layered mica shutters furled at different stages of one long inhalation, all of it lead-grey, all of it new, correct, and unworn, like a word learned from a dictionary and never spoken aloud. Across the lintel, stencilled in the oldest notation layer: CYCLE INCOMPLETE DO NOT WAKE. A sleeper lies where no berth admits sleepers — Rioniru Babaluci, breathing on the room's schedule, not her own.

npc.name: Sevin
npc.voice: Measured, with a low timbre that seems to vibrate through the floorplates. She pauses between clauses as if listening to the hull’s own reply.

greet.says: The city wears a mask of stone and smoke, but down here the metal remembers its true face. Let the three great currents show themselves at their proper scale. When their weight settles in your chest, you will know where your hands belong.

choices.text: I have walked the upper veins and felt the hull’s true pulse.

turnin.says: The hull has spoken. You carry the echo of the deep now. Choose the current that matches your own, and I will show you the way past the threshold.

choices.text: The rind does not demand my oath, only my attention. To mend is to pray, and my joints already know the grammar of broken things.
The council chambers and green decks bear the weight of tomorrow. Continuity will be my sacred trust; the writ will shelter my purpose.
The Braid moves where the air is thin and the maps blur. Circulation is my creed; the markets and archives will never leave me starved for the next horizon.

npc.description: She stands with six arms braided into the damp air, each joint moving with the quiet precision of a slow loom. Her copper-stained tunic hangs like shed bark, and her eyes hold the patient stillness of stone that has learned to breathe.

lore.name: The Fractured Transit Dial
lore.description: Its brass face is scarred by thermal stress, yet the engraved meridians still trace the old axial routes. A faint resonance lingers in the grooves—a quiet testament that the hull’s bones remember every turn it has never taken.

content.name: The Confluence of Gears
content.description: The air carries the metallic tang of ozone and slow oxidation, heavy with the subsonic thrum of dormant turbines. Curved bulkheads recede into a gloom that swallows echo, while overhead, a lattice of support struts groans under centuries of unbroken tension. You stand where the city’s civic fiction dissolves into the vessel’s true skeleton.

npc.name: Dethevaeth of Zyapazdir
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical without warmth; verbs of keeping and tending used for machinery, nouns of machinery used for time.

greet.says: You stand where the count pauses. It does not pause often. Ask, or step aside — the filament dislikes idle weight.

column.says: For? It keeps. We attend what keeps us — Zyapazdir taught that, and the column taught Zyapazdir. Saturn tallies; we do not read the tally. Further down, things are written that answer you better. Not kindly. Better.

choices.text: Nod, and let them return to their argument.

reactions.grief: She gives the wrong liturgy first, the one for spent filament, then hears it and cannot finish, grey knuckles whitening.
reactions.shock: What she keeps stops being kept; the count in her skips a turn, graphite falling from her opened hands.
reactions.bribed: She prices the bribe as an offering, finds it counterfeit, and refuses in the dullest ledger-language she owns.
reactions.accused: Her hands halt mid-mending; no liturgy she keeps has a verse for being named the fault, and it shows.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads to her as a hook dressed as an offering; she credits it to the column, never to herself.
reactions.questioned: She recites her whereabouts like a maintenance roster, each hour named as a part she keeps, nothing unaccounted.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands like a hand on the filament; she keeps still, tending her fear as she tends all else.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She misremembers once and only once, then lays the correction into her own ledger aloud, term by term, jaw tight.
reactions.authority_arrives: She turns only as far as menders turn to interruptions, offering Saturn's writ its exact owed salute, nothing warmer.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder spends a prayer she did not know she was saving; she is at the filament before thought.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She lists the named one's faults of technique too readily, and the readiness indicts something she will not look at.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She refuses as the column refuses, by continuing, and the plea stays on her like paste she cannot mend out.

npc.description: One of the two is Dethevaeth of Zyapazdir, grey to the elbows in graphite paste, a mender's apron gone stiff as shell. She speaks to the column's flank rather than to you, as though you have interrupted a consultation.

lore.name: The Plumb-Filament
lore.description: The filament is drawn, not spun — one continuous thread of metal glass, and where it meets the column it has fused, the column accepting it the way bark accepts a nail grown around.

content.name: Kremlilusha's Unattended Column
content.description: Graphite first — not burnt, but exhaled, the cold-sweet breath of a hundred thousand pencil-leads pressed into one dark sweat. The column rises through it, silver as a suture, and where the eye climbs its width does not agree with its distance; the hand of it reaches your skin before your gaze has finished ascending. Drawn filament runs from its flank to a stanchion no one remembers setting, thrumming like a held breath. Two figures argue at its base — quietly, in the manner of those who have argued before and will again — and stop. Stencilled at knee-height, in a script older than its paint: OFFERINGS ACCUMULATE, ORDER DISBANDED.

npc.name: Leth Staticrunner
npc.voice: Terse, dry, tally-minded — speaks in counts and conditions, never in wonder.

greet.says: Shift's done, and the yard stands down till Mars is done with whatever's holding the weld below us. If you're taking passage down the slope, mind the tagged sections — forty swaps on that one plate alone, and it still holds. That's the whole religion, right there.

choices.text: Why did everyone leave so suddenly?

ask_seam.says: Nobody left. We were called off. Something downslope went quiet that shouldn't be quiet, and Mars doesn't share reasons — Mars shares work. Take a length of fused quartz if you need light; it'll outlast you.

choices.text: Take the quartz and step clear.

reactions.grief: Starts listing the plates that person swapped beside them, dates and all, and stops halfway through a year.
reactions.shock: The trade in them reads the wound like a bad weld before the rest catches up, and then nothing comes.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against a shift's wage, names the difference flatly, and keeps coiling like the deal was never spoken.
reactions.accused: The filament stops winding; they name every hour since shift's start like a receipt, faster than the tally needs.
reactions.flattered: Asks what the praise costs before accepting a word of it, the way they'd price any untagged scrap.
reactions.questioned: Answers in counts without prompting — nine hours in the yard, four coils drawn, no reason to have left early.
reactions.threatened: Cites the tagged plate — forty swaps, still holds — as if endurance were a shield, grip gone bloodless on the strap.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Doesn't deny it — runs the count again under their breath, and this time the number comes out different.
reactions.authority_arrives: Straightens, hooks the helmet to its borrowed ring, and reports the section count before anyone asks for it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Reads the shudder as a shifted load, then looks at the still plate and can't make the two agree.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects on the record alone — that one's swaps never needed redoing, and Mars doesn't tag good work twice.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers the only thing they carry, a length of fused quartz, and says plainly what it can't fix.

npc.description: Leth Staticrunner packs with the economy of someone who has packed this exact satchel a thousand times, winding filament around two fingers without looking at it, casting an occasional glance at the half-hoisted plate as if expecting it to remember how to fall. Their helmet hangs from one of too many hooks on their belt, none of them theirs originally.

lore.name: The Ledger Plate
lore.description: Where a scarred section was cut free, the edge has been stenciled and re-stenciled with dates going back further than the ink can be trusted to run — the oldest layer is etched, not painted, in notation whose letters match the oldest markings in the upper tunnels. Someone has counted them: four hundred and six swaps at this one seam. Each entry ends with a small chiseled tick, and every tick faces the same axial direction, toward whatever lies downslope.

content.name: The Scar Yard of Quiet Ledger
content.description: Nothing moves here, and the nothing is conspicuous: a scar-yard built for the clamor of plating-swap stands hushed, its hoist frames loaded and slack, one dented hull section half-hoisted on its gantries and holding still as a held breath. The floor slopes down toward a weld seam that runs out of sight, and along that seam, where repair has been happening since before anyone's grandmother, the metal has been scabbed green-black with a thousand patches. Leth Staticrunner is coiling drawn filament into a shoulder satchel, quick and quiet, clearly the last one out. A stencil by the opened bay reads: SWAPPED SECTION TAGGED WITH DATE.

npc.name: Uthiosuna Kaenxeasogenes
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, with the Continuant habit of turning sentiment into maintenance language — grief expressed as torque values and duty rosters.

why.says: Because this module was old in a way the deck plans don't record — older than the paint layers, older than the bolt ledger. Things that old get claimed, not copied. The Judge keeps the long table, and the Judge mostly doesn't bother, but mostly isn't never.

choices.text: You've felt it, then. The Judge's attention.
And the forty — where are they now?

felt.says: Once, splicing a feed line through the hall of judgment. You stand in a room built for more people than the Nave holds and you understand you are a rounding error that was noticed anyway. I finished my splice and walked out grateful. That's the whole of my theology and I don't recommend it.

greet.says: Mind the harness. Forty souls rode on that web until six weeks back — verify load, they stencil it because people forget. You'll be the one from Bay 14. Word moves faster than furniture up here.

choices.text: Someone kept count of the residents on a bolt.
I'll leave you to the spooling.

moved.says: Struck and hauled aft, whole, on Mars-end tractors. No notice filed through the council — Factor Solen's people never saw the requisition either, and she's the sort who reads everything. You don't lift a rated dwelling without wanting it somewhere specific.

choices.text: Why take a whole module instead of building new?
And the tally on the bolt?

domain.says: Jupiter's. Court-ground, though the court sits empty more seasons than not. We hold it in trust — that's the arrangement nobody wrote down and everybody keeps. You'll know when you're near the table; the silence changes texture.

choices.text: Then tell me about the module that left.
I'll be careful where I stand.

ledger.says: The brass bolt. My mother's habit — punch the household mass each moon, so the trusses never carry an unwitnessed weight. Continuants keep what we are given; the least we owe what's given is an honest count. The last punch isn't mine, and I've stopped guessing at it.

choices.text: What does the last line say?

lastline.says: Forty strokes crossing to one. Not a death-list — a transfer mark, the kind we use when a household is moved into stewardship rather than dispersed. Someone counted them down and signed the count. Down to a single soul, still carried on the books.

choices.text: This far up, whose ground are we standing on?
Thank you. I'll carry that count with me.

reactions.grief: Recites the dead colleague's last splice in full, every splice-length and clamp, as if precision were a wake.
reactions.shock: Sits down on the empty cradle without deciding to, the foil spool still turning somewhere behind them.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer in inspections it cannot pay for, and declines in those units, without slowing the spool.
reactions.accused: Their hand over-cranks the tensioner past spec, twice, before the denial finishes forming.
reactions.flattered: Their eyes never leave the tensioner during the praise, because praise in their experience is always an invoice.
reactions.questioned: Reels off bay numbers and timestamps like reading a duty roster aloud, unprompted, finished before they were asked.
reactions.threatened: Says nothing, which for a person who answers in torque values is the loudest figure in the room.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Corrects their own lie without being pressed twice, because a wrong figure on record offends them worse than the danger.
reactions.authority_arrives: Straightens, produces their duty roster unasked, and volunteers compliance three questions ahead of the official.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The spool stops mid-feed under their hand, and they time the sway against the vents before permitting themselves fear.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Denies it faster than they have verified anything in years, then asks, quieter, which bay the evidence came from.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers verification, which is the only mercy their trade keeps, and watches it fall short of the plea.

npc.description: Uthiosuna Kaenxeasogenes stands ankle-deep in coiled filament, feeding a foil spool through a tensioner with the unhurried economy of someone who has learned that anything hurried in this place gets worn out by it.
