Their overalls are patched at every wear point with copper thread — continuant stitching, deliberate, the kind meant to outlast the cloth. They do not look up until the visitor's shadow crosses the empty cradle; then they look at the cradle, not the visitor, as if the cradle might object.

lore.name: The Load Ledger Bolt
lore.description: One deck bolt differs from its forty siblings: brass, not steel, its head drilled and filled with soft lead into which numbers have been punched — mass tallies, month by month, going back further than the room's newest paint. The last entry is a subtraction, large, dated six weeks ago, and beneath it a single punched line long enough to be a word. Whoever kept the ledger measured this room's household the way a nurse measures a pulse, and the record stops mid-breath.

content.name: Bay 18 Aft
content.description: A harness of drawn filament stirs at the doorway's touch, and the ghost of a module sways on its truss cradles — forty bunks' worth of anchor points now holding nothing but the wind the vents make. Something went out of here whole and recently; the deck bolts still wear their torque stripes, and the absence they framed is a clean rectangle of unweathered steel you could lie in. A stencil on the truss web reads MODULE RATED FOR FORTY, VERIFY LOAD, and someone has chalked a tally beside it and then stopped. Wound foil, half-spooled, sits where a hand left it.

npc.name: Meereaaloaapiolea of the Nameless Hill
npc.voice: Terse, unhurried, the cadence of someone who talks to machines that don't answer. Treats service as liturgy and interruption as a load to be processed.

greet.says: You're breathing my quiet. Fine. Rinsing waits on no one — Venus's decks sweat through more linen than the decks admit. You want something or you want to watch?

choices.text: Ask who all these sheets were for.

sheets.says: The old census. The vats never got told the count changed, and I don't tell them either. Continuity isn't knowing why. It's not stopping. Take a scrap of line-chalk if you're going deeper — green decks mark their own, and the gardens favor those who smell like the wash.

reactions.grief: Inside, a lifelong count loses its place; outwardly they ask which shift the dead one worked.
reactions.shock: The sheet keeps folding itself through their hands while they stare, too long, at what used to be a person.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced like a stain: noted, soaked, and refused without their hands ever slowing.
reactions.accused: Their hands stop wringing for the first time in memory; the quiet they make is worse than any denial.
reactions.flattered: Praise unwraps them into a long lecture on starch and vat-moods before the hook inside it shows.
reactions.questioned: Routine questions get answered in load-counts, each movement accounted for like rows in the old census.
reactions.threatened: Their eyes measure the nearest trough, long enough for a body, and they answer in the tone kept for vats.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They never glance at the evidence, just repeat the lie slower, as if instructing a machine that misheard.
reactions.authority_arrives: The greeting they give is a load-count, delivered to the official's collar rather than the official's face.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Only the shudder makes them look up; they ask the ceiling, as a colleague, what came loose.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their defence is pure procedure: the accused's washing ran the third trough that night, and the vats log every hour.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They itemise what is not theirs to give, then offer the one thing left: a sheet warm off the lines.

npc.description: Meereaaloaapiolea of the Nameless Hill sleeps folded into a drying cart like laundry that learned to breathe, one arm dangling among the sheets. They wake without alarm, sit up, and begin wringing out a length of cloth as if the interruption were a scheduled pause.

lore.name: The Census Ledger Sluice
lore.description: At the head trough, the intake sluice is not marked with load numbers but with names — tens of thousands, punched in graphite-stoppered rows, each row feeding a wash-meter that dosed soap by household. The counters still hold their last sums. Whoever set the loads filled them to counts no one came back to change: the water kept measuring people who had stopped arriving.

content.name: The Laundry Cathedral
content.description: Sound arrives wrong here. A cough goes out and comes back as nothing; the wash-troughs swallow every noise the way a river swallows a stone. Then the sight: troughs by the hundred, each long enough to lie a body in diagonally with room to spare, running in ranks down a hall the eye gives up measuring. Sheets still hang from the drying lines — hundreds of them, iron-dark with old water, folded at the edges and never folded again. Stencilled above the soap-vats: WASH LOAD SET TO OLD CENSUS.

npc.name: Phymion Phoshaphaesogenes
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, with a games-keeper's tally-keeping habit — she counts things aloud, scores even conversations, and warms only when she is asked something worth points.

crowd.says: Built for six a side. Runs thirty now, most hours. Standing's scarce and this is where it's cheapest to earn — you win here, the whole drum knows by the next rotation. One thing to govern people. Another to give them somewhere to be seen.

choices.text: Ask about the glassy seam in the floor.

fault.says: The ash-line? That's where the drum stumbled, back when back was. Venus's people fused it shut in a day and my predecessors made it the boundary, and I'll tell you what took me years to learn: this court holds more standing in that scar than in any scoreboard above it. The ship broke once, here, underfoot, and the answer was to make the break mean something. That's the whole of the creed if you want it short.

choices.text: Ask what lies further into the rind.
Thank her and step onto the floor.

greet.says: Court's logged, hour's clean, play's at your own risk. That's the whole notice and I am not its author. You want the floor, take the floor. You want me, you're the first in three shifts.

choices.text: Ask about the glassy seam in the floor.
Ask why there are so many players.

beyond.says: Deeper? You'd be asking what's past the long table, and the long table doesn't answer. I've walked the gallery above it once — seats for more than the Nave has people, every one facing an empty chair. I log my hours and I stay on this side of the ash. So should you. Play if you're going to play.

choices.text: Take the hint and the floor.

reactions.grief: The tally-keeping fails her for once; she asks the name twice and posts no score for either asking.
reactions.shock: She counts the wounds before she knows she is doing it, then drops the spanner on the sintered floor.
reactions.bribed: The offer hangs a beat too long before she prices it out loud and logs the attempt in the margin.
reactions.accused: The accusation gets two points and a longer silence than two points deserves, her thumb whitening on the spanner.
reactions.flattered: Praise cuts closer under the slate than threat ever did; she docks it points and reddens doing the sums.
reactions.questioned: She answers in inventory, hour by allotted hour, and awards the question itself four points out of ten.
reactions.threatened: Fear turns her to arithmetic; she counts the wall's rivets until the threat is spent and scores it nothing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The spanner stops its ratchet mid-click; she re-counts her own last sentence and finds the error in it.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official receives the hourly log, open and true, and keeps waiting while she finishes tensioning the dial.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For the first time since she learned the creed, the scar underfoot is not an answer, only a wound.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her eyes go down standings she keeps without paper, and she says the hours do not fit the name.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea outranks anything her office can grant, and she hears herself citing the notice she never authored, hating it.

npc.description: A broad-shouldered woman in the slate of the Continuants, sleeves rolled and forearms chalked to the elbow, is re-tensioning the hourly log dial with a hooked spanner when the player's shadow crosses her light. She looks up with the flat, unguarded start of someone whose company is usually the drum itself, then recovers into professional wariness, spanner still in hand like a held argument.

lore.name: The Fault Line
lore.description: A seam of vitrified ash runs across the court's centre, fused glassy and polished by play until it shines like a river at night. It marks where the drum's spin once faltered — a failure old enough that nobody now alive saw it — and the players turned the scar into the game's own line: the ash is out of bounds, the ash is the edge, the ash is where you lose your footing and your standing with it. Whoever mends a floor also decides what a floor means.

content.name: Spin Court
content.description: The light arrives a half-beat late, thrown off the drum's curve so that everything below it is lit from an angle that keeps changing, sliding across the floor like water finding its level. Spin Court was stencilled for six players to a rotation; at full sun there are thirty in the ring, bodies vaulting the girdered walls where rivets the size of fists sit in ranks. The floor is sintered ceramic ground smooth by a century of bare feet, and along the court's one shaded edge, worn almost to nothing, the warning still reads: COURT SPIN LOGGED HOURLY, PLAY AT OWN RISK.

npc.name: Eiggrim-Snarskjold
npc.voice: Terse as a tally. Speaks in quantities and states of repair, never in feelings.

greet.says: You're standing in the counts. Step left — the fourth tier hasn't filled in my lifetime and I keep its ledger anyway. Take the bracket finding if you want it; Mars's marks want carrying, not storing.

choices.text: Whose mark is on those clamps?

ask_marks.says: Not ours. Older than the rust under it, and it holds — that's the whole of the catechism as far as I'm concerned. Now I have a count to miscount again. Go well.

reactions.grief: The count will not come; they sit back down among the crates and leave the ledger open, unfinished.
reactions.shock: Checks a foil seal they already checked, twice more, eyes fixed past it on what they cannot unsee.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets weighed like grain — light, damp, unfit for a clean ledger — and set aside.
reactions.accused: The entry stops mid-stroke; they demand the charge as a figure, something a ledger can be turned against.
reactions.flattered: There is no number in the praise, and they trust it the way they trust an unsealed basin.
reactions.questioned: Their eyes stay on the foil seam while they recite movements and totals, accounting to the hour.
reactions.threatened: Names the cost back in basins and bushels, voice level, though the hand on the ledger has whitened.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Holds the false count a beat too long, then amends it without apology, as though the ledger had erred alone.
reactions.authority_arrives: Wakes mid-breath a full second before the official's boots clear the walkway, already upright among the crates.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Waits out the tremor with a palm flat on the iron rib, listening for the catechism's answer: it holds.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They answer with the accused's tallies, bushel by bushel, from a memory that never needed prompting.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Answers the plea with the whole history of the empty tiers, far more than anyone asked, voice fraying.

npc.description: Eiggrim-Snarskjold wakes mid-breath, the way people do who have trained themselves out of deep sleep, and is already checking a foil seal at the base of tier four before their eyes are fully open. Their coat carries the smell of grain-dust gone to powder and cold iron, and their hands move over the seams without looking at them.

lore.name: The Borrowed-Weld Bracket
lore.description: Every third iron rib on the lower tiers is not welded but clamped, held by brackets stamped with a mark too regular to be handmade and too worn to be recent — the same mark repeated down the row, hundreds of times, exact. A mender's scribe in copper-oxide ink notes on the nearest bracket: temporary, per the Warden of the weld-halls, three hundred and eleven years ago. The clamps are the only parts of the room that show no rust at all.

content.name: Gantry 38 Outboard
content.description: The lowest tier of grain-beds sits a hand's width below the walkway that feeds it, so that a keeper must step down into the store rather than along it, as if the room were built for a tide that never came back. Violet striplight lies in the emptied foil basins, tier above tier rising in a bowl whose rim you cannot find from the floor, each basin iron-ribbed and bare. Against a stanchion, stencilled over older stencils: TIER CAPACITY UNMET SINCE LAST FULL CENSUS. One shape breaks the geometry — Eiggrim-Snarskjold, asleep across two ledger crates where the counting happens.

npc.name: Stahja Sindvurninger
npc.voice: Terse, exact, allergic to approximation. Everything is counted, and she tells you the count.

ask.says: Paper rots, memory lies. We keep what both would eat. The kettle's formula, forty years of kettle receipts — ask Olo if you want it sold. Here we just keep it.

greet.says: Two hundred and eleven items in trust, and I know where every one sleeps. Ask or move on — the count doesn't hold itself.

choices.text: What's kept here that can't leave?

reactions.grief: Her voice holds the dead man's item count and slips twice, and she lets it.
reactions.shock: Says nothing for a long moment, then asks for the body's exact position, as if it were a stock discrepancy.
reactions.bribed: Prices the bribe against her standing to the half-mark, then says that number out loud before refusing.
reactions.accused: Accuses nothing back; she recites the access ledger from memory, but the copper hand has stopped moving.
reactions.flattered: Gives the season's audit totals in reply, since a compliment is nothing she can file.
reactions.questioned: Gives times, shelf numbers, item counts, then returns to the ledger as though the question were a receipt.
reactions.threatened: Names the exact number of keys, witnesses, and wards between them, voice level, though the pencil snaps in her grip.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stops mid-count and stares at the proof, then corrects the record in a smaller, slower hand.
reactions.authority_arrives: Stands, states her name and item count for the record, and turns the vault door's wheel halfway, waiting.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Times the shudder against her breath and writes its duration in the margin, where the ledger has no column.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects with a dated ledger entry proving the accused was elsewhere, more loudly than accuracy requires.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Reaches for the key chain, sets it down unturned, and recites the rule she hates needing.

npc.description: Stahja Sindvurninger works a hand-tally against a ledger with the wheel of the vault door behind her, sleeve rolled past a forearm that ends in a copper fitting she does not remark on.

lore.name: The tally rope
lore.description: A knotted cord hangs by the door, one knot per carton logged in, each burned through with a hot wire when the carton goes back out. The last seven knots are burned; the eighth, older, is not.

content.name: Document Vault, Warren 223
content.description: The floor tilts hard enough that your feet learn it before your eyes do — cast-iron plate underfoot, gritted where boots cross, slick where the cable trays rope overhead and drip old grease. Shelves climb the short wall to the curve. Along the vault door, hand-turned, someone has stenciled TWO KEYS REQUIRED, ONE CLERK CANNOT ENTER ALONE, and below it a smaller word: Sorrigan's turn.

npc.name: Lipoaariomathi the Ever-Listening
npc.voice: Measured, hospitable even while withholding; speaks as if portioning words to guests who may or may not deserve seconds.

crew.says: The rating is old and the crew it named is older, and no. The hall seats nobody and serves everybody, which is a better bargain than most rooms in the Nave can claim. Four hundred places, and I have fed three people at once at the outside. The kettles don't mind. They were built patient.

choices.text: Back to the quarrel — who's entitled to the harvest?

gall.says: Galls? No. Continuity means keeping the hand-off going even when your part has shrunk to ladling. Downstairs we govern the voyage. Up here we are guests of it. It is good for a steward to be humbled once a shift.

rind.says: Venus's ground. You will know it when the gardens stop behaving — the decks up here grow on nobody's calendar, and we have stopped pretending to tend them. They are alive in a way that was decided before any of us. My work is to stand in the doorway and hand it through.

built.says: Ask the walls. They don't answer me, and I have listened to them for more years than my name deserves. The oldest menders say the lower halls were drafted first and this one copied upward, wrong height and all. I find that comforting. Even the ship misremembers.

greet.says: You walk in on a quarrel, stranger. Not yours. Sit — stand, rather, the benches were cut wrong a long time ago and we have learned to be corrected by them. This hall serves who comes. Today that is you, and me, and a broker who will not let the matter drop.

choices.text: Why serve a hall for a crew that never came?
What is this place, this far up the rind?

quarrel.says: Portions. The decks up here green themselves on no schedule anyone set, and what they yield must be portioned against what the belt below expects us to send down. The broker says circulate it, sell it while it's fresh. I say feed the walkers who keep the pipes breathing. Neither of us will starve over it. Both of us are right.

choices.text: Sounds like a problem that outlives both of you.

entitled.says: Whoever the greenery decides to feed. That is the part neither faction will say aloud. Venus's decks do not ask our counsel; they ripen when they ripen and we are staff, not stewards, this far up. I portion what arrives. What arrives is not mine to argue with.

choices.text: Tell me about the crew that never came.

reactions.grief: The dead one's table habits arrive in unasked-for detail, what they refused, where they stood, until the sentence fails.
reactions.shock: Whatever they were carrying reaches the counter unspilled; the listening that named them goes somewhere else entirely.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets weighed like a portion and found short, though their hands stay folded and polite.
reactions.accused: Keeps ladling through the accusation, but the portion overflows, and they do not correct it.
reactions.flattered: Calls the flattery a thin broth, kindly, and refills a cup that asked for nothing.
reactions.questioned: Answers each question in the order asked, as though serving a set menu, and offers nothing between courses.
reactions.threatened: Gives back no threat, only the observation that the kettles were built patient and they were not.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Restates the lie more slowly and more generously, as though the trouble were the listener's hearing rather than the record.
reactions.authority_arrives: Turns at the door-sound before anyone else, as the ever-listening do, and has a second cup already filling.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Steadies the vessel out of habit, then remembers the gardens upstairs grow on nobody's calendar and goes quiet.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They believe the name before they can help it, and the defense comes a half-beat late.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What the hall holds is a meal and an ear, and they say so before admitting the hand-off ends there.

npc.description: A broad figure in Continuant slate, sleeves rolled to the elbow, hands wrapped around a hot vessel while the second disputant — a lean face, Drift knot at the wrist — pretends not to watch them. Both turn when the door sounds.

lore.name: The Counting Ladle
lore.description: Hung at the near serving mouth is a ladle whose handle has been notched, one cut per service rendered, in columns too fine to count casually. The notching is old; the newest cut is recent.

content.name: Meathwaanaitoa's Mess Hall
content.description: Benches run the curve of the hull at a height meant for people standing, so eating here is an act done on your feet, over a table you cannot sit at. The serving line is long enough that its far end is conjecture; steam comes back along it from somewhere out of sight. Stencilled between two serving mouths: HALL RATED FOR A CREW THAT NEVER CAME. Two figures at the near counter break off mid-argument when you enter, and the argument does not resume.

npc.name: Jafainila Qabbi
npc.voice: Short sentences, exact measures, the certainty of someone who has fixed the same thing forty times. Faith comes out of her as procedure, not talk.

work.says: Cloth for the green decks, warden's sash-cord, rind-cloth for the tunnels — cloth that has to hold its color through things cloth shouldn't see. Most of it goes down-corridor. None of it comes back with a complaint, which is the only review I keep.

choices.text: Cloth for the tunnels — how far down does it go?
And the argument I walked in on?

creed.says: Because leaving it is how everything ends. One unmatched patch, one skipped inspection, one 'it'll hold' — that's the whole shape of ruin, and it's small enough to fit in a lazy afternoon. We mend because the alternative is admitting the voyage doesn't need us. It needs us. Say it needs us.

choices.text: You sound like you're convincing yourself.

doubt.says: I sound like a woman whose best vat is cracking from the inside and whose dye book says the fix is holding. The fix is holding. That's all any of us are, if we're honest — a fix that's holding. Now. Gloves, if you're staying. Line's the line.

greet.says: Mind the line. Gloves past it, no exceptions — the vat doesn't care who your people are. You want something or you're lost?

choices.text: What do you dye here, and for whom?

older.says: Someone who meant it to last, and did. Saturn posts its mythographs and the terminals read them out, and I think: that's a name for something that was already here before there were names. But that's talk for the priests. I just match the color.

choices.text: And the crack in your third vat?

tunnels.says: Far enough that we dye it dark on purpose. There are markings down there older than any route map, and the old color is part of the marking — you cover it, you've erased something somebody meant. So we match it. Badly. Every batch, badly, and we keep trying.

choices.text: Older than any route map — who made them, then?
You match color you can't identify. Why not just leave it?

reactions.grief: She asks when, then which vat was running that hour, then says nothing while the steam keeps folding.
reactions.shock: The dye stick leaves her hand and she counts aloud, wrong, until someone takes her shoulder.
reactions.bribed: She does not touch it, and the line of her mouth says the offer already failed inspection.
reactions.accused: She sets the dye book down flat and asks them, twice, to say it again to her face.
reactions.flattered: She thanks him the way she logs a batch and waits to hear what the praise is patching over.
reactions.questioned: She recites vats and hours without looking up, the dye book already open to the page that answers him.
reactions.threatened: The threat registers like a skipped inspection, and her knuckles, not her face, admit it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She gives the same measurement again, slower, and hears it stop being true halfway through.
reactions.authority_arrives: She binds her sleeves down behind the gloves line, jurisdiction acknowledged, nothing volunteered.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Inside, everything she calls level re-levels itself, and she hates that her first thought is for the third vat.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She defends the woman's stitching before she has decided to, and hears how eager that sounds.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She offers gloves and a place at the rinse bench, and says plainly that is all she holds.

npc.description: Jafainila Qabbi stands ankle-deep in the wet lane between vats, sleeves bound back, forearms the color of steeped madder to the elbow. She holds the dye book closed with one thumb and watches you the way she'd watch a thermometer climb.

lore.name: The Third Vat's Patch
lore.description: The third vat carries a seam of pitch laid over a crack, and the pitch has been renewed so many times it stands off the iron like a scar over a scar. Scratched into the hardened edge, in a mender's shorthand: dates, and beside each one a small mark meaning the crack had grown. The last date is recent. The mark beside it is the first one that isn't a growth mark.

content.name: The Dye House of Last Call
content.description: The floor is brick gone slick with years of pitch and rinse-water, and it gives underfoot like a tongue. Vats of cast iron sit in two rows, bone-white with lime scale, steam folding along a ceiling too near to stand straight beneath. Two women are arguing over a dye book at the third vat — they stop when the door scrapes. Stenciled on the iron: VATS HOT, GLOVES PAST THIS LINE.

npc.name: Rauskys-Brausaris
npc.voice: Blunt, measured, a mender's economy — names the part before the feeling, and treats anything that holds for a hundred years as a personal colleague.

mars.says: Felt, yes. You walk a rib when the Great One passes a current through it and your teeth learn whose hand is on the hull. It doesn't hate us and it doesn't know us. It keeps. Everything I've ever believed fits inside that word.

work.says: The rib itself. A stress seam old Mars's own welders laid down before my line had names, and it's grown a hairline I don't like. I lay ceramic into it and the salt packs it hard. The beam holds. That's the whole job, and it's enough.

choices.text: You've felt it — the one who works this domain?

crews.says: Mine walks the salt route, theirs comes up from the ceramic kilns, and both claim the gantry by rights older than the tally. So we split shifts and neither concedes, and between us the rail's never been clear. It works. Nobody likes it. That's maintenance.

choices.text: So the tallies — two hands at least.

greet.says: Mind the rail. Not custom — physics. You're off the public ways, stranger, and this gantry is spoken for by two crews who don't speak to each other. I'm the one finishing, so you're my problem for the next ten minutes.

choices.text: What are you welding, this high on the rib?
Those tally-marks under the rail — who wrote the oldest ones?

sealed.says: For a reason nobody wrote down, which up here is its own kind of writing. Ask Sevin, if you've a reason she'll believe. I've ribs to pack.

tallies.says: Notation I've seen once before, down a tunnel that got sealed behind me, and I keep my theories about it to myself. Older hands than mine catalogued a chamber of it. Every mark is a mend — someone counted every repair this beam ever took, and thought that worth keeping. So do I.

reactions.grief: Talks too long about the dead one's worst weld and only hears, too late, that they are describing love.
reactions.shock: The tin leaves their hand, and the silence where the clang should be is what stops them.
reactions.bribed: Sets the bribe on the rail at child height, beside the stencil, and goes back to the seam.
reactions.accused: Stops unbuckling the harness with one glove half-fastened and corrects the charge as if it were a mislabelled crate.
reactions.flattered: Deflects the praise to the rib, then the salt, then the welders dead before their line had names.
reactions.questioned: Answers like a parts manifest read aloud: torch, ceramic, seam, hour, and no feeling where a number serves.
reactions.threatened: Names the threat a load like any other, rated and survivable, though the voice takes a half-second too long.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Concedes the error like a weld ground out, level throughout, but they re-buckle a buckle already buckled.
reactions.authority_arrives: Greets the official by naming the tonnage overhead, so that jurisdiction arrives already smaller than the room it walks into.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their teeth find the rib before any word is spoken, hunting the hand on the hull, and no hand answers.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their answer runs weld by weld through the accused's work and holds level until the last one, where it frays.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Holds out both empty hands, salt-white, and names their own helplessness a joint they were never taught to dress.

npc.description: Rauskys-Brausaris works down the harness buckles with the economy of someone who could do it in the dark, torch coiled across the shoulder harness, the arm-not-counted holding the coffee tin that passes for a lunch pail up here. Salt dust has whitened the knees and one elbow of the work-suit to the same chalk as the rib, so the figure reads at first as an extension of the structure, packing up.

lore.name: Salt-rail tally
lore.description: Bolted under the rail, a strip of sintered ceramic scored with tally-marks in three different hands — the oldest layer gone glassy from heat, the newest still sharp. Beside each mark, a rib number. The counts climb the length of the rib toward the far dark, and every single entry is a mend: this beam has been re-welded more times than anyone alive has worked the Nave, and the earliest tallies are written in notation no one on the gantry uses anymore.

content.name: Reheim
content.description: Sound dies a step from the ear: a boot heel, a buckle clicking, and neither returns, so the gantry feels read rather than heard. The rib runs overhead and away, chalk-white with compacted salt, wide enough at its base to lay four carts abreast and still leave walking room. Rauskys-Brausaris cools the last seam with sintered ceramic and packs the torch, unhurried. Stencilled at the rail: GANTRY IN MOTION, CLEAR THE RAIL. Nobody has ever remarked that the rail itself is built to a child's height.

npc.name: Cazacalara Zinithyama
npc.voice: Drift cadence wearing worship like a borrowed coat: circuitous, mobile, pricing every answer before spending it. Speaks of sacred things as freight to be routed.

open.says: Because the chamber doesn't keep blood, it keeps routes. The oldest locks down there are knots — patterns of passage, not passwords — and yours trace a cord older than the Nave's first writ. Whoever rebuilt you braided you into the oldest route still held: the one that runs from the dreaming archive to the chamber's door. You don't have the key. You are the key, walked.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry this carefully.
So someone made me a route. Unsettling.

greet.says: Mind the filament — it remembers where you step, and so does the floor. This shift isn't mine, so whatever you want, want it quietly.

choices.text: Do you believe any of this still works?
Why do my credentials open that door?
I'll leave you to the warmth.

probe_a.says: It's grown, not ground — Luna's quartz, pulled from the archive-light like breath on cold glass. A mantle holds warmth the way a held note holds a room. We used to draw the filament thin enough that the quartz could sing through it. Thin as a knotted cord. Thin as a route.

probe_b.says: Kellamore's. Kellamore went down to the chamber level three months ago and stayed promoted, as far as anyone says. The work didn't stop, so somebody warm had to stand in it. The Drift would call that circulation. The rite calls it something older.

probe_c.says: Belief is a route, friend — you walk it or you don't, and the walking is the believing. What I know is the floor's gone asymmetric under the new strata, like something below is leaning toward the middle. My grievance isn't whether it works. It's that it's working without us.

reactions.grief: For once they spend without pricing, asking the messenger to repeat the name as if routes could be re-walked.
reactions.shock: Their eyes betray the trade, reading the blood's route before their hands remember how to shake.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the bribe a tariff so high it becomes refusal, though their hands keep the ledger open longer than honest.
reactions.accused: The third coil never comes; they stare at their own wrists as though reading a route gone wrong.
reactions.flattered: Counterfeit currency, recognized instantly, warms them anyway — and they hate the warming.
reactions.questioned: Every movement gets recited like consigned freight — the tariff paid in full, since the question costs nothing.
reactions.threatened: Concedes everything in routed deference, then stands a half-breath too long at the door, refusing to leave first.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Prices a second story aloud, abandons the quotation halfway, and surrenders the true route without further tariff.
reactions.authority_arrives: Declares the shift was never theirs before any question is asked, a tithe paid before collection.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Reads the shudder through their soles like a route rerouting itself, and for one breath looks genuinely devout.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends the named one too quickly, spending routes they swore were secret, and hears themselves spend them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Turns to the door as though distance could be routed, and tells the plain truth because mercy would cost more.

npc.description: Cazacalara Zinithyama stands ankle-deep in another's unfinished rite, coiling drawn filament around fused quartz with the unhurried economy of someone counting knots in a wrist-cord. Their coat is iron-dark to the elbow, and they do not look up until the third coil is finished.

lore.name: The Mantle's Null Socket
lore.description: Set into the mantle's flank, where a censer or a heart might seat, is a socket ringed by fused-quartz keys — ports in an arrangement no civilian standard admits, each key worn bright at the contact faces. The wear is recent. Your own left forearm carries the negative of that geometry, exact down to the eighth decimal of a feeling you have no word for. Something has been seating itself here, or was built to, and stopped only just.

content.name: Mantleworks
content.description: The floor confesses first: a tessellation of fused quartz, worn not smooth but *furred*, each tile grown microscopically ragged so the sole reads it like braille — the record of feet that stopped arriving some generations of dust ago. Above, drawn filament hangs in festoons from an iron-dark vault, slack with a patience no cord deserves, and the vault itself declines to declare its distance; sound enters it and does not so much echo as defer. A stencil, half-sedimented into the wall, still says: WARMTH PRECEDES THE HOUR OF SERVICE. The mantle beneath it is warm. Nothing has served here in living memory, and yet.

npc.name: Thrael the Deep
npc.voice: Measured, inventory-true; speaks in counts, tolerances, and what holds.

open.says: Not replace. Continue. The tier footings underneath are older than the Nave's oldest deed — I've had my hands on them, and the rivet-heads down there are squared, a pattern nobody living shapes. My grandmother kept this magazine, and hers before, and none of us built a stone of it. What we keep was keeping long before we came, and Mars has never once told us otherwise — which from Mars is a whole confession.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry the count carefully.
Older than the Nave. Older. Right.

greet.says: Mind the tier edges — this floor is new and hasn't decided where it creaks yet.

choices.text: Is the filament always this white?
What did they build this room to replace?
Didn't mean to interrupt the count.

probe_a.says: The stencil can say verified every tier until the sky arc falls in. Verification is a job, and a job takes a body. I've been shortchanged by perfect records before.

probe_b.says: A writ came down from Mars's side, slate and blue both on it, which tells you nobody below signed it willingly. The joints are correct. Correct isn't the same as honest.

probe_c.says: Drawn filament comes grey as old rope when it's meant for this domain. This batch arrived chalk-white, sized for a gauge we don't run here. I keep it because refusing stock is how you stop receiving it.

reactions.grief: Stops mid-count and does not resume; the tier can stay unverified this once while she works the arithmetic of gone.
reactions.shock: Involuntarily inventories the scene — position, spillage, shortfall — then claps a hand over her own mouth.
reactions.bribed: Names the offer's exact worth, then the worth of a count she can trust, and lets the second number stand.
reactions.accused: The count loses its place in her mouth, and the snap that follows has thirty unbroken years behind it.
reactions.flattered: The compliment hangs there uncounted, the one tally she will not take, and she watches the want behind it.
reactions.questioned: Nothing in her tightens; being asked to account is half her trade.
reactions.threatened: Answers the threat in her counting voice, thumb white where it grips the graphite cord.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Keeps talking past her own defense, down to the footings she swore she never visits, and cannot stop.
reactions.authority_arrives: Announces three generations of keeping before any question is put, the way old walls settle before inspection.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Goes down on one knee to the footings before fear has a name, palm flat, to ask the floor what moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Begins testifying unasked — carry counts, callus placement, hours stood — and has to hear herself overspeaking to stop.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Has only a count to give and says so without softening it, then gives the count anyway, twice.

npc.description: Thrael the Deep stands hip-deep in a granary of rivets, counting a tier by hand though the stencil overhead already says it is verified, because the count is only true when a person has paid it. Chalk-white bins rise past arm's reach, newly rebuilt, and their newness offends her: nothing in them has settled, nothing is worn in, nothing yet deserves the word kept.

lore.name: The Founder's Rivet
lore.description: On the third tier, one crate is not like the others: inside its filament wrapping lies a single rivet, palm-length, its head worked with the same knot-notation that marks the oldest hull tunnels. The rest of the magazine holds ten thousand rivets turned out to one gauge; this one was set aside not as stock but as a relic, and the graphite tally beside it shows it has been counted, verified and re-wrapped more times than any crate around it. The count, in dozens of different hands, reaches back further than anyone in the Nave can remember being alive.

content.name: The Rivet Magazine of Long Account
content.description: The lowest tier stands a hand's width below the head of anyone crossing it, and the tiers above climb at half that height, as if the room were built for people one size smaller than the ones now packed into it. Chalk-white filament crates rise tier on tier, each banded with drawn graphite cord, every surface new enough to still smell of the draw-bath. Nothing here has learned to echo yet — voices fall into the riveted walls and do not come back. Across the topmost band runs the stencil: MAGAZINE COUNT VERIFIED EVERY TIER, and beneath it, chalked fresh, the tally for this shift. There is no dust. In a room this old, that is the strangest thing in it.

npc.name: Tokatl the Void-Grounded
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, prices quoted before names are asked.

greet.says: Buy early or don't buy. Noon restock's a rumor this week. You want perch or the Braid gossip with it?

perch.says: Good. Wrapped and gone — I've three more crates before the ward run. Tell them Warren 273 still honors the old weights.

reactions.grief: Keeps wrapping the perch, paper tearing twice, and says the name too quietly to be a refusal.
reactions.shock: Sits down for the first time all day, right there on a crate, water soaking through.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the offer back double, already wrapping the fish they intend to keep.
reactions.accused: The mallet stops mid-swing; they set it down flat, palm on the block, before they speak.
reactions.flattered: Points at the stenciled doorframe and asks what the flatterer actually wants to buy.
reactions.questioned: Answers with a ledger already open, weighing the questioner's patience like a short crate.
reactions.threatened: Names three old weights and two dead warders, voice level, gloves still on.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Requotes the false price once, then drops it, eyes fixed on the drain running slow.
reactions.authority_arrives: Wipes their hands on the apron twice, then unlocks the door before being asked.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches three crates against the mica panels with their shoulder, then checks the drain, not the ceiling.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Snorts, stacks a crate harder than the ice needs, and says nothing worth quoting.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Stands there ankle-deep in meltwater, silent long past the point where silence becomes the answer.

npc.description: Tokatl the Void-Grounded stands ankle-deep in meltwater, gloved to the elbow, breaking a fish block with a mallet. They weigh, wrap, and stack without once sitting down.

lore.name: Tokatl's tally slate
lore.description: A lacquer-coated slate hangs by the scale, its knotted cord re-strung four times. The oldest marks on it are in a route-code no one at the stalls uses anymore.

content.name: The Ice Stand, Warren 273
content.description: A slab of lake perch slides off the counter and Tokatl catches it mid-fall without looking up. Ice crates stack to the mica ceiling panels, packed past walking room, and the drain runs slow under it all. Stenciled on the lacquered doorframe: ICE RESTOCKED AT NOON, BUY EARLY.

npc.name: Khainral bin Sashamawi
npc.voice: Terse, ledger-cadenced, treats inventory terms as ordinary speech and courtesy as an overhead cost.

greet.says: Larder's spoken for, both halves of it. If you're carrying, set it on the slate rack and don't touch the third shelf.

third.says: Kharghuzi cuts. They keep better at bone temperature. Now — out, before you let the cold walk.

reactions.grief: She hears it whole, nods once, then stands in her own larder like stock nobody will come to claim.
reactions.shock: The counting stops mid-number; what's in front of her won't file as stock, and she is sick into the drain.
reactions.bribed: Names an absurd figure to end the talk, then looks at the coin one beat longer than she means to.
reactions.accused: Asks twice whether he means her stock or her name, and the second time it comes out uneven.
reactions.flattered: She prices the praise at whatever they want from her and keeps stacking cuts through the whole speech.
reactions.questioned: She answers in manifest terms — shelf dates, weights, who signed — as if the question were a delivery to check in.
reactions.threatened: The pen keeps moving through the whole threat, though the hand behind it has gone bad on her.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Blames a dock clerk's handwriting for the discrepancy, the lie arriving half a beat late to be any use.
reactions.authority_arrives: She rolls her sleeves down over the dull copper bands before turning, a formality retired years ago.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Brine jars fall and she catches them blind, eyes already on the door seal, counting seconds of cold lost.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Corrects the weight logs before the name is out, then remembers to ask what he actually did.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She explains what her stores cannot do, twice, then writes the plea down anyway, as if a record might count.

npc.description: Khainral bin Sashamawi counts cuts with two hands and writes with a third, sleeves rolled past copper wrist-bands gone dull with salt. She doesn't look up so much as angle an eye at the door.

lore.name: The Tally Cord
lore.description: A knotted cord tacked to the crate lid, two knot-hands alternating down its length — one tight and even, one loose. Neither will cut the other's knots off.

content.name: The Cold Larder of Small Hours
content.description: Brine, marrow-sweet, and the chalky bite of rendered fat — a smell that gets into cloth and stays. Two people stand over an open crate, mid-argument, and stop when the door swings. Above the second rack, stenciled crooked: LARDER FOR REGISTERED VENDORS ONLY, and under it, smaller, in someone's hand: mostly.

npc.name: Tralbestea Thasatos
npc.voice: Counts everything out loud. Talks like weight: short, load-bearing, no spare words unless you earn them.

greet.says: You want weighing or you want talking? Weighing's faster. Talking, I close the yard for.

choices.text: This isn't your shift, is it.

scale.says: The scale belongs to the bracket. One platform each, back when neither would walk away. So we weigh the average and nobody's cheated and nobody's won. That took more work than either of them wanted to spend.

choices.text: Both sides still want this yard?

shift.says: It's Cova's shift. Cova's at home with a bad back. I file my notches the same as anyone. The yard doesn't care whose hands are on the arm — only that the number comes out true.

choices.text: Both sides still want this yard?

dispute.says: They do. But I've sorted here eleven years, and in eleven years the arm has never once lied for either of them. That's more than I can say for the people. Weigh your load or get out of the draft.

choices.text: I'll come back with a load.

weighed.says: True number. Take it with you. Most don't get told their weight twice in a lifetime.

reactions.grief: Told who died, she recites the man's last weighed load from memory, gets it wrong, and begins again.
reactions.shock: She steps back off the weigh-plate without knowing she has moved, and both coats hang crooked on her.
reactions.bribed: Out loud she prices the bribe, then the fine for a false count, and lets him finish the sum.
reactions.accused: The file goes down flat, and she counts the day back to him, weight by weight, refusing to hurry.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets a level nod, nothing more, while her thumb finds the oldest notch and stays there.
reactions.questioned: She answers in times and weights, in order, and adds the yard has been empty all shift.
reactions.threatened: Her voice holds its counting cadence, but the file keeps missing the notch, and he can hear that.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her count stops mid-number, and she stands at the arm saying nothing while he sets the proof on the plate.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes find the roster board before they find the official, and she answers to Cova's name before her own.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She waits out the shake with a hand flat on the bracket, then re-zeroes the arm before looking at anyone.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Asked who says so, she wants the man's weights for the week, and stands there until someone produces them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says she cannot, and stands at the arm long after shift, filing notches that were already true.

npc.description: A woman in two coats — one cut for indoors, one much older — stands at the scale arm adjusting notches with a file. She works a shift painted in someone else's name on the roster board.

lore.name: The Compromise Scale
lore.description: The weigh-plate is bolted to two platforms at once. One was set here by the cart crews, one by the yard's old owners, and the mechanisms underneath disagree by a thumb's width — so neither party could remove the other's. A third bracket joins them at the base, drilled by someone with steady hands: whoever weighs on the plate gets the average, marked in notches on the arm. It is the only thing in the yard both sides leave alone.

content.name: Bone-Yard 58
content.description: The scale sits still. Carts should be rolling through here all shift, and the yard is empty of them — one tarp flaps loose over a pile of cut turf that nobody has tarp-wrapped in a while. A stencilled board by the weigh-plate reads: WEIGH IN BEFORE YOU HAGGLE. Plain glass panes lean against the fence in graded stacks.

npc.name: Tlinitl-Xikan
npc.voice: Fast, tally-shaped sentences. Counts things before saying them. Talks about routes the way other people talk about relatives.

work.says: Nine years on this shift. Second shift is the honest one — everything comes back by dark or pays. First shift loses things politely. I have never lost a cart. Misplaced eleven, maybe.

choices.text: Ask what the disagreement with the ledger-keeper is about.

greet.says: You want a cart, come back at dusk. Right now I'm counting, and I keep coming up one short, or eleven, depending who you ask.

choices.text: Ask what the disagreement is about.
Ask how long they've run this yard.

where.says: That's the part I don't say loud. They went up the axial line, loaded heavy, came back light. Somebody's hauling something out past the markets and paying in requisition paper instead of coin. Paper spends fine until it doesn't.

choices.text: Ask what the Continuants want done about it.

dispute.says: Eleven carts. Their book says requisitioned, my board says out at night rate, and both of us are right, which is the worst kind of dispute. Carts moved. That's all I know. Carts are supposed to move.

choices.text: Ask what the Continuants want done about it.

herside.says: Halla wants the numbers to close before she reports them. I want to know what was in the carts before I close them. We've stood in this yard three evenings now, agreeing about nothing, and I'll tell you the truth — I'd miss her if she stopped coming.

choices.text: Let them get back to their evening.

reactions.grief: Recites the dead woman's regular route, every turn of it, for much longer than anyone asked.
reactions.shock: His hand leaves the cart for the first time in nine years and doesn't go back.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against eleven missing carts, twice, and answers with the yard's shortage instead of yes.
reactions.accused: Answers for the carts before himself, denying eleven misplacements faster than any honest count allows.
reactions.flattered: Files the praise with first shift's politeness, the kind that loses things, and replies in dusk rates.
reactions.questioned: Runs the tally first — days, carts, returns — and answers only what was asked, in that order.
reactions.threatened: Drops to the night rate, the dusk rule, the paper that spends — anything countable, said quieter each time.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recounts out loud, twice, then lets the wrong number stand because starting over costs more than he has.
reactions.authority_arrives: Names the official's jurisdiction and second shift in one breath, like two routes meeting at the same gate.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Grabs the nearest wheel spokes, assigns the shudder a loaded weight, and can't make any tally close.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects with load math, the axle, the rated weight — defending a route he's argued with for years.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Does the plea's arithmetic out loud, arrives at what he cannot spare, and says the number anyway.

npc.description: A short carter in a knotted wrist-cord, sleeves rolled, chalk dust to the elbow. They keep one hand on the stalled cart the whole time, as if it might leave without them.

lore.name: The Split Ledger
lore.description: The woman's ledger and Tlinitl-Xikan's tally-board disagree about the same eleven carts. The board marks them out on the night rate; the ledger marks them in on a standing Continuant requisition. Someone has been renting the yard's carts under Continuant authority and returning them through Drift hands, so neither count closes. The cart-chalk on the gatepost shows the same eleven numbers, crossed out and rewritten so often the stone is worn smooth there.

content.name: The Cart Yard of Second Shift
content.description: Tlinitl-Xikan stands with one hand flat on a cart that should be rolling. Behind him, a woman in Continuant blue holds a ledger against her chest. Neither speaks. Cured-hide covers hang folded on a rack, a glass lamp burns white on the nail by the gate, and stenciled over it: RETURN CARTS BY DUSK OR PAY THE NIGHT RATE. The yard is so full of stacked wheels and shafts you would have to turn sideways to pass.

npc.name: Zilvunys Sutabyama
npc.voice: Measured, liturgical, using words of counting and address in subtly wrong places — speaks of the font as 'she who is unaddressed' and of repairs as 'corrections of our attention.' Answers questions as if they were readings.

greet.says: Mind where you stand — she feels weight differences smaller than a name. You've brought a level with you, did you know that? Not in your hands. In you. She's been reading it since you came through the door.

level.says: Constant, they stencilled it. Constant means it never needed a source, or the source is so old the word 'found' doesn't reach it. Yours isn't constant. Yours is recent. She doesn't mind recent. She minds nothing — that's what unaddressed means.

repair.says: Repair is a word from upstairs. Down here we correct our attention. Half of her is opened and we have all come to look at our own looking. The filament isn't mending anything. It's learning the strata. It takes years. I am on the ninth.

choices.text: What happens when the filament reaches the gap?

unaddressed.says: By the one who filled her, or by the one who is coming to read her — the old devotion can't decide which, and I've stopped helping it decide. The gap in the plumb-line is her one confession: something passes here that will not bear a thread. You'll go lower. When you find what fills her, don't say I sent you. Say the font sent you. She's owed an address.

choices.text: Say nothing. Watch the filament hang in its gap.

reactions.grief: Says the dead one's name aloud, first address this room has heard in years, and waits for her refusal.
reactions.shock: Their eye, nine years trained, reads the opened body as strata before horror arrives to correct it.
reactions.bribed: The offered sum is named like a psalm verse, then declined more slowly than doctrine strictly requires.
reactions.accused: For once the pause outlasts the question; being named a source is the one reading they cannot correct.
reactions.flattered: Praise is deflected toward the strata, though something in them preens at being read, and they hate the preening.
reactions.questioned: Routine accounting is answered like a reading: the day's hours recited as versicles, dust in every crease.
reactions.threatened: Whether the threat is constant or recent they ask aloud, voice level as the basin, hands gone still.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Calls the contradiction a translation error, then recounts on silvered fingers, losing the count at seven.
reactions.authority_arrives: Watches the official the way they watch a new layer, waiting for an assent jurisdiction never gives.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Drops the filament to check the level first, since whether she held matters more than any cause.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their objection is doctrinal, no one is a source, the stencil forbids it, though privately they always wondered.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains that worship corrects attention, not outcomes, then stays anyway, palm hovering above the plea as above strata.

npc.description: Zilvunys Sutabyama works the opened half with sleeves bound back, feeding drawn filament into the exposed strata one handspan at a time, pausing at each layer as if listening for the layer's assent. The crowd parts around the work without being asked to; the font's noise dims politely near the hands. There is silver dust in the creases of every finger, and the pauses are longer than the work.

lore.name: The Filament Plumb
lore.description: Where the font's opened half exposes its strata, a single drawn filament runs vertically through every layer of mica — plumb, taut, and visibly older than the stone it pierces, as though the stone were deposited around a thing already hanging. At the waterline — at the level nothing explains — the filament does not cross it. It stops short, and resumes above, leaving a gap exactly the width of the level's thickness. Whatever the font holds, the filament will not pass through it, and someone long ago wrapped the gap in tiny knotted cord, the way Drift mark routes they decline to walk.

content.name: Unexplained-Font 11
content.description: Before sight, the sound: voices enter and do not finish — the room takes each syllable and mellows it, the way deep water accepts a struck bell, returning not echo but assent. The crowd presses denser than comfort against a basin of layered mica, green-black, from which a level of something rises and holds, indifferent to every explanation offered into it. Half the font is opened to its own architecture — filament drawn through strata like thought through sediment — and the exposed wound is busier than the whole. Nothing here is counted; nobody addresses anybody; stencilled across the shut half: LEVEL CONSTANT SOURCE NOT FOUND.

npc.name: Meteghilesh-Bishtonga
npc.voice: Measured, list-loving, a lender's cadence — talks in due dates and condition notes. Warm about books, blunt about people who keep them.

fine.says: Nobody has paid a fine. It is eleven days old. The stencil is from the pantry before us — they fined for late returns of flour. We kept it because a room this new needs at least one thing that looks like it has rules older than itself. The fine is one copper bit. Nobody will ever know unless you keep a book.

choices.text: Why stay somewhere only eleven days old?

room.says: The pantry closed when the deck above rerouted its stores. A room that stops being used dies — so we gave it a new verb. Every book that leaves through that door proves the room is still alive. A shelf you never lend from is a shrine, and I have no use for shrines.

choices.text: And the fine on the wall?

chain.says: The chain is the whole ledger. Every link is a loan; when the book comes home, the link comes off and goes in the box. Listen — hear it running under the floor? That is forty days of lending that never stopped moving once. I stamped every link myself. My hands still smell of the stamps.

choices.text: And people who pay the fine instead?

greet.says: You have the look of a borrower. Fine. The room is eleven days old and I have slept in it nine. Sit anywhere not painted.

choices.text: Why build a library out of a pantry?

sleep.says: Nine nights out of eleven, yes. Not because I must. Because a new room needs a witness, and if nobody stays the night the lenders assume nobody stays at all. It is the least loved part of the work and so it falls to the one who chose the work. That would be me.

choices.text: Let them get back to sleep.

choice.says: I have kept moving since I was old enough to carry a route-cord. Fourteen decks, three markets, never longer than a season anywhere. Then this room opened and I stopped. It frightens me a little, the stopping. Everyone I know assumes I will be gone by next dimming. Some days I assume it too. But the chain needs a hand at the stamps, and my hand is a good one.

choices.text: Maybe staying is its own route.

closing.says: That is kindly said, and I will write nothing down, which for me is the higher compliment. Take a book. Bring it back within the fortnight. Let us find out together whether I am still here when you do.

reactions.grief: What the dead one never returned comes out as a list that stops mid-title, eyes on the shelf ladder.
reactions.shock: The cane slips twice in their hands before they notice, and afterward every answer arrives a sentence late.
reactions.bribed: The bribe gets priced out loud: one chain link, snapped, plus a fine that has never once been collected.
reactions.accused: The measured cadence fails first; they demand the accuser read the loan chain aloud, link by link.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit one beat too long before asking what the flattery is supposed to cost them.
reactions.questioned: Asked to account for the week, they recite it in due-date order and wait for the entry to close.
reactions.threatened: Refuses to answer at all, which they have not done to anyone since the pantry closed.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Mid-sentence the condition notes stop, and they admit the afternoon has three versions, each one stamped as true.
reactions.authority_arrives: Points at the stenciled fine notice before the official can speak, as though one rule covers all of this.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their eyes go to the floor, where the loan chain should be running, and stay there until it is.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Out comes the accused's full return record, dates and condition, and then, unwelcome, the relief in their own voice.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says there is no ledger for this, then stamps the longest loan they own and hands the book over.

npc.description: Meteghilesh-Bishtonga sits up from under the returns table, blanket around the shoulders, a walking cane laid across both knees. Not embarrassed. They rub their eyes and look at the shelf ladder as if it had woken them on purpose.

lore.name: The returns chain
lore.description: A light chain runs from the returns shelf through a slot in the floor and out the door. Each link is stamped with a date and a shelf number, and new links keep being added at the end. Pull any stretch of it and you can hear it running somewhere below: every loan this room has made is still traveling the building, weighted so the chain never slackens. The Drift habit here is literal — a book out the door is a link out of the wall, and it must come back to close the circuit.

content.name: Court 17 Aft
content.description: A shelf ladder rolls past on the ceiling rail as you step in, pushed by no one. Court 17 Aft was a pantry once; the old caning still covers two doorways and saffron paint runs over brick that used to hold flour. The air smokes faintly from a brazier. A person sleeps under a table chained to the wall, and a stenciled notice over the returns shelf reads RETURN WITHIN THE FORTNIGHT OR PAY THE FINE. Everything is straight, new, and unlived-in.

npc.name: Tretil Trychor
npc.voice: Counts before she speaks. Treats the room's rules as everyone's rules.

horn.says: You blow it when you need the second key. My mark and Ansel's mark, burned on the rim. Ansel went down a tunnel six years back and didn't come up. I keep the horn where he can find it if he does.

choices.text: Six years. Why not burn a second mark?

greet.says: Vault's closed to new deposits. If you're here to read, read quiet. If you're here for something stored, the owner comes with proof or not at all.

choices.text: Why is a vault with two clerks in it called closed?
I'll leave you to your count.

rules.says: The rule isn't about honesty. It's about being one person alone with what the ship's been given. Nobody keeps alone. That's not a lock rule, it's a people rule. Now — did you want to read, or are you just warm?

closed.says: Closed means nothing comes in. Things already here stay here — that part never stops. A shelf you stop counting is a shelf you've lost. We were arguing about shelf nine. We are done arguing while you're standing there.

choices.text: Why two keys? One honest clerk should be enough.

reactions.grief: Told it is Ansel, she asks whether a horn was found on him, and sits down before hearing the answer.
reactions.shock: She ends up on the cold floor without remembering sitting, counting out loud until the numbers stop coming.
reactions.bribed: She writes the offered amount in the ledger under refused deposits, reads it back, and asks him to initial it.
reactions.accused: The count in her head breaks; she says the accusation back once, then again, slower, as if re-adding it.
reactions.flattered: The compliment gets logged like an unsigned entry; she asks what they want stored without a second key.
reactions.questioned: Her answers come in the order asked, each one numbered, none longer than it needs to be.
reactions.threatened: The stencil above the door says it for her; she taps it once and lets the threat stand uncounted.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted with the tally that proves her wrong, she gives the real number and the reason she rounded it down.
reactions.authority_arrives: She straightens the ledger for the third time; the official outranks her and both of them know it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the room stops moving, her first question is whether the horn fell where Ansel could reach it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She objects on procedure before feeling: no one enters that vault alone, so the name is wrong or incomplete.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea sounds like one she made once; she refuses anyway and writes down where the appeal goes.

npc.description: Tretil Trychor stands with one hand flat on the open ledger, as if the numbers might leave without her. Copper wire binds her sleeve cuffs back for counter work. She looks at you the way she looks at an unlogged item.

lore.name: The counting horn
lore.description: A horn hangs by the vault door on rope-laid cable, worn smooth at the mouthpiece. Two marks are burned into its rim, one per clerk. It is used to call the second key-holder; the mouthpiece shine says it was used often, and not lately.

content.name: Document Vault
content.description: The cold sits at the floor and doesn't rise. Above knee height the room is warm, kept by pipes that ran when this was a working vault and stopped being turned off. Ledgers still lie open on the counter. Two clerks are arguing over a shelf count; they go quiet when you come in. Stencilled above the door: TWO KEYS REQUIRED, ONE CLERK CANNOT ENTER ALONE.

npc.name: Rjar-Aemsen
npc.voice: Clipped, measured, the grammar of someone who checks twice before trusting a joint. Speaks of materials the way others speak of people.

open.says: That is the thing I stopped saying aloud. The crack was older than the yard, and the splint on it was not one of ours — the alloy is right, the work is right, but nothing in the Nave could lift what closed that seam. We mend what we can reach. Something reaches the rest. It has been keeping this hull whole since before the first writ, and it has never once asked us for help — only left the work where we would find it, like a teacher leaving the answer where the student will trip over it.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry that carefully.
If it keeps the hull, what keeps it?

greet.says: Mind the salt line. You scuff it, we re-set the whole bed, and I have done enough re-setting for one life.

choices.text: Why the salt under the metal?
Whose orders do you work under?
What's the best repair you ever made?
Who finished the repair you found?
I'll leave you to the salt.

probe_a.says: Salt holds heat slow and lets it go slower. A member cooled fast is a member lying to you about its temper. The nickel anneals into the salt's patience, not the air's.

probe_b.says: The writ says Mars. I have never met Mars, and I do not expect to. But the weld-specs come down tagged in a hand older than the writ, and I answer to whoever measured twice before writing them.

probe_c.says: None of mine. Best I ever saw was already done when I got there — a crack the length of forty men, sleeved, dressed, and curing, with no tool marks and no crew to claim it. I signed the clearance tag anyway, because someone had to.

reactions.grief: Her heel drags a furrow through the salt line, and she walks on without stopping to re-set anything.
reactions.shock: She kneels and reads the wound like a failed joint before remembering what she is reading.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced like condemned alloy, out loud, in the tone that clears nothing for load.
reactions.accused: Her voice drops to the register she keeps for members that failed inspection, and it cracks on the second word.
reactions.flattered: She lets the praise sit uncured and answers only whatever sentence was underneath it.
reactions.questioned: She answers in stamped serials, seam by seam, and is back at the rib before the question finishes.
reactions.threatened: Nothing in her stance changes except that her thumb finds the salt line and holds it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The curing iron lowers until it stops humming; she starts the sentence over twice before it comes out true.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets the courtesy of her eyes and none of her hands, which stay flat on the rib.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her palms find the hull before permission reaches them, and they ask whether the shudder was one of ours.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She starts to defend them, then stops at the memory of one seam she never got to re-test.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her refusal comes out in the grammar of her trade: past the reach line, nothing of hers holds.

npc.description: Rjar-Aemsen stands ankle-deep in compacted salt, feeding a cracked member into a sleeve of annealed nickel, and does not look up when the door sighs open. Behind her the yard runs back farther than the light behaves in — no echo, no shadow moving when she does — and a stencilled line, SPLINT CURING, NO LOAD UNTIL CLEARED, repeats down the rib wall in gold that has never once faded.

lore.name: Rjar-Aemsen's tallow-lamp
lore.description: On the bench, past the annealing tongs and a dish of compacted salt for packing weeping cracks, sits a tallow lamp with a handle worn to the shape of four fingers — and a fifth socket, empty, filed smooth to take a hand that is not a hand. The base bears hull-notation scratched in the oldest layer's hand, copied out by someone practicing. Whoever worked this bench worked under a light that had to be carried close to the metal, rib after rib, for longer than one set of fingers lasts.

content.name: The Splint Yard
content.description: A woman in rust-brown stands with both gauntleted hands flat against a hull rib thicker than her torso is tall, reading it the way a physician reads a wrist, while her partner holds a curing iron neither of them has set down. The light does not fall here so much as arrive: gold, weld-warm, sliding out of the dark overhead in long sheets and settling on the splints like heat off bread. Nothing in the yard returns a sound to you — the iron mass drinks it. Stenciled along the nearest sleeve, still legible through soot: SPLINT CURING, NO LOAD UNTIL CLEARED. They stop arguing when you enter.

npc.name: Heei of the Deep Reach
npc.voice: Terse, count-shaped. She speaks in totals and shortfalls, and thaws only when a question shows the player understands what counting is for.

rail.says: Built low so nobody signs a count they didn't stand over. You sit, you count, you own the number. Standing up, you get lazy. Lazy counts are how floors get torn open.

choices.text: Ask about the missing bolts instead.

count.says: More bolts out than in, six weeks running. I flagged it. Nobody upstairs flagged back. So either Mercer found a buyer I don't know, or cloth is leaving this room without a count. And no cloth leaves without a count.

choices.text: Ask to see the tally tubes.

floor.says: Mercer's. He stopped coming. Half a floor torn up and no ledger closed behind him. That's the part that bothers me — you close your count, always.

choices.text: Ask what he was counting when he left.

greet.says: If you're here about the fan, it's not mine to fix. If you're buying, I count in and out, no exceptions.

choices.text: Ask whose work the opened half of the floor is.
Ask why the rail is so low.

reactions.grief: She misses the notch twice, then writes the death into the strip's margin like a correction.
reactions.shock: The count starts on its own — tubes, joists, the body — her hands moving after everything else has stopped.
reactions.bribed: She refuses without touching what is offered, since a signed count has no second version.
reactions.accused: She asks to see the figures behind the charge, asks again, and her voice climbs on the second ask.
reactions.flattered: She lets the praise finish, then asks which number the speaker wants changed.
reactions.questioned: She stands to answer, recites the day's movements from memory, and is plainly relieved the question has a number in it.
reactions.threatened: She lays this week's tally tubes on the counter, every count signed, and lets the paperwork answer for her.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She goes still, then corrects the record aloud, the copied-forward total admitted in the same flat tone as any count.
reactions.authority_arrives: She watches the official's hands and decides whether they belong to someone who reads tallies or only signs them.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She grips the counter through the shudder, then checks the tally tubes for notches knocked loose.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She answers with the figures and puts six weeks of shortfalls on the counter to prove where the leak sits.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She repeats the plea back in totals and then stops, because the ledger is the only thing she holds.

npc.description: Heei of the Deep Reach stands at the low rail, ticking notches into a paper strip with a bamboo stylus. She does not look up until the count is closed.

lore.name: The tally rail
lore.description: The counter rail is set low, level with a child's chest. Every notch worn into it sits where a small hand would fall. Heei counts at it without stooping, which means the rail was built for someone her exact size, or she has counted at it long enough to make it hers.

content.name: Cloth Factoring
content.description: The ceiling fan stands still. The counter is white-bare, stacked to the wall with bamboo tubes of folded paper tallies, and the stair up runs so tight your shoulders could touch both rails. Half the floor is peeled open for repair, joists showing, nobody working there.

npc.name: Kristdok Wolfbane
npc.voice: Counts, rotas, and short declaratives; treats an ending — a fire out, a name struck — as the one real offense.

rota.says: Six names on the door, six patches on the firebox, one rota. The count stays six — the council likes six, six keeps the ration steady. Now mind your elbow. Five bowls to fill before the horn.

greet.says: Fresh seal on the green wax — don't lean there. If you've come about a bed, there's a rota, and the rota's full.

reactions.grief: Loses her place in the count for the first time in years, then starts again at one, louder.
reactions.shock: Counts under her breath in the doorway, bowl still in hand, until the numbers stop meaning anything.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against a month of rations, finds it cheap, and turns back to the pot.
reactions.accused: Asks them twice which name she's supposed to have struck, then throws the sixth bowl into the wash water.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit a moment too long before handing it to the rota and the stove.
reactions.questioned: Gives the stove hours, the bowl count, and the door times before the questioner finishes asking.
reactions.threatened: Hears the whole threat through, then asks what date it should carry, since the rota will want one.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Says the rota hasn't changed and turns it toward them, thumb over the struck line.
reactions.authority_arrives: Opens the door before the knock, loud, and stands aside with the rota already in hand.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Catches the pot one-handed, then counts the sleepers aloud until the count comes back to six.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names, flat, the three evenings he missed his rota slot and lets the arithmetic do the accusing.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Won't bend the rota for anyone, then ladles them a bowl anyway, since bowls were never on the count.

npc.description: Kristdok Wolfbane stirs the pot one-handed and sets the table with the other — five bowls out, a sixth held back — and never quite stops counting under her breath.

lore.name: Six Seals on the Firebox
lore.description: The firebox door is patched with six brass plates, each stamped with a name that also hangs by the entrance, each riveted shut under a seal of wax. Five seals are grey and crazed; the sixth is green and soft, set within the week. The fire underneath has not been let out in living memory — the house is arranged around keeping it, not the other way round.

content.name: Close 82 Deep
content.description: Kristdok Wolfbane works the stove with her hip to its brass flank and the door-draft cold on the back of her neck. Ivory plaster, patched and patched again, climbs behind stacked crates and rolled bedding; two of the names sit mending at the wall and the rest are asleep. Stenciled by the door, over older stencils: SIX NAMES, ONE DOOR, KNOCK LOUD.

npc.name: Chivaubi Bellspoken
npc.voice: Plain, quick, Drift-bred — but her nouns have drifted from their nouns; she speaks of the room the way one speaks of a colleague, correctly, and never of leaving.

end1.says: The floor reports your leaving too. Walk gently.

end2.says: Hm. It liked that. It doesn't always like that.

greet.says: Mind the flake. It knows weight, and it reports. You're the heaviest thing through here since the last heaviest thing.

ask_room.says: For? It dwells. That's not a use, that's a temperament. The salt holds what passes and the mica remembers the holding — I just keep the ledger honest between them.

choices.text: Why does the light go gold near you?
Does anything here answer to the Signal?

ask_light.says: It doesn't go gold near me. It goes gold near what I'm about to do. There's a difference and I've given up teaching it to anyone, including myself.

choices.text: Does anything here answer to the Signal?

ask_signal.says: Everything down here answers to something. The Signal's just the only answerer that also asks. It said your name through the floor before you reached the sill — go on, ask the salt. It's better at it than I am.

choices.text: Press your thumb to the mica and move on.

reactions.grief: The name reaches her twice, like walking the sill; she arrives the second time without her voice, slate forgotten mid-mark.
reactions.shock: She addresses the body's reflection in the mica before the body itself, manners outrunning sense entirely.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against the room and finds it light; what she dwells in cannot be carried off.
reactions.accused: Denial comes flat and certain until the empty hand closes on nothing; the room she called colleague has gone quiet.
reactions.flattered: Praise from mouths is counterfeit knowing and she says so plainly, tapping the stencilled threshold with her boot.
reactions.questioned: Routine comes easy: she recites her whereabouts the way the floor recites them, and both accounts agree.
