reactions.threatened: The threat of removal lands where her creed cannot follow; she works slower, eyes fixed on the salt-face.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She does not retract; she revises the knot, retying her story in a pattern that folds back on itself.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction changes nothing; she has presented herself to things that watch since before officials learned her name.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the floor shudders she stops the salt-work and, for the first time, asks it a question aloud.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Too fast she offers the floor's testimony in their defence, then hears herself pleading like someone who owes them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her listening lasts the whole plea, which is the only help she owns; the knot offers no destination.

npc.description: Chivaubi Bellspoken works a salt-face with a slate in one hand and nothing in the other, and it is the empty hand doing the finer work. Her wrist-cord is a Drift knot tied in patterns that fold back on themselves, a route history with no destination.

lore.name: The Belling-Slate
lore.description: A mica leaf the size of a palm, flecked gold, worn concave where generations of thumbs have pressed it to the salt to hear whether the floor answers.

content.name: Recognising-Sill 26
content.description: Underfoot the floor gives like dry riverbed, then rings — compacted salt veined with mica, each step reporting a shallow gold light upward through the flake, as though the ground were answering questions you hadn't asked. The sill narrows both ahead and behind; walking it, you seem to arrive twice. Stencilled along the threshold, in a hand too patient to be human: PRESENT YOURSELF AND WAIT TO BE KNOWN. A钟—no, a pulse—moves through the mica at intervals the room insists are regular and your spine insists are not. Chivaubi Bellspoken works the salt-face without pausing, and the light holds gold where she stands and pale where she does not.

npc.name: Zlyesize Zeshestov
npc.voice: Sparse, exact, devotion expressed as tolerance for error — zero. Speaks of materials the way others speak of saints.

open.says: Farther than the reports went before they stopped being reports. I have carried quartz down stairs that were not stairs, past the last notation anyone filed, and the chamber was still below me — below the below. What the teams found down there ended their telling, not the descent. Saturn keeps what is under everything, and the chamber is under even Saturn's patience.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
Below the below. That's not comforting.

greet.says: Mind the foil. It remembers every crease you put in it.

choices.text: Half this rick is ruined. Why not rebuild it?
How far down does this all go?
I'll come back when you're less busy.

probe_a.says: It is grown, not made — wound around each cell like a promise the cell can read. Quartz holds the sample; foil holds the intent. Consolidate the two and you have made neither.

probe_b.says: Vosk's. Vosk went down and did not come back up, and the cells do not care about grief, so I cover. The roster is a courtesy. The work is the obligation.

probe_c.says: Because you do not rebuild what the deep has opened. We mend to the seam of what we understand and leave the rest honest. A seamless lie is the only heresy I know the name of.

reactions.grief: Keeps winding foil past all usefulness, creasing it badly, and does not notice, which for them is the mourning.
reactions.shock: Their gaze goes past the body to the creased foil, cataloguing damage aloud until the voice loses footing mid-word.
reactions.bribed: Asks, in the tone kept for damaged stock, whether the offer expects a receipt.
reactions.accused: Goes still as a hand mid-seam and denies it once, in the tone reserved for miscounted stock.
reactions.flattered: Accepts the flattery the way foil accepts a crease: permanently, and filed for later reading.
reactions.questioned: Recites their movements to the minute, like a seam-count, and offers the tally again, unasked, in reverse.
reactions.threatened: Weighs the threat like load on a seam — not whether it holds, but when, and from below.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The denial dies; they rewind the sentence as they would a creased seam, slower, eyes on nothing.
reactions.authority_arrives: Identifies the official by the room's late-returned footfall and finishes the winding before granting a nod.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Moves for the cells before the shudder ends, because shaken stacks consolidate, and consolidation is the only heresy they name.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names the hour the suspect's hands were elsewhere, overspeaking by three sentences — a flood, from them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: States plainly that they keep samples, not people, and the plainness costs them something no one else can see.

npc.description: Zlyesize Zeshestov crouches in the gold half-light, winding wound foil around a cell's opened seam with the unhurried exactness of someone bandaging a wound they intend to outlive. Behind them, half the rick stands gutted, its cells exposed like teeth pulled from a jaw.

lore.name: A Tally-Cell Left Open
lore.description: One opened cell still wears the foil's terminal knot, tied in the rindwalker fashion but with a Saturnine quirk: the knot's last pass runs backward, unmaking as it binds. Inside, the sample cradle is empty yet warm, and scratched into the quartz floor of it — a count. The same count, re-scratched deeper, again and again, the hand steadier each time, as if whoever tallies it is being answered.

content.name: Rickworks
content.description: Before anything shows itself, the rick eats the footfall: sound enters and is returned late, thinned, as though the cells were tasting it and would render a verdict later. Then gold — not gilding but a saturation, as if every surface had been steeped in a light that outlived its source. Cells rise in a staggered rick, each sealed in wound foil and fused quartz, each holding its one dark sample; half the stack stands opened to the air, ribs splayed mid-mend, and the opened half is quieter still. A stencil rides the foil seam in letters older than the letterform: ONE PER CELL DO NOT CONSOLIDATE. Depth arrives obliquely — the quartz fluoresces with the afterimage of a sun-strip that died further up than memory goes.

npc.name: Hatl-Qinikan
npc.voice: Terse, exact, allergic to filler. Answers in the shortest true sentence and returns to the work between them.

greet.says: If it's copying, the rate's on the card. If it's questions, the archive's down the hall.

stack.says: Courier pickup tonight. Twelve ledgers, four hands, going up-belt by morning. Nothing stays on this bench past sunset — paint or no paint.

reactions.grief: The count stops; they ask for the name twice, as if the room had swallowed the first answer.
reactions.shock: They freeze at the window, north light on their face, cataloguing details they will spend weeks failing to copy out.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer — copying rate, falsification rate — and note that only one of the two is on the card.
reactions.accused: The pen lifts for the first time all morning, and a blot spreads before they find a single word.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands somewhere unguarded; the thanks comes out too warm, so they repeat it flat, price first.
reactions.questioned: They answer in three flat facts — desk, hour, count — and go back to line forty before the questioner finishes.
reactions.threatened: They answer the threat with bench rules — north light, nothing past sunset — while the count in their head has stopped.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they drop the lie mid-sentence and give the corrected figure, voice level, ears going red.
reactions.authority_arrives: They watch the official's hands, the way they'd audit an unfamiliar ledger, and answer in yes or no only.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The stack slides, the count breaks mid-number, and they hear themselves say the number out loud to an empty bench.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They give one fact that clears the accused, then go back to the page, which for them is a speech.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say no in its shortest true form, then spoil it with the belt schedule until the pleader gives up.

npc.description: Hatl-Qinikan sits at the window copying a market ledger onto fresh stock, wrist cord knot pressed flat against the desk edge so it won't smear the ink. They count silently, lips moving, and the pen never lifts. A finished stack sits squared at their elbow, corners even, ready to be carried somewhere.

lore.name: The Bench's Old Wire Core
lore.description: Under the new magenta paint, the desk's spine is old spun wire, and the wire carries punch-holes. Someone once fed this bench strips of Tabard transcript and worked them through by hand, indexing by touch. The holes don't match any current index; Hatl-Qinikan rebuilt the bench around them because they couldn't bear to straighten the wire flat. The old system sorts by teller first, subject second — the reverse of every archive in the Nave.

content.name: Copying-Bench 12
content.description: The bench swallows sound first. Talk from the square arrives flattened, as if the room were padded, and the scratch of a pen at the window carries further than it should. A long desk of fresh cane and spun wire sits under the glass, painted magenta down its whole length, bright enough to tint the paper. Above the window a stenciled strip reads: NORTH LIGHT ONLY, NO LAMPS AFTER DUSK.

npc.name: Shion Zleisksky
npc.voice: Sparse, exact, liturgical in the way of a trade — words about coverage, closure, and toll, deployed as if they were the only ones left.

new.says: New is the debt's word, not mine. We laid the strata; the ship took them before the pour cured. You've noticed nothing ages down here. That isn't mercy. That's the bill never coming due — until it comes all at once.

choices.text: Debt to whom? The ship doesn't want anything.
Keep your toll. I'll keep out of the air.

debt.says: It doesn't want. It keeps. Keeps are worse than wants — a want you can starve, a keep you can only fail. The plumb went sideways three weeks back and the teams above stopped filing, and you walked in through a door that answered to your hands and not your name. I've been in Saturn's deep forty years. You smell of the thing we cover. That's all I'll say with the salt this thin.

choices.text: Then I'll go where the smell is thickest.

greet.says: Mind the filaments. The salt keeps the toll honest and you're breathing it off the air faster than it settles. Ask what you came to ask.

choices.text: This sheath is new. Days old, at most. Who rebuilt it?
The stencil says damage covered, not corrected. Isn't correcting the whole point of mending?

damage.says: A mender corrects what the world was supposed to keep. Down here nothing was supposed. This wound was in the hull before anyone alive was born and it will outlast the last of us. We don't correct it. We *attend* it. There's a difference and it's the whole of my creed, and you're standing in the part I can prove.

choices.text: Attend it how long? The strata count in thousands.

reactions.grief: Her hands keep their rhythm on the basalt while something behind her eyes gives way, a stratum failing under load.
reactions.shock: The trade's whole liturgy abandons her; she stands in the doorway saying nothing that closes anything.
reactions.bribed: Refuses in the flat grammar of tolls, pricing the bribe aloud like a flaw she would never certify.
reactions.accused: She turns from the wall for the first time in memory, as if the accusation required a face.
reactions.flattered: The praise finds a younger woman in her still; she lets it stand uncounted, knowing the interest accrues.
reactions.questioned: Counts her own comings and goings in coverage and toll, neither inviting suspicion nor fearing it.
reactions.threatened: Inside her something old and patient begins counting the interest, though her face stays ledger-blank.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Lies again, immediately, in finer detail — laying strata over the crack as she would over hull.
reactions.authority_arrives: Straightens to the full depth of her forty years and gives the official the old greeting, salt first, before any name.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Not fear crosses her face but recognition, the look of a mender feeling a bill arrive ahead of schedule.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects in toll arithmetic, then says one fact too many about the accused's whereabouts, and hears herself do it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits the thing her trade never taught her — that she covers, cannot correct — and her voice pays for it.

npc.description: Shion Zleisksky works with her back to the ingress, palms pressed flat to the basalt as though taking its word for something. Salt crusts the seams of her gloves in rime-fans; her sleeves are stiff with dried brine at the elbow, soft with it at the wrist — years of this room, but the strata under her hands are hours old. She does not turn. She is reading the wall the way a blind woman reads a face.

lore.name: The Toll-Plumb
lore.description: Hung from the newest stratum on a copper filament: a plumb-bob of Saturnite lead that hangs not down but *along*, dipping toward some axial weight your feet insist isn't there. Its filament is knotted at intervals — a tale-count, you realise, or the negation of one: each knot a time the sheath thickened without being asked. The last knot is still warm. The plumb has been falling sideways for longer than the Nave has had a name, and it is measuring tonight.

content.name: Node 11 Under
content.description: Hot brine and struck salt — a smell like a wound packed with clean snow — meets you before the gold does. The sheath swells here where the hull was hurt, basalt poured layer over layer like candlewax remembering itself, each stratum still faintly bright, still uncured, still deciding. Somewhere in the depth of it a pressure ticks on a rhythm your pulse keeps trying to match. Stencilled fresh above the seam: DAMAGE COVERED NOT CORRECTED, in a hand that has written it ten thousand times and meant it every time.

npc.name: Nawughtai-Kafailoa
npc.voice: Flat, quick, half-asleep. She answers before she finishes deciding to.

open.says: The Braid. Not a building, not a person — cords. Every runner ties their route into their wrist, and if you can read knots, you can read where a thing has been. It moves faster than anything the council publishes, because it moves person to person and nobody has to authorize it. Most people think the news in the Nave floats free. It doesn't. It has rope under it.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll let you sleep.
So everything I've heard passed through hands.

greet.says: Door said knock loud. You didn't knock at all.

choices.text: Who left all this work half-done?
Anything change on the floor lately?
What actually runs this city's talk?

probe_a.says: I keep the room moving. Six beds, one stove, people in and out on four-day relays. If a name sits too long in this house, it starts to rot. I move names.

probe_b.says: Nobody left. Everybody left, one at a time, which is worse. Tam still owes me three days of stove-duty. He'll come back or he won't, and either way the paper on that shelf is his.

probe_c.says: Word's gotten heavier. Same amount of news, more weight in it. People used to hand me gossip and now they hand me something they wrote down first. That's new, and I don't love it.

reactions.grief: She talks relays and four-day schedules for a full minute before the name lands, then goes quiet mid-word.
reactions.shock: She gets as far as the threshold and stops, one hand on the frame, not going in.
reactions.bribed: She dumps the cold pot and refills it, saying no twice, once for each ear in the room.
reactions.accused: She comes awake all at once, boots on the floor, hands empty and open where they can be seen.
reactions.flattered: The praise goes unclaimed; she points it at the six cots and the four-day relays that actually move names.
reactions.questioned: She gives the last four days in relay order, flat, quick, the way she reads a wrist.
reactions.threatened: She names the three doors out of Nukul without being asked, watching which one the threat cares about.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The corrected version comes out faster than the first, a leg of route nobody in this room can walk.
reactions.authority_arrives: The paper on her chest disappears up her sleeve before the knock finishes rattling the row.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Something moved that she has no knot for, and she counts the sleepers twice before speaking.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She repeats the name once, then dismantles the man's routes out loud, quicker than she meant to.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says no the way she moves names, without slowing, then gives them the next house down the relay.

npc.description: She is asleep in the corner chair, boots on, a folded paper open on her chest. The stove is still warm. A cyan shawl hangs over the rail by the door, damp at the hem.

lore.name: The Route Cord of Cot Four
lore.description: A knotted cord is nailed to the frame of the fourth cot, one knot per leg of a journey, the Drift way. The last six knots are tied in a pattern the others aren't — the same knot, repeated, tightening toward the cord's end. Whoever slept here stopped moving and started recording one place, over and over, until the cord ran out.

content.name: Nukul
content.description: The door takes your knock and gives back a thin rattle that travels the whole row-house before dying. Inside, six cots face one cookstove. A pot sits half-full on the burner, gone cold. Folded papers fill a wall shelf, and sheets of dyed glass lean against every window, casting the room in cyan. Someone sleeps in the fourth cot, boots on.

npc.name: Cithiayoto Rozenne
npc.voice: Trailing, appraising — a Drifter who prices everything and commits to nothing, sentences that loop back on themselves like knotted cord.

open.says: I miked that bay before it was sealed — standard sweep, my own initiative, nothing more. The dust had been arranged. Tools laid out in waiting positions, tolerances pre-set, as if the room had rehearsed an arrival. You weren't found, walker. You were made ready — fitted, tuned, translated — the way a lock is fitted to a key still being cut.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.

greet.says: Careful where you stand — half this nook is in surgery and it bites. You've the look of someone the corridors sent by mistake.

choices.text: What do you even work on down here?
You're a long way from any Braid route.
Someone's scrawled IMPRESSION RETAINED across your wall.
What impression did Bay 14 leave in you?
Sleep on, then. Forget I passed.

probe_a.says: Continuity of interior — that's the trade. I keep the rooms remembering themselves. Mica holds an impression longer than iron does, did you know that? Iron forgives; mica keeps the receipt.

probe_b.says: The Braid ends where the chapters end and the indexing begins. Down here you answer to whatever answers first. It hasn't, in nine years. That's either mercy or neglect.

probe_c.says: Not scrawled — stencilled. Old stencil, older grammar. It means the room keeps what passed through it, whether or not anyone stayed. Most folk find that comforting. I find it clerical.

reactions.grief: They begin pricing the death out loud, then hear what they are doing and stop, having named no sum.
reactions.shock: Their trade betrays them: before horror arrives they have already read the wound's tolerances, and that is the horror.
reactions.bribed: They appraise the offer aloud with genuine admiration, then refuse for reasons they keep, deliberately, unpriced.
reactions.accused: The knotted cadence snaps taut; they recite every hour this room has held them, thumb whitening on the shim.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them loopier, sentences knotting into generous detours, while their eyes itemize what the flatterer will ask next.
reactions.questioned: Answers arrive priced and provisional, each movement accounted for in figures that trail off before committing.
reactions.threatened: The appraisal instinct fails them entirely; they hear their own value being set and cannot meet the assessor's eyes.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Asked to reconcile their own words, they produce three new versions and decline to say which is the forgery.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction, they note, stops at the opened half; they station themselves there and measure the official head to heel.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shim drops; whatever just moved the room moved it against the grain of every impression they trust.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Relief loosens their tongue before discretion can price it; they offer three reasons the named one always fit badly.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Powerless before the plea, they offer the only currency their trade holds — a promise the mica will remember them.

npc.description: The nook swallows sound the way a throat swallows — each footfall arriving muffled, delayed, as though the layered mica deliberated before permitting it onward. In the violet half-light, half the room lies opened to its iron bones, and Cithiayoto Rozenne sleeps folded into the unbroken half's exact negative space, one hand still curled around a mica shim, as if sleep were merely the room performing its function upon them.

lore.name: The Fitted Hollow
lore.description: Where the iron ribs evert, the mica behind them is not broken but grown around a absence: a person-shaped recess, its edges smoothed to the exact tolerances of a body, down to the notch of a port-cluster along the left forearm. It is older than the stencil above it, and it has never been slept in — the surface bears no wear at all, as though the room made it ready and the readiness itself was the purpose. Beside it, a single credential-plate, dead, stamped with a notation matching the oldest layer of the walls — the same hand, you realize, that is on you.

content.name: Govamsaaca
content.description: Sound arrives here already apologized for — the nook drinks each footfall, each breath, and returns it thinned, as though a confessor stood between you and your own noise. Mica in laminated panes, violet as the underside of an eyelid, gives back a light nobody is holding. Half the chamber is opened like a chest mid-surgery, iron ribs everted, and the opened half goes on farther than the wall that should bound it, or farther than belief will follow. In the shut half, Cithiayoto Rozenne sleeps in the posture of one who was fitted here, and stencilled across the mica, in a hand too patient to be human: IMPRESSION RETAINED OCCUPANT UNKNOWN.

npc.name: Saiharai al-Rami
npc.voice: Dry, exact, short of patience but not of attention. Speaks in parts and tolerances.

work.says: Escapement. Belongs to a clock that someone left overnight, which the sign says not to do, so now it's mine until they apologize properly. Everything that comes through that door is tired. My job is to disagree with it.

greet.says: If you're here to collect, the queue's on the board. If you're here to leave something, the queue's still on the board.

choices.text: Ask about the drawer under the table.

sleep.says: That's my sister. She ran the relay bench in the market square until it closed, and now she runs mine, and she won't admit the hours here are worse. Wake her and you take her next repair. Those are the terms.

drawer.says: You saw that. Those aren't stock. A part goes in when its owner doesn't come back, and it stays ready anyway. A thing that was mended once can be mended again. I don't care how long it waits.

reactions.grief: The chalk stops over the tally board; she has begun writing the name before she hears herself doing it.
reactions.shock: A part stays in each hand; she does not sit, or speak, or put them down.
reactions.bribed: She prices the silence like a repair, names the figure, and then declines the job.
reactions.accused: She sets the escapement down first, so nothing breaks, and asks them to say it again at a slower speed.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets checked the way she checks a returned clock, tapped twice and found loose somewhere.
reactions.questioned: She answers without looking up, times quoted like tolerances, and asks whether that closes the entry.
reactions.threatened: She asks whether the threat counts as a deadline or a promise, because she schedules the two differently.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie dies in the middle; she gives the true number instead, quieter, like reading it off the board.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes go to the door, then the sleeping sister, then the official's hands; she reads jurisdiction like wear.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She catches the lamp mid-swing and counts every part on the bench before she looks up.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She recites the accused's whereabouts to the quarter hour, and defends a woman she has never once praised.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She explains exactly what she cannot do, with tolerances, and keeps explaining long after the point is made.

npc.description: Saiharai al-Rami works with four hands and a head-loupe, and does not look up when the door opens. There is a cushion tied to her stool and a tally board by the lamp with more names on it than hours in a day.

lore.name: The loan drawer
lore.description: Under the loupe table is a shallow drawer of cork, divided into small clay cells. Each cell holds one part — a mainspring, a crown, a lens ring — wrapped in paper with a name and a date on it. None are for sale. When a customer's repair needs a part Saiharai doesn't have, she lends one from here and takes the worn one back, and the drawer fills slowly with pieces that have outlived their owners. Some of the dates go back forty years.

content.name: Tashkamab
content.description: A woman sleeps on a cork stool at the loupe table, chin on her folded arms, while the bench lamp keeps working — swinging a little each time the corridor door lets the draught in, then settling back on the same fired-clay bench. The work queue beside her is longer than the table. Above the lamp, stenciled in ochre: NO TICKING CLOCKS LEFT OVERNIGHT.

npc.name: Ghaqthiamana the Oath-Returned
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical. Verbs in the present tense for things finished centuries ago. Speaks of the anvil as a colleague with seniority.

greet.says: Stand off the ring-line. It knows when something breathes near it. You want it said? It has been said. Every strike is said.

choices.text: There's no hammer. What's striking it?

ask_strike.says: The heart counts itself. This is where it shows its work. Take the foil — the seats want fresh winding before the next confession. Now go. I don't stop mid-oath.

reactions.grief: Keeps winding the seat through the whole telling, then winds it twice more, past any honest count.
reactions.shock: Their mirror-polished eyes show the body twice over before their mouth manages any word at all.
reactions.bribed: Asks what denomination of silence is being quoted, then refuses it in the tone reserved for heresy.
reactions.accused: For once the liturgy fails them: they ask whether the accusation has been struck, logged, or merely spoken.
reactions.flattered: Takes the praise as a counterfeit strike and finds its ring late, thin, struck by no honest hammer.
reactions.questioned: Recites their whereabouts like a strike-log, each hour named in the cadence of a rite they did not invent.
reactions.threatened: Their creed gives them nothing here; they recite seniority, the anvil's and their own, to fill the silence.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their slack hands let the foil unwind while oath and evidence quarrel inside one body.
reactions.authority_arrives: Bows to the anvil first and the official second, an order of precedence they do not revise.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The anvil is consulted first: they wait to hear whether it rang with the shudder or passed unlogged.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says the named one's work has been sound for years, too quickly, the way a witness rehearses.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses in one word, then lingers beside the asker past all reason, hands still shaped for a task.

npc.description: Ghaqthiamana the Oath-Returned stands hip-braced against the anvil's shadow, folding wound foil into ceramic seats with the tenderness of someone feeding a mouth. Their face is turned toward the blank anvil-face as if toward an audience. The wear of this place is entirely in them: skin glazed, eyes polished to mirror by years of the silver light.

lore.name: The Wound Foil Spool
lore.description: Foil wound in coils so fine the whole spool passes for a bar of dull tin. A rindwalker's knot marks the first turn — the pattern of a route no tunnel has run in living memory.

content.name: The Struck Anvil of Last Call
content.description: Hot ceramic and ionised foil first — a smell like the inside of a struck bell made oven-sweet, beryllia toasted until it dreams. The anvil sits in its own hemisphere of silver light, and no one is striking it; each ring arrives anyway, arriving late. Beyond the anvil's lip, the room declines to have edges. Stencilled along a stanchion: STRIKES LOGGED NO OPERATOR PRESENT.

npc.name: Ovlevozhi Rothzhyasky
npc.voice: Liturgical trade-slang; measures things in faiths and tolerances, never in years.

open.says: Older than the asking. I was taught the ship was built, and I believed it the way you believe in tomorrow — until I cut into a font-wall and found the tooling beneath the oldest scripture we keep. The scripture was copied from it. We are the latecomers here, child; our whole civilization is a settling, a scum on a surface that was already deep. Whatever set this level wanted it set before there was a Nave to notice.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
Then nothing down here is ours.

greet.says: Mind the rim. It remembers being full, and resents the comparison.

choices.text: What was the level here before?
Who do you file your work to?
You mend this, or worship it?
How old is the thing you serve?
I'll come back when you're finished.

probe_a.says: A holding, not a number. You don't measure what you tend — you keep it kept. The glass still carries the weight of it, if you hold it to the strip-light long enough to go half-blind.

probe_b.says: To the count. Saturn keeps the tale-count, they say, and we keep the fonts, and between us the arithmetic closes. Though of late my filings come back unmarked, which is either forgiveness or a closed mouth.

probe_c.says: Ask a hand that question while it holds a wound shut. The distinction is for people whose work hasn't yet become their kneeling.

reactions.grief: The sheet of black glass slips her grip for the first time in a decade of holdings.
reactions.shock: She kneels to the body as to the font, thumb tracing the rim's curve, tending what cannot be tended.
reactions.bribed: Asks what tolerance of forgetting they're buying, then names her price in faiths they cannot mint.
reactions.accused: Stops mid-lift, the black glass trembling in her grip, and corrects their grammar before their charge.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads to her like a doctored level; she checks it against the rim before answering.
reactions.questioned: Recites her rounds like a versicle, each hour a tolerance kept, and surrenders the ledger unasked.
reactions.threatened: Her eyes go to the basin's rim, checking whether the level heard him say it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Doesn't retract; she re-consecrates the falsehood, calling her old answer a rounding the level allows.
reactions.authority_arrives: Does not look up from the rim; jurisdiction ends where the source begins, and both know it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Every eye finds the walls; hers go to the basin, praying the level holds while the world tilts.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks for the accused in full liturgy, too long, too rehearsed, overspeaking a relief she won't confess.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Answers the plea with the stencil's litany — level constant, source not found — and tends the asker anyway.

npc.description: Ovlevozhi Rothzhyasky stands ankle-deep in a lull of the font, lifting a sheet of black glass against the light as though listening to it refuse. Something vast has gone from the basin — the emptiness has edges, and she works around them the way one mends around a dead tooth.

lore.name: The Plumb of Unanswered Depth
lore.description: Hung from a cantilever above the basin hangs a plumb line of wound foil, long enough that its bob should long since have struck bottom — it has not. Someone has knotted a Rindwalker's route-cord into the line at intervals, measuring against a human scale, and the knots grow further apart the deeper the line goes, as if depth itself were dilating to accommodate the question. The last knot is tied in a pattern Sevin's people use only for sealed tunnels: this way lies something that was measured once and declined to be measured again.

content.name: Fontworks
content.description: The smell arrives first: ozone folded into wet slate, the scent of a thing breathing cold instead of air. The basin before you holds a level of something that does not ripple, does not reflect, does not consent to be depth — and around it the floor steps down in terraces, each older than the last, as though the room had been excavated rather than built. Where the great occupant stood, the dark still holds its shape, a negative posture the light refuses to fill. On the inner curve of the basin, stencilled in a hand gone patient with repetition: LEVEL CONSTANT SOURCE NOT FOUND. A figure works at the rim and does not look up.

npc.name: Feinifeme-Faitonga
npc.voice: Brief, task-shaped. She talks in the rhythm of someone counting what still needs doing. If you ask a real question she slows down and answers it.

her.says: Someone has to carry the knot back down the Braid so the route history doesn't die with them. It's not staying. It's moving last. There's a difference, and nobody on this floor ever believed me.

who.says: My sister's line. Nine of them under this floor, counting births. They took a contract hauling freight up-axle. Boats don't turn around up there. You pack like you know that.

choices.text: What's this rail along the floor?

rail.says: Every name that ever left, burned in by whoever stayed. Rule of the boat. I'm the last cut. After me, nothing. That's why I scrub slow.

greet.says: Mooring's still paid through the month, so you can stand there all you like. I'm stripping the berth before the broker counts it.

reactions.grief: She asks who stayed to burn the name in, and when she hears it was nobody, the brush drops.
reactions.shock: The body is the first thing in years she has looked at without counting, and her hands just hang.
reactions.bribed: She refuses the coin but names what it would have bought down the Braid, so they know she counted.
reactions.accused: She sets the brush down flat and asks them to say it again slower, so she remembers who said it.
reactions.flattered: Under the praise she watches the door and starts costing what the favor will take.
reactions.questioned: Her answer is a count, three bundles and one stove run, and her eyes never leave the boards.
reactions.threatened: Threats to the berth don't land; she goes still only when they say her name will never be burned in.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Mid-count she loses her place, and the second recount gives her away worse than the lie did.
reactions.authority_arrives: She keeps scrubbing until the official says the word dues, then turns around for the first time.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her palm goes flat to the wall before she names the joint the sound came from.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She gives the accusation thirty seconds, then starts listing what the named person could not have lifted alone.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says she has no room to carry anyone, then keeps talking anyway, about the nine who went up-axle.

npc.description: Feinifeme-Faitonga works a stiff brush across the bare floor, sleeves tied back, knuckles white on the handle. Magenta printed silk, cut into work aprons, keeps catching on the brush. She has sorted the cured hide into three bundles by the door, and none of them are hers.

lore.name: The Keel Rail of Names
lore.description: A rail bolted low along the berth's curve, polished smooth by hands. Burned into it, one above another, are names and dates of departure — every family member who has ever left this boat, newest cut still bright. The rail is not decoration. It holds the floor plates down. The family built their home's spine out of leaving.

content.name: Stack 78 Over
content.description: The heat sits low, under the floor plates where the stove pipe used to run. Everything above is cold. The berth is steep and narrow, and a family's worth of bedding is gone from it, leaving pale rectangles on the wall. On the door frame, stenciled: MOORING DUES POSTED FIRST OF THE MONTH. A woman is scrubbing.

npc.name: Seiwibek-Urtonga
npc.voice: Terse, counting under everything. Talks in the rhythm of a deal.

greet.says: Sit or move on, I deal to players. You want the Braid, ask at the market. You want a chair, there's one opening after this hand.

choices.text: What's the house rule about every third hand?

house.says: House takes a cut, cards go in the tray, tray seals, I deal on. Nobody counts past that. Sit down or clear the rail.

reactions.grief: Mid-count she loses the number entirely, thumbs the route-marks on her cord, and finishes the hand on feel.
reactions.shock: Her hands keep dealing square while her eyes stay on the body, and the house rule holds her upright.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the house cut before the offer is done, and tells them the tray seals the same either way.
reactions.accused: The deal stops dead in her hands, nine cards hanging, and she asks them to say the name again.
reactions.flattered: The compliment gets the same nod as a tip, and she deals on without asking what it is they want.
reactions.questioned: Gives the hours in deal-order, terse and squared, and asks whether that finishes it.
reactions.threatened: Threats cost nothing at this table; she sets the burn tray between them and keeps dealing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She repeats the house line once, flat, then hands over a detail nobody asked for.
reactions.authority_arrives: She seats the official away from the trays and deals the next hand louder than she needs to.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For one breath the count in her head goes blank; then she checks the floor, the door, and deals.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names three hands where the man sat, then stops herself two cards into a defense she never meant to start.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: There is nothing she can lend; she pushes back a chair anyway and looks away from the crying.

npc.description: Seiwibek-Urtonga deals at the long table without looking at the cards, sliding them in flat arcs that land square every time. A knotted cord circles one wrist, thick with route-marks. Sweat and saffron dye have made a map of stains across the apron.

lore.name: The Third-Hand Tray
lore.description: Bolted under the dealer's station is a glass tray with three slots. Every third hand, the used cards go in the middle slot, and the slot seals with a click. The tray is scored with tallies scratched into the glass, thousands of them, one per seal. Whatever the house does with those hands, it has been doing it without a break for longer than anyone here has worked.

content.name: Sinadaf's Card Room
content.description: The smell hits first: card-dust, ash from the burn tray, and the saffron dye they soak the felt in, sharp enough to taste. Every table is full and two games run standing at the counter. Under the smoke the lamps burn too bright, and the walls hold nothing but a stenciled line: HOUSE DEALS EVERY THIRD HAND.

npc.name: Lett-al-Lilukk
npc.voice: Quick, sidelong, always handing you half an answer and keeping the route of it. Talks like a bet in progress.

self.says: For myself I keep one bout that didn't settle. Fourteen seasons I've been yards-keeper and every ring I've built, I build it to the same marks, same chalk, same rule on the wall. Some things you rebuild until they answer you. This one hasn't.

choices.text: Rebuild it how many more times?
I'll come back for the eighth bell.

braid.says: Mine run along the Braid, same as everything worth knowing. Difference is mine settle at a bell you can point to. The terminals post mythographs for tellings nobody's had yet — I'll take chalk and a bell over that fog.

choices.text: You don't read the postings at all?

greet.says: First bout's not till the eighth bell. You're early, or you're looking for something the yard doesn't post on the door.

choices.text: I was told the yard keeps the true roster of the range.
The ring's new. Where'd the old one go?

roster.says: True roster. Ha. Everything moves through a yard — bodies, grudge, odds. I keep the odds. The grudge keeps itself.

choices.text: Whose odds? Yours, or the Braid's?
And what do you keep for yourself?

oldring.says: Old ring? There's no old ring. There's this one, corrected to spec, and nothing before it worth a cord's weight. You'd want Sevin for stories like that, and she'd charge.

choices.text: You said 'corrected'. What was wrong with it?

reactions.grief: The wager-talk stops; they say the name back once and sweep the same clean spot of chalk, over and over.
reactions.shock: They freeze with the chalk still raised, then look at the door, the wire, anywhere the body isn't.
reactions.bribed: Weighs it the way they'd weigh a wager, longer than honesty needs, then names the ring unbuyable.
reactions.accused: Their alibi comes out as a bet: a bell, a witness, one count off if anyone checks.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets re-marked at true worth while they watch for the ask still coming.
reactions.questioned: Gives odds and half the route, quick, correct, and never the end of it.
reactions.threatened: Quotes the wall rule back at them, first fall wins, while their free hand finds the wrist knot.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Mid-sentence the route collapses; they build a second story that fits the evidence worse and bet on it anyway.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door moves and they are up off the floor too fast, chalk gone quiet, every answer pre-counted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Palm flat on the new stone, they wait out the shudder, reading it like a ring that won't answer.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name lands and their ring-logic comes out fighting, where the chalk sat, which bell rang, said twice, said louder.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say what the yard can post and what it can't, honest as a bout with no bell.

npc.description: Lett-al-Lilukk is crouched at the ring's edge, sweeping chalk off the new stone with the flat of a hand, sleeves knotted at the bicep. A knotted cord at their wrist catches when they reach. They came up off the floor too fast when the door moved.

lore.name: Chalk tin of Range 279
lore.description: The chalk tin under the shelf is old, dented, and someone has knotted a cord around its lid — one knot for every bout held in the previous ring, if you knew how to read it.

content.name: Wrestling Yard, Range 279
content.description: The floor grit is new-crushed, sharp through boot soles, none of it smoothed to greasy polish the way a good ring gets. White stone rings, chalk circle bright as a first fall of powder, walls close enough to scrape a shoulder on throw. Stencilled over the belt-height shelf: FIRST FALL WINS, NO GRIPS BELOW THE BELT. A coil of spun wire sits by the door, waiting on nobody.

npc.name: Brunbrand Sondgrisen
npc.voice: Short sentences, workshop cadence. Talks about glass the way others talk about people. Doesn't soften anything for a stranger.

work.says: Annealing. Slow cooling, or it carries the fight inside it and splits later. Most things work that way, if you ask me. That shelf you're leaning near disagrees.

choices.text: And the argument I walked in on?

greet.says: Door's for walkers, not watchers. You buying pitch or carrying a message?

right.says: Tolve. He's always right on a long enough count, that's the trouble with him. I'd rather be wrong and still working come morning.

choices.text: Tell me about the glass itself.

shelf.says: Safe as anything here. We propped it four years back, my mother and I, the week before she went down the shafts and didn't come up. The maul's hers. It holds. That's the whole of what I know.

choices.text: Down the shafts — what does that mean?

teach.says: Sit, then. First rule: nothing hot goes anywhere fast. Not glass, not people. Watch the pan and tell me when the shine goes out of it.

shafts.says: It means she went down the shafts. Ask a different walker and you'll get a different answer, all of them true. Me, I cool glass slowly and keep the draft out. That's my faith, and it fits in a shed.

choices.text: Then I'll leave you to it.
Could you teach me the cooling?

argument.says: That was Tolve and me. He wants to strip the third kiln for parts before Terrace 218's run. I say a shed that's still working doesn't get eaten. He says everything gets eaten eventually, so better on our terms.

reactions.grief: She starts explaining that he cooled too fast, carries the fight inside, and her knife hand goes still.
reactions.shock: The ladle stays where she set it down; she looks at the body and keeps looking, work undone.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced aloud, plus the cost of looking away, and the total comes up short.
reactions.accused: Accused of what, she wants first — cracked, split, or dropped — because the answer decides whose work this smells like.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands warmer than she wants it to, and she takes it out on the pitch pot instead.
reactions.questioned: She recites her day the way she reads a kiln log — temperatures, times, nothing volunteered past the question.
reactions.threatened: Her voice keeps its workshop level while her thumb finds the old burn at her wrist and presses.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The second time she tells it, the lie comes out quieter, and she hears the bubble in it herself.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets one look; her creed puts watchers outside, and the pan needs her more.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Glass first, people after — her hands go to the ochre pan before anyone finishes shouting.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She wants to know where he was standing when it happened, because Tolve never had the hands for quiet work.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She refuses the way she'd refuse a repair past saving, then names the work she can still offer.

npc.description: Brunbrand Sondgrisen stands with a pitch knife still in hand, sleeves rolled over forearms mapped with old burn-shine. She looks at you the way she'd look at a crack in a seam — locating it, pricing it.

lore.name: The propped shelf
lore.description: The maul under the sagging shelf is worn smooth on one handle — someone's hand, years of the same grip. It is not a tool for this. It holds anyway.

content.name: The Anneal Shed, Terrace 217
content.description: A horn ladle swings from a rack, still swaying — someone set it down seconds ago. Two figures stand either side of a cooling pan of ochre glass, mid-argument, and go quiet. Pitch pots crowd the bench; the stencil on the door reads KILN COOLING, NO DRAFT, and someone has scratched 'again' beneath it. The third annealing shelf sags in the middle, propped on a spare maul.

npc.name: Qoud Haibani
npc.voice: Short. Values a straight question. Doesn't explain what doesn't need explaining.

why.says: It doesn't. It waits for the next job worth the smoke. Canvas doesn't rot in a dry room. I packed the frames for the loft two terraces up — they'll want sails by next dark. Everything made is made twice.

choices.text: And the line on the slate?

marn.says: A wind-catcher for the axial line, big enough to fill that gap you noticed. She took the cloth upstairs and never cut it. Now you know what every newcomer to this room knows. Mind the chalk on your way out.

greet.says: Cutting room's closed. What's chalked stays chalked. Ask fast or hold the lamp.

choices.text: What happens to a room that stops making?
That line cut into the slate — why not finish it?

slate.says: That was Marn's mark. She drew it, cut everyone else's cloth, and never her own. Some work you stop before the scissors. Not superstition. She said the pattern was wrong and couldn't say how. We keep it marked because she was right more often than any of us.

reactions.grief: She cuts against the grain for the first time in years and finishes the whole length before looking up.
reactions.shock: The chalk stick drops from her fingers and she stands in the dust without sweeping it from her shoes.
reactions.bribed: She considers the offered goods longer than she wants to, then asks what the silence is worth by weight.
reactions.accused: The bung stops short of the crate and she turns, for once, to ask who told them that.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them in four words and holds out the wrong tool to see if they notice.
reactions.questioned: Answers over her shoulder without turning from the bung crate, each movement accounted for in the order it happened.
reactions.threatened: Something cold and small settles in her and she keeps her voice at work-day pitch.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She blames the chalk, says a mark wore away, and her hands keep folding canvas that is already flat.
reactions.authority_arrives: The shears go down on the slate shelf and she stands square until the official states their business.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Chalk sifts from the lowest terrace and she counts the shelves with her eyes before anyone else speaks.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She talks too long about every good seam the accused ever cut, then stops herself mid-list.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says plainly what she cannot make, then chalks the door of someone who might.

npc.description: Qoud Haibani works down the last cork bung into a crate of marking tools. Extra arms fold the waxed canvas squares flat without hurry. She talks with her back to you until a question earns better.

lore.name: The Marking Slate
lore.description: A slate panel three feet square hangs from the stair rail, the workhorse of this room. Patterns for every canvas cut here get chalked onto it first, approved, then traced. Chalk layers on chalk. At the bottom edge, older than the rest, someone scored one line deep with a blade instead of chalk — against the rule, permanent, and still not cut. Whoever did it left the cloth up to the mark and stopped.

content.name: Nwltruddwy
content.description: Smoke from waxed canvas and scorched cork hangs in the air. The room climbs in three steep terraces of slate shelving; chalk dust coats the lowest. A rust stencil on the stair rail reads CHALK LINES ONLY, NO SCISSORS TILL MARKED. One wall holds a clean gap, floor scoured, where something big stood.

npc.name: Nokhu-Pebeiloa
npc.voice: Short, dry, counts everything — cards, words, favors. Talks like the room is already too full for sentences.

who.says: Order came through the Braid, no knot signature on it. A season ago that would've been nothing. Lately the relay traffic carries things nobody will put their cord to, and I've stopped asking. Deal your own hand, friend.

greet.says: Sit or move on. Table's full, floor's full, and the white paint means both parties own it, so mind your elbows.

paint.says: White went up a season back. Before that the walls showed every debt and grudge in chalk, and someone — not me — decided the room should look like nothing had ever happened here. New coat, same debts. Worse, actually. Now nobody can check.

ledger.says: Decides who deals third hand next season, and third hand deals the pot's tithe. Lose the count, lose the floor. Which is why I deal sideways and don't touch the slate. Both counts stay honest as long as neither hand is mine.

parties.says: House crowd plays odd nights, Braid crowd plays even. Nobody surrendered the third hand, so the ledger keeps both counts and the slate has holes in it. That's as settled as it gets.

reactions.grief: No pause in the dealing, and no name said, though they count the finished deck four times before trusting it.
reactions.shock: Their eyes count the body the way they count cards, once, twice, and the third pass takes their voice.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer aloud, down to the coin, then names a debt it wouldn't cover and resumes the shuffle.
reactions.accused: Asks, twice, for the charge in writing — then remembers there is no chalk anywhere, and their hands go still.
reactions.flattered: Thanks them in the tone reserved for weather and deals them a worse hand than the flattery earned.
reactions.questioned: Answers in counts, not stories — four hands dealt, three visitors, one errand — and keeps dealing sideways through it.
reactions.threatened: Names the odds on the threat out loud, three to one it's empty, and deals faster than the count allows.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Deals a hand faceup by accident, the first in years, then repeats the lie exactly, as if it never wavered.
reactions.authority_arrives: Nudges the unclaimed beaded cord a hand's width under the stool with one boot, then greets the official by title.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Says nothing while the room tilts, then recounts the deck twice, as if the shake could have dealt a card.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Has dealt them a hundred hands and says so, flat, then argues longer than they have ever argued anything.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Doesn't refuse aloud; marks the debt on the bare table where chalk used to be, which changes nothing.

npc.description: Nokhu-Pebeiloa deals from a sideways seat, wrist-cord knotted tight, shuffling a deck gone soft as cloth. They wear the bright white like everyone else but theirs is splattered, older, painted over at least twice.

lore.name: The Third-Hand Ledger
lore.description: Under the dealer's chair, taped flat, a slate tallies every third hand dealt in this room for what looks like years. The marks split into two columns with two different hands on them — one tidy, one rushed — and where the columns disagree, someone has drilled a small hole through the slate rather than scratch either side out. The count never stops; it just changes handwriting.

content.name: Shaadan's Card Room
content.description: The dealer's stool sits a hand's width from the table's edge, close enough that Nokhu-Pebeiloa must deal sideways, and everyone pretends this is normal. Bright white paint covers every wall down to the chair legs, and the stencil over the card shelf reads HOUSE DEALS EVERY THIRD HAND. The room holds forty and holds thirty-nine badly; a cane leans by the door beside a knotted beaded cord nobody claims.

npc.name: Shixiorvastro Tiochisthisenne
npc.voice: Careful, precedent-conscious, given to citing what was done before — the cadence of someone who believes a record kept past all reason is the only thing standing between the generation and rupture.

deep.says: No — and I say no without apology, because the shafts beyond the drum-housing are court-ground, and the court there is not the council's and not mine and not, I think, fond of uninvited guests. What I will tell you is this: go up the axial, and when the halls grow too large for the people in them, keep going until you feel watched by something that has not bothered to look in three centuries. That is as close as a clerk should point. Closer than most clerks would.

crowd.says: Stopped? The tally-halt was ordered, yes — writ of the belt council, a year past. But a count interrupted is not a count closed, and these people understand what most of the council does not: that a generation unnumbered is a generation that can be lost without anyone noticing. They stay because staying is the work. I stay because if I left, the last precedent in this room would be abandonment.

choices.text: "What is it the drum keeps finding?"
Nod, and let the drum carry you back around.

greet.says: You'll forgive me for not standing; the lectern comes round again whether I do or not. This is the Census Drum, and the census is not concluded, and while it is not concluded someone must attend it. State your name for the record — or don't, and become one of the ones I can't match.

choices.text: "Unmatched? The drum counts people who aren't on the roll?"
"Why does everyone stay if the work has stopped?"

whose.says: The drum was here before the desks, the desks before me, and the roll-cant before any of us — I have matched handwriting three hundred years older than my grandmother's and it is the same hand. Ask me who runs the belt and I will answer with names. Ask me who runs this, and I will tell you it is above the council, above the decks, up where the skin of the ship begins — and that the one who holds court there does not bother with us often, but the drum's orders were never written by a person.

choices.text: "Could you show me where the orders come from?"
"Then I'll leave the record in your hands."

unmatched.says: Counts itself clean every rotation — forty-one recountings and the same remainder, and Factor Solen has read the audits and elected to read no further, which is her prerogative and, I have come to suspect, her fear wearing its work clothes. The drum does not err. It has never once erred. So either the roll is short or the population is long, and I have not yet decided which of those frightens me more.

choices.text: "Who told the drum what to count?"
"Keep your count. I'll leave you to it."

reactions.grief: The exact hour is her first question, the record's need outrunning her grief, until she cannot recall the deceased's tally-number.
reactions.shock: The body comes round on the drum's circuit, and she watches it pass a second and third time, stylus motionless.
reactions.bribed: Named sums mean nothing to her; she prices the offer in entries falsified and finds the arithmetic refutation enough.
reactions.accused: She demands the accusation be entered in the record, word for word, and her stylus skips on the first letter.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands where the halted tally left her hollow, and she thanks them before remembering to ask the price.
reactions.questioned: She turns to the day's entry and reads her own movements back, dates and all, before the question finishes.
reactions.threatened: Her answer is precedent: what became of the last three who threatened a Continuant, delivered without hurry.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted with the contradiction, she stops defending and opens the amendment ledger herself, voice gone dry as the mineral-crusted tea.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official receives precedent before greeting, the council's writ laid across the lectern pending countersignature.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She times the shudder against the drum's forty-minute turn, and finding no entry for it, goes very still.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She offers three precedents in the accused's favor, then marks a fourth beside their name, uncited.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She recites exactly which powers the writ withholds, more clauses than the plea required, as if precision were mercy.

npc.description: Shixiorvastro Tiochisthisenne stands at a lectern bolted to the drum's rotating flank, riding the slow circuit it forces on anyone who would keep their place — desk, stylus, ledger moving past the same view of the crowd every forty minutes. Continuant slate-blue hangs off her in panels gone shiny at the elbows; she has the look of a person who stopped expecting the room to empty and started organizing around it instead.

lore.name: The unmatched roll
lore.description: The drum's face is banded with tally-windows, each lit with a count — and one band, near the seam where the silver plating was cut back for inspection, burns steady and refuses to resolve. A brass pointer rests against it, worn concave on its underside from years of the same pressure: the clerks kept returning to the number that would not close. Scratched beneath the window, in a small tidy hand: recounted 41 times. The count exceeds the roll by the same figure every audit. Someone aboard the Tabard is alive who was never entered, and the drum has never once disagreed with itself about how many.

content.name: Saedetha's Census Drum
content.description: Something is still turning when you come in — the great drum, silver-shelled, wide as a grain silo, rotating a fraction slow enough that you could almost believe you imagined it. Around its base the Continuants' tally-desks stand exactly as their clerks left them: styluses in their grooves, a cup of tea gone to mineral crust, and the crowd that never left presses shoulder to shoulder among the desks as though the count might resume at any breath. Stencilled along the drum's flank, in letters a hand could lie down inside: DRUM CAPACITY EXCEEDS CURRENT ROLL. Vitrified ash has drifted in through some vent and lies over everything in a grey glass snow that squeaks underfoot.

npc.name: Karainah Nanawi
npc.voice: Short sentences, load-rated. She talks about people the way she talks about fixtures — what they carry, where they're worn.

told.says: By whoever tells anyone anything now. The postings changed their pattern weeks back — ask a Braid wrist if you don't believe me. He read them closer than most. Then he read them like instructions.

choices.text: And you? Do you read them?

floor.says: That's not damage, that's inheritance. You splice the load back into the weave so the next body doesn't fall through a stranger's shortcuts. He understood that much. The last splice is his, and it's rushed, and it bothers me.

greet.says: Room's spoken for. You're standing where the heat doesn't reach — move back a step. Who sent you up a stevedore's stair?

tenant.says: A hauler. Carried more than the stair was built for, and paid for the overage in work, not coin. Left between one shift and the next. Nobody leaves like that unless they were told to.

endnode.says: I read the walls. The walls haven't changed their mind in my lifetime. Sit down if you're staying, the grating's coldest but it's honest.

reactions.grief: The name lands; she stacks the same three coils twice before asking whether anyone checked his last splice.
reactions.shock: Two hands reach the body before she decides to move; one lies flat on it, waiting for lift.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets weighed to the grain, named for what it would cost the next body, and handed back.
reactions.accused: The accusation gets the question she gives any load: rated by whom, tested when, sworn to what.
reactions.flattered: Praise leaves her hands the way unstamped freight does: turned over twice, checked for the weight hidden in it.
reactions.questioned: Her answer comes in manifest order — day, hour, load — each fact already stowed.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands on her like a load check; she names its weight out loud, quieter than she means to.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she rerates the story aloud — a smaller lie, better built — while one hand drifts to block the stair.
reactions.authority_arrives: She doesn't rise; she declares the room's load, its standing rules, and which step he may pass.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her palm goes flat to the floor between tremors, checking the building the way she'd check a chest.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She audits the accusation aloud — wear points, route habits — and clears him faster than loyalty would.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She answers with a refusal rated honestly — past her capacity — then gives the one thing that isn't.

npc.description: Karainah Nanawi stands with one hand flat on the bare floor, the way you'd check a chest for breath. She has more arms than a person should and is using all of them — coiling, sorting, closing the room down. The other one stops arguing the moment you step in.

lore.name: The cable cradle
lore.description: Where the bed stood, rope-laid cable has been woven into the floor bolts themselves — not tied, spliced, each strand worked back into the weave so the whole floor carries the load instead of one fixing. This is how you keep something that isn't yours to keep: you leave the room stronger than you found it, and the next tenant inherits the work without knowing whose hands did it. One splice is newer than the rest, cut and redone in a hurry.

content.name: Lladdpedgae
content.description: The cold comes up through the landing grating and pools at ankle height; the rest of the room stays warm from a pipe someone wrapped in boiled leather and never explained. The bed is gone — four bolt-holes and a clean rectangle in the floor dust say something large left by the steep stair, not the door. On the doorframe, stencilled: NO COOKING PAST THE THIRD STEP.

npc.name: Zyaduna Vothsky
npc.voice: Ledger-cadence, Saturn-slow; they answer questions about the room with weights, never names.

greet.says: You displaced two grains crossing the threshold. I felt it. — Take this foil. It remembers a tension nothing here has caused in my tenure. Saturn may want it read.

choices.text: You sleep among the heaviest goods?

leave.says: Two grains. I'll enter them.

ask_sleep.says: Lightness is a debt down here. I sleep inboard to pay it.

take_foil.says: Mind the gap between the twins. It isn't distance.

reactions.grief: For the first time in memory, Zyaduna writes a name into the ledger, pressing hard enough to tear foil.
reactions.shock: Zyaduna freezes mid-entry, grain uncounted, because the body before them outweighs anything their grades were built to hold.
reactions.bribed: The bribe goes onto the scales out of habit; Zyaduna returns it ungraded, which down here is refusal absolute.
reactions.accused: The accusation lands as a weight Zyaduna cannot grade; they ask, quietly, what unit it should be entered under.
reactions.flattered: Praise unsettles Zyaduna; they credit every ounce of it to the foil, which has never once lied to them.
reactions.questioned: Zyaduna answers in tonnage, never names, and files the interrogation under a column headed 'routine.'
reactions.threatened: Menace finds no purchase; Zyaduna recites the room's stencil, slower each repetition, a creed worn as cover.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted, Zyaduna repeats the false figure in a smaller voice, as if a lighter lie might pass unweighed.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official's arrival shifts the room's gravity; Zyaduna moves one grade inboard and keeps writing, deference measured in inches.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Nothing here arrives on time; Zyaduna waits out the shudder's late echo before believing it happened at all.
reactions.someone_else_accused: When the culprit is named, Zyaduna over-answers, reciting that person's exact load history as though tonnage could be alibi.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Asked for what storage cannot give, Zyaduna opens their hands, empty of foil, and lets the plea sit unentered.

npc.description: Zyaduna Vothsky wakes inside the grades — bedroll laid where the heaviest goods belong, which they will tell you is the point — and rises without hurry, foil dust settling off them like thought leaving a room.

lore.name: the ninth cell's ledger-scratch
lore.description: Etched inside the ninth cell's rim, tally-marks in Saturn's oldest notation — each mark thicker than the last, as if the stone had been accumulating weight of its own accord and someone kept count.

content.name: Warpworks
content.description: A case nearer the wall sits a handspan from the foil it indexes, while its twin hangs far off across the dark, and the pair answer to each other anyway — the gap is a fiction the room maintains. Threaded cells of cast basalt descend in grades of weight, iron-dark, wound in foil like veins bared for counting; the space between them carries footfalls somewhere behind the ear, arriving late. No shelf admits to being a shelf, no scale to weighing, yet everything is held. On the ninth cell, stencilled in rust: HEAVIEST INBOARD ALWAYS. Deep in the lower grades, where nothing light should settle, someone sleeps.

npc.name: Breikbomara Shavel
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical, spoken in the clipped cadence of someone counting a rite they no longer believe will conclude. She uses words correctly and slightly offset — 'shift,' 'debit,' 'return' — as if they were terms in a private contract with the room.

greet.says: You're early. Or I'm behind — the room debits time differently spinward, you learn not to ask. Speak once and wait; I've work between your sentence and its return. What is it you came down to say?

leave.says: Mind the strata on your way up. The salt remembers being an ocean; it resents being told.

ask_signal.says: It's not a signal. It's a return — has been since before the Nave was a word. Something spoke first, and the throat's been paying it back ever since. I just keep the debit square. That's the whole rite.

reactions.grief: Into her knot-cord she writes the name, steady-fingered, then loses the number she was on.
reactions.shock: Her scream arrives before she feels it, and the vault returns nothing, which frightens her more than the body does.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced aloud to the second, found cheap against a century of salt, refused without ceremony.
reactions.accused: The count stops mid-number; she names the accusation a false debit and asks which century the charge was entered.
reactions.flattered: Praise finds her mid-count; she audits the compliment like suspect mint, and her frost whorls tighter.
reactions.questioned: Recites her movements as audited entries, mint-clean, and adds nothing the count does not require.
reactions.threatened: She offers her hands palm-up and names the threat a clause already priced into her shift.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Corrected, she repeats the lie slower, as if errors were hers to sanctify, counting louder.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction enters, and she checks it against the older contract, deciding which authority the throat outranks.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder strikes and she says the room's name twice, like checking whether a debt still answers to its holder.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Bookkeeping, not mercy, is what she offers the named — square debits cited like scripture, her voice edging toward alarm.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to help, she grants the only rite she owns: one sentence spoken once, her silence until its return.

npc.description: Breikbomara Shavel is elbow-deep in a stratum of salt, coaxing something from between two compressed centuries with a pry-bar wound in knotted cord. The cord's pattern is wrong — not the worn-route history of the Braid, nor the worship-knots of the nave, but a personal notation, half devotional, half calender. Frost has built up on her shoulders in symmetric whorls, as if the cold here had opinions about arrangement. She does not startle when you arrive; she finishes her count first.

lore.name: The Deferent Bowl
lore.description: A shallow dish of black glass, chipped once and re-welded, sits at the throat's center on a salt plinth. Every few minutes it fills with a声音less condensation — your own breath, returned cold — and drains through a pinhole drilled with Rindwalker knotwork that no living hand has the pattern for.

content.name: Vault 47 Spinward
content.description: Sound arrives wrong here: a footstep leaves first, its echo comes after, and between them the vault swallows the middle of everything — no reverberation, only a silence so upholstered it has texture. The throat opens off the spinward gallery, walled in compacted salt pressed into strata like mile-deep snow, chalk-white and faintly luminous, and from somewhere within it a voice is already speaking — a beat late, a register low, repeating what you have not yet said. The floor is black glass, warm where no heat source is and cold at the walls; a maintenance cowl has been wedged against the far stratum, its copper holy-sigils worn to nubs, next to a stack of ration crates and a brazier crackling in flagrant contradiction to the frost feathering the glass around it. Across the salt, in old tellurion pigment: SPEAK ONCE AND WAIT FOR RETURN.

npc.name: Kis-Tiaz
npc.voice: Short sentences. Counts things before saying them. Talks about wood the way other people talk about family.

self.says: I think a wheel that fails on the far side of the belt kills someone I'll never meet. That's the whole argument. He thinks a wheel not delivered fails for certain. We're both right. That's the worst kind of disagreement.

greet.says: Bench row's full. Mind the gap or don't come in. You want spokes or you want to stand there?

choices.text: Why so many benches in one room?

kellor.says: Forty years at the bench next to mine. He taught me the knife grip I still use. Now he counts a bad spoke as good if the order needs it, and I can't decide if that's him changing or the work changing him.

choices.text: Which do you think it is?
I hope you two settle it.

settle.says: Time. Or one of us bending. Neither's on order. Pick up a knife if you're staying, or clear the gap. The bell doesn't wait on feelings.

strain.says: Kellor thinks yes. I think we're shaving green wood and calling it seasoned. You can hear the difference when it dries wrong. He doesn't want to hear it.

choices.text: Kellor being the one you were arguing with?

benches.says: Cartwrights' guild gave up its floor two bells east. We took their work because turning away a wheel is turning away the cart behind it. The room didn't grow. We did.

choices.text: Can you keep up with all of it?

reactions.grief: Their answer is a broom: shavings into a neat pile, swept long after the floor is clean.
reactions.shock: Tries to count the benches, gets a different number every time, and stops trusting their own eyes.
reactions.bribed: Refuses before the offer finishes, the way they scrap a spoke over one hidden flaw.
reactions.accused: Puts the knife down flat before answering, like a tool they no longer trust their hands with.
reactions.flattered: Letting the compliment sit until the asker fills the silence with the actual price.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day's spoke count before anything else, as if the tally itself were testimony.
reactions.threatened: Counts the doorways with their eyes the way they'd count spokes, and stays put anyway.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Corrects their own number out loud, even now, and stands there while it costs them.
reactions.authority_arrives: Keeps shaving the whole time the official talks, gripping the spoke hard enough to dent it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Inside, the wheelwright asks which joint failed, and no answer comes, and that silence is the frightening part.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends the old man's forty years, then stops short of vouching for his counts, and hates the gap.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no plainly, offers what the bench can spare, then works twice as long as the bell asks, ashamed.

npc.description: Kis-Tiaz stands at the first bench with a shaving knife flat against a blank spoke, not cutting. Their forearms are clean, the nails scrubbed, and only the creases of their knuckles hold umber dust that washing has given up on. They watch the player the way they watch a spoke for warp.

lore.name: The Count Board
lore.description: A plain glass pane hangs at the end bench, backed by umber cloth, and iron banding clamps it to the bench post. Scratched into the glass are columns of tally marks, one column per bell, going back further than the newest benches have existed. The last three columns are blank. Someone has written BELOW QUOTA beside them in a hand pressed hard enough to chip the glass.

content.name: The Spoke Row
content.description: The third bench sits too close to the fourth, so close the shavings pile into one heap under both. Six benches in a room built for four, and stacked crates leave a walking gap barely wider than a shoulder. The stencil on the wall reads SHAVINGS SWEPT AT EVERY BELL. Two workers stop talking when the door opens.

npc.name: Bygychnor Cor
npc.voice: Terse, practical, not unkind. Talks about the bell like a coworker, not a mystery.

bell.says: Twice is enough for anyone to be told the day's turned. More than that and it's noise, not worship. Now let me get out of here while the light holds.

greet.says: Chapel's finished. Bell rings at dawn and dusk, and not before, whatever you've heard. You want me for anything else?

reactions.grief: By the lamp he goes very still, then says the name twice, as if twice were enough.
reactions.shock: The cloth falls onto the coals unnoticed while he stares at the wound the way he checks his own castings.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the offer has to do with the bell, and, hearing nothing honest, packs faster.
reactions.accused: Stops cinching the tool roll mid-pull, knuckles white, asking which ringing the accuser even means.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit unanswered and wants to know what the roof needs before he believes any of it.
reactions.questioned: Answers by the day's clock, dawn ringing, dusk ringing, the hours between spent on the tool roll and nothing else.
reactions.threatened: He measures the door with a glance, decides the day's light is worth more than his pride, and stands down.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Overexplains the discrepancy down to the hour, naming everyone who saw him, which convinces nobody.
reactions.authority_arrives: Recites the stencil above the rope word for word, as though jurisdiction ended where the paint does.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The rope's swing he checks first, and only then allows that the shudder was nothing he did.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Half-defends the accused, gives it up as unprovable, and studies the swinging rope instead of the speaker.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Hears the plea through to the end without interrupting, then says plainly what he cannot do, and stays anyway.

npc.description: Bygychnor Cor packs tools into a canvas roll, moving with the speed of someone who has already stayed too long. Rope ends hang from a belt loop. A smudge of limewash crosses one cheekbone.

lore.name: Old rope splice
lore.description: The new rope is joined to the old pull-line with a splice wound tight in hemp twine. The old line is dark, stiff, and worn to gloss at the grip point.

content.name: Yard 85 Inboard
content.description: The bell rope still swings when you come in, though nobody is pulling it. Bygychnor Cor cools the lamp and folds a cloth. The limewash on the walls is a week old and unburnished; the air is smoky from the first firing, and daylight comes thin through the louvres. A stencil above the rope reads BELL RUNG AT DAWN AND DUSK ONLY.

npc.name: Fepeish-Khighfeloa
npc.voice: Terse. Answers in route-talk, short as knots.
