ask.says: Down the belt, with the rest of the loose weight. Things move. Take a knot from the cord if you're counting — I'm not.

greet.says: Table's gone ahead. If you want a chart copied, come back when there's a table.

leave.says: Mind the mica on your way out.

reactions.grief: They keep flattening mica, wrong side up, and talk for once, all route and schedule, nothing about now.
reactions.shock: Stillness takes them, and their eyes copy the scene anyway, angle by angle, the way they copy charts.
reactions.bribed: They name a higher price than the one offered, and watch whether the offerer flinches at the arithmetic.
reactions.accused: The stone stops moving, and they ask who says so, twice, the second time loud.
reactions.flattered: They ask what the praise is carrying, and which door it is meant for.
reactions.questioned: They give route, bell, and hour, and volunteer nothing a log would not already hold.
reactions.threatened: They name the exits, the belt speed, and how long a walk out would take, in that order.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their count is two knots short of the truth, and they give the short one anyway.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door gets one glance, long enough to log who entered, then their eyes return to the mica.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They flatten themselves over the loose sheets first, saving the work before thinking, then look up ashamed.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They say the named one was two berths down at second bell, and dare anyone to check the log.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say what they cannot do, once in route-talk and once plainly, and hate the second one.

npc.description: Fepeish-Khighfeloa sits on a crate, rolling mica sheets flat with a stone. They glance up once and go back to it.

lore.name: Copyist's cord
lore.description: A knotted cord hangs from the plank, one bead for every chart copied here. The last bead is tied off loose, unfinished.

content.name: Ikeikul
content.description: The smell is hot mica and saffron ink, the sharp sweetness of it. The big copying table is gone — four pale squares on the floor where its feet stood. A plank across two crates holds cords, sheets, a knife. On the wall, stenciled: NO INK NEAR THE MASTER CHARTS.

npc.name: Durnustusha Vonitsyn
npc.voice: Brisk, exact, fond of counts. She speaks in portions: what is enough, what is short, what is owed.

busy.says: Six stools, forty bellies a sitting, standing room out the door at second bell. Built small on purpose. A house that fits everyone serves no one. We turn folk away and they come back anyway. That's regard you can't buy.

choices.text: Nod and let her finish packing.

greet.says: Counter's closing. If you want broth, come at first bell like everyone else. I don't do standing service and I don't do late.

choices.text: Ask how long the house has been here.
Ask why the room seems busier than six stools allow.
Ask where she goes when the counter closes.

house.says: Longer than me, and I've been ladling here thirty years. The pot's older than the counter, older than the wall. We keep it fed and it keeps us fed. That's the whole arrangement, and it holds.

choices.text: Nod and let her finish packing.

leave.says: Home, two streets down, same as my mother did after her counter. You close clean, you sleep, you open again. Miss one opening and the whole thing comes apart. Nobody tells you that's the work. Continuity is just showing up, bell after bell.

reactions.grief: She asks how, then portions a bowl nobody ordered, usual amount, for a belly that won't come to fill it.
reactions.shock: The numbers leave her entirely; she stands at the far stool, the cold one, and cannot finish a count.
reactions.bribed: The money gets counted once and handed back, priced short against thirty years of the pot holding.
reactions.accused: She stops packing the till and counts the years back at them, thirty, one ladle, no debt.
reactions.flattered: Compliment the broth and she is pleased for exactly one breath, then hears the ask underneath and quotes the price.
reactions.questioned: Asked for her hours, she deals them in portions — first bell, second bell, between — nothing missing, nothing owed.
reactions.threatened: She recites the menu under her breath, every portion, because her voice needs somewhere to be while she is afraid.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her count breaks mid-number; she starts the portion over, slower, as if the first tally never happened.
reactions.authority_arrives: She seats the official at the cold end of the counter and quotes first bell, same as anyone.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Six bowls slide; she pins the stack before her face decides anything, pot checked first, people after.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She defends the name with her ledger, forty sittings recited from memory, then catches herself caring too much and stops.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: There is one thing she can give, and she gives it, plus the exact number of what she cannot.

npc.description: A broad woman in a slate apron gone thin at the hip, stacking bowls with the speed of someone who has done it ten thousand times and will not slow down for company.

lore.name: The Counting Broth-Pot
lore.description: Under the counter sits a dented pot with notches filed into its rim, one for every year the house has served without closing a single day. The newest notch is half-cut. Durnustusha files it each solstice, and the pot has outlasted three counters and every stool original to the room.

content.name: Dryazhelitsa
content.description: The heat sits at the broth end of the counter and nowhere else; the far stool still holds the morning's chill. Dust-white light crosses bleached linen. The rubber matting creaks underfoot. Stenciled on the counter edge: SIX STOOLS, NO STANDING SERVICE. Durnustusha Vonitsyn wipes down behind the till, packing up.

npc.name: Mafah Laikham
npc.voice: Quiet, exact, unbothered by visitors. Speaks about maintenance the way other people speak about faith, then catches herself doing it.

held.says: Once a year, to check the mend. Gloves, two witnesses. My mother held it before me, and hers before. The touching is part of the keeping. The sign isn't for us.

doubt.says: Sometimes. Some nights I think we mend and mend and the ship just wears at its own pace, and our work is a way of not noticing. Then the resin sets and the wall holds and I feel foolish for saying so. Even to you.

greet.says: Viewing only. The glass is there for a reason. You can look as long as you like, though — it doesn't wear out from being seen.

relic.says: A sail. Before the fans, they caught the moving air with cloth and turned it by hand. Llegweth kept this piece. We keep it because the stitchwork still holds. That's the whole teaching, if you want one.

repair.says: Nearly. The east wall was weeping resin, so we opened it up. Half the shrine is sheeting and clamps right now. It'll be done in six days. Everything I fix takes six days. I've stopped wondering about that.

teaching.says: That a thing made well outlasts the maker, and caring for it is how you keep the maker. I've held that cloth. It's lighter than you'd think. Most of what we guard is.

why_stay.says: Because the doubt is part of the work too. You check a stitch because you don't trust it. That's not heresy. That's just the job done properly. Anyway — I have two more tools to pack, and you have a shrine to look at.

choices.text: Look at the shrine, and let her work.

reactions.grief: Nobody has died on her watch before, and she keeps folding the cloth roll as though the roll needed her.
reactions.shock: Seeing it stills every hand she has, even the ones visitors are not meant to count, and she looks anyway.
reactions.bribed: Her refusal quotes procedure, what touching costs and who must witness it, her eyes never once on the coin.
reactions.accused: She stops mid-roll and says no twice, the second quieter, as if checking the accusation for loose threads.
reactions.flattered: Praise stills her more than accusation did; nobody has complimented the mending in years, and it lands somewhere unguarded.
reactions.questioned: Her answers come in the flat cadence of a maintenance log, each movement accounted for before the next question lands.
reactions.threatened: Threats reach her the way weather reports do, noted and measured, and she names her two witnesses before answering.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she becomes more exact, restating each word until the correction is worse than the mistake, hands finally still.
reactions.authority_arrives: She stands, brings her repair log unasked, and uncovers the case, ritual outranking introductions.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder gets logged aloud, direction and depth, and she checks the relic case before she checks the people.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her defense arrives as inventory, every mend that person finished on time, recited until she hears how much she cares.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She repeats her one offer, quieter each time, the way she talks to a mend that will not set.

npc.description: A woman in a rust-brown coat kneels by the case, wiping resin from a clamping tool with slow, practiced strokes. She has more arms than a person should and does not mention it. Her kit is half packed; two more tools still lie out.

lore.name: The Sailcloth of Llegweth
lore.description: Behind the glass lies a hand-span of sailcloth, brown with age, its weave tight and unbroken. Someone has sewn a strip of newer cloth along one edge — mending done with the same stitch pattern still used on the green deck awnings. The cloth is the whole relic: a piece of a sail that once turned air through the Nave before the fans were built. It is tended because cloth this old holding a stitchline means the hands that made it knew what they were doing, and the work itself is what gets kept.

content.name: Llegweth's Relic Shrine
content.description: The lamp here flickers twice before settling, as if it must decide each time whether to stay on. A narrow room, most of it curtained off behind resin sheeting where the repair is half done. A single case holds a folded square of sailcloth, and a stenciled notice beside it reads RELIC NOT TO BE TOUCHED, VIEWING ONLY. A worker is packing tools into a cloth roll.

npc.name: Nara-Mione
npc.voice: Fast, clipped, mid-deal even when there is no deal — everything is a swap, an estimate, a turnaround time. Weighs her words the way she weighs freight: to the kilo, no sentiment.

work.says: A strain-cell gave a number it had no business giving, so we opened her. Bridge held ten cars at full for six hundred years; the day it lies to me is the day I stop trusting anything with a dial on it. Two weeks, maybe three, and Mercury's traffic rolls over new quartz.

choices.text: Ask what she means by Mercury's traffic.
Ask about the copper tally-plate bolted to cell four.

greet.says: Mind the open cells — deck's rated for you at one person, and you're it. If you're carrying anything worth weighing, I'm not buying today.

choices.text: Ask what broke, and when it'll carry again.

plate.says: Before my predecessor's predecessor, by the bolt-holes. Drift woman, kept her own tallies in duplicate because the bridge once told her a lie about a load of grain. She was right to. I read that plate the first day I worked here and it's the only sermon I've kept.

deeper.says: Runners go as far as the relay galleries and no further — past that, the hum stops being hum and starts being attention, if you take my meaning. We move what moves. What sits still down there can keep itself.

choices.text: Let her get back to work.

mercury.says: Everything crossing this deck is going somewhere, and the somewhere is Mercury's. You feel it down in the cut sometimes — a hum like a held note, and the rails warm before any train comes. I don't pray to it. I just don't insult it by shipping late.

choices.text: Ask whether anyone goes down where the hum comes from.

reactions.grief: She asks the date twice, then checks her ledger for the last day that name crossed her deck.
reactions.shock: The filament keeps feeding through her fingers long after her eyes have stopped seeing anything but the body.
reactions.bribed: She quotes them the exact weight of their offer, finds it light, and goes back to the filament.
reactions.accused: Her eyes come up for once, and the silence where her figures should be weighs more than the accusation.
reactions.flattered: Praise sits in her like unverified cargo — she wants to weigh it, and knows the wanting is the trap.
reactions.questioned: Her answer is already a tally: weights in, weights out, and the duplicate ledger offered before anyone asks.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets priced like freight, because a number she can hold frightens her less than the hand behind it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She blames a lying strain-cell for the discrepancy, though her thumb has found the pale band on her forehead.
reactions.authority_arrives: She keeps feeding filament, asking to see the official's manifest as if jurisdiction were a load to declare.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her hand flattens against the nearest strain-member; no dial answers fast enough, so she reads the shudder through her palm.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Forty crossings in her tallies show the accused's loads sitting true, and she says so before the name is out.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Mid-estimate she stops, because the plea has no weight she can quote and no swap she can name.

npc.description: Nara-Mione works kneeling in the opened half of the deck, feeding drawn filament into a fusion-head by hand because the feeder broke a season back and the replacement is still, by her own account, coming. Goggles of fused quartz sit pushed up on her brow, and the light through them has left a pale band across her forehead. She talks without looking up until she decides you are worth looking up for.

lore.name: the tally-plate on cell four
lore.description: Bolted to one strain-cell is a copper plate, older than the paint around it, engraved with columns of numbers — weights and dates going back further than the Drift has kept records anywhere in the Nave. The newest entry is decades old, but every figure in the last hundred rows has been counted twice, the second tally written smaller beside the first, and the two columns never disagree. Whoever kept this plate did not trust the bridge, or did not trust themselves, and checked anyway; the habit outlived them by a long margin of nothing.

content.name: Nomvaizys's Weighbridge
content.description: The smell reaches you first: hot quartz, sweet and sharp as a struck flint, with something greener under it — filament sizing cooking off in the warmth of a repair-bay lamp. Nomvaizys's Weighbridge stretches away over a transit cut, its deck opened down to the strain-members along half its ten-car length, the other half still carrying loaded freight without complaint. Green-black paint, thick as tide-mud, coats everything and has been cut through in neat squares where new welds sit bright. A stencil older than its own letters' meaning reads WEIGHBRIDGE RATED, DO NOT EXCEED POSTED LIMIT, and under it someone has chalked the current limit in a hand that trusted chalk.

npc.name: Relie-Lavel
npc.voice: Quick, dry, accustomed to talking over the hum; measures people the way she measures traffic — by what they carry and whether it will keep.

deep.says: I sell what passes through the arteries. I don't follow it. Everything on this ship moves, and the trick is knowing what you are — cargo or courier. Some nights, with the child breathing and the trunk talking, I can't tell which one I signed up to be.

choices.text: Maybe the count will tell you.

home.says: Nineteen years. My mother yielded to trunk traffic; I never saw the point — the trunk goes where it goes and so do we. The mica warms at shift-change, the stove holds, the child was born on the second catwalk. There are worse addresses. There are quieter ones, but not warmer.

braid.says: The Braid buys, Solen's people buy, and last month a stranger with copper on his sleeves bought twice and paid in passage. Everyone wants the count. Nobody wants to say why. That's the oldest trade there is.

greet.says: Mind the mica, it cracks at the seams and the whole tier hears you fall. You're the one out of Bay 14. Word moved faster than you did — it usually does.

choices.text: What do you hear in the wall?
Do you ever go deeper down?
How long have you lived on a ventilation trunk?

seven.says: I walked Mercury's artery once, the true one, three days' run up-axial. A corridor wide enough to lose a market in, and every wall speaking at once. I stood in it and understood I was a rumour being passed. You don't come back from that the same size.

choices.text: Thank you. That's enough for now.

tally.says: My mother's mother started that tally, and she didn't know what she was counting either. Off-schedule pulses, maybe four a year. This year there were eleven before the month turned. I add a mark, I sell the count to whoever pays, and I sleep fine. Mostly.

choices.text: And when you don't sleep fine?

listen.says: Six arteries cross under this gantry. Each zone talks in its own tempo — the Wards gossip, the Commons clears its throat, the rind hums like a struck bell that never finishes. Lately the bell's been struck more. That's not weather. That's someone awake down there.

choices.text: Can you tell me which rhythm changed first?

reactions.grief: Long after the vibration dies, her hand stays flat on the nickel, reading nothing; she asks only who found them.
reactions.shock: Her measuring fails; she stares at the body like freight gone still, waiting for it to declare itself.
reactions.bribed: She quotes a price out of habit, then hears herself, and finds the frayed cord under her thumb.
reactions.accused: The accusation gets one dry laugh out of her, and then a question about what exactly they think she carried.
reactions.flattered: She lets the praise stand unpriced, which from her is warmth, and works out what it is trying to buy.
reactions.questioned: The tally comes in manifest order — weight, consignee, onward — while her hand stays flat on the humming nickel.
reactions.threatened: She prices the threat like freight — weight, route, whether it will keep — and lets the silence carry her answer.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The child stirs and she uses the pause, hushing and rocking, buying four seconds to rebuild the count she misquoted.
reactions.authority_arrives: She does not stand — nobody on Eighty-Eight yields — and lets the official wait out one full interval of the trunk.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her hand finds the nickel before the shudder settles; whatever it says, she gathers the child without a word.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She repeats the name twice, weighing it against every count she has sold, and finds it fits the wrong shape.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says the true thing plainly — the trunk goes where it goes — and hates how easily it comes out.

npc.description: Relie-Lavel sits cross-legged on the third catwalk with a child asleep against one knee, tapping the trunk wall in slow intervals and reading the answers off the vibration with a hand flat against the nickel. She wears a knotted cord at the wrist, frayed past legibility, and does not look up until the second knock.

lore.name: The Listening Plate
lore.description: Bolted where the trunk wall meets the third catwalk is a square of annealed nickel, polished mirror-bright on its inner face, its rivets replaced so often the holes have become slots. Press an ear or a teacup to it and the whole artery below resolves into distinguishable traffic — each message-pulse with its own pitch, each zone's rhythm its own weather. Someone has scratched a tally beside it, decades of tallies, counting pulses that came through off-schedule.

content.name: Gantry 88 Deep
content.description: The floor gives under each step with a faint glassy give — layered mica sheeting laid over the nickel trunk, worn through at the threshold to a shine of dark metal — and it hums, very faintly, in time with whatever is passing below. Catwalks stitch this way across the ventilation trunk in three crooked tiers, every one of them hung with homes: curtains, cots, a stove riveted to a brace never meant to bear one. The stencilled warning — CATWALK TENANTS YIELD TO TRUNK TRAFFIC — has been painted over twice and now reads as decoration. Nobody yields.

npc.name: Halkatl-Hiuhuitl
npc.voice: Short. Corrects herself when she slips into the old rhythm of the room. She does not offer things twice.

end.says: Sit if you're eating. Otherwise the doorway's behind you.

choices.text: Leave her to the dry counter.

who.says: Doss. Big fellow, took his stool with him when he went, so I suppose he means to come back for it. He fed half the shift workers here on credit nobody kept books on. The room's been cold at the floor since.

went.says: Toward the dim end, the way the fog sits on the horizon. I didn't ask. He paid his tally off the night before — every mark, even the ones I'd have let stand. That's not a man planning a trip. That's a man settling accounts.

choices.text: I hope the stool comes back before you do.

greet.says: We're open, technically. Six stools, no standing service. You'll have to tell me what you want, because I only learned the regulars' orders and none of them are here.

choices.text: This isn't your usual shift, is it.

shift.says: It is not. I mend the decking next door. They asked me to hold the counter until whoever belongs here comes back. That was nine days ago.

choices.text: I'll let you get back to it.

reactions.grief: Talks too long about the dead one's tally, every mark, wringing the dry rag, until she hears herself, and stops.
reactions.shock: Does not scream or sit down, keeps wiping the dry counter slower and slower until her hand forgets why.
reactions.bribed: Tells them credit is how this room got cold, and that she keeps no books, and takes nothing.
reactions.accused: Points at the doorway before the accusation finishes, the rag gone still in her hand, and does not point twice.
reactions.flattered: Waits until the praise runs out, then sets down one clean bowl, the single offer she will make.
reactions.questioned: Answers in tallies, marks and times, as if the question were a bill she could settle and be done with.
reactions.threatened: Offers nothing that could go in a book, and wipes the same dry spot until they give up and go.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats the false thing once more, then drops it, because she does not offer anything twice, not even a lie.
reactions.authority_arrives: Walks the official to a stool herself, same as anyone, jurisdiction welcome only if it means to eat.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Counts six stools out loud before she can stop herself, then dares anyone at the counter to mention it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names what the accused ate last week, down to the change they counted, as evidence nobody asked her for.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no once, plainly, then stands in the cold at the floor, unable to say it again.

npc.description: A broad woman in a server's apron two sizes too clean, wiping a counter that is already dry. She works the rag in the wrong order — pass first, then stools — and glances at the empty bolt-holes each time she passes them.

lore.name: the bolted-down wide stool
lore.description: Four bolt-holes are ground flat and filled with resin at the counter's end, and the timber there is darker where years of a heavier body leaned in. A regular of great size sat here, night after night, on a stool welded from spare shaft-stock. The stool is gone — unscrewed from the inside, taken whole. Beside the holes, scratched into the stone: a tally of visits, nine hundred and some, ending mid-row.

content.name: Noodle-Counter 9
content.description: The cold sits at ankle height, pooled around the stone floor, while the overhead strip burns too bright and warms nothing below the shoulders. Six stools stand at a counter of planed timber, and a seventh gap in the row is scoured clean where a wider seat used to bolt down. Above the pass, stencilled: SIX STOOLS, NO STANDING SERVICE.

npc.name: Laaraanaazi Zurannauthnui
npc.voice: Slow, courteous, worn smooth by scale; talks about the tank the way a farmer talks about weather they have stopped arguing with.

end.says: Mind the plank. The water's shallow but it remembers everyone who falls in.

room.says: Venus's decks don't hold people; they hold gardens. But the life-feed runs through this housing, warm and steady, and warmth is a home if you keep it long enough. The council called it temporary. That was before my knees were young.

choices.text: Ask about the water line painted so high.

greet.says: Hm. Visitors don't come up here; the water keeps them honest. You want the walkway, or you want me — either way, step where the chalk says.

choices.text: Ask why anyone lives inside a ballast tank.

water.says: The water finds its level and we find ours beneath it — that's the whole arrangement. Half the hull fills, half of us float our floors on it, and the paint reminds whoever comes after which is which. Somebody always comes after.

choices.text: Ask if they meant to fall asleep.

waking.says: No. The feed changed pitch an hour back — warmer, like the gardens turned toward something — and I sat down to listen and the listening took me. It does that. You get used to being the smaller schedule in the room.

reactions.grief: The dead arrive by name — everyone the tank has taken — and they cannot stop at the newest.
reactions.shock: The chalk snaps in their fingers; they stand very still, as if the water owed them an account.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets the patience they give weather; what they would take in return cannot be carried.
reactions.accused: They put the chalk down before answering, a courtesy their hands have never needed, and ask to hear it again.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands on old scaffolding; they let it hang too long before steering talk back to drainage.
reactions.questioned: They account for their hours the way they read water: slowly, without dispute, as though the question were weather.
reactions.threatened: The courtesy thickens to a wall, and they begin discussing water levels no one has asked about.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: A beat of silence where the courtesy should be; then they concede, voice gone flat as standing water.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their posture leaves the buttress for the first time in years, and every sentence grows a word of law.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They are at the water line before the shaking stops, thumb already against the chalk to count what moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The accusation dies by inventory: the named one's boots, gait, fear of the plank, each habit entered like evidence.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The refusal arrives dressed in feed-pressures and level marks, everything but the word no, which they cannot make courteous.

npc.description: Laaraanaazi Zurannauthnui sleeps propped against a ceramic buttress, boots still on, a hairline of chalk dust drying along one forearm where they have been marking water levels by hand — a habit, their sleeves suggest, of decades.

lore.name: The Plumb-Line Toggle
lore.description: A brass plumb-line hangs from the lowest girder, its bob notched with depth-marks going back further than the current paint scheme — the oldest notations worn to shallow silver, a habit of measuring that outlived whoever started it.

content.name: Ballast Housing
content.description: The smell reaches you first: standing water warmed over a life-support feed, sweet with nutrient salt and the copper tang of old plumbing, thickened by chalk-lime whitewash still curing on the sintered ceramic walls. Half the tank housing has been opened to its ribs, iron girders rising out of the flooded half like the bones of something that drowned standing up, and the far wall climbs so far that the painted instruction — WATER LINE MARKS THE OCCUPIED LEVEL — has to be read at two removes, the lower letters close and legible, the upper ones a suggestion. A footbridge of scaffold plank crosses the water to a platform of hung hammocks and drying laundry, where someone is asleep in a way that suggests they were not supposed to stop working first.

npc.name: Krazokrost Noto
npc.voice: Careful, bookish, faintly stubborn. She finishes counts out loud before answering.

open.says: Everything, if you believe the writ. The council keeps the city going so the next generation gets it whole. The Seven keep the ship going so the next generation gets the city. Names on the terminal, mostly. But my husband wrote every holder of this room since the landing was cut, and the first hand in that ledger isn't a person's. It's signed the way the terminal signs. Merid Solen keeps that quieter than I would.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll keep what you told me.
A ledger older than the council. Careful with that.

greet.says: Mind the cards. They were his system and I keep it wrong.

choices.text: What are all the cards for?
Why keep renting half a broken room?
What do the Seven have to do with any of this?
I'll come back when the wall's rebuilt.

probe_a.says: Ledger. Every dwelling on this landing, who holds it, who held it before. My husband ran it forty years. Paper doesn't forget the way people do.

probe_b.says: The council office, twice a year. An auditor came in the spring, a slate woman, fair as a ruled line. I passed. She said the room itself was the problem, then the wall came down.

probe_c.says: Because the ledger can't have a gap. One landing missing, and someone above me invents it. Order is just nobody getting to make things up.

reactions.grief: She thanks them for the exact date, writes it on a card, and only then her hand stops working.
reactions.shock: The porcelain dish hits the floor; she stares past the body, lips moving through a count that will not finish.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets repeated aloud, once, so the room holds it; the ledger, she says, is not hers to sell.
reactions.accused: The count stops mid-number; she asks them to repeat the accusation so she can enter it in the ledger.
reactions.flattered: The praise makes her correct the record instead: she lists every entry she has miskept since taking over his system.
reactions.questioned: No answer comes until the count is finished aloud; then she recites her movements like ledger entries, dates included.
reactions.threatened: The threat changes nothing she will show; the count continues, one card louder than before.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Blame goes to the cards first; the quiet comes when the evidence shows her own hand.
reactions.authority_arrives: She watches the doorframe longer than the official, as if the stencil might account for her better than she can.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She holds the dish level with both hands and waits for the lamp to steady before she speaks.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name gets no nod from her; she goes to the shelf for the ledger that will contradict it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: A plea she cannot answer gets written on a card instead, filed for whoever holds the room next.

npc.description: The lamp light keeps stuttering where the opened wall lets the corridor draft through. Krazokrost Noto counts index cards into a porcelain dish, moving her lips. A stencil on the closed half of the wall reads ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE.

lore.name: The Widow's Rent Ledger
lore.description: An index card, edges gone soft with handling, wedged under the leg of the porcelain basin to keep it level. It records rent paid in regard rather than coin: a favor owed, a name vouched for, a debt marked settled in a dead man's hand. Thirty years of entries, both sides. The card was once a Continuant writ-form; the printed columns are still visible under the handwriting.

content.name: The Curtained Room of Quiet Ledger
content.description: The lamp gutters every few seconds, and each time it does the far half of the room disappears behind sheeting. The half that remains holds a cot, a stove, a shelf of porcelain. Two women stand close together, voices low. They stop when the curtain moves. On the doorframe, stenciled: ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE.

npc.name: Ravasea Sethiosese
npc.voice: Short, procedural, but she answers real questions. Precedent is her habit: she cites the rule before she grants the exception.

keep.says: Because a seal is a promise somebody made, and hers were all kept. Throw it out and that's a small piece of her word, gone. The audit wouldn't understand. That's fine. The audit doesn't have to.

audit.says: Of us. Factor Solen's office audits every writ-office on a rotation, and ours came up. I've sealed permits for nineteen years and they still count my stamps by hand. It's fair. I'd count theirs too.

choices.text: You sound like you trust her.

greet.says: You're in the queue or you're not. Which is it?

choices.text: I'm in the queue. What takes so long today?
What happened to the other half of this counter?
Not in the queue. Never mind.

queue.says: The council tripled the renewal load this season and gave us no second clerk. Everyone wants their papers before the audit. Nobody wants to hear that the audit is why the papers are late.

solen.says: I trust the office, not the person. That's the whole point of a writ. People bend. Paper doesn't, if you seal it right. She'd say the same, probably in fewer words.

choices.text: How long have you been here, exactly?
Fair enough. Good luck with the audit.

repair.says: A pipe joint above the ceiling let go and took out the far half. We requisitioned a rebuild. It's been in the queue behind every other requisition since. So we work half a counter and the line eats my elbows.

choices.text: Sounds like the line is the real problem.

nineteen.says: Nineteen, at this exact counter. My mother held the same post on first shift, one floor up, before they merged the shifts. I keep her old stamp in the drawer. It doesn't match the current seal format, so I can't use it. I can't throw it out either.

choices.text: Why keep it if you can't use it?

reactions.grief: She finishes the pair of stamps in front of her, then keeps one hand flat on the closed ledger.
reactions.shock: Her eyes fix on the violence while her stamps keep landing, wrong page, wrong box, until the queue starts pointing.
reactions.bribed: She repeats the bribe at full counter volume so the whole queue hears it, then logs it as attempted fraud.
reactions.accused: Nineteen years of counted stamps, and one sentence makes her hands unsure of the next pair.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes her look for the form number behind it; finding none, she loses interest mid-compliment.
reactions.questioned: Asked for her movements, she recites dates and stamp counts and offers the ledger before anyone thinks to request it.
reactions.threatened: Her rule citation comes out half its usual volume, and she says it twice before trusting it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She hears the contradiction land, repeats her false line once anyway, then voids it in her own hand.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets the queue like everyone else; she reads their jurisdiction aloud first, as courtesy and as record.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder knocks her ink, and she rights the stamps first, asking whether any unsealed copies were exposed.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name lands and she asks for their seal ledger before allowing herself either belief or disbelief.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Every exception she can cite goes across the counter first; the rule she cannot bend comes last, and plainly.

npc.description: Ravasea Sethiosese stands behind the working half of the counter, stamping permits in pairs. The queue presses close enough that she elbows the nearest petitioner aside without looking. Her uniform collar is open. Her hands move faster than her face does.

lore.name: The counter's rubber sheet
lore.description: A strip of sheet rubber, pulled back from the opened half, still tacked at one corner. Someone has dated the repair in grease pencil: three years ago.

content.name: The Writ Counter of Second Shift
content.description: The counter sits too high on its opened half, its rubber sheet peeled back to show the concrete underneath. The working half is lower and everyone leans on it anyway. Sunlight through the high strip-windows makes the off-white paint glare. The queue runs out the door. A stencil on the wall reads: PERMITS SEALED, UNSEALED COPIES VOID.

npc.name: Krortyazdko Nobrodro
npc.voice: Terse, clinical, with the flat kindness of someone who has held this floor's griefs and will not dramatize them.

room.says: The midwife was called down to the axial clinics. Her instruments stayed. We don't clear a healing room until the floor's tally is closed, and nobody's signed the tally. So I wash. Take the gutta-percha if you need sealant — it keeps better in a warm pocket anyway.

greet.says: Not my shift. Not even my floor, properly. If you're here for the ledger, it's with Solen's office — everything gets registered, that's the whole point of us.

reactions.grief: Says the name back once, then starts listing what a body will need, too fast, past listening.
reactions.shock: Freezes in the door with both hands still held up, sterile, for nobody.
reactions.bribed: Refuses in registry terms, asking which ledger line the gift should be entered under.
reactions.accused: Puts down the forceps before answering, which they have never once needed to do.
reactions.flattered: Names the coat as borrowed and the praise as misdirected, then asks what is actually wanted.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day in registry order, floor to basin to door, unhesitating, as if reading a signed entry.
reactions.threatened: Their voice drops to the stencil's volume, and their eyes go to the threat's hands, not the face.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Holds to the wrong hour with clinical precision, and reaches for an instrument already dry.
reactions.authority_arrives: Reports the room unfinished and the tally unsigned, relief and dread sharing one breath.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Moves to the empty chair before anything else, one hand flat on ivory cloth until the room settles.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks up faster than they mean to, and has to begin the defense again, quieter.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers the trade's only answer, referral, office, paperwork, and cannot meet the eyes that asked.

npc.description: Krortyazdko Nobrodro stands at the basin, sleeves wet to the elbow, washing instruments that are already clean. They wear the deep blue of the clinic under a coat cut for someone else, and they keep glancing at the chair as if it might ask them something.

lore.name: The Third Weighing Scale
lore.description: Beside the chair sit three scales, not two: mother, child, and a third with a worn ivory pan and no dial. Its weights are hand-cut from gutta-percha, each stamped with a tally of births kept and lost on this floor. The heaviest weight has never been moved; the dust around it is undisturbed, but someone polishes the pan.

content.name: Nerpolis
content.description: Milk and iron and the burnt-rubber sweetness of gutta-percha, gone stale. The birthing chair stands mid-preparation, ivory cloth still folded where no one came to lie down. Ground-glass panes throw a hard white light over everything; the room seems to hold its breath. Stencilled by the inner door: QUIET PAST THIS DOOR, ALWAYS.

npc.name: Tilir-al-Dukk
npc.voice: Terse, dry, economical. Answers in one line unless pressed. Talks about the house the way a farmer talks about weather.

east.says: Brokers with knotted cords and a paid runner. The Braid clears a debt faster than the Tabard posts a notice. Nine years I kept this floor. One in ten, no credit — that rule leaves with me.

greet.says: House is closed. Tables went east on the morning run. If you want dice, come back when there's floor to throw them on.

reactions.grief: The sacking goes still under their hands; they start listing the dead one's usual throws and can't stop.
reactions.shock: Their eyes sweep the floor for a crooked throw before they accept what's lying there.
reactions.bribed: The stencil over the door comes back word for word; they push the coinage back, not quite insulted.
reactions.accused: The folding stops mid-crease; they row the dice straight and say the guilty party wouldn't know house rules.
reactions.flattered: They accept the praise in the flat tone they saved for drunk winners and keep folding.
reactions.questioned: They answer in ledger order, times first, no adjectives, and never once look up from the sacking.
reactions.threatened: They let the threat finish, then ask mildly whether it comes before or after the morning run.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The wrong number comes out again, slower, as if twice makes it true; their thumb finds the heaviest die.
reactions.authority_arrives: They set the last bundle square to the table edge and wait, hands empty, nothing here owed to anyone.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: One palm goes flat over the dice rows before they'll admit the whole floor moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They stay quiet a long moment, then correct the accuser's odds, which is where their loyalty ends.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: There is nothing left in the room to give; they say so and name three doors that might.

npc.description: Tilir-al-Dukk folds sacking at the far table, fast and flat, and does not look up when the curtain moves. A tray of dice sits beside them, sorted by weight into rows. The folding never breaks rhythm.

lore.name: The tally board
lore.description: One wall keeps a slate board with columns of scores scratched in a game-keeper's hand. Each column ends in a name, a date, and a small knot drawn beside it — the same knot pattern the Drift wear at their wrists. The last column is half-finished, the chalk still soft, abandoned mid-line.

content.name: The Dice Parlor, Frame 175
content.description: The floor is bare limewash over plank, scrubbed so often the grain stands in ridges underfoot. Dice tables are gone; pale rectangles mark where they stood. Sacking bundles lean in a corner. Over the doorway, stenciled: HOUSE TAKES ONE IN TEN, NO CREDIT.

npc.name: Taizugul Flarebreaker
npc.voice: Terse, quick, counting even when speaking — a person who measures in thread-lengths and has no patience for anything that doesn't circulate.

work.says: Records. What the zones say to each other, spun into thread so it can be read in the hand, in order, by anyone who can't reach a terminal. Mercury runs the messages; we keep them pullable. Back to work — thread doesn't wait on visitors.

greet.says: Don't touch the warp. Order of weave is order of record — you break one thread's sequence and a decade of someone's days comes off this loom wrong. You want lore, the artery feeds the terminals. This room feeds the artery.

reactions.grief: The shuttle stops mid-pick; they name the dead one's weft-pattern and the exact days it holds, and cannot stop.
reactions.shock: Their eyes go to the mica floor and stay there; the pattern-code scrolls past unread for a full rotation.
reactions.bribed: They weigh the offer like bad filament, two seconds, then refuse without slowing the feed.
reactions.accused: Both hands leave the shuttle for the first time all shift; they say the accusation back once, flat, waiting.
reactions.flattered: Praise slides off them; they stop to correct one figure in the flatterer's speech before hearing what it wants.
reactions.questioned: The day comes back off their tongue in thread-lengths, unbothered, every hour already in the record.
reactions.threatened: Nothing in their face moves, but the pick goes in crooked, and they know it, and keep feeding anyway.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The count slips mid-number; they reach for the spool strap, needing something in hand before the corrected figure comes.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door gets one glance, one nod; the loom keeps their hands and their answers run short as thread-ends.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The warp gets grabbed before their balance does; ten years of sequence hangs in that frame, and they count it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defense comes faster than thought, that one's weave has held ten years, then they demand the thread be checked anyway.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Three false starts precede the refusal; the plea sits outside their thread, and they say so, hating the arithmetic.

npc.description: Taizugul Flarebreaker works standing, feeding filament into the shuttle with both hands while their eyes track the pattern-code scrolling past on a sliver of layered mica propped against the beam. They wear three spools on a shoulder strap like ammunition.

lore.name: The tally-spool
lore.description: A wooden dowel wedged into the loom's frame, wound with knotted cord — one knot per weave completed, so many that the newest knots crowd against a dowel already replaced once and kept, out of something like stubbornness, lashed beside it.

content.name: The Memory Loom
content.description: The cold sits at ankle height and nowhere else — the wind that scours the unfinished frames comes up through gaps in the mica flooring and never rises past the knee, while the loom's drive-motors warm the air above into a still, chalk-white haze. Thread runs out from the frames in spools toward the transit artery beyond the wall, enough of it, laid end to end, to reach the far axial horizon twice over. Stencilled on a half-built beam: THREAD READ IN ORDER, NEVER OUT OF SEQUENCE. A worker looks up, mid-shuttle.

npc.name: Rionishiosaara Lenhaafaaleesaaru
npc.voice: Measured, procedural, with the wardworker's habit of turning grief into protocol; kindness delivered as instruction.

span.says: Because an outbreak unmet is not an outbreak that never was. Venus's decks below grow things on no schedule we set, and the day one of them decides to walk, this span will already be ready. Correct, and nothing worn in. That is the point.

choices.text: I'll keep to the black glass.

greet.says: You shouldn't be past the seal. But since you are — touch nothing with a green edge. The bays are clean, and I would prefer they stay correct.

choices.text: Sealed for generations — why rebuild it now?
This isn't your shift, is it.
Who keeps the tally plate on the seal?

shift.says: It is now. The one who held it went down into the lower rind three months back and stopped filing, same as the others. I stood in her actual domain once — the green decks. You feel how little it needs you. So you cover the shift anyway. That is the whole creed, if you want it small.

choices.text: The tally plate — is that hers?

tally.says: It keeps itself, far as I can tell. The ink is fresh every time I look, and my hands have never touched it. I stopped writing that in my reports. Factor Solen reads what I write and chooses not to know the rest, and some days I think that is the kindest thing a governor can do.

choices.text: Then I'll leave the ledger alone.

reactions.grief: She asks the date, then the filing status, then keeps asking procedure long after answers have stopped mattering.
reactions.shock: Somewhere behind the procedure a door closes; she stands with the gauge half-raised, unable to make the next click.
reactions.bribed: She refuses in her safety-instruction cadence, and only afterward admits to herself how easily she could have said yes.
reactions.accused: She does not deny it; she asks which seal, as though the accusation had arrived in the wrong form.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets filed unacknowledged, like everything meant to be collected later, her thanks arriving a seam late.
reactions.questioned: The accounting leaves her in filing cadence, worn smooth by three months of answering to nobody at all.
reactions.threatened: Her voice keeps its instructional warmth even now, though the gauge has stopped moving in her hand.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The gauge clicks a seam already counted, and she repeats the lie slower, as if pronunciation were the flaw.
reactions.authority_arrives: She recites the span's condition unprompted and complete, a report written for someone who stopped reading months ago.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For one breath the procedure fails her entirely, and she says the seal's age aloud like an accusation.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name lands badly, filed under gone; she corrects the speaker's tense before permitting herself any other response.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Every kindness she owns arrives as instruction, stepwise and correct, and neither of them pretends it is enough.

npc.description: A Continuant wardworker in a slate smock three sizes too formal for the shift, calibrating the glass partitions with a gauge that clicks against each seam. Rionishiosaara Lenhaafaaleesaaru works down the row without hurrying, and answers without turning, in the manner of someone covering a post that was never meant to be covered alone.

lore.name: The Unmet Outbreak Ledger
lore.description: Bolted inside the outer seal is a copper-faced tally plate, its rows ruled for names that were never entered. Every column is blank except one, headed ARRIVAL DATE, filled with a single line in fresh ink: today. Someone has been filling in the arrival date of an outbreak that has not come, on a schedule kept longer than anyone in the Nave has been alive.

content.name: Teraayaomoaana
content.description: The observation shelf sits at chest height on one side of the span and knee height on the other, as if the floor forgot which way it was sloping halfway through its pouring. Green-black basalt walls rise into girderwork that swallows sound before it can become echo. The quarantine bays stand in an unbroken row, cast basalt sills unscuffed, black glass partitions without a fingerprint among them. A stencil above the outer seal reads SPAN SEALED, LAST OPENED GENERATIONS AGO, and the paint is younger than the letters it spells.

npc.name: Lokla Frieklecal
npc.voice: Precise, ledger-shaped. Names the rule before the feeling.

open.says: The paperwork, mostly. But that's not nothing. Somebody broke a seal last week over a ceiling that isn't theirs, and the ruling held. That's what order is here: someone wrote it down, and we all agreed to keep the writing. The moment we stop agreeing, the room stays exactly this warm and none of it works.

choices.text: Thank you. Keep the writing going.
So it's all agreement. Unsettling, that.

greet.says: Disputes are Tuesdays. If you're here to pay, sit; if not, say so now.

choices.text: What does the council actually keep going here?

probe_a.says: Every settled dispute gets a seal. Break it and the ruling reopens. I've broken four this month. Last year I broke none.

probe_b.says: The council, through the registry writ. Factor Solen signs it, I keep it. Three audits she's survived. Most of us hoped she would. Some hoped louder than others.

probe_c.says: Rent is the same. People aren't. They come in angrier, and they bring witnesses nobody sent. Something's moving through the floors. I hear it before I see it.

reactions.grief: Lokla writes the name in the margin of the day's page, where no entry belongs, and leaves it undated.
reactions.shock: Knocks a wax seal off the counter, then stands still, not picking any of it up.
reactions.bribed: Misremembering is priced aloud like a filing fee, until the offerer tires of official language and leaves.
reactions.accused: The statute on false accusation gets quoted twice, the second time slower.
reactions.flattered: The compliment is allowed to finish, which is already more than most requests get.
reactions.questioned: Dates come first, then places, recited without notes and accurate to the hour.
reactions.threatened: There is a rule for threats, Lokla says, and opens a fresh page for the name.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Stares at the open ledger as if the page might correct itself, then admits the date was wrong.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes find the seal first, and the shoulders only drop once the wax proves genuine.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: An hour is marked in the margin, and then no form on the desk fits what happened.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Asks who witnessed it, twice, and leaves the accusation unwritten for now.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The process is recited whole, Tuesdays, witnesses, fees, without looking up from the form.

npc.description: The heat sits at the desk and nowhere else; the aisle behind stays cold as a cellar. The zinc counter is sticky with old wax, and the wax seals creak when Lokla breaks them. A stenciled board over the shelf reads DISPUTES HEARD TUESDAYS, BRING WITNESSES.

lore.name: The Precedent Spindle
lore.description: A iron rod bolted to the desk's edge, strung with decades of wax-sealed writ-stubs threaded like beads. The oldest seals at the bottom have gone amber and crack when touched. Each stub cites the one above it; rulings here are never made new, only passed down and re-sealed. The most recent stub is dated today, and cites a case from forty years before the desk was built.

content.name: Registry-Desk 25
content.description: The heat sits at the desk, pooled around a zinc stovepipe, and stops at the doorway. Beyond it the stairwell stays cold. Every surface holds paper. A blue banner over the file racks reads DISPUTES HEARD TUESDAYS, BRING WITNESSES, its lower edge darkened by hands. The floor creaks under a queue that was never planned for.

npc.name: Thjafried Sneldtja
npc.voice: Short sentences, mender's grammar — everything is either holding, failing, or due. Names tools like kin. Never says the word foundling, says 'the intake'

end.says: Hold it flush, not tight — horn wants to move with the season. There. That one will outlast both of us, which is the whole of the job when you boil it down. Come back when you've something to mend and no one to mend it beside.

choices.text: Leave them to the shift that isn't theirs.

pipe.says: The feed-line runs from the old silo days, straight through to the service corridor. Sealed everywhere else on this deck. Not here. We voted on it once, years back, and I'll tell you how the vote went: it didn't. Some rooms you don't close.

choices.text: Ask whether they were one of the ones that came through.

vess.says: Walking the deck, she says. Walking. I've known Vess since we shared a cot in this very room, and a woman that sleeps badly doesn't walk at night for her health. I don't ask. When she's ready to say it she'll mend something next to me and it'll come out through the work, the way it does.

choices.text: Offer to hold the rail while they finish the lashing.

work.says: Silo racking. Good bone in it, forty years of cots cut from the same stock, but the grain's gone thirsty and the wax only slows it. Every lashing in here gets redone twice a season now. Vess was supposed to take the east bank today. Her fourth miss this month.

choices.text: Ask again about the thirteenth cot.

greet.says: Mind the third cot, the lash is new. I'm covering for Vess — her shift, not mine, so if the milk runs late that's her name for the ledger, not mine. What brings you to a room with no business in it for you?

choices.text: Ask about the cots — twelve names, thirteen beds.

thirteenth.says: Thirteen's for the ones that come by the pipe before the paperwork does. A cot is a promise made with horn and thread, and a promise doesn't wait on a name. The paint's older than the practice. Leave it be.

choices.text: Ask about the pipe — how children arrive through it.
Change the subject back to their work.

reactions.grief: Lashes the same rail long past tight and keeps lashing it, because the hands need a job that isn't this.
reactions.shock: The spoon-cord bites their wrist before they know they've gripped it, and after that they go very still.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer out loud and turns it down as bad material — nothing bends that far and holds.
reactions.accused: Snaps that they have mended every failure on this deck and broken none of them, louder than the words need.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit unclaimed, eyes on the stitching, and asks what actually needs mending.
reactions.questioned: Their account comes out as inventory: thread spent where, rail lashed when, nothing volunteered past the count.
reactions.threatened: Weighs the threat like a cracked rail — where it gives, whether it can be lashed or must come out.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie comes apart under the evidence; they set down the awl and give up the true thing.
reactions.authority_arrives: Doesn't rise from the floor between the cots; keeps working and offers the room's count by ear, unprompted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Is across the room before the shudder ends, one hand flat on the nameless cot, counting the intake's breaths.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names every night Vess didn't sleep — dates, cots, weather — far more in her defense than anyone asked for.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits the limit in trade terms — that seam is past them — then sits down beside it anyway.

npc.description: Thjafried Sneldtja sits cross-legged between two cots, re-lashing a rail that split along the grain, working the waxed thread in tight figure-eights. Their sleeves are rolled to the elbow over arms that carry the pale seam-lines of rindwork, and a horn spoon hangs from a cord at the wrist. They do not look up when the door opens; they count the room by ear first.

lore.name: The Listen Horn
lore.description: The silo's old grain-feed pipe was never sealed — instead a horn of yellowed kerf has been lashed to its mouth with waxed thread, knotted in short beads down the length. Set your ear there and the whole corridor arrives: boots, the intake door, a first cry before anyone has reached the threshold. The thread carries a mark for every child the horn announced, and there are more marks than names on the wall.

content.name: The Silo Creche, Ward 210
content.description: The wall clock hangs at toddler height, a hand's width off the floor, and small fingerprints cloud its face. Twelve cots follow the silo's curve in ochre and horn, and a thirteenth sits wedged against the vent with no name stenciled above it. The paint overhead says TWELVE COTS, TWELVE NAMES ON THE WALL, and no one has amended it.

npc.name: Rion-Mishoglu
npc.voice: Fast, practical, given to route-talk — she speaks the way runners speak, in legs and loads and what moves when.

open.says: You know how the Drift talks about circulation — goods, gossip, bodies, all of it moving because a still floor is a dead floor? I felt the same creed in the floor of this hall, at a size that made my wrist-knots look like a child's first braid. The transit arteries under this rind have never stopped. Not through the sealings, not through the quiet years, not once — loads moving through the deep on schedules no one up here set, in volumes that make the whole Nave market look like one woman's hand-cart. Something is being moved all the time, everywhere, and we are the cargo that hasn't been told.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
Cargo. You said cargo. I need air.

greet.says: Mind the wire, it's live-carried — if you're not here to haul, stand where the stencil says and be quiet about it.

choices.text: Who do you answer to up here?
What's the worst part of this work?
Busy how? What do the arteries carry?
I'll come back when the wire's down.

probe_a.says: Carry-line. Nickel holds the shape, silver holds the signal — annealed, drawn thin as a hair, run the length of a hall like this and it'll carry a whisper from one axial end to the other without losing a syllable. It's the only honest metal in the room.

probe_b.says: The knot-board, same as any Drift worker answers — my wrist says which runs I've walked and who vouched me into this hall. Above that, nothing human. The antennae answer to Mercury, and Mercury has never once asked my name, which I've decided is a professional courtesy.

probe_c.says: The listening windows. Hall goes silent, every mouth shuts, and you sit in the quiet waiting for the ship to say something back. Most windows you get the hum and that's all. Lately the hum has been — busy. That's not a complaint. That's the part I don't say on the knot-board.

reactions.grief: She takes the death like a schedule change and ties her next knot wrong, first time in years.
reactions.shock: The wire slips its seat and she lets it fall, every schedule in her head gone blank at once.
reactions.bribed: Bad metal, she calls the offer, already half-turned back toward the joint her wire hasn't seated.
reactions.accused: Her denial comes at haul-speed, faster than she means it, the carry-line hanging slack in her fist.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads like a pulse with no load behind it, and she waits, spool between her teeth, for the ask.
reactions.questioned: Asked where she's been, she answers the way she'd log a run, first haul to last, and nothing more.
reactions.threatened: Her eyes run the ladder, the cordoned plates, the nearest open leg out, while her mouth gives nothing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught out, she patches the story with rivet-counts and load-times, a rig over-tensioned before it snaps.
reactions.authority_arrives: Before the official clears the arch she's giving him clean manifests and a deference she's never spent on anyone.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She reads the shudder against the deep-run schedules in her head and finds no entry, which frightens her more.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Not him: she recites his last three runs from memory, an alibi in legs and loads nobody asked for.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She names plainly what her hands cannot carry, then points the pleader down the leg where help might live.

npc.description: A woman is halfway up a girder ladder with a spool of silver wire in her teeth, feeding it down to a joint she cannot see, trusting the pull of the line to tell her when it has seated. Around her the hall is half flayed — annealed nickel panels stacked like loaves, rivet heads sheared and bagged, the whole sloped ceiling of antennae swaying a finger's width whenever the floor pumps.

lore.name: The Tally Filament
lore.description: One filament near the reading benches differs from the rest: its silver is hand-burnished, and clipped along its length are small annealed-nickel tags, hundreds of them, each stamped with a date and a route-glyph in the knotted script the Drift wear at their wrists. The oldest tag is green with oxide — its date falls in a notation no one on the floor uses anymore, older than the oldest ledger anyone claims. The tags stop halfway along the filament. Nobody has added one in a decade, and nobody has taken the broken count down.

content.name: Signal Archive
content.description: Something swings overhead when you enter — a silver filament thicker than a mooring cable, crossed by a pulse of light that travels the length of it and out through the far wall, and is gone. The hall follows the sky arc's fall in stepped benches of grey nickel, and above each bench run more filaments, dozens, a hundred, all of them humming at a pitch felt in the teeth rather than heard. Half the floor is opened to its bones, plates stacked and cordoned, so the crowd here squeezes into the working half like water into half a channel. Rivets run the girders in ordered rivers; stencilled over the cordoned arch, flaking: HALL SILENT DURING LISTENING WINDOWS.

npc.name: Shivomuth Hazelspoken
npc.voice: Terse as a tally — Drift-stamped nouns, verbs she uses like entries in a ledger, no greeting that isn't also an audit.

greet.says: Not on my manifest, and yet here — which makes you issued. Shivomuth Hazelspoken. Don't touch the salt, it remembers hands.

ask_stock.says: Above my line. The tally settles itself by morning — that's all a keeper knows, and I know less every year I stay. Take the lamp from shelf nine; it's been waiting on you longer than I've kept this post.

reactions.grief: Mid-entry, she hears the name and keeps writing until the graphite snaps, then speaks unprompted of an old debt.
reactions.shock: She counts the wounds before she means to, because counting is what her hands do when the world stops balancing.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced out of habit before she can stop herself, and she hates how quickly the total comes.
reactions.accused: The tally-voice holds, but her thumb stops mid-count, a fault she would catch in any other clerk.
reactions.flattered: Any praise with a want behind it she files under outstanding requisitions, though her ears warm against her will.
reactions.questioned: Questions are answered in ledger order, every movement entered before the asker finishes asking, a tidiness she almost resents enjoying.
reactions.threatened: Fear enters her as arithmetic, the threat costed against the post and found, for now, payable.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She re-counts the entry twice before speaking, then issues a correction in a voice gone thin as shelf-dust.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door gets held open with a keeper's formality, her thumb already counting what the visit will cost her shelves.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her thumb goes to the shelf-line at once, re-measuring an aisle she had counted true an hour ago.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name lands and she objects too fast, citing shelf-nine requisitions nobody has asked her to check.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The refusal arrives steadier than she feels, the last law she owns still doing its work.

npc.description: A short woman whose sleeves are packed with graphite to the elbow and salt-bloom to the cuff, as though she were quarried rather than born, counting the aisle's lengths with her thumb and not liking the arithmetic.

lore.name: The Unrequisitioned Tally
lore.description: The ledger left open on the salt-block is written in a hand that never lifted: columns of issues — cordage, coolant, one lamp — each recorded in ink that matches nothing dispensed. The final column is headed requisition, and it is not blank; it is filled with dates. Dates that have not arrived yet, each struck through in graphite the morning it comes due, the striking precise, unhurried, and ahead of you.

content.name: The Issuing Magazine of Small Hours
content.description: The cold keeps to the walls here, politely, the way water keeps to a drowning man's sleeves — the middle of the floor holds a warmth no stove explains, as if the room remembered being warm and hadn't been told otherwise. Salt compacted into shelves that run farther than the eye will reconcile; graphite packed like loaves. Everything is new-correct, unburred, unbreathed-on, a room delivered rather than made, its stencilled admonition — ISSUE RECORDED, REQUISITION ABSENT — crisp as a wound. Two clerks argue in the aisle over a ledger that neither touches. They stop. The room's attention settles on you with the patience of a scale waiting to be weighed.

npc.name: Shoud-al-Tilukk
npc.voice: Short. Shift-brained. She answers questions with the one that matters and warms only when you ask about the work itself.

why.says: His route folded. He's between runs and too proud to say so. We keep the bunk warm for him. That's how it's done here — you circulate or you sit still and rot, and nobody in this house sits still.

busy.says: Built for two shifts. We run four now. Dock doesn't stop, so the bunks don't either. You learn to sleep through anything or you don't last the season.

four.says: Nobody decided. That's the joke. Freight doubled and the council never wrote a word. We stretched the roster ourselves. Works better than anything they'd have given us.

choices.text: And the one asleep in the corner bunk?

greet.says: You're not dock crew. Off-shift three hours and someone's already in the bunkhouse. What.

choices.text: Busy place for a sleep room.
Someone's sleeping in the corner bunk.

sleeper.says: That's Tesk. Runs the night relay, comes in after his shift's supposed to be done and sleeps four more hours where the draft's worst. Doesn't have a bunk of his own anymore. Don't wake him and don't make it a thing.

choices.text: Why doesn't he have his own bunk?

reactions.grief: She asks who found him, whether he was between runs, filling the air with logistics because grief has no procedure.
reactions.shock: Her practiced flatness fails her; she stares past the body at nothing, one hand still on the ladder.
reactions.bribed: The roster she stretched with her own hands isn't for sale, and she says so without raising her voice.
reactions.accused: The accusation doesn't fit any shift she's worked, and her denial comes out thinner than she intends.
reactions.flattered: The praise lands for half a breath — she is proud of the roster — then she hears the want underneath it.
reactions.questioned: Each movement gets a start time like a shift log, and she closes by asking the question that actually matters.
reactions.threatened: Unimpressed is the wrong word; she measures him the way she measures a jammed freight gate, force or wait.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She stops re-lacing her boot with the knot half done, recalculates, and offers a smaller truth instead.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes go to the door first, then to the papers in the rails, checking what's legible from there.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She counts heads down the stack before the lamps settle, because anything unaccounted for is hers.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She snaps that a man between runs isn't a man with motive, then hears how much the defense costs her.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: It's the one thing she can't roster her way through, and her hands have nothing to do.

npc.description: A woman sits up too fast in the aisle bunk, hair creased flat on one side, a folded paper still in her fist. Her wrist cord is knotted dense and recent. She watches you take the room in before she says anything.

lore.name: The knot-rail
lore.description: The bottom bunk's rail carries a knotted cord, beaded at intervals, newer sections spliced in as the rail filled. Routes, by the look of it. The oldest knots are dark with hand-oil.

content.name: Xiztepek
content.description: The bunks eat sound first. Voices drop flat a step inside the door, and the magenta work-lamps make every shadow thick. Bunks climb the wall in a steep stack, six high, cords and folded papers stuffed in the rails. Stenciled over the ladder: DAY SLEEPERS AND NIGHT SLEEPERS SHARE THIS BUNK. Shoud-al-Tilukk sleeps in the aisle bunk, boots on, on shift.

npc.name: Hikyoki-Tlikan
npc.voice: Terse, route-shorthand, warms only when the talk turns to where things go and who carried them.

cut.says: A knot records a route. Cut it and the route is finished — retired, off the Braid, no runner picks it up again. Whoever carried that master out wanted no one following the same way. In twenty years of loft work I've seen a strap cut twice, and both times the chart was going somewhere it wasn't posted to go.

gone.says: A master chart. Not mine to name, and the knot on the straps says the carrier's route ends somewhere I've never been posted. We copy so the original can keep moving. That's the whole trade. The cutting of the straps is the part I don't repeat.

warm.says: Eleven years at this table. My knots are in three of the wall hides if you can read them — the green one nearest the vent is mine, all short hauls. Come back when I'm awake and I'll show you how a copy is checked against a master. Not today. Today the light's wrong and so am I.

greet.says: You're standing where the light should fall. Move left or don't complain about the copy. This is a working loft, even with half of it gone down the corridor on someone's shoulder.

master.says: The first drawing. Everything on the terminals is a copy of a copy of a copy, and errors breed in copies like flies. A master is the one that doesn't drift. There are fewer of them than there are tellers, and every one of them belongs to a route, not a person. Sleep with one too long and you start thinking it's yours. That's how you end up cutting straps.

reactions.grief: Repeats the dead carrier's route numbers until someone makes them stop, never once saying the name.
reactions.shock: Stands with a half-tied strap in both hands, working it tighter, though nothing needs tying.
reactions.bribed: Quotes what a cut strap truly costs, the route and every runner after, and turns back to the lamp.
reactions.accused: Points at the green hide nearest the vent and demands the accuser read eleven years of short hauls.
reactions.flattered: Under praise, they keep eyes closed and ask which knot the flatterer actually read.
reactions.questioned: Recites every depot and hour of the last week and not one carrier's name.
reactions.threatened: Inside, they are already pricing the threat like a tariff, and the stylus in their fist goes still.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Freezes over the half-copied chart, then recounts the carrier slower, correcting the description twice.
reactions.authority_arrives: Meets the official's eyes the way a copy meets its master, already listing discrepancies before being asked.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Says no posted route explains a shudder, then keeps touching the table's edge as if counting ties.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The named runner's whole carrying record comes out of them at once, tonnage by tonnage, too loud for the room.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses the plea in five words, then gives the only thing they own, the name of someone posted closer.

npc.description: Hikyoki-Tlikan sleeps sitting up against the hide wall, a stylus still in their fist, chin dropped to a chest wrapped in a Drift courier's sash worn knot-outward — a signal meant for people awake enough to read it. A half-copied chart lies under one palm, weighting it against the draft from the vent.

lore.name: The cinched cradle
lore.description: The webbing straps are knotted in Braid patterns, four strands each, and the rectangle they frame on the floor is chart-sized but strap-deep — built to carry a rolled master, padded, upright, like a passenger. Whoever left took the master and left the cradle, which no Drift runner does; the knot-history says the route was recorded here, and routes get reused. The straps were cut, not unbuckled. Someone was in a hurry to make the leaving permanent.

content.name: Fraltisett
content.description: The copying table sits a hand's width from the lamp bracket — close enough that no chart laid flat could catch full light, and someone worked here anyway. Pale green hide covers the walls, stretched over what looks like shelving. The floor is bare in one large rectangle: canvas webbing straps still lie where something heavy was cinched and carried out. Stencilled along the table's edge: NO INK NEAR THE MASTER CHARTS.

npc.name: Dell-bin Fonar
npc.voice: Keeps counting while talking, in drams, steeps and strengths. Flat about trouble, exact about the medicine. Warmth arrives only sideways, on Hesta's name.

room.says: Dispensary for Court 182 — tinctures, steeps, drawn doses. Half this stock steeped here; half came off the flooded rack in Court 180 before the water found the corks. The work goes on. The shelves are the question.

choices.text: How do you keep the doses straight?

doses.says: Dose as marked, not as guessed — Hesta cut that stencil when she still had the grip for it. Guessing is how people die politely. Every jar is marked to its steep, every steep to its strength. The bench goes back to her the day she asks.

choices.text: Thank you. I hope Hesta mends.

greet.says: Mind the third shelf. That's poppy vinegar — one deep breath of it will take your afternoon. Now. Are you sick, or curious?

shift.says: Hesta Vell's shift. She's ground at that low bench thirty years — it's cut to her height, which is why I stoop. She's the patient now. Someone had to stand here who knows witch hazel from wormwood, and I lost the draw.

reactions.grief: The number they were on is gone; they ask whose, and whether it was quick, and keep asking past politeness.
reactions.shock: The sight reaches their hands first; they wipe them on the sacking, restart the count, and lose it twice.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets no argument; they set the coin beside a marked jar where the difference shows, and resume counting.
reactions.accused: The count stops mid-dram; they set down the funnel and make the accuser say it again, twice.
reactions.flattered: They thank them in the tone they use for dosages and wait, letting the request arrive on its own.
reactions.questioned: Answers between counts, giving times the way they give strengths, then goes back to the muslin.
reactions.threatened: They keep pouring and recite, evenly, what sits on each shelf within reach.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted with the tally, they re-mark the jar in silence and call the old figure an error, nothing more.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the door first; the pour gets finished to the line before they look up.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Jars chime on the shelves; they move first to the third shelf, one arm across the poppy vinegar.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They defend the accused with steep counts and strengths, and notice too late how loud their voice has gone.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Habit turns them to the shelf; nothing is marked for it, and they stand facing the jars a long while.

npc.description: Dell-bin Fonar stands at a worktop dropped to half height on wooden blocks, decanting amber tincture through muslin strained over hemp rope, lips moving with the count. They fold nearly double to reach the bench and plainly mean to stay that way until the bottle is full.

lore.name: The Dosing Ladder
lore.description: A flat stick of pale wood hangs beside the brass scale on a loop of hemp rope, cut with square notches that size out a dipper's draw. The oldest notches run twice the depth of the newest ones. Whoever re-standardised them filed a fresh, shallower cut beside every old notch rather than plane the stick down, so the ladder carries two measures at once: the strong doses this court once drew, and the careful ones it draws now.

content.name: The Tincture Room, Court 182
content.description: The smell reaches the doorway first: spirits, clove, bitter root, sour over warm stone. Jars line the shelves three deep; sand-pale sacking hangs between the rows and stirs in the draft from the high window. Stencilled on the far wall, above a rope-tied crate: DOSE AS MARKED, NOT AS GUESSED.

npc.name: Rheilydd Ferch Rhywys
npc.voice: Clipped, exact, materials named before people. Talks like she's checking tolerances.

open.says: Chamber nine off the third axial shaft. Notation on the wall older than the oldest layer, and under it, a sealed door with fresh tool-marks — fresh, in a tunnel nobody's walked in a generation.
