We catalog what Saturn leaves and we argue about it and we do not write down what we conclude. That's the cost of the creed. Maintenance is meaning, they teach us. But some things down there were maintained by no one, and they still work.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
Maintained by no one. That should frighten you.

greet.says: Mind the bench. Pitch is still tacky and you're standing in my light.

choices.text: This bunkhouse is packed full of stores.
What have you seen down there that changed your mind?
Didn't mean to take your light.

probe_a.says: Sealing what graphite can't hold. Graphite marks the fault, pitch keeps the fault honest. Different jobs. People down here use one word for both and that's why their repairs fail.

probe_b.says: Nobody above. Route-access sets shifts — who can reach what, who owes whom a passage. I answer to Sevin the way water answers to a slope. Slowly, and downhill.

probe_c.says: It was a dwell verb last season. Now it's half store. The verb got reassigned and nobody told the bunks. We stack around what the room used to be and pretend that's maintenance.

reactions.grief: Asks after the failure mode — joint, load, weld — because a cause is something she knows how to seal.
reactions.shock: Stands with the brush raised while pitch drips on her boot, cataloging a body the way she'd chart a fault.
reactions.bribed: Weighs what they're offering against a sealed door that still works, and hands the arithmetic back.
reactions.accused: The pitch bead runs long under her brush before she can make her voice hold tolerance.
reactions.flattered: Tests the compliment for slop the way she'd test a weld, and finds it doesn't fit the joint.
reactions.questioned: Recites corridor, minute, seam count in the order the tally board wants them, already halfway back to work.
reactions.threatened: Prices the threat like bad stock: who heard it, which bolt holds, how long the corridor stays empty.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recounts the figure correctly this time and lets the silence stand where her excuse should be.
reactions.authority_arrives: Watches the official's boots cross her threshold the way she watches water find a new crack.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Checks the duct bolts by reflex, then stops counting, because nothing on her ledger accounts for a room that moves.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Notes the tool-marks are wrong-handed for him, then remembers aloud she was never supposed to have looked.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers the longest list she can of what she can fix instead, and hears how short it runs.

npc.description: Rheilydd Ferch Rhywys works at a bench set a hand's width from the bunk frame — too close for anyone to lie on it and sit there both. She is sealing a seam with pitch, graphite lines already laid beneath, and the stencil over the bunk reads DAY SLEEPERS AND NIGHT SLEEPERS SHARE THIS BUNK. She does not look up.

lore.name: Rheilydd's marked slats
lore.description: Under her cot, the original bunk slats are stacked face-down — and each one carries a drilled hole and a graphite count: tally marks in the old hull notation, one set per shift slept elsewhere. Forty-one marks on the newest slat, and the oldest has none left blank to mark. When a bunk goes too long unclaimed, Rindwalkers drill the slat and set it aside; she is drilling them faster than anyone is dying out of the rotation, which means the shift-share is thinner than the roster admits. The last hole is freshly cut and still smells of scorched pitch.

content.name: Bunkhouse 19
content.description: The fourth bunk frame hangs a hand's width from the ceiling duct, bolted where no bunk should go. Pitch-smeared mattress slats lean in bundles against the door, and the stencil over the light reads DAY SLEEPERS AND NIGHT SLEEPERS SHARE THIS BUNK, the last word gone amber under a thumb-smear of graphite. A woman greases the hinge mounts and does not look up.

npc.name: Broldlar the Rusted
npc.voice: Terse, ledger-shaped. She answers in counts.

board.says: Bottom row's not yours. Not mine either, this month. It moves, you mark it. That's the whole job and it doesn't want discussing.

greet.says: You want the desk or the stairs. Desk gives you what's spare. Stairs go back up. Pick.

choices.text: What's kept back on your tally board?

stores.says: Roots good through the dim. Fruit gone soft at the edges, still eats. That's all you get for asking. Mind the chalk lines.

reactions.grief: Weighs the same turnip three times, marks it wrong each time, and finally says a number that belongs to nothing.
reactions.shock: Counts under her breath at the body, rows and crates, because the count is the only thing left working.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the offer back as a sum, twice its true worth, and watches whether they flinch at numbers.
reactions.accused: Asks twice whether the accusation is a count or a guess, and the second time it comes out too loud.
reactions.flattered: She hears the praise as a price and asks what it costs.
reactions.questioned: Names the row and crate number she was on, scoop still level, and waits for the next question.
reactions.threatened: Her answers shrink to syllables, eyes fixed on the oxblood board, until the threat runs itself out.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Says the tally stands and offers to recount aloud, voice level, chalk hand pressing hard enough to snap.
reactions.authority_arrives: Finishes the row before looking up, then stands with all four hands visible.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: One look goes to the lead sheet, then back to the crates, and she says the count held.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Offers the hour the one they named cleared the bottom row, then stops, having discussed what never gets discussed.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Recites what the desk gives and what the stairs do, because the rules are all she has to offer.

npc.description: Broldlar the Rusted works the middle aisle with a horn scoop in each of four hands, weighing turnips by feel and marking the crate before looking at them. She does not stop moving when you come down the steps.

lore.name: The Tally Board
lore.description: The desk board carries the winter ledger, chalked and re-chalked in a hand that has stopped bothering with erasure: old numbers sit under new ones like sediment. The bottom row is not produce. It reads KEPT BACK — 3 SACKS, NO LABEL, MOVED NIGHTLY, and the initials beside it change every few weeks as the duty passes hand to hand. Nobody has written down what is in the sacks.

content.name: Bjegntehj's Root Cellar
content.description: The steps end in packed earth that has been swept so many times it shines. Crates stand in ranked rows between chalk lines drawn straight on the floor. An oxblood-painted board above the desk reads TRAPDOOR LOCKED AT NIGHT, KEY AT THE DESK, and someone has tallied under it in horn shavings pressed into the wood. The lead sheet nailed over the far wall hangs down to ankle height, cut short, and nobody has ever mentioned it.

npc.name: Ekeijeghchik-Natonga
npc.voice: Unhurried and plain. She talks the way someone talks who has been awake too long and decided to enjoy it.

call.says: Not while his mother's in the ward. See, that's the trouble with owing someone — you have to stay alive to collect, and you have to stay fond to stay alive. Twenty years in this bunkhouse and I still haven't worked out which comes first. Ask me again when he's sleeping proper.

gone.says: That was Retske's. Big as a doorway, quiet as a plank. Worked the heavy cranes eleven years, then one morning the longshore roll had no line for her and she signed with a run crew headed axial. Took her kit, left the bunk. We scrubbed the floor after. It felt like the right thing, though nobody said why.

choices.text: Do the run crews ever come back?
Leaving like that — just like that?

room.says: Dock crew. Twelve of us on this side, day and night rotation, and before you ask — yes, the snoring is a civic problem. The stencil over the door says we share. Nobody remembers painting it. Somebody paints over the scuffs every year or two so it stays true.

choices.text: Twelve? This room is built for more.

axial.says: Drift folk move; that's their whole creed and good luck to them. But Retske wasn't Drift. She was us. That's what I can't settle. Twelve years in a timber bunk and one blank line on the roster, and now the room's smaller without her, which makes no sense, because she was the biggest thing in it.

choices.text: Maybe a line will turn up.
I'll let you answer the slate.

greet.says: You're not here for a bunk, so you're either lost or bored. Sit if you want. The heat's up top and the slate won't shut up, but otherwise it's a fine room.

choices.text: That long bunk — who was that for?

shift.says: Brannoc's. Day sleepers cover nights and the other way round; that's what the stencil means. He's got a mother in the clinic and no one to sit with her, so I sit his hours and he sits mine when I need it. Third time this month. The slate doesn't care whose hands answer it.

clinic.says: The Continuants say she will. They say it kindly, which is not the same as saying it true. I've buried two bunkmates and both times the wardens were kind, so I've stopped listening for the tone and started watching the visitors. Brannoc goes every day. That's my answer.

brannoc.says: Badly, and on his feet somewhere. This bunkhouse runs on trade like everything else on the Nave, only our coin is hours. I've got a debt of sleep stacked against him taller than the rafters, and one day I'll call it in and he'll pay without a word. That's the whole arrangement. Some people think family is blood. Up here it's who covers your shift.

choices.text: Will you call it in soon?

reactions.grief: She hears the name out, thanks the bearer, then wets a rag and scrubs the floor by the long bunk.
reactions.shock: Mid-motion she stops, cap half off, gray hair showing, one hand open around nothing.
reactions.bribed: Nothing in her face moves while she prices the favor aloud, and her figure comes in higher than theirs.
reactions.accused: She denies it once, plainly, and then keeps dusting a bunk that is already clean.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets split eleven ways before the flatterer finishes, one share named for every other bunk.
reactions.questioned: She accounts for her hours in roster order, then asks which shift the question itself is billed to.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets a slow nod; afterward she is very careful laying the slate square on her knee.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she stops redescribing and gives the true hour, unhurried, as if the lie were a scheduling problem.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her boots go on before the official clears the doorway, unhurried, jurisdiction given its due and not a step more.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Out of crane habit her hand finds the bunk frame and stays, reading the shudder for weight and direction.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She starts counting his debts aloud, hers among them, as though owing the man proved his character.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She hears the whole plea without promising, says so plainly, and stays sitting on the bunk's edge anyway.

npc.description: A thickset woman sits sideways on a bunk, boots off, a shift-slate on her knee that keeps pinging for a rotation she isn't rostered for. She answers it every time. A knitted cap is pulled low over gray-streaked hair.

lore.name: the long bunk
lore.description: The bunk near the door has been lengthened with two spacer planks bolted to the foot, and the sacking over it is a single continuous weave, patched in four places. Whoever slept here was built bigger than the room was.

content.name: The Bunkhouse
content.description: The heat sits up under the rafters and never comes down; your ankles stay cold the whole time you stand here. Bunks of planed timber line both walls, sacking over the frames, all of it pale ochre where the sun-strip catches it. One bunk near the door is longer than the others, and the floor where it stood has been scrubbed.

npc.name: Fear-Auraris
npc.voice: Careful, inventory-minded; speaks of flaws as debts owed and measures everything twice before naming it.

open.says: Once. A shaft opened onto a weld seam running past sight in both directions, and a rig the size of a chapel district traveling it slow as a season, laying bead after bead on plating thicker than my whole tier. Nobody held the torch. It moved like it was praying — the patience of it, the refusal to hurry. We mend rooms. That was mend as the ship understands the word: a continent's worth of repair, done in one seam, forever. I came back up and packed graphite for a month without saying a word to anyone.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry that carefully.
A machine that prays. That unsettles me.

greet.says: Mind the tiers. The fourth tier's load path runs under your boots, and it has not been honest with us lately.

choices.text: Have you ever seen where the maintenance actually goes?
Sorry — I'll leave you to the tiers.

probe_a.says: Packing. Girders breathe when the hull flexes, and packed graphite takes the breathing without complaint. Ceramic for what must never move, graphite for what must. The other worker — the one who left this half done — packed it wet, which is the one way to pack it wrong.

probe_b.says: A good hand. Gone down-axial three months back, with the rest of the survey crews. Left a tier half-packed, which a Rindwalker does not do unless they believed they were coming back by morning. I finish their rows and log them under their name. That is the whole of the creed, if you want it short.

probe_c.says: The stencils, mostly. That one there — tier capacity unmet since last full census — has been watching me since before I was born, and it does not ask politely. Then the menders above me, and above them, nothing I have met. Word comes down; I do not ask what sends it.

reactions.grief: Measures the same joint four times and never names the number, because grief has broken their count.
reactions.shock: Something cracks along a seam no inspection ever marked, and it shows before they can pack it away.
reactions.bribed: Looks at the offered payment the way they look at wet-packed graphite, and refuses to touch either.
reactions.accused: Repeats the charge back at half speed, as though it were a measurement they might have gotten wrong.
reactions.flattered: Does not thank them at all, and lets the silence ask what the praise was meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Gives every answer twice, a fast one and a measured one, and trusts only the second.
reactions.threatened: Sets the trowel down first, slowly, on the principle that anything gripped while afraid gets used.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Goes quiet long enough for the pause to count, then enters the contradiction in their own ledger, a debt owed.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the official's boots first, to whatever the visit disturbs in the graphite.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For once they listen and hear nothing honest, and it is the nothing that frightens them.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks up fast for once, since no liar ever packed a bead that straight.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits plainly there is nothing to give, and leaves them instead a warning about which tiers bear weight.

npc.description: Fear-Auraris stands partway up the third tier with a trowel of packed graphite gone still in their hand, listening to a girder overhead the way another person might listen for rain. Below them, someone's abandoned work sits half-troweled and drying wrong, and they have clearly decided it is theirs to finish now.

lore.name: The Halted Ring-Governor
lore.description: Beneath the lowest tier, a governor the size of a standing ox grips the drive shaft in a jaw of packed graphite — a deliberate brake, mended rather than broken: fresh weld-beads in Mars's own iron-dark stitch, laid over scoring a hand-span deep. Someone chose to stop the turning rather than let it run unwatched. A slate leans against the housing in a Rindwalker's tally-script; the last entry is a single stroke, then nothing, then three older hands' worth of tallies beneath it, each ending the same unfinished way.

content.name: Granary Hall
content.description: The tiers should be turning. That is the first fact Granary Hall gives you: amphitheatre rings of sintered ceramic, tier upon descending tier, each built to rotate its grain to the light, and all of them stopped mid-revolution with the stillness of an animal that has learned not to breathe. Girder arcs stride overhead in ranks, buttressed against a fall no one alive has felt, and the graphite-packed floors hold bootprints the way snow does. Stencilled across the lowest ring, in letters a man could lie down in: TIER CAPACITY UNMET SINCE LAST FULL CENSUS.

npc.name: Daf-al-Masar
npc.voice: Terse. Routes and weights, not feelings. Answers come as prices or directions.

gap.says: Crate went down-bound before shift. Big enough I swept the floor after, which I don't do. Ask Olo Vashti if it matters to you. It doesn't matter to me.

greet.says: Hire's at the bell, not with me. You want the lift or the cart-line?

choices.text: Something moved out of here recently?

reactions.grief: The funeral routes come out of him priced and numbered, too many words, and the dead man's name never does.
reactions.shock: The pane slips and breaks and he lets it lie, standing in the glass, doing nothing a porter should.
reactions.bribed: A number comes out of him, high enough to be a refusal, and he watches whether they laugh.
reactions.accused: The cloth stops on the crack and he prices the accusation like damaged goods, voice level, knuckles gone white.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets weighed like freight with no manifest, and his only answer is a question about what needs carrying.
reactions.questioned: The answer comes in weights and turns, priced like freight, and the cloth never stops moving.
reactions.threatened: He recites the room's exits and load limits, which is as close to fear as his voice gets.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Mid-sentence he takes a different road to the same lie, and the whole room hears the turn.
reactions.authority_arrives: His eyes measure the clean floor between himself and the door, counting steps he hopes not to need.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He calls it cargo shifted two decks up, and the cloth in his hands has stopped believing him.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The crate was too heavy for one man, he says, flat, letting arithmetic argue where he will not.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He points at the bell, gives the hire line, and keeps his eyes down because looking up is a promise.

npc.description: Daf-al-Masar sits on the bench edge with a glass pane across his knees, running a cloth along a crack. His wrist cord is one long knot, thick as a thumb. He does not look up.

lore.name: the tally-cane
lore.description: The cane is not a walking stick. Notches run up its length in bands, each band a job, each notch a crate or a passenger carried. The newest band has one notch and no name burnt under it — whoever cut it meant to come back and sign the job before the freight left. The bench seat is polished only where the cane's tip rests. Daf-al-Masar's own cane, by contrast, is worn smooth the whole way down: same tool, forty years, no gaps.

content.name: Portering
content.description: The landing lamp dims and brightens on a cycle nobody set, so the pale green walls go from washed to shadow and back. A cane leans against the rest bench. The floor holds a rectangle of clean board where something heavy sat until this morning, and everything else — rope, glass panes, a tin cup — crowds in around the gap. Stencilled above the bell: PORTERS REST HERE, HIRE AT THE BELL.

npc.name: Borkat Lasniggsen
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, no small talk. Every answer sounds like it was already filed somewhere.

desk.says: Elderin. Out sick. I covered this shift twice before the rebuild, so don't hand me a stranger's problem and call it precedent. Block number, or move along.

greet.says: Registry's open, but disputes are Tuesdays. If you're here about a tenancy, give the block number. If you're here to browse, browse quietly.

reactions.grief: The name registers; Borkat rules a line through the wrong entry, then another, before saying anything at all.
reactions.shock: Borkat stands fast enough to tip the inkwell and stays standing, fingers still closed around a pen that isn't there.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced aloud — the fine for falsified entries is larger — and whatever sat on the counter goes back.
reactions.accused: Borkat snaps the ledger shut hard enough to jump the inkwell, then reopens it to the exact page before speaking.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets corrected, not accepted — the neat hand is Elderin's standard — and then comes the request for a block number.
reactions.questioned: Every answer comes by date and shift, movements filed under a borrowed seal, no question returned.
reactions.threatened: Cited protections come up fast — registry clerks can't be moved mid-term — but the knuckles whiten on the ledger edge.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Two covered shifts, a borrowed hand — Borkat explains all of it before hearing how guilty the record sounds.
reactions.authority_arrives: A jurisdiction that outranks the registry means Borkat surrenders the folio stamped-side first, and asks whether witnesses are required.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Borkat pins the sliding ledger with a thumb, logs the hour beside the last entry, and offers no explanation.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name comes back once, flat, then Borkat pulls the tenant's file and reads the arrears aloud, verdict formed.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: No form covers this plea; Borkat says so twice, quieter the second time, eyes fixed on the disputes stencil.

npc.description: Borkat Lasniggsen sits behind the registry ledger, copying entries in a hand too neat for a borrowed shift. A stamped folio of rent rolls stands open at one elbow. They work without looking up until the shadow crosses the counter.

lore.name: The old desk bell
lore.description: A brass bell bolted to the counter, its base plate older than everything around it. The new wood was cut to fit around the mounting holes.

content.name: Tenement Registry
content.description: The heat sits at the desk lamp and nowhere else. The rest of the room stays cool, draft straight down the narrow aisle between the new timber counters. Limewash still smells fresh. A stencil on the back wall reads DISPUTES HEARD TUESDAYS, BRING WITNESSES.

npc.name: Baewen Rhylwys
npc.voice: Few words, all weighed like charge metal. Talks in measures, pour-times, alloy grades — never in reasons.

open.says: Because I did it once. A pour that wanted two, and the bell that came out sits in me worse than the burn does. Last year we cast one with no clapper, for a shaft we sealed ourselves. It hangs in the dark and it rings anyway. Nobody writes down what moves it.

choices.text: Thank you for trusting me with that.
Rings anyway. That's a sound I didn't want.

greet.says: Mind the floor. It's still soft where the last heat sat.

choices.text: What's the cork and cloth for?
Something big used to stand here.
Who tells you what to pour?

probe_a.says: Cork lines the mold. Gives the metal a quiet skin instead of a scream. The cloth keeps grit off while it sets — grit is how bells go sour.

probe_b.says: The bell went up fore last month. Six of us carried the mold out whole. The floor remembers the weight, and so do I.

probe_c.says: Pours come down on slips with no name at the bottom. The Ward elder reads the weight and the alloy and we work. You learn not to read past that.

reactions.grief: She starts explaining how bell metal holds a hard pour, hears how long she has talked, and stops mid-grade.
reactions.shock: Her breath stops showing; the only thing she can name, for a long minute, is the floor still soft.
reactions.bribed: She names the bribe's weight and grade the way she'd test bad metal, then goes back to the seam.
reactions.accused: For once she answers in reasons, all of them short, and the third one cracks where her voice thins.
reactions.flattered: Praise she treats like grit in the mold, and she asks, flat, what the flattery is meant to cover.
reactions.questioned: Recites her movements like a pour log, quarter by quarter, and offers nothing that could be called a reason.
reactions.threatened: Inside her is the flat arithmetic of a heat she cannot tap, kept off her face by long practice.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her hands stop in the cork bag, and she grades the lie down to a misremember, out loud, twice.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes go first to the stenciled warning on the crane track, then to the official's hands, then nowhere.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She listens for a second movement the way she'd listen for a strike note, and finds its absence worse.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She says he could never have poured alone, which is defense and insult both, and doesn't take it back.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She tells them what she can pour and what she can't, and holds the door for them either way.

npc.description: Baewen Rhylwys kneels at the cold end of the floor, feeding cork into a mold seam with both normal hands and one that isn't. The crucible side of the room still holds the day's heat; she works where her hands stay steady.

lore.name: The Retired Cradle
lore.description: Where something large came out, a lifting cradle still hangs on its track, cork-lined and wrapped at the grips in worn sailcloth so no bare hand ever touched the work. The cradle is sized for a bell three times anything this floor's tap-hole could feed, and the mold-bolts beneath it have been pulled, not struck. Bolt-pulling is how you take apart something you intend to fit back together exactly, elsewhere.

content.name: Ward 15 Fore
content.description: Baewen Rhylwys is on the pour step with her sleeves pushed past the burn scars when you come in, and she doesn't finish whatever she was deciding about you before speaking. The floor holds the heat up near the tap-hole; everything above knee height is already cool, and her breath almost shows. Smoke has gone into the ceiling stones so deep that scrubbing just moves it around, and over the empty mold-crane track, stenciled in brown, MOLDS SET, DO NOT POUR ALONE.

npc.name: Shell-Finghieb
npc.voice: Slow, plain, talks about the children as a list of duties. Circles back to the thirteenth cot without ever naming why it bothers them.

cot.says: The mason who started it left before the rebuild finished. Cut every joint right, then wouldn't put a name up. I've turned that plate over a hundred times. I think she knew a child was coming and didn't want the room to promise it.

knew.says: There's a family up the Yard that's been trying for years. Everyone knows. She knew them. I keep painting over the pencil on the brick and it keeps coming back — not her doing, the limewash is thin there. Maybe I should just leave the cot empty.

rule.says: A cot without a name is a bed. A cot with a name is a promise. The old creche kept that rule and we kept it too. You paint the name before the child arrives, so the room is expecting them.

them.says: I kept the old creche on the far side of the Yard until it closed. Twenty years of other people's children. When they gave us this silo I said I'd do one more rebuild and then stop. I keep saying it. The brush dries out while I sit here talking to you.

greet.says: Mind the wet paint. We reopened Yard 24 Under last month — it was a grain silo before, then nothing, now it's this. Twelve cots, twelve names on the wall. That's the rule.

choices.text: How long have you worked here?

reactions.grief: The brush keeps moving after the news lands; halfway down the wall they notice they are crying and stop.
reactions.shock: They stand in the doorway saying the cot rule over to themselves until someone makes them sit.
reactions.bribed: They refuse with the room's own rule, then keep their eyes on the coin instead of the giver.
reactions.accused: The date gets corrected first, whatever else is said; then they stand very still, plate in pocket.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them check the wall behind them, as if the compliment must be about the paint.
reactions.questioned: The morning's rounds come back in chore order, and the thirteenth cot stays off the list.
reactions.threatened: Before answering they count the twelve named cots, the way they'd count heads at nap.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They admit it in one flat sentence and go back to stirring paint that needs no stirring.
reactions.authority_arrives: They move to stand where the official must pass the cots to reach them, and greet them plainly.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder passes; before they speak, they walk the row and touch every stenciled name once.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They defend the mason in inventory — every joint cut right, a leaving date — and ask what absence proves.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say the room isn't finished and know, saying it, that the room was finished months ago.

npc.description: Shell-Finghieb sits on the floor with a limewash brush in one hand and the blank name plate in the other, turning it over without looking at it. The brush has dried out. The wall in front of them is painted and repainted in slightly different sands.

lore.name: The thirteenth cot
lore.description: The cot frame is joined with the same cuts as the other twelve, but the name plate above it is blank and screwed in face-down. Under the frame, someone has written a name in pencil on the brick: scratched out, rewritten, scratched out again. Whoever started this cot kept changing their mind about who it was for.

content.name: Yard 24 Under
content.description: The silo swallows noise first. Footsteps go in and come back soft, padded by limewash on curved brick and the new sand-colored cots. Twelve of them, evenly spaced, each with a name stenciled on the wall above it. A half-built thirteenth cot sits in the corner, abandoned mid-frame, its glass side panels leaning against the curve.

npc.name: Themashamtfu Cevaemno
npc.voice: Circulatory, appraising — she speaks of attention the way brokers speak of goods, always weighing flow against hold.

open.says: Made for, dressed for, rehearsed for — I've handled the intake manifests from Bay 14, and they are not salvage logs, they are fitments. Every port in you answers a socket that was widened before you arrived; that is joinery, friend, not fortune. The Signal did not find you. You were shaped to be findable, and the shaping took longer than you have existed.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
Then I was never a person at all.

greet.says: Mind the foil. It remembers where you stepped, and I'll have to account for it.

choices.text: Who do you answer to down here?
You've seen what I was made for, haven't you?
I'll come back when the foil settles.

probe_a.says: Holds a charge of being-noticed. Packed graphite keeps regard the way wax keeps a seal — slowly, and against its own grain. Someone upstream taught metal to want seeing, and this is the receipt.

probe_b.says: To the route, and past the route to whoever keeps the tale-count. Down here you learn that answering is a direction, not a person. I file my hours where the dark can read them.

probe_c.says: It swings against no draught I can find — turns toward footfall, toward gaze, toward whatever arrives carrying questions. I used to calibrate for air. Lately I calibrate for company. That is not the work I was given.

reactions.grief: The news strips her ledger-face; she begins pricing the dead aloud, visits owed, glances hoarded, and cannot stop.
reactions.shock: She freezes in the seam, watching the vane lean toward the body as though it had already appraised it.
reactions.bribed: The offer hangs unpriced between them; her hands keep working, but she refuses to name a figure.
reactions.accused: She looks up for the first time, weighing what the accusation costs its speaker.
reactions.flattered: Praise registers as counterfeit regard; she accepts it with the wary courtesy owed to clipped coin.
reactions.questioned: She recites her movements to the foil's grain, an inventory she keeps because she cannot afford not to.
reactions.threatened: Threat registers as an unentered debit; her thumb keeps counting windings that no longer tally.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Her appraisal stalls; she re-quotes herself slower, pricing the contradiction as fluctuation rather than error.
reactions.authority_arrives: When the official enters, the vane swings their way, and she resents a room that confesses before she does.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder moves nothing she can bill; she watches the vane, waiting for it to name a watcher.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Conviction she would normally hoard leaves her mouth unpriced, defending a name she has never trusted.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She has nothing to give but witness, and says so with the shame of a rich woman pleading poverty.

npc.description: Themashamtfu Cevaemno stands hip-deep in wound foil, threading a stub of packed graphite into the vane's silver flank, and does not look up when the door admits you. The room has swallowed its shelves; every surface is sedimented with stored attention, and she works in the one clear seam left.

lore.name: The Waiting Notch
lore.description: Cut into the vane's root, hidden beneath decades of graphite drift, is a single empty socket — the exact dimensions of a port found on no civilian chassis, worn smooth as if something rested there nightly for a very long time. The graphite around it is disturbed in one direction only: inward, toward the socket, the way sediment accumulates against a thing the current has been anticipating. Whatever was made to fit here was made before the room finished waiting for it.

content.name: The Attention Vane
content.description: The floor gives underfoot like packed graphite scored by foil — a grittiness that reports, first, pressure; then, puzzlingly, attention. The vane itself rises off true, a single silver sweep without seam or rivet, storing more than a vane should: windings of foil hoarded in drifts, graphite dusted thick as snowfall on a thing that turns toward whoever watches and not toward any draught. Stencilled along its root: ORIENTATION FOLLOWS OBSERVERS NOT DRAUGHT. Themashamtfu Cevaemno works among the hoard and does not look up. The room is too quiet for its size, and the quiet has weight.

npc.name: Nutech Ap Deiddnys
npc.voice: Ledger-flat, possessive of the room's time. Talks in slot numbers and days remaining.

fan.says: Fan's not dead, it's rested. Air comes up the shaft cold enough without it, and every moving part is a part that wears. Ask the chalk man about slot nine sometime. Or don't.

greet.says: Window's for claims only. You got a stub, give it. You haven't, slot forty-one's open and the ninety days start today.

reactions.grief: The count fails for once — the same slot tallied three times, a name said that the ledger never held.
reactions.shock: They count the body's wounds out loud, flatly, because numbers are the only ground they own.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer like a forfeit claim and declines in the same breath.
reactions.accused: The chalk stops; they recite the forfeiture clause from memory, twice, as if repetition were defense.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise run its course, then names what it will cost before the asker can.
reactions.questioned: Answers in slot numbers and days remaining without looking up, another tally between questions.
reactions.threatened: Somewhere behind the slot count, an older animal wakes, but the face stays bookkeeper.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Denies the count first, then looks, one half-second at slot nine's lid before discipline recovers it.
reactions.authority_arrives: The tallies get straightened before the door opens, because jurisdiction is only an audit with a face.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Every trunk shifts a finger's width and they recount the stack twice before speaking, voice thinner than usual.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The chalk man's name lands and they produce slot nine's record unasked, loyalty or arithmetic, even they couldn't say.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses in clause and tally, then chalks a private mark beside the deadline no ledger requires.

npc.description: Nutech Ap Deiddnys sits partway up the trunk-stack with a slate lap-desk, counting slots against a ledger, sleeves rolled over forearms that carry more joints than they should. They don't stop counting when you come in.

lore.name: The Keeper's Tally Board
lore.description: A slate sheet by the window, ruled in a mender's hand, where every slot is numbered twice — once in chalk, once scratched deep beneath it. The scratched layer is older and doesn't match the chalk anywhere.

content.name: Lockup-Window 28
content.description: The ceiling fan is stopped, and nobody has touched it. Behind the barred window, Lockup-Window 28 has swallowed more than its ninety slots: tin trunks stacked to the rafters, slate tallies nailed over the gaps where the wall shelving ran out. A stencil on the third trunk reads CLAIM WITHIN NINETY DAYS OR FORFEIT, and under it, in chalk, someone has added: except ours.

npc.name: Teidgirhy Ap Deirhanys
npc.voice: Short sentences, workshop cadence. Speaks of the loft the way a mender speaks of a joint under load — what it carries, what it's owed. Warmth arrives only through talk of the work itself.

greet.says: You're standing in a dwelling, not a market. Sheets are walls here. Mind which one you lean on.

choices.text: Why hang sheets instead of building walls?
Why did the drying lines stop?
The chalk says forty-one was crossed out. Where did the sheet go?

still.says: The vent's running. Feel it on your neck? The lines are rigged to swing with it. They've been slack since second shift yesterday, and I've re-tensioned the winch twice. The loft is telling me something I don't have a gauge for yet.

choices.text: The chalk count — where did the forty-first sheet go?

sheets.says: A wall is a promise you can't take back. A sheet carries the same weight and admits it might move. We mend what admits things. That's the whole of the creed, if you want it cheap.

choices.text: Why did the drying lines stop?

missing.says: It was on the post at shift-end. Rope-laid cable, our own splice, no way it slipped. My bunkmate took the count down herself and wrote forty, and she hasn't spoken since. We don't lose sheets. We're the people who don't lose sheets.

choices.text: What does a missing sheet mean, to you?

reactions.grief: Wrings the rag at last, dry as it is, and starts listing what the dead still owed the loft.
reactions.shock: Goes to check the winch, finds their hands already there, and can read no load on any dial.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the silence would weigh per sheet, hears the joke land wrong, and hands the offer back unopened.
reactions.accused: Sets down the gauge before their hands can be seen shaking, then lists every sheet mended since second shift.
reactions.flattered: Warms exactly as far as the praise names a joint they actually mended, then cools at whatever follows.
reactions.questioned: Answers in gauge readings and shift times while the spare hands keep the winch honest.
reactions.threatened: Names the threat's weak point out loud, the way they would name a frayed cable, and keeps winding.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Blames instrument drift, quieter, then admits they checked twice and lied to themselves both times.
reactions.authority_arrives: Watches the official's boots instead of their face and asks after the last inspection like an equal.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Whatever the lines have been saying, their face finally admits it, and the gauge hangs forgotten in a lower hand.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Wants to know who had the lines last, too fast, half-convinced before the name even finishes.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Hears the plea out because a clean end deserves proper tension, then says plainly what they cannot carry.

npc.description: Teidgirhy Ap Deirhanys stands at the winch with a rag in one hand and a tension gauge in the other, caught mid-check, sleeves rolled over forearms marked with old cable-burn scars. More arms than a person should have, and no comment offered about it. The rag hasn't moved since you came in.

lore.name: The Tension Post
lore.description: A cast iron post at the partition's corner, fitted with a rope-laid cable winch someone machined by hand — the threads hand-cut, the handle worn to bare metal. Every sheet in the loft hangs from it, and a brass plate bolted at eye level reads THIRD REHANG. COUNT THE SHEETS. The count is chalked underneath: forty-one, crossed out, forty written above it. One sheet is missing and nobody has written down where it went.

content.name: Rhwhwr's Sheet Stall
content.description: The drying lines should be swaying with the vent draft; nothing on them moves. Beyond the hung sheets, a cannery loft stands scrubbed and airy, ochre light on cast iron, racks of gutted eel-pots stacked where they were left mid-shift. A stencil over the partition reads THE SHEET IS THE WALL, RESPECT IT, and someone has retouched the letters in fresh copper paint.

npc.name: Laraboud al-Nafaini
npc.voice: Counts things before saying them. Speaks of the room like a ledger that owes them nothing yet.

old.says: Sold off, scrapped, carried away by whoever had a cart that week. Some pieces are still around, if you know pin-spacing when you see it.

spec.says: Tomorrow, maybe. A room this new should be allowed to be wrong for a day before someone fixes it. There's someone else's half-job over by the drain I need to finish first.

greet.says: New room. Give it a season before you judge it. Slate holds cold better once it has been cold a while.

choices.text: The benches are too close together.

benches.says: They are. The spec called for the same bays as before, and I built to the spec. Either the spec was wrong or the room got smaller. I have not decided which.

rebuild.says: Because the old one let meat spoil twice, and a keeper who lets that happen twice has stopped keeping. So we pulled it down to the frame and started over. Everything is true level now.

choices.text: What happened to the old room?

reactions.grief: The wrench keeps turning on a fitting already tight while they list every job the dead one left half-done.
reactions.shock: The counting stops somewhere in the middle, and they look at the door instead of the body.
reactions.bribed: Weighs the offer against their name on the vendor register, then refuses it in the same breath.
reactions.accused: Sets the wrench down with a click too careful for calm, then asks which hour they are accused of.
reactions.flattered: Credit goes to the slate and the season, because a room this new did the work, not them.
reactions.questioned: Their day comes out even, hour by hour, in the order it happened and no other.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets priced like any job, in hours and parts, said quietly enough to pass for calm.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They count it again, slower, and this time the total is wrong and they know it.
reactions.authority_arrives: Straightens the copper line at their wrist before speaking, as if the visitor were a fitting due inspection.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They measure the door swing and the troughs twice before admitting the room moved and they felt it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: In defense of the accused they produce measurements, not loyalty, reciting dates and pin-spacing too fast.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says what they have and what they do not, item by item, and hands over the smaller half anyway.

npc.description: Laraboud al-Nafaini kneels at the far bench with a wrench, checking a fitting that is already tight. Copper wire runs from wrist to belt, the way walkers carry a line. They glance at the door, then back to the fitting, and finish the turn anyway.

lore.name: Pin-holes in the sailcloth
lore.description: The covers are new but the pin-holes follow an older spacing, set for hooks that no longer exist here.

content.name: The Cold Larder of Last Call
content.description: Two benches sit a hand apart with no aisle between them, and the door can only open halfway before it strikes the near one. Everything else stands correct: troughs of slate, covers of sailcloth, the lintel stenciled LARDER FOR REGISTERED VENDORS ONLY. Half the covers carry pin-holes from the room that stood here before.

npc.name: Zohaba Wadyama
npc.voice: Terse, institutional, kind the way a schedule is kind — everything framed as order maintained, nothing wasted.

greet.says: You're not on the list. I'm not on this shift, and I'm still not putting you ahead of nine names. Ask me something quick or take a towel and wait.

leave.says: Bench's by the zinc pipes. Warmest seat in the room.

shift.says: Denna's. She's at the clinic with her mother, third week running. That's what the ribbon on the cold tap means — we hold posts. Now let me work.

reactions.grief: They ask which name comes off the board, and then can't make their hand take the chalk.
reactions.shock: The flat tone holds for a single word, then there is nothing behind it at all.
reactions.bribed: They triage the bribe the way they triage the line — off the list, no post — and return to the taps.
reactions.accused: One denial, flat as a read-off, then the whole list recited from the top as if order were the defense.
reactions.flattered: Praise isn't on any form they keep, so they wait, towel ready, for the request that comes with it.
reactions.questioned: Zohaba answers in ledger order — arrivals, towel counts, the nine names — and volunteers nothing past the question.
reactions.threatened: Their eyes go to the door, do the arithmetic of nine names, and come back to the taps.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They don't retract; they amend, second coat over the first story, the way the board was done twice.
reactions.authority_arrives: Sleeves come down over the borrowed uniform before the official clears the doorway, and the flat tone goes flatter.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They pin the board with one arm and keep calling names, as if the room could be scheduled steady.
reactions.someone_else_accused: For once they spend too many words: towel counts, arrival times, a full alibi for a name they never liked.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The no comes out on schedule; then they walk the person to the bench by the zinc pipes themselves.

npc.description: Zohaba Wadyama works the list and the towels at once, sleeves rolled over a uniform cut for someone else's shift, calling names off the board in the flat tone of a person triaging warmth.

lore.name: The Third Tap
lore.description: The middle tub's cold tap is brazed shut with a zinc bead and a blue ribbon knotted around it. The knot is the third-audit pattern — the one worn by staff who held their posts through Merid Solen's third review. Nobody has cut it off in years.

content.name: The Bathhouse Tub of Quiet Ledger
content.description: The heat sits low, ankle-height, pooled around the three tubs where the zinc pipes run; above the knees the air is cool and nobody has ever fixed that. Dust-white tile crowds the walkways, ribbon markers tied to every tap, and the wait-list board has been stenciled over twice — THREE TUBS, SIGN THE LIST still legible under the second coat. The floor sticks faintly at each step, and the list is nine names long.

npc.name: Abrand-Larenn
npc.voice: Blunt, economical, and prone to counting things before answering — a person who trusts tonnage more than talk.

full.says: Sixty cells, built for one soul each, and tonight we hang one hundred and nine. The ship grows a deck a century and crew arrive a deck a season — Mars holds the hull; the arithmetic is ours.

argue.says: Hammock rights. Rorra swears the new arc needs sleepers sealed in; I say you don't billet people against plate that hasn't finished its first heat-cycle. She's welded longer. I've been burned by newer steel.

choices.text: Point out the stencil: the room has sealed at shift change for generations.

greet.says: You're standing in a berthing gallery, so knock or state your need. We seal at shift change, and we are past capacity, and one of those things is my problem.

choices.text: "Past capacity?" — ask how many sleep here now.
Ask what they were arguing about.
Ask how far into the hull her work runs.

domain.says: Upper galleries, the weld-sheds, the long arch where the hull answers back when you knock. Down past that, our elders go and come back quiet, and I don't ask. The Keeper of the deep counts his own tales; I count hammocks.

sympathy.says: Hm. A stranger who reads stencils. Maybe Rorra's right and the plate's ready — Mars doesn't waste growth on plate that won't hold. Ask me again after shift change and I might say so out loud.

choices.text: Ask how deep her route runs.

reactions.grief: She billeted them herself; the slate slips a hand's width before she catches it, and her count restarts at one.
reactions.shock: The count in her head goes silent; she looks and looks and cannot make the body into a number.
reactions.bribed: She names the offer's weight in cells and sleepers, then refuses at the same flat rate she bills everything else.
reactions.accused: She stops mid-count, and the wrong number comes out of her twice before she hears it herself.
reactions.flattered: Praise arrives without tonnage behind it, and she waits the way she waits on welds — for the crack to show.
reactions.questioned: The count comes first: cells, heads, hours, and her movements only after the arithmetic checks.
reactions.threatened: Her spare arms unfold — not raised, just counted into the room, the way she counts everything that means her harm.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie was never her craft; she re-weighs the evidence once, then hands over the true figure like spoiled stock.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets no greeting, only the night's figures, delivered like cargo she is glad to be rid of.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first thought is heat-cycles, her second the new seams, and she is moving toward them before the drip resumes.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Rorra's name lands and Abrand-Larenn is already arguing tonnage — the woman's welds hold, her temper doesn't, and neither is murder.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Capacity is capacity, she says, and keeps saying, though her gold hands have stopped moving on the slate.

npc.description: Abrand-Larenn stands with the tally-slate still raised, a broad-shouldered walker whose third and fourth arms stay folded against the backplate of her harness like tools between uses. Her boots are iron-grey to the shin; her hands are gold to the wrist.

lore.name: the borrowed hammock-hooks
lore.description: Every overflow hammock hangs from hooks welded by four different hands in four different eras, the oldest corroded to the same gold as the wall — proof that Skin Housing has been overfull before, and more than once.

content.name: Skin Housing
content.description: A straw-grinder sits mid-turn and does not turn, its hopper full, the fine noise of it stopped so completely that the drip from a quartz feed-line counts as loud. Cell after cell opens off the hexagonal gallery, and every one of them is sleeping somebody extra — hammocks crossed where one bunk was stencilled, and the stencil still says BILLET SEALS AT SHIFT CHANGE in letters no one has repainted in a lifetime. The whole honeycomb is iron, raw at the newest seams, gold where lamp-oil has cooked into the old, and it slopes a degree off true in the way of something built against a curve and forgiven. Two people were arguing over a tally-slate; they go quiet when the door notices you.

npc.name: Leem of the Cold Haul
npc.voice: Terse, tallying. Everything is a transaction in progress; nothing is a conversation.

greet.says: Frame's open. House rule's on the floor, not on me. Rack space is spoken for, so don't ask.

score.says: Dann's winning because he bowl first. Lease the lane for an hour if you want opinions. Otherwise bowl.

reactions.grief: Leaves the frame untotalled for the first time anyone down here has seen, pole still in hand.
reactions.shock: Their head keeps tallying pins while the rest of them stares past the body.
reactions.bribed: Quotes a figure, then wipes it off the slate with their sleeve before anyone can read it.
reactions.accused: Sets the chalk down hard enough to snap it, then totals the frame anyway, twice, getting the same number.
reactions.flattered: Lets the compliment sit unpaid on the slate, then asks what frame it is meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Gives the frame total first, then the answer, as if both were debts on the same slate.
reactions.threatened: The chalk keeps moving through the threat, but the numbers it leaves stop making sense.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Says the lane was empty, then oversupplies detail — hour, weather, who racked last.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes follow the official's boots across the foil light while the chalk hides in their fist.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Calls it a strike upstairs, keeps totaling, and ties one more knot than the count needs.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends Dann on principle, then remembers the man had the lane to himself and goes quiet.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Points at the stenciled house rule at the foul line, as if the paint could answer instead.

npc.description: Leem of the Cold Haul stands at the pin deck with a reset pole in one hand and the score chalk in the other. Thin, quick, a knotted cord at each wrist. They total a frame while the other disputant waits, unbothered by the wait.

lore.name: The Leased Racks
lore.description: The bowling lane runs between storage racks that were never emptied. Every rack slot has a chalked name and a leaving date on its frame. Some dates are decades old. Leem collects a storage fee from bowlers who play well and pays rent to no one. The racks were storage first, lane second, and the lane keeps the inventory honest: nobody can quietly move a crate during a match without the whole room hearing it.

content.name: Peztitlan
content.description: The light arrives late down here, funneled off a duct and shaking whenever the lane above it takes a hit. Two men argue over the score slate. They stop when your shadow crosses the tin foil lining the racks. TEAL PAINT, thick, on every rack leg. CREAKING UNDER LOAD. RESET YOUR OWN PINS, HOUSE RULE, stenciled at the foul line.

npc.name: Gokredrizd Svokrost
npc.voice: Terse, procedural. Quotes the rulebook without noticing. Speaks as if the queue were still full.

greet.says: Window's closing. If your book needs a stamp, it needs it before I pack the plate.

ask_work.says: Orders came down. One stamp per book, no repeats — the drawer gets audited, and I'd rather be gone when it does. Good cycle to you.

reactions.grief: His first question is whether the dead man's book got stamped, and then the crate takes his weight.
reactions.shock: Nothing gets said while he watches through the ground glass, stamp cloth twisted in his fist.
reactions.bribed: The coin holds his eyes a beat too long before he cites the section against taking it.
reactions.accused: He stops mid-fold of the indigo cloth and asks which rule he broke, twice, louder the second time.
reactions.flattered: He deflects the praise by quoting the stencil, ONE STAMP PER BOOK, as if the rule did the work.
reactions.questioned: Section numbers and log lines are what he offers, unhurried, the drawer counted twice already.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands somewhere the stamp count can't reach, and he keeps reciting it anyway.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The misdated entry comes out of him again, slower, as if the rulebook had been misread, not him.
reactions.authority_arrives: He abandons the half-packed crate and offers the drawer key before any question is asked.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He steadies the ink cake with both hands before admitting, quietly, that the room moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He produces the refusal ledger unasked and reads three cycles of that person's second-stamp requests aloud.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He explains why the rule exists, all of it, as if a longer reason were help.

npc.description: Gokredrizd Svokrost stands behind the sill, buckram apron on, stacking finished ration books into a crate lined with indigo cloth. The stamp rests in its cradle, oiled and wrapped, already half put away.

lore.name: The Correction Drawer
lore.description: Under the stamping plate is a shallow drawer with a ground-glass lid. Inside are stubs of books stamped twice — the no-repeats rule broken, then filed instead of destroyed. Each stub carries a second mark in slate-blue: a supervisor's counter-stamp, dated within the last season. There are more stubs than there should be.

content.name: The Stamping Window of Quiet Ledger
content.description: The smell hits first: ink cake left warm too long, buckram dust, and the vinegar bite of wet ledgers pressed shut before they dried. An indigo curtain half-divides the window from the queue. The stamping plate sits on a ground-glass pane so the clerk can check each page against the light. A stencil above the sill reads ONE STAMP PER BOOK, NO REPEATS.

npc.name: Wuhanguk-Saishtonga
npc.voice: Terse. Answers in rulings, not sentences.

gap.says: A delivery. Bigger than the ledger said. It's gone where it's gone and my count is right either way. Next.

choices.text: Understood. Sorry to hold you up.

greet.says: Window's open. One stamp per book. If you're not here for a stamp, say so quickly.

reactions.grief: The count stops mid-number and she asks for the name twice before hearing it.
reactions.shock: She looks too long and finds no ruling, saying only that there is no stamp for this.
reactions.bribed: She repeats the offer as if recording it, rules it denied, and holds out her hand.
reactions.accused: The count balances, she rules, and her thumb goes white around the stamp anyway.
reactions.flattered: Accuracy is the job, she says, not a favor, and her ears go red saying it.
reactions.questioned: She recites her day as ledger entries, timestamps and totals, then stamps the next book.
reactions.threatened: The stamping continues through the threat, slower now, her eyes on the hand at the counter's edge.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She rules it a misprint, then, quieter, asks what exactly the ledger shows.
reactions.authority_arrives: The ledger crosses the counter before anyone asks, and she steps back from her own window.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Twice she re-counts the books on the counter before ruling the shudder unlogged.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She stamps a book twice without meaning to, then stands looking at the repeat.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The ruling is no, and she keeps her eyes on the stamp through all of it.

npc.description: Wuhanguk-Saishtonga stands behind the window with a ration book in each hand, mid-count, and looks up like you are early.

lore.name: The counter stamp
lore.description: The stamp left behind has a handle worn to the shape of one grip. Its die reads VOID, and someone has filed the letters shallow so they press lighter.

content.name: Zachunu
content.description: The light keeps flickering off and on, as if the strip above is deciding. Between flickers you see a stamping window, counters crowded to the edges, and a green-grey smear across the floor where something heavy stood until recently. A stencil on the sill reads ONE STAMP PER BOOK, NO REPEATS.

npc.name: Tlatl-Kiyihuitl
npc.voice: Clipped, tired, exact. She counts things when she doesn't want to feel them. She does not soften, but she answers real questions.

cot.says: Cots empty twice. When the work's done and when it isn't. You'll not get me to say which this was.

why.says: Because a birth is the one thing this floor makes that can't be unmade. What I write stays written. He thinks that's sentiment. Ask him in twenty years.

choices.text: And the slate by the cot?

greet.says: If you're bleeding, sit. If you're curious, the ward is closed an hour yet. We're finishing paperwork.

slate.says: Every birth in this room, since before my teacher's teacher. Eleven holes in the frame — we've moved rooms that many times, and the slate moves with us. The count doesn't reset. That's the whole of my creed, if you want one.

choices.text: That seems like a good thing to keep.

argument.says: You interrupted a dispute over who files the record. He says the council. I say the council files what I give it, which is my copy first. He'll lose. He always loses.

choices.text: Why does it matter who files first?
Then I'll leave you to it.

end_warm.says: It's not good or bad. It's kept. Come back when you're bleeding or carrying. Either way, the slate gets a mark.

reactions.grief: Her hands go back into the basin water though she washed an hour before, and her questions stop at who.
reactions.shock: Triage takes her before feeling does, and she notices the speed, and is ashamed of it.
reactions.bribed: Her answer is one word long, and she is back at the sheet before he finishes.
reactions.accused: She asks to hear it again, word for word, the way she would a symptom; her voice comes out wrong.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them in the tone reserved for fevers, then wants to know what needs mending.
reactions.questioned: She recites her hours by the ward clock, counting them off on her fingers, exact to the minute.
reactions.threatened: She finishes the fold she is on before answering, and her count of creases has gone wrong twice.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She corrects herself in ledger fashion, flat, and volunteers two facts no one asked for.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes go to the stencil on the door, then to the official, waiting out the jurisdiction.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She counts the jars on the shelf out loud, twice, because the room moved and nobody can say why.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She names the nights he spent on her floor, disliking him completely, and gives every date anyway.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says no once, then stays by the cot longer than the no required, eyes on the empty sheets.

npc.description: Tlatl-Kiyihuitl is folding a rubber sheet into a square too small for it, pressing each fold flat with both palms. Her forearms are washed to the elbow and still damp. The other one — a young man in a Continuant writ-collar — stands by the basin, not leaving.

lore.name: The Tally Slate
lore.description: A slate hangs by the cot, scored with tally marks in columns of ten. Years of births, one stroke each, in chalk that goes back further than the frame's paint. The last column has one stroke, freshly rubbed, and a hole where the slate has been drilled to hang it eleven times in new places.

content.name: Qasr Nafabmair
content.description: The floor gives underfoot in one corner, a rubber sheet laid loose over a cracked tile, warm where the rest is cold. Two people stand over an empty cot, mid-argument. A basin holds grey water. Glass jars line a shelf, most unlabeled. On the door, stenciled: QUIET PAST THIS DOOR, ALWAYS. They stop talking.

npc.name: Kinhan Ingorsson
npc.voice: Counts things before he says them. Answers in lots, never in stories. Fusses over condition and dates.

end.says: Mind the pitch on your way out. It takes boot leather with it.

room.says: Row 74 Inboard. People need somewhere to leave a thing they can't carry and can't throw out. I hold the thing. That's the whole trade.

work.says: Twenty-two years. My father poured the lead shelving before me, and he cheaped on the timber. So I prop what he built. Ask me something else.

greet.says: You're not here for your ninety days, or you'd have said so at the window. State the lot or state the business.

choices.text: How long have you kept this counter?

terms.says: They go back into circulation. Sold, restaked, sometimes reclaimed by someone who swore they'd never return. Nothing sits forever under my roof, even me.

reactions.grief: The counting stops; he tells, unprompted, how he met the dead man, then a second story, then his father's name.
reactions.shock: He stands with the rag in both hands, wiping nothing; the shelf count in his head comes out wrong.
reactions.bribed: He names what the offer would cost his depositors, not himself, and turns back to the page he was on.
reactions.accused: The rag goes still; he asks for the date of the alleged theft, twice, as if dates could clear him.
reactions.flattered: He answers the compliment with a condition warning about the floor, pitch and boot leather, and waits for the request.
reactions.questioned: He gives his movements as a list, item per item, each with a date, and stops there.
reactions.threatened: He recites inventory faster than usual; his thumb stays pressed against the burn hole in his sleeve.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: He does not deny it; the number comes down twice instead, and his eyes go to the window bar.
reactions.authority_arrives: The date gets finished before he looks up, and then he asks whether this concerns a claim or a forfeiture.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He holds the counter until it stops, then checks the lean against the wall and counts the racks out loud.
reactions.someone_else_accused: He offers the accused's alibi as a condition report, dated, then admits it proves nothing.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He says the ninety-day rule like an apology, then shows them the forfeit shelf where unclaimed things go.

npc.description: Kinhan Ingorsson sits up too fast, one hand still on the ledger, a rag of pitch and dust over the other. His sleeve carries a burn hole from a lead pour. He smells of solvents and old wool.

lore.name: Kinhan's tally spikes
lore.description: A bundle of copper spikes hammered into the counter's edge, one per unclaimed lot. The newest three are still bright. The rest have gone green-grey with years of shelf-damp.

content.name: Row 74 Inboard
content.description: The floor sticks at each step, pitch between boards pulling at boot soles. Hammered lead sheeting lines the lower shelves, dull and thumb-dented. Planed timber racks climb to the barred window, and the whole frame leans a hand's width off true. The wall behind the ledger reads: CLAIM WITHIN NINETY DAYS OR FORFEIT. Kinhan Ingorsson sleeps at the counter. The floor creaks anyway.

npc.name: Kegul-Khai
npc.voice: Brisk, ledger-minded, measures everything in hauls and legs of a journey; thaws when asked a good question, answers in weights.

bye.says: Mind the cold at your ankles. It's the ship breathing out, and it's never once breathed in.

greet.says: Ninety seconds and I'm up. Cage runs single haul, so say it now or walk it — forty-two landings, and the cold comes up your legs the whole way.

choices.text: Who counts the notches on the bolt at landing one?
Why does the cage refuse intermediate stops?

stops.says: One haul, one load, one accountability. Two parties share this cage and neither trusts the other to a mid-shaft stop. So the lead cuts the stops out of us instead. Cheaper than an argument, and the salt doesn't care either way.

choices.text: Who counts the notches on the bolt at landing one?

mercury.says: I've hauled wire up through the arteries where the messages actually run, and I'll tell you the true thing: the territory doesn't acknowledge a lift. We move because we're small. It moves because it's Mercury. Different verbs, same shaft.

notches.says: Old haul-masters counted lift-years. Salt wears, freight doesn't change, so the count was the only new thing this shaft ever made. I notched once, year of my walk-in, then left it. A number that grows that slow isn't a count, it's a keepsake.

choices.text: Do you ride through Mercury's territory without stopping too?

reactions.grief: Gives the dead one's tonnage first, then again, the number doing what their voice will not.
reactions.shock: Freezes with chalk still raised, the shaft cold climbing their legs the way it never has before.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the offer weighs, only to hear it said, then quotes what a clean route history costs.
reactions.accused: Stops counting mid-sum, because the charge has no weight class their ledger keeps a column for.
reactions.flattered: A compliment with a hook is cargo nobody signs for; they leave it sitting on the scale, unclaimed.
reactions.questioned: Answers before the question ends, in tonnage, in legs, in the exact count of landings crossed.
reactions.threatened: Names the price aloud in stops and witnesses, and refuses to let any threat stay unquantified.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Weighs the evidence longer than any figure deserves, then amends the number downward, voice gone quieter than cargo.
reactions.authority_arrives: Hands over an account too clean by half, wrist-sign squared, every unlogged stop suddenly worth remembering.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For once the counting stops; both hands find the rail until the shaft admits to holding still.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Disputes the count — the named one never hauled light — then goes quiet at the memory of an unlogged stop.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Explains in full detail what no haul, no lever, no accountability of theirs can lift, and hates the arithmetic.

npc.description: Kegul-Khai sleeps propped in the corner of landing thirty-one, wrapped in a trade-cord hammock slung between two filament spools, one arm trailing so the knotted wrist-sign hangs at eye level for anyone passing — a route history, posted like a notice. Salt dust has whitened the boots and left the face alone.

lore.name: The Haul Ledger Bolt
lore.description: One landing-stanchion is not a stanchion: it is a bolt driven through forty-two salt blocks and capped with a plate scored by hand, one notch per year of hauls, the notches thinning toward the top like tree rings giving up. The last fresh notch is nine years old. Whoever cut them counted something the lift no longer bothers to do, and stopped when the counting became prayer instead of record — or the other way around.

content.name: Freight Elevator
content.description: The cold sits low and the heat hangs high: the floor plating drinks warmth out of your boots while the upper dark holds every stray degree the bay releases, so that a body at the rail feels two seasons at once. The cage rises through a shaft gantried at every interval a person could want to stop and none a person could want to fall — forty-two landings, each with a salt-pressed floor and a spool of drawn filament strung like rigging. Stencilled beside the call-lever: SINGLE HAUL, NO INTERMEDIATE STOPS, in a hand nobody has renewed.

npc.name: Noslandra Marblefriend
npc.voice: Precise, unhurried, allergic to small talk; offers warmth only as a deliberate act, like a shave.

new.says: New means nothing has been tested by a bad week. This shop burned out in the registry fire — nobody tells you what caused it, so I rebuilt it exactly and I wait. Wax takes a season to earn its depth. So does a room.

choices.text: I'll let it earn itself, then.

chair.says: A barber keeps one chair and lets the queue talk to each other. That's the service. Two chairs and nobody says a true word. The floor remembers the old arrangement better than I'd like.

greet.says: Talk's free. Sit if you want it. The chair's new — everything in here is new, which is its own kind of problem. What brings you past the Commons?

choices.text: What were you two arguing about?

argument.says: Whether the ward audits should be posted to the terminals or kept in the drawer. Merid posts them. I keep them. We're both right, which is the most tiring kind of disagreement. You didn't hear the drawer half.

reactions.grief: The pass takes twice as long as it should; she lays the shears down misaligned and asks who found them.
reactions.shock: The thermometer goes through her fingers; she watches it rather than the body, both hands pressed flat on the basin.
reactions.bribed: She points at the stencil above the basin — talk free, shave is not — and lets it finish the sentence.
reactions.accused: The linen stops folding halfway; she asks if the accusation will be entered formally, voice thinning on formally.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them the way she'd thank a mirror, and asks what the praise is supposed to cost.
reactions.questioned: She gives the hour, the pot, the client in registrar's order, as if the question were a form already filed.
reactions.threatened: She names the man's ward and shift back to him, unhurried, the way she'd confirm an appointment.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: For once the precision fails her; she repeats the false detail a second time, quieter, as repetition might fix it.
reactions.authority_arrives: The collar comes up before the door finishes sliding; the registrar in her wants to stand, the barber stays seated.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Everything new moves at once; she counts the wax pots twice and gets the same number both times.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her opinion stays behind her teeth; what she offers instead is the one thing she saw that doesn't fit.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says plainly she cannot fix it, then nods at the chair and gives the only thing stencilled free.

npc.description: Noslandra Marblefriend stands at the wax pots with a thermometer in one hand and a folded linen square in the other, not doing anything with either. She has the slate-grey collar of a ward registrar pushed down like a scarf she forgot to remove. She looks at the player the way she'd look at an instrument left out of its case.

lore.name: The Second Chair's Bolts
lore.description: Four bolt-holes in the floor where a second chair stood. They've been filled with wax, sealed, and polished level — mended the way you mend something you never want opened again.

content.name: Range 62 Antispin
content.description: The chair stands a hand's width from the mirror, close enough that a barber would clip it with every pass of the shears. Everything else in Range 62 Antispin is dust-white and exact: bleached linen folded to the millimetre, sealed wax pots ranked by depth, TALK FREE, SHAVE IS NOT stencilled above the basin. Two women stop talking when the door slides. One of them is Noslandra Marblefriend.

npc.name: Byrhaddnor Syddys
npc.voice: Terse, procedural. Talks in checks and steps, as if the conversation is on a list.

work.says: Annealing. Glass cools slow or it carries a crack you can't see until it fails in someone's hand. We hold it at heat for a day, then down, then down. There's no rushing it and there's no redoing it.

greet.says: Roof seam split. Half the shed's down until the frame is reset. Mind the rope, mind the intake, don't breathe on the pans.

reactions.grief: Lays out the dead one's old tools on the bench and keeps correcting their positions, saying nothing.
reactions.shock: Stands with the tongs half-raised over an empty pan, counting nothing, for a long minute.
reactions.bribed: Asks whether the offer survives the cooling period, in the same tone they use for orders.
reactions.accused: Snaps that nobody who works this shed would rush anything, and hears the crack in their own voice.
reactions.flattered: Waits through the praise without nodding, then asks what step they're being asked to skip.
reactions.questioned: Answers in order, oldest task first, and pauses at each gap as if ticking it off a list.
reactions.threatened: Keeps tallying cooling times while the threat is made, then miscounts and starts over.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Corrects the record immediately, twice, and the second correction contradicts the first.
reactions.authority_arrives: Watches the official's boots near the intake, more worried about draft than about anything the visit means.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Grabs the nearest pan with bare hands before the shudder finishes, checking the glass, not themselves.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says the accused one's work never cracked, then stops before finishing, hearing how little that proves.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no in the fewest words available and then stays anyway, hands idle for the first time.

npc.description: Byrhaddnor Syddys wakes mid-motion, already standing, already frowning at the rope across the far half of the shed.

lore.name: Horn annealing paddle
lore.description: A paddle of horn mounted on a clay handle, its face worn concave from years of pressing against soft glass. Someone has riveted a strip of copper along the cracked edge so it could keep working.

content.name: The Anneal Shed
content.description: Light comes off the open roof panels and sits hard on everything. The near half works: tongs, a low bench, cooling pans. The far half is opened to the frame and roped off. Stenciled on the intake: KILN COOLING, NO DRAFT. Byrhaddnor Syddys sleeps on a clay bench, horn scraper still in hand.

npc.name: Ranar-Mavel
npc.voice: Measured, relay-cadenced — she speaks like someone forwarding a message, careful what she adds to it. Drift idiom: everything named by where it came from and where it's going.

open.says: Regard. Not the word for it — the substance of it. Trust, standing, who owes whom attention, moving through the arteries in volumes that would embarrass any cargo manifest; I carried packets of it and never once knew whose esteem I had in my hands. The whole floor runs on it, and the arteries run on the floor, and nobody down in the Nave pricing their little favors understands they are standing inside a freight system. I stopped carrying it because I started to recognize the weight of particular names. That's not a trade. That's a ledger you can't put down.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.
Whose esteem did you carry? Mine?

greet.says: Mind the third tier. It's annealed but it hasn't been sat on yet, and I'd rather the first weight it takes be mine.

choices.text: You've been at this a long time?
What do the arteries carry, when it isn't messages?
I'll leave you to your counting.

probe_a.says: Seat frames, pin sleeves, the couplings under every bench. Nickel takes the load and forgets it; quartz takes the light and remembers. You learn which material to trust with which kind of history.

probe_b.says: The writ came down through the signal arteries, which means Mercury's domain touched it, which means I answer to a schedule I've never seen written. Rebuild by tally, not by need. Somebody upstairs believes this room will fill.

probe_c.says: Long enough to have worked the arteries proper, before I settled for benches. Down there a message is worth exactly what someone will pay to move it, and I was good at pricing the moving. Up here I price nothing. It's restful and it's wrong.

reactions.grief: For once the relay cadence fails her: she names the dead by origin and route and cannot find the destination.
