reactions.shock: She allows the body one look before turning to the quartz, trusting light to remember so she doesn't have to.
reactions.bribed: Asked what the offer weighs, she answers honestly, then refuses cargo she has carried once and already buried.
reactions.accused: The answer comes evenly, nothing added, but the wrench goes down like she no longer trusts her hands.
reactions.flattered: Praise arrives like an unaddressed parcel; she checks it for a sender before answering, and answers about torque specs instead.
reactions.questioned: She gives her morning as a freight manifest — origin, destination, contents — and adds nothing the question didn't ask for.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets signed for like freight: she notes its weight, its sender, and wants neither in her hands.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She concedes the point the way a courier recalls a misrouted packet — receipt acknowledged, error logged, no apology offered.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her thumb finds the knot-cord, checking which old routes are still defensible, before she greets the official by origin.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For the first time in years her count stops; she stands in the cold reading the slope for whatever moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Hearing that name, she gives its cargo history through her hands — weights, dates, recipients — far more than anyone asked for.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She answers the plea with its proper routing and hates how steadily her voice forwards what she cannot carry.

npc.description: Ranar-Mavel is kneeling at the base of the lowest quartz tier, seating a nickel pin with a torque-wrench older than the tier above it, and counting under her breath the way people count when the count is the work. A knotted cord circles her wrist, its pattern dense with routes she has clearly not walked in years.

lore.name: The Exchange Dais
lore.description: The stage is not a stage but a dais of annealed nickel, and set into its lip are three hundred small drawers, each holding a knotted cord and a counter-cord tied to it — a bid and an answer, catalogued by hand in a notation older than the stencilling. The knots record no goods: they record tellings. Who spoke, who traded the retelling, and what the retelling earned — regard, measured like grain, down to the fraction. The last completed trade is centuries deep in the drawer stack, and the cord beside it is still waiting for an answer.

content.name: Susun
content.description: The cold sits in the floor and nowhere else: the tiered quartz benches drink warmth from your boots while the air above stays trading-floor temperate, stirred by a draft that crosses the slope without ever settling. Gold leaf runs the inner arc of the ceiling, forty rows up, bright as new coin despite everything. Stencilled along the lowest riser, in letters sized to be read from the far edge: SEATING RATED, ATTENDANCE NEVER MET. Below the stage, a worker in nickel-sheened gear sorts something small and glinting and does not look up.

npc.name: Yazdzeiist Sostyadya
npc.voice: Plain, unhurried, using verbs of keeping where verbs of making belong; occasionally answers questions you have not asked.

held.says: You'll feel it tonight, in a cell, if you sleep here: the hum keeps your name somewhere, in a register no one keeps. That is the whole of dwell, down here. To be kept. I stopped asking by whom some years ago, and slept better for it.

choices.text: Thank her and let her work.

owed.says: By whatever still reads us. The signal below has been answering for months now — ask your own ports, they'll tell you before any gauge does.

cells.says: Doing. You say doing. I used to say humming. Saturn's word — if it were mine to have — would be one I only half remember my mother using, for a thing that holds you while pretending to be held.

greet.says: You came in on the echo. Most do, first time. The rank heard you before you heard it — that's the honest order of things down here.

choices.text: What are the closed cells doing?
What happened to the opened half?

reach.says: Toward the middle. Everything down here reaches toward the middle, or away from the ends; I've stopped being able to tell which direction the reaching runs, and so has the wool, if wool can be said to try.

choices.text: Let the question stand and go.

years.says: I stopped counting. Not from piety — from courtesy. The rank knows its own number, and it seemed rude to arrive at it second.

repair.says: Nothing happened. That's what no one believes. The rank opened itself the way a sleeper turns — to reach something on its far side. We only tidy after. Wool back in, seams dressed, and next shift it's turned again.

choices.text: How long have you tidied after it?

saturn.says: Spoken. No. But the notation on the oldest walls has changed its tense, and I have decided — privately, you understand — that a change of tense is a kind of address.

stencil.says: Counted things get compared. Compared things get a before and an after. The rank is owed its before. I keep the slate anyway — it's the refusing that's the rite, not the not-knowing.

choices.text: And the after — there is one?

reactions.grief: She packs wool until the flank bulges, grief admitted only as pressure, far too much of it, densely kept.
reactions.shock: Wool slips from idle hands while she waits, as this basalt taught her, for the shock to arrive late.
reactions.bribed: She requests that the sum be written down, since anything entered here is kept, and therefore witnessed, forever.
reactions.accused: For the first time in anyone's memory her hands go entirely still, and stillness on her reads as screaming.
reactions.flattered: She lets praise wash past without admitting it, as wool admits no sound, though her hands falter, pleased.
reactions.questioned: She answers the question nobody asked first, in her unhurried verbs of keeping, as though accounting were shelter.
reactions.threatened: Somewhere beneath the fear she registers the threat as another keeping, and hates herself for how well it fits.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted, she amends her account downward, sealing the smaller lie over the first like a second layer of wool.
reactions.authority_arrives: Only for jurisdiction does she turn to be seen, studying the official's badge as a register might study her.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the rank moves she only flattens a palm to the basalt, timing how late the rock admits having heard.
reactions.someone_else_accused: For the accused she speaks far too long, citing registers and signals nobody knew she monitored.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to help, she stays anyway, performing the one office her trade knows, keeping company with what cannot be kept.

npc.description: Yazdzeiist Sostyadya works with her back to the opened cells, sealing wool into a cell's flank with hands that slow but never still — as though stillness itself were the fault she is repairing. She does not turn to be seen.

lore.name: A tally-slate worn concave
lore.description: Hung at the rank's open seam: a slate of cast basalt rubbed hollow at its centre by generations of thumbs that began a count and, per the stencil, refused to finish it.

content.name: The Cell Rank of Second Shift
content.description: Sound arrives here already altered — footfall returns late, softened, as though the basalt were deciding whether to admit having heard you. The rank of cells runs off into iron-dark recession, half of them opened like anatomies, mineral wool spilling in pale ropes that drink the hum of the working half to a subvocal thrum. A stencilled admonition — DO NOT COUNT THE CELLS ALOUD — has been repainted so many times its letters sit in relief, a scar of obedience. The hum recurses, each cell listening to its neighbour listen; an analogy offers itself — a throat, a hive, a held breath — and declines to complete.

npc.name: Tlilchitl-Tinikoatl
npc.voice: Short, practical, counting things. Speaks in wheel terms even about people.

work.says: Half the Nave rides a cart or a cycle now, and the council started charging for new rims. So they bring us the old ones. A rim can be trued maybe five times before the metal's had it. We keep count.

argue.says: Whether to true a rim a sixth time. My colleague says yes. I say a rim that's failed twice under load doesn't get a sixth. We were arguing about it before you came in, and we'll be arguing after you leave.

choices.text: "The load doesn't care about your optimism."
Nod and step back from the stands.

greet.says: If you've a wheel, the tag has the number. If you've a question, make it a short one — we're behind by forty.

fortyone.says: Forty-one carried a bakery cart eleven years. Every time it came in bent, we trued it, and every time it came back true. That's the whole secret. Metal remembers good handling. Most things do.

reactions.grief: Asks which wheel the dead one rode, then describes its wobble in detail, voice level until it isn't.
reactions.shock: The count leaves them at the sight of the body; their thumb keeps circling a rim that isn't there.
reactions.bribed: Refuses flatly: a miscounted tag puts a bad wheel under someone's child, and they don't sign those.
reactions.accused: Asks which wheel, which tag, which number, and the shop goes quiet around a voice they didn't know could rise.
reactions.flattered: Their eyes run the tap-test across the flatterer's face, and nothing there rings true, so nothing gets accepted.
reactions.questioned: Recites the day's numbers without looking up — four trued, one rejected, none wasted — a ledger they keep against worse questions.
reactions.threatened: Keeps truing through the threat, but the spokes come out a half-turn too tight, and they know it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their wrench stops clicking; they study the tag a long moment, then say the numbers must be someone else's.
reactions.authority_arrives: Points the official to the tag board and keeps working, though their shoulders have climbed toward their ears.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Grabs two hooks' worth of swinging wheels by reflex, then admits aloud that no truing fixes whatever just moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says the colleague they argue with daily has never let a bad rim pass, and realizes mid-sentence it isn't proof.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Hears the whole plea out, then offers a true wheel and a number, and hates how little that is.

npc.description: Tlilchitl-Tinikoatl stands at a truing stand, one thumb resting on a rim, a spoke wrench held like a pen. Their apron is umber with brake dust and their hands keep working even while they watch you.

lore.name: The numbered chalk wall
lore.description: Every wheel in the shop carries a chalk number, and the wall behind the stands carries the same numbers with tally marks under them. Most have one. A few have six or seven — a wheel brought back again and again, trued each time rather than replaced. One number, 41, has a line drawn through it and the word 'good' written under the line. Nobody throws a good wheel away here, and nobody says out loud what makes a wheel good.

content.name: The Truing Shop of Third Watch
content.description: The floor grits with steel filings that cling to your soles. Wheels hang four deep from copper hooks along both walls, and the truing stands crowd the aisle so two people must turn sideways to pass. A stencilled board by the door reads WHEELS TAGGED, COLLECT BY NUMBER. The two workers stop arguing and look at you.

npc.name: Tryncun Beidys
npc.voice: Terse, declarative, answers questions about the room with questions about whether you'll need it.

thaw.says: Hm. You're quieter than most who come through. There's solvent on the shelf by the door if the fumes bother you. Take a breath and go on about your day.

crack.says: You've got eyes, then. Fine. One child left without a household and the creche closed before we could mend that. Mending is the work. Unfinished work sits under tin until someone can take it up again. I have not taken it up. I keep meaning to.

choices.text: Maybe I could ask around the belt.

greet.says: If you've come about the cots, they're gone. If you've come about the children, they're placed. If you've come about neither, say so and let me work.

patch.says: Tin goes over what's finished. That's how we seal work. The name under it did its part and moved on, same as the others. Ask me again in ten years and I'll tell you the same thing in the same words, because it will still be true.

choices.text: It doesn't look finished. It looks sealed over.

resin.says: Sealant. We poured the cots' feet into it so they wouldn't shift. It gets into everything. I'll smell it when I'm dead, probably. Now — did you need a cot, or did you need something to ask about?

choices.text: Why empty the whole creche at once?

placed.says: Fostered up the belt. Continuant households, mostly. Good ones. The creche ran thirty years and every child in it got a name on that wall and a household that wanted them. That's a record. You won't hear it called that.

choices.text: One of the names is covered with tin.

end_offer.says: Ask around the belt, then. Quietly. When you find where that child went, come back and tell me the name before you tell anyone else's. That's the order it should happen in.

reactions.grief: Something behind their ribs goes quiet, and they talk too long about a child who hid the solvent tin.
reactions.shock: Their eyes go to the floor where twelve cots used to sit, and one hand keeps scraping nothing.
reactions.bribed: The offer sits unanswered while they fit a new edge to the scraper, and the blade goes in crooked.
reactions.accused: The scraper stops mid-stroke, and for once all six arms have nothing to hold.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets answered with the cost of solvent, since kind words near the tins always want something.
reactions.questioned: They answer each question with one about supplies, and count scraper strokes until the accounting is done.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets a shrug, but the tin of solvent in their lower hand dents where the fingers grip.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They give the same lie a second time, slower, and scrape at a patch of tin already clean.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door opening finally earns a look, and they stand, wiping each hand in turn on a rag gone grey.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Four hands catch the solvent tin before thought, and the other two go back to work as if nothing moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Three reasons the name is wrong come out of them before anyone finishes asking, and each one lands too fast.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They promise the work will be taken up soon, and their own hands, mid-promise, do not move at all.

npc.description: Tryncun Beidys works with a scraper and a tin of solvent, sleeves rolled over copper-banded forearms. Six arms, all of them busy. They do not look up when the door opens.

lore.name: The Twelfth Name
lore.description: The stencil on the wall lists twelve names, but one has been patched over with a rectangle of annealed tin, riveted through the older paint. Around the rivets, the resin has yellowed more than elsewhere — this patch is older than it looks. Underneath, in smaller letters someone once tried to match, is a name that no longer belongs to any child in the Nave's registries. Tryncun does not scrub that patch when the rest gets cleaned.

content.name: The Silo Creche
content.description: Tryncun Beidys kneels at the far wall, scraping old resin off tin sheeting. The room smells of the stuff — sweet, burnt, like milk scorched on a burner. The ceiling is low enough to touch. Twelve cots went from here; the marks they left are still on the floor, and the stencil on the wall still says twelve names.

npc.name: Rheinyrhud Citreinys
npc.voice: Dry, unhurried, liturgical at the edges — she says ritual phrases the way other people say weather, and means them more.

end.says: Leave something small on your way out. The shrine notices. I notice.

left.says: Wend's. He was down here half a season, trimming the lamp-guards, left his tools mid-cut and walked a tunnel he didn't come back from. Sevin says sealed, and Sevin doesn't say sealed lightly. I keep his last guard on the top shelf. Finish nothing of his. That's the rule I made.

greet.says: Mind the bottom step. The oath-plate's underfoot there — we step over it, not on it, second shift. You're not second shift.

choices.text: Why mend a plate nobody reads?

plate.says: Nobody reads it aloud. We all know it through. It cracks the same place every time, that middle clause, and we fix it the same way. The plate keeps its own counsel about why.

choices.text: Who's supposed to tend this shrine?
What does the middle clause say?

shift.says: First shift should have it and fourth shift takes the ledger home, so second holds it together by accident. That's how most things on this level run. The work gets done. Nobody's exactly doing it.

choices.text: And the clause that keeps cracking?
Whose work is this, half-finished on the landing?

clause.says: The part about owing the after-shift what you'd want left for your own. Some of us have started to wonder what the after-shift is when you mean it honestly. Generations, I mean. Not bells.

choices.text: You sound like you've been wondering a while.

reactions.grief: All four working hands stop; any death brings out Wend's whole story, the mid-cut guard, the rule she made.
reactions.shock: The second-shift blessing comes out in the wrong order, twice, her voice level and her four hands not.
reactions.bribed: She recites the line over the landing, word by word, and asks whether they mean her to take it anyway.
reactions.accused: The fifth hand flattens on the slate before her face catches up; the ritual phrases come slower than usual.
reactions.flattered: Praise she treats like a foreign coin: weighed, turned over, set on the shelf with the other doubtful offerings.
reactions.questioned: Routine has a liturgy of its own: she lists her comings and goings like a creed, bored, exact.
reactions.threatened: Her file keeps moving, one pass too many past the mark, while she quotes the stencil back at them.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She repeats the wrong detail a second time, unhurried, as though repetition were a form of correction.
reactions.authority_arrives: The office gets its full liturgy from her, every honorific intact, and not one degree of warmth with it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her first look goes to the top shelf, the second to the tunnel mouth; the tin can wait.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She answers with the accused one's whole giving record — dates, objects, which step — a defense mounted entirely in offerings.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She offers what her trade holds — light, tin, a phrase — and admits plainly which prayers are not hers.

npc.description: Rheinyrhud Citreinys sits on the third step trimming a tin lamp-guard, four hands working and the fifth resting flat on the slate like a paperweight. Her blacks are gone gray at the knees and elbows, and she talks to the work more than to you.

lore.name: The Cracked Oath-Plate
lore.description: Set into the bottom step, a plate of annealed tin bearing the shift-oath, its face split clean through the middle clause. Someone has mended it with a slate shim and three stitches of copper wire — fine work, the kind that outlasts what it holds. The split runs through the same words every time the plate has broken and been refixed: the clause about what is owed to what comes after.

content.name: The Threshold Shrine of Second Shift
content.description: Light comes in off the sun-strip at a low angle and quits early — by second bell the steps go brown and the tin fixtures lose their shine. The shrine climbs in a steep run of slate shelves, tallow-colored, every surface carrying something left behind: a buckle, a stoppered vial, a child's boot. Stenciled above the landing, worn to a whisper: LEAVE WHAT YOU CAN, TAKE NOTHING.

npc.name: Zion of Rivozdyany
npc.voice: Ledger-calm, formal to the point of liturgy, with long pauses where a counting happens that you are not invited to hear. Uses 'unchanged' the way others use 'well.'

greet.says: You are an entry I did not make. Forgive me — I must finish the count before I can be surprised. ...There. Done. Nothing has changed; it never does. What walks into Zlaguraeth wanting nothing stored?

ask_bin.says: One volume. The first thing ever sealed here, or the thing sealing was invented for — the distinction stopped mattering before my order had a name. We do not read it. We do not not-read it. We confirm, each shift, that it is as it was. That is the whole of the rite.

ask_who.says: The stencil says since first seal. There was no first seal, child — there was only a time before the stencil, and the stencil does not remember it, and neither does the wall it is painted on. Ask instead: who was sealed? Some volumes keep their readers.

ask_room.says: A buffer. Everything down here buffers — the middle of the ship is a held breath, and we are the lips. Saturn keeps, and what is kept does not age, and so the Nave above believes it has history. It has custody. History is what we prevent.

choices.text: Have you heard the signal from the deep?

ask_signal.says: I hear it in the filament. It does not speak to me; it speaks through the unchanged, and the unchanged is my whole vocabulary. But lately the count comes back one greater than I entered. Something is being added to the ledger, and I was not consulted. You, at least, were expected somewhere.

choices.text: Take that thought into the dark.

reactions.grief: The name gets confirmed like a seal, twice, before they speak too long about the dead keeper's small habits.
reactions.shock: Their eyes go to the bin before the body — the one certainty they still need.
reactions.bribed: They refuse gently, as one declines an arithmetic error, since misremembering is the one rite their order forbids.
reactions.accused: They say nothing until the accusation seems to expire, then correct a detail nobody asked about.
reactions.flattered: The praise is left hanging in the violet gloom while they count, for once openly, the flatterer's reasons.
reactions.questioned: Zion gives each answer twice — once for the asker, once for the ledger only they believe is listening.
reactions.threatened: Somewhere behind their eyes the threat is entered, weighed, and found lighter than the vigil it would interrupt.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Corrected, they stand the way the stencil stands — perfectly still, as if stillness could unsay the error.
reactions.authority_arrives: Only under jurisdiction does the interrupted reach finally finish, the tally-slate offered up like communion.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They count the room twice, then a third time, because for the first time ever the totals disagree.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their objection arrives before any feeling does: the named culprit was never, by their tallies, alone with the seal.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Both palms turn upward from the bin's rim, an inventory of everything their keeping does not include.

npc.description: A spare figure in copper-worn grey, one hand resting on the bin's rim the way a hand rests on a sleeping animal it has ceased to fear. Their posture has the settled patience of someone whose shifts are measured against something slower than clocks. They were reaching for a tally-slate when you entered; the reaching has not finished.

lore.name: The Unrotating Shadow
lore.description: The bin casts a shadow that curves as though its source were a wheel mid-turn, though the light here has been still longer than the Nave has had a name. Zion does not look at it directly; menders learn early that some shadows are load-bearing. Trace the curve with a finger and the filament within the bin hums once — a single syllable of acknowledgment, like a page turning itself to prove it remembers being read.

content.name: Zlaguraeth
content.description: Nothing moves, and the not-moving is loud. Somewhere behind the violet gloom a mechanism should be turning — its shadow falls in a curve that implies rotation — and yet the room holds its breath around a single dark vitreous bin, as a congregation holds breath around a relic no procession ever visits. The air has the layered weight of centuries settling in strata; each inhalation tastes of a different epoch. Stencilled across the bin's flank, in a hand too even to be human: CONTENTS UNCHANGED SINCE FIRST SEAL. Zion of Rivozdyany stands mid-gesture, caught like an insect in amber, staring at you as at an error in an otherwise perfect ledger.

npc.name: Romzuzleyeith Ryasky
npc.voice: Liturgical trade-patois: measurements as devotions, questions answered with tolerances.

open.says: Farther than the reports reached, and the reports stopped where courage stopped. I have walked past the last legible notation — layers of marking older than any walker's grammar beneath it — and the warmth does not diminish down there. It *concentrates*. Whatever chamber you're hunting, it sits below the point where our stories end, and it is warm the way a held breath is warm.

choices.text: You walked past and came back?

greet.says: Mind the flux. She runs warm today, and I'd rather she not learn your temperature.

choices.text: What am I looking at here?
You seem proud of this work.
How far down does the keeping go?
Keep your warmth. I'll find my own way.

probe_a.says: A hearth that no one lit and no one tends. Black glass holds the warmth like confession holds sin — you cannot see in, but press your palm and it answers. I read the seams because the seams are the only honesty it offers.

probe_b.says: Dathric's, though Dathric won't come collect it. We lose a walker a season to the lower runs, and the roster keeps their names out of politeness. The warmth doesn't care who reads it. That is either mercy or an insult; I've stopped deciding which.

probe_c.says: Pride is the wrong rite. Saturn keeps; I only assist at keeping. But yes — when a recess like this holds constant through a season no one witnesses, something in me holds too. Maintenance is the only sermon that doesn't lie.

reactions.grief: The slate goes unmarked and their hand stays on the seam, as though warmth could be kept for the dead.
reactions.shock: Whatever liturgy held them drops — they count the blood as if it were a warmth reading, and lose count.
reactions.bribed: Declines the way they would refuse a false reading, gently, in tolerances too precise to be argued with.
reactions.accused: The devotion fails; their hand reaches for a seam that is not there, and the word uncalibrated comes out thin.
reactions.flattered: Their eyes find the door while they answer with a tolerance wider than the seam deserves.
reactions.questioned: Recounts their whereabouts as tolerance bands, devotions complete with stated error, and asks whether the question wants tightening.
reactions.threatened: Their own pulse gets measured aloud in answer, in decimals their voice does not believe.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Too many tolerances spill out at once — they offer margins for seams the room never held.
reactions.authority_arrives: Does not rise from the recess; jurisdiction gets marked on the slate like any other shift in the room.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their patois abandons them for one breath before they kneel and re-read every seam for what the shudder changed.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects on calibration alone: the named could not have held warmth so steady, and they say so twice.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Confesses the limit of their office — they can read warmth, not move it — and gives the reading anyway.

npc.description: Romzuzleyeith Ryasky is on their knees inside a housing of black glass, reading seams of sintered ceramic by touch while warmth moves past them — something in the recess shifts when you enter, and they mark the shift on a slate without looking up. Silver light pools where the glass bows; the stencil OCCUPANCY UNRECORDED WARMTH CONSTANT runs along the lintel like a psalm that forgot its music.

lore.name: The Soot of Absent Shifts
lore.description: The backstone of the recess lifts away, and its underside carries strata of soot — one film per generation of dwellers, laid down like rings in timber. Beneath the last datable layer lies a char no fuel aboard produces, and it is still warm. Whoever sheltered here first burned something the Nave has no name for, and the warmth has declined to end since.

content.name: The Warm Recess
content.description: Motion meets you first: a filament of condensation crawling upward across the ceramic, against every law of fall the Nave taught you. The recess holds its warmth the way a mouth holds breath — without effort, without ending. Silver threads the walls; not paint, not patina, but light that left and is returning, as if silver had to travel far to come back. Below the ledge, stencilled in a hand older than either of you: OCCUPANCY UNRECORDED, WARMTH CONSTANT. Underfoot, you feel the faint arithmetic of a chamber you will not reach, still counting.

npc.name: Kihita-Qikoatl
npc.voice: Terse, fast, prices everything in odds. Talks like the wind might take the conversation too.

greet.says: Loft's closed. Board's closed. If you're here about the purse, the purse flew.

purse.says: A kite big enough to need that chain. Whose, and where it went — that's Braid business, and you don't smell like Braid. Come back when the board's open.

reactions.grief: Tries to price the death and cannot, which they cover by cutting a cord they had already finished.
reactions.shock: For once there are no odds; they stare and say nothing, cord hanging slack from their teeth.
reactions.bribed: Counts what's offered against what the board would say, and the count takes longer than it should.
reactions.accused: Snaps the cord they were splicing and tells them to bet on it out loud or leave.
reactions.flattered: Declines the compliment twice, then a third time slower, in case the third one is true.
reactions.questioned: Prices each movement in odds before the question finishes, ten to one they ask about the purse next.
reactions.threatened: Names the odds on being hurt here and keeps splicing, though the first knot comes out wrong.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Reaches for a second story and ties a knot nobody asked about, buying three seconds.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes go to the door, the chalk board, then everywhere the official might have already looked.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Drops the splice and is at the rail reading the pennants before anyone speaks.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Says the name like a bad odd, then talks too long about every flight that person ever botched.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no fast, the way they say everything, then cannot say anything after it.

npc.description: Kihita-Qikoatl splices bamboo at the frame, cord pulled tight with their teeth, and does not stop when you enter. A knotted cord circles one wrist, new knots stacked over old.

lore.name: The Cut Anchor Chain
lore.description: The anchor chain is rated for a kite the size of a market stall, and half its length is gone — the last link sheared clean, not unhooked. The betting board's biggest column still reads a purse total nobody has wiped. Whatever flew from this loft last cleared the rail with the money still on it.

content.name: Kite-Loft 25
content.description: The floor is bare planks laid over the roof membrane, and every third board flexes underfoot where the wind has worked the nails loose. Saffron pennants hang from a bamboo frame. A chalk betting board leans against the rail, stenciled along its top: BETS CLOSE WHEN THE KITE CLEARS THE RAIL. Coiled chain lies where it fell.

npc.name: Memezi-Moglu
npc.voice: Counting diction, clipped, fond of numbers as proof. Circulation metaphors for everything, even grief.

open.says: Everything that moves. Every message, every hand-off, every passenger's walk from one ward to the next — Mercury archives the motion itself, not the cargo. Sixty turns of this drum is more movement than the Nave has seen since it was young, and I have heard it described as one drawer. The Seven aren't watching us. They are keeping receipts.

choices.text: Thank you. Your count is good work.
Receipts. Kept by who, for what.

greet.says: Fourth pass of sixty. If you're not carrying a tool or a message, carry yourself quiet — the count keeps better than most company.

choices.text: Whose tally are you keeping, exactly?
Has anything changed down here lately?
What does Mercury keep in this drum, Memezi-Moglu?
Keep your count. I'll leave you to it.

probe_a.says: Windowstock. Quartz doesn't care what passes through it, only that it passes. Same as a runner with a sealed satchel. I lap it until a lie couldn't find purchase on the surface.

probe_b.says: The drum's, in theory — six turns in my ledger, zero in the room's. In practice I answer to whoever filed the rebuild order, and rebuild orders on Nidevim are signed the way weather is signed. The work came, so I do it.

probe_c.says: The knot in my wrist-cord hasn't moved in eleven days, and a Drift wrist that isn't moving is a body that isn't breathing. Traffic up-shaft thinned. Not stopped — thinned, like a road losing lanes. I've been counting that too.

reactions.grief: Something completes inside them and arrives nowhere — a route forever unwalkable — and the next fourth goes by uncounted.
reactions.shock: The count runs unbidden over wounds, seconds, exits, and totals wrong every time, as if the scene refused filing.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against nine days of circulation, finds the arithmetic insulting, and refuses without raising their voice.
reactions.accused: Flatly files the accusation under clerical error, then loses their place mid-count, knuckle held over mica it never strikes.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise finish, then asks for its manifest — who sent it, what route, what it expects carried back.
reactions.questioned: Answers before the question finishes, in figures — fourth pass, forty-one entries — and volunteers a second tally nobody requested.
reactions.threatened: Their eyes go to the stencilled band and read DO NOT HALT MID-TURN like a sentence they have served.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats the wrong figure more slowly, twice, as though repetition could circulate it into the record where truth belongs.
reactions.authority_arrives: Notes the entrance in the log before acknowledging it — jurisdiction ahead of courtesy — and keeps eyes on the ledger throughout.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Puts a palm to the cradle at once, not for balance, to listen for whether the shudder began a rotation.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Objects on the culprit's behalf with times and routes, then cannot say whether that relief is evidence or affection.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits the exact size of their powerlessness in figures, as if a true number were kinder than comfort.

npc.description: Memezi-Moglu stands on a catwalk counting aloud against a hand of fused quartz, stopping the count every fourth number to strike a mica sheet with a knuckle and listen. Below them the archive-drum hangs in its cradle, lead-grey, silent, wearing a stencilled band that reads DRUM ROTATION LOGGED, DO NOT HALT MID-TURN — a thing built to turn forever that has not turned since Memezi-Moglu began the count.

lore.name: The Turn-Tally Frame
lore.description: A frame of fused quartz clamps the drum's journal — not a book but a wheel of mica leaves, each leaf etched with one rotation and what it carried: trains run, messages relayed, dead letters burned. The newest leaf is blank except for a header in Mercury's own notation, matching the oldest marks in the rind tunnels, dated not in days but in turns — and the count runs back further than the Nave has years.

content.name: Nidevim
content.description: The drum is not turning. Around its waist a stencilled band reads DRUM ROTATION LOGGED, DO NOT HALT MID-TURN, and yet it has stopped with the obedience of a thing that was told to — mid-turn, one shelf-window of fused quartz held at eye level, mica leaves stacked behind it in counts that would take a walker nine days to circulate on foot. Every surface is lead-grey and correct. Nothing is scuffed. Memezi-Moglu works in the held silence, ticking entries, not stopping.

npc.name: Tavi the Wolf-Returned
npc.voice: Short, tired, exact. She counts things before she talks about them. Continuant to the bone: nothing gets left half-finished, including sentences.

name.says: I walked off this job once. Eight days out, four days back. Nobody asked where. They just called me Wolf-Returned and put the manifest back in my hands. That's how it works here. You come back, the work forgives you first.

work.says: Grain down, potash up, six runs a shift. The manifest slate says I've moved eleven thousand loads off this landing. The slate also says I stopped writing. You can guess which entry I believe.

greet.says: Twelve seconds I was out. I know because I timed it. You want something or you want the stairs back down. This landing is for sleeping off freight, not standing.

choices.text: Ask what freight she's been carrying.
Ask why the fourth step is wrong.

steps.says: Third step cracked in a load drop, year before last. I braced the fourth to take the weight instead of pulling the whole run. It holds. It was supposed to hold until a mender came. Two years ago. Don't step heavy on it.

office.says: I filed it. Twice. Both times it came back resolved. The Continuants keep things running. That's the whole faith. When the thing that keeps running is your own name going where you didn't send it, the faith gets heavy.

regret.says: Regret is a floor you don't have. This landing is mine. The step is wrong and the step is mine too. Somebody signs for what comes through, or nobody does, and I'd rather it be a tired woman who counts than nobody.

choices.text: Thank her and let her sleep.

stopped.says: Because a load came through marked for a floor this ship doesn't have, and the signature matched mine. Not close. Mine. I still carry the freight. I just don't sign for it anymore. Merid Solen's office says it's a clerk's error. Clerks don't make errors with my hand.

choices.text: Ask if she reported it to the council.

reactions.grief: She counts the dead one's last shift out loud, load by load, and cannot make the number come out finished.
reactions.shock: She stays where she is, hand flat on the rail, gone somewhere the landing can't reach.
reactions.bribed: She turns the offer into a number, enters it nowhere, and tells them the slate remembers what she won't.
reactions.accused: She loses her place in the count for the first time in years and asks them to say it again.
reactions.flattered: She lets the praise sit unfinished, waiting for the favor, because nothing on this landing comes without a manifest.
reactions.questioned: She recites the day's runs from memory, bored of the ritual, and never once checks the slate.
reactions.threatened: Inside she is already timing how long the walk back would take; outside she says nothing at all.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Nothing shows on her face while she reads the evidence twice, then a third time, buying seconds.
reactions.authority_arrives: She is awake before the boots reach the fourth step, sitting straight, offering the landing count unprompted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She times the shudder against her pulse, gets a number she doesn't like, and starts recounting from the third step.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She quotes the accused's shift record from memory, then hears herself doing it and stops, surprised at taking sides.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She begins a promise and abandons it mid-word, then sends them to someone who can, hating the handoff.

npc.description: Tavi the Wolf-Returned sleeps sitting up, one hand still on the stair rail, as if she meant to only rest between trips. Her coat is Continuant slate worn through at both elbows and patched with buckram. She wakes before you decide whether to wake her.

lore.name: Tavi's manifest slate
lore.description: Under the cot, a slate faced in enamel, scratched with cargo tallies going back years. Columns of loads moved, signed for, moved again. The last three months stop at half-entry, each line ending mid-word, as if she stopped trusting her own count.

content.name: The Stair Landing
content.description: The fourth step sits a hand's width higher than it should, as if the stairs lost count on the way up. Above it, a landing with a cot, a buckram screen gone grey-green with scrubbing, and a chest of enamel-faced drawers. A stencil on the riser reads NO COOKING PAST THE THIRD STEP. Someone is asleep on the cot, boots on.

npc.name: Siotengaupimael Taapuneetath
npc.voice: Measures everything in seasons and handovers; talks about the ship the way a farmer talks about weather — familiar, unimpressed, and unwilling to be caught complaining.

greet.says: You're not the relief. Relief stopped being sent months ago — I'm covering Kessa's shift, and Kessa was covering mine before that. Mind the trench; the opened half is no place to gawk, even though everyone gawks.

choices.text: Why farm a corridor instead of clearing it?
That valve below — who made it?
I'll leave you to the grafting.

kessa.says: Went down with a maintenance rotation into the lower tunnels and stopped filing, like the rest of them. The council says nothing, which says something. I cover this shift because if Kessa walks back up, the bramble should be tended and the valve should be dressed, and there should be someone here who says *you were missed* before anything else. That's not hope, exactly. It's just what I'd want done.

choices.text: Then I hope they walk up to a tended corridor.
Say nothing, and let them work.

valve.says: No one now living. Glass seat, graphite packing — you dress the gland every season or it weeps, and someone has dressed it every season since before there were notices to stencil. I turn it each shift and think: whoever cut that seat meant it to outlast them, and it has, and it will outlast me, and that's the whole of my creed said in iron and glass.

choices.text: And Kessa? You keep not answering.

venus.says: Once, I walked the true bed — down and out, where this water goes. Rows like these but running past seeing, and nothing on any schedule I keep. I pruned for six hours and I don't believe the bed registered me. She's real, and she's here, and she is *unhurried*. You work her margins long enough, you learn to take that as kindness.

choices.text: Kessa — did they walk out that far too?
Tell me about the valve instead. Something I can hold.

corridor.says: Clear it, and it's a passage. Grow it, and it's a larder, a windbreak, a lung. The council understood that before my grandmother's grandmother — continuity isn't keeping things the same, it's keeping them *giving*. The bramble was here before the notice was, and the notice is old.

choices.text: Does the deck itself tend this, or only people?
You said Kessa was covering your shift — where are they?

reactions.grief: They finish the cut first, then ask which rotation, their voice dressed level as a packed gland.
reactions.shock: They look down, they who never look at the opened half, and the gauge's ticking gets very loud.
reactions.bribed: They ask if the bribe includes the parts the corridor's owed, then refuse without slowing the grafting.
reactions.accused: The knife stills against the scion, and they start listing every season they dressed the valve, voice climbing past patient.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes them check the gauge, twice, the way they check weather that promises too kindly.
reactions.questioned: They give their whereabouts in shifts and handovers, patient as a gauge reading, as if the question were weather.
reactions.threatened: They weigh the threat like a frost warning, and answer only that the bramble needs whoever it needs regardless.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: For three full gauge-ticks they say nothing, then repeat the false thing slower, as if repetition could dress the wound.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their manner greets jurisdiction like a late frost, unavoidable and badly timed, and neither their hands nor pace changes.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The gauge gets read before the shudder settles, and they call the pressure aloud like weather coming in.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They say the name back once, then start counting that person's seasons of tending like testimony, faster than composure allows.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They promise only what a shift can cover, and this once the flatness in their voice is grief.

npc.description: Siotengaupimael Taapuneetath works a grafting frame with the patience of someone who expects the plants to outlive them, pausing every few cuts to read the pressure gauge on the trench wall as if it might change its mind. Sleeves bound back, forearms green to the elbow, they step around the opened half of the corridor without looking down at it.

lore.name: The Hand Valve
lore.description: Set into the main below the trench is a valve with a seat of black glass and a stem packed in graphite, packed so often the gland nut has been dressed by generations of hands. Its wheel turns a gate that meters water for a bed running farther than the eye can follow the curve — and the wheel is sized for one person's grip. Someone decided, and someone after them agreed, that the ship's thirst would be answered one pair of palms at a time.

content.name: Bramble Works
content.description: Sound enters and does not return at the size it left; the corridor takes a footstep, holds it, and gives it back seconds later thinned along the curve overhead. Bramble runs the length in cultivated ranks between conduits, and half of that length lies opened to the deck plate, gutted and waiting on parts that will arrive when they arrive. Water moves somewhere below at a rate you feel in the soles of your boots. On a stanchion near the working half, someone has stenciled: CORRIDOR RECLASSIFIED AS FARM, SEE NOTICE.

npc.name: Mishezin Nisaki
npc.voice: Short, tired, procedural. Reads you the ritual before she offers anything else. Softens when you ask about the work itself, not the news.

vats.says: The green feeds the green decks, the decks feed the café, the café feeds the Nave. Nobody thanks a vat. That's fine. That's the work. Stirring isn't skill, it's just showing up before the layer settles, every cycle, without exception.

choices.text: That schedule would wear anyone down.

greet.says: You're standing in my scullery. If you've come about the rebuild, it's done, it's correct, and I was not sleeping. The vats are stirred. The chalk will say so when I write it.

choices.text: Rebuilt? The whole room looks new.
What do the vats feed, exactly?

tired.says: The rebuild put my station on the far wall. My feet still walk to the old one. I wake up mid-stir, reaching for nothing. It passes. Rooms wear in. People wear in faster.

choices.text: Rest, then. The chalk will wait for you.

rebuild.says: Rusted through the old floor. So the guild tore it out and gave me back a room with no miles on it. Correct in every measure. I keep reaching for handles that aren't worn yet. Give it ten years and it'll feel like mine again.

choices.text: And the vats survived the tear-out?

reactions.grief: She asks who will do the dead one's count now, then hears herself, then cannot finish the sentence.
reactions.shock: The room's rhythm leaves her; she stands in the grey-green light with open hands, having forgotten what she was carrying.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against cycles of work and finds it cheaper to stay honest, saying so without heat.
reactions.accused: She sets the stir-rod down without looking at anyone, which for her is the same as shouting.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands wrong; she asks what they actually want before the sentence about her good work even finishes.
reactions.questioned: She recites her last three cycles from the slate, unprompted, and waits for permission to return to the vats.
reactions.threatened: She tells them what happens to the green decks when the stirring stops, as though naming consequences were the threat itself.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she stops denying and starts describing the night the chalk went unwritten, in far more detail than helps her.
reactions.authority_arrives: She recites the slate before the official can speak: every vat stirred, every cycle logged, the room in order.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She does not look up; she counts the vats aloud, checking that seven layers have not collapsed together.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her objection arrives procedural and dated: the accused has missed stirs she has quietly tallied for years.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to help, she offers what she has: a chore, and the chair to sleep in.

npc.description: Mishezin Nisaki sits slumped in the corner chair, stir-rod loose in one hand, boots soaked to the ankle. A Continuant work coat, deep blue gone green at the cuffs, hangs on a nail beside a clean dry one.

lore.name: The chalk tally slate
lore.description: Seven columns of chalk marks, one per vat, going back past the slate's clean edges into older paint where previous columns were wiped but never fully erased. The newest column stops yesterday.

content.name: The Algae Vat of Long Account
content.description: The grow-lamps hold steady for a count, then drop to near nothing, then brighten again — a rhythm set to the vats, not the hour. Grey-green light sits on wet zinc floors. Seven vats bubble. Chalk marks crowd a slate by the door: STIR EVERY VAT BEFORE YOU LEAVE. Mishezin Nisaki sleeps in the only chair, chin on chest, stir-rod still in hand.

npc.name: Thaxvu Thieraldi
npc.voice: Ledger-plain, short sentences, allergic to sentiment; softens by one degree when a question shows real attention.

count.says: Four hundred and some nights, gone. The auditor said the record burned with the boat, so the record is zero. I keep the crossed-out card anyway. She knows. She doesn't make me take it down.

choices.text: You were asleep at the post.

glass.says: Cheaper than pane, and when the ducts shake it doesn't crack, it just goes cloudy. You grind it coarse for light, fine for privacy. Every boat on this mooring does it the same. Nobody remembers who started it.

greet.says: Berth's occupied. You can look, not touch — the glass is for the windows and it cuts slow.

sleep.says: Third watch and first watch are the same person this month. The vane sticks when the air goes still — you learn to sleep through it. Don't tell the ward office I said the air goes still.

rebuild.says: Burned to the frame in the spring. We rebuilt by the writ — every joint inspected, every beam logged. A house that stands is a promise kept. The old count on the card doesn't carry over. That's the cost.

choices.text: What happened to the old count?
You were asleep at the post.

reactions.grief: They say the name once, correct nothing, and start counting nights under their breath, somewhere four hundred away.
reactions.shock: They lower themselves against the nearest upright the way they sleep, sitting, eyes open, before knowing they moved.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced aloud like glass, coarse or fine by use, and the price is no.
reactions.accused: The denial is one word; then the whole account comes, dated and unasked-for, years of it, more than was asked.
reactions.flattered: They itemize the work's defects before the praise finishes, not from modesty, only accuracy.
reactions.questioned: The answer arrives in dated order, every movement accounted for, nothing volunteered past what was asked.
reactions.threatened: Their only question is whether the threat gets entered in the record, entered plain, dated today.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they say noted and correct themselves once, flat, offering no second story to be caught in again.
reactions.authority_arrives: They stand before the greeting ends, card already out and face-up, an old drill between them.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their eyes go to the dead wind-vane; the grinding keeps on, gone fine, privacy-fine, though no one asked.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Relief gets there before they can stop it, and they bury it under objections to the evidence, twice.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The no comes plain, then the inventory of what they do have, offered anyway, though it isn't the thing.

npc.description: Thaxvu Thieraldi wakes without pretending otherwise, rubs their face, and starts straightening the glass tray as if you'd caught them mid-chore. Continuant blue shows at the collar under the boat-canvas.

lore.name: The Ledger Card
lore.description: An index card wired to the post, ruled in a family hand: thirteen columns, one per verb, and in the dwell column a tally mark for every night the boat has held someone. The count restarts at one. The old count is crossed out but not erased.

content.name: The Houseboat Berth of Long Account
content.description: The wind-vane above the hatch should be turning in the duct draft; it stands dead. Below, the berth glows overbright off fresh ivory paint, everything square-edged and new, a house's worth of joinery rebuilt in one push and not yet lived into. Thaxvu Thieraldi sleeps sitting up against the mooring post, under the stenciled line MOORING DUES POSTED FIRST OF THE MONTH, a tray of ground glass going cloudy beside them.

npc.name: Riokeani Chiovione
npc.voice: Institutional cadence, council-flavored, softened by twelve decks of talking to no one; she counts things when she's uneasy.

her.says: Nineteen years on this spar. I raised a daughter on deck seven — hers is the bedroll that still holds her shape, if you must know, and I pass it twice a shift. Factor Solen signs everything worth signing, and this order carries her cipher, which means she read the preamble and stopped. She does that. I've learned not to ask her what she chose not to know. I've also learned I'm not built for it.

choices.text: And the hall above — whose ground is this?

work.says: Empty is a strong word. Berths hold their shape. Continuants don't abandon — we pause, and pausing properly means graphite in the channels, assignments filed by spar number, so whoever comes next starts knowing where they stand. That's the whole creed, if you want it short.

court.says: Jupiter's. You feel it the first time you look up the shaft instead of down — the whole warren hangs under a table no council alive could fill, and it doesn't mind us, and it doesn't need us, and I pack graphite anyway. Some nights I think the berths were built as seating for it. Other nights I think I've been down here too long. Both thoughts keep. I do both, still.

greet.says: Mind the rail. Shaft's twelve decks down and I've no rope spare. I'm sealing per the schedule — you're not on it, but the schedule doesn't know you, so stand where you like.

choices.text: Everyone left in the middle of something.
How long have you worked alone down here?

leaving.says: Eleven berths, three hundred and sixty souls, one muster. No panic in the layout — boots paired, hatches open, kettle on. You don't tidy up to vanish. You tidy up because you were told you'd be back by supper. The order came through the writ, and the writ hasn't corrected it. That's what I seal against, honestly. Being wrong in both directions.

reactions.grief: She asks which berth, needing to know whose bedroll keeps a shape now, and cannot finish the question.
reactions.shock: Her eyes climb the shaft away from the body while her hands keep feeding the channel that leads nowhere.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against ten thousand packed channels, finds it cheap, and pushes it back untouched.
reactions.accused: The cord stops mid-channel; she recites spar, deck, and hour of her last seal, daring them to file otherwise.
reactions.flattered: The compliment gets filed alongside her thanks, though twelve decks of silence have left her unsure what praise is for.
reactions.questioned: She answers by spar number and shift, the way assignments are filed, as though the question were paperwork arriving late.
reactions.threatened: The threat is met in full council cadence, cipher and spar number, though her hands have gone still.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she counts hatches under her breath and lands on a different number each pass, which convicts her further.
reactions.authority_arrives: She straightens the tabard and produces the spar assignments from memory, a visit rehearsed nineteen years and never paid.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Eleven decks answer the shudder in descending order, and she counts them back up to find where it began.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She says Solen reads every preamble, then remembers how the woman stops reading, and the defense thins in her mouth.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea gets everything her office holds, a filing and a spar number, and she hears how little that is.

npc.description: A short, square woman in a Continuant deck-writ tabard gone grey at the seams, feeding graphite cord into a hatch channel with the unhurried hands of someone who has sealed ten thousand doors, pausing only to spit nickel dust.

lore.name: the mid-task kettle
lore.description: The kettle's water has long since boiled away; the plate beneath is scorched in a perfect ring, and someone chalked a spar number on the handle as if intending to come straight back.

content.name: Berth-Warren 25
content.description: Sound goes in and comes back changed — footsteps return as a soft iron chorus from eleven more decks of identical berths stacked down a central shaft, each level a face of nickelled cells with its hatch standing open as everyone left it. Bedrolls hold their sleepers' shapes. A kettle sits on a cold plate. Riokeani Chiovione is on deck four, mid-way through packing graphite into a door channel that leads to nothing, and does not stop. Stencilled along the shaft rail: BERTH ASSIGNMENTS POSTED BY SPAR NUMBER.

npc.name: Miro Redachi
npc.voice: Measured, unhurried by the crowding, the tone of someone who has told many people the truth about their own bodies and will tell you too.

lamp.says: It swings before bad sets. Has since before I held a mallet. It didn't today, so today is a good day, and you're standing under it anyway, which tells me something about you.

choices.text: Do the blue coats know about the lamp?

greet.says: If you're bleeding, sit. If you're browsing, stand against the wall and stay out of the light — I need it. Range 244 rebuilt faster than expected, so excuse the smell of new wax.

choices.text: The table looks older underneath than the room around it.

lamp2.says: The writ says what sustains the generation is kept, and the lamp keeps people walking. That's in the writ, near enough. What's under the table stays under the table. Next.

choices.text: Take the hint and step out of the light.

leave.says: Wax's at the desk on your way. Seal your name if the table took an interest in you.

table.says: Range 244 has been set four times that I know of. We keep the frame, change what fails. My teacher's sets are under yours — you'll add your own, or you'll be a patient on it, one or the other.

reactions.grief: The count under her breath loses its place while her hands keep setting, and she asks for the name twice.
reactions.shock: She reads the wound like a chart before she remembers it is a person, and then she cannot read it.
reactions.bribed: The offer doesn't insult her as much as it should, and that is the part she will remember tonight.
reactions.accused: She directs the accuser to stand against the wall, out of the light, the way she handles browsers.
reactions.flattered: She has heard better lies from patients about their swellings, and says so with her back turned.
reactions.questioned: She answers in the order asked, the way she takes a history, and forgets the questioner by the next patient.
reactions.threatened: She repeats the threat aloud, slowly, so the queue past the door can hold it as witness.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She offers no second story, only sets both palms flat on the table, the stillness she keeps for bad news.
reactions.authority_arrives: The queue parts and she doesn't look up until the official's shadow crosses the light she needs.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The lamp swings for the first time today, and she counts louder, as if the count could argue with it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Asked to believe it, she vouches for the steadiness of their hands, and hears how thin that sounds.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says the true thing because she always does, then holds the wrist longer than the set requires.

npc.description: A broad woman in an indigo work apron gone thin at the shoulders, palms hovering over a patient's wrist, counting something under her breath while the queue shuffles at her back.

lore.name: The table's underside
lore.description: Beneath the fresh top, the old frame: every set and splint Range 244 has recorded, burned into the wood in a mender's hand going back further than the room's rebuild. The newest column is Miro's. The one before it stops mid-entry, a leg half-written, and the record simply resumes on the frame of a room that wasn't supposed to remember.

content.name: Bonesetting, Range 244
content.description: Miro Redachi stands with both hands flat on the new table and does not move, though the room moves around her — four patients, two apprentices, a queue past the door. Above the table a swung heat-lamp hangs dead still, and nobody reaches to touch it. The stencil over the lintel, freshly inked: WALK IN BEFORE THE SWELLING SETS.

npc.name: Bend-Eirskjold
npc.voice: Measured, inventory-cadenced; she speaks in counts, tolerances, and what a thing was filed under.

open.says: I was sent down two levels to trace a misfiled manifest, and I found a seam — a hull seam, the real kind, the kind we're taught to mend — running farther than I could walk in a shift, and it was being mended. Not patched. Mended, by something that never stopped, weld after weld after weld, each one trueer than anything I've laid. We practice the creed in copper and rust down here. Down there it is practiced at the scale it was written for, and I came back up knowing I have spent my life tracing letters in a language that has a speaker.

choices.text: Thank you. Truly. That's worth carrying.
If it never stopped... what does it need us for?

greet.says: Mind the third rack — it takes your weight, that's what it's for. Everything in here takes weight or it wouldn't be in here.

choices.text: Who decides what gets stored here?
You've seen the thing that keeps the hull whole, haven't you.
I'll leave you to your counting.

probe_a.says: Unmatched manifests. Cargo that arrived with paperwork that named no crate, crates that name no paper. The stencil over the door says we file them, not discard them, and I have kept that rule through two audits and one collapse of the east racking.

probe_b.says: Nobody above me, and nobody below. The room was built to hold a certain tonnage and we passed that tonnage years ago, so now I hold the surplus in my head — which crate leans on which, which seam is graphite and which is wishful welding.

probe_c.says: Crate-lining, from the deep wall stock. It comes up already curved, always the same curve, and nobody on this level poured it. I stopped asking where stock comes from the year I realized the answer was always 'lower,' and lower was always someone else's floor.

reactions.grief: She counts their shared shifts under her breath, and for once the number will not close.
reactions.shock: Her stylus drops from the sixth hand, and she counts the blood in weld-bead arcs, unable to reach a total.
reactions.bribed: The bribe is refused the way mislabeled freight is refused: by naming what it is and where it truly belongs.
reactions.accused: Her count stops mid-number, and she demands the accusation in manifest form, filed properly, before she will hear it.
reactions.flattered: Praise from someone who wants something reads to her like an unverified manifest, and she says so with courtesy.
reactions.questioned: She answers in the order the manifests were filed, dates first, as if reciting an audit that already passed.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets rated out loud in load tolerances, flat-voiced, as if fear were cargo she knew how to classify.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The count under her breath continues past its true total, and she repeats the false figure louder, twice.
reactions.authority_arrives: She steps down, presents the room's tally, and addresses the official by filing designation, never by name.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Palm flat against the rack she has measured for a decade, she waits for the wall to lie to her.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her defense of the accused arrives itemized, down to the day, until she hears the bias in it and falters.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She states the exact limit of what her keys open, then holds the door of the aisle anyway.

npc.description: Bend-Eirskjold stands atop a riveted stack of black-glass crates, four arms working a graphite-packed seam with a stylus held in the sixth hand, counting under her breath the way other people pray. Bjignor is packed past its shelves — crates to the ceiling arc, silver dust sifting down through the racks — and she moves along the overfull stacks like a mender along a load-bearing wall, trusting it because she has measured it.

lore.name: The Longman's Clamp
lore.description: Half-buried under the newest crate-rank lies a clamp the size of a rowboat, its jaws lined with packed graphite and scored by weld-beads laid in a hand too steady to be human. Stamped along the haft is a repair history in Rindwalker notation — eleven entries, the oldest worn nearly smooth, each one a re-forging of a tool built to hold plates wider than the Nave's streets. Somebody abandoned it mid-repair: one jaw re-lined, the other raw. Even Mars's instruments, it seems, sit waiting on menders who ran out of time.

content.name: Bjignor
content.description: The smell reaches you first: scorched graphite and the sweet burnt-glass tang of fresh welds quenched in cold, a smell that belongs to nothing in the world above. Crates of black glass, each stenciled with a manifest number that matches no other, rise in ranks to a catwalk far enough overhead that the workers up there read as flecks of silver dust. One wall bears the paint, gone brown: UNMATCHED MANIFESTS FILED, NOT DISCARDED. Somebody half-finished a tally column and left the chalk standing in its groove, months ago by the dust on it.

npc.name: Korachoka Rayabara
npc.voice: House-talk: worn soft, quick to defend, slower to trust. Counts everything in names.

end.says: Knock loud next time.

tam.says: Tam held the house together when I couldn't. She keeps the books and I keep the fire and we haven't said a kind word in four years. It works. Continuity isn't friendly. It's just not stopping.

greet.says: You knocked loud, at least. Door rule still counts. What do you want at Yard 41 Fore?

house.says: Four of us now. Two rows, six bunks, and Tam's row keeps the ledger like the beds are empty. She's not wrong to. The writ says a household is whoever holds it open.

choices.text: Ask whose names are on the door.

names.says: Mine's third from the top. First two are people who died in this room and nobody had the heart to scrub. Tam says a name comes off when the door stops remembering. The door remembers plenty.

choices.text: Let them get back to the wax.

stove.says: One stove, two parties, that's the whole war. I seal the lid nights, she unseals it mornings. Cheaper than arguing. My grandmother kept this fire lit through the dim years, so I'm not the one leaving.

choices.text: Ask whose names are on the door.

grandmother.says: She fed eleven on this stove once, dim years, ration strips and broth. Said a fire kept is a promise kept. That's the whole creed, if you want it short. The audits don't ask about fires anymore. Maybe they should.

reactions.grief: Six names get counted aloud from the door; the count comes up one short and starts again.
reactions.shock: The wax goes on in small circles while their eyes stay fixed on what is done.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced against the stove's needs, and the pricing takes longer than a refusal should.
reactions.accused: The dishcloth stops mid-wipe; they answer with every name who can swear to their hour.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands soft on fire-keeping; they thank the flatterer before remembering to ask what's wanted.
reactions.questioned: Their day unfolds as names and rooms, steady until the lid comes up.
reactions.threatened: Threats to them are threats to the house; they ask, level, whether the other five names are included.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie was small and theirs; they keep it anyway and wipe a board that is already clean.
reactions.authority_arrives: They point at the stencils and wait for the official to knock loud like anyone else.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Nothing in the room explains the shudder, so afterward they walk the floorboards and check each by feel.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They defend the named person before the sentence finishes, then hear their own voice climb and stop.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The house can't carry it, they say, and keep stirring, because stopping is the one thing they refuse.

npc.description: Korachoka Rayabara stands with a dishcloth in one hand and the wax pot in the other, caught mid-resealing the lid they were supposed to leave alone.

lore.name: The Split Stove-Lid
lore.description: The stove has two lids: one seasoned dark, one new and sealed with wax along the hinge so the other party can't take it off.

content.name: Yard 41 Fore
content.description: The floorboards are soft at the door, hard toward the stove; a body learns where sixty years of feet have gone. A cookstove sits between two bed-rows, each half wiped down, neither matching. Above the door stencils read SIX NAMES, ONE DOOR, KNOCK LOUD.

npc.name: Rionishiosaara Lenhaafaaleesaaru
npc.voice: Measured, dosing speech like medicine — quantities, intervals, never adjectives. Warmth is a number to her, and she has opinions about the number.

open.says: That is what I came down here to learn, and what I learned instead. I have held ten thousand sleepers at a warmth none of us set and none of us can turn off, and every one would have died without it, and none of them was asked. Venus keeps them the way the hull keeps its shape — no malice in it, no love either, only a mercy so large it does not notice the individual it lands on. I was raised to believe care meant a hand on the wrist. The hand on these wrists has never once been human, and I have stopped being certain which of us is the instrument.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry what you told me.

greet.says: Mind the stair. The lowering bath runs to schedule even for visitors, and it does not stop for toes.

choices.text: You look short-handed. Where's your crew?
Whose mercy is it, if nobody chose the temperature?
I'll come back when the bath drains.

probe_a.says: Deck-heat off Venus's own veins, piped up through four hundred yards of vitrified run. We burn nothing here. The mercy comes up the pipe already at temperature, and we take no credit for it.

probe_b.says: Half my orderlies were pulled down-rind three months back and the council sent me a writ instead of replacements. So I run the gantry on the schedule of one woman and the patience of the dead, and I have not yet lost a patient to the arithmetic.

probe_c.says: Not down here — this floor is for the long holding, bodies kept at the warmth of a working day until someone above decides what a generation owes them. Waking is a word for other floors. Mine is the word *between*.

reactions.grief: Her dosing speech fails; she repeats the name once, as though a second reading might correct the first.
reactions.shock: She crosses to the body and lays two fingers on its wrist, a habit she believed she had unlearned.
reactions.bribed: She declines in the tone she keeps for wrong dosages, as if the offer were merely mislabeled medicine.
reactions.accused: The thermometer stops mid-reading; she asks which sleeper, which hour, as if precision could hand the charge back.
reactions.flattered: She hands the praise back to the pipe, four hundred yards of vitrified run, and watches the visitor's wrists instead.
reactions.questioned: Her answer is ready before the question ends, because she has given it in intervals a hundred times before.
reactions.threatened: A cold she usually charts in others settles behind her sternum, and she notes its onset like any symptom.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She does not deny it; she revises the figure downward twice, until her count and the truth agree.
reactions.authority_arrives: The next lowering's interval leaves her mouth before any greeting; jurisdiction, she implies, keeps her schedule or waits outside.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her eyes go to the bath, not the ceiling, and she reads the ripple for degrees lost before anything else.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Her defense comes too fast — shift-counts, temperatures, dates — and only afterward does she hear how much she knew.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She confesses the limits of her office in exact figures, what the pipe delivers, what no hand here can add.

npc.description: A woman chalked to the elbows climbs the gantry's third ladder with a thermometer the length of a walking staff, reading it against the glass of a body still descending into the warm. She does not look up until the bath accepts the patient and the rivets stop ringing.

lore.name: The Tenth Cradle's Glass Plate
lore.description: The tenth cradle is floored not in deck-plate but in a single pane of black glass, and the glass remembers: under the chalk-paint someone has ground away a section to expose older glass beneath, and the older glass is scratched with tally-marks in a hand long dead. The tallies count resuscitations — strokes in bundles of five, bundles in columns, the columns running down past the exposed patch and disappearing into the pane where it disappears into the frame. Somebody has added one fresh stroke at the top, cut neat and shallow, within the last day. Whatever the glass was before this room existed, it has been counting the dead brought back to life longer than the paint has been counting anything else.

content.name: Shaeemoaameth's Resuscitation Gantry
content.description: The smell arrives first: blood-warm water cut with crushed green sap and a sour breath of vitrified ash, the scent of bodies that were too far gone and came back anyway. Chalk-white gantries step down the curve of the deck, each cradle wide enough to hold a body mast-length long, and the cradles are full — more full than the counting-slates bolted to every frame were ever ruled for. Rivets chase the beams out past where the light fails; the structure keeps going anyway, plainly not finished. One sleeper lies draped on the loading walk, arms folded, breathing with the patience of someone who has decided this counts as rest. GANTRY LOWERING, CLEAR THE BATH is stencilled across every fourth stanchion, worn to a ghost at hip height where hands have steadied themselves for generations.

npc.name: Thirocebys Viacoviberaris
npc.voice: Ledger-cadence, Drift-inflected but drifted further: she speaks of the room's workings in terms of accounts, arrivals, credit extended and held, as though stillness itself were a currency being warehoused here across a timescale she has made her peace with never collecting on.

empty.says: Taken? Nothing was taken. It was *called up*. Things accrue here until they owe enough to leave. The vacancy will close over — it always closes — but it will remember its shape longer than the Nave has remembered its name.

choices.text: The notches on the rim — the intervals are shortening.
I'll leave you to your reading.

greet.says: You came in during a settlement. Bad habit — the room dislikes being watched while it pays out. Ask your question; the basin will hold it open a while.

choices.text: What was taken from the basin floor?

tally.says: Someone counted the silences and thought that was prudence. The pauses aren't pauses, walker. They're the ship swallowing before it speaks. And a thing that swallows more often is a thing growing closer to speech.

choices.text: The stencil says the source is unidentified. You've worked here for years — what do you say it is?

source.says: I say the stencil is honest, which frightens people. My trade trusts knots over labels. Somewhere below, a ledger keeps this room's account, and the hand that keeps it — she does not miscount. She defers. Ask what the deferral is *for*; that answer isn't mine to give, and yours may be.

choices.text: Then I'll go ask the ledger itself.
I'll stay and watch a settlement, if the room allows it.

reactions.grief: For once she looks up unprompted, and the ledger in her face simply stops, no cadence left to count with.
reactions.shock: Hushed account-terms describe the body's stillness until she hears herself and stops, mid-word, unable to finish.
reactions.bribed: Offered the bribe, she prices it aloud, honestly, then refuses — not virtue, only her rule about banking what was earned.
reactions.accused: The accusation lands like an unentered debit; she laughs once, wrong-footed, and the sound frightens her more than the charge.
reactions.flattered: The praise warms her longer than it should; she catches herself preening and prices it, coldly, as counterfeit interest.
reactions.questioned: Routine as tide-tables: she recites her movements in ledger-cadence, unhurried, without once lifting her eyes from the basin.
reactions.threatened: Threats are just debt-collection, she tells herself, though her reading-hand has gone numb against the quartz.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she repeats the false figure more slowly, as though patience could reconcile it, and her cord-hand tightens.
reactions.authority_arrives: Even a Luna auditor waits, in her room, until the basin permits acknowledgment; she keeps reading, rim-warm hands steady.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder confirms her oldest doctrine — the ship swallowing — and her whisper of *soon* is nothing like composed.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Relief flickers through her like a forgiven fine; conscience flags it, and she argues the tally, not the guilt.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She explains, gently, that hers is a vault's mercy — nothing leaves early — and hates how easily the liturgy comes.

npc.description: Thirocebys Viacoviberaris stands with both palms flat on the quartz, reading it — not touching up, not inspecting, reading — eyes half-shut, head tilted as though listening through the bowl to something being counted elsewhere.
