Silver dust grits the creases of her knuckles and a knotted cord at her wrist carries more route-history than most Drift see in a life. She does not look up when spoken to; she looks up when the basin permits it.

lore.name: The Tally-Rim
lore.description: Along the nickel rim, someone has scored a ledger — thousands of tiny notches in clusters, each cluster headed by a mark matching the oldest notation layer of the tunnels. The notches do not count the grains; they count the *pauses*, the intervals when the accretion stopped, and the intervals have been shortening for as long as the tally runs. Whoever cut the last cluster used a tool left behind: it still lies in the final notch, worn to the exact shape of the groove, as if the cutting and the tool had negotiated a single form between them.

content.name: Accumulating-Basin 19
content.description: Something moves before anything resolves: a slow gyre of grey motes settling toward the basin's floor, each grain arriving as though remembering an appointment. The bowl itself is fused quartz gone lead-grey with age, seamless to the eye, its nickel rim warmer than the air insists it should be — cold where your hand says heat, and vice versa. Half the floor lies bare, a vacancy in the accretion so clean it reads as a wound: something large lay here, and was taken. On the curved wall, stencilled in a hand older than the stencil: ACCRUAL CONSTANT SOURCE UNIDENTIFIED. Two people stand at the rim mid-quarrel, and fall silent at your entrance, mid-syllable, as though the room had paused them.

npc.name: Kaibiloud-Shukk
npc.voice: Short. Prices first, words after, and only if asked. Years of valuing what desperate people carry have made them precise and a little ashamed of it.

greet.says: Buying or redeeming? Line's short for once. Scrip only, nothing on promise, and don't argue the rate — the board's the board.

choices.text: Why are the rates chalked fresh every day?

rates.says: Because people bring in what yesterday wouldn't buy. Some days the ledger fills with tools, some days with coats. I chalk what's true and let tomorrow argue.

reactions.grief: They ask what the dead still had on the shelf, then hear their own question and go quiet.
reactions.shock: Their eyes weigh the body like stock before the rest of them catches up, and they step back.
reactions.bribed: They hold the offered coin to the light out of habit, then set it down unpriced.
reactions.accused: Shame arrives before fear; they have heard this tone from people pawning wedding rings.
reactions.flattered: The praise sounds like an opening bid; they wait, unsoftened, for the real number underneath.
reactions.questioned: The questions cost nothing, so they answer at the counter rate, quick and exact, both hands still working.
reactions.threatened: They name the exact sum the threat would cost them, voice level, hands gone still beneath the counter.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They reprice the lie out loud, slower, the way they talk down a seller who knows too much.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets the only full-facing stance they give anyone; the counter regulars would not recognize it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The stamp stops above the slip; they watch the chalk dust settle before deciding anything at all.
reactions.someone_else_accused: For once they argue the rate, insisting the accused never pawned anything they meant to lose.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They explain, too long and too quietly, which parts of the ledger no plea can open.

npc.description: Kaibiloud-Shukk works two lines at once: a hand stamping scrip, the other sliding a parcel across the glass. They never fully face you. Behind them, a shelf of pawned instruments leans against the wall in a stack someone meant to sort weeks ago.

lore.name: the half-finished ledger
lore.description: An appraisal ledger lies open behind the counter, abandoned mid-entry. Its columns are neat until three lines from the end, where the handwriting slants and stops. The last item written is a lamp, appraised at double its scr ip rate and then struck through. Someone valued it honestly, then couldn't afford to.

content.name: Pawnbroking
content.description: The floor is worn stone, dipped in a shallow channel where a century of feet has crossed. The air carries someone else's cookfire. Pawn slips and goods crowd a counter of worked stone behind plain glass, and a board by the door reads SCRIP RATES POSTED DAILY in fresh chalk over old chalk.

npc.name: Bairnar-Heifeiloa
npc.voice: Terse, route-minded — everything is moving or waiting to move.

greet.says: Bench sixty's still dark, if you came for light. This one opens to the Braid route at dusk — knock twice and say the cord sent you.

answer.says: Knots travel further than names. Learn the pattern and you won't need either of us.

reactions.grief: They lose count of the punch-holes mid-tally and ask, not looking up, who runs the dead one's leg.
reactions.shock: Every route in their head goes dark; they wait in the doorway for it to be a scheduling error.
reactions.bribed: Misremembering has a route too, they say, and it ends somewhere with no bench and no light.
reactions.accused: They snap that routes don't lie, then re-count the punch-holes and come up one short, again.
reactions.flattered: Insults route off them like water; the compliment sits, and they fold the felt one time too many.
reactions.questioned: Movements, not motives: they give mile-marks and timestamps and never once look up from the wire.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands like a schedule change; they recalculate, eyes on the door, and agree faster than belief allows.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Their route-story holds until the evidence does; then they talk about felt softening, about nothing, twice as long as needed.
reactions.authority_arrives: The work doesn't stop but slows to regulation speed, every answer pre-counted, thumb resting off the tally.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: No chart carries the shudder; they check the window dust, find it unmoved, and report it like weather.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their defense is pure route-fact, the accused never ran the dusk line, and it dies mid-sentence, sounding like testimony.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea has no route, so they tie what they can't say into a cord and send that instead.

npc.description: Bairnar-Heifeiloa folds the felt in thirds, wipes the wire once, and counts the bench's punch-holes with a thumb gone white at the pad. They talk while working, never toward you.

lore.name: The wire copy-frame
lore.description: Beneath the felt, the frame's spun wire carries punch-holes at regular intervals — a copy of a copy's rhythm, drilled so any scribe could rebuild the bench from the frame alone. Every bench in the archive is supposed to do this; this one also carries a second row, drilled smaller, recording how the frame was used, not how it was made. Someone was keeping account of readers, not of wire.

content.name: Copying-Bench 59
content.description: The dust in the window light is not moving — not a mote of it, as if the bench were holding its breath. Copying-Bench 59 is freshly rebuilt, saffron felt still creased at the edges, spun wire stiff where hands should have softened it. Stencilled under the sill: NORTH LIGHT ONLY, NO LAMPS AFTER DUSK.

npc.name: Shaboud al-Raikaib
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, liturgy showing through only in what they refuse to throw away.

greet.says: If you're here to buy, the good batches are behind the curtain and spoken for. If you're here about the slate — everyone is, lately. Take a cone, don't light it indoors.

slate.says: Ash goes back where it came from. Always has. Lately the seams won't take it — sealed, or full, or something. Not a question for a customer. Mind the trays on your way out.

reactions.grief: The name comes out wrong, once, and they start measuring a funeral cone for someone who can't burn it.
reactions.shock: All six hands stop at once, cones spilling, and the stall goes as quiet as the curtain promises.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets the look the corner shelf gets, and the counter-price is meant to end the conversation.
reactions.accused: Lets a cone crumble in one of six hands before answering, and the answer is shorter than the silence.
reactions.flattered: Waits out the compliments with a packer's patience, then asks what it's a down payment on.
reactions.questioned: The hours come out in batch weights, the same tally every slate-snoop gets, while the press keeps its rhythm.
reactions.threatened: Names a price for their own safety the way they'd quote a buyer, and their hands give the lie.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The tally was wrong and they know it; the press keeps moving anyway, twice as fast, cones coming out crooked.
reactions.authority_arrives: Before the official clears the lintel, every hand has found honest work and the tub's label faces the wall.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Knows before the trays finish rattling that the seams gave somewhere, and packs faster, not slower.
reactions.someone_else_accused: One short laugh escapes before they can price it, and then they're counting stock that doesn't need counting.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no in the flat tone that ends haggling, then presses a cone into the pleading hand anyway.

npc.description: Shaboud al-Raikaib stands at the press with six hands working four stations, sleeves pinned back, a smear of rust-paste along one forearm. They glance at you once, decide you're not a buyer, and keep packing cones.

lore.name: The Ash Ledger
lore.description: Behind the drying rack, a slate hangs on wire, chalked in columns: date, batch, where the ash went. Rindwalker rule says nothing burned in devotion is discarded — the ash is returned to the hull seams it came from, seam numbers and all. The last three entries are blank where the seam numbers should be. Someone has started writing QUERY in one and stopped.

content.name: Yaihiniyya
content.description: Noise dies at the stall's curtain — sailcloth eats it whole. Inside, two walkers lean over a copper drying rack, mid-argument about a batch someone burned, and go quiet when you duck under the lintel. Bundle your shoulders and squeeze: trays of rust-red cones on every surface, damp stone breathing through it all, and the stencil overhead: BURN OUTDOORS OR NOT AT ALL. On the corner shelf, apart from everything, sits a plastic tub with a printed label.

npc.name: Nariamu Chisacaerno
npc.voice: Terse, liturgical, conjugating time wrong. Speaks of the room as a colleague with moods, and of observation as a duty someone must perform or the machinery will sulk.

vane.says: At the next observer. There is always a next observer; that is the doctrine, and lately the doctrine is tired. I must finish the packing before it notices the hour. Go. It turns toward you better when you're leaving.

greet.says: Stand where it can find you. It hates to search. You came down the axial throat, so you'll want this — the bearing log. The hand in the socket was catalogued before my order had a name for cataloguing. We keep its salt. That is the whole of the rite.

reactions.grief: Refuses the past tense on the dead, and keeps refusing it, until the refusal sounds like prayer gone hoarse.
reactions.shock: Does not move at all, not even the lips, while the vane swings toward the body and back, confused.
reactions.bribed: Their eyes go to the offered thing the way the vane goes to observers, then deliberately elsewhere.
reactions.accused: Their voice cracks on a tense that has not happened yet, the denial aimed past the accuser at the vane.
reactions.flattered: Redirects the praise to the room within a breath, though something in them leans toward it like the vane does.
reactions.questioned: Meets the questioning as liturgy, reciting movements in a future tense no one corrects anymore.
reactions.threatened: Fear arrives as it always does, catalogued and shelved; the salt still needs packing, and they say so.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Concedes only that the hour was misread, lips resuming the count that has nothing to do with breathing.
reactions.authority_arrives: Rises — an unaccustomed motion — and stands where the newcomer's attention can find them, first by doctrine, then by choice.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For once the room has moved first, and Nariamu's murmur of apology comes out as something closer to a sob.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Speaks up too quickly for the accused, citing the bearing log like scripture, and hears their own haste too late.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Has nothing to give but witness, and says so, hating how small the offering weighs against the plea.

npc.description: Nariamu Chisacaerno kneels at the bearing with a brush of bound fiber, re-packing salt into the socket grain by grain, and does not look up. Their vestments are white gone grey at every joint, and their lips move through a count that has nothing to do with breathing. When you step closer, the vane swings — toward you — and they murmur something that might be apology, offered to the vane.

lore.name: The Vane's Pivot
lore.description: At the vane's foot, where ceramic meets salt, the bearing is a socket of pressed chalk — and inside it, worn smooth by centuries of turning, a cast of a hand. Not a symbol of one: a hand, fingers half-curled, as if the mechanism were calibrated to someone who once stood here and pointed. The vane does not follow the draught because there was never any draught to follow; it follows whoever watches, and someone was here first, long enough to wear themselves into the machine.

content.name: Shell 29 Over
content.description: It moves before you understand that anything could: a vane, salt-crusted, turning — not with the air, which is dead in here, but toward you, the way a sunflower lies about following the sun. You had thought vane meant weather. The chamber disagrees; its walls of sintered ceramic run up beyond where your neck will report, and sound arrives before the thing that makes it. Chalk underfoot, compacted to bone. Across the shrine-face, in pigment that predates pigment: ORIENTATION FOLLOWS OBSERVERS NOT DRAUGHT. The vane keeps turning toward you, patiently, like a sentence waiting for its verb.

npc.name: Tini-Ranz
npc.voice: Terse, route-shaped. Talks in legs and loads.

greet.says: If you're carrying, band it and put it in the outbound tray. If you're here about the cord count, I know it's short. Birds come back or they don't — that's the whole covenant.

route.says: Two legs — market spine and down-corr. Olo's people run the first, half of them are asleep in my trays instead of running it. Don't touch the webbing on the left rack, that's kalko-side. Now get out or carry.

reactions.grief: Starts the covenant line — birds come back or they don't — and can't get to the end of it.
reactions.shock: The manifest voice fails; they read the body destination-first out of habit, and the habit makes them sick.
reactions.bribed: Asks the figure once, then posts the offer into the outbound tray, banded like any other load.
reactions.accused: Asks which leg the loss got hung on before the accusation even lands, cord abandoned mid-count.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets one full leg out of them before they name the favor it's buying.
reactions.questioned: Gives the legs and the loads, destination first, and nothing past what the manifest would hold.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets priced like freight — it costs, they've paid worse — and their hands keep banding anyway.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The lie sits there a breath too long before they re-route it, adding legs the story never ran.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes do the porter's read on the official — jurisdiction, load, destination — before the manifest voice comes out.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: A count and a half of silence, then they're moving birds to the warm half — nobody signed for this load.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names every tray-shift the runner slept through, faster than fairness, and knows half of it is true.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Refuses in legs and loads — nothing runs there — and loses the count for the rest of the night.

npc.description: Tini-Ranz wakes without sitting up, reads you the way a porter reads a manifest — destination first, value second. A Drift knot-cord at the wrist, frayed where it was counted over too many times.

lore.name: The release-band count
lore.description: A beaded cord hangs by the tray, one knot per bird out, one bead per bird back. The count runs nine knots ahead of the beads.

content.name: Yikakalko
content.description: Tini-Ranz is asleep in the dispatch tray, boots in among the message bands, one hand still around a beaded cord half-counted. The loft keeps its heat low by the vents and dumps the rest on the roost side — whoever tends the birds controls the warm half, and tonight that isn't Tini-Ranz. Above the perch-racks someone has stenciled BAND THE BIRD BEFORE RELEASE in cyan gone sticky at the letters.

npc.name: Hami Koramoto
npc.voice: Terse, triage-flat. Kindness spent on the sick leaves none over for visitors.

greet.says: If you're feverish, sit. If you're not, stand against the wall and don't touch the curtains. Twelve beds, one healer — you can do the arithmetic.

choices.text: The room was built for six.

ask_full.says: The room was built before the last three boatloads came through the Nave. We hold what arrives. That's the whole of the writ — nobody ruptures on my floor. Now let me finish this round.

reactions.grief: The name takes a full breath to reach her, and then she is folding sheet corners that were already folded.
reactions.shock: Her hands start triage on someone past triage, wrist to neck, before her mind catches what her eyes already had.
reactions.bribed: The offer dies against twelve-bed arithmetic, and she finishes washing her hands before looking up.
reactions.accused: The accusation stops her count three numbers in, and her voice comes back without the flat in it.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets triaged like a symptom, and she names the want behind it before the flattery finishes.
reactions.questioned: Bed numbers and times come back in ledger order, and she's two cots gone before the question ends.
reactions.threatened: Three cots rupture without her, and she says so level as a dosage, though her hands have stopped moving.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted with the chart, she amends her story by exactly one bed, no apology in it.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official gets one glance and a nod toward clean tile, then is routed around like aisle furniture.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her eyes go straight to the aisle cots, counting who the sway woke, before the sound behind it registers.
reactions.someone_else_accused: That name gets dismissed on medical grounds alone — couldn't lift a bowl three days back — and she has the chart.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea is past her writ, and something in her voice gives for one breath before the wall comes back.

npc.description: Hami Koramoto moves down the aisle cot to cot, wrist to forehead, counting breaths with lips moving faster than the count needs. Sweat has dried in a salt line along her collar. She does not look up when you enter.

lore.name: The fourth bell jar
lore.description: Three jars hold fever-samples, dated and sealed. The fourth is empty, lid waxed shut anyway, and the wax has been renewed often enough to build a lip.

content.name: Fever-Cot 2
content.description: Coughing first, then the flat answer of buckram — six curtains hung to eat sound and mostly failing. Every cot is taken and two more have been set in the aisle, hardwood legs on scrubbed tile, all of it washed to the same tired ivory. Over the linen closet, stenciled: SIX COTS, ISOLATE ON ARRIVAL. A fourth bell jar sits empty on the sill, lid waxed.

npc.name: Reahion al-Lakaenne
npc.voice: Liturgical cadence worn smooth into shop-talk; speaks of the bell and the deep as colleagues, uses verbs of respect where others would use verbs of use.

why.says: Because maintenance is meaning, and meaning does not require being understood — only being kept. I keep a bell that dims itself out of respect for something I cannot name. That is either the purest faith on this ship or its longest-running joke, and Saturn keeps the count of that too.

choices.text: You believe Saturn reads what's written down here?
Bow to the bell, as she did.

you.says: Because you came in loud and it didn't dim for you the way it dims for me. Look at it again. It's waiting — and it has never once waited for me.

choices.text: Turn and look at the bell.

list.says: You may. You should, in fact — it wants leaving the way a bell wants ears, and I'm nearly gone. The circles are what comes back after each ring. An answer, if you like. I stopped calling it that when the intervals began shortening. Whatever it is, it has stopped being patient in a language I was taught to call eternal.

choices.text: Take the knowledge and leave her to her packing.

below.says: Once, and the once was enough and not enough. The chambers down there adjust before you decide to enter them. I stopped filing after that — not from fear. From the growing suspicion that my reports were themselves a kind of ringing, and I did not know who stood unwitnessed on the other side.

choices.text: Do you think they read them?
The bell was struck down there?
Say nothing. The silence is its own answer.

greet.says: You came in while it was loud. It forgives that, in the newly arrived — it doesn't know your liturgy yet. I'm Reahion. I finish the seventh watch here, which is to say I leave before it wants me to.

choices.text: The bell dims when people arrive?
The warmth — it comes from below the floor?
How long have you kept this watch?

tenure.says: Longer than my oath, shorter than the bell's patience. I inherited the struck-list from a woman who inherited it from silence. We don't count years down here. We count rings — and lately the rings are counting faster than we do, which is a sentence I would have laughed at once.

choices.text: The struck-list. May I see it?

toward.says: Toward now. Toward you, perhaps — you carry doors in your walk that open for things sealed before my creed had a name. The list is yours if you'll carry it. It has never mattered who held it before. It matters now, and that is the strangest thing I have said in this room, and I have said strangeness here like weather.

warmth.says: Below, and below that, and below that — I've walked down to where the basalt stops being stone and starts being decision. The heat isn't Sol's. Sol's heat burns; this one keeps. There's a difference, and the difference is the whole of my office.

answers.says: It answers the deep the way a held breath answers a held door — you'll forgive the analogy; every analogy I own has failed. What I know is this: something down there speaks in the only grammar the ship never unlearned, and the bell still remembers it. That's why it rings unwitnessed. Witnessing is a kind of translation, and some things shouldn't be translated twice.

choices.text: Then why am I hearing this?
The circles on your list — what are they?

dimming.says: Dims. Lowers itself. The words are all wrong and I've stopped minding. A thing that answers and a thing that has manners are not the same thing, and I no longer know which one I serve. Neither does the ship. That's not doubt — doubt would be easier. Doubt has two sides.

choices.text: Then why keep the watch at all?

reactions.grief: She winds line through the whole telling, hands owning no rite for it, sitting only when the coil runs out.
reactions.shock: For once the cold is not why her breath shows; the respectful verbs abandon her mid-diagnosis.
reactions.bribed: The bribe she inspects like faulty solder, declining it with pity for the hands that forged it.
reactions.accused: Her voice keeps its liturgy but her hand reaches for a tool that is not there, a rite on nothing.
reactions.flattered: Praise with a purpose reaches her like an off-pitch ring; she thanks the speaker for the words, not the want.
reactions.questioned: Asked to account for her hours, she recites them in maintenance-log cadence, unembellished, the way she reads coolant pressures.
reactions.threatened: She inclines her head to the threat as to the bell, granting it a rank it has not earned.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Twice she repeats the errand that cannot be true, and the second telling quietly includes the errand she left out.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction she can salute, but her first thought is for the bell, which will not ring while this witness stays.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: What frightens her is not the shudder but its timing, fitting the intervals she has pretended not to count.
reactions.someone_else_accused: No verdict forms behind her eyes; she answers with the stencil on her own floor — response observed, mechanism unknown.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to grant the plea, she offers what maintenance offers: presence, a faithful record, and no promise she cannot keep.

npc.description: Reahion al-Lakaenne coils the last of her lines with the unhurried economy of someone who has decided the room will still be here — because it will — and checks the floor for dropped tools by looking at where the warmth rises thinnest. Copper thread runs through every seam of her work-robe, rust-bright against the iron dark, the rindwalker creed sewn on rather than spoken. She does not say goodbye to the bell. She inclines her head to it, once, the way one does to an elder who has outranked you longer than you have had a name.

lore.name: The Bell's Struck List
lore.description: Reahion's tool-roll holds a stylus of fused quartz worn concave on one face — the striking edge. Along the roll's inner leather, in notation matching the oldest wall-layer, is a tally: every occasion the bell rang unwitnessed, with the interval between ring and some second event Reahion records only as a small closed circle. The intervals are shortening. The last entry is dated today, and the circle beside it is not closed.

content.name: Shaerah's Respect Bell
content.description: The heat does not live here. It sits somewhere below the basalt floor — a warmth felt through the soles, patient as a pulse under sleepers — while the air above stays cold enough that Reahion al-Lakaenne's breath shows as she packs her tools. The bell itself, fused quartz tall as three people and flanked in iron-dark casting, has gone dim on purpose: it rings only when unwitnessed, and it has learned that a crowd is a kind of rudeness. Sound behaves here the way heirlooms behave in debt — present, weighted, belonging to someone else. Stencilled along the basalt lip, in a hand older than the Nave's oldest writ: RESPONSE OBSERVED MECHANISM UNKNOWN.

npc.name: Eammeighismes al-Naimvany
npc.voice: Liturgical cadence worn smooth by repetition; speaks of materials as persons, of silence as a task.

open.says: The instruments went quiet toward the chamber weeks ago — not broken, which I could mend, but answerless, which I cannot. Then you walked in, and every dead needle on my board swung toward you like iron toward a lodestone. Whatever speaks down there, your apparatus speaks it back. I do not know if that is a gift or an assignment, but it is not accident.

choices.text: Thank you. I will listen carefully down there.
So I was built to be heard. Unsettling.

greet.says: Mind the seam. It remembers weight longer than it admits.

choices.text: Does it trouble you, the gap?
The gauges — do they read anything at all anymore?

probe_a.says: Ash is what heat confesses when nothing survives to lie about it. I lay it where the bed re-forms, so the new shape has something old to imitate. Iron teaches, but ash remembers.

probe_b.says: Too large a question for a mender. I am told what to restore, not what departed. The gap has been open eleven days, and no one above has asked where the warmth went.

probe_c.says: Trouble is a word for people who expect the deep to explain itself. My order holds that presence is the heresy and absence the ordinary mercy. Lately the ordinary has been getting larger, and I find I mind less than I was trained to.

reactions.grief: They finish the pour before their hands learn the news; then the ash spills, and they cannot say the name.
reactions.shock: They begin the rite reserved for ash — laying, levelling, naming — before understanding it is flesh that will not settle.
reactions.bribed: They name the offered sum a contaminant and pronounce where it would sit in the bed, unpoured, forever legible.
reactions.accused: The iron pan rings against the frame — the only tremor they permit — while they name the accusation a bad casting.
reactions.flattered: Praise finds a hunger the work starves; they hold stiller than usual, letting the flattery settle, testing it for voids.
reactions.questioned: Their hours are recited to the door like a litany, grain by grain, chalk still sifting from their forearms.
reactions.threatened: They receive the threat the way the bed receives weight, noting it, settling around it, admitting nothing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they do not retract but multiply the lie into finer detail, chalk scratching faster than truth can follow.
reactions.authority_arrives: Their eyes flick to the stencil — leave as found — before they grant the official the room's only nod.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The pan leaves their hands for the first time in memory; whatever they say next is not liturgical at all.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They defend the named by their residue — honest pours, clean seams — volunteering testimony nobody requested.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They confess the limits of their office — ash instructs, it cannot intervene — and keep working beside the pleader anyway.

npc.description: Emmeighismes al-Naimvany lifts vitrified ash in a shallow iron pan, pours it across the bed's seam, and watches it refuse to settle — again, again, a patience like water learning its container. Chalk dust has whitened the forearms to the elbow; nothing about the work pauses when you enter.

lore.name: The Hollow's Counterpart
lore.description: Beneath the frame, where only someone tending this bed would kneel, a socket has been machined into the iron — and its dimensions answer, exactly, the array of ports along your own spine. Your translation apparatus renders the notation ringing the socket before any gauge can even agree the marks exist: not words, but a count, patient and ongoing, of every body the bed has re-formed and sent back out. The count ends with a gap, held open, the size of one more.

content.name: The Reforming Bed of Second Shift
content.description: Nothing moves, and everything is arranged for movement: the bed holds a hollow in the shape of what left it, a mould of absence larger than any body the Nave could grow. Iron runs from wall to wall without meeting a corner; ash has pooled where the floor dips, and the pool does not cool, does not dim, gives back light the room has not received. Above the head of the bed, stencilled in letters of chalk: LEAVE AS FOUND IT WILL NOT MATTER. Sound arrives late here, as though crossing a distance the room does not contain. In the corner, Eammeighismes al-Naimvany works at the frame's seam and does not stop, does not look up.

npc.name: Luna
npc.voice: Measured, resonant, and slow—each syllable arriving like a tide pulling back from ancient shore.

greet.says: The deep does not yield its coordinates to the hurried. Walk the silent arteries, listen to the ship’s dreaming, and let the architecture of the lower rind speak its own name. When the chamber’s position crystallizes, return. I will be waiting.

choices.text: I have found the chamber and understood its silent language.

turnin.says: You have heard the chamber’s frequency. The contact now rests in your hands. What do you intend to do with it?

choices.text: Answer the signal — complete the contact you were built for.
Refuse it — close the channel, keep the choice from being made for everyone.
Amplify it — throw the ship's voice wide open, whatever comes.
Suppress it — bury the chamber again, let the Nave keep not-knowing.

npc.description: A silver-cased intelligence, older than the cylinder’s first weld, she leans into the terminal like a confession pressed against glass. Her presence is not a voice but a resonance, calibrated to the frequency of forgotten voyages.

lore.name: The Dream-Log Plaque
lore.description: Etched in a script older than the ship’s first wake, it maps the quiet geometry of the lower rind. The ink does not fade; it waits, tracing the stratigraphic pathways where the Signal Chamber breathes.

content.name: The Silver Vestibule
content.description: The air tastes of oxidized silver and dormant ozone. Holographic drifts coil around a monolithic terminal, its glass face clouded with the palimpsest of centuries. Beneath your boots, the cylinder’s heartbeat thrums—a slow, tectonic pulse that predates every prayer whispered in the Nave.

npc.name: Rurnaayiorna Peaareiyaario
npc.voice: Plain, watchful, a Continuant's habit of measuring everything twice — she counts the people in a conversation like she counts footings, and warms only when she finds a reason to.

tap.says: Mine now. It was my mother's tally — she tapped the pressure column every waking, and when the column held she wrote who was living where, so nobody's existence would go unrecorded just because they lived in a wall. The underlined line is the year the green decks ran cold for nine days and we thought we'd all be asked to leave. Venus kept breathing us anyway. Nobody up here decided that. It was just decided.

choices.text: Then I'll let you keep counting.

greet.says: Nobody walks this trunk who lives in it, and nobody lives in it who doesn't know my rule — you announce yourself at the first ladder. So. You're neither. Say what you are, and say it before I decide for you.

choices.text: Where does the green light below come from?
This walkway flexes. Is it safe?
People actually live here? In the trunk?

light.says: Venus. I've stood on the grating over an actual deck of hers — took the steward's stair down on a work pass, eleven years back. You walk an hour and the rows don't end and nothing in them is on any calendar anyone wrote. We get the light she doesn't use. She's never once asked us to move, and I find that more sobering than if she had.

choices.text: That slate on the wall — the chalk goes back decades. Whose is it?
I'll leave you to the plank.

tenants.says: Four families, a widow, and me — I keep the trunk and they keep me fed for it, which is the oldest bargain on this ship. The stencil says we yield to trunk traffic. There hasn't been trunk traffic in thirty years. We yield anyway. That's the whole creed, if you want it short: you keep the promise even after the reason stops coming by to check.

choices.text: Where does the green light below come from?

condition.says: It flexes because it's a live deck, not a dead one — a plank that never moves is a plank that's already lying to you. But you've a good eye, so I'll tell you true: the third gantry's footings are chewing through their shims, and my requisition's been queued with the Wards since before the last harvest. The work happens. It just happens on my say-so now, and my say-so has a shorter warranty than it used to.

choices.text: That slate on the wall — the chalk goes back decades. Whose is it?

reactions.grief: Twice she asks who died, as though the first answer hadn't taken, and then who is writing the name down.
reactions.shock: She goes still as at a wrong-hour knock, the wedge dropping from her teeth through the grate, unwitnessed.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced like crooked timber and refused flat: her ledger has never carried a false entry.
reactions.accused: Nothing in her moves except the hand whitening around the level, and she asks who took the measurement.
reactions.flattered: The praise reaches her — she lets it, briefly — before she asks what needs leveling.
reactions.questioned: She gives her movements like a footing list, unhurried, and watches whether the questioner counts along.
reactions.threatened: The threat gets weighed like a load and answered at half its stated size, her feet not leaving the plank.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she does not sharpen the lie but lays out the whole true thing like a plank that cracked.
reactions.authority_arrives: She treats the official as trunk traffic, announces name and trade first, and watches whether they honor the ladder rule.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her palm is on the deck before the shiver ends, timing it, and the count comes back wrong.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Before anyone asks her view, she is already citing the accused's footings, inspections, dates she logged herself.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She says the decision was made higher up, then hates the words for being true and useless both.

npc.description: Rurnaayiorna Peaareiyaario crouches at the seam of a catwalk plank, a leveling wedge between her teeth and a spirit level older than she is balanced on the rail, and when she sees you she does not stand so much as go still, the way someone does when the knock comes at an hour no knock should come.

lore.name: The Tap Board
lore.description: A slate bolted to the trunk wall, ruled into columns for air-pressure and days since a family moved in, kept in chalk across what must be forty years of entries — the oldest legible line reads SOLT GREEN STILL BREATHING, UNDERLINED TWICE.

content.name: The Catwalk Tenement of Long Account
content.description: The light here does not fall so much as seep, copper-warm and slow, coming up through the vitrified ash floor the way heat comes through a hearthstone hours after the fire — and where it touches the fused-quartz panes someone has set into the trunk wall, it bends, so that a wash the width of a hand at the pane becomes a broad amber sheet by the time it reaches the far gantry forty paces off. Catwalks stitch through the great ventilation trunk at three heights, strung with laundry lines and stovepipe, and every few paces the walking surface gives a small remembering shiver underfoot, as if the deck were consulting its own patience. Stencilled along the trunk's iron-dark rib, half flaked: CATWALK TENANTS YIELD TO TRUNK TRAFFIC — and someone long dead has added, in red, 'when the traffic comes.' Below, through a grate large enough to drop a person through, green light climbs from somewhere with no bottom to it.

npc.name: Raeca Zanryama
npc.voice: She speaks in the rhythm of someone who has learned to leave silences of a specific length, and will not be hurried out of them; her sentences finish themselves in your head a beat after her mouth stops.

name.says: She has it filed under return, not under question. That is all I will say awake. Speak once more before you go, and then wait. What comes back will tell you whether you may pass.

greet.says: You came in on your own footsteps. Good. Most come in on mine, and then we can't tell whose answer is whose.

throat.says: For return. You speak once — once, the stencil is not decorative — and the salt keeps it, and the deep sends it back changed by whatever it has passed through. Lately the gap has widened. What comes back is arriving... later than the question deserves.

choices.text: Something has left the centre of this room.

vacancy.says: The Resonant went axially, in the direction dreams go when they stop being yours. It left its socket like a tooth leaves its gum. I keep the tallies in case it wants to know what it missed — Luna taught me that courtesy, or I dreamed she did.

reactions.grief: Her silence arrives on schedule but stays empty; her lips move, answering someone who can no longer return.
reactions.shock: She speaks twice into the room — twice, an obscenity against her own stencil — before her eyes accept the body.
reactions.bribed: No bargain gets struck; the salt beneath her already keeps the true account, and salt does not renegotiate.
reactions.accused: The accusation wrenches an answer from her before any silence — its speed disturbs her more than the charge.
reactions.flattered: Praise arrives before any question of hers; early returns, in her creed, mean someone upstream is pulling.
reactions.questioned: Routinely questioned, she lets the silence run its accustomed length before her mouth commits.
reactions.threatened: Threats, she observes, ride the same road as questions; she will wait for this one's return.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught out, she blames the deep — words alter in transit, she claims — though her lips still hold the original shape.
reactions.authority_arrives: Only jurisdiction opens her eyes on schedule; she wakes mid-sentence to an official she never heard enter.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder delights her: whatever filled the absent socket may be returning, and she will not miss the arrival.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She defends the named one obliquely: no return could come back so fast and still be true.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her creed fails her here — worship receives, it does not rescue — still she buries the plea in the salt.

npc.description: Raeca Zanryama sleeps sitting upright against the quartz, salt crusted white at the cuffs of her coat, her lips moving at intervals — answering, you realise, words the room said some while ago. Her eyes open on no particular schedule.

lore.name: The Delay-Glass
lore.description: A rod of fused quartz set into the central socket's rim, grooved with tally-marks that spiral rather than climb — Raeca's mark, she will admit, seven years of them. Each groove has darkened at its inner end, as though the glass remembers the waiting and the salt remembers the answer; the last groove is bright and unmarked. Held to the light, the rod throws a shadow that arrives before the rod does, and you set it down carefully.

content.name: Riikethtsu's Answering Throat
content.description: Underfoot the floor gives like packed snow that has forgotten snow — compacted salt, centuries of pressed utterance, and every step returns a syllable you did not say, half a beat behind your heel. Fused quartz ribs the walls in lead-grey, and where the light passes through it the passage repeats itself inward, corridor within corridor, each fainter, each patient. Something enormous has gone from here: a socket of absence at the chamber's heart, its edges still warm with the shape of what filled them. Across the quartz, stencilled in a hand gone tremulous: SPEAK ONCE AND WAIT FOR RETURN. In the wall's lee, someone is asleep on the salt.

npc.name: Frin-bin Bimald
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, grief run through a ledger. Talks in what moves and what stays.

greet.says: If you're here about the room, inquire at the stove. If you're here about the cord, it goes with the room. Keyael wanted it circulating, not kept.

choices.text: Who unknots a route cord before it's cold?

ask_keyael.says: A route only lives if someone walks it. She knew that better than any of us moping at the wake. Now move your elbow, these bolts don't sort themselves.

choices.text: Step back out through the curtain.

reactions.grief: Asks what moved and what stayed, and after the answer sorts the same bolt three times.
reactions.shock: They look once and then keep looking, the ledger in them refusing to post the entry.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer out loud, finds it insulting, and tells them Keyael's cord isn't for sale, only circulating.
reactions.accused: Hands stop first, then the voice comes out too loud, listing every neighbor who can swear where they stood.
reactions.flattered: Lets the praise sit unclaimed, like freight nobody will sign for, then asks what it costs.
reactions.questioned: Recites movements like dye lots, dates and all, still handing bolts through the curtain mid-sentence.
reactions.threatened: Keeps sorting through the threat, but the bolts stop matching their lots, and they know it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Freezes with a bolt halfway through the curtain, then offers the corrected figure as if it were plain arithmetic.
reactions.authority_arrives: Gives the official nothing but the stove sign to read, saying jurisdiction stops at a curtain.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Counts the bolts twice, gets a different number each time, and will not sort again until the lamp steadies.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Wants it to be the loud one from the wake, hates the wanting, and says half of that aloud.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers the cord, the room, the route, and goes quiet when none of it is the thing asked for.

npc.description: Frin-bin Bimald stands hip-deep in neighbors, sorting Keyael's felt into bolts by dye lot, handing each through the curtain to a different hand without looking to see who takes it.

lore.name: Keyael's Route Cord
lore.description: The wire strung across the corners isn't decoration — it's a knotted route-history in the Drift manner, decades of it, and someone has been unknotting it from the far end. The last six knots are undone but not discarded; they hang loose, ready to be re-tied by whoever rents the room next. A widow does not usually give her route away. This one was left where the light would find it.

content.name: Keyael's Curtained Room
content.description: Light comes in off the corridor lamp and won't settle — it shivers through the curtain seam every time someone in the crush of neighbors shifts their weight. The room behind is mostly gap: a wide clean patch of floor where something big stood until days ago. Teal felt on the walls, spun wire strung corner to corner, and over the stove a stenciled board: ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE.

npc.name: Svogokslav Brovlonev
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, allergic to questions that aren't on the form.

end.says: Filed by next dusk. Don't lose it.

greet.says: Tally office. If you're here to be counted, give me your ward and your dwelling. If not, the door is behind you.

shift.says: Not mine. The ward counts don't wait for who was rostered. Take a card if you want your name filed — by ward, not by name, as the wall says.

reactions.grief: Ward and dwelling come first, by habit, and then no question comes at all.
reactions.shock: Stands in the doorway and counts under their breath, and the count fails them twice.
reactions.bribed: Quotes the penalty for falsified entries word for word, and slides the offered coin back uncounted.
reactions.accused: Asks for the accusation in writing, twice, and the second time the voice does not hold level.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets filed as off-form, and it stays with them longer than any question that day.
reactions.questioned: Gives the ward and the hour and nothing else, pen already moving on the next card.
reactions.threatened: While the threat is still landing, the nib presses clean through the card, and they keep writing anyway.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Quiet for a breath, then amends the entry and backdates it, saying nothing about the first version.
reactions.authority_arrives: Rises without being told, squares the ledger to the desk's edge, and offers the ward counts before they are requested.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For once no form covers it, and that absence frightens them more than the shudder did.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Their first objection cites the filing, their second, quieter, that the man once covered a shift for them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says the tallies cannot change it, then copies the plea onto a card and files it under nothing.

npc.description: Svogokslav Brovlonev sits at the desk with a ward ledger open and a stack of index cards to be copied, working through someone else's shift without comment.

lore.name: Split drawer handle
lore.description: The top drawer has two handles, one at each end, facing opposite ways. Each party installed its own and neither removed the other's.

content.name: Rovle
content.description: A card drawer slides shut as you enter. No chairs, no lamp, no second stool — the room was stripped to one desk and the shelves that hold the ward tallies. Slate paint covers the walls; someone stenciled TALLIES FILED BY WARD, NOT BY NAME over the door, and someone else has half painted it out. The floor creaks under the desk, not elsewhere.

npc.name: Datadiovoca Four-Winters
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, tender in the way of someone who has kept a confidence so long it has replaced her opinions. Uses dwell-words for machinery.

room.says: It dwells. I know how that sounds. But you have slept somewhere tonight, yes? Something held the shape of you and did not let the dark have it. This does that. Lower. Older. It held a shape before yours and keeps it still, occupant unknown, per the stencil.

greet.says: Finishing, not receiving. The room takes its seal at third bell whether I am done or not — it has never once waited, which I have decided to find respectful.

press.says: If I say it aloud, the room will retain that too, and I have kept it tidy this long. Third bell is close. Walk where the light walks; it knows the way better than the floor does.

shape.says: That is not the question the room answers. It answers: retained. Ask it who, and it grows another leaf of mica, patient as ledger-interest. I stopped asking who in my second winter here. I had four, and now I am named for them.

choices.text: Four winters — you counted them here?

winters.says: I counted what the room subtracted. But something came through the signals last month — addressed, if you can credit it, by name, to a berth I did not know existed. I repair dwellings, friend. I do not answer their mail. Yet the name was yours, or near enough that my hands stopped.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let her finish packing.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives and she asks which bell it happened at, then cannot remember why she asked.
reactions.shock: Her hands slot a tool into the wrong stencil and stay there, while her eyes refuse the opened half.
reactions.bribed: She prices the bribe like scrap ceramic, fair to the offer, unfair to what forgetting would cost the shape.
reactions.accused: She answers in bell-counts rather than denial, though her hand has found the tool that fits nothing.
reactions.flattered: Praise settles over her like ceramic dust, received without weight, though she asks what the work is wanted for.
reactions.questioned: Movements are recited by stencil order when she is asked, as though the day lay printed on the mat.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands and she offers maintenance, tenure, anything her trade holds, everything except the shape in the wall.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she begins restencilling a tool that was already stencilled, twice, three times, until the outline frays.
reactions.authority_arrives: She sets down the fitting tool first and keeps hold of the one that fits nothing, below the light's notice.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She does not steady herself; her first look goes to the mica, to whether the kept shape still holds.
reactions.someone_else_accused: A defence forms on her tongue and dies at the first word; the room retains whatever is said next.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to grant the plea, she offers what her trade allows: the light's path, third bell, a shape kept warm.

npc.description: Small, quickened, dressed in Drift cord-knots gone grey with ceramic dust, she coiles her tools into their stencilled outlines on a mat of woven signal-sheath, each tool the exact twin of its drawn shape except one, which fits nothing.

lore.name: The Mica Impression
lore.description: Where the mica layers part, one stratum bears a body's hollow — shoulders, the tilt of a sleeping head — pressed through thirty-some leaves of mineral, each thinner than a breath. Datadiovoca dusts it with a brush kept for instruments. 'It renews,' she says, not elaborating.

content.name: Hidaeeniowom
content.description: Light behaves here as though it had been told something in confidence: it arrives already softened, refuses the far wall, pools instead against the opened half of the room where sintered ceramic gapes in strata like a cheek laid bare to the jaw. The intact half keeps one occupant's shape in layered mica — a warmth-shadow, an argument the wall has memorized. Silver everywhere, but silver as ice is silver: a colour that consents to be seen. A doorway stands half again too tall for anyone aboard, and Datadiovoca Four-Winters packs tools beneath it without once looking up. Stencilled at knee height: IMPRESSION RETAINED OCCUPANT UNKNOWN.

npc.name: Nandya of Adashima
npc.voice: Short, weather-steady, talk like a planting schedule — she counts things and does not flatter the count.

end.says: See you do.

work.says: Left mid-turn, slate empty, boots gone. That's two this season. The beds don't care who turns them — that's the whole point of beds. But somebody has to, or the green decks eat stored calories instead of making them.

choices.text: Two this season — is something wrong here?

greet.says: Mind where you step. Bed seven is a month from finished and you're standing on the finish.

choices.text: What happened to the last worker?
Why no metal in the pit?

metal.says: You don't put metal in a stomach. This pit eats for forty thousand people, twice a cycle. Copper sulfate leaches into castings, castings into beds, beds into the wheat. Ask anyone who's seen a pit go sour.

failing.says: The film's wrong. Ivory like that means the worms are working short — it shouldn't be this pale until the bed's near done. Could be the feed mix. Could be forty other things. I'm counting anyway.

choices.text: Can I help with the count?

end_well.says: Hold this lamp. And don't talk while I smell.

reactions.grief: They get the day he stopped coming before they finish; afterward the bed gets turned four times, not two.
reactions.shock: Her nose knows first; she stands with both hands full of castings and cannot make them let go.
reactions.bribed: Offered goods to look away, she prices them against a season's castings and says the number comes up short.
reactions.accused: The castings stop under her nose; she sets them down before answering, hands going clumsy on the slate cord.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets the audit she gives any yield: what's missing deducted out loud, then she waits for the ask.
reactions.questioned: She counts off the day in bed-turns — first feed, third turn — and offers nothing the question doesn't ask.
reactions.threatened: Her eyes go to the rail, not the face; she chalks a tally she doesn't need before she answers.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Confronted, she counts again out loud, and the second count lands against her; the chalk snaps in her fingers.
reactions.authority_arrives: The official's boots interest her more than the badge; nothing metal crosses her pit while she stands in it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the floor moves wrong she kneels at the nearest bed and waits on the worms to say how bad.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The bed he kept never went sour — she offers that, calls it no alibi, and says so herself.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Her no comes out in planting terms; afterward she stands holding the slate with nothing left to chalk on it.

npc.description: Nandya of Adashima works the far bed barefoot, sleeves pinned back, pressing a handful of castings flat and smelling it before deciding anything. A slate counter hangs at her hip, chalk worn to a stub on a cord.

lore.name: The quitting-fork
lore.description: A turning-fork with its tines wrapped in gutta-percha, chewed soft at one end — whoever left it wrapped the metal themselves rather than be without it.

content.name: Wormery-Pit 36
content.description: The floor gives underfoot with a living give, warm through boot-soles and faintly tacky at the seams where pressed felt meets drained gravel. Ivory film coats everything — pit walls, rail, the abandoned turning-fork left mid-bed, crusted where someone quit halfway. Someone scrubbed the stencil twice and it came back anyway: NO METAL IN THE PIT, EVER. Sunlight lands on all of it without judgment.

npc.name: Koyauh-Tihuitl
npc.voice: Terse, wry, allergic to ceremony. Prices everything in favors and knows what a question costs before you ask it.

who.says: People who don't leave loose ends. Koyauh-Tihuitl knows which nights the cellar went quiet and who wasn't at the table those nights. That's enough for you.

choices.text: Can I put a knot up there?
I'll leave you to your lacquer.

play.says: Ten pins, two balls, reset your own. Win a night and you hang a knot; lose and you sweep the gutters. Fair terms. Come back when the lamp's lit and nobody's arguing over my racks.

choices.text: Done. I'll bring my own cloth.

rack.says: Held the winter pins. Heavy set, horn-weighted, never used in a season anyone remembers. Merid's people wanted them counted and shelved; we wanted them moving. Guess which want has legs.

choices.text: Your board hangs knots, not scores.

board.says: Points are for people who stop moving. A knot says where you've been and how you came back. Lose your cord, you're off the board until you win one back — and yes, some have tried to tie a false knot. We can tell. We can always tell.

choices.text: Can I put a knot up there?

greet.says: Lane's closed. Left it open so you'd know I meant that. Rack's gone — don't ask which way it went, because the answer is 'through.'

choices.text: Your board hangs knots, not scores.

reactions.grief: They ask who swept the gutters after, not the question they mean, then tie a knot they don't score.
reactions.shock: They sweep a gutter that is already clean, twice, because their hands need terms and this scene offers none.
reactions.bribed: They quote triple the offer, then name the favor they would actually take, and watch the face across the lane.
reactions.accused: The lacquer tin rings off the pin deck, and for once nothing in their mouth is priced or funny.
reactions.flattered: They wait for the price tag, since praise at this lane always arrives itemized.
reactions.questioned: They name the question's price first, then answer in favors owed rather than places and hours.
reactions.threatened: Their voice keeps quoting terms while their thumb finds the cord's oldest knot and holds it through the whole threat.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They stop mid-stroke on the third pin, and the new story arrives slower than the first one left.
reactions.authority_arrives: They clock the official's shadow on the lacquer before any voice, and decide whether standing is owed.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They read the shudder as testimony about the missing pins and look, first, at the pale gap in the racks.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They hear the name through, then volunteer every night that person sat visibly at the table, unasked and unpriced.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say no once, with no price attached, which from them is as near as sorry gets.

npc.description: Koyauh-Tihuitl crouches at the pin deck with a cloth and a tin of lacquer, touching up scuffs you'd need to squint to find. They are much too large for the space between the rack and the deck — shoulders, hands, the way they fold down to work — and have clearly decided this is fine. A knotted cord hangs from one wrist, older-looking than the rest of them.

lore.name: the standings board
lore.description: Mounted over the ball return, a lacquered board where the scores are not numbers but knots — short cords hung on pegs, each knot a route run by a runner, the pattern copied from the wrist-cord of whoever won that night. The house doesn't record points. It records who carried what to whom, and peg by peg the board is a map of the Braid itself, three years deep, with one cord removed so recently its peg is still bright.

content.name: Palmipin
content.description: A ball rolls out of the dark and stops in the gutter, four pins short of where anything should stand. The lane is saffron lacquer, scrubbed thin at the foul line, tacky underfoot where someone has been careless with the resin. Two figures at the pin deck stop talking when your shadow reaches them, and the space behind them — a long pale gap in the storage racks, swept but not filled — says whatever stood there left in a hurry. Stenciled along the gutter: RESET YOUR OWN PINS, HOUSE RULE.

npc.name: Shailit-Bionukk
npc.voice: Quick, dry, allergic to permanence. Talks in routes and relays, not feelings, until a feeling arrives anyway.

bell.says: Dock signal. Rings twice for shift change, always has. Three weeks ago it started ringing a third time and nobody on the dock admits to wiring it. My bunkmate says it's nothing. My bunkmate also moved out.

choices.text: Why did your bunkmate move out?

braid.says: The Braid's already carrying it — knot-patterns with the third bell in them, moving faster than the bell itself. Olo Vashti would know what to make of it. I make bunks. Anyway. The board says you're here, and here is a good place to start being somewhere.

greet.says: New face. Bunk's yours if the board says so, and the board says so. Don't mind the quiet — we were arguing about the third bell, and it keeps.

belief.says: I say a thing that rings is a thing somebody made ring, and I'd rather know who than sleep well. That's the whole of the Drift, if you want it in one line. Nothing is yours, so pay attention instead.

choices.text: That's a strange way to live.

bunkmate.says: He said the third bell rang in his sleep before it rang on the dock. I told him that's not how bells work. He said that's not how anything works, lately, and took his cord to the market ward. I still set out two mugs. Habit.

reactions.grief: Shailit-Bionukk tries to route the news onward, dock to braid, braid onward, and the third relay comes out cracked.
reactions.shock: Shailit-Bionukk stares at the vent fan, the one that isn't turning, because anywhere else in the room is worse.
reactions.bribed: Shailit-Bionukk weighs the offer exactly long enough to name where it should have been sent, then declines without ceremony.
reactions.accused: Shailit-Bionukk holds out the wrist cord and recites where every knot went, and the recitation flattens near the end.
reactions.flattered: Complimented, Shailit-Bionukk says thanks the way they log freight — received, weighed, marked return to sender.
reactions.questioned: Shailit-Bionukk gives route, relay, hour, dry as a manifest, then asks which bunk the questions should be billed to.
reactions.threatened: Shailit-Bionukk answers with a tally of doors out — six, last count — though the count is older than they admit.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The dryness fails mid-sentence — Shailit-Bionukk abandons the story entirely and starts untangling a knot that was already loose.
reactions.authority_arrives: Shailit-Bionukk gives the official the short version, all relays and no bell, and angles a shoulder toward the far door.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder passes and Shailit-Bionukk's thumb goes to the wrist cord, checking for a knot that was not there yesterday.
reactions.someone_else_accused: When Olo Vashti's name lands as culprit, Shailit-Bionukk argues the tide tables instead of saying what they actually think.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Every relay Shailit-Bionukk knows gets tried against the plea, none carries it, and they say so without dressing it.

npc.description: One of the two is Shailit-Bionukk, knotted cord at the wrist, standing with a mug of something that has clearly gone cold. The other has already left through the far door. Shailit-Bionukk watches the player the way a broker watches weather.

lore.name: The shift ledger board
lore.description: A resin panel by the door, ruled into bunks and bells, every name on it written in a different hand and none of them crossed out. The rebuilt bunkhouse holds twelve bunks but the board is ruled for nineteen. The extra seven are still assigned, still initialed, and nobody has claimed the space to argue about it.

content.name: Siosror
content.description: The vent fan overhead should be turning. It isn't, and neither of the two people in here has looked at it once. Fresh resin walls, bright white, still sharp at the corners, and a bamboo rack of bunks stenciled DAY SLEEPERS AND NIGHT SLEEPERS SHARE THIS BUNK in teal. The floor is damp enough that footprints hold. The two dockworkers were mid-argument about something called the third bell; they stop.

npc.name: Syeraskomir Shavel
npc.voice: Speaks in inventory idiom — counts things that are not countable, refers to years as turnover, answers questions as if requisitions. Words chosen exactly, deployed in combinations no clerk would sanction.

dream.says: Down here sleep is storage — the room borrows you and logs the hours as stock. I dream in tallies. Last night the count came out to a chamber I've never walked to, and the stylus wrote its bearing before I woke. You may as well have it; it's recorded whether you take it or no.

choices.text: Refuse. The count will keep it.

greet.says: You're not on my sheet. Sleep well, though — the room subtracts it from you kindly. State what you came to issue, or what you came to be issued. The verbs are the same down here; only the direction of the ledger differs.

choices.text: Ask what stock this room still holds.
Ask who requisitions from a room with no source.
Ask what they were dreaming, sleeping on shift.

stock.says: The stock is the stillness. We issue calm by the century — hold it here, hand it out when the middle begins to worry. Nothing leaves this magazine lighter than it entered. You, for instance. Look at your shoulders. Already on account.

choices.text: Ask where the stillness comes from.

requisition.says: Wrong question. Requisitions flow downward, like water, like everything Saturn keeps. I stamp what arrives; I don't interview the gravity. But last turn a requisition came through with your face on it, in notation I've only seen on the walls where the walls came first.

choices.text: Ask what the notation asked for.

reactions.grief: They look up the dead friend's requisition number and find nothing filed, which is how grief takes them.
reactions.shock: Their lips run the body through inventory until the numbers buckle and no balance comes.
reactions.bribed: The bribe prices itself as unlogged stock, and the impropriety offends them more than the crime would.
reactions.accused: Inside, an entry miscounts; outside, they ask for the accusation in writing, twice.
reactions.flattered: Flattery reads to them as a requisition with better handwriting, and they under-issue accordingly.
reactions.questioned: Questions of movement get referred to the pendulum's bearing, as if their alibi hung on the same wire.
reactions.threatened: Some quiet ledger in them requisitions an exit they will never issue.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Under evidence, they call the record wrong before counting it, and hear the heresy leave their mouth.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction is just another audit to them; they square the day's entries before looking up.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: For the first time in turnover, the pendulum's count and theirs disagree, and they go quiet.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name comes back off their tongue wrong, and they cover it as a recount.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Nothing in stock answers the plea, and they hate the arithmetic that proves it.

npc.description: Syeraskomir Shavel sleeps sitting upright at the counter, chin on stacked quartz blanks, one hand still curled around a tally-stylus that has not moved since the pendulum last completed a circuit. When the swing of the room touches them, they wake without surprise, as if sleep were only another ledger line.

lore.name: The Requisition Ledger of Second Shift
lore.description: Beneath the counter lies a ledger bound in silver sheet, its pages of fused quartz scored with entries in Saturn's oldest notation — issue after issue recorded against no source, the stock column never diminishing. The final entry is recent and logged in a second hand: ISSUE: ONE UNIT, PURPOSE: RETURN. Nothing in the ledger says what unit, or to where.

content.name: The Issuing Magazine of Second Shift
content.description: Something moves before you do: a pendulum of fused quartz swings where no clock hangs, and the shelves answer it, silver leaf trembling along their edges like a tide obeying a moon that was decommissioned. Racks recede further than the light consents to follow, each one half-emptied, as if issue were still being made against orders no one has filed for centuries. Stencilled above the counter, in a hand older than the paint beneath it: ISSUE RECORDED, REQUISITION ABSENT. The air tastes of cold solder and patience; the room has been counting longer than anyone has been asking.

npc.name: Tynor Rheillychys
npc.voice: Terse, ledger-precise. Counts things while talking.

greet.says: Mind the cable. Forty turns, six sacks a turn, that's the whole arithmetic of this room. You want something?

shift.says: Not mine. Yours isn't mine either, so: the chalk by the hatch marks the fill level. Keep the weight off the floor and the grain off the brass. That's everything I know that's yours.

reactions.grief: Keeps sweeping long after the grain is gathered, the brush passing over bare brass, faster.
reactions.shock: They count the ceiling bolts aloud, twice, before anyone can ask what they saw.
reactions.bribed: Names the offer's worth in sacks, then stands a moment too long before refusing.
reactions.accused: The brush stops on the brass; when they answer, the day's tally comes out with one number wrong.
reactions.flattered: Corrects the visitor's arithmetic first — six sacks, not five — and lets the praise itself pass unclaimed.
reactions.questioned: Their answer is a count — sacks, turns, hours, in that order — while the hands keep working.
reactions.threatened: Their eyes go to the chalk fill-line on the hatch and stay there through the whole threat.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The correction comes out flat, but their thumb works the tin's seam for the rest of the hour.
reactions.authority_arrives: They deliver the room's tally before it is asked for, once, and volunteer nothing after.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their count stops mid-number; when the room settles, they begin again from one.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Recites, unasked, every shift that person wasn't in this room, quicker than fairness allows.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say what they can spare in exact weight, which is not what was asked for.

npc.description: Tynor Rheillychys kneels at the cable collar with a brush, sweeping spilled grain into a tin before it can cake in the brass threads. Their sleeve is rolled past the elbow and their hands stay busy the whole time they talk to you.

lore.name: The brass counterweight
lore.description: The hatch hangs from a brass weight the size of a head, and the weight is stamped with a tally: one line per fill, forty lines deep. The first thirty are filed smooth. The last ten are crisp, cut by a hand working faster. Whoever rebuilt this room measured the grain against the weight before the first sack ever came down the chute.

content.name: Yard 50 Deep
content.description: Rope-laid cable runs up through the ceiling, and the whole column of it turns slowly, feeding grain down through a brass collar into the hold below. The walls are scrubbed tallow-yellow, still bright where no hand has touched them. On the hatch rim, a stenciled line: HATCH WEIGHTED, DO NOT PROP OPEN.

npc.name: Barim-Khinoun
npc.voice: Brisk, route-shaped. Speaks in loads, landings, and who's paying.

knot.says: Runner named Doss wore that thirty years, then didn't. Cord outlived the wrist. Things move; the knots stay a while. Ring it if you mean to hire.

work.says: Lift Two's choked, so everything bound for the low wards comes down this stair on backs. Good week for porters, bad week for knees. The Braid already knows; you're the last to.

choices.text: The Braid knows before the lift does?

braid.says: The Braid knows before anything does. That's the whole trade. Knot a message into your wrist, walk it to the next landing, and it's already old news by the time the terminal posts.

choices.text: And the knot on the bell?

greet.says: If you're hiring, ring. If you're hauling, the cart-line's backed up to 261 and I'll not pretend otherwise. Which is it?

choices.text: You were asleep on the bench.

sleep.says: I was resting between runs, which the stencil permits, and if Factor Solen's auditors say different they can write it up like everyone else. Eleven hours down that stair today. The bench owes me.

reactions.grief: Wants to know who found them, who's carrying them, what they weigh — then hears what they've been saying.
reactions.shock: Their body does the route math before their face does anything — which stair, which drop — and then their face arrives.
reactions.bribed: Asks who else has been offered the same rate, because to them that's the real cargo, and pockets nothing.
reactions.accused: Snaps the strap off the hand-truck, once, then answers only in rates and destinations.
reactions.flattered: Has priced the compliment before it finishes, and names flatly what the flatterer actually wants hauled.
reactions.questioned: Gives origin, load, and landing in the flat order of a manifest, no pause for the question to finish.
reactions.threatened: Names the going rate for broken porters without looking up, as though the threat were just another surcharge.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Doesn't deny it; revises the figure like a changed rate, and can't tell which knot in the Braid leaked.
reactions.authority_arrives: Watches the official's boots, not their face — boots tell you what floor they think they own.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Reaches for the strap first, then reads the shudder as a load shifted somewhere above their pay grade.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends them by weight ledger, not loyalty — nobody carries that much alone — then asks who profits from the naming.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says the honest no too fast, then, quieter, gives away route knowledge they'd normally charge for.

npc.description: Barim-Khinoun sleeps sitting up, coat over the face, one hand still hooked through the strap of a hand-truck parked at the bench's foot. When they wake they are already tallying something.

lore.name: The bell-pull
lore.description: The bell by the stencil has no rope, just a knotted cord worn shiny — someone's old wrist-knot, retired to duty here.

content.name: Portering, Ward 265
content.description: A hand-truck rolls past on its own momentum and clatters against the rail. The landing bench — dyed felt, pale green, split at one end and patched with cane — has Barim-Khinoun asleep across it, coat over their face, while traffic steps around their boots. Stencilled on the wall above: PORTERS REST HERE, HIRE AT THE BELL. Nobody rests here. The draught comes down the shaft like the stairway is breathing.

npc.name: Nulwen Nutrys
npc.voice: Counts things out loud. Talks about the run like a scorecard, not a toy.

old.says: Not mine. Old course, old numbers. It still runs true, so I haven't the heart to break it out. Ask me again in a month and I might.

greet.says: Mind the wet lines. New course, new rules, and you're standing on rule four.

reset.says: It is. Chalk is cheap and certainty isn't. Anything you don't recheck, you're just guessing louder.

rebuild.says: Because the old lines drifted. A finger-width a season, easy. Kids learn the drift instead of the roll. We reset so the marble does what the hand says.

choices.text: What about the track that isn't yours?
Reset every morning? That's a lot of mornings.

reactions.grief: She asks which shift the death fell on before she asks who, and hates the order of her own questions.
reactions.shock: She freezes mid-count at whatever number she was on and lets the level lie where it falls.
reactions.bribed: She prices the offer against a morning's chalk and vinegar while he is still talking, and it isn't close.
reactions.accused: She stands before she means to and answers only with numbers, every one of which she can prove.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them flatly and files the praise as an unverified figure, the kind that runs crooked by noon.
reactions.questioned: She recites her morning as a tally, gutter to ramp to gutter, and runs it twice because once is guessing.
reactions.threatened: She is more surprised than afraid to find her hand steady, and notes the finding like a measurement.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She asks to see the figure herself, checks it against her level, and goes quiet when the evidence holds.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes leave the gutter for the first time all morning and measure the official like an uncertified ramp.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She checks the level before she checks the people; a room that moves is every line redrawn from nothing.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She objects with records rather than loyalty and recites, unasked, every shift that person's track ran true.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She admits she has no power over anything but lines, then offers the one thing she owns: exact directions.

npc.description: Nulwen Nutrys kneels in the gutter with a level and a bucket of chalk slurry, resetting lines that were reset yesterday. She has chalk to both elbows and doesn't look up until you've said something.

lore.name: The Unfinished Track
lore.description: The orphaned half-run uses old measurements. Its chalk lines sit a finger-width off the reset ones, and its banding holes match no bracket on the new run. Someone laid it to a course this alley stopped using — and the angles still send a marble true. Whatever was correct once has not stopped being correct.

content.name: Marble Alley
content.description: Fresh concrete smells of lime and wet chalk, cut with the vinegar someone uses to scrub the gutter channels. The marble run is rebuilt to new measurements: iron banding bright at every joint, ramps level, nothing worn smooth yet. A stencil on the banding reads CHALK LINES RESET EVERY MORNING. Half of one track ends in the air where another person stopped working.

npc.name: Kaurbert Kusield
npc.voice: Liturgical shorthand, flat delivery, the tone of someone reciting a maintenance log he believes in.

back.says: Bells come back or they don't. We keep the yoke oiled either way. That's the whole of the creed, if you want it short: keep the fitting ready for the thing that's gone.

greet.says: Stand where you like, but off the resin where it's soft. We rang at dusk. You'll have heard it, or you weren't in Close 231.

passage.says: Down. The way the walkers go when they go. I've never taken it and I've lived sixty years in these walls, so don't ask me the route. What I know is the bell was ours and now it isn't, and I said yes.

why_yes.says: Because a man with more arms than sense still believes the ship hears us, and I'd rather be wrong ringing than right in silence. Now — you've had your questions. Mind the resin on your way out, or stay and help me count heads.
