bell_gone.says: Taken down for the passage. Not stolen — taken, with rites, by people who knew what they were carrying. It goes to a shaft that needs a voice more than we do. I signed the manifest myself, which is why everyone keeps asking me.

choices.text: And when does it come back?

dawn_dusk.says: Twice a day the ship turns its face, and twice a day we answer. Anything more is showing off. My grandmother rang a third service for a full season and went deaf in the left ear, and the season accomplished nothing she could name.

choices.text: Your family has kept this chapel?

grandmother.says: Four generations of Kusield on this stair. She taught me the rope before she taught me to walk, and she never told me what the ringing was for, only that a chapel that doesn't answer is a room with furniture in it. I've thought about that more than is healthy.

choices.text: And what do you think it's for?

reactions.grief: Sixty years of names, and this one leaves him holding the rag over the oil, doing nothing.
reactions.shock: His eyes go to the pale rectangle where the bell hung, not to the body, and stay.
reactions.bribed: The offer is weighed in his units, hangable, ringable, oilable, and found wanting on every count.
reactions.accused: The accusation gets his shift schedule in return, dates and oilings, as if duty were the same as innocence.
reactions.flattered: Praise gets treated like an inspection: he offers up his worst repair before remembering to be modest.
reactions.questioned: His hours come out in log order, dawn to dusk, and the stair stays out of the account.
reactions.threatened: He asks for the threat in writing, since nothing counts here that isn't entered in the log.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: He repeats the sentence in the same order, word for word, and finds sudden work for the wrench.
reactions.authority_arrives: At the stencil he stops, one hand flat against the oxblood letters, waiting to be counted himself.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: He calls it ice in the iron, log-standard, and his voice does not believe the entry.
reactions.someone_else_accused: One flat no, then six rehearsed reasons, like a creed written overnight for a single name.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He points to the stair and does not follow, all four hands hanging useless for once.

npc.description: Kaurbert Kusield stands at the foot of the stair with a wrench he isn't using, one of his four hands keeping count of the crowd as they come in. He answers questions without turning his head.

lore.name: The Empty Yoke
lore.description: An iron yoke bolted to the beam where the bell hung, its hook burnished bright by decades of rope. Someone has left the rope coiled on the hook still, ready for a bell that isn't there.

content.name: The Tower Chapel, Close 231
content.description: The floor gives underfoot in a way stone shouldn't — resin poured over iron plate, worn through at the threshold to a dull shine. The bell's absence is a shape on the wall: a pale rectangle where something heavy hung, and the crowd packed below it keeps glancing up anyway. Oxblood paint covers everything, even the stencil by the stair: BELL RUNG AT DAWN AND DUSK ONLY.

npc.name: Stun-Masenn
npc.voice: Dry, spare, fluent in tolerances. She speaks of iron the way the devout speak of saints — without ornament, because none is needed.

who.says: A walker named Illun, before your time and mostly before mine. Kept the tally on his ladle — every seal he tested at pressure and held. Four hundred and change, then a row that ends short. The molds waited out the dawn without him, and the dawn came anyway, and no one came to read it. So it sits. Iron holds; that is the whole of the creed. Someone just has to be here to see it hold.

choices.text: Will you run the pressure test at dawn?

dawn.says: Not this dawn. These seals cure for a collar that stopped being scheduled, and yet they cure on, because that is what iron does and what we do. When Mars wants them read, Mars will send word the way Mars sends everything — by not being absent. You should go down deeper than this if you're going down at all. But take the lesson first: everything here holds longer than the people who watched it pour.

greet.says: Mind the edge. It lies about being cool for another six hours. You've walked a long way to watch nothing cure.

choices.text: Why did the work stop mid-pour?

stopped.says: It didn't stop. It paused. There's a difference — a stop you walk away from, a pause you wait out. He waited out longer than he had. Mars's own crew does not idle in this room without cause; the floor remembers who is standing on it.

reactions.grief: The name lands; she answers with a ladle's tally, four hundred seals and the row that stops, though nobody asked.
reactions.shock: For once the creed has no answer — iron holds, and this did not — and her hands hang useless.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets weighed like scrap and found under tolerance — she names no number, because iron takes no payment.
reactions.accused: She stops mid-check and dares them to lay a palm on the seal and call it failed to iron's face.
reactions.flattered: Praise makes her suspicious the way a cool edge does — she checks it again, twice, before trusting either.
reactions.questioned: Her hours come back numbered from the pour, exact to the minute, unoffended, the way she would read a cure.
reactions.threatened: The threat is filed with Mars's other silences, though her palm has left a damp print on the cooling mold.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she does not retract; she re-casts the claim in narrower tolerances, as if precision were the same as truth.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction receives the face she keeps for scheduled weather; the cure-log goes on being read aloud beneath it.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Her hand leaves the mold fast, the first fast thing in years, and she counts the four bays twice.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She recites every seal that person ever poured and held, as if a record at pressure counted as testimony.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Nothing in her power answers the plea, so she pays the only coin she holds — the lesson about iron holding.

npc.description: Stun-Masenn stands knee-deep in the shadow of the near mold, sleeves rolled and forearms powdered grey to the elbow, running a bare palm along the seal's cooling edge the way another person might check a sleeping child's forehead. She does not startle when you enter; she looks at you the way you look at weather that arrived on schedule.

lore.name: The Ladle That Does Not Pour
lore.description: Among the hanging ladles, one is different: its rim is worn mirror-smooth from decades of pours, and bolted to its shank is a bracket of newer iron fitted to grip a filament guide — a modification, mender's work, done by someone who meant to adapt the tool for drawn-filament feed and then never used it. The bracket's bolts show no wrench marks recent enough to shine. Beneath it, scratched into the shank in hull-notation, a tally runs to several hundred strokes and then stops mid-row, as if the counter was called away in the middle of a number.

content.name: Gasket Casting
content.description: The light here does not fall so much as flinch — it comes off the cooling lip of a poured seal the size of a threshing floor and throws everything backward, so that the girders overhead hold their darkness longer than the floor holds its noon. Four seals lie in their molds mid-cure, one for each bay of a docking collar you have never seen and cannot picture; ladles of iron hang from their chains exactly where they were set down, slag already cold in the cups. Stenciled along the near mold's rim, in letters a hand could stand inside: SEAL CURING, PRESSURE TEST AT DAWN. The dawn in question is not marked on any calendar visible here.

npc.name: Ibein-Sethenne
npc.voice: Circulation-minded: measures everything by what moves through it and how fast, speaks in the short rhythms of relay code, distrusts anything that stands still for long — including this room.

her.says: Because the tank held our drinking water before it held their core — my mother's household drank from this line, and her mother before. Somebody should hear the room empty. That's not on any route chart. It's just the debt of having been somewhere.

choices.text: What will you do when the room is done being heard?

debt.says: Retie the cord. New knot, new loop, whatever loop the reroute leaves me. Everything on this ship moves eventually — my creed says so and my mother's water line says so. I only stayed long enough to be the one who didn't leave first.

choices.text: Then I'll leave first. Fair passage.

left.says: A resonator core, if you want the inventory word. It answered the pulse from the deep arteries — kept the whole junction's timing honest. Mercury's people drew it down the axial shaft eleven days ago. It walked out of my house and the water didn't even slop.

choices.text: Mercury drew it? You've seen them?

greet.says: Nobody walks here. The artery that fed this house was rerouted last month and took everyone with it. So either you're lost, or you came on purpose, and I don't get the second kind often.

afraid.says: It unsettled the knot, let's say. My cord says I've run the same four-deck loop for nineteen years, and a thing that old doesn't notice a loop. Unless it counts loops. I've stopped deciding which thought is worse.

choices.text: And now you wait here alone.

mercury.says: Seen? I've been addressed. Once. A maintenance pulse came through the wall with my shift-number in it, which no machine has reason to know. You work the arteries long enough, you learn the difference between weather and attention. That was attention.

reroute.says: Up and over, through the quartz galleries — forty seconds faster to the Nave, which is everything in my trade. The Drift's maps already carry it. This whole house is a deleted route now. You're standing in a knot someone tied and cut.

choices.text: Then why are you still here?

reactions.grief: Relay habit outlives the news; she keeps giving timestamps for a woman who will use none of them.
reactions.shock: She freezes mid-count, and the doubled echo arrives twice around a silence she cannot route anywhere.
reactions.bribed: She refuses the number twice, once for the offer and once for the silence it wanted.
reactions.accused: She stops counting the room's echo, and the accusation hangs in her like water with nowhere left to drain.
reactions.flattered: Praise stops her like a blocked line; she checks the flatterer's hands for what they want moved.
reactions.questioned: She keeps closing the relay wires in their order and recounts her day, tidy inside the doubled echo.
reactions.threatened: She takes the threat like a dropped beat, answers in the flattest relay code she owns, and does not blink.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Rerouting mid-sentence, she offers a true small fact to cover the larger one she dammed.
reactions.authority_arrives: She measures the official by how fast the room's echo reaches him and where he chooses to stand.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder settles something in her; everything moves, her creed says, and she almost thanks the ship.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She snaps that water tells you who moved it, and the named one never once touched her line.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She admits no route exists, then does not leave, because someone must be last out of the water.

npc.description: Ibein-Sethenne sits on the tank rim with a signal-relay open across her knees, its wires laid out in the exact order she'll close them, as if the room's doubled echo required her to be tidy. She wears a knotted cord at the wrist, old enough that the route-pattern has worn smooth in the middle.

lore.name: The gauging chain
lore.description: A brass chain hangs from the rim into nothing, links flattened and re-flattened by decades of the same thumb, each link stamped with a depth nobody now can check.

content.name: The Tank Housing of Long Account
content.description: Sound arrives twice here — once raw and once delayed by a full breath, off the curved gold wall — so a dropped tool keeps its own echo as company. The tank housing opens into a dry well of fused quartz panels and spun mineral wool, water-stained to mid-height in a tide-line of old gold. Half the floor is wet no longer: something large lived in the water and has lately gone, and its absence stands in the room like furniture. Stenciled above the line: WATER LINE MARKS THE OCCUPIED LEVEL.

npc.name: Nozlost Raedaerekov
npc.voice: Slow, liturgical, prone to addressing the work rather than the listener.

open.says: It sealed itself, before there were seal-makers to be older than — the notation on the deepest wall is a record of the sealing, not an instruction for it, which means the ones who wrote there arrived after and mistook the scar for a door. I have handled the closure itself. It is not construction and it is not growth; it is the ship refusing a room the way a body refuses a splinter, and it happened before the Tabard had a middle to keep stable. The seal-makers built their order around a wound they believed they had made. They were pilgrims at it.

choices.text: Thank you. I will carry it carefully.
The ship refuses rooms. What else does it refuse?

greet.says: Mind the cold seam. It has opinions about being touched, and I have not finished disagreeing with them.

choices.text: What sealed the chamber — and when?
Keep your strata. I'll leave you to it.

probe_a.says: Grief, mostly. Graphite takes an impression and keeps it — you pack it against whatever you want remembered, and it forgets nothing, forgives nothing. The salt beneath it is the opposite: it swallows shape. Between the two, we negotiate with what the column wants to become.

probe_b.says: No one living. The work order predates my grandmother's grandmother, and it names tools we no longer make. I answer to the column, not the council — the column noticed its own wound before any of us did. That is the whole of my authority, and it is enough.

probe_c.says: The cold has moved. Fourteen paces, over a season, toward the sealed galleries — and cold does not walk, down here, unless something is metabolizing it. I have stopped entering my findings in the ledger. The last mender who entered hers was invited to stop filing.

reactions.grief: The trowel keeps moving; his mouth finishes a prayer to no stratum at all before admitting he heard anything.
reactions.shock: Overshares obscenely — the notation, the salt, the wound — because description is the only place he can hide from what he saw.
reactions.bribed: Looks at the offered gold as at forged leaf, tells the giver that graphite keeps impressions, and the giver should remember that.
reactions.accused: Stops mid-stratum, graphite dust drifting from both hands, and repeats the accusation once, softly, like testing a false seal.
reactions.flattered: Flushes at the praise like a man unused to visitors, agrees to far too much before recalling his order disbanded.
reactions.questioned: Answers as though reciting from the deepest stratum, unhurried, addressing the column as much as the questioner.
reactions.threatened: Considers the threat with the patience of a mason reading grain, then names aloud what the cold seam does to hands.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Does not amend the falsehood; simply keeps packing, voice thickening into liturgy until the contradiction drowns.
reactions.authority_arrives: Bows toward the intact flank, not the official, citing jurisdiction of the floor over anyone's writ.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Lays one palm flat against the open strata, whispering to it as a healer would, though his shoulders betray fear.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends the named culprit with a rehearsed calm that cracks exactly once, at the word culprit.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Admits his powerlessness plainly, then keeps talking anyway, mourning, listing what the column cannot spare either.

npc.description: The heat sits in the floor and refuses the column entirely — cold pours off the opened half like water finding a lip, though nothing here burns. Nozlost Raedaerekov is elbow-deep in packed graphite, packing it in strata with a mason's patience, and gold leaf older than any calendar flinches at the disturbance.

lore.name: The Column's Inner Tally
lore.description: Inside the opened half, each stratum of packed graphite is scored with fine grooves — a count, kept in the column's own body, of something it performed. The deepest grooves are worn smooth by grooves laid after them, meaning the tally was already ancient when the salt above it was laid down, and the salt was laid by hands who believed they were founding it. Whoever sealed the column sealed over a record older than their word for sealing.

content.name: Mliashizdslav's Unattended Column
content.description: The warmth is wrong-footed: it pools at ankle height where the floor should be coldest, and abandons the opened half of the column entirely, as though heat were a tenant still paying rent on only one address. Gold suffuses everything — not gilding but saturation, salt and graphite both blushed with it. Half the column lies open like a dissected thing, its strata exposed and still adjusting. Nozlost Raedaerekov straightens from the work, visibly recalculating your existence. Stencilled along the intact flank, in a hand older than the stencil: OFFERINGS ACCUMULATE ORDER DISBANDED. The room's silence has a floor you cannot find.

npc.name: Xeumeanos Xealphorakis
npc.voice: Clipped, procedural, a Continuant's grammar of custody — everything is either sealed, pending, or unaccounted-for, and she does not speculate where the record does not.

why.says: Because a cell that stands empty in Jupiter's hall gets understood as vacant, and vacant gets reassigned, and reassigned gets forgotten. I don't hold with forgetting mid-wall. The Continuants keep what sustains the generation — well, this mica was somebody's generation. It finishes or it stays pending on the record. Pending is honest.

choices.text: What's it like, working this far up in the court's ground?

greet.says: Mind the clamp line. This billet's pending — half-press is structural until it's finished, and I don't finish other people's presses. Billet seals at shift change, but this one's been pending longer than my rotation. State your business or stand clear of the glass.

owner.says: Unaccounted-for. That's the word the writ uses and the word I'll use. Forty-one nights tallied on the girder, and I'm not scrubbing them off — the tally belongs to the billet now, same as the press-marks. Rind registry shows the cell allocated, says nothing about to whom. That's not my ignorance to fill.

choices.text: Why rebuild a billet nobody's living in?

scale.says: You learn to size yourself against the girder pitch and nothing else. These bays could hold the whole green deck stacked twice over and the judgment floor beyond them held more seats than the Nave has people — you feel it in your knees the first week, then you stop, because you have to. Whoever sat at that table wanted the room to say something about them. It still does. We just can't hear it.

choices.text: I'll leave you to the press.

reactions.grief: The custody grammar fails her once: she says the name aloud and lays a palm flat against the mica.
reactions.shock: Clamp-line distance is as close as she lets herself get, and she makes herself look anyway, because unrecorded is worse.
reactions.bribed: She names the offer out loud, once, so the room holds it, and gets back to the clamp line.
reactions.accused: The vacuum-clamp goes down harder than procedure asks; her denial arrives in full registry format, every rotation accounted.
reactions.flattered: She thanks them the way she signs receipts, and keeps her eyes on the hands doing the praising.
reactions.questioned: Registry terms serve her answer, rotation by rotation, and she stands where the tally on the girder can be read.
reactions.threatened: The threat of reassignment lands where it must: she keeps seating mica, but the sheets go in crooked.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Whatever she said, she stops saying it, and the correction goes back through her record like a warped lamina re-pressed.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction gets its honors; she reads the presented writ upside down and notes which seventh-cell paragraphs go unquoted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Before her own footing, she checks the seventh cell, because an unfinished wall is the first thing a shudder claims.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Whether she likes the name or not, she won't co-sign it; the record convicts first or not at all.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: A yes she cannot manufacture; what she gives instead is a promise — the plea entered, pending, under her own name.

npc.description: Xeumeanos Xealphorakis works the frame of the seventh cell with a vacuum-clamp, seating mica sheet by sheet, pausing after each to listen to the billet as if the wall might dispute the fit. She has cleared nothing away — the abandoned press, the tally-marked girder, all of it sits where its owner left it, and she works around it with the economy of a person who has decided the arrangement is correct until told otherwise.

lore.name: The Half-Pressed Mica Wall
lore.description: The unfinished billet's mica sheeting is keyed to a hand other than Xeumeanos's — the press-marks are fine, left-fingered, patient. Under the last pressed sheet, scored into the girder in notation older than any stencil on this level, someone has tallied shifts: forty-one marks, then nothing. The billet was being claimed by someone who kept count of their own nights here, and stopped between the forty-first and the forty-second.

content.name: Veleus's Bulkhead Billet
content.description: The floor gives first: black glass underfoot, fused and rippled like something poured and abandoned mid-cooling, and each cell of the honeycomb sounds a half-step different when crossed, so a person learns to hear their own progress home. Sixty cells rise in the girdered wall, each a billet for one, and all of them are finished except one — the seventh down, where someone's layered mica sheeting stops mid-wall, its violet laminae unpressed, its cot unmade by nobody. Along the girder above the door, in stencil fresh enough to flake: BILLET SEALS AT SHIFT CHANGE.

npc.name: Vorozozd Nengostich
npc.voice: Clipped, institutional, softened at the edges by years of talking to one person who is no longer here. Corrects herself when she says something warm.

away.says: Away. That's the whole of what I write down. Eleven years is a long rotation of kettle-fills for someone away, but the room stays warm and the name stays chalked, and that is continuity too. Don't ask me to justify it to an audit.

board.says: Every repair since before I took the wardenship. Thirteen columns because a room does thirteen things or it isn't a room. Read it if you like — it's honest, which is more than the terminals can say lately.

choices.text: Ask what she means about the terminals.

greet.says: This room is mid-repair and let. If you're here about the stove, the stove is spoken for. State your business and mind the open wall.

choices.text: Ask why she sleeps on the floor.

sleep.says: The bed is not mine to sleep in. It's kept made for the room's tenant, who is away. I'm the warden of record and I keep the record. The floor is fine. I've slept worse on duty.

repair.says: Felt backing was rotting behind the slate. I do the work myself — a room should be kept by the hand that knows it. The Wards sends crews, but crews fix things to a standard, not to a person.

standard.says: The council's standard. Fine for corridors. But this room held a marriage, and a crew with a checklist doesn't know what that means for where a nail goes. Factor Solen would understand, if she had time. She doesn't.

terminals.says: The new postings read strange. Motif indices out of order, tellers posting at hours the tellers don't keep. I chalked my worry in the govern column and left it there. Whatever's moving through the Tabard these weeks, it isn't asking the Wards first.

reactions.grief: Keeps stirring a kettle that isn't lit, and says the name once in a register no audit has heard.
reactions.shock: Stands in the doorway of the open wall and counts until the number comes out different twice.
reactions.bribed: Declines in audit phrasing, then quotes the one price that would move her, and calls it a joke.
reactions.accused: Goes still against the bedframe and asks whether the accusation is entered formally or only spoken.
reactions.flattered: Meets the compliment with a fault count from her own log, as if praise were an audit error.
reactions.questioned: Answers in column order, thirteen items, and waits for the next question without offering one.
reactions.threatened: Hears the threat land somewhere behind her, on the chalked name, and answers only about herself.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Repeats the false entry verbatim, as though the slate will back her if she says it slower.
reactions.authority_arrives: Directs the official to inquire at the stove, then hears herself and starts again, smaller.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The kettle swings and she has it by the handle before the shudder ends, name checked second.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Before the name finishes, she has the repair log open to a dated column that puts them elsewhere.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says no in full procedural form, then keeps talking, eleven years of reasons spilling past the no.

npc.description: Vorozozd Nengostich wakes on the second creak of the floor, sits up against the bed, and takes stock of you before speaking. A Continuant uniform shirt, sleeves rolled, collar gone soft from washing. One hand rests on the slate board as if it might need defending.

lore.name: The Ledger of Small Repairs
lore.description: A slate board hung inside the curtain, ruled into thirteen columns, one per verb. Every fix in this room is chalked and dated in the same careful hand going back decades — hinge, kettle, curtain-ring, the stove moved twice and moved back. The last column, dwell, has one entry: a name chalked in and never scrubbed out, though the date beneath it is eleven years old.

content.name: Curtained-Room 15
content.description: The bed sits a hand's width from the stove, closer than any fire-warden would allow, and the ceiling slopes down until a standing person must bow to it. Half the room is opened to the studs — slate wall-pieces stacked, pressed felt rolled and tied. The other half is kept like a shrine: navy cloth folded, kettle hung, a stencil over the curtain-rail reading ROOM TO LET, INQUIRE AT THE STOVE. Vorozozd Nengostich is asleep on the floor beside the bed, not in it.

npc.name: Vyeshamana Vibozhaer
npc.voice: Liturgical and literal at once, with long pauses where a reading of the room should be — sentences that treat silence as a material to be worked.

bell.says: Taught? No one alive. It was already obedient when the first knot was tied. We do not ring it because ringing is a demand, and this place makes no demands. It lowers its voice the way you would lower yours at a sickbed — the whole deep is a sickbed, if you must know, and recovering.

greet.says: Mind where you stand — the bell is declining, and what is declining prefers not to be jostled. You came breathing like the upper decks. It will take the room a while to accept your noise.

choices.text: The bell dims itself. Who taught it that?
What are you counting with that stick?
They say something below has been answering. Do you hear it here?

tally.says: I count the hush. There is a number to it — the same number, every turning. I have notched it four thousand times and the total has never moved. Do you understand what that means? It means the room is patient on a scale I am a rounding error in. It means I am the variable.

signal.says: Hear it? My teeth have heard it. The bell dims a fraction early now, on no schedule the foil predicts — as if something deep in the keeping has begun to nod back. We wrote RESPONSE OBSERVED on that yoke long before I was wound into this work. The mechanism stayed unknown. The response did not.

choices.text: Observed — by the bell, or on the bell?

observed.says: Yes. That is the correct question, and I have carried it four thousand turnings without an answer that holds weight. The old ones painted it as a warning. I have begun to think it was a confession — theirs, not the bell's. Stand quietly. You may be the thing being observed.

choices.text: Then I'll be quiet about it.

variable.says: Because Saturn counts the tales, and someone must count the counter. Maintenance is meaning, Walker. Even the meaningless tally. Especially the meaningless tally — that is where the creed stops being comfort and starts being true.

choices.text: Even a count that never changes.

recovering.says: From being looked at. The tally does not change, the bell does not finish, the middle does not move — and still it mends. What do you call a thing that heals without being tended? I call it by no name. Names are upper-deck currency. Here we pay attention.

choices.text: I'll leave the bell to its courtesy.

reactions.grief: The tally-stick rises out of habit and then simply stops, their hands unable to say what a death counts as.
reactions.shock: For the first time in four thousand turnings the total moves; they watch their hand mark what no hush authorized.
reactions.bribed: The offer is let drop the way the room drops sound, unfiled, unacknowledged, beneath the dignity of any response.
reactions.accused: For once they answer the questioner and not the bell, and the voice that arrives is small, unpracticed, new.
reactions.flattered: For one unguarded instant the praise pleases them, and a mark is notched afterward in penance for the pleasure.
reactions.questioned: Answers arrive only after the pause they reserve for the bell, the question rerouted through hush before meaning is granted.
reactions.threatened: They apologize to the room rather than the threatener, because fear in them has only ever been about noise.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, they continue notching the unchanged total, as though arithmetic were an alibi the room might countersign.
reactions.authority_arrives: They bow first to the half-light and second to the official; jurisdiction, for them, sorts by proximity to the bell.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: When the hull groans they look up — truly up — murmuring that the patient may at last be turning over.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The answer comes too fast for someone who trades in pauses, loyalty outrunning liturgy before the hush can vet it.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea is heard to its end before they gesture at the yoke's flaking letters, where their office stops.

npc.description: Vyeshamana Vibozhaer stands at the bell's foot with a tally-stick of iron, notching marks that never change total, lips moving around numbers in an order only the stick understands. Foil has been wound into the creases of their knuckles until the hands themselves look kept, maintained past reason. They do not look up when spoken to; they look at the bell's half-light, and answer it.

lore.name: The Diminished Bell
lore.description: The bell is not rung; it lowers its own brightness, minute by minute, in increments the eye registers as devotion rather than mechanics. Wound foil is spliced into its clapper — a repair so old the foil has grown into the iron, and the splice matches no pattern in any Rindwalker knot-book. Someone taught this bell restraint, and the bell has been obeying longer than anyone can count the obeisance.

content.name: Thesovo
content.description: Light here declines before it arrives — a courtesy, as if the dark had agreed to receive it and the glow, understanding the terms, enters slower than it should, pooling like breath held for someone else's sake. The crowd presses in past any sane capacity, shoulder to wound-foil and iron, and their numbers make no sound the ear can file; the room eats noise the way deep water eats names. Overhead the great bell hangs mid-hush, mid-dim, and every pilgrim reads its half-light as a sentence not yet finished. Painted along the bell's yoke, in letters flaked to almost-nothing: RESPONSE OBSERVED MECHANISM UNKNOWN.

npc.name: Bas the Ice-Flagged
npc.voice: Terse, transactional, allergic to staying. Talks like everything is on a timer, because here it is.

greet.says: Half-hour turn starts when you sign. Chalk's on the sill. Don't touch the mount — it holds because it's never been asked to hold anything else.

ask_scope.says: Fixing the sky so it can't move without us noticing. The Braid wants the positions before the next turn ends. So do you, if you're smart. Sign or leave.

reactions.grief: Keeps logging until the entry comes out as the dead one's name, then scrapes the felt with a thumbnail.
reactions.shock: Looks once at the body and back at the felt, and the next three numbers come out wrong.
reactions.bribed: Asks the amount, writes it in the chart margin, then crosses it out and says the numbers stay true.
reactions.accused: Sets the chalk down whole and slow, something nobody in the loft has seen, and asks who sent them.
reactions.flattered: Times the flattery against the turn and tells the speaker exactly how many minutes of sky it cost.
reactions.questioned: The answer comes minute by minute, without their eyes leaving the felt, and costs the asker nothing.
reactions.threatened: Asks whether the threat ends with the turn or follows them down the stair, and the chart trembles.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Goes quiet long enough that the draught is audible, then names a higher price for the true version.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door stencil gets recited word for word, and the official's half-hour starts at the same rate as anyone's.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Stops mid-number and marks the felt where the shudder caught, because the sky held still, so the room moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Offers every late arrival in the accused's sign-in history, unasked, and does not pretend this is neutral.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says plainly that nothing up here answers that need, then writes down who can and what they charge.

npc.description: Bas the Ice-Flagged sits wedged between the scope and the wall, chart in one hand, chalk in the other, writing star positions onto the white felt overhead. They don't look down when the door opens.

lore.name: The Drift Ledger Scope
lore.description: The scope's mount is not original. Someone bolted it to a salvaged plastic base and cut notches into the rim — one for every night the loft was open, Bas says, going back nine years. The notches stop short of the newest arc by exactly one. The missing notch lines up with the night the last mythograph posted late.

content.name: The Scope Loft of Third Watch
content.description: The scope stands a hand's width from the wall — too close to swing, so the whole loft is built around the angle it can't take. Bright white felt lines the ceiling, taped at the seams with salvaged plastic. A draught comes through the floor grate. Stenciled by the door: SCOPE BOOKED IN HALF-HOUR TURNS.

npc.name: Kroveslava Nitsyn
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, a woman whose sentences are ledger entries. Faith expressed as shift discipline — what continues, she keeps.

box.says: Came down from the Factor's office with the new vat, all in one delivery, which tells you the vat wasn't decided here. We didn't ask. Continuity means somebody upstream is doing the asking for you. Now let me work — Nine's due a second skim before the strip dims.

greet.says: Stir before you leave, or don't leave. The account runs to the day and I don't backfill for strangers. You want a look, look at the box — it's the only thing in here that's honest.

choices.text: The printed cards — where did they come from?

reactions.grief: Midway through the news her logging stops, and Nine runs a full pass unrecorded for the first time in years.
reactions.shock: She stands in the drain-side doorway with the rod still raised, and Nine's second skim goes overdue behind her.
reactions.bribed: The offer hangs a beat too long before she gives it the answer she gives bad batches.
reactions.accused: She stops counting mid-vat, which for her is a scream, and asks to hear it said again.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads to her like a tampered card, and she asks what it costs before accepting any of it.
reactions.questioned: Questioned, she reads dates off the pinned cards, hour by hour, and is back at Nine before the visitor finishes.
reactions.threatened: Her answer stays level, but the rod knocks twice against the rim before she can stop it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The card contradicts her; she reads it twice, then says the true date aloud, quieter than anything else this shift.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her count goes audible the moment the official crosses the threshold, every number spoken like a tithe.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Nine's surface registers the shudder before she does, and her card has no column for it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Three cards come out of the box already flagged, dated weeks back, and she reads them out without comment.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She cannot alter what the Factor's office sends, and says so twice, the second time almost gently.

npc.description: Kroveslava Nitsyn works two vats at once, wand in one hand, tasting rod in the other, without looking at either. Her apron is continuant slate gone stiff with dried algae at the hem, and she logs each stir on a card pinned to her sleeve rather than walk to the box. She has spoken to you already with a nod and a tilt of the rod: *you're not taking a card's worth of anything.*

lore.name: The Long Account Card-Box
lore.description: Index cards, one per vat per shift, going back past anyone's grandmother — the same hand recording the same stir, decade on decade, in navy ink. The newest card is different: printed, not written, with a column nobody's card before had — BATCH LINEAGE — already filled in down forty rows in someone else's typing. Kroveslava's own cards stop mid-month. Whatever the printed ledger is feeding upward, it started taking over the account before the new vat arrived.

content.name: The Algae Vat of Long Account, Terrace 257
content.description: Something moves before you do — a skimmer arm dragging green scum off Vat Nine, slow as a milk-paddle. Nine glazed-brick vats crowd a floor meant for six, and every gap between them holds crates, wands, and a navy-painted card-box gone rusty at the corners. Six workers stir, taste, log. Over the drain, stenciled twice: STIR EVERY VAT BEFORE YOU LEAVE. A seventh vat, still shrink-wrapped, sits where the door was supposed to open.

npc.name: Sambaibeem al-Jaihami
npc.voice: Careful and exact. Names materials before people. Pauses to check a word the way they check a seam.

open.says: Because the ship does not stop needing hands, and someone has to be those hands when it is their turn. That is the whole of it, as the Walkers teach it. You mend, you store, you make, you pray, and you do not ask the hull to love you back. The city thinks we are superstitious tunnel-folk. Let them. The lights stay on either way, and they will never know it was a trade.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll think about that.
A trade. That's a cold way to pray.

greet.says: Careful where you step. The resin is still tacky and I just laid that sheet.

choices.text: Why lead sheet on a new floor?
This floor is new. What happened to the old one?
Why do you fix things for people who never thank you?
Sleep well. I'll let myself out.

probe_a.says: Lead takes the mold's shape and forgives the hand. Resin holds it after. Two materials, one pour. You learn which one argues.

probe_b.says: Cracked crucible. Full rebuild, down to the subframe. I was off-shift when it went and I have not stopped being angry about the timing since. A floor should fail from work, not from luck.

probe_c.says: Sevin walks through when she can, and the menders after her. But the first check is mine, and the last is mine. The council audits paperwork. A bell either rings true or it does not.

reactions.grief: Grief arrives as a scheduling problem, and it takes them three tries to say the person's name.
reactions.shock: What they do first is look for the fault line, a spoiled pour's habit, and the shaking starts after.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets priced out loud, down to the coin, and then they name what their name would cost.
reactions.accused: They ask to hear the charge twice, the way a doubtful seam gets re-checked.
reactions.flattered: Their arms stay crossed while they repeat the praise back, word for word, like a measurement taken down.
reactions.questioned: Questions about their movements get answered in work order — resin, lead, light — with pauses to check each fact.
reactions.threatened: Whether the threat outranks the pour schedule is the only question they ask, hands flat on the bench throughout.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The correction costs them a full breath, and they make it anyway, eyes fixed on the accuser's face.
reactions.authority_arrives: They rise from the cooling shelf too fast and salute with a resin-stiff hand, ready to be counted.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Their knuckles whiten on the ladle while a number gets muttered over whatever moved the room.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The defense they offer is pure inventory — shifts worked, metals poured — and not one kind word survives.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea outruns their hands, and they say exactly that, then stand a long time by the unfinished molds.

npc.description: Sambaibeem al-Jaihami is asleep in the cooling rack, head on folded arms, a foot above where the bench ends. The floor is clean, the molds are set, and nothing here has a mark of use on it yet.

lore.name: The Tuning Wedges
lore.description: Beside the molds sits a rack of copper wedges, each cut to a different length and stamped with a number. They are not tools for the pour. They are driven into a bell's rim while it cools, to pull its note up or down. The highest numbers are the most worn. Whoever works this floor tunes bells by hand, one strike at a time, until the note is true — and one wedge, the thinnest, has been ground down and rechucked so many times it is half its stamped size. It has kept one bell honest for years.

content.name: Tjathragghelm's Pour Floor
content.description: The ladle hangs a hand's width above the crucible channel, too high by half for any pour. Sunlight cuts through the doorway across a floor still sticky with spilled resin. Draughts stir the smoke-stained walls. The lead sheeting on the near bench is bright, unbent. Stencilled by the molds: MOLDS SET, DO NOT POUR ALONE. Sambaibeem al-Jaihami sleeps on the cooling shelf.

npc.name: Nolana Krosttyalich
npc.voice: Writ-cadence. She answers in the language of procedure, and when procedure fails her, she goes quieter, not louder.

open.says: I copied two of them before re-addressing, which is a dismissal offense, so weigh that. They were homes, specific homes in this ward — listed with their regard-flows charted and then a word in the margin I've only ever seen in old doctrine: withhold. Brannet flagged the same pattern in restitutions. Payments and care routed around certain houses, cleanly, like someone decided in advance which dwellings were going to stop being lived in. The gap at my desk isn't a reassignment. Nobody leaves a registry. They're being taken out of it.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry this carefully.
You copied them. That frightens me.

greet.says: Registry's open. If you're filing, take a form. If you're not, stand clear of the drafts, they curl the buckram.

choices.text: Who do you answer to, exactly?
What did the sealed folios say, Nolana?

probe_a.says: Brannet's. He handled restitutions. Got reassigned — that's the word they used. His folders were half-done and nobody above me has claimed them, which is not how the registry works. Things get claimed. That's the whole point of a registry.

probe_b.says: The ward office, then Factor Solen, then the writ itself, in that order of usefulness. Solen signs what reaches her desk. What doesn't reach her desk, I've stopped asking after. There's a class of report that goes up in sealed folio and nothing comes back down.

probe_c.says: A dispute heard on its Tuesday with its witnesses present, entered so a stranger in forty years could pick up the thread. Continuity isn't a sermon, it's a filing habit. I've watched people mistake it for the other thing and it's cost them.

reactions.grief: She asks which form covers it, and when told there isn't one, she starts closing Brannet's folders anyway.
reactions.shock: She notes the hour for the report, by the stopped clock, and the pen knocks against the desk.
reactions.bribed: She declines in the language of forms; misremembering is an amendment, and amendments need her signature.
reactions.accused: She asks them to enter the charge in writing, and the second time her voice is thinner.
reactions.flattered: Praise that is not entered anywhere costs nothing, she says, and thanks them in the flat register anyway.
reactions.questioned: She gives her movements by the half-hour, addresses for witnesses, and the page number where each is filed.
reactions.threatened: They say her name the way the margin said withhold; she goes still and looks at Brannet's chair.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she stops denying and starts dictating the filing number of the thing she swore she never copied.
reactions.authority_arrives: She stands, gives her name for the record first, and asks to see the writ of jurisdiction.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The room moves; she pins the loose pages under both forearms and waits, counting, before she looks up.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They name Brannet; she corrects them like a filing error, citing a reassignment paper she has never seen.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to help, she takes their name down in full and enters it where the record cannot lose it.

npc.description: The registry pen of Third Watch has stopped mid-word, ink pooling on a dispute form nobody signed. Nolana Krosttyalich works alone at a desk sized for two, the second chair pushed against the wall with its cushion still dented. Someone's half-finished filing stands in buckram folders, navy spines stenciled DISPUTES HEARD TUESDAYS, BRING WITNESSES, and she has not touched a page of it.

lore.name: The sealed rider file
lore.description: Under the counter, wedged where the ledger should sit, is a dispute file with its rider sealed in blue Continuant wax — the wax Factor Solen reserves for findings too hot to circulate below her level. The rider's tabs run the length of a tenement block: every unit, every rent dispute from the past year, cross-filed not by tenant but by staircase. Someone was mapping pressure in the building — who owed whom, where it would break first — and stopped at the stairs leading down to the freight level. The last tab is blank except for a date three days from now.

content.name: The Registry Desk of Third Watch
content.description: The pendulum clock on the writ-wall has stopped, and nobody has touched it. A rent desk of navy-painted buckram faces the door, half a dispute file still open under its enamel weight, the chair pushed back at the angle of someone who left mid-sentence. Stenciled above the shelf: DISPUTES HEARD TUESDAYS, BRING WITNESSES. The draught from the stairwell lifts the loose pages — Third Watch papers, filed to a case number two days early.

npc.name: Tuna-Ione
npc.voice: Quick, looping, always circling back on herself mid-sentence — a trader's cadence applied to sealant and joints. Measures everything in time saved or time owed.

open.says: Mercury's, or close enough that it doesn't matter. I ran a relay splice up the signal artery last season and saw the archives — everything that moves on this ship gets written down, every packet, every body, every knot of cord, and it's been going on longer than there have been people to write about. The trunk hums because it's being read. Your route, my graphite, the wind in here — all of it logged somewhere below us that nobody this high has ever stood in. I stopped feeling watched and started feeling counted, which is worse.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll carry it carefully.

greet.says: Hold the rail or hold still — graphite doesn't wait and neither does the trunk. You want something, ask it while my hands are busy.

choices.text: That notation — where does it actually come from?
Work on. I'll leave you to it.

probe_a.says: Seals the joint where the trunk flexes — every time the ship breathes, this wall moves a finger's width, and graphite forgives it. Wool holds the heat, graphite holds the motion. You learn which material owns which problem or you learn nothing.

probe_b.says: Nobody sends me, that's the point — the work circulates and I circulate with it. A job comes down the Braid, I take it, I pass what I learned down the line to whoever holds this trunk next. Nothing stays mine, not even my mistakes.

probe_c.says: Because leaving is the creed, not the accident. You finish a room, you mark what you used, you walk. Though — these weren't marked the way we mark. The notation's older. I've been working around it for a month and it doesn't match anything I was taught.

reactions.grief: She starts tallying seasons of barter with the dead and cannot find where the sum ends.
reactions.shock: Her trade betrays her — she reads the wound like a failed joint, noting where it gave, until her hands shake.
reactions.bribed: Asked to misremember, she catches herself asking for the offer in writing, then slides it back across the rail.
reactions.accused: Her looping cadence stalls; she recites her last four watches, then hears the fear underneath her own arithmetic.
reactions.flattered: Flattery gets priced inside its first sentence, though it lands warmer than she'll admit, and her hands keep working anyway.
reactions.questioned: She keeps packing the joint while itemizing her hours, redundantly, for an archive that already holds them.
reactions.threatened: The threat lands as arithmetic; she prices staying against running before her face agrees to show nothing.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught, she reprices on the spot, trading the lie for the truth like correcting an invoice, and never apologizes.
reactions.authority_arrives: Her eyes go to the stenciled sign before the official's face, checking which rules are about to be enforced.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She counts the flex by habit — finger's width, two — and stops counting when the number outgrows graphite's forgiveness.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She talks over the accusation, listing the small debts the accused honored, overspeaking because being wrong about people frightens her.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She offers what her trade holds — wool, sealant, a boiled kettle — and hears how small the inventory sounds.

npc.description: The light here refuses to settle — it comes down the trunk in gusts, silvering and dimming like breath on a spoon, and Yarys works inside its rhythm, feeding packed graphite into a wall-joint with the patience of someone caulking a hull that will outlive her. Spun mineral wool hangs in unspun batts from the gantry above, and the stencil on the trunk-plate reads CATWALK TENANTS YIELD TO TRUNK TRAFFIC, though the only traffic in years has been wind.

lore.name: The Tenant's Tally Rail
lore.description: Notched into the catwalk railing itself, in someone's knife-work: a running count of everything that has passed through the trunk below, kept in bundles of ten — six thousand bundles deep, the notches wearing smoother the older they get. Whoever cut them learned the trunk's rhythm well enough to tally in the dark between light-pulses, each mark one breath long. The last bundle stops at four, mid-row, the knife's angle changed as if the hand was called away — and beneath the final notch, small as a signature: a knotted-cord glyph, cut over and re-cut so many times the metal around it is proud with wear.

content.name: Yarys's Catwalk Tenement
content.description: The light here does not fall; it passes — a silver wash pulled trunk-ward every few seconds by whatever breathes below the floor grating, so that the spun mineral wool bedding and the packed graphite packed into every seam seem to take turns existing. Forty meters of catwalk carries a household: three bunks gantried off the trunk wall, a kettle, a curtain of stitched salvage, and a stenciled admonition — CATWALK TENANTS YIELD TO TRUNK TRAFFIC — which the tenants have framed with copper wire like a joke kept too long. Wind-scour has polished the railing to a shine the hand trusts before the eye does. Two figures stand mid-argument among it all, and stop.

npc.name: Brunbrand Vahylf
npc.voice: Slow, exact, fond of counting. Doubt arrives as arithmetic.

end.says: Mind the bin rim on your way out. It takes knees.

rule.says: A reading is a question you ask of something that does not answer twice the same way. If it did, it would be arithmetic, and you would not need me. One spill, one reading. After that you are asking yourself.

apron.says: Dalla's. She did readings here eleven years, then stopped mid-apron and walked a tunnel I do not walk. I keep it where she left it. She has not come back for it, and I have not finished it, and that is the whole of what I know.

greet.says: One reading per visitor. That is the rule and I keep it. Sit, though. I have barley to sort and no reason not to talk while I sort it.

spill.says: Grain is grain. It falls how it falls. But lately the same shapes come up — the gap, the lean, the cluster at the rim. I wrote it on the board because writing makes it a record and not a worry. Then I stopped writing. Both of those were cowardice, in different directions.

choices.text: What do the shapes mean to you?

meaning.says: Nothing. That is the doctrine — nothing, until a visitor gives it a question. But I notice the shapes strongest on days I do not want to be here. So either the grain knows me, or I know the grain, and I have given up deciding which is worse.

reactions.grief: A tunnel, an apron, eleven years — they give the messenger all of it, far more than was asked.
reactions.shock: They keep sorting spilled grain through all of it, both working hands moving, neither one deciding to.
reactions.bribed: The offer gets counted aloud, twice, and both sums land on something they cannot take.
reactions.accused: All four hands stop at once, and the count they were keeping will not come back.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads to them as a second reading, the kind the stencil forbids, and earns no thanks.
reactions.questioned: Answers come in counts: three sacks moved, two spills read, one apron untouched, and the sum closes clean.
reactions.threatened: Their eyes go to the bin rim, the one that takes knees, and stay there while they agree.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The corrected number arrives half a beat late, repeated once as if the first attempt never happened.
reactions.authority_arrives: Dalla's apron goes under the counter before the official clears the door, quick work from hands that never hurry.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The grain in the dish shifts, and for the first time in years they decline to read it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The accused's last three visits, each timed to the minute, come out of their memory like a defense nobody requested.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The one-reading rule gets explained twice, as if repetition were a kind of mercy.

npc.description: Brunbrand Vahylf sits behind the bin, sleeves rolled, sorting spilled grain into a cracked dish with two of their four hands. The other two rest on a half-strung leather apron that is not theirs and does not fit them. They have not touched it in a while.

lore.name: The Count Board
lore.description: A slate hangs inside the bin lid, tallied in chalk: reads given, readings matched, days. Under the last column someone stopped mid-number and wrote, small: same spill every third visitor since the dimming. The tally has not been resumed.

content.name: Oracle Stand
content.description: The reading stool sits a hand's width from the grain-bin, too close; anyone seated knocks the rim with a knee. Sacks of resin-hardened barley crowd the ceiling down to shoulder height. A stencil on the bin lid reads ONE READING PER VISITOR, NO REPEATS SAME DAY. The air smells of boiled leather.

npc.name: Riaciyoza the Thrice-Forgotten
npc.voice: Drift-bred: everything phrased as transit, nothing owned, sentences that pack up and leave mid-thought. She names things by what they do, never what they are.

open.says: Counting, yes. Toward, not down. The chamber lies through the Voronoi deep — take every cell that narrows, never the one that widens; the widening cells are its breathing, and you don't walk into a lung. The deep honeycombs for maybe nine days' walk, and at the center of the foam the cells stop being rooms and start being one room. It was pointed out to me once by the notation on the walls, and I have regretted knowing which way ever since.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll take the narrowing cells.
You regret it? That unsettles me.

greet.says: Mind the open side. It doesn't like being breathed on, and neither do I, this late.

choices.text: Who writes in that register, if no one does?
Why pack up mid-repair? Doesn't that bother you?
What's the strangest thing you've handled down here?
The marks — are they counting down to something?
Don't let me keep your satchel waiting.

probe_a.says: Salt keeps score. That's all a register is — a medium that remembers pressure. The marks are honest; it's only the authorship anyone invents. I've stopped asking whether someone is writing or whether the room simply refuses to forget.

probe_b.says: Everything I mend gets undone on a scale I can't bill for. A Driftworker learns to love the interval — the knot before the unknotting. What bothers me is that this repair was ordered finished by something that never filed a name. You answer to no one long out here, or you answer to something worse.

probe_c.says: A casting, once, whose grain matched the register's marks. Same hand, if hands are the right word at all. I sold the comparison along the Braid and bought silence with the proceeds — the wisest trade of my career.

reactions.grief: The road she kept them on in her head closes; the name leaves her once, a destination with no route.
reactions.shock: She freezes mid-fold, cloth open, unable to say what the thing in front of her does, so it goes unnamed.
reactions.bribed: She asks first what the offered thing does, then declines to carry it anywhere, including away from here.
reactions.accused: For once her sentences stay put; she stands owned in one place, hating how much stillness resembles guilt.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands on her like the salt's nightly marks, and she notes the pressure, declines the authorship, keeps packing.
reactions.questioned: She gives her account as passage rather than presence, going, never being, every stop a thing she passed through.
reactions.threatened: By what it does she names the threat, a door shutting early, and holds her transit evenness by main force.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The contradiction lands; she keeps talking, tacking on tides nobody asked about, one sentence trying to outrun its witness.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction enters and her hands find the satchel straps, settling her instruments the way one settles witnesses.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Movement without destination undoes her worst; she goes to the salt at once, needing a mark that witnessed it.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She starts recounting what the salt would and wouldn't score, faster and fuller than she has spoken all day.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: The plea outruns anything knowing can do; she offers a route where rescue was asked, and hates the exchange rate.

npc.description: Riaciyoza coaxes the last of her instruments into a satchel with the tenderness of someone putting children to bed, though the register beside her — half-flayed, its basalt face opened like a dissected animal — receives no such affection. Compact salt glitters in the wound of it, still accreting marks no hand has made.

lore.name: The Register's Broken Quire
lore.description: A half-slab of compacted salt, cracked open mid-entry, its pages of crystal showing the marks continuing *through* the break — the record unbothered by its own fracture. Riaciyoza has indexed three months of entries and found that every ninth line, without exception, drifts a hair's-breadth toward the same vector, and that the drift deepens as the entries near the present. Whatever writes this register leans, nightly, a little further toward the lower aft through the Voronoi deep — as if the chamber it serves were pulling on it, gently, like sleep.

content.name: Authorless-Register 33
content.description: Light arrives here the way tidings arrive — already old, already elsewhere — crawling the basalt in bands that lean, all of them, toward the lower aft, as if the room were tilting toward some appointment it will not name. The register's slabs of compacted salt stand half-opened, their interiors gleaming green-black, and the marks inside accrue in no hand at all: entries the salt remembers without being told. Where the seal is broken you can watch a line inscribe itself, patient as frost. Stencilled above the unlit half: ENTRIES ADDED NIGHTLY SCRIBE UNKNOWN. A worker folds her tools into cloth by the threshold, unhurried as one leaving a room she expects to outlast her.

npc.name: Hatl-Kikan
npc.voice: Unhurried, wry, allergic to sentiment but loyal to gossip. Answers questions with better questions unless something's worn through.

line.says: Grandmother tied most of it. Rule on this boat: you don't untie a knot you didn't tie, and you don't add one unless you mean to stay. I've been meaning to stay for twenty years. The boat finds that funny — it's still here and so am I, which is more than any Drift is promised.

choices.text: Why did you stay, when your kind moves on?

stay.says: Because everything moves, but not everything has to be carried. Some things you moor and tend, and that's a route too — one place, walked daily. She'd have called that heresy. I call it the shift I never finish covering.

braid.says: Already did, first night. That's the part I don't tell the family: I asked before I was worried, which means I was worried before I admitted it. Nothing comes back. Nothing going out is free either — favors spent on quiet ports don't refill themselves.

greet.says: Mind the mats, they're the only floor this boat has. You're not ward census — I'd know. Sit, there's nowhere worth standing anyway.

choices.text: Ask about the knotted line by the bunk.

leave.says: Shut the hatch behind you. The smoke knows the way, but the cold doesn't need inviting.

shift.says: My cousin's. She ran cargo up-spin and didn't post when she'd be back, which with her is a way of life, not an accident. Someone has to keep the lantern lit or the whole mooring knows we've gone soft.

choices.text: Does she usually go quiet this long?

worry.says: Longer than I like, shorter than I'll say out loud. The Braid hasn't carried her name in nine days. Nine days means nothing, or it means everything, and I've stopped pretending I know which. That's the honest cost of a floor that only lives if things move through it — sometimes it's your people moving.

choices.text: Could you put out word through the Braid?
Change the subject — the knots on the line.

reactions.grief: Keeps talking through the shift rota until the sentence thins mid-word, then ties a knot nobody asked for.
reactions.shock: At the sight of the body, their hands for once have nothing to hold.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the offer costs the giver, because nothing going out is free, and waits for the lie.
reactions.accused: Laughs once, wrong-sized, then names every mooring line tended this month instead of saying no.
reactions.flattered: Hands them the wrench that fits nothing and waits to see if the praise survives the weight.
reactions.questioned: Returns every question with a better one and checks the wrist knots like a ledger.
reactions.threatened: Measures the distance to the ladder and stays seated, which costs more than the threat deserved.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: For once no question comes back; they study the mica in the matting and recut the lie smaller.
reactions.authority_arrives: Strips the lantern at half speed until jurisdiction learns whose room it is.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Watches the lamp swing longer than the swing lasts; the boat has joked before, and this isn't a joke.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Comes armed with gossip about where the named one really was, too fast and far too invested.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says plainly what they can't untie, then spends a favor they'll miss, and hates the arithmetic.

npc.description: Hatl-Kikan sits amid a half-dismantled lantern, sleeves rolled, a wrench that doesn't fit the work still in hand. Their wrist cord carries more knots than the mooring line does.

lore.name: The mooring line
lore.description: Coiled at the bunk's foot, a line knotted end to end in patterns nobody on the Nave ties anymore. Route history, the Drift way — this family came up from the spinward markets three generations back, and the knots still say so.

content.name: Ward 44 Spinward
content.description: Felt mats give underfoot, gritted with mica that catches the lamp when it swings. Bunks, crates, and a stove crowd a berth built for half of it; smoke finds the hatch or nowhere. Stenciled over the ladder: MOORING DUES POSTED FIRST OF THE MONTH.

npc.name: Reir-Veinagl
npc.voice: Blunt, sparing, the cadence of someone who measures words the way they measure weld — only what holds. Speaks of the ship as a body they are personally indebted to.

greet.says: Pods are numbered and none of them are yours, so sleep standing if you sleep here. I'm behind on the count and Mars doesn't wait on hospitality.

choices.text: The count on the girder — it goes past the sealed bays.

reactions.grief: Says the name once, then talks too long about the dead one's pod number and who inherits it.
reactions.shock: Looks at the body like a weld that should have held, and does not speak at all.
reactions.bribed: Prices the offer against what the ship is owed, finds it short, and says so in one word.
reactions.accused: Asks, once and quietly, which seam failed, and the second pair of arms goes still before the accuser answers.
reactions.flattered: Somewhere behind the visor a vain old welder glows, and they smother it by asking what needs fixing.
reactions.questioned: Gives the account like a weld log — bay, hour, seam — without looking up from the filament.
reactions.threatened: Lets the threat finish, then asks for its requisition number, because on this ship everything else carries one.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught on the count, they repeat the wrong number once, correct it flatly, and offer nothing after.
reactions.authority_arrives: The door gets no greeting beyond the finished welds angled toward it, the torch still lit.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Stops the feed mid-bead, head tilted, listening to the girder the way a doctor listens to a chest.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names three ways the accused couldn't cut a seam straight, which is the closest they come to taking a side.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Hears the plea to its end without interrupting, then recites the waiting list by heart instead of answering.

npc.description: Reir-Veinagl sits half-inside an open pod, feeding filament into a hand-welder with the unhurried economy of someone who has done this ten thousand times, and the second pair of arms — because there are two pairs — holds the seam steady without being asked. The look turned on the player is not hostile, only accounting: one more body in a nest already past its count.

lore.name: The Tally-Girder
lore.description: One girder at the nest's heart has been kept bare of wool for its whole length, and along it, in hull-notation, someone keeps a count — pod by pod, name by name, struck through and rewritten as the population swells. The oldest marks are burnished into the metal itself, worn glossy by a thumb that returned to them nightly. The bottom of the column is the strange part: the count does not stop at the pods in this nest but continues past them, numbering bays that were sealed before anyone here was born, and the hand that wrote those is older and slower than the rest.

content.name: The Girder Nest of Last Call
content.description: The heat sits high, pooled under the girders where the welding runs, while the floor stays cold enough that the chalk-white mineral wool has gone stiff with it — you stand between the two without either touching you. Pods of drawn filament hang off the lattice like wasp-work, each numbered in stencil, and the stencil has been painted over and re-cut so many times the numerals stand up in relief. The latest pods have been welded into bays meant for machinery, and the machinery has been moved somewhere to make room. Something here was built for a handful and is holding forty, and the welds have been told to agree.

npc.name: Naisanail al-Jaimani
npc.voice: Terse, procedural, speaks in the vocabulary of the work — marks, seams, what a sail owes the wind. Warms by one degree when the work is respected.

mend.says: Everything is mending that's honest about itself. I make a panel, the wind unmakes it, I mend it, twenty years later someone else mends my mend. If that offends you, take it up with the cloth.

choices.text: Fair enough. Keep your solder dry.

work.says: Cutting. Sailcloth, tarpaulin, anything the decks need hung or squared. You don't scissors a panel before it's chalked — the stencil means it. Cloth remembers a bad cut longer than you will.

choices.text: Whose cloth is this, that it can't lie flat?
You mend more than you make, don't you?

cloth.says: Table's borrowed and the wall isn't. We've been cutting in the corridor all month, which nobody will say is a scandal but everyone marks. The beams go back up and the room rights itself. Things here get put right. That's the whole of it.

choices.text: And when it's put right — where do you go?

greet.says: Mind the open floor. We're rehanging the rack beams and I don't need you under them. Looking for work or looking for gossip?

choices.text: What is this room for, exactly?
Why close a cutting room mid-repair?

leave.says: Down the tunnels, where you don't get to follow without a reason and someone vouching. Nothing personal. The corridors belong to everyone; the tunnels belong to whoever knows them.

choices.text: Understood. Good luck with the beams.

closing.says: Rack beams. The old ones sagged — you'd see it in every panel that came off this table, a finger of bow along the selvedge. We noticed. That's most of the job, noticing.

reactions.grief: They say the name twice, then talk too long about the dead one's first seam, voice level, hands not.
reactions.shock: One look and they sit down on the stacked planks, uninvited, the counting gone out of them.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer aloud against what their name earns and hand it back without heat.
reactions.accused: They set the tin down harder than the work needs, repeat the charge once flatly, then deny it.
reactions.flattered: They warm one degree at the praise, then wait, unhurried, for the ask they know is coming.
reactions.questioned: They give where, when, and how long, nothing volunteered, and go back to counting sticks into the tin.
reactions.threatened: Their eyes stay on the offcuts until the threat finishes, then they look up and take its measure.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They hold the first story one beat too long, then correct it the way a bad line gets re-chalked.
reactions.authority_arrives: They answer while watching the pried floor planks, sure the official will mark the disorder before anything else.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They know settling from failing and name this one a failing seam before anyone thinks to ask.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They weigh the name like cloth under tension and allow that its owner lies badly, nearly a defense.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They say plainly what they cannot mend, then stay anyway, hands quiet on the borrowed table.

npc.description: Naisanail works with a steadiness that says the packing is the end of a long day, not a long career — solder sticks counted into a tin, each one slid to the same depth. They answer without looking up until the second question.

lore.name: The marked bolt
lore.description: One bolt of sailcloth on the shelf carries a full set of chalk lines already cut and sewn over in copper thread — a panel that was marked, cut, and then kept whole anyway, presumably for its pattern.

content.name: Naehunwy
content.description: The cutting table sits nearly touching the far wall, close enough that a bolt of sailcloth can't lie flat across it — the table was moved and the wall was not. Half the room is opened up, floor planks pried and stacked, bone-colored cloth baled and waiting. A stencil on the doorframe reads CHALK LINES ONLY, NO SCISSORS TILL MARKED, worn to near-illegibility. Naisanail al-Jaimani is wrapping solder sticks in offcuts, nearly done.

npc.name: Shyslonmari Arogenes
npc.voice: Precise, inventory-minded, thawing only when a question respects the work. Speaks of the hall's emptiness as a supply problem, never a grief.

empty.says: Because nickel keeps and bread doesn't, and we are sworn to keep. Every tray in that aisle is a service held in trust for a congregation that will come back — continuity is not a hope, it is a logistics discipline. Wipe the dust and it would serve tonight. That is the point of it.

greet.says: You'll excuse the state of it — service paused, storage overtaking. This isn't my shift; the roster thinned and someone must set the tables, so I set them. What brings a stranger past the green decks?

choices.text: Why store all this in a dining hall?
Whose shift was it, before you covered it?

domain.says: You've felt it already or you wouldn't ask — the ceiling too far, the tables too many, the sense of a judgment hall built for tenants who never came to dinner. The old ones hold this ground; I have walked to the far wall and back and it did not once acknowledge me. We keep it anyway. Keeping is what we are for.

choices.text: Let them finish setting the tables.

roster.says: Three names deep, now, and each of them mine to cover until the council rules otherwise. The last steward went down-rind on a maintenance writ and the writ never closed. I set the places in her hand's habit, not mine — a table set wrong is a small rupture, and we do not begin them.

choices.text: Does anyone rule over this place at all?

reactions.grief: They tell the nearest table before they tell you, then cannot remember which tray their hands were holding.
reactions.shock: Their gaze inventories the room out of habit and fails halfway down the aisle, the count gone wrong.
reactions.bribed: Bribery gets filed under perishables: what is offered cannot keep, and neither, they decide aloud, can the offerer.
reactions.accused: The fork they were straightening goes down crooked for the first time in years, and they leave it lying.
reactions.flattered: Praise lands where the hall never reached them, and they despise how readily their spine straightens toward it.
reactions.questioned: Their alibi arrives in the cadence of a stock-take, quietly pleased that someone finally wants a tally.
reactions.threatened: They answer menace as procedure, asking whether the threat is formal, written, filed, already counted somewhere.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Slower, in exactly the same cadence, they repeat the false figure once more, as if repetition were provenance.
reactions.authority_arrives: They go to the door and hold it level, presenting the hall the way one presents a ledger.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The trays outrank their own footing; they steady the stack first and only then admit the room moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They leap to the named culprit's defence the only way they can, itemising everything that person has kept.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Unable to grant the plea, they offer instead a place set and kept, which is all their office holds.

npc.description: Shyslonmari Arogenes moves down the tables resetting places nobody will use, straightening each fork to a line an inspector could run a finger along. The shift sash is a Continuant weave in the wrong colours — borrowed, and they wear it like a debt. They talk to the tables more readily than to you.

lore.name: The Headcount Board
lore.description: At the hall's head hangs a slate ruled for a thousand names, wiped and rewritten so many times the nickel beneath has gone thin as foil where the rag passes. Every column stops mid-generation — attendance tallied faithfully, then a gap, then a different hand resuming with fewer names. The last entry is a single line in a careful, lonely script: served one.

content.name: Common Service
content.description: The tureens should be steaming; four hundred places sit chalk-white with graphite dust and not one cup moves. Long tables of annealed nickel run out past where the eye can count them, gantried overhead like the ribs of some upended hull, and the stencil on the nearest gantry still reads TABLE COUNT FIXED, ATTENDANCE VARIES. The room was built for a service that comes and goes — what it holds now is stored: crates in the aisles, sealed trays stacked to the second rail, a pantry become a warehouse. Nothing here has been eaten in a long while.

npc.name: Verdeko Yezdshayei
npc.voice: Liturgical plainness gone slightly wrong — service words used for measurement, measurement words for prayer.

count.says: Hours of service, we assumed. But the count runs ahead of any hour I've served, and lately — lately it runs ahead of itself. Warmth precedes the hour. Perhaps the hour is coming to be preceded.

greet.says: Mind the impression. It is still warm, and warmth here is not weather. You stand where something kneeled — or was knelt, the grammar hasn't settled.

shift.says: Ainsel's. Ainsel stopped coming. Not left — stopped, the way a note stops and the chord holds anyway. I log the tensions so the interval has a witness. Witness is most of the rite, when the celebrant is elsewhere.

choices.text: The notation under the foil — who wrote it?
I'll leave you to the log.

mantle.says: For? We say warming, but the word is a loan. It pre-heats the hour. Before service there must be readiness, and readiness must be made of something — this is the something. The rite nobody performs still needs its stove lit.

choices.text: The notation under the foil — who wrote it?
Say nothing. Touch the warm impression.
