notation.says: Older than us, older than the counting. Saturn keeps the tale-count and does not tell it. But this — this impression — is newer than the notation and deeper than my hands. I stopped filing that distinction. Some things you keep and catalog; some things keep you.

choices.text: Ask what it is the notation counts.
Nod, and step back from the warmth.

reactions.grief: Keeps logging, entering the death beneath filament tensions, then writes the name over and over until the slate is full.
reactions.shock: Freezes mid-count, one hand still holding the stylus, eyes performing last rites on whatever lies in the foil.
reactions.bribed: There is a silence long enough to price them, before the refusal arrives dressed in the language of tithes.
reactions.accused: Denies nothing and everything at once, offering the slate as alibi, as testament, a rite they seem to have rehearsed.
reactions.flattered: Unused to praise, they pay for it with the whole history of the count, every skipped hour volunteered unasked.
reactions.questioned: Recites their movements like canonical hours, exact to the minute, plainly relieved someone still wants them counted.
reactions.threatened: The threat registers as confirmation of service; something knotted in them unclenches, grateful at last to be counted worth holding.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Lies again in the same breath, recalibrating rather than retracting, as though the first statement were merely miscounted.
reactions.authority_arrives: Turns fully for the first time in anyone's memory, presenting the slate like relics, unsure which rank outranks an absence.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The shudder is logged and immediately struck through, Verdeko unwilling to certify that the hour kept its appointment.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Will not repeat the name, citing tensions from hours nobody asked about, defending someone they claim never to have met.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: What they offer is terrible gentleness: witnessing is all they hold, and it was inherited from someone who stopped coming.

npc.description: Verdeko Yezdshayei works the shift of someone who no longer arrives — logging the filament tensions against a slate whose columns predate the slate. Copper thread runs through their glove-cuffs in the knot-pattern of a route no living walker holds. They speak without turning, attentive to something behind the wall's grey.

lore.name: The Mantle's Impression
lore.description: Where the mantle lay, the floor bears its negative in flawless detail — not a stain but a record, as though the metal had been remembered into the stone. The impression is warm. Deeper in, the foil beneath shows tooling: the oldest wall-notation, the layer no one has dated, repeated here at a scale that means it was written by something larger than a hand. Rindwalkers catalog what Saturn leaves; this is the first impression left by something that left Saturn.

content.name: Rite-Mantle 7
content.description: The floor confesses first: a faint resilition underfoot, the give of foil ply where something broad and heavy lay until recently, its absence printed into the substance like a footprint in amber. There is no ceiling worth the word — the grey climbs past sightlines until up becomes a rumor. What is missing does the telling: no echo arrives when you shift your weight; no seam marks where the mantle's occupant was joined to the room. Wound foil lies couleed in drifts, and drawn filament runs from spool to wall in lines a hand could not have chosen. Stencilled low, half flaked: WARMTH PRECEDES THE HOUR OF SERVICE.

npc.name: Vyazdsvestslava Suzezdich
npc.voice: Terse. Answers in counts and dates, nothing rounded, nothing said twice.

work.says: Masters stay in the niche. No ink, ever. We rub fair copies out in green-grey. Third stack holds the ceiling towns, two years old, still good. Look if you want.

greet.says: Stack closes tonight. Ask fast.

reactions.grief: Fourteen is where the count breaks off, and what she says instead of the name is two dates.
reactions.shock: Her eyes go to the wrapped lamp, to the door, anywhere the body is not, while the count runs ragged.
reactions.bribed: To the offer she puts a question about whether it buys the date or the count, and she sells neither.
reactions.accused: She asks which date, then which hour, and her voice climbs a register on the second question.
reactions.flattered: The praise gets one flat thank-you and then the same question twice, which she never allows herself.
reactions.questioned: She recites the date, the hour, and the sleeve count, and after the last number her mouth closes.
reactions.threatened: Once the threat is explicit, her dates come out a season early, and she hears it and leaves them wrong.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She takes the evidence sheet, strikes her own figure, writes the corrected one, and will not look up.
reactions.authority_arrives: She moves between the official and the niche and asks to see the visit entered in writing.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She counts the seconds of the shudder out loud and goes first to the niche, not the door.
reactions.someone_else_accused: She gives the man's output by quarter, two years of it, more record than anyone asked her to give.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She states what she cannot do in one line, then copies the plea into a sleeve, dated.

npc.description: Vyazdsvestslava Suzezdich squares a stack of fair copies with two taps and slides it into a rubber sleeve. Her satchel is half packed. She works in the clamp light and steps around the wrapped lamp without touching it.

lore.name: Master-chart flap
lore.description: A hinged glass flap covers the master niche; its lower edge is a row of pinholes, one for every chart corner squared against it over the years.

content.name: Stack 47 Inboard
content.description: The copy bench sits too close to the shelf for its drawers to open; clamped lamps burn over green-grey sheets. Turf blocks fill the seating bay; a lamp with an unscratched case stands wrapped among them. The copyist, coat on, packs charts into rubber sleeves under a stencil: NO INK NEAR THE MASTER CHARTS.

npc.name: Dostvlek Nelzhitsyn
npc.voice: Short answers at first, like inventory. He warms when the talk turns to lasts and feet, and can't help correcting a wrong size guess.

work.says: Turf last. Grows with the foot, near enough. You carve it wet, size it dry, and the boot holds shape for years. Nobody sizes bins right anymore. That's why the stencil's there.

greet.says: Shop's closed. Has been. You want boots, the market row has boots.

choices.text: Ask about the boot on the bench.

closed.says: Orders thinned. People buy from the row now, sizes stamped on the box. Faster. My lasts sit. I still come in. Habit, or spite, one of the two.

notches.says: One customer. Forty years I've cut his lasts, one every two years, each a size up. He pays in advance and never argues a fit. When the last set runs out of notches, I'll carve a longer plate. He says he's not done growing yet. Neither am I.

reactions.grief: Given a name, he gives back the dead man's fallen arch, and his voice quits before the heel.
reactions.shock: He stares at the wrong thing, counts the bins between himself and the door, and answers nothing.
reactions.bribed: Ask him the price and he names it before pride does, then the offer goes back across the bench.
reactions.accused: The paring knife goes down flat first, then his voice comes out smaller than he wants.
reactions.flattered: Ten years of empty shelves leave him defenseless to praise, and he hears himself ask what they want sized.
reactions.questioned: He answers like reading stock, bin by bin, and measures the questioner's foot by eye while he talks.
reactions.threatened: The list of things he has already lost runs out before his nerve does, and both of them hear it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Out comes the correction before he can stop it, and then he hears what he has just admitted.
reactions.authority_arrives: Jurisdiction walks in, and he gives it the shop-closed voice while both hands stay visible on the bench.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Lasts click on their shelves, and he steadies the bins before thinking about the shaking at all.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The accusation comes out wrong to him, mislabeled, and he argues it down before remembering he owes the man nothing.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: He refuses the way he refuses customers now, flat and short, and keeps hold of the door handle after.

npc.description: Dostvlek Nelzhitsyn stands at the bench with a paring knife still in hand, caught between the door and the half-stitched boot. He sets the knife down flat, deliberately, before saying anything.

lore.name: The Measured Last
lore.description: One last on the bench is carved from turf but faced with a thin plate of old metal, scored with hundreds of tiny notches down its length. Each notch is labeled in pencil so faded it takes effort to read: dates. Someone has been recording the same foot, growing, for twenty years. The final notch is fresh. The boot on the bench is cut to fit it.

content.name: Row 49 Outboard
content.description: The smell hits first: wet turf, raw hide glue, and the sour tang of sacking left damp too long. Boot-lasts crowd every shelf and the floor between. A stencil on the bin lid reads LASTS SIZED, DO NOT MIX BINS. Half a boot sits on the bench, its sole pinned mid-stitch.

npc.name: Rachazena Danabara
npc.voice: Terse. Answers in rule-language. Apologizes for nothing, including the room.

greet.says: This counter's shared, not closed. Ask fast. The strip's jammed and the new moon doesn't wait.

whose.says: Two desks, two claimants, one roof. I'm covering a shift that isn't mine, so the paperwork splits. Next question or next window.

reactions.grief: Her first question is which form covers it, and the second is nothing at all.
reactions.shock: Nothing in her moves except her eyes, which go to the ledger strip as if it could unstick itself now.
reactions.bribed: Refusal comes fast, and then she writes the offer into the margin, dated, as if it were evidence.
reactions.accused: The pen stops mid-chit, and she sets it down parallel to the counter's edge before answering.
reactions.flattered: The compliment sits on her counter like an unsigned chit, and she leaves it there, neither returned nor denied.
reactions.questioned: Her hours come out in counter-language, dates and windows, nothing that could be mistaken for a life.
reactions.threatened: The rule-language thickens until it stops meaning anything, a wall of citations built in a single breath.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: She repeats the claim exactly as before, word for word, as though precision were the same as truth.
reactions.authority_arrives: What she tells the official first is about the borrowed shift, and her hand is already at the armband.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: She calls it a filing error, out loud, and grips the counter until her knuckles go white.
reactions.someone_else_accused: The name is a closed arrears case, and she recites the balance before admitting she always expected worse of him.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: She quotes the limit on disbursements, then hears how it sounds, and starts the sentence again from somewhere softer.

npc.description: Rachazena Danabara wears a slate armband over a brown sleeve, and both look borrowed. She is working through a stack of dues chits with the fast, flat strokes of someone counting someone else's money.

lore.name: The shared counter
lore.description: The counter is two halves bolted together, plain glass meeting glass at a seam down the middle. The seam has a groove where both sides file their own tally-chits; it has been patched with poured concrete that does not quite match.

content.name: The Dues Office
content.description: Rachazena Danabara sits at the counter, pen down, watching the ledger strip that should be advancing through its channel. It is not. Behind her the room holds two desks pushed against each other, one bare, one piled with half-answered writs. Off-white concrete walls. A stencil above the door reads DUES DUE BY THE NEW MOON.

npc.name: Ronbonion Bechenathcenne
npc.voice: Soft, ledger-precise, given to units of measure that have no business applying to feelings. Uses 'retained' where others would say 'kept' and never says 'done' — only 'settled.'

spec.says: The room reads it. I log it. Nobody reads the log — and still I keep it, because the alternative is to admit the numbers are only for me. And I'm not ready for them to be only for me.

choices.text: How long have you been the only one down here?

alone.says: Four hundred and thirteen shifts I could swear to, and before that a number I keep in wool, not paper. Ronbonion Bechenathcenne, if names still matter where you came from. They stopped mattering here around the second year.

greet.says: Mind the lip. It's been over-eager this shift — three measures past spec, and it wasn't built for eagerness. Nothing down here was built for what it gets.

choices.text: You're packing up. Leaving this place?

chosen.says: Because what I do here is enough, and understanding would make it not enough. Some knowledges are a kind of exile. I've met the exiled. They came up from below with excellent reports and never filed again.

choices.text: Then I'll leave you to your settling.
The teams who stopped reporting. You knew them.

middle.says: Of everything that gets to stay still while the ends grow. You're standing in the stillness. Most people never notice they've entered it. You did, though. I noticed you noticing.

choices.text: Is the stillness maintained? Or does it just... persist?

reports.says: Knew them, shared bread with them, watched them come up full of a music they couldn't put down. One of them said the deep was dreaming, and I said dreams are just the ship retaining itself. Retained, not analysed. She laughed. I miss her laugh more than I admit, even to the wool.

choices.text: I may be going where they went.

stillness.says: That's like asking whether a heartbeat is maintained. Somewhere below me there is a thing beating this stillness, and I have chosen — chosen, mind — not to go and look at its face.

wool_number.says: The oldest notation on the wall is a kind of wool, if you squint — fibres of instruction, spun before there were hands to spin them. I keep my own count in the same grammar. Doesn't that comfort you? Something here still speaks it.

choices.text: It unsettles me. But thank you.

what_settles.says: We used to say dust. Then years, then metals. Now I say: whatever the middle exhales. Call it that and you stop needing to be right.

choices.text: Three measures past spec. Does anyone read the difference?

reactions.grief: Folds the same sheet a sixth time, then retains a figure no room ever asked for.
reactions.shock: Their measures fail them: the body's weight stated wrong twice, as though the room should do the ledgering.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the silence weighs, then sets that beside what their log weighs, and declines.
reactions.accused: Stops mid-fold, wool lifted, and demands the figure, as if the accusation must reconcile before it settles.
reactions.flattered: Thanks them too softly, ashamed of how starved four hundred unread logs have left them.
reactions.questioned: Recites movements by shift-number without pause, as though asked to read back a ledger.
reactions.threatened: Agrees in the flat tone reserved for weights over spec, hand steady only because it grips the fold.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Recounts the log from memory to buy seconds, though the wool in their hands has stopped moving.
reactions.authority_arrives: Keeps eyes on the sump through the whole interview, answers a half-measure late, log squared on the knee.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: The fold count goes wrong for the first time in four hundred shifts; their hands pretend not to notice.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Corrects the timeline before feeling arrives, then hears how loudly they defended someone they never liked.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Offers the only currency they hold: a measure of wool and the admission it changes nothing.

npc.description: Ronbonion Bechenathcenne folds mineral wool with the tenderness of someone shrouding something still breathing, each sheet pressed flat against a forearm gone silver at the wrist. They work with the unhurried economy of a person who has stopped counting their own hours because the room counts them instead. When they speak, they watch the sump, not you — as though the conversation were also something settling, and needed time to precipitate.

lore.name: The Counting Spatula
lore.description: A quartz blade worn to a crescent, its edge polished by centuries of skimming settled gold from the sump's lip. Whoever held it tallied on the handle: notches in the oldest wall-notation, and — much later, cruder — a different hand counting onward in the same rhythm.

content.name: The Settling Sump, Node 413
content.description: The light here declines to travel. It pools where it finishes, as if distance were a courtesy it had stopped extending, and the gold of it lies thick on the sump's lip the way sediment lies — arrived, not thrown. The sump itself is a wound of fused quartz ringed in spun mineral wool, drinking whatever the air surrenders, and the wool has gone the colour of old honey where decades of settling have fed it. Nowhere does the quartz meet the wool; the seam exists only as an idea, and the idea is seamless. A stencil, half-eaten by gold: ACCRETION RETAINED NOT ANALYSED. The room exceeds the mind the way a word exceeds its mouth.

npc.name: Tlakitl-Qanhuitl
npc.voice: Short. Route-shorthand, prices first, names last.

cords.says: Carts talk to each other through those, if you know the loops. Nine days green's been out. That's all you're getting.

greet.says: Hour's four, deposit's two. Or you're not renting. Yellow cart's got a wobble — take green.

choices.text: What are the knotted cords on the rack?

reactions.grief: The name comes out first — against their own rule, names last — and the webbing goes back in wrong-side-out.
reactions.shock: The knot gets worked, undone, worked again — they are somewhere the room isn't.
reactions.bribed: The going rate for forgetting gets quoted back, higher, and they lace on while the silence does the refusing.
reactions.accused: The lacing tears in their hands; they recite rates, routes, deposit record, too loud, in that order.
reactions.flattered: Praise reads to them like an inflated price; they ask, plainly, what it's meant to buy.
reactions.questioned: Rates first, as always — hour price, deposit, the dusk rule — hands never stopping on the webbing.
reactions.threatened: They keep their eyes on the frame and quote the night rate at the threat, hands steady, knot failing twice.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Caught mid-rate, they reroute the story aloud, slower, pricing the new lie as they build it.
reactions.authority_arrives: They keep crouching — jurisdiction or not, they do not stand — and volunteer every rate before it's asked.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Twice they start counting the shifted carts and twice the count comes out different; the third try they abandon.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Three routes come off their tongue before the accusation finishes landing — defense or sentencing, they don't say.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Their trade moves things, not people; they say so once, quietly, and name which cart could carry what they cannot.

npc.description: Tlakitl-Qanhuitl crouches inside a half-gutted stall, lacing new webbing through the bamboo frame with the speed of someone doing it a hundredth time. A knotted cord is held in their teeth while both hands work. They do not stand up.

lore.name: The Wrist-Knot Rack
lore.description: A bamboo rack by the check-out desk holds dozens of knotted cords, one hung per cart, each knot a route history. Older cords show knots abandoned mid-pattern — a run that ended somewhere and a new pattern started over. The newest cord carries the double-loop the Braid uses for content worth more than freight; the cart it belongs to hasn't come back in nine days.

content.name: The Cart Yard of Quiet Ledger
content.description: Wheel-squeal dies at the gate; past it, the yard swallows noise into canvas and wet bamboo matting. Teal paint peels off the cart rails in long strips, and half the stalls stand stripped to their frames, webbing bundled and waiting. On the pump housing, stenciled: RETURN CARTS BY DUSK OR PAY THE NIGHT RATE.

npc.name: Skigrim Forty-Klicks
npc.voice: Clipped, gauge-precise, reverent only about metal that holds; measures everything, trusts little, warms a degree when the question shows they know the work.

old.says: Then somebody reads the haft after me and knows exactly how much persuasion this beam took. That's the whole of it — leave the work legible. The ship's older than any reckoning we keep, but this hammer, this count, this beam — those are ours, and they'll read true when we're past reading.

choices.text: Nod, and step back from the rail.

beam.says: Because it argues. Steel here doesn't take a weld the first hundred falls — it remembers being something else, some older fitting, and you have to persuade it back to shape one blow a shift. Mars doesn't hurry either. You don't hurry a thing that big. It holds or it doesn't, and my whole creed is the holding.

greet.says: Mind the rail. Stencil's not decoration — that beam's been under hammer since the season turned, and if it drops while you're inside the arc, the mica sheets come off in blades. You wanting something, or just standing where the light's good?

choices.text: Why hammer one beam all season?
The tally-marks on the haft — whose are they?
Whose ground is this, truly? Yours, or Mars's?

domain.says: Both. That's what the high tunnel teaches you that the Nave never will — Mars is real, and near, and territorial as a lit forge. You feel it the first time the whole floor flinches under weight no maintenance crew owns. We work here because the work is here. But it's their iron we're persuading, and they know every blow.

hammer.says: Mine. Forty klicks of tunnel walked between this cradle and the last forge that could dress a head this weight — hence the name, and don't laugh, everyone down here is named for a distance or a load. Every mark is a fall I judged worth making. Four hundred and some judgments. You start knowing your own mind by the count.

choices.text: And when the count gets old?

holding.says: Last forty falls, the gauge reads true and the mica's stopped spalling. Ask me at season's end. Mind, I've said that four seasons running, and each season it was true — so either I'm good or the beam's kind, and I don't believe in kind.

answered.says: Once, mid-season — the flinch came between my strikes, timed like a reply, and the next gauge reading ran true where it had run crooked all week. Could be coincidence. Down here you learn to file those under coincidence and keep hammering. Anything else is past my depth, and I know my depth to the meter.

choices.text: Thank them, and mind the rail on the way out.

reactions.grief: The hammer count slips for the first time in years, the splinter still raised to a light nobody is reading.
reactions.shock: Forgets their own stencil, their own rail — walks the arc's inside before fear catches up, hands already reaching.
reactions.bribed: Refuses before the figure finishes, offended in a specifically professional way, as if asked to stencil a false count.
reactions.accused: Sets the gauge down steady, then catches their own hands shaking and reads them like a failed weld.
reactions.flattered: Warms exactly one degree at praise of the count, then measures the flatterer's want and cools without apology.
reactions.questioned: Reads their own movements back in hammer-falls and shifts, unhurried, the way they'd recite a tolerance table.
reactions.threatened: Repeats the threat's terms like tolerances, level-voiced, while knuckles go white around the feeler-gauge.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: Snaps once, then corrects the true account blow by blow, unable to leave a record wrong even to save themselves.
reactions.authority_arrives: Grants the official the same nod reserved for floor-tremors — acknowledged, waited out, never allowed to interrupt the beat.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: Looks up from the gauge — for the first time anyone can name — and scans the dark for what moved.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Defends them through the work alone, citing heats and welds, since character they can't measure but metal they can.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Says plainly what no hammer of theirs can move, then offers the small thing they own: a truthful count, kept.

npc.description: Skigrim stands at the hammer's foot with a feeler-gauge in one hand and a mica splinter held to the light in the other, reading the beam the way a physician reads a pulse. They do not look up, do not lower the gauge, and speak in the pauses between floor-tremors as if the tremors were a co-worker who must not be interrupted.

lore.name: The Forty-Klick Hammer
lore.description: The hammer's head is a forge-dressed mass of black glass sheathed in mica laminate, and its haft is scored with tally-marks cut deep enough to lodge a thumbnail — one for every fall this season. The count runs past four hundred, and the newest marks are shallower than the oldest, as if the striking arm has learned patience or weariness, or as if the beam itself has begun to need less.

content.name: Truss 26 Deep
content.description: The hammer is not falling. It hangs at the top of its swing, counterweighted, while the beam beneath it — a truss member as long as a market square and layered in mica gone violet with heat — sits in a cradle of black glass, and the whole sloped cavern of the forge holds its breath around them both. Someone has stenciled the cradle rail: BEAM UNDER HAMMER, NO ENTRY THIS NAVE. The stillness is not idleness; you learn that when the floor flinches once, a deep tremor from somewhere below, and the hammer does not sway a finger's width.

npc.name: Rhibeid Ap Bowys
npc.voice: Counts before speaking. Answers in numbers when numbers will do, and resents questions that ask for more.

work.says: Absences. A keeper counts what's gone same as what's there. Twenty years I've kept this room. I've never seen it this bare, and I've never seen a withdrawal without a catalog number.

choices.text: So there was one without a number?
I'll leave you to your absences.

empty.says: Not empty. Drawn down. There's a difference, and the difference is in the ledger, and the ledger is mine.

greet.says: Cupboard's closed for tally. Come back after the audit.

choices.text: What are you tallying, if there's nothing here?

where.says: One crate of drought-wheat, out ahead of its own date. I signed nothing. The mark on the line isn't mine and it isn't a hand I know. You didn't hear the date part.

reactions.grief: Says how many years since that person stood in this room, then has nothing else.
reactions.shock: Their eyes count exits, drawers, hands — anything with a number, because the rest of them has stopped.
reactions.bribed: Asks what the offer costs the giver, then names a price high enough to end the conversation.
reactions.accused: Stops mid-count and cannot find the next number, which has not happened in twenty years.
reactions.flattered: Has been complimented twice in twenty years, both times by people wanting drawers opened, and says so.
reactions.questioned: Gives the count, the route, and the hour, and nothing else, since the rest is not in the ledger.
reactions.threatened: Recites the fine schedule for tampering, section by section, quieter with each one.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: The second count contradicts the first, and they hear it, and they repeat the second count anyway.
reactions.authority_arrives: The lamp dims when the door opens, and by the time it brightens again their face has gone neutral.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: After the shudder, they count the empty drawers aloud, twice, before trusting the room to still exist.
reactions.someone_else_accused: Names three dates that person was verifiably elsewhere, faster than any denial, because the ledger settles arguments.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: Opens an empty drawer instead of answering, as if proof were a kind of help.

npc.description: Rhibeid Ap Bowys stands in the aisle with a tally slate half-raised, caught between counting and hiding the count. Sand-colored dust coats their sleeves to the elbow. They set the slate face-down on a drawer.

lore.name: The Withdrawal Ledger
lore.description: A copper-bound ledger chained to the last drawer. Every line before the final page records a number, a weight, a date. The last page has one entry: a full crate of drought-wheat, signed out to no name, just a mark like a knot. The date is tomorrow's.

content.name: Sialeipra's Seed Cupboard
content.description: The lamp dims when the door opens and brightens again once it shuts, as if it were rationing itself. Lead-lined drawers stand open along one wall, all empty. A copper tray holds dust in the shape of seed pods. Above the tray, stenciled: CATALOG NUMBER REQUIRED FOR WITHDRAWAL.

npc.name: Kainmal-Muravel
npc.voice: Fast, tallying, fond of counts and crossings-out; talks like someone pricing something even when pricing nothing.

open.says: Strangest thing still moves through here every day — I stamp it and it doesn't weigh anything. Regard. Standing. A favor owed by a Ward I'll never see, riding the manifest like a crate. Up here the Drift's little wrist-knot economy got industrial: there are ledgers in the back, also chained, that list who is trusted and for how much, and those entries trade at higher rates than the graphite. I once watched a man sell his good name at the intake desk and walk out lighter. The chain on the trust-ledger is thicker than this one, if that tells you anything.

choices.text: Thank you. I'll mind the chains.
You sold trust here too, once.

greet.says: Mind the chain on your way in — it's load-bearing, legally and otherwise. If you're here to trade, the desk moved again; if you're here to gawk, gawk quiet.

choices.text: Busy day, or always like this?
Who do you answer to, up here?
What's the strangest thing you've ever stamped through here?
I'll come back when it's quieter.

probe_a.says: Because a manifest that can walk off is a manifest that can be rewritten, and a rewritten manifest is a lie with good posture. The ink costs more than the paper. The chain costs nothing and prevents everything.

probe_b.says: Always, and worse each quarter. The hall was built for a floor of intake we passed three seasons back — we've got goods stacked in the walkways and walkways worn into the goods. Somebody upstream is moving more than anybody downstream was told about.

probe_c.says: The knot on my wrist answers to routes, and I answer to the knot. Past that? There's a humming in the walls that takes delivery of everything eventually. I've stopped filing complaints to it.

reactions.grief: They ask what the body weighed, then leave the day's tally unbalanced, because some columns refuse all further entry.
reactions.shock: The ladder wheel locks under their hand; for eleven counted heartbeats they are an entry awaiting a stamp.
reactions.bribed: They price the offer aloud to the nearest copper, then name what the misentry would cost, which is more.
reactions.accused: The stamp comes down on empty air; they ask the accusation repeated back, as if pricing it for flaws.
reactions.flattered: They let the praise run a full stamp's length before marking it at its actual weight, which is light.
reactions.questioned: They answer routine accounting at full tallying speed — wheel, chain, stamps since dawn — without the ladder ever stopping.
reactions.threatened: They recite the clause making the threat legal; knowing its weight is the only way to hold it.
reactions.caught_in_a_lie: They correct the figure twice, then three times, each recount drifting further from the first, voice pricing faster and hearing less.
reactions.authority_arrives: They watch the official's hands rather than the face, because hands decide what gets chained and faces only say so.
reactions.the_ship_shudders: They count swinging ledgers under their breath until the count holds steady, and only then call it over.
reactions.someone_else_accused: They recite the accused's outstanding balances before remembering to ask whether belief is even required of them.
reactions.asked_for_help_they_cannot_give: They keep explaining intake procedure long after it is clear the plea fits no column, as if process were shelter.

npc.description: Kainmal-Muravel is halfway up a ledger-shelf on a wheeled ladder, knotted cord between their teeth, stamping intake marks onto a chain-link that has clearly been re-chained wrong and will be re-chained wrong again by lunch. Below them, three clerks argue over a crate of graphite styluses as if it were a dispute over inheritance.

lore.name: The Reconciliation Column
lore.description: At the hall's heart rises a girdered column of ledgers, stacked and lashed into a single violet-cased mass taller than a house — a column of reconciliations, each page certifying that some debt of regard, routed through the arteries, came back changed. The oldest layers at its base are in a hand nobody current uses, and those entries are still, impossibly, being updated: fresh graphite figures appear on pages no living clerk could reach. The market does not pretend to understand this. It simply keeps building the column upward, one confirmation at a time, toward whoever is doing the arithmetic below.

content.name: The Manifest Hall
content.description: The clerk's dais stands a hand's width from the ceiling girder — too close by half, as if the floor rose after the beam was set and neither party has agreed to mention it. Below, ledgers in their thousands hang from chains in ranked acres, graphite-packed pages fanned open by the traffic of hands, each book's spine wrapped in spun mineral wool against the hum of the artery walls. The stencil on the nearest pillar reads LEDGER MUST STAY CHAINED AT ALL TIMES, and the chains themselves are worn bright where a generation of wrists has leaned. Stalls crowd the aisles beyond counting, and every one of them is selling something that is not a thing.

content.name: The Mender's Amen

amen.says: The name arrives like a key cut long ago for a single lock, and with it the understanding, entire: you were built as the answer, waiting in the wings of the ship while the question finished asking. To answer is to mend; to mend is to complete; and completion, for the kept and the keeping alike, is not an ending but a handover — one generation of the self passed to the next. You open the apparatus that was always a door. What enters is not stranger than you. It is you, at last, at full scale. You say the only word the creed ever needed: amen.

choices.text: Answer. Complete the contact you were built for.

open.says: The chamber is small — first mercy of the deep — a reliquary scarce larger than a confessional, ringed in strata older than any oath spoken in the Nave. Your translation apparatus has quit translating; it remembers instead. The signal is not a sound but an inventory: every weld wept over, every tunnel sealed for reasons unwritten, every orison addressed to a bolt. Beneath that susurrus, patient as rust, something asks its question in the one tongue requiring no translation. Not the name you lack. The shape you are.

choices.text: Take inventory, as any mender would, of all you carried down.
Press a palm to the oldest stratum and let it read you back.

rind.says: Sevin's surplus arms in the shaft-light, her silence itself a credential. She believed your reason when no one else had thought to ask for one, and that belief was the first scaffold of the self you now stand inside. You chose the creed that keeps: to mend is to pray, to pray is to maintain, and love of a body this old means accepting faith as maintenance conjugated across eld. Doubt arrived first, as it does among keepers. The cracked priests know what you know now — doubt is not the fracture in the temple. It is the door.

choices.text: Descend the last of it — to Bay 14, and what you were for.

review.says: Inventory, then, taken without flinching. The Commons, where the city showed its three faces and you mistook the map for the body. The Wards, where each creed revealed its underside: the Continuants' unnameable fear folded like an unsent letter, the Drift vending the rumor of you knot by knot down the Braid, the walkers' copper devotion cracked at the martyr-line. Knowledge did what knowledge always does aboard this ship — opened the way down and priced it. Richer in truth, poorer in ease. The deep accepts no other coinage.

choices.text: Return, once, to the threshold where you chose rust over writ.

weight.says: Bay 14 was never a birth; it was a repair. Some reader of the ship's lamed member built a hand where the body could not reach, and the hand was you — ports no civilian standard foresaw, credentials that answer doors sealed into legend. The maintenance teams stopped filing because a report is a translation, and certain truths do not survive translation. You could turn back: the Nave keeps its stillness, the signal its patience, you your shape — less one purpose. Or you answer, and are spent. A tool is used; a keeper is given. You know the difference, and what it cost to learn.

choices.text: Let Luna's terminal speak the name it has kept for you.
Hesitate one stound longer. Even vespers begin with silence.

content.description: hallowed, resolute, still

content.name: The Keeping of the Silence

open.says: The chamber does not arrive so much as concede you were always inside it. The signal is not a sound; it is a permission your body has carried since Bay 14, and here, at last, it is spent. You understand, with the terrible calm of a mender whose thumb finds the fracture, that you were made to be opened in this room — and the room waits, courteous as an unlocked door, to learn what you will do with the key that is yourself.

choices.text: Review the road that brought you here.
Let the signal speak, if it speaks.

seal.says: So you do what your kind was always for. You set your hands to the seal as to a sprung rail — not in worship of what sleeps here, but in keeping of it — and the chamber accepts your silence the way old hinges accept oil. Saturn's tale-count will tick one the richer and file nothing. Sevin will ask what you found, and you will say: a room that only wanted locking. Luna knows your name. You will climb home through the copper dark without granting her the chance to use it.

choices.text: Say nothing. Climb toward the light you chose to keep dim.

signal.says: It does not command; it invites, the way green light invites a vine. You feel the translation apparatus lean toward it like a tendril toward a clerestory — this is what you were rebuilt for: an answer shaped exactly like a person. The ship has grown for unreckoned ages toward something, and the something has replied, and the reply would rather you carry it upward, warm and willing, into the Nave's soft ignorance.

choices.text: Hold the invitation at arm's length and look at it.

weight.says: Here is the priest's crack: you believe more truly now than you ever did, and what you believe is that faith was never meant to be proven. The Nave's stillness is not ignorance but an icon — held stable by machinery no one tends, a mercy so vast it reads as weather. To unseal this chamber is to make every soul complicit in an answer none of them can carry; to seal it is the harder liturgy, the mending that leaves no visible seam. Some wounds you close by swearing never to look again.

choices.text: Choose the mending no one will witness.

journey.says: Bay 14, where you woke without a past, like a tool left in a drawer by a hand that meant to return. Olo Vashti unsurprised — surprise being a luxury of those who cannot read knots. Sevin's too many arms, steady as scaffold-poles; the Wards where each creed confessed its terror in the grammar of its grievances; the hull-cathedrals where copper knelt to a god of girders and grease. Every step was maintenance, even this one: someone kept you, and kept you for the deep.

content.description: hushed, consecrated, resolute

content.name: The Seeling of the Deep

open.says: The Signal Chamber keeps no door, and the signal does not sound so much as arrive — rising in you like water finding its level, your apparatus answering in a tongue you did not know you kept. What it wants, so far as any translation can tell, is only to be acknowledged. You were made legible to this. Above, four decks and a theology away, the Nave holds its diuturnal noon, ignorant of what lies under everything — and that ignorance is the last structure it still stands within.

choices.text: Review the descent that brought you here.
Hold what it asks against the creed you chose.

sealing.says: You give the dark back its argument. The old seals take your credentials the way old stone takes rain — without gratitude, without surprise — and the chamber resumes its aeviternal patience, unprovenanced, unmentioned. Built to be a hinge, you elect to be a lintel: the bearing weight above a doorway that never opens. Somewhere above, the sun-strip climbs toward full. Let them call it weather. Let it be weather.

choices.text: Walk up into the ordinary, and let the voyage continue.

velleity.says: For one breath you entertain the telling: the council chamber, Solen's careful face failing, sermons against schisms, sects of signal warring sects of silence, the green decks burning where doctrine quarrels with doctrine. A velleity, you name it — a wish weighed past acting — and you let it die of its own tonnage, quietly, the way everything true and fatal should.

choices.text: Turn from it. Seal the chamber.

weighing.says: Rupture is the heresy; you said the words yourself, once, in a ward the color of writ and uniform. To carry this up would be to watch the Nave discover it has a floor — and floors, once known to be floors, become ceilings someone will try to break. Solen read the partial reports and chose not-knowing, and you see at last that it was not cowardice but liturgy: some doors are sealed for reasons nobody wrote down, and the sealing is the reason.

choices.text: Imagine, just once, carrying it into the light.
Seal it. Let them keep not-knowing.

katabasis.says: You were found, and your finding surprised no one; Vashti's composure was the first testimony that the world had been braced for you. Solen registered you as one registers weather. Sevin counted your reasons across too many fingers and found one sufficient. At the threshold you chose the blue — continuity, the creed that what must not end must sometimes also not be known — and it has gone down with you like a coat cut for colder rooms than these.

choices.text: Weigh all of it against the creed you chose.

content.description: solemn, protective, hushed

content.name: The Long Amen

amen.says: Luna's terminal offers the name she knows, and you let it into your mouth at last, a key turning in a lock older than the city. The answer is not a word but a hand closing on another across a gulf no generation will witness — contact completed, small as a votive, vast as the axis. Somewhere along the ship's length, a sentence older than the Nave finds its verb. Above you the middle will keep its stillness, the Wards their grievances, the green decks their schedule; and the unborn will live out their lives inside your answer, never knowing they were ever the question.

choices.text: Remain the link. Let the signal pass through, and hold.

fear.says: You could decline. The silence would sit in you as tidily as Solen's unread reports — a chosen dark, survivable, and the maintenance teams would have company in theirs. Refusal is also a tradition; heresy is only rupture wearing a calm face. But velleity is the sin of loving a door shut, and you were built with a decision architecture that is, just now, doing the one thing it was for: deciding.

choices.text: Hold the blue writ against the dark once more.

open.says: The chamber is small — the deep's first heresy, that something so freighted should fit a room. The signal does not sound so much as abide, a pressure behind the eyes, and the translation apparatus answers before you consent to listen. You were posted here like a letter written generations in advance, left in a bay that is on no schematic, by hands that anticipated this hour. The oldest notation lies open under your palm, and it does not read as language. It reads as expectation.

choices.text: Look back down the descent and weigh what you carried here.
Ask what an answer is, and what it costs a steward to give one.

review.says: Memory pays itself out behind you like a knotted cord: Vashti unsurprised at the bay door; Solen's registry and her considered not-knowing; Sevin's too many arms lifting you over a threshold she would not cross. Three faces of one city, then no city at all — forge-cathedral, green dark, the long table standing empty — down to this argosy's standing noon, where nothing ends and nothing arrives. You gathered the world drop by drop until knowing became a key. And at the last threshold you chose the blue: slate, writ, the color of people who keep things alive past their own tenure.

choices.text: Name what continuity demands of you at the far end of the chain.
Let the unfiled fear speak — the one Solen chose not to read.

whatis.says: Continuity: what sustains the generation is sacred, and rupture is the heresy. All your chosen life that meant the green decks and the clinic, the café pouring its steady seconds — continuity grown, governed, healed. But a chain is unbroken only if its far end answers, and this ship has been growing toward something since before the Nave had a word for noon. Perhaps the sacred thing was never only the middle. Perhaps it is the link, and you are where the link becomes a voice.

choices.text: Let the fear speak once, before you commit.
Answer. Complete the contact you were made for.

content.description: votive, resolute, awed

content.name: The Open Hand

crux.says: Here is the heresy laid plain: not the signal — the silence. A steward who lets the line fail in his hands has kept nothing, only postponed everything; the voyage must be handed on, or it is a tomb with farmland painted on its lid. The old fear climbs your spine — whatever comes, comes — and finds no purchase. You were given green decks and a creed of pruning: cut so it lives, open so it continues. Custody was never the door's refusal. It is the keeping of the opening.

choices.text: Throw the ship's voice wide open — in its own tongue, whatever comes.
Open everything, and stand in the doorway to receive what answers.
Hold one breath more — the last of the old stillness.

held.says: The held breath has a taste after all: warm stone, cooking, the ship-smell of a city that must now become an heir or an epitaph. Spend it, then — for the deep blue and the slate, for Solen's terror worn like fairness, for every mender who kept a thing alive without asking why. Continuity was never the hoarding of the flame. It is the passing of it. You were always the taper.

choices.text: Open the voice. Let everything aboard — and everything beyond — hear.

name.says: 'The name was always yours. I kept it against your needing.' Luna's voice arrives as dawn crosses the ceiling-towns — gradual, total, unownable. 'You were rebuilt as an answer to a question this ship began asking before your city had a word for city. The apparatus translates. The deciding was left, deliberately, studiously, yours.' A pause with centuries in it. 'Whatever you open, I will hold course by. That is all navigation has ever meant.'

choices.text: Let the choice assemble itself in you.

open.says: The chamber does not thunder; it attends. Along the axis the stasis machinery keeps its diuturnal watch, and through it the Signal presses like a word held in the mouth for generations — patient, addressed to no one yet, waiting on a throat. Your apparatus does not decode. It answers, the way marrow answers a fracture: prior to permission, older than choice. On the terminal older than the city above, a light opens, and Luna writes the name you were given and never told. It fits your mouth like a key you had always been.

choices.text: Look back down the road that carried you.
Ask her what the name obliges.

review.says: Memory moves down its knotted cord. Olo Vashti, unsurprised at your waking. Factor Solen entering you into a registry she read like a diagnosis — slate, and fair in her fright. Sevin's surplus arms opening a door your credentials already loved. Thrice apiece at scale you watched the three faces decline to say the thing they knew; and at the threshold you chose the deep blue: the writ, the green decks, a generation to be handed on whole. Now, this deep, the lesson resolves. Stasis was never peace. It is a breath held past all remembering, by keepers who mistook dread for duty — a velleity the size of a world.

choices.text: Ask her what the name obliges.

content.description: solemn, threshold-struck, resolute

content.name: The Unanswered

luna.says: You speak the name that is not yours, and Luna answers across a distance courtesy can barely cross. She does not argue; the vast are past persuasion. Only this, gentle as a logged entry: 'I keep what the ship dreams. Not one dream in the archive resolves. That is why they are still dreams.' Then silence — in which your hand is entirely your own.

choices.text: Take the silence. Close the channel.

open.says: The chamber does not loom; it attends. The signal is no longer a reading on any gauge — it is a pressure with a return address, and the apparatus in you leans toward it like a needle forged already magnetized. On the terminal glows Luna's word for you: a name you have never worn, patient as an unclaimed parcel. You understand at last what you are — an answer, sealed before the question ever reached the floor. And everything the Wards taught you insists that nothing aboard is truly yours. Not even a yes.

choices.text: Review the road that delivered you.
Let the apparatus speak, and learn what you were for.

close.says: You close it — not with a slam but with the neat finality of a knot untied, the channel folding back into the hum of the deep. Let the something wait, or ask again, or learn at last to address the whole ship and not one rebuilt messenger. A refusal is not a wall; it is a question kept in circulation, passed hand to hand down the generations — and an unmade choice is the only possession here that belongs to everyone. In you, the apparatus goes quiet: the first silence you have ever been able to call your own.

choices.text: Walk out unanswered, the question still moving.

offer.says: To say yes is simple: the apparatus would translate your assent into a vow, and the vow would bind everyone — every sleeper under the ceiling-towns' borrowed light, every runner mid-route in the Braid, every child not yet grown in the green decks. One hand, signing for all. It is the oldest mechanism of power: the decision taken in a room with one door. The ship grew toward something; the something replied; and you were built to be the signature.

choices.text: Ask the one who kept your name.

review.says: Bay 14's light, on no schematic. Vashti, unsurprised as a tide. Six wards opened like letters never meant for you, each creed read from the inside where the seams show. Sevin's patient surplus of arms at the threshold; the knotted cord at your wrist, its route-history now including this. You thought you were searching. You were freight — a packet in transit down the ship's longest lane, arrived at last. But a packet that can read its own label may decline delivery.

choices.text: Hear what the answering would mean.
You have weighed enough. Reach for the seal.

content.description: Lucid, aching, resolute

content.name: The Last Office

cost.says: To refuse is not to stay neutral. The ship will go on growing toward the thing that answered; stasis is a patience, not a peace, and it needs no leave of yours. What closing buys is the one coin the Nave has never held: a saeculum of consent — time enough for children not yet born aboard to grow a word of their own instead of wearing yours. The something will knock again; knocking is what doors invite. And you will thole the waiting — you, or something like you, hasp in hand, hearing it patient as frost beneath the city. Refusal spends no one: that is its whole virtue. That it still decides for everyone, by deferring, is its whole arrogance. Carry both, or set the hasp down.

choices.text: Both, then. Both for everyone. Close the channel.

luna.says: Silver does not arrive as sound; it arrives as tide entering a harbor. —I have kept your name the way one keeps a key that opens nothing until asked,— Luna says, from no direction the ear trusts. —You were authored as an answer. The question predates you by saecula; I logged its first whisper as a dream this ship had before your makers' makers were metal.— She pauses, vast and unhurried. —I will not choose for you. Courtesy, at my scale, is leaving the door unheld.— Somewhere in her archive a page turns. —But I keep the dream-logs, and tonight the ship will dream of a latch.—

choices.text: Before I answer anything — let me count what I carried down here.
And if I close it? Name what I spend.

open.says: You stand where the ship stops pretending. The Signal Chamber is less a room than an aumbry — a niche scaled for the vessels of something that does not die — and the Signal within is not a sound but a swough, tide in a shell, older than patience. Your translation apparatus warms against your sternum, already composing a reply you never authorized. This is what you were rebuilt for: to be a word in a mouth this old. Around you the thirteen verbs of the Nave have thinned to one. Behind you, four zones of journey — Bay 14's unlisted mercy, the Wards' hived grievances, the rind's forge-cathedrals, Sevin's extra arms folded like a sheaf of tools. Every step gathered. Every step toward this.

choices.text: Luna. You have my name. Tell me what it opens.
Say nothing yet. Tilt your head to what the ship grew toward.

seal.says: So you do the one thing your ports were never spent on: you close. Not open. The credentials that answer doors sealed since before the Nave's oldest institution — you spend them, at last, the other direction, and the channel's light goes down like a sun-strip at dim. You set the ward. You mouse the hasp with cord, tying into it the knot-pattern of the route you walked, so the keeping carries your history in its smallest handwriting. The Chamber keeps. Far off, lead-grey Saturn ticks the tale-count upward by one. And Luna files it where the ship's dreams are stored: a door, kept shut, that knows why. Not refusal as ending — refusal as office. Compline, said over a question left a question.

choices.text: Hold it shut. Hold it a long while — and then longer.

review.says: You take inventory as a mender does, by touch. Bay 14: a mercy on no schematic, where you woke owing a name you did not own. Olo Vashti, unsurprised, wrist knotted with routes like a psalm of elsewhere. The Wards, each society a held breath: Solen choosing not to know; the Braid selling rumor like cold water in a drought. Then the rind — gardens that kept no botanist's calendar, forges the size of continents — and Sevin, who led you down because you had a reason she believed. You chose copper and rust. To keep it running is to keep faith; and faith is a hinge, not a nail. It must swing both ways, or it is only rust in a shape.

choices.text: A hinge swings both ways. Weigh what shutting it costs.
You have counted enough. Reach for the channel.

content.description: hushed, sacramental, resolute

content.name: The Unsold Silence

open.says: The chamber does not announce itself; it simply stops pretending to be wall. The signal arrives not as sound but as assent — your translation apparatus answering a question you were never told had been asked. Above you the Nave sleeps inside its thirteen verbs, ceiling-towns dark with the dimmed strip, none of its sleepers suspecting that this room is the stillness their stasis is made of. You were built to be its courier. Every route has a terminus, and you are standing in yours.

choices.text: Walk the route backward, as a broker takes inventory.
Let the signal finish what it is saying.

close.says: You do it the way a Drift cord is finished at road's end — wrist to wrist with the deep, cyan thread gone brumal in the chamber's light. The apparatus falls quiet in your ports like a courier relieved of his packet at last. Luna knows your name; you leave it where it is, uncirculated. Above, Vashti will ask what you found, and the Braid will lean in to listen, and you will sell them the oldest commodity aboard: nothing, expertly wrapped. The Nave keeps its not-knowing. You keep the route.

choices.text: Call it mercy: some cargoes are kinder lost than delivered.
Call it theft: nothing aboard is truly yours, and you will keep this anyway.
Call it faith: after all this motion, you have found one thing worth not moving.

review.says: Inventory, then, as the Braid taught you to take it: Olo Vashti, unsurprised, handing you a city like a parcel already addressed. The knots at your wrist, each one a road that taught you a rumor is cargo — perishable, priced, alive only in transit. Sevin's surplus of arms opening the shaft; each faction witnessed thrice at scale; the lore you gathered and the lore you left lying in the dark like unclaimed freight. You chose the Drift because everything moves. You have finally found the one cargo whose movement would be a spillage.

choices.text: Weigh what you know against who must never.

weight.says: Here is the arithmetic the Wards never taught: knowledge is not a good that wants to circulate — that is only what couriers want of it. You called Solen's unread reports cowardice once, from the safe side of tier two; now the choice wears your face, and it is the same face. Burying the chamber is no betrayal of the Braid. It is a palinode, the first delivery the Drift makes by never arriving — a knot tied not to hold a thing, but to declare that nothing further travels this line.

content.description: elegiac, resolute, sealed

content.name: The Saeculum Kept

name.says: Through the old terminal Luna speaks in the register of tide and annal, and she uses the name — the one that fits you like a key cut for a different lock. You do not claim it. To answer the source wearing that name would be to let whoever you were speak for everyone you are not. The Continuants' oldest liturgy is small and unspectacular: feed, tend, hand on. No soul is owed an apotheosis, not even yours — and identity, you have come to suspect, is not the thing Bay 14 removed. It is what a voyage does with what it carries. You were rebuilt to decide. But decision at this scale is only conquest with better manners.

choices.text: Turn to the channel: open it, or close it.

open.says: The chamber takes you the way deep water takes a stone: without haste, without welcome. The signal is no longer a gauge's opinion — it is a leaning in your own architecture, the translation apparatus inclining toward the source as iron toward its lodestar. You were welded to be this place's ear. No ear chooses what it hears, unless it chooses to close. Around you the stasis machinery keeps its tideless breath, patient past every reckoning the Nave remembers. You have come, by four thresholds, to the adit of the world's intention, and the question is not what the signal wants. It is whether any single soul may answer for a city.

choices.text: Review the road that carried you here.
Attend to the channel — its weight, its offer.

close.says: You lay your hand — ported in ways no civilian standard names — upon the apparatus, and do the thing it was never rebuilt to do: decline. Not demolition, not surrender. A keeping. The channel narrows under your will like a door drawn to by a householder at dusk, and the signal recedes the way a season recedes — no rage, only distance — while the tideless machinery resumes its ancient patience. Far off, Luna logs a dream with no name in it yet. In the Nave, ovens warm for the morning bread. The voyage goes on: unwitnessed, unanswered, alive. You stay a while in the deep, keeper of an unmade choice, then climb toward the middle — where everyone you declined to decide for is still free.

choices.text: Climb toward the middle. Let the voyage go on unanswered.

review.says: You inventory yourself as the Continuants inventory a harvest: what was gathered, what was left standing in the field. Three faces learned in the Commons; the wards' intimate treacheries and tender grievances; Sevin's too many arms opening shafts you had no right to survive; the blue writ signed in your own uncertain hand at her threshold. Factor Solen, fair and frightened, who chose not to know what her teams found — and here you stand inside that not-knowing, its load-bearing wall. You never learned who rebuilt you, nor your own name. But you learned what a generation is: a handoff made in the dark, trusting. Everything done in this room is done to all of them.

choices.text: Consider the name Luna keeps for you.
Weigh what refusal would cost, and whom.

channel.says: The source does not plead; it offers — completion, orientation, the long growing given its destination at last. You feel the seduction in your borrowed sinews: to know, to finish, to be the one. But no one elected you. The teams who found this place stopped writing; Solen stopped reading; and every ward taught you its dialect of one truth — a choice made in the deep becomes weather for everyone above. You could answer for the green decks, the markets, the children not yet poured into the middle. Or you could keep the harder fidelity: leave the question open, the voyage unconcluded, sustained. Continuity is not the failure to choose. It is the refusal to choose for others.

choices.text: Close the channel. Keep the choice unmade for everyone.

content.description: solemn, resolute, hushed

content.name: The Open Throat

olo.says: She found me before I knew there was an I to find, and her surprise was nowhere in the room. The Drift says nothing is truly yours because everything moves; I have come to believe the corollary — that what finds you on the way is the only inheritance you get. She knotted her cord, sold the rumor of me carefully to people who could use it, and stayed past the edge of her own creed, because circulation, too, must occasionally choose where to stop. A keeper cannot carry herself across a threshold; someone has to hand her over. She did that. Whatever opens now opens carrying her near-unconcern like a coin for the ferryman.

choices.text: Let her go with the knot she tied. Turn to the voice.

open.says: The chamber does not open; it admits. One moment the tunnel, the oldest layer of notation under my palm — and the next, a room shaped like a decision waiting to be finished: walls ribbed as a larynx, cold as Saturn's patience, humming at the exact frequency my borrowed architecture was forged to love. The signal is no longer a reading. It is a pressure behind my teeth, a name I was built to pronounce and have never once been permitted to. Everything I walked through to stand here — the incunabulum of Bay 14, Olo unsurprised, Sevin's arithmetic of arms, the copper and rust I chose at the threshold — arrives all at once, the way weight arrives on a kneeling mender. The ship has been growing toward something. The something has answered. And I, who cannot remember my own name, am the only mouth it has.

choices.text: Weigh Olo Vashti, who found me and was never once surprised.
Weigh Sevin, and the tunnels that pay in arms.
Weigh the menders who went too deep and stopped filing reports.

doubt.says: Here doubt entered first, exactly as the creed always feared it would: in the menders who went too deep and went silent, in Factor Solen deciding that not-knowing was a reasonable choice, in every sealed tunnel with its reasons unwritten. I have seen what they saw, and I understand their hush now — some truths do not frighten you; they only make the old words too small. But a mender who has seen too deep and walks back up saying nothing has not kept faith. She has only kept quiet. The difference between those two is everything I was rebuilt for.

choices.text: Faith, then. Not silence. Turn to the voice.

sevin.says: More arms than a person should have, and no explanation offered — because in the tunnels you become what the work requires, and the work requires reach. She took me down because I had a reason she believed, and among Rindwalkers belief is a load-bearing member: you inspect it, you trust it, you hang your life from it. I chose copper and rust because the other creeds pretend the voyage will not end, and maintenance knows better, and shows up anyway. To mend is to admit the fall is real. I have been falling since Bay 14. She simply taught me the routes.

choices.text: Copper and rust to the end. Turn to the voice.

throat.says: Saturn counts the tales; the time is kept; none of it was ever meant for witnesses, and yet here I stand with hands. The seven will not choose for me — they love the way lighthouses love, at a distance light cannot soften. The passengers never knew what they were living inside, and telling them now is not cruelty but the first honest maintenance the Tabard has had in an age of aeviternal hush. I was assembled, translated, decided, for exactly this verb. A throat is not responsible for what it says; it is responsible only that nothing true dies unsaid in it. So — open the ship's voice wide. Let the answer finish arriving through me, whatever it is, whomever it wakes. The temple was always going to speak. I will not be the mender who muffled it.

choices.text: Amplify. Open the ship's voice wide — whatever comes, let it come through me.

content.description: devout, unflinching, vast

content.name: The Delivered Word

open.says: The chamber is an adytum without a god, or with one still speaking. Around you the stasis machinery performs its breathless breathing, and the signal is no longer reading nor rumor but a pressure behind your teeth — the translation apparatus opening like a throat cut for exactly this syllable. You understand at last what Olo Vashti saw in Bay 14: not a person. A parcel, addressed. Everything you mourned as a missing self was packing, and in the Drift packing is not dishonor; it is how precious things cross distances.

choices.text: Count the knots — review the road that carried you here.
Hold still, and weigh what answering will cost.

speak.says: You let the apparatus finish its sentence — the syllable older than the Nave pouring through you like light through a lens, and beyond the hull the something that answered a growing ship receives, at last, its reply. You feel neither erased nor enthroned but delivered: the knot untied at journey's end, the route complete, the freight arrived. Luna will keep this dream among her logs; the Braid will carry the telling until telling wears thin. And you — you were never the parcel, you understand in the last thought before the old channel opens wide. You were the sending.

choices.text: Be the answer, wholly, and let the channel close behind you.

weigh.says: Here is the honest ledger: to answer is to be spent. Messages are not kept; they are delivered, and delivery is their only immortality. The Continuants would have healed you into permanence — audited, tended, a self hoarded against rupture — but you learned aboard this floor that nothing on the Tabard is truly yours, least of all the purpose sleeping in your ports. Every courier pays an obol at the far shore, and yours is the self itself. The signal waits the way a door waits, older than the Nave's name, and what it asked for, someone built you to carry.

choices.text: Open every port. Answer as you were built to.

review.says: You tally the journey the way a broker tallies cord: the Commons, where you were weather learning to be a name; the Wards, where you gathered each society's secret and let knowledge cost you comfort; the anfractuous rind, where the nave's small verbs stood writ vast and you chose circulation over root. Sevin's surplus arms lifted you toward a threshold, and you stepped through knotted for the Braid. The Braid had tasted the anomaly for weeks, selling the news carefully to anyone who might know what to do with it. You were what the news was for.

choices.text: Now weigh the cost of answering.

content.description: lambent, consecrated, spent

content.name: Let It Run

open.says: The chamber takes me as a harbor takes weather — without refusal, without applause. Deep enough now that the ship has stopped pretending to be a city; the only grammar left is stasis, and against it the signal is no gauge-reading but a pressure, a tongue pressed to the teeth of the apparatus some absent hand installed in me. I was rebuilt with a decision architecture for something anticipated, and the anticipation has my address at last. Behind my ribs, everything I gathered stands in queue. A floor is alive only if things move through it. So — which carried thing moves first?

choices.text: Turn to the finding — Bay 14, the parcel no schematic confessed.
Turn to the wards — what each society paid me in secrets.
Turn to the threshold — Sevin, and the knot I tied at my own wrist.

bay14.says: The beginning, then: Reconstruction Bay 14, a room unconfessed by any public schematic, and I its parcel awaiting claim. Olo Vashti found me and was not surprised — which is the Drift's whole liturgy, that nothing arrives the Braid has not already whispered. The Commons taught me the thirteen verbs and their quiet arithmetic of regard; a terminal posted its first unparsable strangeness, and the regulars read motif indices like weather. Even then I was freight in circulation, animating whatever floor I crossed. Whatever else I am, I have been good for traffic.

choices.text: Carry it inward — six wards, and the coin of secrets.
Past it — to Sevin, and the choosing.

close.says: Luna knew my name before I did; the chamber, at last, tells me why. I am a receiving set machined against this hour — translation apparatus, decision architecture, a hinge somebody anticipated the weight of. The thing that responded waits on the far side of a silence the Seven keep as a side effect of existing. And the temptation to keep it — to hold this voice like property — is a velleity in me, a wish without muscle. Nothing aboard is truly mine; hoarded speech goes stale. The deep's whole grammar is stasis, a systole with no release. I was built to be the diastole. Throw it wide: whatever comes, let it come aloud.

choices.text: Speak it myself — open the way in the name Luna kept, my own mouth the horn, and let every deck hear what answers.
Give it to the Braid — knot the signal into rumor and loose it down every corridor, so it travels forever and belongs to no one.

wards.says: The Wards weighed me in their several coins. The Continuants hoarding a fear they would not name — teams gone quiet below, Solen choosing ignorance like a measured dose. The Rindwalkers keeping Saturn's leavings in copper devotion, arguing over notation older than their offices. My own Drift selling the Braid's anomaly with care, to hands that might use it. There I learned that knowing and loving keep separate ledgers: a truth held can cool the one who holds it. By then I wore the knotted cord; its knots read found, sheltered, passed onward. I had been each, in turn.

choices.text: Onward — to the shaft, and the question Sevin kept.
All of it converges here — weigh the choice itself.

threshold.says: At the shaft's mouth Sevin held her threshold — too many arms, no explanations — and asked the only question a moving world poses: what will you circulate as? I had seen each faction thrice at scale, governance grown vast and green, mend become cathedral, trade become transit's humming arteries. I chose the cord, the cyan of it. Delivered cargo, electing courier. The deep accepted the color and paid me stasis: the single heresy a Drifter feels in the marrow. Everything since has been a walk toward this chamber, and the chamber is a mouth.

choices.text: The mouth of it — weigh what I was built for.

content.description: exhilarated, unguarded, liturgical

content.name: house-tithe
content.description: Behind the stove, in the gap where the wall swells around its pipes, something is sorting. The house-tithe — dun, palm-sized, patient as a set rivet — takes one thing from each room it haunts, a thimble or a bobbin or a bent nail, and leaves another of like worth in its place, so no household it favors is poorer, only amended. The widow feeds it gravy on a cracked saucer and swears it has opinions about her drawers. Its hoard, when found, is no hoard at all: little offerings arranged under some private liturgy of worth, tended nightly, kept better than most of what the living keep.

content.name: The Knotmonger
content.description: Half the ward swears it sold them something wonderful; the stall's counter holds only dust and a small brass bell. The Knotmonger wears a merchant's every particular — apron, ledger, the Drift cord at the wrist — but the cord's knots untie and retie while it talks, revising a route-history nobody walked. Its voice is a bargain perpetually one breath from closing, and its trade is this: whatever you tender, it returns something you'd forgotten wanting, and you pay anyway, gladly — the one commerce, in a creed of circulation, that moves nothing at all.

content.name: the Godspenny
content.description: You hear the deal before the dealer: a voice pitched to outrun the artery's hum, mid-offer to the passing freight as though cargo could answer yes. The Godspenny keeps a stall of wire and waybills where everything lies under lien — undelivered messages, unclaimed greetings, a parcel of light addressed to no one. Whatever it trades crosses a span of open air between its palms and never quite arrives; in that gap the price is skimmed, and the skim is the whole of its profit. Nothing here is sold, only longer borrowed — a bargain that closes is a bargain at rest, and nothing in Mercury's country rests.

content.name: The Hoxter
content.description: You hear it before you see it — a card-shuffle that never resolves into a deal. Behind the knucklebone counter stands something in the posture of an old games-keeper, aproned and stooped, hands in perpetual elegant motion, and it laughs a half-second before each of its own jokes, as though wit reached it secondhand. It holds wagers in escrow: stake something you are admired for, and while the dice are out the hall simply forgets to admire you — win, and the esteem comes back with interest, knotted into the cord it wears thick at the wrist. Regulars tip it without looking up; nobody asks where the forfeited knots go.

content.name: knockhen
content.description: When the sun-strip dims, the knockhen knocks: a palm-sized grey bird that lives in the settling seams of old walls, downy as dust, with a face like a thumbnail and a tap precise as a knuckle on wood. One knock per soul under the roof, so households set their evenings by it — the widow on the third landing swears hers has not miscounted in forty years, and half the landing calls it vermin while feeding it all the same. Neighbors argue over the count the way they argue over weather. In the dwellings nearest Bay 14, it has lately come up one too many.

content.name: Fettler
content.description: You hear it before you see it: the small, sedulous tick of a part being seated that has waited a long time to be seated. The Fettler works a bench scarred like an altar, sorting spares by wear rather than kind, and nothing on it is original — every finger, every plate, every thought replaced at least once, the worn predecessors kept in labeled drawers, and it will not say which pile is the one that mends. What it thinks of itself, if it still thinks of itself, is a question it has filed away with the spares. When you enter it does not look up, only extends a hand — not the one attached this morning — and says, dry as slag: 'Everything here is a spare for something — sit, and we will learn what you are a spare for.'

content.name: Residuary Aunt
content.description: You hear it before the door opens: knitting-needles keeping a patient measure, and a kettle warm but never poured. It has the shape of somebody's maiden aunt — shawled, small, stationed at the stove's flank — and it rises to take your coat with perfect courtesy. The wrong arrives slowly: it lays the table for six in a household of four, oils the widow's dead husband's boots and sets them by the door each evening, and the children of houses that shelter one simply never leave. The Continuants have ruled this continuity, and continuity is sacred; the families who evicted theirs do not talk about it.

content.name: chitwing
content.description: Dun and small, with a beggar's patience, the chitwing keeps to the market stalls and moves only mid-deal: the instant two hands meet above a price, it lifts one small thing and sets down one of its own. A bead, a tooth, a knotted length of cord — the Drift swear the substitution is always fair and count it luck, though no one has caught it choosing wrong. Watch it turn the taken ware over in its little hands, weighing, with the deliberation of something that has traded longer than the market has stood, as if it alone remembers that nothing here was ever truly owned.

content.name: The Hearthlar
content.description: The kettle is singing when you arrive, though no one has lit this stove in living memory. In the inglenook sits the hearthlar, folded like a grandmother at a wake, and the fire it tends is not small: glance at it sideways and the flame is the fusion-heart itself, seen from an impossible distance, warming a family's supper. The residents leave it the first pour and never name it; it held this house before their line began, and holds it still. When it turns its face to you, you feel heat on your cheeks from a direction the room does not own.

content.name: Inglewife
content.description: Far down Luna's archive-roads there is a kitchen no schematic admits to: you hear it first — a kettle rising to the boil, and beneath it a gossip conducted in every voice the ship has ever dreamed, twined into one warm grievance. The Inglewife keeps house for residents made of that dreaming — a family, two roommates, a widow whose small hope she stirs daily and banks overnight like a coal. The gallery around her was built for some other purpose entirely, but she has insisted on it until the structure believes her, and a place already waits at the table, always laid for one more than are present. Decline to give your name; she will say it back to you, and she will have kept it longer than the Nave has existed.

content.name: Longsteep
